VILLAGE PRESIDENT
§ 30.001 ELECTION; TERM OF OFFICE; QUALIFICATIONS.
   The President shall be elected to office for a four-year term, according to
the method provided by statute, and until his or her successor is elected and
qualified. He or she shall be a citizen of the United States, a qualified
elector and shall have resided within the corporate limits of the village at
least one year next preceding the election at which he or she is a candidate.
No person shall be eligible for the office of President if he or she is a
defaulter to the village.
(1988 Code, § 1-5-1)
§ 30.002 OATH.
   The President shall take the customary oath of office before entering upon
the duties of his or her office.
(1988 Code, § 1-5-2)
§ 30.003 BOND AND SALARY.
   (A)   Bond. The President shall, before he or she enters upon the duties of
his or her office, execute a bond to the village in the penal sum of $3,000
with sureties to be approved by the Board of Trustees and conditioned as
required by statute. He or she shall file the same with the Village Clerk.
   (B)   Salary. The compensation and expenses of the President shall be as may
be provided for in the annual Appropriation (Budget) Ordinance and Resolution
Setting Salaries, Compensation, Expense Accounts and other Remuneration for
Employees of the Village of Dolton, as from time to time amended. The corporate
authority may fix the salary of all officers who hold elective office for a
definite term in an ordinance other than the appropriation or budget ordinance.
Said compensation, as fixed by ordinance, shall neither be increased, nor
diminished, during that term and shall be fixed at least 180 days before a
general municipal election in which voting is held for that office.
(1988 Code, § 1-5-3) (Ord. passed 12-14-1976; Ord. 00-153, passed 10-2-2000)
§ 30.004 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   General. The President shall be the executive officer of the village
and shall devote as much of his or her time to the duties of his or her office
as a faithful and efficient discharge thereof may require. He or she shall
perform all duties prescribed by law, including the village ordinances, and
shall take care that the laws and ordinances are faithfully executed.
   (B)   Approval and veto of ordinances, resolutions and motions.
      (1)   Ordinances. The President shall carefully inspect all ordinances
passed by the Board of Trustees and fix his or her official signature to such
as he or she may approve, and return them to the Village Clerk. Such ordinances
as he or she shall not approve he or she shall return to the Board of Trustees
with his or her objections thereto in writing, at the next regular meeting of
the Board of Trustees occurring not less than five days after the passage
thereof. Such veto may extend to any one or more items or appropriations
contained in any ordinance making appropriations, or to the entire ordinance.
In case the veto only extends to a part of such ordinance, the residue thereof
shall take effect and be in force. In case the President shall fail to return
any ordinance with his or her objections thereto by the time aforesaid, he or
she shall be deemed to have approved such ordinance and the same shall take
effect accordingly.
      (2)   Resolutions and motions. All resolutions or motions, as follows,
passed by the Board of Trustees, shall be deposited with the Village Clerk. If
the Mayor approves of them, he or she shall sign them. Those of which he or she
disapproves, he or she shall return to the Board of Trustees, with his or her
objections thereto in writing, at the next regular meeting of the Board of
Trustees, occurring not less than five days after the passage thereof. Such
veto may extend to any one or more items or appropriations contained in any
resolution and motion making appropriations, or to the entire resolution and
motion. In case the veto only extends to a part of such resolution and motion,
the residue thereof shall take effect and be in force. In case the President
shall fail to return any resolution and motion with his or her objections
thereto by the time aforesaid, he or she shall be deemed to have approved such
resolution and motion and the same shall take effect accordingly:
         (a)   Which create any liability against the village;
         (b)   Which provide for the expenditure or appropriation of the
village’s money; or
         (c)   To sell any village property.
   (C)   Signature.
      (1)   Sign commissions. The President shall issue certificate of
appointment to all persons appointed to office. The certificates shall be
issued under the corporate seal to the Village Clerk and shall also be signed
by the Village Clerk.
      (2)   Sign warrants. The President shall sign all warrants drawn upon the
Village Treasurer. The warrant shall state the particular fund and the
appropriation to which the warrant is chargeable and the person to whom
payable. The Village Clerk and the Village Treasurer shall countersign the
warrant.
      (3)   Authorize another to affix his or her signature.
         (a)   He or she may designate another to affix his or her signature to
any written instrument which is required to be signed by him or her. However,
before such action shall be effective, he or she shall send written notice to
the Board of Trustees of the person so designated stating:
            1.   The name of the person he or she has so designated;
            2.   What instrument the person will have authority to sign; and
            3.   Attaching to the notice a written signature of the President
executed by the designated person, with the signature of the person so
designated underneath.
         (b)   Such notice with the attached signatures shall be recorded in
the journal and then filed with the Village Clerk. When the signature of the
President is placed on a written instrument at the direction of the President
in the specified manner, the instrument in all respects shall be as binding on
the village as if signed by the President in person.
   (D)   Licenses and permits. The President shall sign all licenses and
permits granted, issued or ordered by the Board of Trustees or authorized by
the ordinances of the village, and may revoke any such license or permit for
causes provided by statute or ordinance.
   (E)   Release prisoners. The President may, for good and sufficient reason,
release any person imprisoned for violation of any village ordinance, and shall
report such release with the cause thereof to the Board of Trustees at its
first session thereafter.
   (F)   Examine records of village personnel. The President may, at any time,
examine and inspect the books, records and papers of any agent, employee or
officer of the village.
   (G)   Call for aid.
      (1)   The Village President may, when necessary, call on every male
inhabitant of the village over the age of 18 years to aid in enforcing the laws
and ordinances.
      (2)   The Village President may, subject to the authority of the
Governor, as commander in chief of the militia, call out the militia to aid in
suppressing riots and other disorderly conduct or to aid in carrying into
effect any law or ordinance.
   (H)   Reports and recommendations.
      (1)   The President shall, annually, give the Board of Trustees
information relative to the affairs of the village.
      (2)   From time to time, he or she may recommend for its consideration
such measures as he or she believes expedient.
   (I)   Conservator of the peace. He or she shall be a conservator of the
peace and shall have power to arrest or cause to be arrested, with or without
process, all persons who break the peace or are found violating any village
ordinance or any criminal law of the state. He or she shall have power to
commit arrested persons for examination and, if necessary, to detain arrested
persons in custody overnight or on Sunday in any safe place, or until they can
be brought before the proper judicial officer.
   (J)   Membership on boards and commissions.
      (1)   Electoral Board. He or she shall be a member of the Municipal
Officers Electoral Board for the purpose of hearing and passing upon objections
to nominating petitions filed in accordance with Ill. Rev. Stat. Ch. 46, para.
10-8, being 10 ILCS 5/10-8 as now or hereafter amended, and shall comply with
and perform those duties set forth in Ill. Rev. Stat. Ch. 46, para. 10-9 and
10-10, being 10 ILCS 5/10-9 and 5/10-10 as now or hereafter amended.
      (2)   Firefighters’ Pension Fund Board. He or she shall also be president
of the Board of Trustees of the Firefighters’ Pension Fund of the village.
   (K)   Liquor Control Commissioner. The President shall be the Liquor Control
Commissioner of the village and perform those duties stated in the Liquor
Control Ordinance.
   (L)   Administration of oaths. The President shall have power to administer
oaths and affirmations upon all lawful occasions.
   (M)   Rebate taxes. He or she shall have power to rebate or remit the
village taxes levied upon property listed or assessed for municipal taxation
whenever such property is destroyed by fire, in whole or in part, before the
levy thereon of the village taxes.
   (N)   Call for special election. In the event there is a vacancy in an
elective office and if for any reason there is not a quorum in office of the
corporate authorities, he or she may call for a special election to fill the
vacancy and, at the time of calling the special election, he or she shall
appoint the time and place, give notice thereof and appoint the judges of the
election.
   (O)   Execute leases and deeds.
      (1)   He or she shall have power to execute, on behalf of the village,
all leases entered into by the corporate authorities.
      (2)   He or she shall have the power, together with the Village Clerk, to
execute, on behalf of the village, all deeds of conveyance of real estate to
those parties purchasing said real estate, after the purchase price has been
paid or secured; provided, however, that, the deed of conveyance shall state
the purchase price of said property and be under the Corporate Seal.
   (P)   Duty under Diseased Animal Act. When called upon by the Director of
the state’s Department of Agriculture, the President has the duty to assist in
carrying out the provisions of the Diseased Animals Act of the state, being 510
ILCS 50/1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended.
   (Q)   Acknowledgment of instruments. The President shall have the power to
take acknowledgments of deeds, mortgages, conveyances, releases, powers of
attorney or other writings relating to the sale, conveyance or other
disposition of real estate or any interest therein whereby the rights of any
person may be affected in law or in equity.
   (R)   Employment.
      (1)   Appoint. Except as otherwise expressly provided for by the rules
and regulations of the Civil Service Commission or the Board of Fire and Police
Commissioners, or by contractual agreement entered into by the corporate
authorities, the President may appoint any employee necessary to carry into
effect the business of the village.
      (2)   Termination. Except as otherwise expressly provided for by the
rules and regulations of the Civil Service Commission or the Board of Fire and
Police Commissions, or by a contractual agreement entered into by the corporate
authorities, the President may terminate any employee whenever the President is
of the opinion that the interests of the village require termination.
(1988 Code, § 1-5-4) (Ord. 95-288, passed 8-1-1995; Ord. 99-100, passed 1-4-
1999; Ord. 13-001, passed 4-15-2013; Ord. 15-011, passed 5-4-2015; Ord. 16-015,
passed 6-6-2016; Ord. 19-009, passed 5-6-2019)
§ 30.005 VICE-PRESIDENT AND INTERIM PRESIDENT.
   (A)   Office created; appointment. There is hereby created the office of
Vice-President of the Board of Trustee of the village. The Vice-President of
the Board of Trustees of the village shall be elected bi-annually by the Board
of Trustees from among its members. The Vice-President shall serve until his or
her successor is elected.
   (B)   Duties and responsibilities.
      (1)   If a vacancy, as defined in the Illinois Compiled Statutes, as
amended, occurs in the office of President, the Vice-President of the Board of
Trustees shall immediately become the Interim President and take the customary
oath of office prescribed by statute. The Interim President, having been duly
sworn, shall immediately assume and perform the duties and possess all the
right and powers of the President until the Board of Trustees of the village
shall meet and elect one of their members Acting President.
      (2)   When a Trustee Vice-President assumes the role of Interim
President, the Trustee Vice- President designated as Interim President shall
continue to vote in his or her capacity as Trustee Vice- President. The Interim
President remains Trustee Vice-President and no Trustee vacancy is created by
the Trustee Vice-President assuming the position of Interim President.
      (3)   In the temporary absence of the President and the President Pro
Tempore, the Board of Trustees shall elect from among its members the Presiding
Officer of the Board of Trustees. The Presiding Officer of the Board of
Trustees shall vote on all questions on which the vote is taken by yeas and
nays, his or her name being called last.
(Ord. 99-102, passed 1-4-1999; Ord. 99-122, passed 9-20-1999)
§ 30.006 MAYOR PRO TEM.
   (A)   The permanent position of Mayor Pro tem shall be filled by the Senior
Trustee, unless a majority of the corporate authorities choose another Trustee
to fill the role of Mayor Pro tem. The Mayor Pro tem, during the absence,
disability or any other incapability of the Mayor, including the inability or
refusal to perform the duties of Mayor, as prescribed by statute and the
ordinances of the village, shall have the powers and duties of the office of
Mayor (Village President) while the Mayor is absent or unable to perform his or
her duties, or refuses to perform those duties as prescribed by statute,
ordinance or case law.
   (B)   (1)   Division (A) above allows for the Senior Trustee, or another
Trustee as appointed by the corporate authorities, to act as the Mayor during
his or her refusal to perform the duties of the Mayor’s office, including, but
not limited to, signing checks, payroll, contracts or other village documents
as authorized by the corporate authorities.
      (2)   The ministerial function of signing checks, payroll, contracts and
other official village documents shall vest in the Mayor Pro tem during the
Mayor’s refusal to perform and execute his or her duties, including, but not
limited to, the signing of checks, vouchers, payroll, contracts and other legal
documents approved by a majority of the corporate authorities at any regular or
special Board meeting of the Mayor and Board of Trustees.
      (3)   The name of the Mayor Pro tem appointed to fill this position shall
be added to the banks and financial institutions servicing the village.
(Ord. 24-005, passed 5- -2024; Ord. 24-008, passed 8-8-2024)
BOARD OF TRUSTEES
§ 30.020 COMPOSITION; ELECTION AND TERM; QUALIFICATIONS.
   (A)   The Board of Trustees shall consist of the President and Trustees. It
shall sit with open doors and shall keep a journal of its proceedings.
   (B)   The Village Board of Trustees shall consist of six Trustees, who shall
be elected at large. Three Trustees shall be elected at the appropriate
consolidated election every two years until their successors are elected and
have qualified. Trustees shall be elected to office according to the method
provided by statute for four-year terms. Each Trustee shall be a citizen of the
United States, a qualified elector and shall have resided within the corporate
limits of the village at least one year next preceding the election at which he
or she is a candidate. No person shall be eligible to act as a Trustee who is a
defaulter to the village.
(1988 Code, § 1-6-1)
§ 30.021 OATH.
   Before entering upon the duties of office, the members of the Board of
Trustees shall take the customary oath of office prescribed by statute.
(1988 Code, § 1-6-2)
§ 30.022 BOND AND COMPENSATION.
   (A)   Bond. No bond shall be required of any Trustee before entering upon
his or her duties.
   (B)   Compensation. The compensation and expenses for each Trustee hereafter
elected shall be as provided for in the annual Appropriation (Budget) Ordinance
and Resolution Setting Salaries, Compensation, Expense Accounts and other
Remuneration for Employees of the Village of Dolton, as from time to time
amended. The corporate authority may fix the salary of all officers who hold
elective office for a definite term in an ordinance other than the
appropriation or budget ordinance. Said compensation, as fixed by ordinance,
shall neither be increased nor diminished during that term and shall be fixed
at least 180 days before a general municipal election in which voting is held
for that office. Any Trustee serving as the Finance Committee Chairperson and/
or the Public Safety Committee Chairperson shall receive additional
compensation of $100 per month.
(1988 Code, § 1-6-3) (Ord. passed 12-14-1976; Ord. 00-153, passed 10-2-2000)
§ 30.023 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   General. The Board of Trustees shall be the legislative department of
the village government and shall perform such duties and have such powers as
may be delegated by statute to it. It shall pass ordinances, resolutions and
motions.
   (B)   Conserve peace. Each Trustee shall be a conservator of the peace and
shall have power to arrest or cause to be arrested, with or without process,
all persons who break the peace or are found violating any municipal ordinance
or any criminal law of the state. He or she shall have power to commit arrested
persons for examination and if necessary to detain arrested persons in custody
overnight or Sunday in any safe place or until they can be brought before the
proper judicial officer.
   (C)   Prescribe duties and fees. The Board of Trustees and the President may
prescribe the duties and fees of appointed officers and may require them to
execute whatever bonds are prescribed by ordinance.
(1988 Code, § 1-6-4)
§ 30.024 MEETINGS.
   (A)   Regular meetings. The Village Board shall hold its regular meetings on
the first Monday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Village Board will hold a
regular committee-of-the-whole meeting on the third Monday of each month at 6:
30 p.m. Absent an emergency, an item may not be placed on an agenda for Board
approval without that item having first been reviewed at a committee-of-the-
whole meeting.
   (B)   Special meetings. Special meetings may be called by the President of
the village or any three Trustees upon at least 24 hours’ notice to all members
and the President. Such call shall be in writing duly signed and shall be
presented to the Clerk who shall immediately cause such notice to be served
upon the President and Trustees in person or by mail. If notice is served by
mail, such notice must be mailed in the village at least 48 hours prior to the
time of the scheduled meeting. Such notices shall describe in brief the nature
or object of the call. No special meeting may be held without such written
notice being served and any action taken in the absence of such written notice
shall be void; provided, however, that, if announcement of the date and time of
a special meeting is made at a regular meeting, the requirements of written
notice shall not be necessary. Any member of the corporate authorities absent
at such regular meeting shall receive written notice of said special meeting
from the Clerk.
   (C)   Place of meetings. The Village Board’s regular and special meetings
will be held in the Village Hall at 14014 Park Avenue, Dolton, Illinois. The
Board may consider, discuss and take final action on any matters through a
conference telephone call in lieu of an in-person meeting. Additionally, any
absent member of the Board may participate in any public in-person meeting
through the use of a telephonic conference call. The call shall be broadcast
over a speaker phone or other similar device and such broadcast shall be open
to the media and the public.
   (D)   Meetings open to the public. All meetings of the Board of Trustees or
any committee or commission of the village shall be meetings open to the
public, except for:
      (1)   Personnel or collective negotiating matters between the village and
its employees or their representatives;
      (2)   Meetings where the acquisition of real property is being considered
or where a pending court proceeding against or on behalf of any unit of the
village government is being considered; and
      (3)   Meetings to consider information regarding appointment, employment
or dismissal of any employee or officer; except that, no final action may be
taken at a closed session.
(1988 Code, § 1-6-5) (Ord. passed 8-24-1971; Ord. 96-307, passed 8-20-1996;
Ord. 15-034, passed 9-8-2015; Ord. 19-010, passed 5-6-2019)
§ 30.025 PRESIDENT; VOTING POWERS.
   (A)   (1)   The Village President shall be the presiding officer of the
Board of Trustees and shall have a vote only in the event of a tie or where
one-half of the Trustees elected have voted in favor of an ordinance,
resolution or motion, even though there is no tie vote, or where a vote greater
than a majority of the corporate authorities is required to adopt an ordinance,
resolution or motion. In each instance so specified, the President shall vote.
      (2)   Nothing in this division (A) shall deprive a President pro tem from
voting in his or her capacity as Trustee.
   (B)   In the absence of the President, the Trustees shall elect one of their
number to act as a temporary Chairperson. He or she shall have only the powers
of a presiding officer and a right to vote in his or her capacity as Trustee on
any ordinance, resolution or motion.
(1988 Code, § 1-6-6)
§ 30.026 RULES AND ORDER OF BUSINESS.
   (A)   Definitions. As used in these rules on order of business for the
village, a home rule unit of government, the following terms have the meanings
ascribed to them in this subchapter unless the context clearly requires a
different meaning.
      APPROPRIATION ORDINANCE. An ordinance adopted by the Board of Trustees
appropriating funds for the purpose of conducting village business.
      APPROVED EXPENDITURE. The payment to a person, with or without approval
of the Board, in which the payment has been authorized or approved by a Trustee
or the Mayor and the payment is within the amount appropriated for such use.
      BOARD OF TRUSTEES or BOARD. The legislative body of the village and the
repository of all municipal powers which have not been specifically delegated
to some other commission, office or department of the village.
      COMMITTEE. A committee of the Board and includes standing committees and
special committees. The procedural and notice requirements applicable to the
Board shall apply to COMMITTEES.
      COMMITTEE CHAIRPERSON. The Trustee who serves as the Chair of the
committee.
      COMMITTEE MEMBER. A Trustee appointed to a committee.
      CONSTITUTION. The Constitution of the State of Illinois.
      CORPORATE AUTHORITIES. The President and Trustees of the village, then
holding office.
      MAJORITY. A simple majority of those members present and voting on a
question. Unless otherwise specified with respect to a particular Board rule,
for purposes of determining the number of members present and voting on a
question, a “present” vote shall not be counted.
      MAJORITY OF THOSE APPOINTED. An absolute majority of the total number of
Trustees appointed to a committee.
      MAYOR PRO TEM. Trustee elected from the Trustees to serve as Mayor or
President in the absence of the Mayor or President.
      MEMBERS APPOINTED. The total number of Trustees appointed to a committee.
      MEMBERS ELECTED. The total number of Trustees entitled to be elected to
the Board, irrespective of the number of elected or appointed Trustees actually
serving in office so long as six Trustees are entitled to be elected pursuant
to state law.
      PASS. The voting member is yielding to the prevailing majority and shall
be counted as a vote with the prevailing side.
      PERSON. Any individual, partnership, corporation, joint stock association
or any federal, state or local government entity or agency, and includes any
trustee, receiver, assignee or personal representative of any of those
entities.
      PRESIDENT. The chief executive officer of the village. The PRESIDENT may
be referred to as the MAYOR. The PRESIDENT or the MAYOR performs all of the
duties prescribed by law, including municipal ordinances and resolutions and is
required to see that the laws ordinances and resolutions are faithfully
executed.
      TRUSTEE. Any of the duly elected or duly appointed members of the Board
of Trustees, but not the President or Mayor.
      VICE-CHAIRPERSON. The Trustee designated by the committee to serve as
Vice-Chairperson of a committee.
      VICE-PRESIDENT and INTERIM PRESIDENT. The Vice-President is appointed
elected bi-annually by the President Board of Trustees from among its members
to serve as the Interim President in the event of a vacancy in the office of
President of the Board of Trustees.
      VILLAGE CLERK. The elected official that is the keeper of the corporate
seal and all papers belonging to the village. The Village Clerk attends all
meetings of the corporate authorities and keeps full record of their
proceedings in the journal, or as prescribed by statute.
   (B)   Organization.
      (1)   Adoption of rules. At the commencement of a term or sometime
thereafter, the Board shall adopt new rules of organization and procedure by
ordinance setting forth such rules in their entirety. Such ordinance must be
adopted by a majority of the Board of Trustees. A majority may revise or amend
these rules of the Board of Trustees of the village.
      (2)   Powers and duties of the President.
         (a)   The President shall have those powers conferred upon him or her
by the Constitution, the state and any ordinances, resolutions or motions
adopted by the Board.
         (b)   The duties of the President shall include the following:
            1.   To preside at all meetings of the Board. If the President is
absent or temporarily absent from the meeting, the President Pro tem shall
serve as the President and preside temporarily;
            2.   To open the meeting at the time at which the Board is to meet
by taking the podium and calling the members to order. The President may call
on any member, or the Village Clerk, to open the meeting;
            3.   To recognize when those members entitled to the floor may
speak;
            4.   To state question and put to vote all questions which are
regularly moved or which necessarily arise in the course of the proceedings;
            5.   To protect the Board from frivolous or dilatory action;
            6.   To restrain the members when engaged in debate;
            7.   To preserve order and decorum;
            8.   To decide all points of order subject to appeal, and to speak
thereon in preference to other members;
            9.   To inform the Board when necessary, or when any question is
raised, on any point of order or practice pertinent to the pending business;
            10.   To sign, veto or resubmit to the Board for further
consideration all acts, proceedings or orders of the Board. All writs, warrants
and subpoenas issued by order of the Board shall be signed by the President and
attested by the Village Clerk;
            11.   To sign or veto all motions, resolutions or ordinances passed
by the Board;
            12.   To sign all official documents relating to the business of
the village, including contracts, deeds and applications;
            13.   To have general supervision including the duty to protect the
security and safety, of the Board chamber, and adjoining and connecting
hallways and passages, including the power to clear them when necessary;
            14.   To have general supervision of all employees of the Board;
            15.   To enforce all constitutional provisions, statutes,
resolutions, ordinances and rules and regulations applicable to the Board;
            16.   To guide and direct the proceedings of the Board as provided
in these Board rules;
            17.   To direct the Village Clerk to correct non-substantive errors
in the minutes, resolutions or ordinances;
            18.   To decide, in accordance with these Board rules, all
questions relating to the priority of business;
            19.   To administer oaths;
            20.   To submit the names of appointees for all boards and
commissions;
            21.   To appoint temporary personnel to a vacant position whenever
there are justifiable reasons certified by a department head to the President;
            22.   These rules may be suspended by a majority vote of the
corporate authorities; and
            23.   To exercise emergency powers to appoint a qualified person to
a position for a period of 180 business days whenever the President deems that
a serious emergency exists in which substantial impairment, harm or loss of
village property, or a program of the village will result. Such person shall be
employed only during such emergency, but not to exceed 108 business days.
      (3)   Powers and duties of Vice-President and Interim President.
         (a)   The Vice-President of the Board of Trustees of the village shall
be elected bi-annually by the Board of Trustees from among its members. The
Vice-President shall serve until his or her successor is elected.
         (b)   If a vacancy, as defined in the Illinois Compiled Statutes, as
amended, occurs in the office of President, the Vice-President of the Board of
Trustees shall immediately become the Interim President and take the customary
oath of office prescribed by statute.
         (c)   The Interim President, having been duly sworn, shall immediately
assume and perform the duties and possess all the rights and powers of the
President until the Board of Trustees of the village shall meet and elect one
of their members Acting President.
         (d)   When a Trustee Vice-President assumes the role of Interim
President, the Trustee Vice-President designated as Interim President shall
continue to vote in his or her capacity as Trustee Vice-President. The Interim
President remains Trustee Vice-President and no Trustee vacancy is created by
the Trustee Vice-President assuming the position of Interim President.
         (e)   In the temporary absence of the President and the President Pro
Tempore, the Board of Trustees shall elect from among its members the Presiding
Officer of the Board of Trustees. The Presiding Officer of the Board of
Trustees shall vote on all questions on which the vote is taken by ayes and
nays, his or her name being called last.
      (4)   Powers and duties of the Village Clerk. The duties of the Village
Clerk shall include the following:
         (a)   To have custody of all papers and records of the Board, which
shall not be taken out of the Village Clerk’s custody, except in the regular
course of business of the Board;
         (b)   To keep the journal of the proceedings of the Board and, under
the direction of the President, correct errors in the journal at the next
regular Board meeting;
         (c)   To keep the minutes of the meetings of the Board and make them
available to the public under reasonable conditions;
         (d)   To keep the necessary records for the Board and to prepare the
Board calendar for each meeting;
         (e)   To certify passage or adoption of any motions, proclamations,
resolutions or ordinances by the Board, and to note thereon the date of the
Board action. Any corrections suggested regarding the certification of the
passage of a legislative matter to the President by the Village Clerk and
thereafter approved by the Board, shall be entered upon the journal;
         (f)   To attest to the President’s signature and official acts of the
Board;
         (g)   To timely file documents and records with the appropriate
government entity as required by federal, sate or local laws;
         (h)   To attend, or designate an appropriate person to attend, every
meeting of the Board; record the roll; and read such papers as directed by the
President;
         (i)   To establish the format for all documented forms and committee
records prepared by the Village Clerk;
         (j)   To administer oaths;
         (k)   To publish the Treasurer’s annual report in a newspaper
published in the village. The Village Clerk shall attach to the copy of the
Treasurer’s annual report filed with the appropriate government entity to the
effect that the copy is correct and the report was published; and
         (l)   To perform those duties as may be delegated to the Village Clerk
by the state, the county or the Board and as may be assigned by the President.
      (5)   Committees.
         (a)   From time to time, the Board of Trustees shall organize itself
into the standing committees identified below. All standing committees shall
consist of three members and shall be appointed by the Village Board. The
person named first on the committee shall be the chair thereof. Standing
committees are as follows:
            1.   Committee on Police and Fire;
            2.   Committee on Housing;
            3.   Committee on Public Works;
            4.   Committee on the Melanie Fitness Center;
            5.   Committee on Personnel;
            6.   Committee on Youth;
            7.   Committee on Public Safety; and
            8.   Committee on Finance.
         (b)   The standing committees shall be appointed annually. The
President shall be ex officio a member of all committees.
      (6)   Powers and duties of the Sergeant-at-Arms. The Chief of Police
shall be the Sergeant-at- Arms and shall perform those duties assigned to him
or her by law or as ordered by the President. Such duties shall include the
following:
         (a)   To attend the Board during its meetings and execute the commands
of the Board together with all such process issued by authority thereof; as
shall be directed to him or her by the President;
         (b)   To maintain order among spectators admitted into the Board
chambers, galleries and adjoining or connecting hallways and passages;
         (c)   To take proper measures to prevent interruption of the Board’s
meetings or proceedings; and
         (d)   To perform those duties as assigned by the President.
      (7)   Power and duties of Trustees.
         (a)   To elect from among the corporate authority, a Mayor pro tem;
         (b)   To elect from among the corporate authority, all members of
standing committees and to designate all chairpersons and vice-chairpersons of
committees; and
         (c)   To function as a legislative body pursuant to federal, state and
local laws.
      (8)   Power and duties of Mayor Pro tem. The Mayor or President Pro Tern,
during the Mayor’s or President’s absence or disability, shall perform the
duties and possess all the rights and powers of the Mayor or President but
shall only vote in his or her position as trustee.
   (C)   Conduct of business.
      (1)   Schedule. The Board shall hold its regular Board meetings on the
first and third Mondays of the month at 7:30 p.m. at Village Hall, with such
schedule subject to revision at the discretion of the President.
      (2)   Daily order. The order of business of the regular meeting of Board
of Trustees shall be as follows:
         (a)   Call to order;
         (b)   Roll call;
         (c)   Pledge of allegiance;
         (d)   General announcements;
         (e)   Citizen’s address - limited to discussion of agenda items;
         (f)   Village Clerk report:
            1.   Minutes; and
            2.   Communications.
         (g)   Engineer’s report;
         (h)   Committee reports;
         (i)   Corporate bills;
         (j)   Old business;
         (k)   New business;
         (l)   Mayor’s report;
         (m)   Citizens address - general; and
         (n)   Adjournment.
      (3)   Quorum.
         (a)   A majority of the corporate authority shall constitute a quorum
to do business. Acts done by the Board of Trustees without a quorum shall be
void. A quorum of the corporate authority must be present to begin a meeting
but also at the time of a roll call vote on any matter. Where less than a
quorum remains at a meeting, business must be suspended.
         (b)   The President shall be counted in determining whether a quorum
is present. At least four Trustees, or the President and three Trustees must be
present to constitute a quorum. Where a member of the corporate authorities
submits his or her resignation effective at the close of the meeting, he or she
shall participate in the meeting and be counted in establishing a quorum.
         (c)   In determining whether there is a quorum, members present at the
meeting are counted as present whether or not they occupy their respective
seats.
         (d)   A quorum of a committee shall be the majority of the Trustees
appointed to the committee.
         (e)   The President shall be, ex officio, a member of all committees,
but shall not be counted in determining the quorum at any committee meeting and
shall not be permitted to vote.
      (4)   Vacancies; elective offices.
         (a)   The Board of Trustees shall elect one of its members as acting
President and Mayor in the event there is a vacancy in the office of the
President. The Acting President or Mayor shall perform the duties and possess
all the rights and powers of the President or Mayor. The Acting President or
Mayor shall serve out the term of the Mayor who has vacated the office.
         (b)   If a vacancy occurs in the office of Trustee, and there remains
an unexpired portion of the term, the vacancy shall be filled by a qualified
person for the unexpired balance of the term upon recommendation by the
President, with the consent of the Board. The appointment shall be made within
60 days of the vacancy.
         (c)   If a vacancy occurs in any elective office other than that of
the President, and Trustees, and there remains an unexpired portion of the
term, the vacancy shall be filled by a qualified person for the unexpired
balance of the term upon recommendation by the President and consent of the
Board.
      (5)   Public meetings.
         (a)   The Board of Trustees shall comply with the state’s Open
Meetings Act, being 5 ILCS 120/1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended. A meeting
is any gathering of a majority of a quorum of the members of the Board of
Trustees or a Board committee, held for the purpose of discussing public
business.
         (b)   The Village Clerk must give not less than 48 hours’ pubic notice
for all meetings. The Village Clerk shall give public notice of the schedule of
regular meetings at the beginning of each calendar or fiscal year, listing the
times and places of such meetings. The annual notice must also cover the
meetings of committees of the Board and formally created advisory groups. The
Village Clerk shall also send the annual notice and changes in the schedule of
regular meetings must also be sent to any news media that has filed an annual
request for such notice.
         (c)   A special meeting may be called by the President or three
Trustees. Public notice, except for an emergency meeting, along with the
agenda, must be given at least 48 hours before the meeting by posting the
notice at Village Hall and the place where the meeting will be held and
furnishing notice and agenda to the registered news media. The President,
Village Clerk and the Trustees shall each be served notice of the special
meeting by U.S. certified mail return receipt requested or by leaving a copy at
the President, Village Clerk or members respective residence delivered via
messenger, messenger service or overnight carrier, with proof of service.
         (d)   An emergency meeting may be called by the President when the
President deems it necessary. Notice of the emergency meeting must be given as
soon as practicable, but in any event prior to the holding of such meeting, to
any news medium which has filed an annual request for notice. Notice must also
be posted in Village Hall. Trustees may be notified of an emergency meeting via
telephone with certification of said telephone notice or facsimile transmission
with proof of transmission.
      (6)   Closing meetings to the public.
         (a)   Board meetings and committee meetings of the Board of Trustees
may be closed to the public, only if:
            1.   The subject to be considered at that meeting is one of the
enumerated exceptions listed in of the Open Meetings Act;
            2.   A majority of a quorum at a meeting open to the public has
voted to have such a closed meeting;
            3.   Proper notice was given for the meeting at which the vote was
taken;
            4.   The vote of each member on the question of holding the meeting
closed is recorded and entered into the minutes of the open meeting; and
            5.   The motion to hold the closed session and the minutes of the
meeting contain a citation to the specific exception which the authorizes tie
closing of the meeting to the public.
         (b)   All final action must take place in open session. The President
may, prior to the Board taking final action, provide or recognize a Trustee to
provide an explanation of the matter to be considered.
         (c)   A closed session authorized by a proper vote can take place as
part of a properly noticed meeting open to the public without need for any
further notice or an indication in the agenda that
closed session will be held. Where a closed session is to be held other than as
part of an open meeting, separate notice regarding that meeting must be given
to the public and the registered news media.
         (d)   The Board may, by a single vote, authorize a series of meetings,
a portion or portions of which are proposed to be closed to the public;
provided that, each meeting in the series involves the same particular matter
or matters and is scheduled to be held within three months of the vote.
      (7)   Voting.
         (a)   Voting upon all ordinances and upon any resolutions or motions
creating liabilities or expenditures, shall be by “yeas” and “nays” shall be
taken by roll call of each member, and shall be recorded in minutes of the
meeting. The official copy of the ordinance or resolution itself shall list the
names of each person voting and how he or she voted. The Board shall not
conduct any votes by secret sealed ballot even if the process is conducted at a
public meeting.
         (b)   Voting upon matters not involving the adoption of a ordinance
for whatever purpose or a resolution creating a liability against the village
or requirement the expenditure or appropriation of money or any other matter
not required by statute to receive any particular vote may be adopted by a
simple majority of the quorum.
         (c)   Unless otherwise specified herein, all ordinances, for whatever
purpose, and only those resolutions or motions which create any liability
against the village, or are for the expenditure or appropriation of money,
shall require the concurrence of a majority of the corporate authorities then
holding office, including the President.
         (d)   All ordinances, resolutions or motions to convey real estate
when no longer needed or in the best interest of the village to keep, to lease
to another for terms up to 99 years when in the best interest of the village,
acceptance of bids and contracts for the sale of real estate, and the purchase
o or lease from another by installment contract not exceeding a 20-year term
with accompanying special taking authority, shall require the affirmative vote
of a majority of the corporate authorities then holding office, including the
President.
         (e)   All ordinances, resolutions or motions for the appropriation of
money, for supplemental appropriation of money, the transfer of money within a
fund, or additional appropriations of money, shall require the affirmative vote
of a majority of the corporate authorities then holding office, including the
President.
         (f)   All ordinances, resolution or motions for the sale of personal
property by ordinance with or without bids; by converting into some other form
of personal property useful to the village by using the material in the
property; or by trading in on the purchase of similar article, with or without
bid, shall require the affirmative vote of a majority of the corporate
authorities then holding office, including the President.
         (g)   The President may vote:
            1.   Where the vote of the Trustees has resulted in a tie;
            2.   Where one-half of the Trustees elected have voted in favor of
an ordinance, resolution or motion, even though there is no tie;
            3.   Where a vote of the corporate authorities is required; or
            4.   Where a vote greater than majority of the corporate
authorities is required by state statute or local ordinance to adopt an
ordinance, resolution or motion.
         (h)   The Mayor shall have authority to veto all ordinances,
resolution or motions without regard to their subject, and the power to veto a
line item on appropriation ordinances. If the Mayor vetoes an ordinance or a
resolution or a motion susceptible to veto, the Board, upon the receipt of the
Mayor’s written objections, shall reconsider the same at “the next regular
meeting”. The Board may, at its next regularly scheduled meeting after a
measure adopted by the Board has been returned to it with a veto, move to
reconsider the vote by which the measure was originally adopted. If a majority
of the quorum adopted the motion to reconsider, the Board may then move to
adopt the measure notwithstanding the veto or that it be passed over the veto.
Two-thirds of the members of the Board then holding office must vote in favor
of that motion in order for the measure to be adopted. If the measure does not
receive two-thirds of the vote of the members of the Board then holding office,
the measure fails.
         (i)   The Board may reconsider its vote and actions upon questions,
motions, resolutions or ordinances and reverse or rescind its previous actions
upon a motion to reconsider brought by any Trustee, at any subsequent or
regular Board meeting; except that, where the rights of other parties have
intervened. The Board may reconsider its vote where a third party has
intervened and the Board seeks to reconsider its previous action based upon an
erroneous legal view.
         (j)   Amendments to resolution and or ordinances must be in writing
and submitted to the President.
         (k)   Telephone voting.
      (8)   Public participation. At the conclusion of scheduled business of
all regularly scheduled Board meetings, the public will be allowed 30 minutes
for public views and participation.
(1988 Code, § 1-6-7) (Ord. 95-278, passed 6-6-1995; Ord. 98-365, passed 4-20-
1998; Ord. 98-387, passed 10-5-1998; Ord. 99-103, passed 1-4-1999; Ord. 99-123,
passed 9-20-1999; Ord. 99-124, passed 9-20-1999; Res. 13-R-0013, passed 6-3-

passed 3-2-2020; Ord. 21-018, passed 10-4-2021)
§ 30.027 ORDINANCES, RESOLUTIONS AND MOTIONS.
   (A)   Approval and veto. All resolutions and motions which create any
liability against the village, or which provide for the expenditure or
appropriation of its money, or which authorize the sale of any village
property, and all ordinances shall be decided by a roll call vote, and all
ordinances passed by the Village Board shall be deposited with the Village
Clerk. If the President approves of them, he or she shall sign them; those of
which he or she disapproves, he or she shall return to the Board of Trustees
with his or her written objections at the next regular meeting of the Board of
Trustees occurring not less than five days after their passage. The President
may disapprove of any one or more sums appropriated in any ordinance,
resolution or motion making an appropriation and, if so, the remainder shall be
effective. However, the President may disapprove entirely of an ordinance,
resolution or motion making an appropriation. If the President fails to return
any ordinance or any specified resolution or motion with his or her written
objection within the designated time, it shall become effective despite the
absence of his or her signature.
   (B)   Passing over veto. Every resolution, motion or ordinance which is
returned to the Trustees by the President with his or her written objections
shall be reconsidered by the Trustees. If, after such reconsideration, two-
thirds of all the Trustees then holding office shall agree to pass an
ordinance, resolution or motion, notwithstanding the President’s refusal to
approve it, then it shall be effective. The vote on the question of passage
over the President’s veto shall be by yeas and nays and shall be recorded in
the journal.
(1988 Code, § 1-6-8)
§ 30.028 RESTRICTION ON HOLDING OTHER OFFICE.
   No Trustee may accept or be appointed to or hold any lucrative office by
appointment of the President during the term of office for which said Trustee
was elected. Any such appointment is void.
(1988 Code, § 1-6-9)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 31.001 APPOINTMENT TO AND REMOVALS FROM OFFICE.
   (A)   Appointments. The President, by and with the advice and consent of the
Board of Trustees, shall appoint all officers of the Village whose appointments
are not otherwise provided for by law, and whenever a vacancy shall occur in
any office which by statute or ordinance the President is authorized to fill,
he or she shall, at a regular meeting of the Board of Trustees, communicate to
the Board of Trustees the name of his or her nominee to such office, who shall
be appointed upon a majority vote of the Board of Trustees. If the Mayor’s
nominee fails to obtain the majority vote of the Board of Trustees, the Mayor
may appoint a different nominee as a temporary or interim officer at that
regular meeting after the vote by the Board is taken, the temporary or interim
officer shall occupy the office until the next regular meeting of the Board of
Trustees, but in no event shall the temporary or interim appointee serve as a
temporary or interim appointee for a period in excess of 14 days. At the end of
this interim or temporary appointee’s term, at a regular meeting, the Mayor
shall submit a nominee for the appointed office to the Board of Trustees for
its consent. The Mayor may not present a nominee for the same appointed office
more than twice during his or her term of office.
   (B)   Removals. Except where otherwise provided by statute, the President
may remove any officer appointed by him or her on any formal charge whenever he
or she is of the opinion that the interests of the village demand removal. He
or she shall report the reasons for the removal to the Board of Trustees at a
meeting held not less than five, nor more than ten, days after the removal. If
the President fails or refuses to report to the Board of Trustees the reasons
for the removal or if the Board of Trustees, by a two-thirds vote of all its
members authorized by law to be elected, disapproves of the removal, the
officer thereupon shall be restored to the office from which he or she was
removed. The vote shall be by yeas and nays and shall be entered in the
journal. In the event of restoration, the officer shall give a new bond and
take a new oath of office. No officer shall be removed a second time for the
same offense.
(1988 Code, § 1-8-1)
   (C)   Employee hiring. The hiring of all employees, other than appointed
officers, and the amount of their initial salary shall be approved by the Board
of Trustees prior to an offer of employment is made. The Board of Trustees
shall be provided with the resumes and any additional information compiled by
the village for all applicants prior to their approval.
   (D)   Appeal of employee termination. Any employee, other than appointed
officers and employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement, may appeal
their termination of employment to the Board of Trustees. The Board of Trustees
shall approve or disapprove the termination after allowing the employee and
mayor to submit written evidence no later than the second regular Village Board
meeting after termination. If the Board of Trustees disapproves the
termination, the employee shall be restored to the position from which he or
she was removed.
(Ord. 18-002, passed 5-7-2018; Ord. 24-014, passed 10-7-2024)
§ 31.002 RESIDENCY REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   All village officers or employees, except for paid on call fire and
police personnel, and Village Commissioners, unless otherwise exempt by state
statute or village ordinance, shall reside within the village or establish
their residency within the corporate limits of the village within one year from
their date of employment or date of promotion. Failure to timely establish such
residence shall result in the termination of employment.
   (B)   All village officers and employees hired prior to 12-1-1997, unless
otherwise exempted herein or by state statute or village ordinance, shall
reside within the corporate limits of the village or not more than 22 miles
from the nearest corporate limits of the village.
   (C)   All village officers and employees hired prior to 12-1-1997, who
reside within the corporate limits of the village or reside not more than 22
miles from the nearest corporate limits, are hereby “grandfathered in” at their
said current address and current position for the purposes of compliance with
this section.
(1988 Code, § 1-8-2) (Ord. 86-101, passed 1-6-1986; Ord. 93-227, passed 9-21-
1993; Ord. 97-350, passed 12-1-1997; Ord. 98-391, passed 12-7-1998)

   The salaries and classifications for village employees and officials are
hereby adopted by reference and incorporated herein as if set out in full.
