§ 31.004 VACATIONS.
   (A)   Vacations for other than fire and police personnel. Annual vacation
periods with full pay shall be allowed each full-time employee and full-time
appointed officer of the village, including those paid on an hourly pay basis,
according to the following schedule:
      (1)   Two weeks of vacation each year for those who have served the
village for a period of one year and less than seven years. Such allowance
shall not vest until the full year of service has been completed. After
completion of the first year, such allowance shall vest on the first of each
calendar year following;
      (2)   Three weeks of vacation each year for those who have served the
village for a period of seven years and less than 20 years. Such allowance
shall not vest until seven full years of service have been completed and shall
vest each year thereafter on the first of the calendar year following;
      (3)   Four weeks of vacation each year for those who have served the
village for a period of 20 years. Such allowance shall not vest until 20 full
years of service have been completed and shall vest each year thereafter on the
first of the calendar year following;
      (4)   Only one vacation allowance shall be given in any one calendar
year; and
      (5)   Each such employee and officer shall be allowed an additional day
of vacation in the event, during the vacation period taken, one of the
following holidays occurs: Juneteenth; Memorial Day; New Year’s; Christmas;
Thanksgiving; Labor Day; Independence Day; Lincoln’s Birthday; or Veteran’s
Day.
   (B)   Vacations for Fire Department and Police Department personnel. Annual
vacation periods with full pay shall be allowed each full-time member of the
Fire Department and of the Police Department according to the following
schedule:
      (1)   Two weeks of vacation each year for those who have served the
village for a period of one year and less than seven years. Such allowance
shall not vest until the full year of service has been completed. After
completion of the first year, such allowance shall vest on the first of each
calendar year following;
      (2)   Three weeks of vacation each year for those who have served the
village for a period of seven years and less than 20 years. Such allowance
shall not vest until seven full years of service have been completed and shall
vest each year thereafter on the first of the calendar year following;
      (3)   Four weeks of vacation each year for those who have served the
village for a period of 20 years. Such allowance shall not vest until 20 full
years of service have been completed and shall vest each year thereafter on the
first of the calendar year following;
      (4)   Only one vacation allowance shall be given in any one calendar
year; and
      (5)   In addition to the allowance set forth in divisions (B)(1), (B)(2)
and (B)(3) above, there shall be allowed ten days of furlough for members of
the Police Department and eight days of furlough for members of the Fire
Department.
   (C)   Designation of vacation periods. The head of each department may
designate by rule the time when each employee under his or her supervision may
take a vacation, and shall submit his or her rulings to the President for
purposes of information and approval. The times which heads of departments or
appointed officials choose to take their vacations shall be approved by the
President. When practicable, due consideration shall be given to employees
having the longest period of continued service.
   (D)   Vacations not cumulative. The above designated vacation periods shall
not be considered cumulative, and no vacation with pay shall be allowed in any
calendar year in excess of the periods above established. It is mandatory that
a vacation be taken during the calendar year and no employee or officer shall
be permitted to work and collect vacation pay.
   (E)   Number on vacation limited. The respective heads of the departments of
the village are authorized to limit the number of employees on vacation at any
time.
   (F)   Divided vacations. A vacation may be divided into more than one period
within any calendar year at the reasonable discretion of the department head.
(1988 Code, § 1-8-3-2) (Ord. passed 9-9-1975)
§ 31.005 HOLIDAY PAY.
   In the event an individual other than a firefighter or police officer is
scheduled to work on one of the holidays listed in §
31.004(A)(5) of this chapter, such individual shall be paid an additional
amount equal to the individual hourly rate of pay for the number of hours
worked on said holiday.
(1988 Code, § 1-8-3-3)
§ 31.006 CIVIL SERVICE.
   (A)   General. The offices and places classified by the Civil Service
Commission shall constitute the classified civil service of the village. No
appointment to any of such offices or places shall be made except under and
according to the rules hereinafter mentioned.
   (B)   Rules. The Commission shall make rules, and make changes in such rules
as will carry out the purpose, intent and provisions of this section and for
procedures relative to examinations, appointments, promotions and removals in
offices and places. All such rules and changes shall be printed immediately and
be available for distribution. Notice must be published in the local newspaper
as follows:
      (1)   Of the place where the rules may be obtained; and
      (2)   Of the date not less than ten days subsequent to the date of
publication when the rules or changes in the rules shall become effective.
   (C)   Civil service examinations.
      (1)   Applicants to be examined. All applicants for offices or places in
the classified service shall be subject to examination. Such examinations shall
be public, competitive and open to all citizens of the United States subject,
however, to specified limitations as to residence, age, health, habits and
moral character as may be determined by the Commission in the adoption and
publication of its rules. However, the age limitations in such rules shall not
apply to persons entitled to military preference in accordance with the
provisions of 65 ILCS 5/10-1-16 as now or hereafter amended. The examinations
shall be practical in their character and shall relate to those matters which
will fairly test the relative capacity of the applicants to discharge the
duties of the positions to which they seek to be appointed, and shall include
test of physical qualifications and health, and when appropriate, of manual
skill. No part of said examination shall relate to political or religious
opinions or affiliations.
      (2)   Notice of examinations. Notice of the time, place, general scope
and fee of every examination shall be given by the Commission by publication
for two weeks in a local newspaper. Such notice shall also be posted in a
conspicuous place in the Village Hall for two weeks before such examination.
      (3)   Register of eligibles. A register of persons for each grade or
class of positions in the classified service of the village shall be prepared
by the Commission. Such persons shall take rank upon the register as candidates
in the order of their relative excellence as determined by examination, without
reference to priority of time of examination.
   (D)   Appointments. The head of the department or office in which a position
classified under this section is to be filled shall notify the Commission of
that fact, and the Commission shall certify to the appointing officer the name
and address of the candidate standing highest upon the register for the class
or grade to which the position belongs. However, in cases of laborers where a
choice by competition is impracticable, the Commission may provide by its rules
that the selections shall be made by law from among those candidates proved fit
by examination, but laborers who have previously been in the service and were
removed because their services were no longer required shall be preferred and
be reinstated before other laborers are given positions, preference being given
to those who have had the longest term of service, and laborers in the employ
of the municipality who have been employed under temporary authority for three
years or more or during parts of three or more calendar years shall be
preferred also and shall be placed upon the register for such positions without
examination and shall be certified before other laborers are given positions,
preference being given to those laborers under temporary authority who have had
the longest term of service in such positions. In making such certificate, sex
shall be disregarded, except when some statute, the rules of the Commission or
the appointing power specifies sex. The appointing officer shall notify the
Commission of each position to be filled separately and shall fill such place
by the appointment of the person certified to him or her by the Commission
therefor. Original appointment shall be on probation for a period of not to
exceed six months to be fixed by the rules. The Commission may strike off names
of candidates from the register after they have remained thereon more than two
years. At or before the expiration of the period of probation, the head of the
department or office in which a candidate is employed may, by and with the
consent of the Commission, discharge him or her upon assigning in writing his
or her reason therefor to the Commission. If he or she is not then discharged,
his or her appointment shall be deemed complete. To prevent the stoppage of
public business or to meet extraordinary exigencies, the head of any department
or office may, with the approval of the Commission, make temporary appointment
to remain in force not exceeding 120 days, and only until regular appointment
under the provisions of this section can be made.
   (E)   Removals or suspensions.
      (1)   Except as hereinafter provided in this division (E), no officer or
employee in the classified civil service of the village who is appointed under
the rules and after examination shall be removed or discharged or suspended for
a period of more than 30 days, except for cause upon written charges and after
an opportunity to be heard in his or her own defense. Such charges shall be
investigated by or before the Civil Service Commission or by or before some
officer or board appointed by the Commission to conduct such investigation. The
finding and decision of such Commission or investigating officer or board, when
approved by the Commission, shall be certified to the appointing officer and
shall forthwith be enforced by such officer. Nothing in this section shall
limit the power of any officer to suspend a subordinate for a reasonable
period, not exceeding 30 days; except that, any employee or officer suspended
for more than five days or suspended within six months after a previous
suspension shall be entitled, upon request, to a hearing before the Civil
Service Commission concerning the propriety of such suspension. In the course
of an investigation of charges, each member of the Commission and of any board
so appointed by it and any officer so appointed may administer oaths and may
secure by its subpoena both the attendance and testimony of witnesses and the
production of books and papers relevant to such investigation.
      (2)   Any person who shall be served with a subpoena to appear and
testify or to produce books and papers, issued by the Commission or by any
Commissioner or by any board or person acting under the orders of the
Commission in the course of an investigation conducted by the Commission, and
who shall refuse or neglect to appear or to testify or to produce books and
papers relevant to the investigation as commanded in such subpoena, is guilty
of a misdemeanor and shall, on conviction, be punished by a fine as provided
for in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances. The fees of witnesses for attendance and
travel shall be the same as the fees of witnesses before the circuit courts of
the state and shall be paid from the appropriation for the expenses of the
Commission. Any circuit court of the state, upon application of any such
Commissioner or officer or board, may, in its discretion, compel the attendance
of witnesses, the production of books and papers and giving of testimony before
the Commission, or before any such Commissioner, investigating board or
officer, by attachment for contempt or otherwise in the same manner as the
production of evidence may be compelled before such court. Every person who,
having taken an oath or made affirmation before a Commissioner or officer
appointed by the Commission authorized to administer oaths, shall swear or
affirm willfully, corruptly and falsely shall be guilty of perjury and upon
conviction shall be punished accordingly.
   (F)   Exemptions from provisions.
      (1)   Effective 4-15-1986, all employees included in the certified
bargaining unit(s) hereinafter described shall be removed from all provisions
of this section and similar provisions of the Illinois Revised Statutes
pertaining to civil service commissions in cities and villages. Hereafter, all
matters pertaining to promotions, suspensions, discharges and all rules of
employee conduct shall be solely governed by agreement between the village and
the bargaining unit. Except, however, that, nothing herein shall prohibit the
Village President and Board of Trustees from designating the Civil Service
Commission as the authority responsible for testing and processing applicants
for entry level positions within said bargaining unit so long as all other
provisions of the applicable agreement relating to the filling of vacancies are
complied with.
      (2)   The following classifications of affected employees are subject to
the exemption described in this division (F): all employees in the Public Works
Department; classifications of driver, laborer, equipment operator, mechanic
and custodian, but excluding all clerical employees, foreperson, confidential
and managerial employees and supervisors as defined by the Act; and all other
employees of the village.
(1988 Code, § 1-8-4) (Ord. 86-115, passed 4-15-1986)
§ 31.007 ELECTIONS.
   Elections for village officers shall be held as provided by statute and at
the time prescribed by statute, pursuant to appropriate provisions of Ill. Rev.
Stat. Ch. 24 and 46, as may be from time to time amended.
(1988 Code, § 1-11-1)
§ 31.008 CHECK SIGNING REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   The village hereby establishes a standard operating policy for the
purposes of signing checks.
      It is the intention of the village to implement these practices in order
to maintain the proper Internal controls for financial matters of the village.
   (B)   Check-signing authority shall reside with the following:
      (1)   Mayor;
      (2)   Mayor Pro tem or most senior Trustee; and
      (3)   Village Clerk.
   (C)   Signing of checks shall be authorized as follows.
      (1)   All village-issued checks will require a minimum of two of the
three signatures identified in division (B) above.
      (2)   Individuals shall not be a signatory for a check to which he or she
is the payee.
      (3)   Each authorized signer may choose to sign village checks manually
or with a signature stamp.
(Ord. 2024-12, passed 9-12-2024)
VILLAGE CLERK
§ 31.020 ELECTION; TERM OF OFFICE; QUALIFICATIONS.
   The Village Clerk shall be elected to office according to the method
provided by statute. His or her term shall be for a period of four years and
until his or her successor is elected and qualified. He or she shall be a
citizen of the United States, a qualified elector and shall have resided within
the corporate limits of the village at least one year next preceding the
election at which he is a candidate. No person who is a defaulter to the
village is eligible for the office of Village Clerk.
(1988 Code, § 1-7-1)
§ 31.021 OATH.
   The Village Clerk shall take the customary oath of office prescribed by
statute before entering upon the duties of office.
(1988 Code, § 1-7-2)
§ 31.022 BOND AND SALARY.
   (A)   Bond. The Village Clerk shall execute, acknowledge and deliver to the
village a bond in the penal sum of $50,000 with two good and sufficient
sureties or with an insurance company authorized by the state’s Director of
Insurance to engage in surety business in the state. Said bond shall be
conditioned as provided by law and must be approved by the President and Board
of Trustees. Such bond must be delivered within ten days of taking the office
of Village Clerk and must be filed with the Village Treasurer.
   (B)   Salary. The compensation and expenses of the Village Clerk as may be
provided for in the annual Appropriation (Budget) Ordinance and Resolution
Setting Salaries, Compensation, Expense Accounts and other Remuneration for
Employees of the Village of Dolton, as from time to time amended. The corporate
authority may fix the salary of all officers who hold elective office for a
definite term in an ordinance other than the appropriation or budget ordinance.
Said compensation, as fixed by ordinance, shall neither be increased nor
diminished during that term and shall be fixed at least 180 days before a
general municipal election in which voting is held for that office.
(1988 Code, § 1-7-3) (Ord. passed 7-8-1980; Ord. 00-153, passed 10-2-2000)
§ 31.023 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   Administer oaths. The Village Clerk shall have power to administer
oaths and affirmations on all lawful occasions.
   (B)   Additional duties. The Village Clerk shall, in addition to the above,
perform the following duties.
      (1)   Office. He or she shall keep his or her office for the transaction
of village business at the Village Hall.
      (2)   Issue notices. He or she shall issue notices to the President and
members of the Village Board and, when directed by that body, to the members of
the different committees of that body, and to all persons whose attendance will
be required before that body or any such committee when so directed, and shall
also issue and cause to be served notices of meetings.
      (3)   Attest licenses. He or she shall attest all the licenses granted by
the President or Board of Trustees under the ordinances of the village.
      (4)   Deliver documents and ordinances.
         (a)   He or she shall, without delay, deliver to the officers of the
village and to all committees all bills, resolutions, communications and other
documents referring to such officers or committees.
         (b)   He or she shall, without delay, deliver to the President all
ordinances or resolutions under his or her charge, which may require approval
or other action by the President, with all papers and information on which the
same were founded.
      (5)   Custodian of Corporate Seal. He or she shall keep the Corporate
Seal and affix the same to all papers which require it.
      (6)   Keeper of records. He or she shall keep all records and papers
belonging to the village.
      (7)   Attend meetings. He or she shall attend all the meetings of the
President and Board of Trustees, and keep a full record of its proceedings in
the journal.
      (8)   Record ordinances. All ordinances passed by the President and Board
of Trustees shall be recorded by the Clerk in a book kept and used exclusively
for that purpose before the next regular meeting after they go into effect. He
or she shall cause ordinances imposing a fine or penalty or making an
appropriation to be duly published. The Clerk shall note at the foot of the
record of each ordinance a memorandum of the date of its passage and approval
or otherwise becoming effective and, if published, the date of the publication
of such ordinance. The original shall be filed in the office of said Clerk with
a certificate of publication or posting attached to ordinances requiring
publication.
      (9)   File tax levy ordinance. He or she shall, on or before the second
Tuesday in September in each year, file with the County Clerk a certified copy
of the ordinance in which the total amount of appropriations for all corporate
purposes of the village legally made are levied and assessed for the current
fiscal year.
      (10)   Furnish information to the state’s Health Department. He or she
shall, annually before May 1, furnish the state’s Department of Public Health
with a list of the names of the President, the Clerk, the Health Inspector and
all members of the Board of Health. This list shall indicate which person is
charged with the enforcement of quarantine regulations. He or she shall also
advise of vacancies as soon as they exist.
      (11)   Warrants.
         (a)   He or she shall countersign all warrants drawn upon the
Municipal Treasurer. Such warrant must state the particular fund and
appropriation to which the warrant is chargeable and the person to whom
payable. He or she shall prepare all warrants for the payment of money, sign
and deliver the same when called for after they have been countersigned by the
President, taking a proper receipt therefor.
         (b)   He or she shall sign all warrants of commission to all municipal
officers, elected or appointed, except the Municipal Clerk, Trustees and
President and shall affix the Corporate Seal to said warrant.
      (12)   Certify transcripts as evidence. He or she shall have authority to
certify, for use as evidence in court, copies of all papers duly filed in his
or her office and transcripts from the journal and other records and files of
his or her office.
      (13)   Filing bonds. He or she shall keep on file all bonds required to
be filed by all elected or appointed officers. He or she shall keep in his or
her office in a book used exclusively for that purpose, a correct list of all
the outstanding bonds of the village showing the number and amount of each and
for and to whom the bonds were issued.
      (14)   Nomination and election duties.
         (a)   Nominations for elective office. He or she shall receive and
file all objections to nomination papers.
         (b)   Conduct elections. He or she shall be deputy registrar of voters
and shall conduct all regular and special village elections.
         (c)   Provide election facilities. He or she is hereby directed to
prepare the necessary ballots, ballot boxes, instructions to voters, polling
places and other election supplies and equipment and take all steps provided by
law to properly hold and conduct each municipal election in accordance with
this code and any of the village ordinances and the laws of the state.
         (d)   Publish sample election ballot. Prior to the date of each
election, he or she shall cause a sample of each ballot to be voted upon at
such election to be published in one or more newspapers published in the
village.
         (e)   Notice of election. He or she shall cause notice of each
election to be given not more than 30, nor less than 15, days in advance of the
election by publication in one or more newspapers published in the village. The
notice shall state the time and places of election, the officers to be elected
and the proposition or propositions, if any, to be voted upon at the election.
         (f)   Notify elected officer. Within five days after the result of an
election is declared or an appointment made, he or she shall notify all persons
elected or appointed to office of their election or appointment, and unless
such persons shall respectively qualify in ten days after such notice, the
office shall become and be vacant.
         (g)   Call for special election. In the event there is a vacancy in an
elective office and if for any reason there is not a quorum in office of the
corporate authorities, and if there be a vacancy in the office of President, he
or she may call for a special election to fill the vacancy and, at the time of
calling the special election, he or she shall appoint the time and place, give
notice thereof and appoint the judges of election.
      (15)   Membership on boards and commissions.
         (a)   Electoral Board. He or she shall be a member of the Electoral
Board which passes on objections to nomination papers.
         (b)   Board of Local Improvements. The Village Clerk shall be the
Secretary of the Board of Local Improvements and shall keep the minutes of said
Board of Local Improvements and perform such other duties as may be required of
said office.
         (c)   Zoning Board of Appeals. The Village Clerk shall serve as the
secretary of the Zoning Board of Appeals and shall keep the minutes of said
Zoning Board of Appeals and shall perform such other duties as may be required
of said office.
         (d)   Planning Commission. The Village Clerk shall serve as Secretary
of the Planning Commission and shall keep the minutes of said Planning
Commission and shall perform such other duties as may be required of said
office.
         (e)   Firefighters’ Pension Fund Board. He or she shall be a member of
the Board of Trustees of the Firefighters’ Pension Fund of the village.
      (16)   Treasurer’s annual report.
         (a)   He or she shall publish the Treasurer’s annual report at least
once in one or more newspapers published in the village.
         (b)   He or she shall furnish the Treasurer an affidavit with a true
and correct copy of the Treasurer’s annual report filed with him or her and
that the account was published, the date of publication and the name of the
newspaper in which published.
      (17)   Notice of injury. He or she shall receive notices of injury from
persons about to commence an action for injuries to the person against the
village and shall for-ward the same to the insurance carrier insuring the
village for such actions.
(1988 Code, § 1-7-4)
§ 31.024 RESTRICTION ON HOLDING OTHER ELECTIVE OFFICE.
   The Village Clerk shall hold no other elective office in the village
government during his or her term of office.
(1988 Code, § 1-7-5)
§ 31.025 VILLAGE COLLECTOR.
   (A)   Clerk shall not serve as Collector. Effective upon the expiration of
the 2001-2005 term of elected office for the Village Clerk, the Village Clerk
shall cease to serve as the Village Collector. Effective upon the commencement
of the 2005-2009 term of elected office for the Village Clerk, the Village
Collector shall be a position appointed by the Mayor, and said Collector
position shall be and operate separate and apart from the Village Clerk and the
Village Clerk’s Office.
   (B)   Duties. The Village Collector shall have the following additional
administrative duties: such duties as directed and assigned by the Mayor.
   (C)   Salary. The salary of the Village Collector shall be payable in 26
equal installments, and shall be set annually by ordinance.
(1988 Code, § 1-7-6) (Ord. 97-340, passed 8-4-1997; Ord. 02-188, passed 7-23-
2002; Ord. 03-212, passed 4-21-2003)
§ 31.026 DEPUTY CLERK.
   (A)   Office created. There is hereby created the office of Deputy Clerk in
and for the village.
   (B)   Appointment, powers and duties.
      (1)   The Mayor, under the conditions hereinafter set forth, is hereby
authorized to appoint one Deputy Clerk with the advice and consent of the Mayor
Board of Trustees, who shall have the power and duty to execute all documents
required to be executed by the Village Clerk and affix the seal of the village
thereto whenever required, such Deputy Clerk to act at such times as
hereinafter provided. In signing any documents, said Deputy Clerk shall sign
the name of the Village Clerk followed with the word “By” and the Deputy
Clerk’s own name and the words “Deputy Clerk”.
      (2)   The Deputy Clerk shall have the authority and powers herein
described and such further power and authority as provided for by statute in
such case made and provided, and such further powers and authority as may
hereinafter be granted pursuant to statute or village ordinance.
   (C)   Conditions of authority. The powers and duties herein described shall
be exercised by such Deputy Clerk only under the following conditions:
      (1)   If the Village Clerk is unavailable or, in the absence of the
Village Clerk, from the Village Clerk’s office in the Municipal Building,
Dolton, Illinois.
      (2)   When written direction has been given by the Village Clerk to such
Deputy to exercise such power, or when the Village President and Board of
Trustees have determined by resolution that the Village Clerk is temporarily or
permanently incapacitated to perform such functions.
      (3)   In the event that the Deputy Clerk is appointed by the written
direction of the Village Clerk, such appointment must be confirmed by the
President and Board of Trustees before such appointment will become effective.
      (4)   The appointment of the Deputy Clerk will not become effective until
such Deputy has taken an oath of office and has filed a surety bond, as
provided by state statute, conditioned upon the faithful performance of the
duties of the Deputy Clerk.
(1988 Code, § 1-7-7) (Ord. 94-263, passed 9-20-1994; Ord. 03-211, passed 4-21-
2003; Ord. 08-451, passed 10-20-2008)
§ 31.027 OFFICE HOURS.
   (A)   Normal workweek of the Village Clerk’s office.
      (1)   Effective 6-1-1997, the normal workweek of the Village Clerk’s
office shall be Monday through Friday. The Village Clerk’s office shall be open
to the public on Mondays and Thursdays from 9:00 a.m. until 7:30 p.m; and on
Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Fridays from 9:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m.
      (2)   The Village Clerk’s office shall be closed on Saturdays and
Sundays.
   (B)   Normal workday.
      (1)   The normal workday for the employees of the Village Clerk’s office
shall be eight consecutive hours per day, 40 hours a week.
      (2)   The normal workday or weekly work schedules of the employees of the
Village Clerk’s office shall be staggered so as to accommodate the office hours
of the Village Clerk’s office as set forth in division (A) above.
(Ord. 97-325, passed 5-19-1997)
VILLAGE TREASURER
§ 31.040 OFFICE CREATED; APPOINTMENT.
   There is hereby created the office of Village Treasurer who shall be
appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Board of
Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 1-8A-1)
§ 31.041 OATH.
   The Treasurer shall take the customary oath of office prescribed by statute
before entering upon the duties of his or her office. His or her subscribed
oath shall be filed in the office of the Village Clerk.
(1988 Code, § 1-8A-2)
§ 31.042 BOND AND COMPENSATION.
   (A)   Bond. The Treasurer shall give a bond, before entering upon the duties
of his or her office, in the sum required by the Board of Trustees, and such
amount shall not be less than that required by statute. This bond shall be
conditioned upon the faithful performance of his or her duties as the Treasurer
and shall be conditioned to indemnify the village for any loss by reason of any
neglect of duty or any wrongful act of the Treasurer. The bond shall also be
conditioned for faithful performance of his or her duty as treasurer of the
Firefighters’ Pension Fund and shall be conditioned for the faithful
performance of his or her duty as Treasurer of the Police Pension Fund. Such
bond shall be filed with the Village Clerk.
   (B)   Salary. The Treasurer shall receive as compensation such sum as shall
be set in the annual appropriation ordinance.
(1988 Code, § 1-8A-3)
§ 31.043 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   The Village Treasurer shall have the power and perform the duties
provided by statute and by the ordinances of the village.
   (B)   Among other things, it shall be his or her duty as follows:
      (1)   Receive and pay out moneys. To receive all moneys due or belonging
to the village and pay all orders or warrants, including special assessments
and other bonds and interest coupons, authorized by the Board of Trustees and
duly executed by the proper officers of the village;
      (2)   Books of account; register of warrants. To keep, or cause to be
kept, suitable books of account, showing in a simple and methodical manner all
moneys received by him or her and from whom and on what account or fund they
have been received, and all moneys paid out by him or her, to whom and on what
account or fund paid, and for what purpose. The books shall be balanced by him
or her monthly. He or she shall keep a register of all warrants which shall
describe each warrant showing the date, amount and number, the fund from which
paid, the name of the person to whom paid and when paid;
      (3)   Account of taxes levied. To keep a separate account for taxes which
are levied for a specific purpose;
      (4)   Reports.
         (a)   Monthly reports. To make a monthly report of his or her
transactions as Treasurer to the President and Board of Trustees, which report
shall be under oath filed with said Board together with cancelled vouchers
covering all transactions embraced in said report. The report shall show the
state of the treasury as of the date of the account. He or she shall accompany
the account with a statement of all money received into the treasury and on
what account, together with warrants redeemed and paid by him or her. On the
day the account is rendered, the warrants with all vouchers shall be delivered
to the Village Clerk and filed together with the monthly account in the Clerk’s
office.
         (b)   Annual report.
            1.   Within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year, he or she
must make out an annual report which must show:
               a.   All moneys received by the village indicating the total
amounts in the aggregate received in each account of the village; and
               b.   A statement showing the state of the village treasury at
the close of the fiscal year.
            2.   The annual report must be filed with the Village Clerk. A copy
of such report as filed with the Village Clerk and bearing the affidavit of the
Village Clerk that such copy is a true and correct copy of the one filed with
him or her, that said report was published, the date of publication and the
name of the paper in which published shall be filed with the County Collector
before November 1 as required by statute.
         (c)   Report fees. To make and return to the Village President every
May and every November a semi-annual report, verified by affidavit, of all fees
and other compensation received by him or her.
      (5)   Deposit of village funds; village and personal accounts to be
separate. To deposit the village funds in such depositories as may be selected
from time to time as provided by law; and to keep the deposit of the village
money separate and distinct from his own money and not make private or personal
use of any village money.
(1988 Code, § 1-8A-4)
§ 31.044 FIREFIGHTERS’ AND POLICE PENSION FUNDS.
   (A)   Firefighters’ Pension Fund. The Treasurer shall be ex-officio member
of the Firefighters’ Pension Fund of the village and Treasurer of said Fund.
   (B)   Police Pension Fund. The Treasurer shall have custody of the Police
Pension Fund and shall annually, on the second Tuesday in May, make a sworn
statement to the Board of Trustees of the Police Pension Fund of the village
and to the Village President and Board of Trustees of all moneys received and
paid out of the said Pension Fund, the amount of such funds then on hand and
the amount owing to the Pension Fund.
(1988 Code, § 1-8A-5)
§ 31.045 DEPUTY VILLAGE TREASURER.
   (A)   Office created; appointment. There is hereby created the office of
Deputy Village Treasurer in and for the village. The Deputy Village Treasurer
shall be appointed by the President, with the advice and consent of the Board
of Trustees.
   (B)   Oath. The Deputy Treasurer shall take the customary oath of office
prescribed by statute before entering upon the duties of office, which oath
shall be filed in the office of the Village Clerk.
   (C)   Bond. The Deputy Treasurer shall give a bond with surety, before
entering upon the duties of office, in the sum required by the Board of
Trustees and such amount shall not be less than required by statute. This bond
shall be conditioned upon the faithful performance of duties as Deputy
Treasurer and shall indemnify the village for any loss by reason of any neglect
of duty or any wrongful act of the Deputy Treasurer. The bond shall be also
conditioned for faithful performance of duty as Deputy Treasurer of the
Firefighters’ Pension Fund and the Police Pension Fund. Such bond shall be
filed in the office of the Village Clerk.
   (D)   Compensation. The Deputy Treasurer shall receive as compensation such
sum as shall be set forth in the annual appropriation ordinance.
   (E)   Powers and duties. The powers and duties of the Village Treasurer, as
contained in this subchapter, shall be exercised by the Deputy Village
Treasurer only under the following conditions:
      (1)   In the absence of the Village Treasurer from the Treasurer’s office
in the Municipal Building; and
      (2)   When written direction has been given by the Village Treasurer to
such Deputy to exercise such power, or when the Village President and Board of
Trustees have determined by resolution that the Village Treasurer is
temporarily or permanently incapacitated to perform such functions.
(1988 Code, § 1-8A-6) (Ord. 85-116B, passed 7-9-1985)
§ 31.046 ASSISTANT VILLAGE TREASURER.
   (A)   Creation of office. There is hereby created the office of Assistant
Village Treasurer in and for the village.
   (B)   Appointment of Assistant Treasurer. The Assistant Village Treasurer
shall be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Board of
Trustees.
   (C)   Oath. The Assistant Treasurer shall take the customary oath of office
prescribed by statute before entering upon the duties of office. The oath shall
be filed in the office of the Village Clerk.
   (D)   Bond. The Assistant Treasurer shall give a bond with surety before
entering upon the duties of office in the sum required by the Board of
Trustees, and such amount shall not be less than required by statute. This bond
shall be conditioned upon the faithful performance of duties as Assistant
Treasurer, and shall indemnify the village for any loss by reason of any
neglect of duty or any wrongful act of the Assistant Treasurer. The bond shall
be also conditioned for faithful performance of duty as Assistant Treasurer of
the Firefighters’ Pension Fund and the Police Pension Fund. Such bond shall be
filed in the office of the Village Clerk.
   (E)   Powers and duties. The powers and duties of the Village Treasurer as
contained in this subchapter shall be exercised by the Assistant Village
Treasurer only under the following conditions:
      (1)   In the absence of the Village Treasurer and the Deputy Village
Treasurer from the Treasurer’s office in the Municipal Building;
      (2)   When written direction has been given by the Village Treasurer to
such Assistant to exercise such power, or when the President and Board of
Trustees of the village have determined by resolution that the Village
Treasurer and Deputy Village Treasurer are temporarily or permanently
incapacitated to perform such functions.
   (F)   Compensation. The Assistant Treasurer shall receive as compensation
such sum as shall be set forth in the annual appropriation ordinance.
(1988 Code, § 1-8A-7) (Ord. 87-141, passed 12-22-1987)
VILLAGE ATTORNEYS
§ 31.060 VILLAGE ATTORNEY.
   (A)   Office created; appointment. There is hereby created the office of
Village Attorney. The Village Attorney shall be appointed by the Board of
Trustees pursuant to a majority vote. Following his or her appointment, the
Village Attorney shall take office. If deemed appropriate by the Village Board,
the Village Attorney shall serve in accordance with a written retainer
agreement or contract approved by the Village Board. If the Village Board does
not expressly approve a written retainer agreement or contract, the Village
Attorney’s duties shall include those duties as set forth in division (D)
below, and his or her service shall continue at the pleasure of the Village
Board for an indefinite term.
   (B)   Bond. The bond of the Village Attorney shall be in the penal sum of
$1,000 conditioned for the faithful discharge of his or her duties.
   (C)   Compensation. The Village Attorney shall be paid such sum as is set in
the annual appropriation ordinance for his or her general services and advice.
For services rendered in the conduct of suits, bonding problems and other
problems requiring unusual expenditure of time not contemplated in the duties
enumerated herein, he or she shall receive such additional compensation based
upon the fair and reasonable value of such services.
   (D)   Duties. The Village Attorney shall:
      (1)   Be a legal advisor to the President and the Trustees and shall
render advice on all legal questions affecting the village whenever requested
to do so by the President or the Trustees. Upon request, he or she shall reduce
such opinion to writing;
      (2)   Draw such ordinances, deeds, leases and other papers as may be
required of him or her by the President and Trustees;
      (3)   Attend meetings of the Village Board;
      (4)   Prosecute or defend any and all suits or actions at law or in
equity to which the village may be a party or in which it may be interested, or
which may be brought against it or by any officer of the village on behalf of
the village or in the capacity of such person as an officer or employee of the
village;
      (5)   Take such action as may be necessary to accomplish the full
enforcement of all judgments and decrees rendered or entered in favor of the
village;
      (6)   Be a member of the Board of Trustees of the Firefighters’ Pension
Fund of the village; and
      (7)   Process and carry through to completion all special assessment
proceedings in the village.
(1988 Code, § 1-8B-1) (Ord. 08-453, passed 10-20-2008)
§ 31.061 SPECIAL PROSECUTING ATTORNEY.
   (A)   Office created; appointment. There is hereby created the office of
Special Prosecuting Attorney. The Special Prosecuting Attorney shall be
appointed by the Village President, with the advice and consent of the Board of
Trustees.
   (B)   Bond. The bond of the Special Prosecuting Attorney shall be in the
penal sum of $1,000 conditioned for the faithful discharge of his or her
duties.
   (C)   Compensation. The Special Prosecuting Attorney shall be paid the sum
as is set in the annual appropriation ordinance for his or her services.
   (D)   Duties. The Special Prosecuting Attorney shall prosecute all ordinance
violations and traffic or motor vehicle violations of state statutes committed
in the village, and appeals thereof, to which the village may be a party.
(1988 Code, § 1-8B-2)
§ 31.062 SPECIAL ATTORNEYS.
   (A)   Appointment. Notwithstanding any other provisions to the contrary, the
Village President, with the consent of the Board of Trustees, may appoint an
additional attorney or additional attorneys to perform special legal services
designated by the President and the Board of Trustees.
   (B)   Bond. The bond of any special attorney shall be in the penal sum of
$1,000 conditioned on the faithful discharge of his or her duties.
   (C)   Compensation. Any special attorney shall receive for services rendered
compensation based upon the fair and reasonable value of his or her services.
(1988 Code, § 1-8B-3)

responsible to the Superintendent of Public Works.
   (B)   He or she shall be appointed by the President, with the advice and
consent of the Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 1-8D-1)
§ 31.091 QUALIFICATIONS.
   (A)   No person shall be appointed as Village Plumber unless he or she has
been a resident of the village for one year.
   (B)   He or she must be a journeyman plumber licensed by the state under the
state’s Plumbing License Law, being 225 ILCS 320/1 et seq. as now or hereafter
amended.
(1988 Code, § 1-8D-2)
§ 31.092 DUTIES.
   It shall be the duty of the Plumber to perform the following:
   (A)   Repair, service, replace (when necessary) water meters in the village;
   (B)   Maintain and repair the equipment of the Water Department;
   (C)   Make all water tap connections for the village;
   (D)   Perform all plumbing and accessory appurtenance work required in
village-owned buildings;
   (E)   Maintain and repair the sewer system of the village, as directed;
   (F)   Attend to village affairs 40 hours a week; and
   (G)   Perform such other duties as may from time to time be directed by the
President and Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 1-8D-3)
§ 31.093 COMPENSATION.
   The Plumber shall receive compensation as set forth by ordinance.
(1988 Code, § 1-8D-4)

§ 31.105 OFFICE CREATED; APPOINTMENT.
   (A)   Office created; appointment. There is hereby created a full-time
position in the village to be known as the Director of Inspectional Services,
at the salary to be provided in the annual appropriations ordinance.
   (B)   Appointment and authority. The Director of Inspectional Services shall
be appointed by the President and shall be under the direct supervision of the
Village President’s office, and shall perform a variety of functions for all
departments in a non-sworn capacity.
(Ord. 15-030, passed 3-21-2011)
§ 31.106 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   In addition to other powers conferred herein, the Director of Inspectional
Services shall perform the following powers and duties: performs any and all
duties assigned by the President or Village Administrator, including, but not
limited to the following:
   (A)   Enforces village ordinances regarding parking, zoning, housing, health
and other village code related violations:
      (1)   Unauthorized handicap/fire lane parking;

   (F)   Supervises other employees in the Department.
(Ord. 15-030, passed 3-21-2011)
§ 31.107 MINIMUM JOB REQUIREMENTS.
   High school diploma or GED; with the village approval, a combination of
training and experience which provide equivalent knowledge, abilities and
skills. He or she must have a valid driver’s license and be insurable and
bonded by the insurance carrier of the village. Successful completion of
criminal background check, reference checks and must pass security clearance.
Applicants must be of good moral character and habits.
(Ord. 15-030, passed 3-21-2011)
INSPECTOR GENERAL
§ 31.120 OFFICE ESTABLISHED.
   There is established an office of the village government which shall be
known as the office of Inspector General, which shall include an Inspector
General and such other deputies, assistants and other employees as may be
provided for in the annual appropriation ordinance and/or the annual salary
resolution.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
§ 31.121 RETENTION.
   (A)   Retention. The Inspector General shall be appointed to the office of
Inspector General by the Mayor, either as an employee of the village or in the
capacity of a consulting contractor with any and all such rights and benefits
that inure to an employee as the parties may agree.
   (B)   Powers and duties. It shall be the duty of the Inspector General to:
      (1)   Receive and register complaints and information concerning
misconduct, inefficiency and waste within village government;
      (2)   Investigate the performance of governmental officers, employees,
functions and programs, either in response to a complaint or on the Inspector
General’s own initiative, in order to detect and to prevent misconduct,
inefficiency and waste within the programs and the operations of the village
government;
      (3)   Promote economy, efficiency, effectiveness, integrity in the
administration of the programs and operations of the village government by
reviewing programs, identifying any inefficiencies, waste and potential for
misconduct therein and recommending to the President and Board policies and
methods for the elimination of inefficiencies and waste and the prevention of
misconduct;
      (4)   Report to the Mayor and/or Board of Trustees concerning the results
of investigations undertaken by the office of Inspector General;
      (5)   Request information related to an investigation from any employee,
officer, agency or licensee of the village;
      (6)   Conduct public hearing, at his or her discretion, in the course of
an investigation hereunder;
      (7)   Administer oaths and examine witnesses under oath;
      (8)   To issue subpoenas to compel the attendance of witnesses for
purposes of examination and the production of documents and other items for
inspection and/or duplication. Issuance of subpoenas shall be subject to the
restrictions contained in §
31.122 of this chapter; and
      (9)   Promulgate rules and regulations for the conduct of investigations
an public hearings consistent with the requirements of due process of law and
equal protection under the law.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
§ 31.122 SUBPOENA ISSUANCE AND CONTENTS; OBJECTIONS.
   (A)   (1)   The Inspector General shall issue subpoenas only if:
         (a)   He or she is conducting an investigation authorized by this
subchapter;
         (b)   The investigation relates to misconduct within the programs and
operation of village government by any person described in §
31.123 of this chapter;
         (c)   The Inspector General has a reasonable belief that such
misconduct has occurred; and
         (d)   The testimony of the witness or the documents or items sought by
the subpoena are relevant to the investigation.
      (2)   A subpoena shall be served in the same manner as subpoenas issued
under the rules of the state’s Supreme Court to compel appearance of a
deponent, and subject to the same witness and mileage fee fixed by law for such
subpoenas.
   (B)   (1)   A subpoena issued under this subchapter shall identify the
person to whom it is directed and the documents or other items sought thereby,
if any, and the date, time and place for the appearance of the witness and
production of the documents or other items described in the subpoena.
      (2)   In no event shall the date for examination or production be less
than seven days after service of the subpoena.
   (C)   (1)   No later than the time for appearance or production required by
the subpoena, the person to whom the subpoena is directed may object to the
subpoena in whole or in part.
      (2)   The objection shall be in writing, delivered to the Inspector
General and shall specify the grounds for the objection.
      (3)   For seven days after receipt of timely objection to a subpoena, the
Inspector General shall take no action to enforce the subpoena or to initiate
prosecution of the person to whom the subpoena is directed.
      (4)   During this seven-day period, the Inspector General shall consider
the grounds for the objection and may attempt to resolve the objection through
negotiations with the person to whom the subpoena is directed. The seven-day
period may be extended by the Inspector General in order to allow completion of
any negotiations.
      (5)   Negotiations may include such matters as the scope of the subpoena
and the time, place and manner of response thereto.
      (6)   The filing of an objection to a subpoena, and negotiations pursuant
to an objection, shall not constitute refusal to comply with the subpoena, or
interference with or obstruction of an investigation.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
§ 31.123 CONDUCT OF VILLAGE OFFICERS, EMPLOYEES AND OTHER ENTITIES.
   (A)   The powers and duties of the Inspector General shall extend to the
conduct of the following:
      (1)   All elected and appointed officers of the village government in the
performance of their official duties, except as provided below;
      (2)   All employees of the village government in the performance of their
official duties;
      (3)   All contractors and subcontractor providing goods or services to
the village pursuant to a contract;
      (4)   Business entities in seeking contracts or certification of
eligibility for village contracts; and
      (5)   Persons seeking certifications of eligibility for participation in
any village program.
   (B)   (1)   Not withstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, the
office of Inspector General shall have no power or authority over the Village
Mayor or the Village Trustees.
      (2)   If the office of the Inspector General receive any complaint
alleging misconduct, inefficiency or waste against the Village Mayor or the
Village Trustees, the Inspector General shall promptly transmit said complaint
to the Chairperson of the Committee on Committees Rules and Ethics, or such
successor committee, shall conduct an investigation of each complaint referred
to it by the office of Inspector General.
      (3)   Nothing in this section shall preclude the Inspector General from
referring a complaint or information concerning the Village Mayor or a Village
Trustee to the appropriate federal, state or local law enforcement authorities.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
§ 31.124 INVESTIGATION REPORTS.
   (A)   (1)   Upon conclusion of an investigation the Inspector General shall
issue a summary report thereon.
      (2)   The report shall be filed with the Mayor and may be filed with the
head of each department or other agency affected by or involved in the
investigation.
      (3)   The report shall be provided to the Village Trustees, upon request.
   (B)   The report shall include the following:
      (1)   A description of any complaints or other information received by
the Inspector General pertinent to the investigation;
      (2)   A description of any illegal conduct, inefficiencies or wasted
observed in the course of the investigation;
      (3)   Recommendations for correction of any illegal conduct,
inefficiencies or waste described in the report; and
      (4)   Such other information as the Inspector General may deem relevant
to the investigation or resulting recommendations.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
§ 31.125 CONFIDENTIALITY OF EX-INFORMANTS; EXCEPTIONS.
   The summary report shall not mention the name of any informant, complainant,
witness or person investigated, except in the following instances:
   (A)   When the copy of the report given to the head any department or agency
recommends disciplinary action against an employee of that village or agency;
   (B)   Where the report makes recommendations concerning any contractor,
subcontractor, applicant for a contract, or person seeking a license, permit or
certification of eligibility for a contract;
   (C)   Where the copy of the report given to the head of a department or
agency make recommendations concerning a person seeking certification of
eligibility for a program administered by the department or agency; and
   (D)   Where the copy given to the Mayor recommends disciplinary action the
head or any employee of an executive department or agency.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
§ 31.126 INVESTIGATIONS NOT CONCLUDED WITHIN SIX MONTHS.
   If any investigation is not concluded within six months after its
initiation, the Inspector General shall notify the Mayor of the general nature
of the complaint or information giving rise to the investigation and the reason
for failure to complete the investigation with in six months.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
§ 31.127 COOPERATION IN INVESTIGATIONS.
   (A)   It shall be the duty of every officer, employee, department, agency,
contractor, subcontractor and licensee of the village and every applicant for
certification of eligibility for a village contract or program, to cooperate
with the Inspector General in any investigation or hearing undertaken pursuant
to this subchapter.
   (B)   Every village contract and every bid, proposal, application for
certification of eligibility for a village contract or program shall contain a
statement that the person understands and will abide by all provision of this
subchapter.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
§ 31.128 FILES AND REPORTS CONFIDENTIAL; PUBLIC STATEMENTS AUTHORIZED WHEN.
   (A)   All investigator files and reports of the office of Inspector General
shall be confidential and shall not be divulged to any person or agency, except
to the United States Attorney, the state’s Attorney General or the State’s
Attorney of the county, or as otherwise provided in this subchapter.
   (B)   The Inspector General is authorized to issue public statements
concerning:
      (1)   An investigation that exonerates an individual who is publicly
known to have been under investigation, where the subject requests such a
state; and
      (2)   An investigation that concern inefficient or wasteful management,
as opposed to individual misconduct or illegality.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
§ 31.129 CONDITIONS FOR REMOVAL FROM OFFICE.
   (A)   The Inspector General may be removed prior to the expiration of his or
her term only for cause.
   (B)   The Mayor shall give written notice:
      (1)   To the Board of Trustees of the termination; and
      (2)   To the Inspector General of the cause of his or her intended
removal.
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
COMPTROLLER AND REVENUE ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES
§ 31.140 OFFICE CREATED; APPOINTMENT.
   There is hereby created the office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative
Services. The office shall consist of a Comptroller, and a Deputy Comptroller,
who shall be appointed by the President, and such other persons as are deemed
necessary and appropriate to carry out the duties of the office.
(Ord. 03-213, passed 4-21-2003)
§ 31.141 OATH.
   The Comptroller and Deputy Comptroller shall take the customary oaths of
office prescribed by statute before entering upon the duties of his or her
office. The subscribed oaths shall be filed in the office of the Village Clerk.
(Ord. 03-213, passed 4-21-2003)
§ 31.142 BOND AND COMPENSATION.
   (A)   Bond. The Comptroller and Deputy Comptroller shall give a bond, before
entering upon the duties of his or her office, in the sum required by the Board
of Trustees, and such amount shall not be less than that required by statute.
This bond shall be conditioned upon the faithful performance of his or her
duties as the Comptroller and shall be conditioned to indemnify the village for
any loss by reason of any neglect of duty or any wrongful act of the Village
Comptroller.
   (B)   Salary. The Comptroller and Deputy Comptroller shall receive as
compensation such sums as may be provided for in the annual Appropriations
(Budget) Ordinance and Resolution Setting Salaries, Compensation, Expense
Accounts and other Remuneration for Employees of the Village of Dolton, as from
time to time amended.
(Ord. 03-213, passed 4-21-2003)
§ 31.143 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   The Comptroller shall have the power and perform the duties provided
by ordinances of the village and assigned by the Mayor.
   (B)   Among other things, it shall be his or her duty as follows:
      (1)   General powers and duties. To administer and enforce all of the
responsibilities, powers and duties delegated to it by village ordinance,
pursuant to the village municipal code;
      (2)   Special assessments. The Comptroller shall collect all special
assessments and other warrants which by law or the ordinances of the village
may be executed by the Comptroller. To exercise general supervision over
special assessments, as provided in and the preparation and issuance of special
assessments bills, which bills shall be prepared with interest computed thereon
as may be required. The Comptroller shall prepare and safely keep all of the
books and records relating to the special assessments and issuance of bills
therefor. The Comptroller shall prepare and safely keep all books and records
relating to the payment of special assessments;
      (3)   Water collections. The Comptroller shall be responsible for the
billing of water accounts, collection of water bill payments and for the proper
accounting of such collections: To exercise general supervision over water
bills and accounts as provided in the village municipal code, as amended. The
office of Comptroller and Administrative Revenue Services shall see that all
water meters are read for billing purposes; that such meters are kept in a good
state of repair; and that samples of the water supply be taken monthly and
analyzed to ensure the safety of the water supply;
      (4)   Water transfer stamp tax. To exercise general supervision over the
water transfer stamp tax process as set forth in §§
151.235 through
151.244 of this code of ordinances, as amended. The water transfer stamp shall
be issued by the office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services
after payment of the tax to the Comptroller. The office of Comptroller and
Revenue Administrative Services shall issue an adhesive stamp or stamps, in a
form prescribed by the village and such stamp(s) shall be affixed to the face
of the deed or instrument of conveyance;
      (5)   Business and license applications. To exercise general supervision
over the approval and issuance of license process as provided in Title XI of
this code of ordinances, as amended. Licenses shall be granted and signed by
the Village President and issued by the office of Comptroller and Revenue
Administrative Services. All applications for licenses and permits, and the
regulations relating thereto as provided in, shall be submitted to the office
of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services, in writing on forms to be
prescribed and furnished by the Village Board and the village as provided in
Ch. 110 of this code of ordinances, as amended. The Comptroller shall keep a
record of all applications;
      (6)   Duplicate licenses; vehicle tags. To exercise general supervision
over the issuance of duplicate licenses; vehicle tags, as provided in §
110.08 of this code of ordinances, as amended.
         (a)   Duplicate licenses. The office of Comptroller and Revenue
Administrative Services, upon satisfactory evidence of such loss or destruction
being filed with the office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services
and the payment to the village of $5 for such duplicate, the office of
Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services shall issue a duplicate
thereof.
         (b)   Vehicle tags. The office of Comptroller and Revenue
Administrative Services shall furnish each licensee with a tag or sticker for
each vehicle covered by the license.
      (7)   Notices of license terminations. To exercise general supervision
over the issuance of Notices of License Terminations, as provided in §
110.10 of this code of ordinances, as amended;
      (8)   Transfer of license or permit; change of location. To exercise
general supervision over the transfer of license or permit, change of location
process, as provided in §
110.11 of this code of ordinances, as amended;
      (9)   Fishing, hunting and trapping licenses. To exercise general
supervision over the issuance of fishing, hunting and trapping licenses as
provided in by the village. The office of Comptroller and Revenue
Administrative Services shall issue said applications and licenses for fishing,
hunting and trapping. The Comptroller shall accept and remit all fees paid for
hunting and trapping licenses in accordance with the Illinois Revised Statutes.
The Comptroller shall remit all fees collected for said licenses on behalf of
the state to the state’s Department of Conservation and make reports as
required by said Department. He or she shall name the state’s Department of
Conservation in the Village Clerk’s official bond to cover the full value of
license payments received, but unaccounted for. The Clerk shall be permitted to
charge an additional fee of $0.25 in the case of resident hunting and trapping
licenses, and $0.50 in the case of non-resident hunting licenses;
      (10)   Fishing licenses. The Comptroller shall have authority to issue
licenses for the taking of fish and shall remit all fees collected for said
licenses and make reports as required to the state’s Department of
Conservation. He or she shall name the state’s Department of Conservation in
his or her official bond to cover the full value of licenses sold or
unaccounted for. The Comptroller shall be permitted to charge as an additional
fee those sums permitted;
      (11)   Collections of fines. To exercise general supervision over the
receipt and collection of moneys due and owing the village pursuant to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances;
      (12)   Collection of parking violation fines. To exercise general
supervision over the receipt and collection of moneys due and owing the village
pursuant to as §§
75.55 through
75.57 of this code of ordinances, as amended:
         (a)   Computing the fees owed for release of vehicle;
         (b)   Collection of any fees assessed at hearing; and
         (c)   Computing the fees owed to the towing company for impounded
vehicles.
      (13)   Collect fees; remit to Treasurer. The Comptroller shall collect
and account for vehicle license fees and collections; shall collect all
building and zoning fees; water and sewer tap charges and inspection fees;
deposits to ensure construction of sidewalks; and such other deposits as are
required by the Building Code and ordinances of the village. The Comptroller
shall also be responsible for the collection of special events, hall rents and
business fees. The Collector shall make proper accounting of such collections
and all other collections received by the office of Comptroller and Revenue
Administrative Services and shall remit to the Village Treasurer all moneys
received from time to time as required by ordinance;
      (14)   Statistical records. To establish, maintain and preserve
statistical records of revenue and to report to the Mayor from time to time, or
as often as the Mayor deems necessary, upon such statistics;
      (15)   Books and records. To prepare, maintain and safely keep all books
and records relating to such collection of moneys; shall make proper accounting
of such collections and other collections received by the Department of
Revenue; and shall timely remit to the Treasurer all moneys received from time
to time as required;
      (16)   Rules and regulations. To make and enforce such reasonable rules
and regulations as may be necessary to effectively administer any of the powers
herein granted now which may be granted by other ordinances adopted by the
corporate authorities, and to publish such rules and regulations and make the
same available to such members of the public as may desire them;
      (17)   Payment records. To investigate and maintain records of all
persons required by the municipal code to pay debts, fines or fees, determine
whether all persons have complied with such provisions, and in cases of evasion
of payment, to serve notices of delinquency and upon advice, counsel and
representation by the Village Attorney, request proceedings to be instituted to
enforce such provisions and collections;
      (18)   Indebtedness to village. To report to the Village Treasurer all
persons owing and indebtedness to the village. Said notice shall include the
name, address, date debt was incurred, ticket numbers (if applicable) and the
total amount due and owing the village; and
      (19)   Prosecution. To take such steps, actions and to request
prosecution by the Village Prosecutor, for the purpose of enforcing ordinances
relating to revenue receivable by the village.
(Ord. 03-213, passed 4-21-2003)
§ 31.144 BOOKS AND RECORDS; EXAMINATION.
   The Comptroller, Deputy Comptroller or any person certified by the Mayor or
the Comptroller may enter the premises of any business establishment for
inspection and examination of books and records in order to effectuate the
proper administration and enforcement of any collection of revenue owed to the
village. It shall be unlawful for any person to prevent, hinder or interfere
with the Comptroller, or his or her duly authorized deputy or representative,
in the discharge of the duties in the performance of this subchapter. It shall
be the duty of every owner of a business to keep accurate and complete books
and records to which the Comptroller, or any deputies or representative
thereof, shall at all times have full access, which records shall include
employees, wages, assets, income, expenses and the like.
(Ord. 03-213, passed 4-21-2003)
§ 31.145 PAYMENT FOR DEBTS OWED TO THE VILLAGE.
   All payments for debts, fines, fees, licenses, fees and the like, the
collection of which are the responsibility of the office of Comptroller and
Revenue Administrative Services, shall be made payable to the office of
Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services.
(Ord. 03-213, passed 4-21-2003)
VILLAGE MARSHAL
§ 31.160 OFFICE CREATED; APPOINTMENTS.
   There is hereby created the office of Village Marshal. The Village Marshal
shall be appointed by the Village President, with the advice and consent of the
Board of Trustees. The President is hereby authorized to appoint one or more
Village Deputy Marshals. The office of Village Marshal shall consist of the
Village Marshal, the Deputy Village Marshals and such other members as may be
provided from time to time by the President and the Board of Trustees. Neither
the Village Marshal, nor any of the Deputy Village Marshals, shall be
considered employees of the village, but they shall be considered officers of
the village.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)
§ 31.161 OATHS.
   The Village Marshal and the Deputy Village Marshals, shall also, before
entering upon the duties of his or her office, take and subscribe the oath or
affirmation prescribed by § 3 of Art. XIII of the Constitution, which shall be
filed in the office of the Village Clerk.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)
§ 31.162 TERM OF OFFICE.
   (A)   The Village Marshal and the Deputy Village Marshals serve at the will
of the President and the Board of Trustees.
   (B)   The appointments of the Village Marshal and the Deputy Village
Marshals may be terminated by the Village President subject to the advice and
consent of the Board of Trustees.
   (C)   The appointment, if not terminated sooner, expires upon the expiration
of the term of the appointing President.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)
§ 31.163 QUALIFICATIONS.
   The Village Marshal and the Deputy Village Marshals shall not be members of
the regular Police Department of the village. Deputy Marshals need not be
residents of the village. Deputy Marshals need not be residents of the village.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)
§ 31.164 CRIMINAL RECORD.
   Prior to appointment, the Village Marshal and the Deputy Village Marshals
shall be fingerprinted and their fingerprints shall be checked with the Federal
Bureau of Investigation, Washington, D.C., for any possible criminal record. No
person shall be appointed as Village Marshal or Deputy Village Marshal if he or
she has been convicted of a felony or other crime involving moral turpitude.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)
§ 31.165 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   It shall be the duty of the Village Marshal and every Deputy Marshal,
when any criminal offense or breach of peace is committed or attempted in his
or her presence, forthwith to apprehend the offender and bring him or her
before a judge, to be dealt with according to law; to suppress riots and
unlawful assemblies; to keep the peace; to without delay to serve and execute
all warrants and other process to him or her lawfully directed; and to exercise
all other powers as conservators of the peace that the corporate authorities
may prescribe.
   (B)   Deputy Marshals shall have the following powers and duties when
properly assigned and on duty:
      (1)   To aid or direct traffic in the municipality;
      (2)   To aid in the control of natural or human-made disasters;
      (3)   To aid in the case of civil disorder; and
      (4)   To perform normal and regular police duties when assigned by the
Chief of Police on occasions when it is impractical for members of the regular
Police Department to perform normal and regular police duties.
   (C)   The Village Marshal and the Deputy Village Marshals shall, at all
times during the performance of their duties, be subject to the direction and
control of the Chief of Police of the village.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)
§ 31.166 TRAINING REQUIRED.
   (A)   The Village Marshal and the Village Deputy Marshal, prior to entering
upon any of their duties, shall receive a course of training in the use of
weapons and other procedures by the Village Chief of Police.
   (B)   (1)   Such course of training shall be not less than 30 days or 25
hours in duration.
      (2)   Upon completion of the course of training, the Chief of Police
shall file a certificate attesting to the auxiliary police officer’s completion
of said course with the Village Clerk.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)
§ 31.167 IDENTIFICATION.
   Identification symbols worn by the Village Marshal and the Deputy Village
Marshals shall be different and distinct from the regular Police Department and
the auxiliary police and shall be selected and chosen by the Chief of Police of
the village.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)
§ 31.168 FIREARMS.
   The Village Marshal and the Deputy Marshals shall not carry firearms, except
with the permission of the village’s Chief of Police.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)
§ 31.169 COMPENSATION.
   The Village Marshal and the Deputy Village Marshals shall be paid such sums
as is set forth in the annual appropriation ordinance for each hour of service
performed; provided, such service is performed at the direction of the Chief of
Police.
(Ord. 97-324, passed 5-19-1997)

Administrator.
(Ord. 93-207, passed 4-27-1993)
§ 31.181 ASSISTING MAYOR.
   The Village Administrator shall assist the Mayor in the direction of the

§ 31.182 APPOINTMENT AND REMOVAL.

removed by the Mayor with the advice and consent of the Board of Trustees.
(Ord. 93-207, passed 4-27-1993)
§ 31.183 COMPENSATION.
   The Village Administrator shall receive compensation at a rate to be
determined by the Mayor and the Board of Trustees through the appropriate Board
salary resolution.
(Ord. 93-207, passed 4-27-1993)
LEGISLATIVE COUNSEL
§ 31.195 OFFICE CREATED.
   It is in the best interests of the village for the Village Board of Trustees
to retain legislative counsel independently to serve as legal advisor to the
Village Board and the village.
(Ord. 21-009, passed 9-2-2021)
§ 31.196 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The Legislative Counsel shall counsel on matters relating to their
legislative duties, which may include, but are not limited to, the drafting of
ordinances, contract documents, opinions on the powers of the legislative
branch, analysis of the validity of actions taken by the village, review and
defense of litigation issues, representation of the corporate authorities
regarding legislative matters in litigation, defend the Village Board and its
members against claims and lawsuits, advise the Village Board on other proposed
amendments to this code of ordinances, settlement of litigation, tax increment
financing, economic development, other economic, finance and tax related issues
as may come before the Village Board and any committees thereof, and providing
other advice on matters within the purview of the legislative branch of
municipal government including labor matters. The legislative counsel shall
attend meetings of the Village Board, and any committees thereof, as requested
by the members of the Village Board. The Legislative Counsel shall be
parliamentarian of the Village Board and, upon request, shall render opinion
and advice on questions of parliamentary law and procedure applicable to
matters arising before the Village Board. The Trustees shall each be authorized
to direct questions related to their legislative duties to the independent
legislative counsel. Trustees may seek legal counsel regarding any matters
within the range of items specified above.
(Ord. 21-009, passed 9-2-2021)
§ 31.197 COMPENSATION; RATES.
   (A)   The independent legislative counsel shall be retained at a rate
authorized by the Village Board for any term, but not exceeding the term of the
Village President. The hourly rate shall be equal to the rate paid to the
Village Attorney or special counsel.
   (B)   The legislative counsel shall be appointed by majority vote of the
members of the Village Board.
(Ord. 21-009, passed 9-2-2021)
§ 31.198 ASSISTING THE LOCAL ELECTION OFFICIAL.
   The Legislative Counsel shall assist the village’s Local Election Official
as may be deemed necessary and prudent with respect to the nomination paper and
objection filing processes and in the initial preparations and empaneling of
any municipal officers electoral board, including, but not limited to, advising
and assistance with any notices, proper service, draft rules of procedure and
any other matters required by law for any electoral board and/or the Local
Election Official.
(Ord. 24-015, passed 11-6-2024)
INTERNAL AUDITOR
§ 31.210 ESTABLISHMENT OF POSITION.
   The Board of Trustees hereby create the position of Internal Auditor, who
shall have full access to all village financial statements, including bank
records, TIF records, village fund records, payroll records, accounts payable
and accounts receivable and any other accounts/funds the Internal Auditor deems
necessary to provide updates to the Board of Trustees as to the current state
of the village’s finances.
(Ord. 24-001, passed 1-24-2024)
§ 31.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty has been prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   Retaliation prohibited; penalty. No person shall retaliate
against, punish or penalize any other person for complaining to cooperation
with or assisting the Inspector General in the performance of his or her
office. Any person who violates the provisions of this division (B)(1) and §§
31.120 through
31.129 of this chapter shall be subject to a fine of not less than $300 and not
more than $500 for each violation.
      (2)   Obstructing or interfering with investigation; penalty. No person
shall willfully refuse to comply with a subpoena issued by the Inspector
General or otherwise knowingly interfere with or obstruct an investigation
authorized by §§
31.120 through
31.129 of this chapter and conducted by an announced investigator of the office
of Inspector General. Any person who willfully violates the provisions of this
division (B)(2) shall be subject to a fine of not less than $300, and not more
than $500, for each such offense, or imprisonment for a period of not less than
30 days and not more than six months, or both a fine and imprisonment. Each day
that a violation continues shall constitute a separate and distinct offense.
Actions seeking the imposition of a fine only shall be filed as quasi-criminal
actions subject to the provisions of the state’s Code of Civil Procedure, being
735 ILCS 5/1-101 et seq. as now or hereafter amended. Actions seeking
incarceration, or incarceration and a fine, shall be filed and prosecuted as
misdemeanor actions under the procedure set forth in § 1-2-1.1 of the state’s
Municipal Code, as amended.
      (3)   Violation; penalty; discharge or other discipline. Any employee or
appointed officer of the village who violates any provision of §§
31.120 through
31.129 of this chapter shall be subject to discharge (or such other discipline
as may be specified in an applicable collective bargaining agreement) in
addition to any other penalty provided in this division (B).
(Ord. 06-340, passed 5-1-2006)
