**** DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS ****
§ 32.001 CREATION.
   There is hereby created a Department of Public Works which shall consist of
a Superintendent of Public Works, an Assistant Superintendent for Water and
Sewer Operations and an Assistant Superintendent for Streets, Alleys and
Sanitation Operations and such numbers of other employees as may from time to
time be determined by the President and Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 1-9-1)
§ 32.002 FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES.
   The functions and duties of the Department of Public Works shall be to
supervise and control within the village:
   (A)   Streets, alleys and sanitation to include:
      (1)   The maintenance of all public streets and alleys in the village;
      (2)   The maintenance of parkways, trees and shrubbery in the village;
      (3)   The maintenance of all motor vehicle equipment owned by the village
other than the Police Department and Fire Department motor vehicles; and
      (4)   The collection and disposal of refuse by the village.
   (B)   Sewage;
   (C)   Water distribution; and
   (D)   All village-owned properties and buildings.
(1988 Code, § 1-9-2)
§ 32.003 OFFICES CREATED.
   There are hereby created the offices of Superintendent of Public Works,
Assistant Superintendent of Public Works for Water and Sewer Operations and
Assistant Superintendent of Public Works for Streets, Alleys and Sanitation
Operations.
(1988 Code, § 1-9-3)
§ 32.004 QUALIFICATIONS AND SELECTION.
   The Superintendent of Public Works, the Assistant Superintendent of Public
Works for Water and Sewer Operations and the Assistant Superintendent of Public
Works for Streets, Alleys and Sanitation Operations shall be appointed by the
President of the village, with the advice and consent of the Board of Trustees
and shall be required, prior to such selection, to possess the following
qualifications:
   (A)   Minimum five years’ experience in public works and/or a degree in
public administration;
   (B)   High school diploma;
   (C)   Comply with residency regulations in effect at time of selection;
   (D)   Possess basic knowledge of all streets and alleys located in the
village;
   (E)   Possess basic knowledge of all departments as enumerated in §
32.002 of this chapter;
   (F)   Possess basic knowledge of the operations of all village mechanical
equipment;
   (G)   Possess the ability to read and interpret architectural drawings as
well as water and sewer atlases;
   (H)   Possess a working knowledge and understanding of the state motor fuel
tax funds as they apply to the village; and
   (I)   The Assistant Superintendent of Public Works for Water and Sewer
Operations shall possess a state Class C public water supply operator
certificate of competency.
(1988 Code, § 1-9-4) (Ord. 86-135, passed 7-29-1986; Ord. 90-106, passed 2-27-
1990)
§ 32.005 COMPENSATION OF OFFICERS.
   Compensation of the Superintendent and Assistant Superintendents of Public
Works shall be set by appropriation ordinance.
(1988 Code, § 1-9-5)
§ 32.006 DUTIES OF OFFICERS.
   The Superintendent of Public Works shall have immediate supervision and
control over the Assistant Superintendents of Public Works for Water and Sewer
and for Streets, Alleys and Sanitation and the Assistant Superintendents shall
have responsibility for the supervision and control of their respective
departments.
(1988 Code, § 1-9-6)
§ 32.007 REPORT REQUIRED.
   Within 60 days after the beginning of the fiscal year, the Superintendent of
Public Works shall make a report to the President and Board of Trustees of the
activities for the preceding fiscal year, together with such recommendations as
may be appropriate.
(1988 Code, § 1-9-7) (Ord. 86-135, passed 7-29-1986)
§ 32.008 FIELD SUPERVISOR.
   (A)   General.
      (1)   There is hereby created the position of field supervisor (formerly
known as “foreperson”). The number of such positions shall be determined from
time to time by the President and Board of Trustees.
      (2)   Field supervisors shall be selected by appointment by the President
of the village with the advice and consent of the Board of Trustees.
   (B)   Duties.
      (1)   Field supervisors shall be required to direct operations of
Department of Public Works equipment operators, drivers and laborers and shall
coordinate such operations with the Superintendent and Assistant
Superintendents for the Department.
      (2)   Additionally, field supervisors shall be immediately responsible
for the discipline of subordinates, response to citizens complaints, as
required and directed by the Superintendent and Assistant Superintendents, and
shall assist in the preparation of budget and planning for the Department.
   (C)   Termination. Any person appointed to the position of Superintendent,
Assistant Superintendent or field supervisor shall, upon termination from such
position, be entitled to resume service in any civil service classified
position that such person may have held or any position held under
classification in the Department of Public Works of driver, laborer, equipment
operator, mechanic or custodian pursuant to the collective bargaining agreement
between the village and the American Federation of State, County and Municipal
Employees, Council 31, AFL-CIO, unless such person has been discharged for
cause or otherwise surrendered entitlement to their original position or
classification.
   (D)   Compensation. Compensation for field supervisors shall be as may be
provided for in the annual Appropriations (Budget) Ordinance and Resolution
Setting Salaries, Compensation, Expense Accounts and other Remuneration for
Employees of the Village of Dolton, as from time to time amended.
(1988 Code, § 1-9-8) (Ord. 89-132, passed 12-12-1989; Ord. 97-315, passed - -
1997)
BOARD OF HEALTH
§ 32.020 CREATED; MEMBERSHIP.
   There is hereby created and established a Board of Health in and for the
village, which shall consist of the President who shall, by virtue of this
office, be a member and President of the Board of Health, and of two Trustees
of the village to be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of
the Trustees. The Board of Health may employ a qualified and reputable licensed
physician and surgeon and such other persons possessing necessary technical
qualification to assist the Board in the superintendence and enforcement of the
provisions of this subchapter and all other provisions of this code relative to
or affecting public health.
(1988 Code, § 2-1-1)
§ 32.021 JURISDICTION.
   The jurisdiction of the Board of Health shall extend over the village and to
a point one-half mile beyond the limits of the village and all rules and
regulations of the Board of Health relating to sanitation and public health and
the abatement of nuisances shall apply to and be in force over such territory.
(1988 Code, § 2-1-2)
§ 32.022 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   General. The Board of Health shall exercise a general supervision over
the health of the village and of the people residing and being therein and
shall take such steps and employ such measures as are necessary or expedient to
promote the cleanliness and sanitation of the village.
   (B)   Organization. The Board is hereby vested with power to adopt bylaws
and reasonable rules and regulations to secure the objects of its organization.
   (C)   Nuisances and nuisance abatement. The Board shall have power to define
what shall be deemed nuisances and to abate the same.
   (D)   Disease control.
      (1)   The Board shall have full charge of the prevention, restriction and
suppression of communicable diseases in its jurisdiction, herein described, and
it shall be the duty of the Board to make and enforce such rules and
regulations tending to check and suppress the spread of the disease or diseases
as may be necessary. For this purpose, it shall have power to quarantine any
house or place where any infected person may be, and cause a notice or notices
of warning to be put thereon, and to require the disinfection of the house or
place; and, in general, it shall have authority in matters of quarantine, may
declare and enforce quarantine when none exists and may modify, relax or remove
quarantine after it has established same.
      (2)   It shall be the duty of the Board to investigate into the cause of
dangerously contagious or infectious diseases, especially when existing in
epidemic form, and to take means to restrict and suppress the same. Whenever
any dangerously contagious or infectious disease shall become or threaten to
become epidemic in the village, the Board may enforce such measures as it may
deem necessary to protect the public health.
   (E)   Enforce state rules and regulations. It shall be the duty of the Board
to enforce and observe the rules, regulations and orders of the state’s
Department of Public Health and all state laws pertaining to the preservation
of the health of the people in its jurisdiction.
   (F)   Investigations; duty powers; arrest powers.
      (1)   Investigations. The Board shall have authority to make or cause to
be made such sanitary investigations as it may from time to time deem necessary
for the preservation and improvement of the public’s health.
      (2)   Duty powers; arrest powers. For the purpose of carrying out the
provisions of this subchapter, the members of the Board of Health, its
employees and officers and any police officer acting under direction of said
Board or its members or officials, shall be permitted to enter at any
reasonable hour any premises, house, store, stable, manufactory or other
building, and they shall have the right to arrest or cause to be arrested any
person who shall violate any of the provisions of this subchapter.
   (G)   Additional powers and duties. The Board shall have such further powers
and duties as may from time to time be conferred or placed upon it by
ordinance.
(1988 Code, § 2-1-3)
§ 32.023 UNHEALTHY PREMISES.
   Whenever it shall come to the knowledge of the Board of Health that the
condition of any building or premises is injurious to the health and dangerous
to the lives of the occupants or the public, it shall be the duty of the Board
of Health to make a thorough examination of such building and premises and
direct and instruct the owner or owners or occupants or the person or persons
responsible therefor, or some of them, as to the remedy of such conditions and,
if this be not remedied within a reasonable time, the owner or owners of such
building, and the person or persons putting any such building or premises into
any such condition or responsible therefor shall be jointly and severally
guilty of an additional violation of this section for each period of 24 hours
that shall elapse after they have been notified by the Board of Health that the
condition of such building or premises is injurious to the health or dangerous
to the lives of the occupants or the public and until they shall have remedied
the condition or premises.
(1988 Code, § 2-1-4)
§ 32.024 POLICE TO ASSIST.
   The village’s police officers shall assist the Board of Health in the
performance of its duties when called upon by said Board of Health or any
member thereof.
(1988 Code, § 2-1-5)
BOARD OF LOCAL IMPROVEMENTS
§ 32.035 CREATED; MEMBERSHIP.
   There is hereby established in and for the village a Board of Local
Improvements, consisting of the Village President who shall be president of the
Board and the six Village Trustees who shall be members of the Board of Local
Improvements.
(1988 Code, § 2-2-1)
§ 32.036 SECRETARY OF THE BOARD.
   The Village Clerk shall be ex-officio secretary of the Board of Local
Improvements and for such services shall receive compensation of $1,200 per
year, payable in equal monthly installments of $100 per month.
(1988 Code, § 2-2-2) (Ord. passed 1-14-1974)
§ 32.037 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The Board of Local Improvements shall have all of the powers and authorities
conferred pursuant to Ill. Rev. Stat. Ch. 24, Art. 9, Div. 2, being 50 ILCS 15
as now or hereafter amended, and shall perform the duties assigned to it by
said statute.
(1988 Code, § 2-2-3)
§ 32.038 COMPENSATION.
   The following salaries are hereby established for the president and members
of the Board of Local Improvements:
   (A)   Salary of the President: $1,200 per year, payable in equal monthly
installments of $100 per month; and
   (B)   Salary of each member of the Board of Local Improvements: $1,200 per
year, payable in equal monthly installments of $100 per month.
(1988 Code, § 2-2-4) (Ord. passed 1-14-1975)
PLAN COMMISSION
§ 32.050 CREATED; MEMBERSHIP AND APPOINTMENT.
   (A)   There is hereby created and established a Plan Commission, which shall
be a department of the village government.
   (B)   (1)   The Plan Commission shall consist of five members who shall be
residents of the village.
      (2)   The members shall be appointed by the Village President to serve a
term of one year, or until a successor is appointed, and said appointments are
subject to the approval of the village’s Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 2-3-1) (Ord. 04-273, passed 10-18-2004; Ord. 11-518, passed 3-7-
2011)
§ 32.051 OFFICERS.
   (A)   Secretary. The Village Clerk shall be ex-officio secretary of the Plan
Commission and is empowered to employ a recording secretary for the purpose of
recording and transcribing the proceedings of the Commission.
   (B)   Chairperson of the Commission. One of the members of the Plan
Commission shall be designated by the President, with the consent of the Board
of Trustees, as Chairperson and shall hold office of Chairperson until his or
her successor is appointed.
(1988 Code, § 2-3-2)
§ 32.052 MEETINGS.
   (A)   Regular meetings.
      (1)   Regular meetings shall be held on the second Wednesday of each
month at the hour of 6:30 p.m. in the Village Hall, unless such day shall be a
recognized holiday. In that event, the regular meeting shall be held on the
next day, providing it is not a holiday.
      (2)   Regular meetings may be cancelled by the Chairperson not less than
48 hours’ notification to members.
   (B)   Special meetings. Special meetings may be called by the Chairperson on
48 hours’ written notification to the members.
   (C)   Quorum. A quorum shall consist of four members and no final action
shall be taken on any measure before it, except on the concurrence of four of
the members.
   (D)   Absences from meetings.
      (1)   Three consecutive absences from any regularly scheduled meeting or
three absences in any municipal year shall constitute resignation of said
member unless such absence was for good cause.
      (2)   GOOD CAUSE shall mean only illness of the member, serious illness
of one of the member’s immediate family, death in the member’s immediate family
or absence from the county by reason of scheduled annual vacation.
(1988 Code, § 2-3-3) (Ord. 04-255, passed 5-17-2004)
§ 32.053 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The Plan Commission shall have the following powers and duties:
   (A)   To prepare and recommend to the President and Board of Trustees a plan
or plans for the development and redevelopment of the village and contiguous
unincorporated territory not more than one and one-half miles beyond the
corporate limits of the village and not included in any other municipality.
Such a plan or plans when adopted by the President and Board of Trustees shall
be known as the Official Plan, or part thereof, of the village. Such plan or
plans may be adopted in whole or in separate geographical or functional parts,
each of which when adopted shall be the Official Plan, or part thereof, of the
village. To provide for the health, safety, comfort and convenience of the
inhabitants of the village and contiguous territory, such plan or plans shall
establish reasonable standards of design for subdivisions and for
resubdivisions of unimproved land and of areas subject to redevelopment,
including reasonable requirements for public streets, alleys, ways for public
service facilities, parks, playgrounds, school grounds and other public
grounds;
   (B)   To prepare and recommend to the President and Board of Trustees from
time to time, such changes in the Plan or any part thereof as may be deemed
necessary by the President and Board of Trustees or by the Plan Commission;
   (C)   To prepare and recommend to the President and Board of Trustees from
time to time, plans and/or recommendations for specific improvements in
pursuance of such Official Plan;
   (D)   To give aid to the officials of the village charged with the direction
of projects for improvements embraced within the Official Plan, to further the
making of such improvements and generally to promote the realization of the
Official Plan;
   (E)   To arrange and conduct any form of publicity relative to its
activities for the general purpose of public understanding;
   (F)   To cooperate with municipal or regional planning commissions and other
agencies or groups to further the local planning program and to assure
harmonious and integrated planning for the area;
   (G)   To exercise such other powers germane to the powers granted under
authority of the statutes of the state as may be conferred by the President and
the Board of Trustees under such statutes;
   (H)   To keep written records of its proceedings which shall be open at all
times to public inspection;
   (I)   To file an annual report with the President and Board of Trustees,
setting forth its transactions and recommendations; and
   (J)   To designate land suitable for annexation to the village and to
recommend zoning classification for such land upon annexation.
(1988 Code, § 2-3-4)
§ 32.054 ASSISTANCE AUTHORIZED.
   (A)   The Commission may, at the discretion of the President and Board of
Trustees, employ necessary help whose salaries, wages and other necessary
expenses shall be provided for by adequate appropriation made by the President
and Board of Trustees from the public funds.
   (B)   If said Plan Commission shall deem it advisable to secure technical
advice or services, it may be done upon authority from the President and Board
of Trustees and appropriations therefor by said President and Board of
Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 2-3-5)
CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION
§ 32.065 CREATED; MEMBERSHIP.
   There is hereby created a Civil Service Commission which shall consist of
five members. The members of the Commission shall be considered officers of the
village.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-1) (Ord. 95-284, passed 7-5-1995)
§ 32.066 APPOINTMENT; TERMS OF OFFICE; VACANCIES.
   (A)   The members shall be appointed by the President and each member shall
hold his or her office for three years and until his or her respective
successor has been appointed and qualified. No appointment may be made within
30 days of the expiration of the term of the office of the President, and any
purported appointment made within such time shall be void. All members
heretofore appointed shall remain in office until the expiration of their terms
of office. Not more than three members of the same political party shall be
appointed to the Commission.
   (B)   Whenever a vacancy occurs by reason of death or resignation of a
member, the appointment shall be for the balance of the unexpired term.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-2) (Ord. 85-140, passed 12-12-1985; Ord. 95-284, passed 7-5-
1995; Ord. 00-139, passed 1-18-2000)
§ 32.067 QUALIFICATIONS.
   (A)   Each member must be a citizen of the United States.
   (B)   (1)   At the time of his or her appointment, he or she may not hold
any lucrative office or employment under the United States, the state or any
municipality or other political subdivision of the state, and the acceptance of
such an office during his or her term of appointment shall constitute a
resignation as a member of the Civil Service Commission.
      (2)   Before the President shall appoint any new member, such person must
file an affidavit as to his or her local political party affiliation or, if
such person does not belong to a local political party, then as to his or her
state or national political party affiliations.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-3) (Ord. 00-138, passed 1-18-2000)
§ 32.068 OATH.
   Each member, before entering upon his or her duties, shall take and
subscribe to the oath prescribed by the Constitution. This oath, so subscribed,
shall be filed with the Village Clerk.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-4)
§ 32.069 BOND AND COMPENSATION.
   (A)   Bond. Each member, before entering upon his or her duties, shall
execute a bond to the village in the penal sum of $1,000 conditioned upon the
faithful performance of his or her duties. Said bond shall be for the term of
office of the member. He or she shall file the same with the Village Clerk.
   (B)   Compensation. Each member shall serve without compensation.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-5)
§ 32.070 DUTIES.
   The Commissioners shall classify all of the offices and all of the places of
employment in the village, except for the elected officials, appointed
officials subject to confirmation by the corporate authorities, election
judges, heads of departments, the police and fire personnel, seasonal
employees, which means those persons whose employment does not exceed 90 days
in any one calendar year, and private secretaries of elected officials, if
provided by the corporate authorities.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-6)
§ 32.071 ANNUAL REPORT.
   (A)   (1)   The Commission shall submit to the President, annually, on or
before January 15 of each year, a report of its activities and submit a copy of
its rules or changes.
      (2)   The report may make suggestions which the Commission believes would
result in greater efficiency in the civil service functions of the village.
   (B)   The President shall transmit the report to the Board of Trustees and
may require a report from the Commission at any other time.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-7)
§ 32.072 FACILITIES FOR MEETINGS.
   Suitable rooms for meetings and examinations shall be provided to the
Commission by the President.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-8)
§ 32.073 EXPENDITURES.
   Provision shall be made in the annual appropriation ordinance to provide
adequate funds for the duties and functions of the Commission.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-9)
§ 32.074 ATTORNEY FOR THE COMMISSION.
   The Village Attorney shall be the legal representative of the Commission.
(1988 Code, § 2-5-10)
ZONING BOARD OF APPEALS
§ 32.085 DEFINITION.
   The word BOARD, when used in this subchapter, shall be construed to mean the
Zoning Board of Appeals.
(1988 Code, § 2-4-1)
§ 32.086 CREATED; APPOINTMENT; TERMS OF OFFICE.
   (A)   (1)   A Zoning Board of Appeals is hereby authorized to be
established.
      (2)   Said Board shall consist of seven members appointed by the
President of the Board of Trustees by and with the consent of the Board of
Trustees.
      (3)   The members of the Board shall serve respectively for the following
terms (or until their respective successors are appointed and qualified): one
for one year; one for two years; one for three years; one for four years; and
one for five years; for the first five appointed and five years each for those
following the first five appointed.
      (4)   One of the members of the Board shall be designated by the
President of the Board of Trustees, with the consent of the village, as
Chairperson of said Board and shall hold his or her office as Chairperson of
the Board until his or her successor is appointed.
      (5)   The Chairperson or, in his or her absence, the acting Chairperson
may administer oaths and compel the attendance of witnesses.
(1988 Code, § 2-4-2)
   (B)   Each member must be a resident of the village for at least one year
prior to the date of his or her appointment and must be a citizen of the United
States.
(Ord. 98-373, passed 6-1-1998)
§ 32.087 REMOVALS FROM OFFICE; VACANCIES.
   (A)   The President of the Board of Trustees shall have the power to remove
any member of the Board for cause and after a public hearing.
   (B)   Vacancies upon said Board shall be filled for the unexpired term of
the member whose place has become vacant in the manner herein provided for the
appointment of such member.
(1988 Code, § 2-4-3)
§ 32.088 MEETINGS AND PROCEDURES.
   (A)   All meetings of the Zoning Board of Appeals shall be held at the call
of the Chairperson and at such times as the Board may determine.
   (B)   All hearings conducted by the Board shall be open to the public.
   (C)   (1)   The Board shall keep minutes of its proceedings showing the vote
of each member upon each question or, if absent or failing to vote, indicating
such fact, and shall also keep records of its hearings and other official
actions.
      (2)   Findings of fact shall be included in the minutes of each case of a
requested variation and the reasons for making or denying such variation shall
be specified.
   (D)   Every rule or regulation, every amendment or repeal thereof, and every
order, requirement, decision or determination of the Board shall be filed
immediately in the office of the Board and shall be a public record.
   (E)   The Board shall adopt its own rules of procedure not in conflict with
this code or with the state statutes in such case made and provided.
   (F)   The Chairperson or, in his or her absence, the acting Chairperson may
administer oaths and compel the attendance of witnesses.
   (G)   No hearing may be conducted without a quorum of the Board being
present, which shall consist of a majority of all the members.
   (H)   Any absent member who certifies that he or she has read the transcript
of the proceeding before the Board may vote upon any question before the Board.
(1988 Code, § 2-4-4)
BLOOD COMMISSION
§ 32.100 CREATED; MEMBERSHIP.
   There is hereby created for the village the village’s Blood Commission,
composed of ten members, two of whom shall serve as Co-Chairpersons.
(1988 Code, § 2-10-1)
§ 32.101 APPOINTMENT; TERM OF OFFICE.
   (A)   The members and Co-Chairpersons of the village’s Blood Commission
shall be appointed by the Village President with the advice and consent of the
Board of Trustees to whom recommendation can be made by the Commission.
   (B)   The term of office of each member of the Commission shall be for one
year and until his or her successor shall be appointed and shall qualify.
(1988 Code, § 2-10-2)
§ 32.102 QUALIFICATIONS.
   (A)   Each member of the village’s Blood Commission shall have been a
resident of the village for at least one year prior to his or her appointment.
   (B)   A non-resident may serve as a member of the village’s Blood Commission
at the request of said Commission and shall be appointed by the President with
the advice and consent of the Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 2-10-3)
§ 32.103 ORGANIZATION.
   (A)   The village’s Blood Commission shall meet and elect a Secretary from
its members as soon as possible after its appointment, and the Commission shall
also establish the following committees:
      (1)   Public Relations;
      (2)   Businesses and Schools;
      (3)   Host Groups;
      (4)   Sites; and
      (5)   Telephone.
   (B)   The name of the Secretary and members of the committees, as provided
for in this section, shall be submitted to the President and Board of Trustees
for confirmation and appointment.
(1988 Code, § 2-10-4)
§ 32.104 MEETINGS.
   (A)   The Commission shall hold meetings as may be necessary.
   (B)   Said meetings shall be held in the Village Hall or in some other
suitable place as may be designated by the President and Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 2-10-5)
§ 32.105 PURPOSE AND DUTIES.
   (A)   The purpose of the village’s Blood Commission shall be to implement
the cooperative blood replacement plan.
   (B)   (1)   The Commission shall help to educate the citizenry of the
village of the need to participate as a voluntary blood donor so that the needs
of the individual residents of the village as they relate to an adequate supply
of raw blood for such individuals may be met.
      (2)   The Commission will mobilize community resources and encourage the
participation of residents in the cooperative blood replacement plan.
      (3)   The Commission shall be responsible for conducting a community-wide
education effort to publicize the needs for volunteer donors; the date and
places that which donors may give blood; and the benefits of membership in the
cooperative blood replacement plan.
      (4)   The Commission shall also solicit other civic groups to obtain
their assistance in increasing the number of residents who would become
volunteer blood donors.
      (5)   The Commission shall continue to study the volunteer blood
situation regarding shortages of blood, the question of coverage for
participants in the program, identify and satisfy special areas of need such as
hemophiliacs and solicit from residents such information as may further help
implement the program.
(1988 Code, § 2-10-6)
§ 32.106 INCURRING FINANCIAL LIABILITY.
   Neither the Commission, nor any member thereof, shall incur any financial
liability in the name of the village without specific authority from the
Village President and Board of Trustees and the appropriations therefor by said
President and Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 2-10-7) (Ord. passed 7-31-1979)
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY
§ 32.120 DECLARATION OF POLICY.
   It is hereby found and declared that:
   (A)   The village determines it essential to the continued growth and
stability of the community to provide for business development within the said
village; and that utilization of commercial real estate creates tax base
benefits for all the citizens of the village;
   (B)   Support of commercial and business expansion and development within
the village creates a favorable employment climate, providing opportunities to
the citizens of the village as well as for other south suburban residents;
   (C)   It is deemed a legitimate concern of local government to provide for
the highest and best use of the business and commercial property and that the
economic cultivation of the various types of properties, as determined by
zoning classification, will benefit the economy of the area as well as provide
for the general welfare of the citizens of the village; and
   (D)   Article VII of the 1970 Constitution of this state provides for the
exercise of home rule authority, and that creation of an economic development
authority is a function of government within the general powers of home rule,
and that no state preemption of this power has occurred through any legislative
act.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.121 CREATION OF AUTHORITY.
   There is hereby created the village’s Economic Development Authority.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.122 AUTHORITY.
   Authority for the creation of this body is predicated upon the general home
rule powers articulated in the 1970 Constitution of the state along with the
express grants pursuant to the Business District Development and Redevelopment
Act, being 65 ILCS 5/11-74.3-1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended, and the
Large Business Development Act, being 30 ILCS 750/10-1 et seq. as now or
hereafter amended.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.123 CREATED.
   (A)   There is hereby created a political subdivision heretofore known as
the village’s Economic Development Authority.
   (B)   The Authority may sue and be sued in its corporate name or in the name
of the village, a municipal corporation, and the principal office of the
village’s Economic Development Authority shall be located within the village.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.124 BOARD ORGANIZATION.
   The village’s Economic Development Authority shall be governed by a Board of
Directors comprised of the President, Clerk and the six members of the Board of
Trustees of the village. The President of the Board of Trustees shall serve as
President of the village’s Economic Development authority. The Village Clerk
shall serve as the Secretary of said DEDA and shall keep the minutes of DEDA
and shall perform such other duties as may be required of said office by the
voting members of DEDA. All members shall have voting authority, except for the
President and the Clerk; however, in the case of a tie vote, the President may
then cast a vote.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.125 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The Authority shall have the following powers and duties:
   (A)   To approve all development and redevelopment plans and proposals with
which the Authority shall participate either directly or indirectly;
   (B)   To acquire, make, convey, lease or otherwise dispose of real and
personal property pursuant to economic development or redevelopment purposes;
   (C)   To exercise the use of eminent domain for the acquisition of real or
personal property pursuant to a plan of economic development or redevelopment;
   (D)   To apply for grants and loans from the United States of America, the
state, the county or any political subdivision of any of these, for economic
development or redevelopment purposes;
   (E)   To enter into any contracts with any public or private agency or
person;
   (F)   To employ personal and professional services pursuant to a plan of
economic development or redevelopment;
   (G)   To borrow and lend funds pursuant to a program for economic
development or redevelopment;
   (H)   To establish and promulgate rules and regulations governing the
implementation of any program designed to further the economic development or
redevelopment within the village;
   (I)   To expend such public funds as may be necessary to establish and
implement a plan of economic development and redevelopment; and
   (J)   To exercise such other powers as may be necessary or incidental to the
stated purposes.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.126 INITIAL FUND CREATED.
   There is hereby created a Village Economic Development Fund. Said Economic
Development Fund may be utilized in accordance with the powers and duties
enumerated in this subchapter. The Board of Directors may designate the
Treasurer for the village as the custodian of Authority funds.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.127 SURPLUS FUNDS.
   Any surplus funds remaining at the end of any fiscal year shall be applied
first to abate any tax levy accruing from the General Obligation Bond, Series
1988, Taxable, and, thereafter, to retire any other debt or obligation of the
Authority. Any assets or surplus funds remaining following the dissolution of
the village’s Economic Development Authority funds shall be turned over to the
village for deposit in the Corporate Fund.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.128 DOLTON DEVELOPMENT CENTER; MANAGEMENT.
   Responsibility for administration and management of the property commonly
known as the former Dolton Extrusion Co./Indalex Aluminum Solutions site at
14200 Cottage Grove, Dolton, IL, PIN: 29-02-101-009-0000, shall be transferred
to the village’s Economic Development Authority upon the adoption and passage
of this subchapter.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.129 BUDGET; FISCAL YEAR; ANNUAL REPORT.
   (A)   The Authority shall adopt an annual budget and fix a fiscal year
consistent with the financial plans and objectives of the village and from time
to time, but in no event less than annually, to the extent funds are available
or have been expended during said fiscal year, and shall issue a report on the
administration of funds and programs of the Authority.
   (B)   The fiscal year of the village’s Economic Development Authority shall
be May 1 to April 30.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.130 NO TAXING AUTHORITY.
   The Authority shall not have the power to levy taxes whatsoever.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
§ 32.131 BOARD MEETINGS AND PUBLIC RECORDS.
   Regular meetings of the Board of Directors of the village’s Economic
Development Authority shall be subject to the provisions of the state’s Open
Meetings Act, being 5 ILCS 120/1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended, and be
held at the time and place fixed by the Board. A majority of the authorized
members of the Board shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business
and the Authority may promulgate such rules and regulations as it deems
necessary and appropriate from time to time.
(Ord. 05-282, passed 3-7-2005)
SENIOR CITIZENS’ COMMISSION
§ 32.145 CREATED; APPOINTMENT; OFFICERS.
   There is hereby created a commission to be known as the “Village Senior
Citizens’ Commission”, hereinafter referred to as the “Commission”. The
Commission shall consist of nine members appointed by the Village President
with the advice and consent of the Village Board. The President shall designate
one of the members as Chairperson and the Commission shall select from its
members such other officers as it may deem necessary.
(1988 Code, § 2-12-1) (Ord. 89-128, passed 11-14-1989)
§ 32.146 TERMS OF OFFICE.
   The members of the Commission shall be appointed upon the effective date
hereof. Three members shall be appointed for a term expiring 5-1-1990; three
members shall be appointed for a term expiring 5-1-1991; and three members
appointed for a term expiring 5-1-1992. Thereafter, all appointments shall be
for a period of three years.
(1988 Code, § 2-12-2) (Ord. 89-128, passed 11-14-1989)
§ 32.147 QUALIFICATIONS.
   All members of the Commission shall be persons 55 years of age or older and
shall be residents of the village.
(1988 Code, § 2-12-3)
§ 32.148 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   In addition to authority otherwise provided by law, the Commission shall
have the following powers and duties:
   (A)   To evaluate all programs, services and facilities for the aged within
the village in order to determine the extent to which present public or private
programs, services and facilities meet the needs of the aged;
   (B)   To coordinate and evaluate all programs, services and facilities for
the aging presently furnished by the village and make appropriate
recommendations regarding such programs, services and facilities to the
President and the Village Board;
   (C)   To assist community agencies on aging and other groups developing
local services for senior citizens;
   (D)   To promote community education regarding the problems of senior
citizens;
   (E)   To cooperate with agencies of the state and federal government in
studies and conferences designed to examine the needs of senior citizens;
   (F)   To promote throughout the village “Senior Citizens’ Day” which shall
be observed on the third Sunday of May of each year, as a day to honor and
remember senior citizens; and
   (G)   To establish and fund projects, as approved by the President and
Village Board, to fulfill the intent of this subchapter and the abovementioned
powers and duties.
(1988 Code, § 2-12-4)
§ 32.149 COMPENSATION.
   Members of the Commission shall serve without compensation, but may be
reimbursed for actual expenses incurred in the performance of their duties if
approved by the President and Village Board.
(1988 Code, § 2-12-5) (Ord. 85-117, passed 6-18-1985)
YOUTH RESOURCES COMMISSION
§ 32.160 ESTABLISHED; MEMBERSHIP AND APPOINTMENT.
   (A)   There is hereby established a Youth Resources Commission consisting of
seven members to be appointed by the Village President with the advice and
consent of the Board of Trustees.
   (B)   The Village President shall serve the Commission as an ex-officio
member.
(1988 Code, § 2-13-1) (Ord. passed 11-20-1973; Ord. 12-783, passed 12-3-2012)
§ 32.161 TERM OF OFFICE; VACANCIES.
   (A)   The term of office of each member of the Commission shall be for one
year and until his or her successor shall be appointed and shall qualify.
   (B)   The Village President, with the advice and consent of the Board of
Trustees, is authorized to fill any vacancy which may arise for its unexpired
term. Nothing herein contained shall preclude the reappointment of any member
or the Chairperson of the Commission.
(1988 Code, § 2-13-2) (Ord. passed 2-6-1973; Ord. passed 11-20-1973)
§ 32.162 QUALIFICATIONS.
   The persons appointed to the Commission shall be residents of the village,
or persons employed within the village, or persons whose business, occupation
or professional activity is carried on in a substantial degree within the
village. When such residence, employment or professional activity within the
village no longer exists, a member shall be deemed to have resigned from the
Commission.
(1988 Code, § 2-13-3) (Ord. passed 2-6-1973)
§ 32.163 ORGANIZATION AND PROCEDURES.
   (A)   Officers.
      (1)   The Village President, with the advice and consent of the Board of
Trustees, shall designate one of its members to act as Chairperson.
      (2)   The Commission may elect from its members a Secretary and such
other officers as it may deem advisable.
   (B)   Conduct of business.
      (1)   The Commission may adopt rules of order and procedure for the
conduct of its business.
      (2)   Five members of the Commission shall constitute a quorum.
   (C)   Special meetings. The Chairperson of the Commission, the Village
President or any three members of the Commission shall have the authority to
call special meetings of the Commission.
   (D)   Attendance at meetings. The Chairperson of the Commission, or some
person designated by him or her, shall maintain a record of attendance of each
member thereof.
(1988 Code, § 2-13-4) (Ord. passed 11-20-1973)
§ 32.164 PURPOSE.
   The purpose of the Commission is to conserve the human resources represented
by the village’s youth, and to protect and preserve the village’s community by
creating and providing programs designed to promote good adjustment,
responsibility, independence, citizenship and sportsmanship among the village’s
youth by utilizing available facilities, inaugurating programs and methods of
education and re-education and training directed toward the well-being of the
youth of the village.
(1988 Code, § 2-13-5)
§ 32.165 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The Commission shall perform and exercise the following functions and
powers:
   (A)   To cooperate with the Village President, the Board of Trustees,
village departments, agencies and officials in carrying out a comprehensive
program of youth welfare involving all public and voluntary agencies of the
community in promoting the providing of services and facilities to the youth of
the village and their families;
   (B)   To recommend such legislative action to the Board of Trustees as it
may deem appropriate to effectuate the policies of the Commission. The
Commission, through its Chairperson or other designated member, shall report
annually in writing to the President and Board of Trustees, on or before June 1
of each year. Such report shall cover the activities of the Commission for the
preceding municipal year;
   (C)   To invite, enlist and encourage the cooperation of all public and
private voluntary agencies, religious and ethnic groups, community
organizations, labor and business organizations, fraternal and benevolent
societies, and other groups in the village, in carrying out their mission as
the same affects the youth of the village and their families; and
   (D)   Through a program of education, training, promotion and organization,
to encourage the formation of neighborhood groups and to assist these groups in
conducting activities aimed at developing and extending constructive programs
for youth, and by encouraging adequately-trained adult sponsors for the youths.
(1988 Code, § 2-13-6)
§ 32.166 FACILITIES AND SERVICES AVAILABLE.
   The facilities of the Municipal Building shall be available to the
Commission for all its meetings. The service of all village departments and
agencies shall be made available to the Commission on request. Any information
in the hands of any department or agency shall be offered to the Commission
upon request, except such information as by law cannot be divulged to the
public.
(1988 Code, § 2-13-7)
§ 32.167 INCURRING FINANCIAL LIABILITY.
   Neither the Commission, nor any member thereof, shall incur any financial
liability in the name of the village without specific authority from the
Village President and Board of Trustees and the appropriations therefor by said
President and Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 2-13-8) (Ord. passed 2-6-1973)
§ 32.168 COMPENSATION.
   The members of the Commission shall serve without compensation.
(1988 Code, § 2-13-9) (Ord. passed 11-20-1973)
HISTORIC PRESERVATION COMMISSION
§ 32.180 ESTABLISHED; MEMBERSHIP; APPOINTMENT.
   (A)   There is hereby established the village’s Historic Preservation
Commission consisting of seven voting members and three non-voting members. The
seven voting members, which includes the Chairperson, shall consist of four
residents of the village and up to three non-residents. All members of the
village’s Historic Preservation Commission, including the Chairperson, shall be
appointed by the Village President and with the advice and consent of the
Trustees.
   (B)   The seven voting members of the Commission shall be appointed on the
basis of demonstrated expertise, experience or interest in any of the areas of
anthropology, architecture, art, building construction, engineering, finance,
historical and architectural preservation, history, law, community development,
planning, real estate and related professions.
   (C)   The Mayor, with the approval of the Board of Trustees, may appoint
three people to serve as non-voting members of the Commission. Such members
shall be appointed on the same basis as voting members, but the non-voting
members need not be residents of the village. Non-voting members shall not hold
any officer positions. Each non-voting member shall serve a two-year term.
(1988 Code, § 2-14-1) (Ord. 25-005, passed 10-6-2025)
§ 32.181 TERM OF OFFICE; VACANCIES.
   (A)   The Chairperson and each member shall be appointed for the length of
the term of the Mayor and each appointment shall expire on April 30 of the year
of the regular election for the office of Mayor. Any three consecutive absences
or any three absences in any municipal year by any member shall be considered
as the resignation of said member unless such absence was for good cause. GOOD
CAUSE shall mean only illness, death of a member of the family or regular
vacation of the member absenting himself or herself from the county.
   (B)   Upon the certification by the Chairperson that a vacancy exists by
reason of said absences, the Mayor shall appoint a successor to fill out the
unexpired term of said member.
(1988 Code, § 2-14-2) (Ord. passed 11-1-1983; Ord. 25-005, passed 10-6-2025)
§ 32.182 QUALIFICATIONS.
   Each voting and non-voting member of the village’s Historical Preservation
Commission shall be appointed on the basis of demonstrated expertise as
indicated in §
32.180(B).
(1988 Code, § 2-14-3) (Ord. 85-110, passed 6-4-1985; Ord. 25-005, passed 10-6-
2025)
§ 32.183 ORGANIZATION AND MEETINGS.
   (A)   Secretary. The Commission shall have a Secretary who shall be
appointed by the Mayor. The Secretary may be appointed from the membership of
the Commission.
   (B)   Meetings.
      (1)   Regular meetings. The Commission shall determine the time and place
of all of the official meetings of the Commission and give proper notice
thereof.
      (2)   Special meetings. The Chairperson of the Commission, the Mayor or
any three members of the Commission shall have the authority to call special
meetings of the Commission. Written notice of special meetings shall be given
to all members.
   (C)   Minutes and records. The Commission shall keep minutes and records of
all meetings and proceedings.
   (D)   Disclosure of interest. Any members of the Commission having a
pecuniary interest or personal interest in any matter coming before the
Commission shall disclose such interest to the other members and such interest
shall not be made a matter of record. Any member having such an interest shall
not participate in such matter as a member of the Commission, nor shall he or
she be counted in determining a quorum for consideration of such matter.
(1988 Code, § 2-14-4) (Ord. 25-005, passed 10-6-2025)
§ 32.184 DUTIES.
   The Commission shall have the following duties:
   (A)   To make recommendations to the Village Board for the designation of
landmarks, historic districts and urban conservation districts within the
corporate limits of the village in accordance with the procedures and standards
hereinafter set forth;
   (B)   To issue, modify, deny, suspend and revoke certificates of
appropriateness and economic hardship in accordance with the procedures and
criteria hereinafter set forth. The Commission may selectively delegate its
authority to grant a certificate of appropriateness for the more routine
requests, i.e., like-for-like alterations that are clearly appropriate and so
consistent with the purpose of this subchapter and adopted design guidelines
that further review is not required;
   (C)   To adopt rules and regulations, including such guidelines as may be
deemed necessary for review of applications for certificates of appropriateness
and economic hardship;
   (D)   To keep a register of all property and improvements which have been
designated for preservation. This register shall include the information
required of each designation, along with the appropriate maps;
   (E)   To provide technical and professional assistance to the owners of the
property and improvements which have been designated for preservation;
   (F)   To retain, upon approval of the Village Board, such specialists as may
be required from time to time;
   (G)   To engage in mutual cooperation with other village departments and
commissions on matters affecting the property and improvements which have been
designated for preservation;
   (H)   To make suggestions and recommendations related to the nomination of
designated property and improvements to state and national registers;
   (I)   To perform any and all functions which will foster the marking and
maintenance of designated property and improvements in accordance with the
respect to which they are entitled and as will aid the public in visiting such
property so acquired, all in accordance with the purposes, procedures and
standards set forth herein;
   (J)   To recommend the village’s acquisition by donation, purchase or
eminent domain of a fee or lesser interest in designated property and
improvements, including, but not limited to, easements, covenants and leasehold
interests, and to reconstruct, maintain, operate or transfer such property so
acquired, all in accordance with the purposes, procedures and standards set
forth herein;
   (K)   To induce by contract or other consideration the creation of covenants
or restrictions binding on land;
   (L)   To seek, on behalf of the village, funds from federal, state and
private sources for deposit in a separate account of the village, to be
referred to as the Preservation Fund, of which funds shall only be loaned or
expended in accordance with procedures established by the Village Board for
such purposes as set forth herein;
   (M)   To recommend the village’s acquisition by donation, purchase or
eminent domain of a fee or lesser interest in property which is within the
public view and adjacent to, immediately surrounding or in the nearby vicinity
of designated property and improvements for the alteration, clearance or
maintenance of which is important for the proper preservation and use of the
designated property and improvement, including property outside the corporate
limits;
   (N)   To recommend the issuance of bonds or liens by the corporate
authorities; and
   (O)   To cooperate with other governmental bodies or agencies and not-for-
profit organizations with purposes similar to those set forth in this
subchapter, including, but not limited to, the execution of contracts and the
conveyance of property whether by purchase or donation.
(1988 Code, § 2-14-5) (Ord. 25-005, passed 10-6-2025)
§ 32.185 INCURRING FINANCIAL LIABILITY.
   Neither the Commission, nor any member thereof shall incur any financial
liability in the name of the village without prior approval of the Mayor and
Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 2-14-6) (Ord. 25-005, passed 10-6-2025)
§ 32.186 COMPENSATION.
   Each member shall serve without compensation.
(1988 Code, § 2-14-7) (Ord. passed 11-1-1983)
HUMAN RELATIONS COMMISSION
§ 32.200 CREATED; MEMBERSHIP.
   (A)   There is hereby created a commission to be known as the “Village Human
Relations Commission”, hereinafter referred to as the “Commission”. The
Commission shall consist of nine members appointed by the President with the
advice and consent of the Village Board, one of which shall be designated by
the Mayor as Chairperson. Vacancies in the Commission shall be filled in the
same manner as the original appointments: at least two-thirds of the members of
the Commission shall be residents of the village.
   (B)   The initial members of the Commission shall be appointed as soon as
possible after the effective date hereof. These appointments shall be for a
term ending 5-1-1987 and thereafter for a term of one year. All appointments
shall terminate on May 1 after the original term of appointment.
(1988 Code, § 2-15-1) (Ord. 97-332, passed 7-7-1997)
§ 32.201 OFFICERS.
   The Commission shall select from its membership such other officers,
excluding the Chairperson, as it may deem necessary. The Commission shall not
employ any employees, assistants, research assistants nor enter into any
contracts unless approved by the President and the village’s Board of Trustees.
Members of the Commission shall serve without compensation, but may be
reimbursed for actual expenses incurred in the performance of their duties if
approved by the Mayor and Village Board.
(1988 Code, § 2-15-2)
§ 32.202 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   The Commission shall have the responsibility to administer this subchapter
and may exercise powers including, but not limited to, the following:
   (A)   Receive and investigate complaints charging unlawful and/or
discriminatory acts and unfair housing practices;
   (B)   Initiate complaints charging unlawful discriminatory acts and unfair
housing practices;
   (C)   Attempt to resolve any such complaints through conciliation;
   (D)   Recommend educational and other programs designed to promote the
purposes of this subchapter;
   (E)   Gather and provide for the exchange of information related to the
provisions of this subchapter among real estate agents, lending institutions,
developers, employers, municipal officials, community relations, and other
persons with an interest in effective enforcement of this subchapter;
   (F)   Conduct discussions in churches, residences and other public locations
for the purpose of listening to concerns of residents, communicating accurately
to residents the policies and programs of the village that are responsive to
their concerns;
   (G)   Facilitate responses of appropriate village departments to concerns of
residents; and
   (H)   Such duties as may be delegated by the President or Board of Trustees
to accomplish the objectives of the Commission.
(1988 Code, § 2-15-3)
§ 32.203 FUNDING.
   (A)   In the performance of its duties, the Commission may accept grants of
funds from the Federal or State Government, or any agency thereof, or from
foundations or other public or private organizations.
   (B)   Any funds received shall be audited annually by the Village Treasurer
and the Village Auditor.
(1988 Code, § 2-15-4) (Ord. 86-140, passed 11-5-1986)
KEY OUTREACH COMMISSION
§ 32.215 CREATED.
   (A)   There is hereby created a commission to be known as the “Village Key
Outreach Commission”, hereinafter referred to as the “Commission”.
   (B)   The Commission shall consist of 11 members appointed by the President
with the advice and consent of the Village Board, one of which shall be
designated by the President as Chairperson.
   (C)   The Commission shall select from its members such other officers as it
may deem necessary.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
§ 32.216 STRUCTURE AND COMMITTEES.
   (A)   The Commission shall adopt bylaws within 90 days after the appointment
of sufficient members to constitute a quorum. Upon adoption, the bylaws shall
be filed with the Village Clerk and a copy shall be tendered to the President
and Board of Trustees. The Commission shall meet not less than every 45 days
and shall submit annual reports to the Board of Trustees. The Commission shall
establish standing committees which shall consist of at least three Commission
members. There shall be standing committees for each of the areas of services
provided by the Commission, as well as additional special committees to
consider and report on matters referred to the special committee. The special
committees shall terminate upon the completion of the business referred to
them. The Chairperson shall be an ex-officio member of all committee, but shall
not be counted in determining the quorum at any committee meeting and shall not
be permitted to vote.
   (B)   No report from any standing or special committee shall be presented
for consideration at a Commission meeting unless the same has been sent to all
members 48 hours prior to the meeting date; provided, however, the Chairperson
may authorize the presentation of emergency matters without prior submission to
members. The Chairperson shall refer the matters approved by the committees to
the Board of Commissioners for consideration.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
§ 32.217 MEMBERS.
   (A)   The members of the Commission shall be appointed upon the effective
date hereof. Four members shall be appointed for a four-year term; four members
shall be appointed for a three year term; and three members shall be appointed
for a two-year term.
   (B)   Thereafter, all appointments shall be for a period three years.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
§ 32.218 QUALIFICATIONS.
   (A)   The persons appointed to the Commission shall be residents of the
village, or persons whose occupation or professional activity is carried on in
a substantial degree within the village.
   (B)   The village’s Police Department shall fingerprint and perform
background checks for all members of the Commission within 30 days of the
appointments. No member shall have been convicted of a felony and said
conviction shall be grounds for removal from the Commission.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
§ 32.219 PURPOSE.
   (A)   It shall be the mission of the Commission to mobilize resources that
encourage the delivery of services which enhance and promote positive character
traits in the village’s youth. This will be achieved by developing,
implementing and monitoring activities and programs in coordination with
community and agencies.
   (B)   The Commission shall provide supportive services to the village’s
youth that have been identified and referred through various agencies and
entities, including, but not limited to, the village’s Police Department
through station adjustments, the county’s Court System or educational
institutions. All participation must be voluntary and the youth must have the
written consent of a parent or guardian.
   The types of services provided or coordinated on behalf of the youth or
juveniles shall include:
      (1)   The identification of the youths in need of services;
      (2)   Assessment of the specific areas of need for each individual youth;
      (3)   Provision of services directly or through referral that are
specifically designed to meet the youth’s individual needs;
      (4)   Identification of alternatives to the current life style of the
youth which may be contributing to the problematic behavior, including
employment referrals; and
      (5)   Such other appropriate relief as deemed appropriate.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
§ 32.220 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES.
   In addition to authority otherwise provided by law, the Commission shall
have the following powers and duties:
   (A)   To evaluate programs, services and facilities for youth within the
village to determine the extent to which present public or private programs,
services and facilities meet the need of the youth;
   (B)   To assist community agencies on youth and other groups developing
local services for youth;
   (C)   To cooperate with agencies of the state and federal government in
studies and conferences designed to examine needs of youth involved in criminal
and quasi-criminal activity; and
   (D)   To establish and fund projects as approved by the President and
Village Board, to fulfill the intent of this subchapter and the above-mentioned
powers and duties.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
§ 32.221 FACILITIES AVAILABLE.
   The facilities of the Village Municipal Building, or other village-owned
facilities, upon the advice and consent of the President, shall be available to
the Commission for all its meetings.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
§ 32.222 CONFIDENTIALITY.
   (A)   The services of village’s Police Department shall be made available to
the Commission on request.
   (B)   The village’s Police Department shall assist and provide relevant
information to the Commission, upon request, and to the extent required, the
Commission members shall be bound by the same code of confidentiality as the
members of the village’s Police Department.
   (C)   No confidential information regarding any youth shall be divulged, to
the extent required by law.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
§ 32.223 INCURRING FINANCIAL LIABILITY.
   Neither the Commission, nor any member thereof, shall incur any financial
liability in the name of the village without specific authority from the
Village President and Board of Trustees and the appropriations therefor by said
President and Board of Trustees.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
§ 32.224 COMPENSATION.
   The members shall serve without compensation.
(Ord. 97-346A, passed 10-6-1997)
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES
§ 32.235 CREATION.
   (A)   There is hereby created a Department of Administrative Services, which
shall consist of a Director and such number of employees as may from time to
time be determined by the President and the Board of Trustees.
   (B)   The Department of Administrative Services shall be subject to the
direction and authority of the Chief of Staff.
(Ord. 02-186, passed 7-23-2002)
§ 32.236 OATH.
   The Director of the Department of Administrative Services shall take the
customary oath prescribed by statute before entering the duties of the office.
The subscribed oath shall be filed in the office of the Village Clerk.
(Ord. 02-186, passed 7-23-2002)
§ 32.237 FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES.
   The functions, duties and responsibilities of the Department of
Administrative Services shall be as follows:
   (A)   To administer and enforce all of the responsibilities, power and
duties delegated to it by village ordinance, pursuant to the village’s
municipal code;
   (B)   To exercise general supervision over the water transfer stamp tax
process as set forth in §§
151.235 through
151.244 of this code of ordinances, as amended.
      (1)   The water transfer stamp shall be issued by the Department of
Administrative Services after payment of the tax to the Village Collector.
      (2)   The Department of Administrative Services shall issue an adhesive
stamp or stamps, in a form prescribed by the village and such stamp(s) shall be
affixed to the face of the deed or instrument of conveyance;
   (C)   To exercise general supervision over the business and license
applications. All applications for licenses and permits, and the regulations
relating thereto as provided in, shall be submitted to the Department of
Administrative Services, in writing on forms to be prescribed and furnished by
the Village Board and the village as provided in Ch. 110 of this code of
ordinances, as amended. The Department of Administrative Services shall keep a
record of all applications;
   (D)   To exercise general supervision over the issuance of §
110.08 of this code of ordinances, as amended.
      (1)   Duplicate licenses. The Department of Administrative Services, upon
satisfactory evidence of such loss or destruction being filed with the
Department of Administrative Services and the payment to the village of $5 for
such duplicate, the Department of Administrative Services shall issue a
duplicate thereof.
      (2)   Vehicle tags. The Department of Administrative Services shall
furnish each licensee with a tag or sticker for each vehicle covered by the
license.
   (E)   To exercise general supervision over the Approval and Issuance of
License process as provided in §
110.09 of this code of ordinances, as amended. Licenses shall be granted and
signed by the Village President and issued by the Department of Administrative
Services;
   (F)   To exercise general supervision over the issuance of notices of
license terminations, as provided in § 
110.10 of this code of ordinances, as amended;
   (G)   To exercise general supervision over the transfer of license or
permit, change of location, process as provided in §
110.11 of this code of ordinances, as amended;
   (H)   To exercise general supervision over special assessments, as provided
in and the preparation and issuance of special assessments bills, which bills
shall be prepared with interest computed thereon as may be required. The
Department of Administrative Services shall prepare and safely keep all of the
books and records relating to the special assessments and issuance of bills
therefor;
   (I)   To exercise general supervision over water bills, accounts and
samples, as provided in the village’s municipal code, as amended. The
Department of Administrative Services shall be responsible for the billing of
water accounts. The Department of Administrative Services shall see that all
water meters are read for billing purposes; that such meters are kept in a good
state of repair; and that samples of the water supply be taken monthly and
analyzed to ensure the safety of the water supply;
   (J)   To exercise general supervision over the issuance of fishing, hunting
and trapping licenses as provided in the village. The Department of
Administrative Services shall issue said applications and licenses for fishing,
hunting and trapping; and
   (K)   To exercise general supervision over the zoning regulations of the
village, as provided in this code of ordinances. The Director of the Department
of Administrative Services shall be the Zoning Administrative Officer and as
such shall be charged with the enforcement of the zoning regulations of the
village.
(Ord. 02-186, passed 7-23-2002)

the bylaws shall be filed with the Village Clerk and a copy shall be tendered
to the President and Board of Trustees.

annual reports to the Board of Trustees.

and procedures:

scholarship award; and
   (C)   For monitoring and reporting activities.

facilities, upon the advice and consent of the President, shall be available to
the Commission for all its meetings.
(Ord. 07-422, passed 11-5-2007)

required, the Commission members shall be bound by the same code of
confidentiality as the members of the village’s Police Department. No
confidential information regarding any student applicant shall be divulged, to
the extent required by law.
(Ord. 07-422, passed 11-5-2007)

(Ord. 07-422, passed 11-5-2007)
