CIVIL EMERGENCIES
§ 33.001 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CIVIL EMERGENCY.
      (1)   A riot or unlawful assembly characterized by the use of actual
force or violence or any threat to use force, accompanied by immediate power to
execute by three or more persons acting together without authority of law.
      (2)   Any natural disaster or human-made calamity including flood,
conflagration, cyclone, tornado, earthquake or explosion within the corporate
limits of the village resulting in the death or injury of persons or the
destruction of property to such an extent that extraordinary measures must be
taken to protect the public health, safety and welfare.
   CURFEW. A prohibition against any person or persons walking, running,
loitering, standing or motoring upon any alley, street, highway, public
property or vacant premises within the corporate limits of the village,
excepting persons officially designated to duty with reference to said civil
emergency.
(1988 Code, § 5-3-1)
§ 33.002 DECLARATION OF EMERGENCY; PROCEDURES.
   (A)   Declaration of emergency; expiration. When, in the judgment of the
Village President, a civil emergency as defined herein is deemed to exist, he
or she shall forthwith proclaim in writing under oath the existence of same and
shall set forth in the proclamation the facts upon which the proclamation is
based and shall describe the nature of the emergency. Such statement shall be
filed with the Village Clerk as soon as practicable. Such state of emergency
shall expire not later than the adjournment of the first regular meeting of the
corporate authorities after the state of emergency is declared.
   (B)   General curfew. After proclamation of a civil emergency by the
President, he or she may order a general curfew applicable to such geographical
areas of the village or to the village as a whole as he or she deems advisable,
and applicable during such hours of the day or night as he or she deems
necessary in the interest of the public safety and welfare.
   (C)   Movement restricted. After proclamation of a civil emergency by the
President, he or she may restrict or prohibit movement into, out of or within
the affected area or areas.
   (D)   Orders permitted. After proclamation of a civil emergency, the Village
President may also, in the interest of public safety and welfare, make any or
all of the following orders:
      (1)   Order the closing of all retail liquor stores;
      (2)   Order the closing of all taverns;
      (3)   Order the closing of all private clubs or portions thereof wherein
the consumption of intoxicating liquor and/or beer is permitted;
      (4)   Order the discontinuance of selling, distributing or giving away
gasoline or other liquid flammable or combustible products in any container
other than a gasoline tank properly affixed to a motor vehicle;
      (5)   Order the closing of gasoline stations and other establishments,
the chief activity of which is the sale, distribution or dispensing of liquid
flammable or combustible products;
      (6)   Order the discontinuance of selling, distributing, dispensing or
giving away of any firearms or ammunition of any character whatsoever;
      (7)   Order the closing of any or all establishments or portions thereof,
the chief activity of which is the sale, distribution, dispensing or giving
away of firearms and/or ammunition;
      (8)   Prohibit or limit the assemblage of persons; and
      (9)   Issue such other orders as are imminently necessary for the
protection of life and property.
(1988 Code, § 5-3-2) Penalty, see §
33.999
§ 33.003 OBEDIENCE TO ORDERS.
   No person shall fail to obey the lawful orders of any police officer or
other authorized person, and no person shall in any way intentionally interfere
with any person in the protection or preservation of life or property during
the existence of a state of emergency as proclaimed, as provided in §
33.002(A) of this chapter.
(1988 Code, § 5-3-3) Penalty, see §
33.999
EMERGENCY SERVICES AND DISASTER AGENCY (ESDA)
§ 33.015 ESTABLISHMENT.
   (A)   There is hereby created the village’s ESDA to prevent, minimize,
repair and alleviate injury or damage resulting from disaster caused by enemy
attack, sabotage or other hostile action, or from natural or human-made
disaster, in accordance with the state’s Emergency Services and Disaster Act of
1975.
   (B)   This ESDA shall consist of the Director and such additional members as
may be selected by the Director.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-1)
§ 33.016 DIRECTOR.
   (A)   The Director of the village’s ESDA shall be appointed by the Village
President and shall serve until removed by same.
   (B)   The Director shall have direct responsibility for the organization,
administration, training and operation of the ESDA, subject to the direction
and control of the Village President as provided by statute.
   (C)   In the event of the absence, resignation, death or inability to serve
as the Director, the Village President, or any person designated by him or her,
shall be and act as Director until a new appointment is made as provided in
this subchapter.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-2)
§ 33.017 FUNCTIONS.
   The village’s ESDA shall perform such ESDA functions within the village as
shall be prescribed in and by the state’s ESDA Plan and Program prepared by the
Governor, and such orders, rules and regulations as may be promulgated by the
Governor and, in addition, shall perform such duties outside the corporate
limits of the village as may be required pursuant to any mutual aid agreement
with any other political subdivision, municipality or quasi-municipality
entered into as provided by the state’s ESDA Act of 1975.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-3)
§ 33.018 SERVICE AS MOBILE SUPPORT TEAM.
   (A)   All or any members of the village’s ESDA may be designated as members
of a mobile support team created by the Director of the state’s ESDA as
provided by law.
   (B)   The leader of such mobile support team shall be designated by the
Director of the village’s ESDA.
   (C)   (1)   Any member of a mobile support team who is a village employee or
officer while serving on call to duty by the Governor, or the state’s Director,
shall receive the compensation and have the powers, duties, rights and
immunities incident to such employment or office.
      (2)   Any such member who is not a paid officer or employee of the
village, while so serving, shall receive from the state reasonable compensation
as provided by law.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-4)
§ 33.019 AGREEMENTS WITH OTHER POLITICAL SUBDIVISIONS.
   The Director of ESDA may negotiate mutual aid agreements with other
municipal corporations or political subdivisions of the state, but no such
agreement shall be effective until it has been approved by the President and
Board of Trustees and by the state’s Director of ESDA.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-5)
§ 33.020 EMERGENCY ACTION.
   If the Governor declares that a disaster emergency exists in the event of
actual enemy attack upon the United States or the occurrence within the state
of a major disaster resulting from enemy sabotage or other hostile action, or
from human-made or natural disaster, it shall be the duty of the village’s ESDA
to cooperate fully with the state’s ESDA and with the Governor in the exercise
of emergency powers as provided by law.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-6)
§ 33.021 COMPENSATION.
   Members of the ESDA who are paid employees or officers of the village, if
called for training by the state’s Director of ESDA, shall receive for the time
spent in such training the same rate of pay as is attached to the position
held; members who are not such village employees or officers shall receive for
such training time such compensation as may be established by the Board of
Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-7)
§ 33.022 REIMBURSEMENT BY STATE.
   The Village Treasurer may receive and allocate to the appropriate fund, any
reimbursement by the state to the village for expenses incident to training
members of the ESDA as prescribed by the state’s Director of ESDA, compensation
for services and expenses of members of a mobile support team while serving
outside the village in response to a call by the Governor or state’s Director
of ESDA, as provided by law, and any other reimbursement made by the state
incident to ESDA activities as provided by law.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-8)
§ 33.023 PURCHASES AND EXPENDITURES.
   (A)   The Board of Trustees may, on recommendation of the village’s Director
of ESDA, authorize any purchase or contracts necessary to place the village in
a position to combat effectively any disaster resulting from the explosion of
any nuclear or other bomb or missile, and to protect the public health and
safety, protect property and provide emergency assistance to victims in the
case of such disaster or from human-made or natural disaster.
   (B)   In the event of enemy-caused or other disaster, the village’s Director
of ESDA is authorized, on behalf of the village, to procure such services,
supplies, equipment or material as may be necessary for such purposes, in view
of the exigency without regard to the statutory procedures or formalities
normally prescribed by law pertaining to village contracts or obligations, as
authorized by the state’s ESDA Act of 1975; provided that, if the Board of
Trustees meets at such time, he or she shall act subject to the directions and
restrictions imposed by that body and subject to the directions and
restrictions imposed by the Village President.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-9)
§ 33.024 OATH.
   Every person appointed to serve in any capacity in the village’s ESDA shall,
before entering upon his or her duties, subscribe to the following oath, which
shall be filed with the Director:
“I,                                                  , do solemnly swear (or
affirm) that I will support and defend and bear true allegiance to the
Constitution of the United States and the Constitution of the State of Illinois
and the territory, institutions and facilities thereof, both public and
private, against all enemies, foreign and domestic; that I take this obligation
freely, without any mental reservation or purpose of evasion; and that I will
well and faithfully discharge the duties upon which I am about to enter. And I
do further swear (or affirm) that I do not advocate, nor am I, nor have I been,
a member of any political party or organization that advocates the overthrow of
the government of the United States or of this State by force or violence; and
that during such time as I am affiliated with the Dolton ESDA Organization, I
will not advocate nor become a member of any political party or organization
that advocates the overthrow of the government of the United States or of this
State by force or violence”.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-10)
§ 33.025 OFFICE.
   The Village President is authorized to designate space in the Village Hall
or elsewhere as may be provided for by the Board of Trustees for the village’s
ESDA as its office.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-11)
§ 33.026 APPROPRIATION; LEVY OF TAXES.
   The Village Board may make an appropriation for ESDA purposes in the manner
provided by law, and may levy, in addition for ESDA purposes only, a tax not to
exceed $0.05 per $100 of the assessed value of all taxable property in addition
to all other taxes, as provided by the state’s ESDA Act of 1975; however, that
amount collectible under such levy, shall not exceed $0.25 per capita.
(1988 Code, § 2-6-12)
BOARD OF FIRE AND POLICE COMMISSIONERS
§ 33.040 CREATED; MEMBERSHIP.
   There is hereby created a Board of Fire and Police Commissioners which shall
consist of seven members. The members of the Board shall be considered officers
of the village.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-1)
§ 33.041 APPOINTMENT; TERM OF OFFICE.
   (A)   The Board of Fire and Police Commission shall consist of five members
who shall be residents of the village.
   (B)   The members shall be appointed by the Village President to serve a
term of three years, or until a successor is appointed, and said appointments
are subject to the approval of the village’s Board of Trustees.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-2) (Ord. 85-139, passed 12-12-1985; Ord. 94-239, passed 3-1-
1994; Ord. 97-341, passed 9-15-1997; Ord. 99-107, passed 4-19-1999; Ord. 11-
519, passed 3-7-2011)
§ 33.042 VACANCIES; REMOVALS FROM OFFICE.
   (A)   Whenever a vacancy occurs by reason of death or resignation of a
member, the appointment shall be for the balance of the unexpired term.
   (B)   (1)   No member during his or her term may be removed except for
cause, upon written charges, and after an opportunity to be heard within 30
days after receipt of the written charges, before a regular meeting of the
Board of Trustees.
      (2)   A majority vote of the elected members of the Board of Trustees
shall be required to remove such member from office.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-3)
§ 33.043 QUALIFICATIONS.
   Each member must be a resident of the village for at least one year prior to
the date of his or her appointment and a citizen of the United States. At the
time of his or her appointment, he or she may not hold any office under the
village and the acceptance of such an office during his or her term of
appointment shall constitute a resignation as a member of the Board of Fire and
Police Commissioners. Such member may not be related either by blood or
marriage up to the degree of first cousin to any elected officer of the
village. Before the President shall appoint any member, such person must file
an affidavit as to his or her local political party affiliation, or if such
person does not belong to a local political party, then as to his or her state
or national political party affiliations. The President shall not appoint more
than four members of the same political party.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-4) (Ord. 85-139, passed 12-12-1985; Ord. 97-341, passed 9-15-
1997)
§ 33.044 OATH.
   (A)   Each member, before entering upon his or her duties, shall take and
subscribe to the customary oath of office.
   (B)   This oath, so subscribed shall be filed with the Village Clerk.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-5)
§ 33.045 BOND AND COMPENSATION.
   (A)   Bond.
      (1)   Each member, before entering upon his or her duties, shall execute
a bond to the village in the penal sum of $1,000 conditioned upon the faithful
performance of his or her duties.
      (2)   Said bond shall be for the term of office of said member and shall
be filed with the Village Clerk.
   (B)   Compensation. Each member shall serve without compensation.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-6)
§ 33.046 SECRETARY OF THE BOARD.
   The Board shall designate one of its own members to act as Secretary who
shall have the following duties:
   (A)   To keep the minutes of the Board’s proceeding;
   (B)   To be the custodian of all records pertaining to the business of the
Board;
   (C)   To keep a record of all examinations held; and
   (D)   To perform all other duties the Board shall prescribe.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-7)
§ 33.047 DUTIES.
   The Board of Fire and Police Commissioners shall have the following duties:
   (A)   To appoint all full-time members and officers of the regular Police
Department; except that, the Police Chief, the Assistant Police Chief, the
Chief of Police Clerk and all other exempt positions shall be appointed by the
Village President with the consent of the Board of Trustees. The Police Chief
shall appoint, with the advice and consent of the President of the Board of
Trustees, the Assistant Police Chief; and the Fire Chief shall appoint, with
the advice and consent of the President of the Board of Trustees, the Assistant
Fire Chief;
   (B)   To appoint all full-time members of the Fire Department; except that,
the Fire Chief and Deputy Fire Chief shall be appointed by the President with
the consent of the Trustees;
   (C)   (1)   To make and make changes in such rules as will carry out the
provisions of this subchapter and for procedures to be followed relative to
appointments or removals of members and officers from the Police Department or
Fire Department. Rules shall apply only to the following:
         (a)   Conduct of examinations for original appointments;
         (b)   Conduct of examinations for promotions; and
         (c)   Conduct of hearings on charges brought against a member of the
Police Department or Fire Department. No rules may be made relative to
governing the operation of the Fire Department or Police Department, such
authority being reserved to the Board of Trustees.
      (2)   All such rules and changes shall be printed immediately and be
available for distribution. Notice must be published in the local newspaper as
follows:
         (a)   Of the place where the rules may be obtained; and
         (b)   Of the date not less than ten days subsequent to the time of
publication when the rules or changes in the rules shall become effective.
      (3)   These rules shall be applicable only to full-time firefighter and
full-time police officers and not to any other personnel of any kind or
description.
   (D)   To submit to the President, annually, between May 1 and June 1, a
report of its activities and submit a copy of its rules or changes. The report
may make suggestions which the Board believes would result in greater
efficiency in the Fire Department or in the Police Department. The Board shall
also submit its budget request for the ensuing year in said report. The
President shall transmit the report to the Board of Trustees; and
   (E)   (1)   In addition to other disciplinary actions authorized by the
state, the Board of Fire and Police Commissioners are hereby authorized to
demote any officer one grade for cause shown, upon written charges, and after
an opportunity to be heard in his or her own defense. The Board of Fire and
Police Commissioners shall conduct a fair and impartial hearing of the charges,
to be commenced within 30 days of the filing thereof, and may be continued from
time to time. If the Board of Fire and Police Commissioners determine that the
charges are sustained, the officer shall be demoted to the next lower rank.
      (2)   In the conduct of this hearing, each member of the Board shall have
power to administer oaths and affirmations, and the Board shall have power to
secure by its subpoena both the attendance and testimony of witnesses and the
production of books and papers relevant to the hearing.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-8) (Ord. 85-113, passed 6-11-1985; Ord. 85-135, passed 10-15-
1985; Ord. 97-319, passed 4-15-1997)
§ 33.048 FACILITIES FOR MEETINGS.
   Suitable rooms for meetings and examinations shall be provided to the Board
by the Village Clerk.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-9)
§ 33.049 EXPENDITURES.
   Provision shall be made in the annual appropriation ordinance to provide
adequate funds for the duties and functions of the Board.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-10)
§ 33.050 ATTORNEY FOR THE BOARD.
   The Village Attorney shall be the legal representative of the Board.
(1988 Code, § 2-7-11)
§ 33.051 RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The rules and regulations of the Board of Fire and Police Commissioners are
hereby adopted by reference and incorporated herein as if set out in full.
(Ord. 12-572, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 33.052 ALTERNATE PROCEDURE FOR HIRING FULLY-QUALIFIED OFFICERS.
   (A)   For purposes of this section, QUALIFIED POLICE OFFICER shall mean an
individual possessing all certifications required by the state’s Department of
Law Enforcement and other applicable regulations in order to serve as a full-
or part-time police officer, and who is presently or who has previously been
employed as a full- or part-time police officer in a state unit of local
government.
   (B)   (1)   Whenever the Police Chief certifies in writing to the Mayor and
Board of Trustees and Village Manager that there is a present need to hire one
or more qualified police officers to fill a vacancy, the Village Mayor is
authorized to hire a fully qualified officer for such vacancy based on the
recommendation of the Chief.
      (2)   The Mayor shall advise the Board of Fire and Police Commissioners
when this process is invoked and shall keep the Commission apprised of
interviewing and hiring progress.
   (C)   The hiring established pursuant to this section shall take precedence
over any names appearing on an eligibility list developed by the Board of Fire
and Police Commissioners.
   (D)   In order to be eligible for hiring a qualified officer, an applicant
must meet all other eligibility criteria established by the Board of Fire and
Police Commissioners or this code for newly-hired employees.
   (E)   Nothing in this section authorizes the hiring of any employees over
and above the number of employees authorized and budgeted by the Mayor and
Board of Trustees from time to time.
   (F)   Police officers hired under this section shall be placed at entry
level on the salary scale pursuant to the applicable collective bargaining
agreement.
(Ord. 15-015, passed 5-4-2015; Ord. 15-049, passed 11-2-2015)
POLICE PENSION FUND BOARD OF TRUSTEES
§ 33.065 BOARD AND FUND ESTABLISHED.
   There is established a Police Pension Fund and a Board of Trustees thereof
in and for the village. The Board shall be known as the “Board of Trustees of
the Police Pension Fund of the Village of Dolton”.
(1988 Code, § 2-8-1)
§ 33.066 APPOINTED AND ELECTED MEMBERS; TERM OF OFFICE.
   (A)   The Board of Trustees of the Police Pension Fund shall consist of five
members: two shall be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of
the Board of Trustees; two shall be elected from the regular police force; and
one member shall be elected by and from the beneficiaries of the Pension Fund.
   (B)   (1)   The election shall be conducted by ballot at elections to be
held on the third Monday in April of the applicable years under the Australian
ballot system.
      (2)   The Board of the Police Pension Fund shall prescribe regulations
for the conduct of the election.
      (3)   Only the active police officers shall vote for the members chosen
from the active police officers and only the beneficiaries shall be entitled to
vote for the member from among the beneficiaries of the Fund.
   (C)   Each elected or appointed member shall hold his or her term for a
period of two years.
(1988 Code, § 2-8-2)
§ 33.067 ORGANIZATION.
   (A)   At the regular July meeting, the Board shall select from its members a
President, Vice- President, Secretary and Assistant Secretary to serve for one
year and until their successors are elected and qualified.
   (B)   The Village Treasurer shall be ex-officio Treasurer of the Board of
Trustees of the Police Pension Fund. The bond he or she executed as Village
Treasurer shall also be conditioned for the faithful performance of his or her
duty as Treasurer of the Police Officers’ Pension Fund. On the second Tuesday
in May, he or she shall make a sworn statement to the Board of Trustees of the
Police Pension Fund and to the Village President and Board of Trustees of all
moneys received and paid out on account of the Pension Fund during the
municipal year and of the amount of such funds then on hand and owing to the
Pension Fund.
(1988 Code, § 2-8-3)
§ 33.068 MEETINGS.
   The Board shall hold regular meetings on the second Tuesday of July,
October, January and April and shall hold such additional meetings as may be
called by the President of the Board of Trustees of the Police Pension Fund.
(1988 Code, § 2-8-4)
§ 33.069 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   It shall be the duty of the members of the Police Pension Board to
manage, invest and control the Police Pension Fund and all moneys pertaining
thereto in the manner provided by 40 ILCS 5/3-132 to 5/3-140 as now or
hereafter amended.
   (B)   Their powers and duties shall include:
      (1)   To exclusively control and manage the Pension Fund and all money
donated, paid or assessed for the relief or pensioning of disabled, super-
annuitied and retired members of the Police Department, their widows, minor
children and dependent parents. All such moneys shall be placed by the
Treasurer to the credit of the Fund, subject to the order of the Board;
      (2)   To order and direct the payment of pensions and other benefits
provided by statute and to issue certificates signed by its President and
Secretary to the persons entitled thereto of the amount ordered paid to such
persons from the Fund. The certificates shall state the purpose of the payment.
No order or resolution for the payment of money shall be valid unless approved
by a majority of the members of the Board, and any order for such payment shall
be signed by the President and Secretary of the Board;
      (3)   (a)   To submit to the Village President and Village Board of
Trustees each May a report setting forth:
            1.   A list of persons entitled to payments from the Fund stating
the amount and purpose of the payment; and
            2.   Items of income accrued to the Fund during the preceding
fiscal year.
         (b)   The report shall be under oath and signed by the President and
Secretary of the Board.
      (4)   To report to the Village President and Board of Trustees at least
annually, and its annual report shall be given in the month of May stating:
         (a)   The assets in its custody;
         (b)   The estimated receipts during the next succeeding calendar year
from deductions from the salaries of police officers and from all other
sources; and
         (c)   The estimated amount required during said calendar year to:
            1.   Pay all pensions and other obligations provided in the Police
Pension Fund Act of the Illinois Municipal Code; and
            2.   Maintain the reserve Fund provided in 40 ILCS 5/3-127 as now
or hereafter amended.
      (5)   To invest funds in the name of the Board of the Police Pension Fund
in interest bearing bonds or in tax anticipation warrants of the United States,
or of Illinois, or of any county, township or municipal corporation of
Illinois, and in insured shares of state-chartered building and loan
associations and insured shares of federal chartered saving and loan
associations. All securities shall be deposited with the Treasurer;
      (6)   To issue subpoenas for witnesses to attend and testify before it
and to have authority to administer oaths;
      (7)   To appoint a clerk and define the duties of said clerk. No person
drawing a police pension shall be employed as clerk by the Board, nor shall any
person related by blood or marriage to any pensioner or police officer be
employed as a clerk;
      (8)   To provide for the payment from the Fund of all necessary expenses,
including clerk hire, printing and witness fees;
      (9)   To keep a public record of all its proceedings; and
      (10)   To make rules and regulations concerning the Pension Fund which
shall be published by the Board and copies transmitted to all pensioners and
contributors.
(1988 Code, § 2-8-5)
§ 33.070 COMPENSATION.
   No member of the Board shall receive any compensation for services performed
as a member of the Board.
(1988 Code, § 2-8-6)
§ 33.071 FUNDING.
   (A)   There shall be deposited in the Pension Fund the sums required to
establish and maintain a reserve to ensure the payment of all obligations. The
reserve shall be not less than $10,000 for each police officer and each
beneficiary; provided that, the reserve to be accumulated shall not exceed the
estimated total actuarial requirements of the Fund.
   (B)   All children of a police officer shall be considered as a single
beneficiary for purposes of reserve requirements.
(1988 Code, § 2-8-7)
FIREFIGHTERS’ PENSION FUND BOARD OF TRUSTEES
§ 33.085 BOARD ESTABLISHED; MEMBERSHIP.
   (A)   (1)   There is established a Board of Trustees of the Firefighters’
Pension Fund. Beginning on the third Monday in April 2006, the Firefighters’
Pension Fund Board of Trustees shall consist of five members: two members of
the Board shall be elected from active participants; one member of the Board
shall be elected from retired members; and two members of the Board shall be
appointed by the Mayor. The members of the Board selected from the active and
retired firefighters shall be elected by ballot at an election to be held on
the third Monday in April of the applicable years under the Australian ballot
system.
      (2)   The Board of Trustees of the Firefighters’ Pension Fund shall
prescribe regulations for the conduct of the election. The membership shall
elect from its members a Board President and Secretary.
   (B)   (1)   Only the active participants of the Firefighters’ Pension Fund
shall vote for the members chosen from the active participants of the Pension
Fund and only the persons retired under the Firefighters’ Pension Fund Act
shall be entitled to choose the retired pension fund participant.
      (2)   For purposes of this section, a firefighter receiving a disability
pension shall be considered a retired firefighter.
      (3)   In the event that there are no retired firefighters under the Fund
or if none is willing to serve on the Board, then an additional active
firefighter shall be elected to the Board in lieu of the retired firefighter
that would otherwise be elected.
(1988 Code, § 2-9-1) (Ord. 06-338, passed 4-3-2006)
§ 33.086 TERMS AND VACANCIES OF ELECTED MEMBERS.
   Each elected member shall hold office for a term of three years and until
his or her successor has been duly elected and qualified. In the event of
failure, resignation or inability of any elected member to act, his or her
successor shall be elected at a special election called by the Board.
(1988 Code, § 2-9-2)
§ 33.087 TREASURER OF THE BOARD.
   The Village Treasurer shall be ex-officio treasurer of the Board of Trustees
of the Firefighters’ Pension Fund. The bond he or she executes as Village
Treasurer shall also be conditioned for the faithful performance of his or her
duty as Treasurer of the Firefighters’ Pension Fund.
(1988 Code, § 2-9-3)
§ 33.088 DUTIES.
   (A)   Control of Firefighters’ Pension Fund. The Board of Trustees of the
Firefighters’ Pension Fund shall have control of the management of all funds
belonging to or designated by law as part of the Firefighters’ Pension Fund and
of the administration of such funds, as provided by 40 ILCS 5/4-123 to 5/4-129
as now or hereafter amended.
   (B)   Reports. The Board shall report to the President and Board of Trustees
at least annually, and its annual report shall be given in the month of May
stating:
      (1)   The assets in its custody;
      (2)   The estimated receipts for the period of January 1 to December 31
from deductions from salaries or wages of firefighter and from all other
sources; and
      (3)   The estimated amount required for:
         (a)   Paying all pensions and other obligations provided for in the
Firefighters’ Pension Fund Act; and
         (b)   Maintaining the reserve provided for in 40 ILCS 5/4-120 as now
or hereafter amended.
(1988 Code, § 2-9-4)
§ 33.089 COMPENSATION.
   No member of the Board shall receive any compensation for service performed
as a member of the Board.
(1988 Code, § 2-9-5)
§ 33.090 FUNDS.
   There shall be deposited in the Firefighters’ Pension Fund the sum required
to establish and maintain a reserve to ensure the payment of all obligations.
The reserve shall be not less than $1,000 for each 1,000 inhabitants of the
village.
(1988 Code, § 2-9-6)
POLICE DEPARTMENT
§ 33.105 DEPARTMENT CREATED; MEMBERS.
   There is hereby created a Police Department, an executive department of the
village. The Police Department shall consist of the Chief of Police and such
other members as may be provided for from time to time by the President and
Board of Trustees. Neither the Chief of Police, nor any of the police officers
or other employees of the Police Department, shall be considered as officers of
the village, but they shall all be considered employees of the village.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-1)
§ 33.106 CHIEF OF POLICE.
   (A)   Office created. There is hereby created the office of Police Chief.
   (B)   Appointment. The Police Chief shall be appointed by the Village
President by and with the consent and advice of the Board of Trustees.
   (C)   Duties.
      (1)   Generally. He or she shall be responsible for the performance by
the Police Department of all its functions, and all persons who are members of
the Department shall serve subject to the orders of Chief of Police.
      (2)   Keeping Village Jail. The Chief of Police shall be the keeper of
the jail and shall have custody over all persons confined therein and of all
property pertaining thereto.
      (3)   Arrest records. It shall be the duty of the Chief of Police to keep
a record of the names of all persons arrested or committed to the Village Jail
or County Jail in a book to be provided for such purpose. Such record shall
show the date of arrest or committal, the number of days imprisoned, the amount
of the fine, when and to whom paid, and the date of discharge or other
disposition of such persons.
      (4)   Post notice of rights. The Chief of Police shall post in every
room, other than cells, of the building where persons are held under arrest or
are held in custody, in conspicuous places where it may be seen and read by
persons in custody and others, a poster printed in large type containing a
verbatim copy in the English language of the provisions of Ill. Rev. Stat. Ch.
38, para. 103-2, 103-3, 103-4, 109-1, 110-2, 110-4 and subp. (a) and (b) of
para. 110-7 and 113-3.
      (5)   Custodian of abandoned, stolen property. The Chief of Police shall
be custodian of all lost, abandoned or stolen property in the village and shall
make disposition of same in accordance with state statute.
      (6)   Execute orders of Health Inspector. The Chief of Police shall
execute or cause to be executed all orders directed to him or her by the Health
Inspector, so far as they relate to the preservation of the health of the
village.
      (7)   Reports required. The Chief of Police shall, prior to the first
meeting of the Village Board in June of each year, make an annual report in
writing to the Village Board of the state of the Police Department with a
detailed report of the transactions of the Department for the preceding year,
with such statistics and suggestions in regard to the requirements of the
Department as he or she may deem advisable; and shall also make reports of any
matter or thing concerning such Department, whenever requested by the President
or Village Board.
      (8)   Rules and regulations. The Chief of Police may make or prescribe
such rules and regulations for the guidance of the members of the Department as
he or she shall see fit; and such rules, when approved by the President and
Board of Trustees, shall be binding on such members.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-2) (Ord. passed 6-13-1978)
§ 33.107 ORGANIZATION AND OPERATION OF DEPARTMENT.
   The Police Department shall be organized and the police officers and
employees thereof shall be appointed and shall function as provided by
ordinance and the rules and regulations applicable to the Police Department.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-3)
§ 33.108 SERGEANT.
   (A)   An additional sergeant position in the village’s Police Department is
hereby created.
   (B)   The position created in division (A) above shall be subject to the
rules and regulations of the Board of Fire and Police Commissioners and the
1997-2000 Collective Bargaining Agreement between the village and the Police
Officers’ Benevolent Protective Association Labor Committee, Inc.
   (C)   The additional sergeant position in the village’s Police Department
shall be at the annual salary and shall include the duties and responsibilities
as provided for in the 1997-2000 Collective Bargaining Agreement between the
village and the Police Officers’ Benevolent Protective Association Labor
Committee, Inc.
(Ord. 99-121, passed 9-7-1999)
§ 33.109 POLICE CAPTAIN.
   (A)   (1)   The following position is hereby established, at the salary
provided by the village: Police Captain.
      (2)   The duties of the Police Captain shall be the same duties
prescribed in the village’s job description for Police Captain attached hereto
and made a part hereof. The position of Captain shall include the benefits as
set by the village.
   (B)   The Police Captain(s) shall be entitled to the following specified
employee benefits as are set forth in the Police Officers’ Benevolent and
Protective Association Labor Committee, Inc. Collective Bargaining Agreement
for Police Sergeants and Lieutenants, and amended from time to time,
retroactive to the effective date of said collective bargaining agreement:
holidays, vacations, sick leave, personal leave days, and longevity pay. No
other provisions of the BPBA Police Sergeants and Lieutenants collective
bargaining agreement, as amended, shall be applicable to the position of Police
Captain(s).
(Ord. 05-288, passed 5-16-2005; Ord. 09-492, passed 1-4-2010)
§ 33.110 APPOINTMENTS, PROMOTIONS AND DISCHARGES OF MEMBERS.
   Appointments to and promotions within the Police Department shall be made by
the Board of Fire and Police Commissioners in the manner provided by law. No
police officer shall be discharged from the Department, except after a hearing
on charges before the Board of Fire and Police Commissioners as provided by
law.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-4)
§ 33.111 OATH.
   (A)   The Chief of Police and all regular police officers shall, before
entering upon their duties, take and subscribe an oath to faithfully and
impartially discharge the duties of their position as fixed by ordinance. The
oath shall be as follows:
“I,                                               , do solemnly swear (or
affirm) that I will support the Constitution of the United States, the
Constitution of the State of Illinois, and the ordinances of the Village of
Dolton, and that I will faithfully discharge the duties of
                                         to the best of my ability”.
   (B)   This oath or affirmation, so subscribed, shall be filed in the office
of the Village Clerk.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-5)
§ 33.112 POWERS AND DUTIES OF DEPARTMENT.
   (A)   Generally. The Chief of Police and all members of the police force of
the village, when on duty, shall devote their time and attention to the
municipal affairs of the village, to preserve the peace, order, safety and
cleanliness thereof; and, to this end, they shall execute and enforce all
ordinances and police regulations and orders of the President and Village
Board. They shall take notice of all nuisances and at all times render all
necessary assistance to all village departments in the abatement thereof. They
shall take notice also, of the impediments, obstructions and defects in the
walks, streets, avenues, alleys and public places of the village and shall
remove the same or cause immediate notice to be given the proper person, whose
duty it may be to attend to the same according to the ordinances of the
village.
   (B)   Issue warrants and processes. The members of the police force of the
village shall have power and authority, and it shall be their duty, in the
village and outside of the same, when necessary and lawful, to serve and
execute warrants and other process for the apprehension and commitment of
persons charged with a violation of any of the village ordinances or any crime
or misdemeanor or violation of any law or ordinance of the village; and they
shall have the power and authority, and it shall be their duty, to serve and
execute any civil process issued on behalf of the village by any court of
proper jurisdiction; and while serving or executing or assisting in the service
or execution of any such warrant or process, they shall be vested with and have
all the powers and authority conferred on constables at common law and by the
laws of the state.
   (C)   Arrests. The members of the village police force shall have the power,
and it shall be their duty, to arrest on view, all persons in the village found
in the act of violating any law or ordinance or aiding or abetting in such
violations and to bring such persons so arrested before the court of proper
jurisdiction to be dealt with according to law.
   (D)   Appear as witness. All police officers making arrests shall attend as
witnesses before the court where the trial may be had, and shall procure all
necessary evidence in their power, and furnish a list of witnesses to the court
and the village’s Prosecuting Attorney, and no village police officers shall be
entitled to any witness fees to be taxed against the village in any action for
the violation of an ordinance where the village is plaintiff.
   (E)   Aid Fire Department. It shall be the duty of the Police Department to
aid the Fire Department by giving alarms in case of fire and clearing the
streets or grounds in the immediate vicinity of the fire so that the members of
the Fire Department shall not be hindered or obstructed in the performance of
their duties.
   (F)   Regulate traffic. The members of the police force of the village shall
regulate and direct, when necessary, the travel and movement of all persons and
vehicles traveling or going in the public streets or other thoroughfares within
the village, for the purpose of preventing injuries to persons or property and
of preserving peace and public order. All persons so traveling or going, or
having charge of such vehicles, are required to obey the orders and directions
of members of the police force of the village for the aforesaid purpose.
   (G)   Remove abandoned vehicles. The members of the police force shall
remove any abandoned or unattended vehicle standing on the main traveled part
of a street or highway in the village. They shall provide for the removal of
such vehicle to the nearest garage or other place of safety.
   (H)   Report of property seized or found. It shall be the duty of police
officers to report and deliver to the Chief of Police all property seized or
found by them immediately after the same shall have come into their possession,
which property, with the date of delivery and description of the same and the
name of the police officers depositing the same, shall be entered in a book
kept for that purpose by the Chief of Police who shall be responsible for the
same.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-6)
§ 33.113 ACCIDENT REPORTS.
   (A)   It shall be the duty of each and every police officer of the village,
whenever any accident shall occur within the municipal limits of which he or
she has notice or knowledge, to report forthwith in writing to the Chief of
Police, the place, day and nature of the accident; the hour of the day or night
when it occurred; the condition of the weather; if at night, whether cloudy,
clear or moonlight and whether the street lights were or were not lighted; the
name of each person injured and the extent and nature of the injury suffered;
the names and residences of the principal witnesses and the name and residence
of the examining physician, if any, which shall be entered in full upon a
record to be kept for the purpose in the office of the Chief of Police.
   (B)   The Chief of Police shall make a report to the state’s Department of
Public Works and Buildings for each motor vehicle accident occurring within the
village within ten days after investigation of such accident.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-7)
§ 33.114 BADGE OF POLICE OFFICERS.
   (A)   Every member of the Police Department shall wear a suitable badge to
be furnished by the village, and any member who shall lose or destroy the same
shall be required to pay the cost of replacing it.
   (B)   Whenever any member shall leave the Department, he or she shall
immediately deliver to the Chief of Police his or her badge and all other
articles in his or her possession belonging to the village.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-8)
§ 33.115 DUTY TO AID POLICE.
   (A)   It shall be the duty of any person in the village, when called upon by
any member of the Police Department, to promptly aid and assist him or her in
the execution of his or her duties.
   (B)   No person shall neglect or refuse to give such aid and assistance.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-9) Penalty, see §
33.999
§ 33.116 PROHIBITED ACTS AND CONDITIONS.
   (A)   Interference with police. Any person who, in the village, shall resist
any member of the Police Department or any other person duly authorized to
perform police duty in the discharge of his or her duties, or shall in any way
interfere with, prevent or hinder him or her in the discharge of his or her
duty as such member, or shall offer or endeavor to do so, and any person who
shall in any manner assist any person in the custody of any member of the
Police Department to escape or attempt to escape from such custody, or attempt
to rescue any person from custody, shall be punished as provided herein.
   (B)   Impersonating or imitating a police officer.
      (1)   No person, other than a member of the Police Department or duly
authorized auxiliary police officer, shall assume to act as a police officer in
any capacity within the village.
      (2)   No person shall impersonate any of the members of the Police
Department, or shall maliciously or with intent to deceive, use or imitate any
of the signs, signals or devices adopted and used by the Police Department, or
shall wear in public the uniform adopted as the police uniform, after having
been removed or suspended.
   (C)   Police officers furnishing bail. No member of the police force shall
become or furnish bail for any person arrested for violation of any ordinances
of the village or for the criminal laws of the state.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-10) Penalty, see §
33.999
§ 33.117 PRESS CARDS.
   (A)   (1)   The Chief of Police has power to issue press cards entitling the
holder thereof to pass police and fire lines for the purpose of gathering and
editing spot news or photographing news events in the village.
      (2)   Such press cards shall be issued only to those engaged in
gathering, reporting, editing or photographing current news events for
newspapers, press associations, newsreels, radio and television stations. The
application for such press cards shall be made in writing by the employer on
behalf of the employee qualified to hold press cards.
      (3)   The employer shall represent that the employee on whose behalf an
application for a press card is made is a full-time reporter, editor, writer,
photographer or broadcaster of spot news, is of good moral character and is a
citizen of the United States.
   (B)   No such card shall be issued unless the applicant meets these
requirements and unless and until the fingerprints of the prospective holder
are filed in the office of the Chief of Police.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-11)

                          Fee
Accident/incident reports $15

(Ord. 09-466, passed 3-2-2009; Ord. 15-020, passed 6-1-2015)
PART-TIME POLICE
§ 33.130 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   BOARD. The Illinois Law Enforcement Training Standards Board.
   PART-TIME POLICE OFFICER. A law enforcement officer who has completed his or
her 18- month probationary period and is employed on a part-time basis as a law
enforcement officer by a participating unit of local government.
   POLICE TRAINING SCHOOL. Any school located within the state whether
privately or publicly owned which offers a course in police training and has
been approved by the Board under this code of ordinances and the state’s Police
Training Act (50 ILCS 705/1 et seq.) and the rules and requirements of the
ILETSB.
   PROBATIONARY PART-TIME POLICE OFFICER. A recruit part-time law enforcement
officer required to successfully complete initial minimum part-time training
requirements within 18 months to be eligible for employment on a part-time
basis as a local law enforcement officer.
   RECRUIT. Any part-time law enforcement officer who is enrolled in an
approved training course.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.131 QUALIFICATIONS.
   (A)   A part-time police officer shall:
      (1)   Be a member of the regular Police Department, except for pension
purposes;
      (2)   Not be assigned under any circumstances to supervise or direct
full-time police officers of the village’s Police Department; and
      (3)   Shall not be used as permanent replacements for permanent full-time
police officers (65 ILCS 5/3.1-30-21).
   (B)   A person hired to serve as a part-time police officer must obtain,
from the Board, a certificate:
      (1)   Attesting to his or her successful completion of the ILETSB part-
time police training course;
      (2)   Attesting to his or her satisfactory completion of a training
program of similar content and number of hours that has been found acceptable
by the ILETSB under the provisions of the state’s Police Training Act; and
      (3)   Attesting to the Board’s ILETSB’s determination that the part-time
police training course is unnecessary because of the person’s extensive prior
law enforcement experience.
   (C)   Qualification dates:
      (1)   A person hired on or after 1-1-1996 must obtain the Board
certificate within 18 months after the date of hire; and
      (2)   A person hired before 1-1-1996 must obtain the Board certificate
within 24 months after the effective date of the amendatory Act of 1995.
   (D)   (1)   The village may seek a waiver from the Board extending the
period for compliance as allowed by ILETSB.
      (2)   A waiver shall be issued only for good and justifiable reasons and
may not extend the initial period by more than 90 days as allowed by ILETSB.
      (3)   If training is required and not completed within the applicable
time period, as extended by any waiver that may be granted, then the officer
must forfeit his or her position.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.132 HIRING STANDARDS.
   Any person employed as a part-time police officer must meet the following
standards:
   (A)   Be of good moral character, of temperate habits, of sound health and
physically and mentally able to perform assigned duties;
   (B)   Be at least 21 years of age;
   (C)   Pass a medical examination;
   (D)   Possess a high school diploma or GED certificate;
   (E)   Possess a valid state driver’s license;
   (F)   Possess no prior felony convictions; and
   (G)   Any individual who served in the U.S. military must have been
honorably discharged.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.133 APPOINTMENT.
   The Village President, subject to the advice and consent of the Board of
Trustees of the village, is authorized to appoint, discipline or terminate
part-time police officers as employees of the village’s Police Department.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.134 RESIDENCY REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   All part-time police officers shall reside within 22 miles of the
nearest corporate limit of the village within one year from the date of the
original employment. Any village employee who shall fail to comply with the
provisions of this section shall be discharged from the employment of the
village in the manner provided by law.
   (B)   All part-time police officers who now reside more than 22 miles from
the nearest corporate limit of the village must become residents within the 22-
mile radius within 12 months after the effective date hereof.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.135 CRIMINAL RECORD.
   (A)   Prior to appointment, all proposed part-time police officers shall be
fingerprinted and their fingerprints shall be checked with the Federal Bureau
of Investigation, Washington, D.C., for any possible criminal record.
   (B)   No person shall be appointed as a part-time police officer if he or
she has been convicted of a felony or other crime involving moral turpitude.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.136 PART-TIME POLICE TRAINING COURSE.
   For purposes of this subchapter, the part-time police training course
referred to shall be of similar content and the same number of hours for full-
time officers and shall be provided by Mobile Team In-Service Training Units
under the Intergovernmental Law Enforcement Officer’s In-Service Training Act,
being 50 ILCS 720/1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended, in a manner prescribed
by the Board.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.137 HOURS WORKED.
   A part-time police officer, who is a member of the village’s Police
Department, shall be employed for 1,560 hours or less per 12-month period
beginning on January 1 of any calendar year.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.138 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   Part-time police officers shall have the following powers and duties,
when properly assigned and on duty:
      (1)   To aid or direct traffic in the municipality;
      (2)   To aid in control of natural or human-made disasters;
      (3)   To aid in case of civil disorder;
      (4)   To perform normal and regular police duties when assigned by the
Chief of Police on occasions when it is impracticable for members of the
regular Police Department to perform normal and regular police duties;
      (5)   To arrest or cause to be arrested, with or without process, all
persons who break the peace or are found violating any municipal ordinance or
any criminal law of the state;
      (6)   To commit arrested persons for examination;
      (7)   If necessary, to detain arrested persons in custody overnight or
Sunday in any safe place, or until they can be brought before the proper
magistrate;
      (8)   To serve and execute all warrants for the violation of municipal
ordinances or the state criminal law within the limits of the village, and for
this purpose, to have all the common law and statutory power of sheriffs; and
      (9)   To exercise all other powers as conservators of the peace that the
corporate authorities may prescribe.
   (B)   Part-time police officers shall, at all times during the performance
of their duties, be subject to the direction and control of the Chief of Police
of the village.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.139 IDENTIFICATION.
   Identification symbols worn by part-time police officers shall be different
and distinct from those used by the regular Police Department and shall be
selected and chosen by the Chief of Police of the village.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.140 FIREARMS.
   Part-time police officers shall carry firearms with the permission of the
village’s Chief of Police and then only when in uniform and in the performance
of their duties.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.141 COMPENSATION.
   Part-time police officers shall be paid such sum as the corporate authorizes
shall from time to time determine in the annual Appropriations (Budget)
Ordinance and Resolution Setting Salaries. Compensation, Expense Accounts and
other Remuneration for Employees of the Village of Dolton.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
§ 33.142 DISCIPLINE.
   Part-time officers shall be under the disciplinary jurisdiction of the Chief
of Police. Part-time police officers serve at the discretion of the village
authorities, shall not have any property rights in said employment, and may be
removed by the village authorities at any time. Part-time police officers shall
comply with all applicable rules and general orders issued by the village’s
Police Department.
(Ord. 12-782, passed 11-19-2012)
FIRE DEPARTMENT
§ 33.155 DEPARTMENT ESTABLISHED.
   (A)   There is hereby created and established a Fire Department consisting
of a Chief of the Fire Department and such other officers and firefighter as
may hereafter be necessary to operate said Department and as may be provided
for in the annual appropriation ordinance.
   (B)   Said Department shall work in conjunction with the village’s Volunteer
Fire Department; however, the members of the village’s Volunteer Fire
Department as such, shall not be entitled to any benefits of this code relating
to pensions and tenure.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-1)
§ 33.156 APPOINTMENT OF CERTAIN OFFICERS.
   (A)   (1)   The Fire Chief, Assistant Chiefs, Deputy Chief and such other
volunteer officers as may be deemed necessary and in the vest interest of the
village’s Fire Department shall be appointed by the President by and with the
consent and advice of the Board of Trustees.
      (2)   Their appointment shall be from May 1 to April 30 of the next
succeeding year, or until their respective successors are duly appointed and
qualified.
   (B)   The Fire Chief shall be a full time salaried employee of the village.
The Assistant Fire Chiefs shall be two in number and shall be full time
salaried employees of the village. The Deputy Chief shall be chosen from the
ranks of the village’s Volunteer Firefighters and shall be compensated by
stipend as such volunteer.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-2-1) (Ord. 88-151, passed 10-11-1988; Ord. 92-179, passed 4-
28-1992)
§ 33.157 FIRE CHIEF; POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   Generally. The Chief of the Fire Department shall have sole and
absolute control and command over all persons connected with the village’s Fire
Department and he or she shall possess full power and authority over its
organization, government and discipline. He or she shall be subject to the
authority of the Village President.
   (B)   Entry powers; stop work order. The Chief of the Fire Department shall
have power to enter upon the premises wherein any fire has occurred, if
necessary, in order to investigate the origin of the fire; and he or she shall
have power to stop the construction of any building when the same is being done
in violation of any provision of the Fire Code of the village.
   (C)   Examine dangerous buildings and those to be altered; report required.
The Chief of the Fire Department shall examine all buildings and walls reported
dangerous or damaged by fire or accident, and shall, when requested by the
Village President, also examine all buildings under application for permit to
raze, enlarge, alter or rebuild, and he or she shall make a report of the
condition thereof to the President.
   (D)   Custody of Department property and equipment, examinations and
reports.
      (1)   The Fire Chief shall have the custody, subject to the direction of
the Village President, and be accountable and responsible for all property and
equipment belonging to the Fire Department.
      (2)   He or she shall, at least four times in every year, examine into
the condition of the apparatus and hoses and report the same to the President
and Board of Trustees at the next subsequent meeting, together with such
recommendations as he or she may deem advisable in the premises.
   (E)   Annual report. The Chief of the Fire Department shall, in January of
each year, make a full and complete report of all transactions of the Fire
Department for the preceding year. Such report shall also show, as nearly as
can be ascertained, the number of fires, causes thereof, of accidents by fire
and the number of and a brief description of the buildings destroyed or
injured, together with the names of the owners and occupants, the amount of
property destroyed by fire and insurance thereon, and shall include such other
statistics and suggestions as he may deem advisable.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-2-2)
§ 33.158 DEPUTY FIRE CHIEF.
   (A)   Qualifications. No person shall serve as Deputy Fire Chief unless such
person is a member in good standing of the village’s Volunteer Firefighter
Association and shall possess a state certification as a Firefighter II by the
Personnel Standards and Education Division of the Office of the State Fire
Marshal or its successor.
   (B)   Responsibilities. The Deputy Fire Chief shall be a volunteer
firefighter of the Village Fire Department, shall perform those administrative
duties assigned by the Fire Chief and shall assume all powers, duties and
responsibilities of the Chief of the Fire Department in the absence of said
Chief.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-2-3) (Ord. 92-179, passed 4-28-1992; Ord. 92-180, passed 5-
12-1992)
§ 33.159 ASSISTANT FIRE CHIEF.
   (A)   Qualifications. No person shall serve as Assistant Fire Chief unless
such person shall possess a state certification as a Firefighter III by the
Personnel Standards and Education Division of the Office of the State Fire
Marshal, or its successor, and a valid certification by the state’s Department
of Public Health or its successor, as an emergency medical technician;
provided, however, that, the Assistant Fire Chief chosen from the village’s
volunteer firefighters shall not be required to possess the certification by
the state’s Department of Public Health or its successor, as an emergency
medical technician. No person shall serve as the Assistant Fire Chief chosen
from the village’s volunteer firefighters unless such person is a member in
good standing of the village’s Volunteer Firefighter Association.
   (B)   Responsibilities. The Assistant Fire Chief, on duty, shall assume all
powers, duties and responsibilities of the Fire Chief in the absence of said
Chief, and the Deputy Fire Chief, in the absence of said Deputy Chief.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-2-4) (Ord. 92-179, passed 4-28-1992; Ord. 92-180, passed 5-
12-1992)
§ 33.160 APPOINTMENTS, PROMOTIONS, REMOVALS AND SUSPENSIONS.
   (A)   Except for the Fire Chief and Deputy Fire Chief, Assistant Fire Chiefs
and the Deputy Fire Chief, all appointments and promotions within the regularly
paid Department shall be made by the Board of Fire and Police Commissioners. No
member, except the Chief, shall be dismissed until after a hearing by the Board
of Fire and Police Commissioners.
   (B)   The Fire Chief shall have power to suspend any regular firefighter
from duty, but he or she shall report such suspension to the Board of Fire and
Police Commissioners within 24 hours and the reasons for his or her action. On
such report being made, the Board shall take such action thereon as shall seem
to it just and right in the premises. Any regular firefighter so suspended
shall not be entitled to pay while so suspended, nor until he or she shall be
returned to duty by the proper authority.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-3) (Ord. 85-136, 10-15-85; Ord. 92-179, passed 4-28-1992)
§ 33.161 DEPARTMENT DUTIES.
   It shall be the function and duty of the Fire Department and every member
thereof to extinguish accidental or destructive fires and to prevent the
occurrence or spread of such fire. It shall be the duty of the Chief, if within
his or her power, or the Deputy Chief to attend all fires occurring in the
village, and in case of absence from any fire, it shall be the duty of the
officer in command of the fire company first on the ground at such fire to take
charge of the Department, and during the absence of the Chief, Deputy Fire
Chief or Assistant Fire Chief, he or she shall have and exercise all the powers
of the Chief of the Fire Department.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-4) (Ord. 85-136, passed 10-15-1985)
§ 33.162 BUREAU OF FIRE PREVENTION.
   The Fire Department shall have a Bureau of Fire Prevention, which shall be
operated under the supervision of the Chief of the Fire Department. The Chief
may designate any member of the Department an inspector of the Fire Prevention
Bureau and may prescribe and establish from time to time such rules and such
regulations as he or she may deem advisable, subject to the approval of the
Village President.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-5)
§ 33.163 ARSON INVESTIGATORS.
   (A)   Position established. There is hereby established the position of
arson investigator in the village’s Fire Department, which position is not a
rank, but is an assignment of duty and is exempt under the rules and
regulations of the Fire and Police Commission of the village.
   (B)   Appointment; qualifications. The arson investigator shall be appointed
by the Village Fire Chief and shall be a sworn employee of the village’s Fire
Department. He or she shall be enrolled in any school which is required of
village police officers and shall successfully complete same. In the event that
the school is not successfully completed, then the person shall no longer be an
arson investigator.
   (C)   Powers and duties.
      (1)   The arson investigator appointed herein shall have the authority to
investigate the causes and origins of all fires in the village and shall have
the authority and power to arrest any person, in accordance with the laws of
the state, suspected of involvement in an arson.
      (2)   The primary duties of the arson investigator shall be to
investigate possible arsons occurring in the village and to which said
investigator shall be assigned to investigate by his or her supervisors. He or
she shall also follow through on all legal process in the arson cases under the
supervision of the commander of the Investigation Division of the village’s
Police Department.
   (D)   Determination and command of arson investigation. The command
personnel from the Fire Department and/or the Police Department on the scene of
a fire or explosion will make the determination to notify the arson
investigator(s) who will then be notified and will respond to the scene if not
already present. Immediately upon notification by command personnel to begin an
investigation of a fire or explosion, the arson investigator shall come under
the direct supervision of the commander of the Investigation Division of the
village’s Police Department. Said commander will be responsible to the Chief of
Police and will keep the Fire Chief informed as to the progress of the
investigation.
   (E)   Rules and regulations. The sworn employees of the village’s Fire
Department who are assigned as arson investigators shall be subject to the
rules and regulations of the village’s Fire Department and while on duty and
actively investigating a possible arson, will be subject to the rules and
regulations of the village’s Police Department.
   (F)   Registration required; issuance of identification. The village shall
register arson investigators in accordance with the laws of the state and in
the same manner as is required for police officers. Arson investigators shall
be issued identification by the village identifying him or her as an arson
investigator and giving the arson investigator a peace officer status as
provided in Ill. Rev. Stat. Ch. 127-1/2, para. 501.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-6) (Ord. passed 4-3-1985)
§ 33.164 RESCUE SQUAD.
   (A)   Rescue squad established. Since the Fire Department has been
instituted to promote fire prevention, fire inspection and fire suppression for
all property in the Fire District and for the protection and health of the
people within the village, there shall be established under the jurisdiction of
the village’s Fire Chief, emergency rescue and first aid service in the
following situations: heart attack; suffocation; drowning; automobile accident;
and any other incident within the village where emergency first aid treatment
is needed. This emergency rescue and first aid service shall be known as the
rescue squad service and shall be a part of the village’s Fire Department. All
members of the squad shall be under the supervision of the Chief of the Fire
Department or, in his or her absence, under the supervision of the senior
officer at the scene of the incident.
   (B)   Rules and regulations. The corporate authorities of the village may
make such rules and regulations for the operation of the rescue squad as they
may deem feasible from time to time or may approve, by resolution, such rules
and regulations submitted to them by the Chief of the Fire Department
henceforth.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-7)
§ 33.165 INVESTIGATION OF FIRES.
   It shall be the duty of the Chief of the village’s Fire Department to
investigate the cause, origin and circumstances of every fire occurring within
the village, by which property has been destroyed or damaged, and especially to
make investigation as to whether such fire was the result of carelessness or
design, or cause such investigation to be made by the Bureau of Fire
Prevention. Such investigation shall be begun immediately after the occurrence
of such fire. If the fire is of suspicious origin, the Chief shall be
immediately notified of the fact. He or she shall take charge of the physical
evidence, shall notify the proper authorities designated by law to pursue the
investigation of such matters and shall further cooperate with the authorities
in the collection of evidence and in the prosecution of the case. He or she
shall forthwith notify the Department of Public Safety and within one week of
the occurrence of such fire, furnish to the Department of Public Safety a
written statement of all facts relating to the cause or origin of the fire and
such other information as may be called for by the blanks provided by said
Department. He or she shall also cooperate with and assist the Department of
Public Safety in any investigation the Department of Public Safety shall deem
expedient or necessary to make.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-8)
§ 33.166 DUTIES OF BYSTANDERS.
   (A)   Obedience to Fire Department officials. Every person who shall be
present at a fire shall be subject and obedient to the orders of the Chief of
the Fire Department and other officers of the Fire Department in extinguishing
a fire and in the removal and protection of property, and in case any person
shall refuse to obey such orders, he or she shall be fined according to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Aid to Fire Department. It shall be lawful for the Chief of the Fire
Department or officers in command of any fire company to require the aid of any
driver of any licensed, motor-driven vehicle, or any citizen, inhabitant or
bystander, in drawing or conveying any engine or fire apparatus to any fire,
and in working and using the same while at a fire, and on the refusal or
neglect of any person to comply with such requisition, the offender shall for
such refusal, be fined according to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-9)
§ 33.167 DESTRUCTION OF BUILDINGS TO CHECK FIRES.
   The Chief of the Fire Department or, in his or her absence, the officer in
command, or in case of the absence of such officers at any fire, the President
or any two members of the village’s Board of Trustees, may direct the members
of the Fire Department to cut down and remove any building, structure or fence
for the purpose of checking the progress of any fire; and the Chief of the Fire
Department or other officer in command shall have the power to blow up, or
cause to be blown up, with powder or otherwise, any building or structure
during the progress of a fire for the purpose of extinguishing or checking the
same.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-10)
§ 33.168 RESTRICTED AND PROHIBITED ACTS.
   (A)   Entering fire houses. It is declared unlawful for any person or
persons to enter the Fire Department house or any place where the equipment and
apparatus of the Fire Department is stored at any time, except on business
pertaining to the Fire Department or other village business.
   (B)   Unlawful use of fire key. Should any person have in his or her
possession or make or cause to be made any key of any engine house or fire
alarm telegraph box, or use or cause to be used any such key without the
consent of the proper authority, every such person shall be subject to a fine
as set forth in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (C)   Tampering with signal box. No persons, except those connected with the
management of the same, shall open any signal box unless it be to communicate
an alarm of fire; or break, cut, deface, damage or in any manner meddle or
interfere with any signal box or fire alarm or telegraph wires under a penalty
as set forth in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (D)   Obstructing fire hydrant. No person shall in any manner obstruct the
use of any fire hydrant or have or place any material or vehicle in front
thereof or within 15 feet from either side thereof under a penalty of $25 for
each offense; and any and all material or vehicles found as an obstruction as
aforesaid may be forthwith removed by any member of the Fire Department and at
risk, cost and expense of the owner or claimant.
   (E)   False fire alarms. Whoever, without reasonable cause, by outcry or
otherwise, makes or circulates, or causes to be made or circulated, any false
alarm of fire shall be fined in accordance with §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-11) Penalty, see §
33.999
§ 33.169 BUILDING INSPECTIONS.
   It shall be the duty of the Chief of the Fire Department to make or cause to
be made the inspections provided by Ch. 151 of this code of ordinances, and for
that purpose, the Chief or any officer or member of the Department is hereby
empowered and authorized at any and all reasonable times to enter upon and into
any of the aforesaid buildings and premises.
(1988 Code, § 4-1-12)
