FOREIGN FIRE INSURANCE BOARD
§ 33.185 CREATION.
   There is hereby created a four-member Foreign Fire Insurance Board for the
village comprised of officers elected as set forth below, whose purpose is to
establish rules and regulations with respect to the management of money to be
received by the village as foreign fire insurance tax receipts as provided for
by 65 ILCS 5/11-10-2, as amended.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.186 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   BOARD. The Foreign Fire Insurance Board.
   DEPARTMENT. Village of Dolton Fire Department.
   FUND. Foreign Fire Insurance Tax Fund.
   MEMBERS OF THE DEPARTMENT. Any sworn personnel currently employed full-time
in the village’s Department in the positions of firefighter, engineer, shift
lieutenant, civilian inspector of the Bureau of Fire Prevention and
Inspections, Chief or Assistant Chief.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.187 TAX IMPOSED.
   All corporations, companies and associations, not incorporated under the
laws of this state and which are engaged in the village in effecting fire
insurance, shall pay to the village annually, at the time of filing the reports
hereinafter mentioned, as a tax, a sum equal to 2% of the gross receipts for
premiums received by said corporations, companies or associations or their
agency or agents respectively, for business effected or transacted for fire
insurance within the village, for the year ending July 1 preceding such report.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.188 ANNUAL REPORT OF PREMIUMS.
   (A)   Every person acting as agent or otherwise for or on behalf of any
corporation, company or association taxed under this subchapter, shall on or
before July 15 of each year, file with the Village Treasurer a full report
verified by his or her oath, of all the premiums which during the year ending
on July 1 preceding such report shall have been received by him or her, or any
other person for him or her, in behalf of any such corporation, company or
association, and shall fully and specifically set out in the report the amounts
received as premiums for fire insurance.
   (B)   Provided, however, that, in cases where a firm acts as agent or
otherwise, the said verified report may be made by one member on behalf of the
firm.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.189 UNLAWFUL TO TRANSACT BUSINESS IF REPORT NOT FILED AND TAX NOT PAID.
   (A)   If the report required by this subchapter, is not filed on or before
the day herein designated for that purpose, or if the amount of the tax shall
remain unpaid after such date, as hereinbefore provided, it shall be unlawful
for any such corporation, company or association to transact any business of
fire insurance in the village until the requirements of this subchapter have
been fully complied with.
   (B)   This section shall not relieve any such corporation, company or
association from the payment of any risk that may be taken in violation
thereof.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004) Penalty, see §
33.999
§ 33.190 PENALTY FOR FAILURE TO FILE REPORT AND PAY TAX.
   If any corporation, company or association subject to tax under this
subchapter fails to file the report herein required by the required day, or if
the amount shall remain unpaid after July 15 of any year, every such
corporation, company or association shall forfeit and pay to the village the
maximum fine set forth in accordance with the general penalty, as found in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances, for each and every offense, and in addition
to such penalty, the village shall recover in an action in its name, and for
its use, against such corporation, company or association so failing to make
such report or pay such rates, the full amount of the fees which may be due
under the provisions hereof.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.191 FOREIGN FIRE INSURANCE FUND.
   (A)   General. There is hereby established a Foreign Fire Insurance Fund to
be managed and administered by the Foreign Fire Insurance Board in accordance
with this section and operating on a fiscal year beginning on May 1 and ending
April 30.
   (B)   Transfers to Foreign Fire Insurance Fund. Each year, the Village
Treasurer shall collect foreign fire insurance taxes in the amount prescribed
in §
33.187 of this chapter and shall forward all moneys to the Foreign Fire
Insurance Fund Board within 15 business days of receipt. Such taxes shall be
appropriated for transfer to the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund in the manner
provided by law.
   (C)   Management and administration of the Fund. The Foreign Fire Insurance
Board shall administer the Foreign Fire’ Insurance Fund in accordance with the
following rules and regulations.
      (1)   Fund account. All money in the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund shall be
kept in a fully insured or collateralized interest-bearing account in a bank or
savings and loan located within the village, and designated by the village’s
Board of Trustees.
      (2)   Budget. Annually, by May 1, the Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall
prepare and adopt a budget for the foreign fire insurance fund, listing fund
balance beginning of the year, estimated revenues, budgeted expenditures and
fund balance end of the year for the fiscal year beginning on the following May
1. Such budget shall be forwarded to the corporate authorities for adoption and
inclusion in the village’s annual budget.
      (3)   Use of Fund.
         (a)   Money from the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund may be used for the
following purposes and no others:
            1.   Maintenance of existing village’s Fire Department
firefighting, emergency medical treatment and department facilities and
equipment;
            2.   Purchase of equipment for firefighting, emergency medical
purpose and training purposes. All such equipment shall be purchased in the
name of the village’s Fire Department and shall become the property of the
village; and
            3.   Expenses related to operating the Fund.
         (b)   No such money shall be used for the personal benefit of any
person; or for any person, use or function not directly related to the
village’s Fire Department; or for food or beverages; or for any recreational or
entertainment activity.
   (D)   Designations of uses.
      (1)   List of appropriate expenditures. The Foreign Fire Insurance Board
shall develop and maintain a list of those items that the Board determines to
be appropriate expenditures under § 11-10-2 of the Illinois Municipal Code, 65
ILCS 5/11-10-2, and division (C) above. The Board shall review and, if
necessary, update this list at least once each year no later than May 1 of each
year. The list shall be a public document. All actions must be in accordance
with the budget review and adoption process.
      (2)   Annual meeting; notice. The Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall
authorize use of money from the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund by annual written
resolution only, setting forth with particularity the items on which funds may
be expended and the amounts approved for expenditure. Such action shall be
adopted at or after an annual public meeting conducted no later than May 1 of
each year, which public meeting shall be noticed and conducted in accordance
with the state’s Open Meetings Act, 5 ILCS 120/1 et seq.
      (3)   Recommended uses. Not fewer than 30 days prior to the date of the
aforesaid public meeting, the Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall submit to the
Village Manager, and make available to the general public, a list of items
recommended for approval and funding from the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund.
      (4)   Purchases. All purchases will be made in accordance with this
subchapter and in accordance with the purchasing requirements as set forth in
this municipal code.
      (5)   Necessary vote. An affirmative vote of at least three members of
the Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall be required to authorize any use of
money from the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund.
   (E)   Fund pay outs. The Foreign Fire Insurance Board Treasurer shall payout
money from the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund only upon the written order of the
Foreign Fire Insurance Board and only for maintenance, use and benefit of the
village’s Fire Department as permitted by this ordinance and authorized by
resolution of the Foreign Fire Insurance Board pursuant to division (D) above.
The written order of the Foreign Fire Insurance Board may consist of a notation
in duly approved minutes, an order signed by the President of the FFI Board, or
some other writing as may be designated by an authorized rule of the FFI Board.
The signatures of both the Board Treasurer and either the Board President or
the FFI Board Vice-President shall be required on any check, draft or other
order drawn on the account of the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.192 LIMITATION ON DEBT AND EXPENDITURES.
   The Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall not be permitted to incur debt or to
enter into any contract or agreement for maintenance of existing equipment or
for new equipment in excess of the unencumbered funds currently on deposit in,
and authorized for expenditure from, the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund at the
time of execution of such contact or agreement.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.193 FUND RECORDS; MEETING MINUTES.
   The treasurer of the FFI Board shall keep accurate and current records of
the foreign fire insurance fund and all accounts maintained there under,
including all deposits thereto, withdrawals and disbursements there from,
balances therein, and all other regular and customary financial and accounting
information. The Secretary of the Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall keep
accurate and current minutes of all meetings conducted by the Foreign Fire
Insurance Board.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.194 ANNUAL REPORT.
   The Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall, on or before May 30 each year, make
and file with the Village Treasurer, an annual report of the activities during
the prior year ended April 30, including a full and detailed account of all
receipts and disbursements made from the Foreign Fire Insurance Fund during the
village’s fiscal year ended immediately prior to the filing of such report. The
Foreign Fire Insurance Fund and all records relating thereto shall be subject
to and part of the annual audit of the village, including a balance sheet and a
detailed account of all revenues and expenditures in accordance with generally
accepted accounting principles for the fiscal years beginning May 1 and ending
April 30.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.195 COMPATIBILITY.
   All purchases shall fall within recognized industry standards and comply
with the safety and compatibility requirements of the Fire Department as
determined by the Fire Chief.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.196 ELECTION PROCEDURE.
   (A)   There is hereby established a temporary village Fire Department
Election Committee. The Temporary Election Committee shall consist of three
members: the Chief of the village’s Fire Department; the President of the
village’s Professional Firefighters Association; and one other member to be
appointed by the Chief from the sworn members of the village’s Fire Department.
   (B)   The Temporary Election Committee shall be responsible for organizing,
conducting and supervising the initial election of Department members to serve
on the Board. The Temporary Election Committee shall establish election
procedures consistent with this subchapter. Thereafter, the elected Board shall
establish its own election procedures consistent with this subchapter.
   (C)   The FFI Board shall develop a procedure for governing the nomination
of members to serve on the FFI Board. The nominating procedure shall be
established a minimum of 30 days prior to the expiration of the initial FFI
Board members’ terms of office.
   (D)   The FFI Board shall develop a procedure for the final election of
Department members on the FFI Board. The final election procedure shall be
established a minimum of 30 days prior to the expiration of the FFI Board
members’ terms of office.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.197 ELECTION OF OFFICERS.
   (A)   The Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall consist of five full-time sworn
members of the Fire Department with one vote each. The members of the village’s
Fire Department shall elect three full-time sworn members of the Fire
Department who shall serve as the members of the FFI Board. The fourth position
shall be filled by the Fire Inspector, and the fifth position shall be filled
by the Chief of the Dolton Fire Department (or the Assistant Chief as the Fire
Chiefs designee).
   (B)   Elected members of the FFI Board shall serve two-year terms and until
their successor are elected and installed. The first FFI Board elected will
consist of two members elected to serve from the date of the election until 4-
30-2005, and one member elected to serve from the date of election until 4-20-
2006. All subsequent terms shall begin on May 1.
   (C)   Vacancies shall be filled by election of the members of the Department
for the balance of the unexpired term, if more than three months remain in the
term of the member leaving the FFI Board; otherwise, such vacancies shall be
filled by appointment of the Fire Chief from among the members of the Fire
Department.
   (D)   The members of the FFI Board shall then elect from among themselves
the following officers: Chairperson; Vice-Chairperson; Treasurer; and
Secretary.
   (E)   No probationary member of the Department may hold such office during
the time of his or her probation. Each candidate shall only be eligible for
election to the office that the candidate designates prior to the election. The
sworn member receiving the most votes for each of the offices of President,
Vice-President, Treasurer and Secretary shall be elected to such office. An
elected member of the Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall be eligible for
reelection, but no member shall serve in any office for more than three
consecutive terms. All full-time active members of the Fire Department at the
time of the election shall be eligible to vote. Eligible voters shall vote for
only three of the listed candidates.
   (F)   All elections will be organized, conducted and supervised by the
Village Comptroller/Director of the Department of Revenue.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.198 OFFICERS; QUORUM; SPECIAL MEETINGS.
   (A)   The FFI Board shall, in accordance with the Open Meetings Act, being 5
ILCS 120/1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended, establish a regular time and
place for its meetings. The Chairperson shall preside at the meetings.
   (B)   Three members of the FFI Board shall constitute a quorum for the
transaction of the business. The affirmative vote of three members of the FFI
Board shall constitute approval of business before it.
   (C)   Special meetings may be called by the Chairperson, or by no less than
three members of the Board.
   (D)   Members on duty at the time of any meeting of the Foreign Fund
insurance Board shall be excused from duty to attend said meetings.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.199 DUTIES AND POWERS.
   (A)   FFI Board. The FFI Board shall have the power to approve the
expenditure of moneys for the maintenance, use and benefit of the Fire
Department. The FFI Board may adopt rules and regulations for governing the FFI
Board and the execution of the duties of the Board, and provide for election of
the FFI Board and management of funds. The FFI Board may amend or revoke rules
and regulations so adopted. The FFI Board shall, in accordance with the village
budget and appropriations procedures, annually prepare a budge which shall be
reviewed by the village’s Board of Trustees together with the Fire Department
budget.
   (B)   President. The President shall preside at all meetings of the Foreign
Fire Insurance Board. The President shall have such other powers as may be
given from time to time by action of the Board of Trustees of the village
consistent with the Illinois Municipal Code.
   (C)   Vice-President. The Vice-President shall carry out the duties of the
President during the absence or inability of the President to perform such
duties and shall carry out such other functions as are assigned from time to
time by the Foreign Fire Insurance President or the Board of Trustees of the
village.
   (D)   Secretary. The Secretary shall take minutes at any and all meetings of
the Foreign Fire Insurance Board. The Secretary shall keep a record of
resolutions, proceedings, minutes and actions of the FFI Board and these
records shall be open to the public. The records and minutes shall be kept in a
manner identical to the manner in which Village Board minutes are kept. The
Secretary shall also perform any other duties and functions as are assigned
from time to time by the President of the Foreign Fire Insurance Board or the
Board of Trustees of the village.
   (E)   Treasurer. The Treasurer shall:
      (1)   Have charge and custody of and be responsible for all funds
collected by the village from the foreign fire insurance company fees as
described in 65 ILCS 5/11-10-2;
      (2)   Deposit all such moneys in the name of the village’s Fire
Department in such banks, savings and loan associations or other depositories
as shall be selected by the Board of Trustees of the village;
      (3)   Invest said funds as are not immediately required in such
securities as the Board of Trustees of the village shall specifically or
generally select from time to time;
      (4)   Maintain the financial books and records of the Department;
      (5)   In general, perform all duties incidental to the office of assigned
to him or her by the Foreign Fire Insurance Board President or the Board of
Trustees of the village;
      (6)   The Treasurer of the Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall give a
sufficient bond to the village. This bond shall be approved by the Village
President, conditioned upon the faithful performance by the Treasurer of his or
her duties under this subchapter and the rules and regulations provided herein;
said bond shall be paid for from the funds collected from the foreign fire
insurance company fees; and
      (7)   The Treasurer of the Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall receive the
foreign fire insurance company fees so paid and shall pay out the money upon
the order of the Foreign Fire Insurance Board for the maintenance, use and
benefit of the Department.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.200 ANNUAL AUDIT.
   The Foreign Fire Insurance Board shall provide to the Board of Trustees of
the village, an annual audit not less, than 90 days after, the close of the
fiscal year, an annual audit of the financial affairs of the Foreign Fire
Insurance Board to be made by a certified public accountant at the end of each
fiscal year in accordance with the generally accepted auditing principals. The
annual report shall be delivered to the Village President, each Village
Trustee, Village Treasurer, Village Attorney and the Village Auditor. Said
audit shall be paid for from the funds collected from the foreign fire
insurance company fees. The village reserves the right to include in the annual
audit of the village the funds paid to the FFI Board to verify that the same
are used for maintenance, use and benefit of the Fire Department, and the FFI
Board shall reimburse the village for the cost of the audit of said funds.
(Ord. 04-267, passed 7-19-2004)
§ 33.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty has been prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Any person convicted of violating any order issued in accordance with
§§
33.002 and
33.003 of this chapter shall be guilty of an offense against the village and
may be fined not less than $50, nor more than $500, and imprisoned for a period
not exceeding six months or both.
(1988 Code, § 5-3-4)
   (C)   Any person who violates any section of §§
33.105 through
33.118 of this chapter shall be fined according to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances, and a separate offense shall be deemed
committed on each day during or on which a violation occurs.
(1988 Code, § 5-1-12)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 35.001 ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS.
   (A)   During the first quarter of each fiscal year, as required by statute,
the President and Board of Trustees shall enact an appropriation ordinance in
which shall be itemized all anticipated expenditures to be met during the
coming year, other than those payable from bond issues.
   (B)   This subchapter shall be published as required by law within ten days
after its enactment.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-1)
§ 35.002 ANNUAL TAX LEVY.
   Not sooner than ten days after the publication of the appropriation
ordinance, a tax levy ordinance shall be enacted as required by law, levying
such taxes as may be needed to meet the anticipated expenses of the coming
year, together with such taxes as may be required to meet outstanding bond
issues or for purposes payable from special taxes properly authorized. A
certified copy of the tax levy ordinance shall be filed with the County Clerk
not later than the second Tuesday in September. Such ordinance shall show the
total appropriated for each item and the amount of tax levied therefor.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-2)
§ 35.003 LIMIT TO INDEBTEDNESS.
   (A)   Limitation. The corporate authorities may borrow money on the credit
of the corporation for corporate purposes, and issue bonds therefor, in such
amounts and form, and on such conditions as the corporate authorities
prescribe. Before, or at the time of incurring any indebtedness, the corporate
authorities shall provide for the collection of a direct annual tax sufficient
to pay the interest on the debt as it falls due, and also to pay and discharge
the principal.
   (B)   Borrowing funds. The corporate authorities may borrow money from one
fund for the use of another fund; providing, such borrowing shall be repaid
within the current fiscal year.
   (C)   Refunding of debt. The corporate authorities may provide for the
consolidation or refunding of maturing bonds and the funding of judgment debts,
and to issue bonds in place of maturing bonds or judgment debts.
   (D)   Preceding ordinance. During the first quarter of any fiscal year,
before the enactment of the current appropriation ordinance, the village may
operate under the appropriation ordinance of the preceding year.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-3)
§ 35.004 CONTRACTS AND PURCHASES.
   (A)   General contracts.
      (1)   The Village President or any other person designated by the Board
of Trustees may sign, on behalf of the village, any contract authorized by the
Village Board. No contract other than contracts with service providers may be
entered into without the authority of the Village Board.
      (2)   All contracts with service providers in an amount greater than
$1,500 shall require prior approval of the Board of Trustees. For purposes of
this section, SERVICE PROVIDERS shall mean individuals or firms who provide
technical, consulting, property maintenance or similar service activities, not
involving the sale of supplies to the village.
   (B)   General purchases. The necessary supplies, materials and equipment for
the operation of the various departments of the village shall be on requisition
of the proper officer or employee of the department; provided that, funds for
the purchase of such supplies, services and equipment have been duly
appropriated; and, provided that, such purchases have been authorized by the
President and Board of Trustees in the manner prescribed by and subject to the
limitations imposed by law.
   (C)   Contracts over $10,000.
      (1)   All necessary supplies, materials or equipment or any work or other
public improvement which is not to be paid for in whole or in part by special
assessment or special taxation, when the expense thereof will exceed $10,000
shall be let by contract to the lowest responsible bidder after advertising for
bids in a publication of general distribution printed or distributed in the
village for proposals for furnishing such supplies, material or equipment or
any work or other public improvement. Plans and specifications for same shall
be first placed on file in the office of the Village Clerk before such
advertisement shall be made, and shall be open to public inspection. Unless
otherwise required by law, the advertisement shall be published not less than
ten days before the day fixed for receiving bids; provided, however, that, any
such contract may be entered into by the proper office without advertising for
bids, if authorized by a vote of two-thirds of all the Trustees then holding
office.
      (2)   In all cases involving the advertisement for bids for furnishing
the matter called for in this division (C), there shall be accompanied a
deposit where required by law or the corporate authorities, and named in the
advertisement, which deposit shall not exceed 10% of the estimated cost of the
supplies, material, equipment, work or other public improvement.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-4) (Ord. 87-106, passed 2-17-1987; Ord. 12-560, passed 5-21-
2012; Ord. 17-014, passed 5-15-2017)
§ 35.005 BILLS; PAYROLL.
   (A)   All bills payable by the village shall be submitted to the President
and Board of Trustees for approval before payment.
   (B)   The Treasurer shall pay out money in payment of all bills, or for
salaries, or for any other purpose other than the retirement of principal or
interest on bonds or tax anticipation warrants only upon warrant signed by the
Village President and the Village Clerk, as provided by statute. Such warrants
shall also be signed by the Village Treasurer and shall designate the items to
be paid and the funds from which they are to be paid.
   (C)   All warrants drawn on the Treasurer must be signed by the President
and countersigned by either the Village Treasurer and/or the Finance Committee
Chairperson and/or the Village Clerk, stating the particular fund or
appropriation to which the same is chargeable and the person to whom payable,
and no money shall be otherwise paid, except as may be provided by statute.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-5) (Ord. 03-218, passed 4-21-2003; Ord. 04-248, passed 4-19-
2004)
§ 35.006 TRANSFER OF FUNDS.
   (A)   Money shall not be transferred by the Treasurer from one fund to
another, after it has been received by him or her, nor appropriated to any
other purpose other than that for which it has been collected or paid, except
as may be ordered by the majority of the corporate authorities.
   (B)   Except as otherwise expressly set forth herein, all transfers of funds
shall be in the manner and form prescribed by statute.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-6) (Ord. 98-363, passed 4-9-1998)
§ 35.007 AUDIT OF ACCOUNTS.
   As soon as practicable at the close of each fiscal year and no later than
six months thereafter, there shall be an audit of all accounts of the village
made by a competent person authorized to act as an auditor under the laws of
the state, to be designated by the Village Board. Copies of such audit report
shall be filed with the Village Clerk and with the Director of the state’s
Department of Revenue and in such other places as may be required by law.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-7)
§ 35.008 SPECIAL ASSESSMENT FUNDS.
   (A)   All moneys received on any special assessment shall be held by the
Treasurer as a special fund to be applied only to the payment of the
improvement or bonds and vouchers issued therefor, together with interest
thereon, for which the assessment was made, and said money shall be used for no
other purpose unless to reimburse the village for the money expended for such
improvement. Payments on bonds or vouchers shall be made in accordance with the
statutes and the Treasurer shall keep his or her books and accounts in such a
manner so that proper prorations in payments of principal and interest can be
made and ascertained.
   (B)   Nothing herein shall prevent the transfer of excess reserve funds as
may be determined by audit and upon direction of the President and Board of
Trustees in the manner and form provided by statute.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-8)
§ 35.009 COPIES OF VILLAGE DOCUMENTS; CHARGES.
   (A)   The Village Clerk is authorized to collect the following charges for
the furnishing of certain documents:
      (1)   For furnishing copies of any page of this code: $0.25 per page and
$0.50 for the certificate with seal affixed thereto. Minimum charge for this
service shall be $1; and
      (2)   For furnishing a certified copy of any document, instrument or
other paper: $0.25 per page and $0.50 for the certificate with seal affixed
thereto. Minimum charge for this service shall be $1. No charge shall be made
to any officer or employee for any documents needed by said officer or employee
in the furtherance of the business of the village.
   (B)   All funds received under the provisions of this section shall be
deposited in the General Corporate Fund of the village.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-9)
   (C)   Costs incurred by the village for furnishing any copies under this
section shall be deemed a debt to the municipality. Court costs and reasonable
attorneys fees shall be awarded to the village in any action in which the
village seeks to enforce the provisions of this section.
(Ord. 94-266, passed 10-4-1994)
§ 35.010 HOUSING COURT ADMINISTRATIVE FEE.
   In the event of a finding of a violation of any of the village’s housing
related ordinances as determined through the administrative adjudication
process in housing court, the adjudicator shall assess an administrative
processing fee of $25 in addition to imposing a fine.
(Ord. 14-009, passed 5-5-2014)
§ 35.011 PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENTS OR ADVERTISEMENTS PAID FOR WITH PUBLIC
MONEY.
   (A)   No public service announcements or advertisement, including, but not
limited to, those paid with public moneys, that is made on behalf of the
village, any village department or village-sponsored or administered program
shall refer to or contain the name of any elected official, appointed official
or employee of the village.
   (B)   As used herein, PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENTS OR ADVERTISEMENTS shall
include any village signs, village vehicle signs, village posters, village
advertisements, village newsletters, print media, visual medium, broadcast
media, website or similar type of official communication. Notwithstanding the
foregoing, the following shall not be considered PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENTS
OR ADVERTISEMENTS:
      (1)   A publication listing elected officials along with other relevant
staff members for contact purposes only;
      (2)   Reference may be made to the elected official or employee by
personal name or likeness if required by law to execute official duties;
      (3)   Reference to an elected officer’s name only in the letterhead as
part of the stationary, forms or envelope of the village, except that:
         (a)   The names of all elected officials of the village must appear in
the same type size, typeface, type color and general location; and
         (b)   Such item may not include an elected officer’s photograph.
      (4)   Business cards which do not contain the elected officer’s
photograph or more than one mention of the elected officer’s name;
      (5)   Any items sent by the village to administer a program, to persons
subject to that program, in any instance where the mailing of such item is
essential to the functioning of the program, where the item does not include
the elected officer’s photograph, and where use of the elected official’s name,
office, title or signature is necessary to the functioning of the program; and
      (6)   A single response to an unsolicited request, wherein a written
communication from a third party, which reasonably requires a response and
which is not requested or induced by the recipient elected official or by any
third person acting at his or her behest.
   (C)   (1)   No elected official, officer or employee of the village shall
expend public moneys in violation of this section.
      (2)   Any and all invoices received in conflict with this section shall
not be paid.
   (D)   A copy of the ordinance codified herein shall accompany every purchase
order related to print media, visual medium, broadcast media, billboards,
signs, website or similar type of official communication.
   (E)   Any public service announcements or advertisements paid for with
public moneys, but generated prior to the effective date of this section shall
not be subject to the limitations set forth herein.
(Ord. 24-003, passed 1-24-2024)
OCCUPATION TAXES
§ 35.025 HOME RULE MUNICIPAL RETAILERS’ OCCUPATION TAX.
   (A)   Tax imposed.
      (1)   Effective 1-1-2026, the Home Rule Municipal Retailers’ Occupation
Tax imposed by the village on all persons engaged in the business of selling
tangible personal property at retail within the village, other than items of
tangible personal property titled or registered with an agency of this state’s
government, is hereby established at the rate of 1% on the gross receipts from
such sales, all in accordance with the provisions of 65 ILCS 5/8-11-1.
      (2)   Appropriate notification shall be served upon all businesses within
the village with relation to which the taxes are imposed and appropriate forms
shall be prepared by the village relative to the reporting and payment of the
taxes so imposed.
   (B)   Accounting. Every such person engaged in such business in the village
shall file reports as required under § 3 of the Retailers’ Occupation Tax Act
(35 ILCS 120/3), as amended.
   (C)   Payment of tax. At the time such report is filed, there shall be paid
to the state’s Department of Revenue the amount of tax hereby imposed on
account of the receipts from sales of tangible personal property during the
preceding month.
   (D)   Department of Revenue to administer. The tax hereby imposed, and all
civil penalties that may be assessed as an incident thereto, shall be collected
and enforced by the state’s Department of Revenue. The state’s Department of
Revenue shall have full power to administer and enforce the provisions of this
section.
(1988 Code, § 3-2-1) (Ord. passed 12-19-1978; Ord. 93-218, passed 8-3-1993;
Ord. 93-228, passed 10-5-1993; Ord. 13-003, passed 6-17-2013; Ord. 2025-010,
passed 9-2-2025)
§ 35.026 HOME RULE MUNICIPAL SERVICE OCCUPATION TAX.
   (A)   Tax imposed.
      (1)   Effective 1-1-2026, the Home Rule Municipal Service Occupation Tax
imposed by the village on all persons engaged in the village in the business of
making sales of service of tangible personal property transferred by such
servicepersons as an incident to a sale of service is hereby established at the
rate of 1%, all in accordance with the provisions of 65 ILCS 5/8-11-5.
      (2)   Appropriate notification shall be served upon all businesses within
the village with relation to which the taxes are imposed and appropriate forms
shall be prepared by the village relative to the reporting and payment of the
taxes so imposed.
   (B)   Accounting. Every such supplier or serviceperson required to account
for municipal service occupation tax for the benefit of the municipality shall
file as required under § 9 of the Service Occupation Tax Act (35 ILCS 115/9),
as amended.
   (C)   Payment of tax. At the time such report is filed, there shall be paid
to the state’s Department of Revenue the amount of tax hereby imposed.
   (D)   Department of Revenue to administer. The tax hereby imposed, and all
civil penalties that may be assessed as an incident thereto, shall be collected
and enforced by the state’s Department of Revenue. The state’s Department of
Revenue shall have full power to administer and enforce the provisions of this
section.
(1988 Code, § 3-2-2) (Ord. passed 12-19-1978; Ord. 93-218, passed 8-3-1993;
Ord. 93-228, passed 10-5-1993; Ord. 13-003, passed 6-17-2013; Ord. 2025-010,
passed 9-2-2025)
§ 35.027 MUNICIPAL USE TAX.
   (A)   Tax imposed.
      (1)   A tax is hereby imposed in accordance with the provisions of § 8-
11-6 of the Illinois Municipal Code (65 ILCS 5/8-11-6) upon the privilege of
using in the municipality any item of tangible personal property which is
purchased at retail from retailer, and which is titled or registered at a
location within the corporate limits of the village with an agency of state
government. The tax shall be at the rate of 0.5% of the selling price of such
tangible property with selling price to have the meaning as defined in the Home
Rule Municipal Use Tax Act, being 65 ILCS 5/8-11-1 et seq.
      (2)   Appropriate notification shall be served upon all businesses within
the village with relation to which the taxes are imposed and appropriate forms
shall be prepared by the village relative to the reporting and payment of the
taxes so imposed.
   (B)   Collection and payment of tax. Such tax shall be collected by the
village and shall be paid before the title or certificate of registration for
personal property is issued.
(1988 Code, § 3-2-3) (Ord. passed 10-1-1974; Ord. 93-218, passed 8-3-1993; Ord.
93-228, passed 10-5-1993)
§ 35.028 HOTEL OR MOTEL ROOM RENTAL TAX.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates a different
meaning.
      HOTEL ROOM or MOTEL ROOM. A room within a structure offered for rental on
a daily basis and containing facilities for sleeping. One room offered for
rental with or without an adjoining bath shall be considered as a single HOTEL
OR MOTEL ROOM. The number of HOTEL OR MOTEL ROOMS within a suite shall be
computed on the basis of those rooms utilized for the purpose of sleeping.
      OWNER. Any person having an ownership interest in or conducting the
operation of a hotel or motel room or receiving the consideration for the
rental of such hotel or motel room.
      PERSON. Any natural person, trustee, court appointed representative,
syndicate, association, partnership, firm, club, company, corporation, business
trust, institution, agency, government corporation, municipal corporation,
district or other political subdivision, contractor, supplier, vendor, vendee,
operator, user or owner, or any officers, agents, employees or other
representative, acting either for himself or herself or for any other person in
any capacity, or any other entity recognized by law as the subject of rights
and duties. The masculine, feminine, singular or plural is included in any
circumstances.
   (B)   Tax imposed, payment and collection.
      (1)   There is hereby levied and imposed upon the use and privilege of
renting a hotel or motel room within the village a tax of 5% of the gross
rental receipts received by such hotel or motel. This tax, however, shall not
be levied and imposed upon any person who rents a hotel or motel room for more
than 30 consecutive days or to a person who works and lives in the same hotel
or motel, or persons or corporations that are billed monthly.
      (2)   The ultimate incidence of and liability for payment of said tax is
to be borne by the person who seeks the privilege of occupying the hotel or
motel room, said person hereinafter referred to as “renter”.
      (3)   The tax herein levied shall be paid in addition to any and all
other taxes and charges. It shall be the duty of the owner of every hotel or
motel to secure said tax from the renter of the hotel or motel room and to pay
over to the Village Collector said tax under procedures prescribed by the
Village Collector, or as otherwise provided in this section.
      (4)   Every person required to collect the tax levied by this section
shall secure said tax from the renter at the time he or she collects the rental
payment for the hotel or motel room. Upon the invoice receipt or other
statement or memorandum of the rent given to the renter at the time of payment,
the amount due under the tax provided in this section shall be stated
separately on said documents.
   (C)   Transmittal of tax revenue.
      (1)   (a)   The owner or owners of each hotel or motel room within the
village shall file tax returns showing tax receipts with respect to each hotel
and motel room during each three-month period, commencing on and including
January 1, April 1, July 1 and October 1, upon forms prescribed by the Village
Collector. The return shall be due on or before the fifteenth day of the
calendar month succeeding the end of the quarterly filing period (i.e., return
for January, February and March tax receipts, due on or before April 15; return
for April, May and June tax receipts, due on or before July 15; and the like).
         (b)   Notwithstanding the provisions above, the first taxing period
for the purpose of this section shall commence on January 1, and shall cease on
March 31. The tax return and payment for such period shall be due on or before
April 15. All subsequent reporting periods shall be full calendar quarters, as
provided in division (C)(1) above. At the time of filing said tax returns, the
owner shall pay to the Village Collector all taxes due for the period to which
the tax return applies.
      (2)   Any owner of a hotel or motel who, for the preceding quarterly
period, has failed to file a proper return and pay over the proper amount of
tax to the Village Collector, may be required by the Village Collector, in his
or her discretion, to file subsequent returns and pay the tax herein imposed on
a monthly basis, in which case payments of the tax shall be made to the Village
Collector on or before the fifteenth day of the month succeeding the month for
which the tax was due.
      (3)   If for any reason any tax is not paid when due, a penalty at the
rate of 1% per 30-day period, or portion thereof, from the day of delinquency
shall be added and collected.
   (D)   Books and records; examinations. The Village Collector, or any person
certified by him or her as his or her deputy or representative, may enter the
premises of any hotel or motel for inspection and examination of books and
records in order to effectuate the proper administration of this section and to
assure the enforcement of the collection of the tax imposed. It shall be
unlawful for any person to prevent, hinder or interfere with the Village
Collector, or his or her duly authorized deputy or representative, in the
discharge of his or her duties in the performance of this section. It shall be
the duty of every owner to keep accurate and complete books and records to
which the Village Collector, or his or her deputy or representative (authorized
by him or her), shall at all times have full access, which records shall
include a daily sheet showing:
      (1)   The number of hotel or motel rooms rented during the 24-hour
period, including multiple rentals of the same hotel room where such shall
occur; and
      (2)   The actual hotel or motel tax receipts collected for the date in
question.
   (E)   Enforcement.
      (1)   Action to force payment of tax. Whenever any person shall fail to
pay any tax as herein provided, the Village Attorney shall, upon the request of
the Village Collector, bring or cause to be brought an action to enforce the
payment of said tax in behalf of the village in any court of competent
jurisdiction.
      (2)   Suspension of license. If the President, after hearing held by or
for him or her, shall find that any person has willfully avoided payment of the
tax imposed by this section, he or she may suspend or revoke all village
licenses held by such tax evader. The owner shall have an opportunity to be
heard at such hearing to be held not less than five days after notice of the
time and place of the hearing to be held, addressed to him or her at his or her
last known place of business. Pending notice, hearing and finding, any license
of which he or she may be in possession may be temporarily suspended. Any
suspension or revocation of any license shall not release or discharge the
owner from his or her civil liability for the payment of the tax nor from
prosecution for such offense.
   (F)   Disposition of proceeds. All proceeds resulting from the imposition of
the tax under this section, including penalties, shall be paid into the
treasury of the village.

§ 35.029 FOREIGN FIRE INSURANCE COMPANIES.
   (A)   Tax imposed. All corporations, companies and associations not
incorporated under the laws of the state, and which are engaged in effecting
fire insurance, shall pay to the Village Treasurer for the maintenance, use and
benefit of the Fire Department, a sum of money equal to 2% of the amount of all
premiums which during the year, ending on every July 1, shall have been
received for any insurance effected or agreed to be effected by or with such
corporation, company or association on any property within the village. Such
payments shall be made for the year ending July 1 of each year.
   (B)   Reports required; payment of tax. Every person acting as agent or
otherwise, for or on behalf of any such corporation, company or association
shall, on or before July 15 of each and every year, render to the Clerk a full,
true and just account, verified by his or her oath, of all premiums which,
during the year ending on July 1 preceding such report, shall have been
received by him or her, or by any other person for him or her, in behalf of any
such corporation, company or association and shall specify in such report the
amounts received for fire insurance on property within the village. Such agent
shall also, at the time of rendering the aforesaid report, pay to the Treasurer
the sum of money for which the companies, corporations or associations
represented by them are severally chargeable by virtue of the provisions of
this section.
   (C)   Recovery; effect on policies.
      (1)   The sum of money for which such company, corporation or association
is so chargeable may be recovered of it or its agent or agents, by an action in
the name of and for the use of the village as for money had and received.
      (2)   Nothing in this division (C) shall be held to exempt any person,
corporation, company, or association from indictment and conviction under the
provisions of an act of the General Assembly of the state entitled an Act to
Enable Cities, Towns, Villages and Fire Protection Districts Organized under
the General or Special Law, to Levy and Collect a Tax or License Fee from
Foreign Insurance Companies for the Benefit of Organized Fire Departments, and
amendments thereof.
   (D)   Insurance brokers restricted. No insurance broker shall place any
insurance with any company, association or corporation not incorporated under
the laws of the state which shall be in default for not reporting or making
payment as hereinbefore provided until it shall have complied with all the
requirements of this section.

§ 35.030 VIDEO STORES OCCUPATION TAX.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      GROSS RECEIPTS. The consideration received for the leasing of
videocassettes valued in money whether received in money or otherwise,
including cash, credits, services, and property of every kind and nature, and
shall be determined without any deduction on account of the cost of
videocassette, the labor or service costs or any other expenses whatsoever.
      PERSON. Any natural individual, firm, trust, estate, partnership,
association, joint stock company, joint adventure, corporation, municipal
corporation, or political subdivision of the state, or a receiver, trustee,
conservator or other representative appointed by order of any court.
      TAXPAYER. A person engaged in the business of leasing videocassettes
within the corporate limits of the village.
      VIDEOCASSETTES. A relatively wide magnetic tape used to record television
images, usually together with associated sound, for subsequent playback and/or
broadcasting.
   (B)   Imposition of tax.
      (1)   A tax imposed upon all persons engaged in the business of leasing
videocassettes within the corporate limits of the village at the rate of 8% of
the gross receipts from the business effective 1-1-1992.
      (2)   (a)   On or before the fifteenth day of each calendar month, each
taxpayer shall make a return to the Village Treasurer for the preceding
calendar month accompanied by a report form supplied by the Village Collector,
indicating the information as listed below:
            1.   The taxpayer’s name;
            2.   The address of the taxpayer’s principal place of business in
the village;
            3.   The taxpayer’s gross receipts from the leasing of
videocassettes;
            4.   The amount of tax computed on division (B)(1) above; and
            5.   Other reasonable information that the Treasurer may require.
         (b)   Each video store owner shall transmit to the Village Collector
for receipt by said official, no later than the fifteenth day of each calendar
month, a sum of money equal to the amount as listed on the form as referenced
in division (B)(2)(a) above, and such other information as the office may
require for enforcement of this section.
      (3)   In making the return, the taxpayer shall determine the value of
actual consideration other than money received by the taxpayer. This
determination shall be subject to review and revision by the Treasurer as
provided in division (C) below for correction of returns.
   (C)   Return corrections. If the Village Collector has reason to believe and
does believe that any return is incorrect, after notice to the taxpayer and an
opportunity to be heard, according to the Village Collector’s best judgment and
information. Any return so corrected by the Village Collector shall be prima
facie correct.
   (D)   Rules and regulations. The Village Collector is authorized reasonable
rules and regulations relating to the administration and enforcement of this
subchapter as may be deemed expedient.
   (E)   Failure to make return. In case any taxpayer fails to make a return
when and as required by this section, the Village Collector, after notice to
the taxpayer and an opportunity to be heard, shall determine the amount of the
tax according to the Village Collector’s best judgement and information. This
amount, when so fixed, shall be prima facie correct.
