GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 37.001 MEETINGS.
   (A)   Public notice.
      (1)   Public notice of the schedule of regular meetings of any board,
committee or commission of the village shall be given at the beginning of each
municipal year. Public notice of any special meeting, or of any rescheduled
regular or any reconvened meeting shall be given at least 24 hours before such
meeting. However, this requirement of public notice of reconvened meetings does
not apply to any case where the meeting is to be reconvened within 24 hours,
nor to any case where announcement of the time and place of the reconvened
meeting was made at the original meeting and there is no change in the agenda.
      (2)   Public notice shall be given by posting a copy of the notice at the
Village Hall. Copies of the notice of regular meetings and of the notice of any
special rescheduled or reconvened meeting will be supplied to any local
newspaper of general circulation or any local radio or television station that
has filed an annual request for such notice. Any such news media shall also be
given the same notice of all special, rescheduled or reconvened meetings in the
same manner as is given to members of the body; provided, such news media has
given the corporate authorities of the village an address within the village at
which such notice may be given.
   (B)   Schedule of meetings.
      (1)   In addition to the notice required by division (A) above, the
Village Clerk shall prepare and make available a schedule of the regular
meetings of all boards, committees or commissions of the village, listing the
time and places of such meetings.
      (2)   If a change is made in regular meeting dates, at least ten days’
notice of such change shall be given by publication in a newspaper of general
circulation in the village. Notice of such change shall also be posted at the
Village Hall and shall also be supplied to those news media which have filed an
annual request for notice as provided in division (A) above.
(1988 Code, § 1-13-1)
§ 37.002 PROPERTY ACQUISITION BY CONDEMNATION.
   (A)   Eminent domain powers. The corporate authorities may exercise its
power of eminent domain to condemn property for any public purpose. A public
purpose shall exist if the property, after its acquisition, is useful,
advantageous or desirable for municipal purposes. The corporate authorities may
exercise their condemnation power for any public purpose authorized to a
municipal corporation by statute or any other public purpose which will be
useful, advantageous or desirable within its home rule powers as established by
ordinance. The corporate authorities shall commence such condemnation by an
ordinance or resolution which shall state the purpose or purposes for which the
property is to be acquired and shall be used.
   (B)   Procedure. In all cases where property is acquired or sought to be
acquired by condemnation, the procedure shall be like that provided for in an
Act to Provide for the Exercise of the Right of Eminent Domain, approved 4-10-
1872, as heretofore and hereafter amended.
   (C)   Economically deteriorating areas. The corporate authorities have the
power to acquire and redevelop economically deteriorating areas within its
corporate limits.
(1988 Code, § 1-13-3) (Ord. passed 5-30-1978)
§ 37.003 INVESTIGATION AND ENFORCEMENT OF RULES.
   (A)   (1)   The President and Board of Trustees (hereinafter “authorities”)
may investigate the enforcement of the municipal ordinances, rules and
regulations, and the action, conduct and efficiency of all officers, agents and
employees of the municipality.
      (2)   In the conduct of such investigations the village authorities may
hold public hearings.
      (3)   Each member of the village authorities shall have power to
administer oaths, and the Village Clerk, by order of the village authorities,
shall issue subpoenas to secure the attendance and testimony of witnesses and
the production of books and papers relevant to such investigations and to any
hearing before the village authorities or any proper member thereof.
   (B)   Any circuit court of jurisdiction, upon application of the village
authorities, or authorized member thereof, may in its discretion compel the
attendance of witnesses, the production of books and papers and the giving of
testimony before the village authorities or any member thereof, by attachment
for contempt or otherwise in the same manner as the production of evidence may
be compelled before the court.
(Ord. 90-104, passed 1-20-1990)

Comprehensive Plan is hereby adopted as the official comprehensive plan of the
village.
   (B)   Public inspection. The Comprehensive Plan shall be available for

§ 37.005 JUANITA NEWELL COOK SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM.
   (A)   Subject to donation and/or receipt of sufficient funds, the Juanita
Newell Cook Rewarding Dolton’s Students Educational Scholarship Program is
established. The Scholarship Program is to be administered by the Board of
Trustees of the village.
   (B)   There is hereby established an independent commission to be
responsible for the oversight and administration of the Juanita Newell Cook
Rewarding Dolton’s Students Educational Scholarship Program to be known as the
Juanita Newell Cook Rewarding Dolton’s Students Educational Scholarship
Commission. The Commission shall promulgate rules, regulations and procedures
necessary to accomplish the stated purpose.
   (C)   The Juanita Newell Cook Rewarding Dolton’s Students Education
Scholarship Program shall be funded, in whole or in part, from donations from
residents, business owners and friends of the village.
   (D)   The Mayor is hereby authorized and directed to establish and implement
a mechanism via which a contribution of $1 may be added to and/or included with
the payment of any water and/or sewer account bills being paid by village
residents and business owners, and for the receipt of other contributions of
varying amounts. All monetary contributions, from any and all sources, shall be
held in a segregated escrow account established solely for the purpose of
administering the Juanita Newell Cook Rewarding Dolton’s Students Education
Scholarship Program. Said scholarship account program shall be audited
annually.
   (E)   A resident of the village who receives a high school diploma from a
village school district or an accredited non-public school in the village in or
after the 2007-2008 school year and who otherwise meets the award
qualifications, is eligible to receive the Juanita Newell Cook Rewarding
Dolton’s Students Educational Scholarship under the program if the student is
accepted by and enrolled to attend an approved post-secondary eligible
institution, full time. ELIGIBLE INSTITUTION, for purposes of this section,
means a degree or certificate granting accredited post-secondary education:
      (1)   Public or private college or university;
      (2)   Junior college or community college; and/or
      (3)   Vocational or technical educational program.
   (F)   In addition to the requirements division (E) above, to be eligible for
a scholarship under this program, an individual must:
      (1)   Be a citizen of the United States or has been classified as a
permanent resident alien of the United States immigration and naturalization
service;
      (2)   Have a cumulative high school “C” grade point average;
      (3)   Have satisfactorily met the entrance requirements for admission as
a full-time student to an eligible institution;
      (4)   Have received a high school diploma from a village school district
or an accredited non- public school in the village or the high school
equivalency diploma not more than one-year period preceding the submittal of
the scholarship application;
      (5)   Have not received a scholarship under this program for more than
the equivalent of eight semesters; and
      (6)   Have not been convicted of a felony, or any crime relating to
assault, physical injury or death.
   (G)   The scholarship amount shall be $500 per student in any fiscal year,
and the number of scholarships awarded shall be based upon the availability of
scholarship funds. The Board of Trustees may adjust the amount of the Juanita
Newell Cook Rewarding Dolton’s Students Educational Scholarship available to
eligible students based upon its determination of available resources, but the
Board shall not increase or decrease in an amount by more than 5% in any fiscal
year.
   (H)   The Juanita Newell Cook Rewarding Dolton’s Students Educational
Scholarship Program is being established in honor of the life and work of the
late Juanita Newell Cook. A copy of the proclamation issued in honor the life
of Juanita Newell Cook is attached to the ordinance codified herein and made a
part hereof as if fully set forth herein.
(Ord. 07-421, passed 11-5-2007)

UNCLAIMED PROPERTY
§ 37.020 PRESUMPTION OF ABANDONMENT.
   The following property held by the village is presumed abandoned:
   (A)   Any deposit made to the village in compliance with an ordinance of the
village requiring said deposit unless the owner has, within three years:
      (1)   Increased or decreased the amount of the deposit;
      (2)   Corresponded in writing with the village concerning the deposit;
and
      (3)   Otherwise indicated an interest in the deposit as evidenced by a
memorandum on file with the village.
   (B)   Any sum payable on checks issued by the village on which the village
is liable for payment which has been outstanding for a period of three years
from the date of its issuance unless the owner has, within three years:
      (1)   Corresponded in writing with the village concerning it; or
      (2)   Otherwise indicated an interest as evidenced by a memorandum on
file with the village.
   (C)   All funds and intangible personal property held by the village in a
fiduciary capacity for the benefit of another unless the owner has, within
three years after it becomes payable or distributable:
      (1)   Accepted payment of principal or interest;
      (2)   Corresponded in writing concerning the property; or
      (3)   Indicated an interest in the property as evidenced by a memorandum
on file with the village.
   (D)   All other funds and intangible personal property not otherwise covered
by this subchapter, except for personal property held by the village’s Police
Department pursuant to 765 ILCS 1030/1 through 1030/5 as now or hereafter
amended, and property of which custody and control is prescribed by Art. II of
Ch. 4 of the Illinois Vehicle Code, being 625 ILCS 5/4-201 et seq. as now or
hereafter amended, and held for the owner by the village, and that has remained
unclaimed for a period of more than three years.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-10-1) (Ord. 93-215, passed 7-20-1993)
§ 37.021 NOTICE TO OWNERS.
   (A)   Notice required.
      (1)   After the funds or intangible personal property held by the village
is presumed abandoned, in accordance with the provisions of §
37.020 of this chapter, the Village Clerk shall cause notice to be published
once in an English language newspaper of general circulation in the county in
the state in which is located the last known address of any person to be named
in the notice.
      (2)   If no address is listed or if the address is outside the state, the
notice shall be published in an English language newspaper of general
circulation in the village.
   (B)   Contents of notice. The published notice shall be entitled “Notice of
Names of Persons Appearing to be Owners of Abandoned Property” and shall
contain:
      (1)   The names, in alphabetical order and last known addresses, if any,
of persons listed in its report and entitled to notice within the county as
hereinbefore specified;
      (2)   A statement that information concerning the amount or description
of the property and the name and address of the holder may be obtained by any
persons possessing an interest in the property by addressing an inquiry to the
Village Clerk; and
      (3)   A statement that if proof of claim is not presented by the owner to
the Village Clerk and if the owner’s right to receive the property is not
established to the Village Clerk’s satisfaction within 65 days from the date of
the published notice, the abandoned property will be placed, not later than 85
days after such publication date, in the custody of the Treasurer to whom all
further claims must thereafter be directed.
   (C)   When publication not required. The Village Clerk is not required to
publish in such notice any item of less than $200 unless he or she deems such
publication to be in the public interest, nor any item of which the name of the
owner is unknown.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-10-2) (Ord. passed 12-11-1979; Ord. passed 7-5-1983)
§ 37.022 SALE OF PROPERTY.
   (A)   Public sale. All abandoned property other than money delivered to the
Treasurer under this subchapter shall, within one year after the delivery, be
sold by her to the highest bidder at public sale. The Treasurer may decline the
highest bid and reoffer the property for sale if she considers the price bid
insufficient. He or she need not offer any property for sale if, in his or her
opinion, the probable cost of sale exceeds the value of the property.
   (B)   Notice of sale. Any sale held under this subchapter shall be preceded
by a single publication of notice thereof at least three weeks in advance of
sale in an English language newspaper of general circulation in the village.
   (C)   Transfer of title. The purchaser, at any sale conducted by the
Treasurer pursuant to this subchapter, shall receive title to the property
purchased free from all claims of the owner or prior holder thereof and of all
persons claiming through or under them. The Treasurer shall execute all
documents necessary to complete the transfer of title.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-10-3) (Ord. passed 12-11-1979)
§ 37.023 REVENUE FROM PROPERTY SALES.
   (A)   Disposition of revenues. All funds received under this subchapter,
including the proceeds from the sale of abandoned property under §
37.022 of this chapter, shall forthwith be transferred by the Treasurer for
deposit in the Corporate Fund of the village; except that, the Treasurer is to
retain in a separate trust fund an amount not exceeding $700 from which he or
she shall make prompt payment of claims duly allowed by the village as
hereinafter provided. However, should any claim be allowed or any refund
ordered under the provisions of this subchapter in excess of $700, the village
shall increase the amount of such separate trust fund to an amount necessary
for prompt payment of such claim in excess of $700 and the Treasurer shall make
prompt payment thereof.
   (B)   Records kept. Before making the deposit, the Treasurer shall record
the name and last known address of each person appearing to be entitled to the
abandoned property which record shall be available for public inspection at all
reasonable business hours.
   (C)   Deduction of village costs. Before making any deposit pursuant to this
subchapter, the Treasurer may deduct:
      (1)   Any costs in connection with sale of abandoned property;
      (2)   Any costs of mailing and publication in connection with any
abandoned property; and
      (3)   Any costs in connection with the maintenance of records or
disposition of claims made pursuant to this subchapter.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-10-4) (Ord. passed 12-11-1979)
§ 37.024 CLAIMS FOR PROPERTY.
   (A)   Authority to file claim. Any person claiming an interest in any
property delivered to the Corporate Fund under this subchapter may file a claim
thereto or to the proceeds from the sale thereof on the form prescribed by the
Village President and Board of Trustees.
   (B)   Determination of claims; hearing. The Village President and Board of
Trustees shall consider any claim filed under this subchapter and may, in their
discretion, hold a hearing and receive evidence concerning it. No hearings
shall be held if the payment of the claim is ordered by a court, if the
claimant is under court jurisdiction, or if the claim is paid under the Probate
Act, being 755 ILCS 5/25-1 as now or hereafter amended.
   (C)   Payment of claim; deduction of village costs. If the claim is allowed,
and after deducting an amount not to exceed $20 to cover the cost of notice,
publication and related clerical expenses, the Treasurer shall make payment
forthwith upon notification by the Village President and Board of Trustees.
   (D)   Restriction on accrued income. When property is paid or delivered to
the Treasurer under this subchapter, the owner is not entitled to receive
income or other increments accruing thereafter.
(1988 Code, § 1-10-10-5) (Ord. passed 12-11-1979)
HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCE AND MATERIAL INCIDENT REIMBURSEMENT
§ 37.035 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   COSTS. All expenses incurred by the Fire Department or any other public
agency assisting the Fire Department as a result of any removal or remedial
action.
   EMERGENCY RESPONSE AGENCY. A unit of local government or volunteer fire
protection organization that provides:
      (1)   Firefighting services;
      (2)   Emergency rescue services;
      (3)   Emergency medical services;
      (4)   Hazardous materials response teams;
      (5)   Emergency service and disaster agency/civil defense; and
      (6)   Public works departments and/or maintenance departments.
   FACILITY. Any building, structure, installation, equipment pipe or pipeline
including, but not limited to, any pipe into a sewer or publicly-owned
treatment works, well, pond, lagoon, impoundment, ditch, landfill, storage
container, tank, motor vehicle, truck trailer, rolling stock or aircraft. Also,
any site or area where a hazardous material has been deposited, stored,
disposed of or otherwise managed.
   HAZARDOUS MATERIALS OR SUBSTANCES. Any material, substance or mixture of
materials or substances which are toxic, flammable, corrosive, explosive,
carcinogenic or radioactive including, but not limited to, any substance or
material which is designated as a hazardous material pursuant to the Hazardous
Materials Transportation Act (49 U.S.C. §§ 5101 et seq.) in a quantity and form
which may pose a substantial present or potential hazard to human health,
property or the environment when improperly released, treated, stored,
transported, disposed of or otherwise managed.
   MUTUAL AID. Any action taken by the Fire Department or any public agency
pursuant to an intergovernmental agreement, including, but not limited to, any
agreement that is part of the mutual aid box alarm system (“MABAS”).
   RELEASE. Any spilling, leaking, pumping, pouring, emitting, escaping,
discharging, injecting, leaching, dumping or disposing of a hazardous material
into or on any land, air, water, well, stream, sewer or pipe so that such
hazardous material or any constituent thereof may enter the environment.
   REMEDIAL ACTION. Any action consistent with permanent, remedy taken instead
of or in addition to removal actions in the event of a release or threatened
release of a hazardous material into the environment, to prevent or minimize
the release or a hazardous materials so that they do not migrate to cause a
substantial present or potential hazard to human health, property or the
environment. The term includes, but is not limited to, such actions at the
location of release as storage, confinement, perimeter protection using dikes,
trenches or ditches, clay cover, neutralization, cleanup of released hazardous
materials or contaminated materials, recycling or reuse, diversion,
destruction, segregation, or reactive wastes, repair or replacement of leaking
containers, collection of leachate and runoff, on-site treatment or
incineration, provision of alternate waste supplies and any monitoring
reasonably required to assure that such actions protect the public health and
welfare and the environment.
   REMOVAL. The cleanup or removal of released hazardous materials from the
environment; such actions as may be necessary or appropriate to monitor, assess
and evaluate the release or threat of release of hazardous materials, the
disposal of removed material, or the taking of such action as may be necessary
to prevent, minimize or mitigate damage to the public health or welfare of the
environment.
   RESPONSE. Any removal or remedial action.
   RESPONSIBLE PARTY. Any person, company, firm, corporation, business,
partnership, an unincorporated association, association, estate, trust, joint
venture or legal entity, or their legal representative, agent or assign. Also,
any unit of federal, state or local government.
(Ord. 06-341, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 37.036 PROHIBITED ACTS.
   No person shall cause, threaten or allow the release of hazardous materials
into the environment unless such release is in accordance with an appropriate
permit granted by the state’s Environmental Protection Agency or other state or
federal agency having primary jurisdiction over the release and such release is
in such place and manner as will not create a substantial present or potential
hazard to human health, property or the environment.
(Ord. 06-341, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
37.999
§ 37.037 RESPONSE AUTHORITY.
   (A)   The Fire Chief or designee shall have authority to respond to any
release or threatened release of hazardous materials within the village or
affecting the public water supply, wells or sewage treatment works located
within the village or pursuant to any lawful intergovernmental agreement of
which the Fire Department is a party. This authority includes, but is not
limited to, remedial action and removal.
   (B)   (1)   The Fire Chief or designee shall have primary authority to
respond to any release or threatened release of hazardous materials as
described above. The Fire Chief or designee shall ensure the reporting of any
release or threatened release of hazardous materials to appropriate federal,
state and local public health, safety and emergency agencies within 24 hours of
any substantial release of hazardous materials.
      (2)   The Fire Chief shall relinquish response authority at such time, if
any, as the federal, state or local public health, safety or emergency agency
having primary jurisdiction over the release or threatened release has assumed
responsibility for response to the release or threatened release.
   (C)   The Fire Chief or designee shall be authorized to utilize all
Department personnel and equipment and has sole discretion to take such
remedial or removal action as may be deemed necessary or appropriate to respond
to the release of hazardous material.
   (D)   All responding personnel shall cooperate with and operate under the
direction of the Fire Chief or other person then exercising response authority
under this subchapter until such time as the person exercising such response
authority has determined that the response is complete or responsibility for
response is assumed by the federal, state or local public health, safety or
emergency agency having primary jurisdiction over the release or threatened
release.
   (E)   The person exercising response authority under this subchapter shall
coordinate and/or cooperate with other federal, state or local pubic health,
safety or emergency response agencies involved in response to the release or
threatened release of hazardous materials.
(Ord. 06-341, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 37.038 LIABILITY FOR COSTS.
   Notwithstanding any other provision or rule of law, and subject only to the
defenses set forth herein, the following persons shall be jointly and severally
liable for all costs of removal and remedial action incurred by the village,
including, but not limited to, the village’s Fire Department, Police Department
and Public Works Department, as a result of a release or threatened release of
a hazardous material:
   (A)   The owner and operator of a facility or vessel from which there was a
release or substantial threat of release of a hazardous material;
   (B)   Any person who, at the time of disposal, transport, storage or
treatment of a hazardous material, owned or operated the facility or vessel
used for such disposal, transport, treatment or storage from which there was a
release or substantial threat of a release of any such hazardous material;
   (C)   Any person who by contract, agreement or otherwise has arranged with
another party or entity for transport, storage, disposal or treatment of
hazardous materials owned, controlled or possessed by such person at a facility
owned or operated by another party or entity from which facility there is a
release or substantial threat of a release of such hazardous materials; and
   (D)   Any person who accepts or accepted any hazardous materials for
transport to disposal, storage or treatment facilities from which there is a
release or substantial threat of a release of a hazardous substances.
(Ord. 06-341, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 37.039 DEFENSES.
   There will be no liability hereunder for a person otherwise liable who can
establish by a preponderance of the evidence that the release or substantial
threat of release of a hazardous material and the damages resulting there from
occurred in accordance with any of the permitted defenses enumerated in 415
ILCS 5/22-2.
(Ord. 06-341, passed 5-15-2006)
“INVEST IN DOLTON”; AUCTIONING VACANT HOMES TO BE REHABILITATED
§ 37.050 AUTHORIZATION AND ESTABLISHMENT.
   (A)   The corporate authorities of the village hereby authorizes the
commencement of legal action for acquisition and sale of vacant residential
properties to be owned by the village to support the program “Invest in
Dolton”, to be established as follows.
   (B)   The Village Manager is hereby authorized and directed to establish a
program to raffle or auction village-owned vacant homes to a village resident
or any persons who seeks to live and own a home in Dolton to rehabilitate said
home to comply with all village codes.
(Ord. 17-048, passed 11-30-2017)
§ 37.051 PROCEDURES, RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Village-owned vacant homes may be sold by raffle or auction for a cost
of acquisition of $5,000 to financially qualified persons.
   (B)   All raffles or auction candidates must show proof of access to funds
in a minimum amount of $40,000 to rehabilitate the property to qualify, by way
of line of credit or cash or bank approval loan.
   (C)   Once a candidate is deemed qualified, a list of vacant residential
properties shall be prepared and all qualified candidates will be allowed to
participate in the “Invest in Dolton” auction program of any property offered
by the village.
   (D)   Raffle or auction winners will receive an “AS IS” conditional purchase
offer.
   (E)   Properties shall not be conveyed to the raffle or auction winner until
the rehabilitation is completed and the work approved by the village.
   (F)   However, to support and comply with lending regulation, the village
may issue a reversionary deed or deposit deed with a closing escrow agent to
assist in satisfying lending requirements.
   (G)   All rehabilitation work shall be performed by a licensed contractor
registered with the village.
   (H)   Candidates will be required to execute a one-year renovation agreement
including a deed restriction that the property must remain owner occupied for
five years after completion of the rehabilitation.
   (I)   Failure to comply with the terms of the renovation agreement shall
result in forfeiture of the property.
   (J)   The Village Manager is authorized to establish all program rules and
regulations to implement and manage this program. A law firm will serve as
special legal counsel for the program entitled “Invest in Dolton” by acquiring
the properties for the cost of acquisition.
(Ord. 17-048, passed 11-30-2017)
§ 37.052 FUNDING.
   All professional service costs for legal services for the “Invest in Dolton”
program shall be paid from the village’s Legal Services Account. All moneys
paid shall be restored to the legal services account upon the village’s receipt
of funds from the execution of purchase contracts with village for raffled or
auctioned properties pursuant to the program.
(Ord. 17-048, passed 11-30-2017)
§ 37.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty has been prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   Any person who is liable for the release or threatened release
of a hazardous material who fails without sufficient cause to pay for or
provide removal or remedial action upon or in accordance with a notice and
request of the Fire Department, or in accordance with any order of any court
having jurisdiction of the matter, shall be liable to the village for any costs
incurred by the Fire Department as a result of such failure to provide or take
such removal or remedial action, together with the cost of any removal or
remedial action taken by the Fire Department in accordance with the ordinance,
and all attorneys fees and related legal costs incurred in connection
therewith.
      (2)   In addition, any such person shall be guilty of a violation of §§
37.035 through
37.039 of this chapter and shall be filled not less than $100, nor more than
$700, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed for each
day on which a violation occurs or continues.
      (3)   Charges for removal or remedial action when rendered by the Fire
Department or any other responding agency rendering mutual aid or assistance to
the Fire Department shall include, but not be limited to:
         (a)   The reasonable cost of each vehicle responding as determined by
the responding agency;
         (b)   The cost of all personnel including any overtime costs to the
village of or to any responding agency, incurred as a result of the removal or
remedial action; and
         (c)   The cost of all materials and equipment used, expended,
depleted, destroyed or removed from service in accordance with federal, state
or local ordinance as a result of the mitigation or containment operations if
or at the request of the Fire Department or any responding agency.
(Ord. 06-341, passed 5-15-2006)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 50.001 SYSTEMS COMBINED; ADMINISTRATION.
   (A)   There was, heretofore on 6-13-1961, combined into one utility a
waterworks system of the village and an existing combined sewer system of the
village, which is presently known as the “Combined Waterworks and Sewerage
System of the Village of Dolton, Cook County, Illinois”.
   (B)   The combined waterworks and sewerage system shall be under the
administrative control of the President and Board of Trustees.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-1)
§ 50.002 USE OF PUBLIC SYSTEMS REQUIRED.
   (A)   No building permits shall be issued for the erection of any building
on any lot or parcel of land within the village unless such proposed building
shall be connected with the sewer and water systems of the village whenever
such sewer or water system is available or adjacent to such lot or parcel of
land.
   (B)   Every building in which plumbing fixtures are installed and are for
human use, occupancy or habitation shall be connected to the public water
supply if available, otherwise, suitable provisions shall be made for water in
accordance with the provisions of §
50.003(A) of this chapter providing for the construction of private water
supply.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-2)
§ 50.003 PRIVATE SYSTEMS.
   (A)   Permit to construct; covenant to connect to public system when
available. In the event that the sewer or water system of the village is not
available to or adjacent to such lot or parcel of land, a building permit will
be issued only after application is made to the President and Board of Trustees
for special permit to construct a private well, septic tank and seepage system.
The President and Board of Trustees may grant such special permit after setting
standards and specifications for the construction of wells, septic tanks and
seepage systems, setting permit fees, inspection fees and requiring a covenant
from the permittee in regard to the ultimate connection to the water and sewer
systems of the village.
   (B)   Private catch basins, manholes and vaults.
      (1)   The construction of private catch basins or manholes outside the
lot lines or inside the area or building walls will not be permitted unless
special written permission is given by the Building Commissioner and the Health
Inspector.
      (2)   No private catch basins, manholes or vaults shall be permitted in
any street or alley pavement without direct authority to so place the same
being first obtained from the President and Board of Trustees.
   (C)   Prohibitions.
      (1)   Outhouses and vaults. Outhouses shall not be maintained or
constructed; nor shall any old vault be connected to a sewer.
      (2)   Cesspools. Cesspools shall not be allowed by this code of
ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-3) Penalty, see §
50.999
§ 50.004 CONNECTION TO COMBINED SYSTEM.
   (A)   The President and Board of Trustees is hereby authorized to make such
rules and regulations consistent with this chapter for the connection to the
combined waterworks and sewerage system, specifying the types and sizes of
pipes and all the other appurtenances and extensions thereto and amend the same
from time to time as may be deemed necessary. All service pipes and connections
to the combined waterworks and sewerage system shall comply with the said
specifications and rules. Any person not complying with the specifications and
rules for connections to the combined waterworks and sewerage system shall be
subject to a penalty provided in §
50.999 of this chapter.
   (B)   The connection to the village sewer or water systems shall be made by
the Building Department and the charge to be made for such connection shall be
determined by the President and Board of Trustees.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-4)
§ 50.005 MAINTENANCE OF PIPES AND FIXTURES.
   The customer shall be responsible for maintaining all pipes and fixtures on
the owned premises and no credit will be given on excess meter charges caused
by leakage and waste on the customer’s premises, whether known or not.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-5)
§ 50.006 EXCAVATIONS FOR WATER PIPES OR SEWERS.
   (A)   Permit required. No work of excavating for laying or repairing water
pipes or sewers in the street or parkway or other public rights-of-way shall be
lawful unless the required permit is obtained.
   (B)   Deviating from grade. Should water, gas or other pipes or drains be
encountered in the direct line of a house sewer during its construction, the
method of carrying such sewer under, over or around such or similar
obstructions or of doing anything involving a deviation from the proper line of
standard grade shall be approved by the Building Commissioner.
   (C)   Disturbing private sewers or drains. Whenever it may be found
necessary to pass through or in any way disturb any existing house drain or
private sewer in actual use, such drainage pipe or private sewer shall not be
interfered with, nor cut through, nor connected in any way, without the
approval of the Building Commissioner.
   (D)   Sewer trenches. All excavations for sewer and drain trenches shall
have a uniform slope at the bottom with cross grooves cut in to receive the
hubs of the pipe. Each length of pipe shall be given a solid bearing using
concrete, if necessary, and the soil on each side of the pipe shall be well
rammed.
   (E)   Protection of utility mains, equipment and pipes. Should gas or water
mains, electrical equipment or other pipes be encountered during the laying of
sewers or drains, the pipes encountered shall be carefully and thoroughly
protected against injury or settlement by the contractor at his or her own
expense. Long sections of pipe shall be so placed that undue strain to any part
thereof, through expansion or contraction, cannot occur.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-8) Penalty, see §
50.999
§ 50.007 ACCESS TO PREMISES.
   Employees of the combined waterworks and sewerage system shall have the
right at all times of access to any person’s premises for the purpose of
ascertaining the number and type of water and sewer connections to the combined
system. Any person refusing the right to permit the said employees of the
combined waterworks and sewerage system the above-described right of access to
his or her premises shall be subject to a penalty as provided in §
50.999 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-9) Penalty, see §
50.999
§ 50.008 NOTICE TO USERS OF THE SYSTEM.
   A copy of this chapter, properly certified by the Village Clerk, shall be
filed in the office of the Recorder of Deeds of the county, and shall be deemed
notice to all owners of real estate of their liability for service supplied to
any user of the service of the combined waterworks and sewerage system of the
village on their properties, and it shall be the duty of the Village Clerk and
such other officers of the village to take all action necessary or required by
the laws of the state thereunto enabling to file all claims for money due to
the village and to prosecute and enforce such claims in the manner, form and
time as permitted by the laws of the state.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-10)
WATER USE AND SERVICE
§ 50.020 PERMIT TO USE WATER; UNLAWFUL USE.
   (A)   No person shall take water from any fire plug, hydrant, valve, faucet,
pipe or any other opening connected with the village’s waterworks system, nor
shall any person open any such fire plug, hydrant, valve or faucet for the
purpose of taking water, or for any purpose, unless such person shall first
have made application for use of water for such purpose and shall have received
permission from the Building Commissioner, or unless such person is an employee
of the village and is acting in the discharge of his or her duties as such.
   (B)   No person to whom a permit is issued for the use of water for any
purpose whatsoever, including construction purposes, tamping, irrigating,
testing, flushing, domestic supply and the like shall use or consent to the use
of any water not authorized by said permit, or consent to the use of such water
by any other person. Any person to whom such permit is issued shall at all
times use precaution to prevent any waste of water or damage and, upon
completion of the work for which such use of water is authorized, or upon the
expiration of the time specified in such permit, he or she shall be required to
close off all stopcocks and valves; provided, however, that, if a permit has
been issued for service from water service pipes controlled by such valves they
may be allowed to remain open.
   (C)   The water supply may be cut off from any premises if the permit
therefor was obtained through misrepresentation or if any unauthorized use or
willful waste of water is found.
   (D)   Adoption of rules governing the conservation of water.
      (1)   Title. This division (D) shall be entitled “Water Regulations”.
      (2)   Rules and regulations. The Village President or his or her lawful
designee shall be empowered to issue and promulgate such regulations or rules
as may, from time to time, be necessary to conserve water and otherwise ensure
the integrity and sufficiency of the waterworks system for the village. Such
regulations shall be filed with the Village Clerk and shall be published and
enjoy the same force and effect of ordinances of the village and violations
shall be punishable as provided for in this chapter.
   (E)   For the period commencing on May 15 through September 15, of each
year, no one shall sprinkle, water or irrigate lawns or residential vegetation
between the hours of 12:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.
   (F)   None of the provisions of division (E) above are intended to preclude
the Village President or his or her lawful designee from promulgating rules
further restricting the use of water as may be determined necessary in the case
of water shortage as prescribed by division (D) above.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-6-1) (Ord. 88-126, passed 6-28-1988; Ord. 90-113, passed 7-
10-1990) Penalty, see §
50.999
§ 50.021 TURNING ON WATER.
   (A)   Within 48 hours after completing any attachment or connection to the
waterworks system, the plumber to whom the permit was issued shall make report
in writing to the village on forms to be furnished by the village that such
work is completed.
   (B)   The water will not be turned into any house or private service pipe
until the proper requests for permit have been received and work has been
approved by the Building Commissioner who shall issue a certificate of approval
to that effect. Plumbers will be allowed to leave the water turned on for 24
hours to test their work, but at the end of such time and before request for
permit is made, they shall turn off the water. For all other purposes, plumbers
are strictly prohibited from turning the water into any service pipe, except
upon written order or permission of the Building Commissioner.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-6-2)
§ 50.022 CONSTRUCTION REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Water taps.
      (1)   Authority to tap. No person, except an employee of the village,
duly authorized by the Board of Trustees, shall be permitted under any
circumstances to tap the street main or insert service cocks therein. The
builder or construction contractor shall perform the necessary uncovering in
order for the Village Plumber to make the tap.
      (2)   Notice requesting water taps. Notice must be filed in the office of
the Building Department by the plumber, fixing the day on which he or she
wishes the service cock inserted. This notice must be filed prior to commencing
any excavation in the street for the purpose of laying the service pipe or
inserting the service cock. Notice shall be filed on or before 9:00 a.m. for
taps desired on the same afternoon of the notice. In case the hole is not
properly dug and it becomes necessary for tapper to return to the job a second
time, an additional charge of $45 will be made.
      (3)   Preparation of private tapping. All service cocks must be inserted
at or near the top of the street main, and in no case nearer than two feet of
the bell of the pipe; except that, when the street main shall be less than five
feet below curb grade, such tap shall be made in a manner to least expose the
service pipe to damage by frost. The building contractor or builder’s plumber
shall prepare the trench for the water service pipe from the water main to the
buffalo box, and shall furnish the water service pipe for tapping, and after
tapping by the Village Plumber, shall backfill in accordance with the
provisions of this chapter.
      (4)   Fee. The tapping fee shall be in addition to the service charge for
meters as set forth in §
50.045 of this chapter.
      (5)   Non-liability of village. Nothing in this division (A) contained
shall render the village liable to the plumber or relieve the plumber from the
duty and expense of protecting trenches until such time as the village is able
to make the tap and inspections required, and do any incidental work it is
required to perform.
   (B)   Construction specifications.
      (1)   Water service pipes and appurtenances.
         (a)   Each and every water service pipe must have a minimum three-
quarter inch T handle roundway stopcock inserted not less than one foot, nor
more than six feet, inside of the curb in parkway. Such stopcock or valve shall
be known as a service cock. The line of the service pipe shall be approximately
at right angles to the main, and the sidewalk service cock shall be located
directly opposite the tap in the main. Where the sidewalk covers the entire
parkway, the service cock shall be inserted into the service pipe not less than
two feet inside the edge of the curb. Each and every service cock must be
protected with a cast-iron buffalo stop box at least five feet long or longer,
as required by the Building Department, and with the word “water” cast on the
cover. Such service cock and box must be placed by the plumber as hereinafter
provided. The stop box in all cases must be placed plumb and square over the
service cock and level with the top of the sidewalk or curb. Rules governing
service cock and stop box in a street shall apply to these appurtenances when
placed in an alley; except that, the service cock shall be placed in the alley
not more than one foot from the lot line and that the stop box shall be of
extra heavy iron and shall be set level with the grade of the alley.
         (b)   The service pipe may be laid in the same ditch with the house
sewer, but shall not be laid directly over the sewer. The service pipe shall be
laid not less than five feet below the established grade of the street nor with
less than five feet of cover. The service pipe shall be laid to the depth above
specified without regard to the depth of the street main. Service pipe shall
have sufficient length to prevent fracture by settlement of earth. The
backfilling over the service pipe in any roadway in clay soil must be filled
with sand and rammed or puddled to the satisfaction of the Building
Commissioner. At the ferrule, the earth must be carefully rammed under the main
distribution pipe to a level with the top of the service pipe. In wet or soft
ground, a solid support of brick, stone or wood shall be placed under the
“gooseneck” to prevent breaking the coupling.
         (c)   1.   Service pipes for a dwelling having not more than eight
rooms may be three-quarter inch at service cock, and continue as such size to
and inside of the building; provided that, such building is not located more
than 50 feet from such service cock.
            2.   Every apartment building of five stories or more shall have
two water services connected in series.
         (d)   Should it become necessary to replace or repair old service
pipes, the provisions of this division (B)(1) above shall apply.
         (e)   All service pipes for household purposes shall be of three-
quarter inch internal diameter, except when a special permit for a larger
service and corresponding tap is obtained from the Building Department.
         (f)   The service pipes of all fountains set out of doors must be
provided with stopcocks, under the control of the Building Commissioner.
         (g)   All water service pipes shall be Type K soft copper excepting
that water service pipes larger than two inches shall be American Water Works
Association, Class B, cast iron pipe of the bell and spigot type and shall
conform to the village’s specifications. No water service pipe of an internal
diameter less than three-quarter inch shall be installed in any public way nor
connected to the mains of the village waterworks system.
         (h)   Yard hydrants located in yards, open lots or fields or as a
temporary supply for buildings or other purposes or where subject to use by the
public shall be on a metered service pipe.
         (i)   It shall be the duty of the tapper to see that the proper
connection is made with the ferrule; that the water is turned on; that joints
are tested for leaks; that the pipe is unobstructed; and that the service cock
is in good working order. He or she shall make and record accurate measurements
as to location of box and depth of service pipe.
         (j)   The tapper shall refuse to tap any street main for any one of
the following reasons: incorrect size, grade or quality of pipe, service cock
or stop box; improper joints; also when pipe is not in the ditch, or when
service cock and stop box are not properly set; or when there is not sufficient
surplus pipe at main; or when ditch is not properly dug. The tapper, for any
such cause, may require the plumber to obtain a new order for the tapping in
question.
         (k)   The service pipe on house side of service cock shall not be
covered before it has been inspected and approved by the Building Commissioner.
         (l)   The service pipe shall enter the building in a direct line with
the stop box and tap where practicable. Such pipe shall be provided with a gate
valve the full size of the house service. Such shut-off shall be known as “main
building cock”. The service pipe shall be three-quarter inch Type K copper
minimum to the location of the water meter inside of the building. Distributing
main and supply pipes shall conform to this chapter. Such fixtures shall be
provided with a pipe not less than three-quarter inch inside diameter.
         (m)   Any person who shall hereafter lay down or alter any service
pipe contrary to the provisions of this chapter shall be subject to punishment
as provided in this chapter; and, in addition thereto, shall be prohibited from
doing any further work relating to the village water supply until he or she
shall have paid all fines and corrected his or her work in compliance with this
division (B)(1).
      (2)   Rat-proofing. All exterior openings provided for the passage of
piping shall be properly sealed with snuggly-fitting collars of metal or other
approved rat-proof material securely fastened in place. Interior openings
through walls, floors and ceilings shall be rat-proofed.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-6-3) Penalty, see §
50.999
§ 50.023 WATER METERS.
   (A)   General.
      (1)   No free service of the water shall be furnished to any person,
firm, organization or corporation, public or private. Every user of water shall
have a metered water connection to said system and every water meter shall be
sealed by the Village Plumber. Such water meter shall be approved by the
corporate authorities.
      (2)   The flat rate charged for water supplied under any building permit
shall terminate when occupancy of premises begins. All water used after
beginning of occupancy shall be supplied through a meter.
   (B)   Installation of meters. Water meters shall be set in the following
manner.
      (1)   Inside of the buildings, all meters shall be placed on the service
pipe where such service pipe enters the building, except no water meters shall
be installed in any water closet room. Such meters shall be provided with two
shut-off valves, one on supply and one on house side of meter. The size of
meters shall be as prescribed by the Building Department.
      (2)   Outside of buildings, the water meter shall be set in a basin or
vault. All meter basins or vaults shall be made to specifications prescribed by
the Board of Trustees. The location of meter boxes outside of buildings shall,
so far as practicable, be between the sidewalk and curb lines.
   (C)   Maintenance and repair.
      (1)   In no case will anyone be allowed to remove or replace any water
meter connected to the service, except the Village Plumber. In case of any
trouble with, or repair necessary to any water meter, the Building Department
must be notified. The Building Department shall repair and put in proper
condition the water meter, replacing and sealing same; except, in emergency
cases, a registered master plumber may remove such meters from connection and
insert connection piece in its place. The master plumber must make a detailed
report within 24 hours to the Building Department. Each 24 hours’ continuance
of delay in making a report shall constitute a separate offense.
      (2)   The Superintendent of Public Works shall from time to time cause to
be inspected and tested water meters as routine procedure. Between routine
tests, the Superintendent shall cause to be inspected and tested such water
meters as may appear to be out of order or indicate faulty registration. Any
meters found faulty on such test shall be repaired or replaced at village
expense unless such faulty meter shall have been damaged by the negligence of
the customer, in which case the village will charge the customer the cost of
such repairs or replacement.
   (D)   Meter sizes. The following size water meters shall be installed as
indicated:
Size of Dwelling Meter Size
Size of Dwelling              Meter Size
1-family dwelling
   3/4” tap and 3/4” pi5/8” water meter
2- and 3-family dwelling
   1” tap and 1” pipe  1” water meter
4-, 6- and 8-family dwelling
   1-1/2” tap and 1-1/2�1” water meter
10-, 12-, 16-, 18- and 20-family dwelling
   2” tap and 2” pipe  2” water meter
 
   (E)   Hot water returns. In all dwellings other than one-family dwellings,
there shall be a hot water return.
   (F)   Remote water meter reading. In all new construction of buildings, the
owner thereof shall install a one-half inch conduit from a front side location
on the building, to be determined by the village’s Superintendent of Public
Works. Said conduit shall be through the wall of the building to the water
meter location and shall be one foot back of front corner of the building and a
minimum of two feet above grade to a maximum of four feet above grade. The
conduit, when installed, shall be for the exclusive use of the village’s Water
Department for the installation of wire for remote water meter readings.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-6-4) (Ord. passed 4-13-1976) Penalty, see §
50.999
§ 50.024 UNAUTHORIZED WATER CONNECTION.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to connect to, disconnect, repair or
alter the village water system, or any part thereof, including, but not limited
to, any water line or water meter, or to open any fire hydrant, property stop,
valve or other fixtures attached to the system of water supply without first
obtaining written permission from the village.
   (A)   Tampering with or altering water system prohibited.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to meddle, tamper with, alter,
deface or make changes to any public water system facilities or appurtenances
thereof including the building water service line to any premises, or any
building plumbing fixtures ahead of the meter, or to interfere in any way with
a meter or meter set plumbing.
      (2)   Should it appear that water has been stolen by way of altering any
piping, unauthorized connection, straight piping, meter tampering or otherwise,
the village shall have the right to discontinue service until all defects,
alterations and tampering have been corrected, and appropriate compensation and
restitution has been made by the offending person.
      (3)   When a water meter is found to have been tampered with or unmetered
water has been otherwise diverted or used, the customer shall be billed at the
current commodity rate for the estimated unauthorized volume as determined by
the village. The consumption shall be estimated on the basis of previous
consumption records or any other appropriate basis at the discretion of the
village in accordance with generally accepted utility practices.
   (B)   Meters.
      (1)   Inspection and adjustment. Meters may be checked, inspected or
adjusted at the discretion of the village and they shall not be adjusted or
tampered with in any manner or removed by the user or any other person.
      (2)   Meter interference. No person shall:
         (a)   Prevent water from passing through any meter connected directly
or indirectly with the public water mains;
         (b)   Prevent any meter from accurately registering the amount of
water passing through such meter; or
         (c)   Prevent or obstruct a meter from accurately registering the
quantity of water supplied or in any way interfere with the purpose, action or
just registration of a meter.
   (C)   Inspections of water meters.
      (1)   A duly authorized employee of the village, bearing proper
credentials and identification shall be permitted to enter upon the premises at
any time and at all reasonable hours and shall have access to the meter for the
purpose of inspection, reading and examining the water meter whenever the
village suspects or determines that there is an unauthorized water connection.
If access is refused, the supply of water may be shut off without further
notice.
      (2)   An inspection of the water meter and connection to the village
water supply shall be conducted prior the issuance of the village real estate
transfer stamp for the sale of property and whenever there is a change in
tenant when the premises is being rented or leased.
      (3)   In addition to the right to inspect under divisions (C)(1) and (C)
(2) above, the village shall have the right to conduct an inspection of the
water meter and connection to the village water supply on a yearly basis.
   (D)   Inspection by warrant. If the owner, agent, occupant or person in
charge of the premises does not consent to the attempted inspection, the
Superintendent of Public Works, or his or her duly authorized agent, shall seek
a search warrant in the Circuit Court of the county. The warrant shall be for
the purpose of making an inspection to determine whether there is an
unauthorized connection to the village’s water supply. An owner, agent,
occupant or person in charge of the premises who is presented with a search
warrant obtained pursuant to this division (D) shall not refuse, impede,
inhibit, interfere with, restrict or obstruct entry and free access to any part
of the premises where an inspection authorized by the search warrant is sought
to be made.
   (E)   Unauthorized water service; theft of services.
      (1)   Prohibited. It shall be unlawful to provide oneself or others with
(or make use of) water service from the village water system without
authorization form the village. When water service has been discontinued by the
Public Works Department for non-payment of water charges, non-compliance with
this section or for any other reason, it shall be unlawful to restore water
service or receive water service by any means without the authorization by the
village. The presence at any time on or about any meter, water line or water
main of the village (whether such meter is owned or operated by the village or
others) of a pipe or any other device which diverts water or results in taking
of any water, except through an authorized meter shall constitute prima facie
evidence on the part of the person owning or having custody or control of the
premises (where such a device or pipe is located) of the knowledge of the
existence thereof. The knowledge of such existence by the person who would
benefit by the failure of the water to be accurately metered, and shall further
constitute prima facie evidence of intention on the part of such person to
violated this section.
      (2)   Meter removal. If water service has been discontinued by the Public
Works Department due to non-payment or for any other reason, and the customer
turns the service back on or otherwise restores service without approval, the
Public Works Department may remove the meter and plug the service.
(Ord. 16-006, passed 3-7-2016) Penalty, see §
50.999
§ 50.025 WATER CONSERVATION MEASURES.
   (A)   Secondary water.
      (1)   Definition. SECONDARY WATER shall be known as water from any source
other than water from the village water system.
      (2)   Secondary supplies to be kept separate from potable water.
Secondary waters from shallow or deep aquifers, sumps, retention basins and
reclaiming units, whenever in a system of water supply piping, shall be kept
entirely separate from the domestic supply of potable water and there shall be
no connection of any kind between the two supplies.
      (3)   Pipes to be painted, warning signs required. Secondary water
systems and piping shall be painted a color of yellow as prescribed by the
village. A sign shall be attached to any faucet, valve or opening where the
secondary water could accidentally become ingested. The sign shall read: “THIS
WATER IS NOT FOR HUMAN OR ANIMAL CONSUMPTION”.
   (B)   Flushing sanitary sewers. Flushing of sanitary sewers with potable
water from the village water system shall not be allowed. Water used for
flushing shall be secondary water and used through a high velocity type sewer
jet.
   (C)   Water-using fixtures regulated.
      (1)   Generally. In all new construction and in all repair and/or
replacement of water-using fixtures, only fixtures not exceeding the following
flow rates and/or water usage shall be installed. These ratings are based on a
pressure at the fixture of 40 to 50 psi:
 
Lavatory sink faucets           3.0 gal. per minute
Shower heads                    3.0 gal. per minute
Urinals, flushometer type       1.50 gal. per flush
Urinals, tank type              Illegal
Water closets, flushometer type 3.0 gal. per flush
Water closets, tank type        3.5 gal. per flush
 
      (2)   Lavatories for public use. In addition to the requirements above,

installed on all new construction or new remodeling.

§ 50.026 RESTRICTED AND PROHIBITED ACTS.
   (A)   Fire hydrants.
      (1)   Use restricted. No person, except a regularly authorized agent of
the village, shall cause water to flow from any public or private fire hydrant;
except that, a person other than such an agent of the village may operate and
use water from a fire hydrant only after a written permit has been issued by
the Village President permitting such use and only after suitable arrangements,
approved by the President for payment for such water used, have been made.
      (2)   Damage or obstruction. No person shall willfully or carelessly
break or injure any of the public hydrants, or pollute or unnecessarily waste
the water at any such hydrant, or obstruct the use of any fire hydrant, or
place any material in front thereof, or within five feet from either side
thereof.
   (B)   Tampering with or injury to water utility.
      (1)   No person, other than a regularly authorized agent of the village
in line of duty, shall interfere in any manner with any public or private fire
hydrant, water main, main line valve or box or commit any act tending to
obstruct the use thereof without first obtaining a permit from the President
and Board of Trustees.
      (2)   No person shall willfully or carelessly break, injure, mar, deface,
interfere with or disturb the walls, fixtures, buildings, machinery, apparatus,
fencing reservoirs, storage tanks or any of the appurtenances of the water
system.
   (C)   Excavation near water mains. Any person making an excavation in the
vicinity of existing water mains shall be fully responsible for any damage or
leakage to or from said water mains and shall repair immediately such damage or
leakage to the satisfaction of the Building Commissioner and upon failure to do
so shall be subject to the penalties provided herein.

WATER RATES AND CHARGES
§ 50.040 WATER RATES ESTABLISHED.
   (A)   Water rates.
      (1)   RESIDENTIAL USERS (defined to mean single-family residences or
multi-family residences with fewer than four dwelling units, and multi-family
residences with four or more dwelling units which are owner-occupied) shall pay
a rate of $7.50 per 100 cubic feet of water consumed.
      (2)   Effective 5-1-2027, all NON-RESIDENTIAL USERS (commercial,
industrial, institutional and multi-family residential units of four or more
dwelling units which are not owner-occupied) shall pay a rate of $7.50 per 100
cubic feet of water consumed. Non-residential users shall also pay a basic user
rate for the use of and for service supplied by the wastewater collection
system of 20% of the total water charges.
   (B)   Cost of living increase. Effective 5-1-2018, and each May 1
thereafter, a 2% cost-of-living increase shall be imposed on the non-
residential water rate.
   (C)   Chicago-imposed increase. Effective 5-1-20217, any increase imposed on
the village by the City of Chicago for water service to the village shall be
passed on to non-residential customers.
   (D)   Unusual use of system. In cases where the character of sewage from any
commercial or industrial buildings shall be such as to impose a burden upon the
sewerage system of the village, then the President and Board of Trustees
reserve the right to enter into separate contracts for special rates and
charges where the particular circumstances render the regular rates for
servicing inadequate or unjust.
   (E)   Refuse/garbage charge. The refuse/garbage pick-up charge as authorized
by §
51.005 of this code of ordinances and collected as part of the water bill shall
be $20.50 per month. Beginning 7-1-2018, and every July 1 thereafter, there
shall be an increase in the quarterly charge for refuse/garbage pick-up service
corresponding to the increase, if any, established by the village’s approved
garbage-hauling vendor. In addition, beginning 7-1-2018, and every July 1
thereafter, there shall be a 2% cost-of-living adjustment added to the rate.
   (F)   Billing errors. An error in billing shall not constitute waiver of
claim for adjustment.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-7-1) (Ord. 25-009, passed 9-2-2025)
§ 50.041 DETERMINATION OF CHARGES; ESTIMATES.
   Charges at the rates as set forth in §
50.040 of this chapter shall be made on the readings of water meters made by
persons employed by the village for such purpose. Reading shall be made every
three months. In the event there is no one present on the premises at the time
the water meter reader makes his or her regular call, the water meter reader
shall leave a U.S. postal card, appropriately printed, to permit the consumer
to record the present reading of the water meter on said card, instructing the
consumer to record and send the reading into the office of Comptroller and
Revenue Administrative Services. In the event the consumer does not mail in
such card in the time limit designated on said card, the office of Comptroller
and Revenue Administrative Services shall render an estimated bill for water
consumption, which bill shall be in an amount equal to the highest bill
rendered said consumer or to the premises serviced within the preceding
municipal year.
(Prior Code, § 7-6-7-2) (Ord. 03-217, passed 4-21-2003)
§ 50.042 RED TAGGING AND SHUTTING OFF WATER.
   (A)   Red tagging. In accordance with the provisions of §
50.041 of this chapter concerning meter readings taken once every three months,
if after a second reading is taken and a U.S. postal card is left for return to
the office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services which has not
been returned within ten days of the second reading, said meter may be
considered for “red tagging” in preparation for “shut off’ of water to the
premises.
   (B)   Authority to enter premises. The officers of the Department of Public
Works of the village and any person delegated by the Superintendent of the
Department shall have free entry and access to every part of any building,
structure or premises whenever such entry or access is deemed necessary or
advisable. Wherever any person, in possession, charge or control of any such
building, structure or premises into which any such officer or designated
representative of the Superintendent of the Department of Public Works shall
desire entry or access, shall refuse to permit such entry or access, or shall
do or cause to be done any act or thing for the purpose of preventing such
entry or access, the Superintendent may turn off the water service from said
building, structure or premises, until notice shall have been given the
Superintendent, in writing, that entry or access will be permitted or provided,
and until such entry or access shall have been accomplished.
   (C)   Private persons supply water.
      (1)   No person, whether owner or occupant, or in possession, charge or
control of any building, structure or premises into which water service is
introduced, shall be allowed to supply other persons or families, or to supply
any water from such buildings or premises to a building, structure or premises
other than the one for which such water service is introduced, unless a permit
from the Department of Public Works shall first have been secured.
      (2)   If any person, either as owner or occupant, or in possession,
charge or control of any such building, structure or premises of such person
shall be shut off and stopped forthwith, any amount which shall have been paid
for water service shall be forfeited to the village. Where the water service
shall be cut off for a violation of the provisions of this section, it shall
not be turned on again until there has been paid to the village such sum of
money as the Department of Public Works shall deem properly due for the amount
of water furnished or used in violation of the provisions of this section and
until the expense for cutting off the water service on account of such
violation shall have been paid.
   (D)   Presumption of suspicion of tampering with water supply. Any building
or structure concerning which no entry thereto has been permitted for a period
of one year shall be presumed, by virtue of such delay, to be subject as to
tampering with the water supply system and shall fall under the provision of
“red tagging”, provided hereinabove.
   (E)   List of premises. After the expiration of the time for payment
specified hereinbefore, a list shall be compiled of those premises for which
assessed rates and charges remain unpaid, and the water supply of the premises
against which such rates and charges remain so outstanding shall be authorized
for “red tagging” and “shut off”. The office of Comptroller and Revenue
Administrative Services shall send specific notice to the owner of the premises
scheduled for “red tagging”, personally delivered by the water meter reader for
said premises. Said notice shall specify the day and time the meter will be
“red tagged” and water shut off.
   (F)   Limitation on shut-ff days. Water shut-off shall be limited to Monday,
Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. Absent an emergency, there shall be no shut-
offs on Friday, Saturday or Sunday.
