GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 91.001 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   AIR CONTAMINANT. Particulate matter, dust, fumes, gas, mist, smoke or vapor,
or any combination thereof.
   AIR POLLUTION. Presence in the outdoor atmosphere of one or more air
contaminants in sufficient quantities and of such characteristics and duration
as to be injurious to human, plant or animal life or to property, or which
unreasonably interferes with the enjoyment of life and property.
   BOARD. The Air and Water Pollution Control Board of the village.
   GARBAGE. Any rejected or waste household food, offal, swill or carrion, and
every accumulation of animal, fruit or vegetable matter that attends the
preparation, use, cooking and dealing in or storage of meat, fish, fowl, fruits
or vegetables and any other matter of any nature which is subject to decay,
putrefaction and the generation of noxious or offensive gases or odor which,
during or after decay, may serve as a breeding or feeding material for flies or
other germ-carrying insects.
   OPEN BURNING. Any burning of combustible materials wherein the products of
combustion are emitted directly into the open air without passing through a
stack or chimney.
   PERSON. Includes the singular and plural and also means any individual,
occupant, owner, owner’s agent, lessee or tenant, family, persons, groups,
firm, corporation, association, governmental agency or municipal or quasi-
municipal corporation.
   WASTE. Any or all of the following: domestic garbage; refuse; ashes; tin
cans; household trash, including discarded household furniture, fixtures and
appliances of all kinds; manure; dead animals or parts thereof; trees; tree
branches; tree roots; tree trunks; brush; shrubs; grass clippings; plant stalks
and leaves.
   WATER POLLUTION. The placing or discharge of any noxious, toxic or other
deleterious substance into any waters of the village, or upon the banks or
margins thereof, which may tend to affect the properties of such waters in a
manner which may tend to render such waters harmful or inimical to the public
health, safety or welfare, to animal or aquatic life, to the use of such waters
for domestic water supply, and for industrial, agricultural or recreational
purposes consistent with applicable water quality standards of the state.
   WATERS OF THE VILLAGE. That part of all streams, lakes, ponds, marshes,
watercourses, waterways, wells, open drainage systems, storm sewers and all
other bodies or accumulations of water, surface and underground, natural or
artificial, which are within the jurisdiction of the village, except those
private waters which do not combine or effect a junction with natural surface
or underground waters.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-1)
§ 91.002 AIR AND WATER POLLUTION CONTROL BOARD.
   (A)   Board established; qualifications. There is hereby established an Air
and Water Pollution Control Board, which Board shall consist of seven members,
all of whom shall be residents of the village.
   (B)   Appointment, terms, vacancies in office. The Village President, with
the advice and consent of the Board of Trustees, shall appoint two members for
a term of one year, three members for a term of two years and the remaining two
members for a term of three years, of which one member shall be appointed
Chairperson. Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired term of any member
whose place has become vacant in the manner herein provided for the appointment
of such member.
   (C)   Quorum. Four members shall constitute a quorum.
   (D)   Powers and duties. A majority of the Board is hereby vested the
following jurisdiction and authority:
      (1)   To administer this subchapter;
      (2)   To investigate or cause to be investigated such complaints about
air or water pollution in the village that are filed with the village;
      (3)   To set up procedure for prompt notification of all persons
concerning whom reports of violations of this subchapter have been received by
the village;
      (4)   To arrange for and conduct hearings on the receipt of official
reports of violations of the provisions of this subchapter and on receipt of
citizens’ complaints or on petitions of any persons;
      (5)   To have power to recommend to the Village Board to cause legal
action in the name of the village to be taken by the Village Attorney to abate
nuisances or to enjoin owners or operators from continuing violations of the
provisions of this subchapter or perpetrating nuisances;
      (6)   To appoint a Secretary of the Board to routinely process smoke and
nuisance reports, to record the Board proceedings and actions and to maintain
records of the Board;
      (7)   To make a study of the types and kinds of air pollution and water
pollution present in the village; and
      (8)   To recommend to the President and Board of Trustees provisions
relative to the control of all emissions of air and water contaminants for
inclusion on a comprehensive air and water pollution control ordinance which
would regulate those air and water contaminants that are of such quantities and
of such characteristics and duration as to be injurious to human, plant or
animal life or to property or which unreasonably interfere with the enjoyment
of life and property.
   (E)   Compensation. Members of the Board shall receive such compensation as
may be fixed from time to time by the corporate authorities of the village.
   (F)   Technical advisory staff. The Village President, with the advice and
consent of the village’s Board of Trustees, shall appoint to a technical
advisory staff, persons who shall be by profession chemists, engineers, medical
doctors or persons knowledgeable in the fields of air and water pollution, to
advise and assist the Board on technical, scientific and other matters.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-2) (Ord. 97-314, passed 1-21-1997)
§ 91.003 EMISSIONS PROHIBITED.
   (A)   General. No person shall cause or allow to be emitted into the open
air any foreign materials such as dusts, gases, fumes, mists, vapors, smokes
and odors in quantities which, by reason of their objectionable properties,
shall be considered a nuisance because they:
      (1)   Injure or have a harmful effect upon the health and safety of any
person or the public;
      (2)   Create a disagreeable odor in the atmosphere;
      (3)   Cause damage to property; and/or
      (4)   Have a deleterious effect upon trees, plants or other forms of
vegetation.
   (B)   Emissions from operation of equipment.
      (1)   No person shall operate or cause to be operated, maintain or cause
to be maintained, any equipment or device which by its operation will cause the
emission of dusts, gases, fumes, mists, vapors, smokes and odors without
maintaining and operating efficiently while using such equipment or device.
Such equipment means, methods, devices or contrivances to reduce the quantity
of dusts, gases, fumes, mists, vapors, smokes and odors emitted into the open
air, and which is operated in conjunction with said equipment or device so that
the quantity of dusts, gases, fumes, mists, vapors, smokes and odors emitted
into the open air shall not violate the above provisions.
      (2)   Application of the provisions of this division (B) to specific
cases shall take into account the number of boilers or other fuel burning
devices connected to a given stack or chimney because the emission from a given
stack or chimney is a function of the number of units connected to it.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-3-1) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.004 OPEN FIRES.
   No paper, wood or other combustible waste, refuse, garbage, leaves, trees or
any other materials shall be burned in any open fire, except upon an
application for an issuance of a permit by the Control Board. At least three
hours prior to the time of starting any such fire pursuant to a permit so
issued, the holder of such permit shall notify the Fire Department of the
village of his or her intention to start such an open fire at a designated
time.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-3-2) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.005 PARTICULATE MATTER; PREVENTING ESCAPE.
   (A)   No person shall permit the handling, transporting, depositing or
storage of any material in a manner which may allow unreasonable amounts of a
particulate matter to become airborne.
   (B)   No person shall permit the use, construction, repair or demolition of
any structure, site or open area without applying such reasonable measures as
may be necessary to prevent particulate matter from becoming airborne
including, but not limited to, paving or frequent cleaning of roads, driveways
and parking lots, application of dust-free surfacing, application of water and
the planting and maintenance of vegetative ground cover.
   (C)   No person shall perform sandblasting operations, blowing on fire-
proofing over steel building members, tuck-pointing, building cleaning and
similar operations without adequate means for preventing particulate matter
from become airborne. ADEQUATE MEANS may include, but are not limited to, wet
process of sandblasting, temporary enclosures and the like and the immediate
cleanup of the materials that have fallen to the ground, floor, platform or
other surface.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-3-3) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.006 ODOR NUISANCE.
   No person shall unreasonably permit the emission of any substance into the
ambient air which causes an objectionable odor so as to cause discomfort or
endanger the public health or welfare, or in such manner as to cause injury or
damage to business or property; and such air pollution is hereby found and
declared to be and shall constitute a public nuisance.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-3-4) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.007 CIRCUMVENTION.
   (A)   No person shall build, erect, alter, install or use any article,
equipment or other process, the purpose of which is to dilute or conceal an
emission without resulting in a reduction in the total release of air
contaminants into the atmosphere.
   (B)   This restriction shall not apply to the dilution of odors.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-3-5) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.008 WATER POLLUTION CONTROL.
   (A)   Nuisance declared. It shall be unlawful for any person to permit the
placing or discharge of any substance in any location which causes or may tend
to cause pollution of the waters of the village, and such water pollution is
hereby found and declared to be, and shall constitute a public nuisance.
   (B)   Storage of materials in enclosures. No person shall place, store or
hold any liquid or solid material in any existing or new impoundment such as a
reservoir, dike or other enclosure which causes or tends to cause pollution of
the waters of the village if the material escaped therefrom, without first
having obtained the approval of the Board for said enclosure.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-4) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.009 EQUIPMENT MALFUNCTION.
   (A)   Emissions exceeding any of the limitations established in this
subchapter which are directly caused by unusual conditions or malfunctions or
shutdown of any process, fuel burning, refuse burning or pollution control
system, or the shutdown of such equipment for scheduled maintenance, shall not
be deemed in violation of this subchapter if the Board Chairperson finds that
the circumstances of the particular situation warrant the exemption and that
the violation was unforeseeable and unavoidable and not caused by the
negligence of the person responsible therefor and the following requirements
are met.
      (1)   Notice of such occurrence, in the case of any malfunction of
equipment, shall be given to the Board Chairperson immediately by telephone,
telegraph or by messenger, and confirmed in writing on the next business day.
      (2)   The person responsible for the equipment or source shall use every
reasonable effort to abate the pollution without undue delay and shall notify
the Board Chairperson forthwith when this has been accomplished.
      (3)   If a shutdown of any equipment which is directly related to a
source of pollution is required for scheduled maintenance, the intent to shut
down shall be reported to the Board Chairperson at least 24 hours prior to the
shutdown, and maximum efforts, including off-shift labor, have been used to
accomplish such maintenance during periods of curtailed operations; and then,
only when it would be impossible to shut down the source operation during the
maintenance period.
      (4)   The person responsible for such pollution shall submit a full
written report of such occurrence to the Board Chairperson as soon as
practical, including a statement of all known causes and the actions which such
person proposes to take to minimize or eliminate future occurrences. Within 14
days after receipt of such report, the Board Chairperson shall approve or
disapprove the proposed abatement program and shall state his or her reasons
therefor, and grant or deny the exception herein provided. The Board
Chairperson may require that standby equipment be installed or that the entire
process be shut down while the equipment causing the malfunction is being
repaired or otherwise cured. Failure to submit a report or failure to comply
with any condition upon which the Board Chairperson approves a report shall be
a separate violation of this subchapter and, thereafter, said person shall not
be entitled to the relief afforded herein without the approval of the Board
Chairperson.
   (B)   (1)   If said emission causes an accumulation or deposit of material
or other damage or undesirable condition on public property, then the person
responsible shall immediately cure said condition and shall pay for damage
caused thereby.
      (2)   Should such person fail to comply with the written demand of the
Board Chairperson to accomplish the foregoing, the Board Chairperson may take
such measures as are reasonable and necessary to cure the condition, subject to
the approval of the Village President and the Board of Trustees, and all
necessary expenses incurred thereby shall be assessed against the property and
the person in charge of the operation and may be recovered by the village in
appropriate civil proceedings before a court of competent jurisdiction.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-5) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.010 INSPECTIONS, TESTS AND ANALYSES.
   (A)   Entry powers. The Board Chairperson or any other member of the Board
may enter at any reasonable time, with reasonable notice, into or upon any
private or public property, except the administrative offices of any person,
for the purpose of inspection and investigation of any condition or equipment
which the Board Chairperson shall have reasonable cause to believe to be
causing pollution in violation of this subchapter.
   (B)   Records inspected. The Board Chairperson or other members of the Board
may inspect at any reasonable time and in a reasonable manner, with reasonable
notice, any record relating to the use of equipment or control apparatus which
may effect the emission of air or water contaminants, or record relating to the
use of fuel, or the distribution, storage or transportation of fuel.
      (1)   Tests and analyses. During the course of an inspection, if the
Board Chairperson or other member of the Board obtains a sample of contaminant,
fuel, process material or other material which may effect the emission of
contaminants, he or she shall give the person in charge a receipt for the
sample obtained, if requested to do so prior to leaving the premises.
      (2)   Samples. If samples of air or water contaminants are taken for
analysis, a duplicate of the analytical report shall be furnished upon request
to the person in charge.
   (C)   Photographs. If photographs are taken on private property, said
photographs must be offered for inspection to the person in charge, and the
Board Chairperson shall cooperate in providing copies of said photographs at
the expense of the person requesting them.
   (D)   Consultants during inspections. If the Board Chairperson believes that
a consultant is needed to accompany him, her or other member of the Board in
making an inspection or assisting in conducting test(s), the person in charge
is to be given advance notice thereof.
   (E)   Interference with inspections prohibited. No person shall refuse
entry, nor obstruct, delay, prevent or in any way interfere with the Board
Chairperson or other member of the Board while carrying out an inspection, or
in the performance of their duties.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-6) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.011 CONFIDENTIALITY OF RECORDS.
   (A)   Any records or other information furnished to or obtained by the Board
Chairperson or his or her Board members concerning air or water equipment
sources which are certified in writing by the owner to be confidential because
it relates to production sales or process unique to the owner, shall be used
only in the administration of this subchapter and shall not be published or
made available to the public by the agency or the Appeals Board.
   (B)   All such information shall be considered as confidential and shall not
be disclosed in any manner without the prior written consent of the person
responsible.
   (C)   Nothing herein shall be construed to prevent the use of such
information by the Board Chairperson in compiling or publishing analyses or
summaries relating to the general condition of the outdoor atmosphere or of the
waters of the village; provided that, such analyses or summaries do not
identify any owner or reveal any information otherwise confidential under this
section.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-7)
CLEAN INDOOR AIR
§ 91.025 OTHER FIRE RESTRICTIONS.
   Nothing in this subchapter overrides any existing elimination of smoking
that is already covered by Fire Code restrictions.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007)
§ 91.026 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ARCADE. A public place of amusement, as defined in Title XI of this code of
ordinances, which contains four or more automatic amusement devises and is not
licensed to serve alcoholic liquor.
   BAR/TAVERN. An establishment that is subject to a license for the sale of
alcoholic liquor for consumption on the premises and that derives 65% or more
of its gross proceeds from the sale of alcoholic liquor. Each BAR/TAVERN shall
provide such documentation as may be requested by the Department of Business
Affairs and Licensing and Revenue to enable those departments to determine
whether the establishment meets the percentage requirement of this definition.
   BUSINESS. Any sole proprietorship, partnership, joint venture, corporation,
limited liability company or other business entity formed for profit-making
purposes, including, without limitation, retail establishments where goods or
services are sold as well as professional corporations and other entities where
legal, medical, dental, engineering, architectural or other professional
services are delivered.
   EMPLOYEE. Any person who is employed by an employer in consideration for
direct or indirect monetary wages or profit, and a person who volunteers his or
her services for a non-profit entity.
   EMPLOYER. Any person, business, partnership, association, corporation,
including without limitation a municipal corporation, trust or non-profit
entity that employs the services of one or more individual persons.
   ENCLOSED AREA. All space between a floor and a ceiling, that is enclosed or
semi-enclosed with:
      (1)   Solid walls or windows (exclusive of doorways); or
      (2)   Solid walls with half-wall petitions and no windows (exclusive of
doorways) which extend from the floor to the ceiling, without limitation to
lobbies and corridors.
   ENCLOSED OR SEMI-ENCLOSED SPORTS ARENA OR RECREATIONAL AREA. Any sports
pavilion, stadium, gymnasium, health spa, boxing arena, swimming pool, roller
and ice rink, bowling alley and other similar places where members of the
general public assemble either to engage in physical exercise, or participate
in athletic competition or recreational activity, to witness sports, cultural,
recreational or other events.
   HEALTH CARE FACILITY. Any office or institution providing medical care or
treatment of diseases, whether physical, mental or emotional, or other medical,
physiological or psychological conditions, including without limitation
hospitals, clinics, homes for the aging or chronically ill, laboratories and
offices of surgeons, chiropractors, physical therapists, physicians, dentists
and all specialists within these professions. The definition shall include all
waiting rooms, hallways, private rooms, semi-private rooms and wards within
health care facilities.
   PLACE OF EMPLOYMENT. Any enclosed area under the control of a public or
private employer that employees frequent during the course of employment,
including without limitation work areas, employee lounges, restrooms,
conference rooms, classrooms, employee cafeterias, hallways and vehicles. A
private residence is not a PLACE OF EMPLOYMENT unless it is used as a
childcare, adult day care or health care facility or home-based business of any
kind open to the public.
   PUBLIC PLACE. Any enclosed area to which the public is invited or in which
the public is permitted, including without limitation banks, educational
facilities, government buildings, health care facilities, laundromats, museums,
public transportation facilities, reception areas, restaurants, bars/taverns,
retail food production and marketing establishments, retail service
establishments, retail stores, shopping malls, sports arenas, theaters and
waiting rooms. A private residence is a not a PUBLIC PLACE unless it is used as
a childcare, adult day care, health care facility or home-based business of any
kind open to the public.
   PRIVATE FUNCTION. A gathering of persons for the purpose of deliberation,
education, instruction, entertainment, amusement or dining where membership or
specific invitation is a prerequisite to entry and where the event is not
intended to be open to the public.
   RESTAURANT. Any retail food establishment, as that term is defined in §
120.40 of this code of ordinances and that derives less than 65% of its gross
proceeds from the sale of alcoholic liquor. The term RESTAURANT shall include,
if applicable, a restaurant bar area. Each RESTAURANT shall provide such
documentation as may be requested by the Department of Business Affairs and
Licensing and Revenue to enable those departments to determine whether the
establishment meets the percentage requirements of this definition.
   RESTAURANT BAR AREA. An area of a restaurant that is primarily devoted to
the serving of alcoholic liquor.
   RETAIL TOBACCO STORE. Any retail store utilized primarily for the sale of
tobacco products and accessories and in which the sale of other products is
merely incidental and where no one under 18 is permitted.
   SERVICE LINE. Any indoor line at which one or more persons are waiting for
or receiving services of any kind, whether or not the service involves the
exchange of money.
   SHOPPING MALL. Any enclosed walkway or hall area that serves to connect
retail or professional establishments.
   SMOKING. Inhaling, exhaling, burning or carrying any lighted cigar,
cigarette, pipe, weed, hookah or other lighted tobacco product in any manner or
in any form.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007)
§ 91.027 SMOKING IN VILLAGE FACILITIES.
   (A)   Prohibition.
      (1)   Smoking in village facilities. Smoking by inhaling, exhaling,
burning or carrying any lighted cigarette, cigar, pipe or other lighted tobacco
product in any other form (“smoking”) is not permitted in any areas of any
village facility, including, without limitation, those village facilities
housing administrative offices, courthouses, detention facilities or jails.
This ban on smoking applies to all public areas of village facilities as well
as all areas used only by village employees or officials, including without
limitation individual offices.
      (2)   Smoking in village vehicles. Smoking is prohibited in all vehicles
owned or leased by the village.
   (B)   Reasonable distance. Smoking is prohibited within 15 feet of an
enclosed area of any village facility so as to prohibit congestion at exits
that could constitute a fire hazard in the event of an emergency evacuation of
the village facility. However, if the village operates village facilities
within buildings owned by third parties and the village’s use in those
buildings is not exclusive, this division (B) shall apply only insofar as it
restricts the conduct of village employees.
   (C)   Implementation. All appropriate village representatives and all
elected officials shall implement the foregoing policy.
   (D)   Effect of section.
      (1)   This section supersedes and replaces any and all earlier
resolutions and ordinances pertaining to the subject of a smoking policy for
village facilities. It is intended for this section to apply to village
facilities.
      (2)   However, to the extent that any provision of this section is less
restrictive in regulating smoking than another ordinance, the more restrictive
provision shall apply.
      (3)   This section shall take effect immediately upon passage.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.028 SMOKING IN PUBLIC PLACES.
   Smoking shall be prohibited in all enclosed public places and places of
employment within the village, including, without limitation, the following
places:
   (A)   Arcades, if persons under the age of 18 are permitted entrance;
   (B)   Aquariums, galleries, libraries and museums;
   (C)   Convention facilities;
   (D)   Facilities primarily used for exhibiting a motion picture, stage,
drama, lecture, musical recital or other similar performance;
   (E)   Health care facilities and adult care facilities;
   (F)   Day care centers, nursery schools, elementary schools, high schools,
community colleges, technical training establishments, specialty schools,
colleges and universities;
   (G)   Lobbies, hallways and other common areas in apartment buildings,
condominiums and enclosed common areas in trailer parks;
   (H)   Polling places;
   (I)   Public transportation facilities under the authority of government
agencies, including without limitation, buses, trains, taxicabs and limousines,
and ticket, boarding and waiting areas of public transit stations;
   (J)   Restrooms, lobbies, reception areas, hallways and other enclosed
common-use areas;
   (K)   Public elevators and all retail stores where merchandise is displayed
and offered for sale;
   (L)   Rooms, chambers, places of meeting or public assembly, including
without limitation school buildings, under the control of an agency, board,
commission, committee or council of the village or a political subdivision of
the state, to the extent the place is subject to the jurisdiction of the
village;
   (M)   Service lines;
   (N)   Shopping malls;
   (O)   Sports arenas or recreational areas, including, without limitation,
enclosed places in outdoor arenas;
   (P)   Public meetings;
   (Q)   Gymnasiums;
   (R)   Government vehicles used for village business such as maintenance
trucks or fleet vehicles; and
   (S)   Public and private school buildings.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.029 REASONABLE DISTANCE.
   Smoking is prohibited within 15 feet of any entrance to an enclosed area in
which smoking is prohibited.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.030 WHERE SMOKING IS NOT REGULATED.
   Notwithstanding any other provision of this subchapter to the contrary, the
following areas shall be exempt from the provisions of §§
91.027 through
91.034 of this chapter:
   (A)   Private residences, except when used as a licensed childcare, adult
care facility, health care facility or home-based business of any kind open to
the public;
   (B)   Hotel and motel sleeping rooms that are rented to guests and are
designated as smoking rooms; provided, however, that, not more than 25% of the
rooms rented to guests in a hotel or motel may be so designated;
   (C)   Retail tobacco stores; provided that, smoke from these places does not
infiltrate into areas where smoking is prohibited under the provisions of §§
91.028 and
91.029 of this chapter;
   (D)   Private clubs, lodges, fraternities, societies and/or orders;
   (E)   Bar/tavern;
   (F)   Restaurant or restaurant bar area;
   (G)   Grocery stores;
   (H)   Bingo facilities;
   (I)   Bowling alleys; and
   (J)   Any public place or place of employment otherwise subject to this
subchapter whose owner or operator can demonstrate, to the satisfaction of the
village’s public health officials, Fire Inspector and environmental officials
that such area has been equipped with air filtration or purification devices or
similar technologies as to render the exposure to secondhand smoke in such
area, notwithstanding the fact that smoking may be occurring in such area,
equivalent to such exposure to secondhand smoke in the ambient outdoor air
surrounding the establishment. The village’s public health and environmental
officials are jointly authorized to promulgate regulations specifying what
types of technologies, when and if available, and taking into account any
applicable federal and/or state standards, satisfy the requirements of this
division (J).
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007)
§ 91.031 DECLARATION OF ESTABLISHMENT AS NON-SMOKING.
   Notwithstanding any other provision of this subchapter, an owner, operator,
manager or other person in control of an establishment, facility or outdoor
area may declare that entire establishment as a non-smoking place.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007)
§ 91.032 POSTING OF SIGNS.
   (A)   Every public place and place of employment where smoking is prohibited
by this subchapter shall have posted at every entrance a conspicuous sign
clearly stating that smoking is prohibited.
   (B)   The operator, manager or other person having control of an area where
smoking is prohibited by this subchapter shall remove all ashtrays and other
smoking paraphernalia intended for use where smoking is prohibited.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.033 NON-RETALIATION.
   No person or employer shall discharge, refuse to hire, or in any manner
retaliate against an employee, applicant for employment or customer because
that employee, applicant or customer exercises any rights afforded by this
subchapter or reports or attempts to prosecute a violation of this subchapter.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007) Penalty, see §
91.999
§ 91.034 ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   Any law enforcement agency and certified local public health official
(department) with jurisdiction shall be authorized to enforce this subchapter
within its jurisdiction.
   (B)   Any citizen who desires to register a complaint under this subchapter
may file a complaint with the village’s Fire Inspector.
   (C)   The village’s public health and environmental officials, Fire
Inspector and environmental officials, or their designees, shall, while an
establishment is undergoing other public health inspections, inspect for
compliance with this subchapter.
   (D)   Any owner, manager, operator or employee of an establishment regulated
by this subchapter shall inform persons violating this subchapter of the
appropriate provisions thereof.
   (E)   In addition to the remedies provided by the provisions of this
subchapter, the applicable certified local Health Department or any person
aggrieved by the failure of the owner, operator, manager of other person in
control of a public place or a place of employment to comply with the
provisions of this subchapter may apply for injunctive relief to enforce these
provisions in any court of competent jurisdiction.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007)
§ 91.035 OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS.
   This subchapter shall not be interpreted or be construed to permit smoking
where it is otherwise restricted by other applicable laws.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007)
§ 91.036 APPLICABILITY.
   This subchapter shall apply to all areas within the village, except those
areas which are governed by an ordinance of another governmental entity (which
by law may not be superseded by this subchapter).
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007)
§ 91.037 AMENDMENTS.
   This subchapter may be amended at any time by a majority vote of the members
of the Board of Trustees.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007)
§ 91.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   Any person convicted of violating any of the provisions of §§
91.001 through
91.011 of this chapter or any rule or regulation of the Control Board shall be
fined according to §
10.99 of this code of ordinances, and each day of such violation shall
constitute a separate offense.
      (2)   All persons owning, operating or in charge or control of any
equipment who shall permit any violation of §§
91.001 through
91.011 of this chapter shall be individually and collectively liable for any
penalties imposed by §§
91.001 through
91.011 of this chapter.
      (3)   The village may, in addition to the prosecutions hereinabove
authorized, maintain any other legal or equitable action for the abatement of
pollution.
      (4)   The imposition of a penalty or restriction in §§
91.001 through
91.011 of this chapter shall not be construed to abridge or otherwise impair
the right of any person to maintain any action or take other appropriate
measures to obtain damages or other relief on account of injuries to persons or
property.
(Prior Code, § 4-5-8)
   (C)   (1)   A person who smokes in an area where smoking is prohibited by §§
91.027 through
91.033 of this chapter shall be guilty of an infraction, punishable by a fine
not more than $100.
      (2)   A person who owns, manages, operates or otherwise controls a public
place or place of employment and who fails to comply with the provisions of §§
91.027 through
91.033 of this chapter shall be guilty of an infraction, punishable by:
         (a)   A fine not exceeding $100 for the first violation;
         (b)   A fine not more than $500 for the second violation within one
year of the first violation; and
         (c)   A fine not more than $2,500 for each additional violation within
one year and a 60-day suspension or revocation of any permit or license issued
to the person for the premises on which the violation occurred.
      (3)   Each day on which a violation of §§
91.027 through
91.033 of this chapter occurs shall be considered a separate and distinct
violation.
(Ord. 07-387, passed 3-19-2007)

CHAPTER 93: PARADES AND OPEN AIR MEETINGS
Section
   
93.001   Definitions
   
93.002   Permit required; exceptions
   
93.003   Permit application
   
93.004   Permit fee
   
93.005   Bond requirements
   
93.006   Permit issuance; notice to officials
   
93.007   Permit rejection; alternate permit
   
93.008   Permit contents
   
93.009   Conflicting permit applications
   
93.010   Permit conditions
   
93.011   Public conduct
   
93.012   Permit revocation
 
   
93.999   Penalty
§ 93.001 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions apply unless the
context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   OPEN AIR MEETING. Any congregation of citizens held outdoors and upon any
public property for the purpose of hearing speakers or discussing some matter
of common interest where the number of participants expected may reasonably be
assumed to exceed 50.
   PARADE. Any parade, march, ceremony, show, exhibition, pageant or procession
of any kind, or any similar display, in or upon any street, park or other
public place in the village.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-1)
§ 93.002 PERMIT REQUIRED; EXCEPTIONS.
   (A)   No person shall participate in a parade or open air meeting held on
any public way or on any public property unless a written permit therefor shall
first be obtained from the President and Board of Trustees.
   (B)   This chapter shall not apply to:
      (1)   Funeral processions;
      (2)   Students going to and from school classes or participating in
educational activities, providing such conduct is under the immediate direction
and supervision of the proper school authorities; or
      (3)   A governmental agency acting within the scope of its functions.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-2) Penalty, see §
93.999
§ 93.003 PERMIT APPLICATION.
   (A)   An application to conduct a parade or open air meeting shall be made
in writing to the President and Board of Trustees by a representative of the
group seeking a permit. The application shall be filed with the Village Clerk
not less than 21 days before, who shall transmit a copy of the application to
the President and each Trustee. The President and Board of Trustees shall act
on the application at the first regular Board meeting after receipt of the
application or at any special meeting prior to said regular meeting.
   (B)   The application shall set forth the following information:
      (1)   The name, address and telephone number of the person seeking to
conduct such parade or open air meeting;
      (2)   If the parade or open air meeting is proposed to be conducted for,
on behalf of or by an organization, the name, address and telephone number of
the headquarters of the organization, and of the authorized and responsible
heads of such organization;
      (3)   The name, address and telephone number of the person who will be
the parade chairperson or chairperson of the open air meeting;
      (4)   The date when the parade or open air meeting is to be conducted;
      (5)   The route to be traveled, the starting point, the termination point
and the location of speakers’ platforms;
      (6)   The approximate number of persons who, and animals and vehicles
which, will constitute such parade or open air meeting; the type of animals;
and description of the vehicles;
      (7)   The hours when such parade or open air meeting will start and
terminate;
      (8)   A statement as to whether the parade will occupy all or only a
portion of the width of the streets proposed to be traversed;
      (9)   The location by streets of any assembly areas for such parade or
open air meeting;
      (10)   The time at which units of the parade will begin to assemble at
any such assembly area or areas;
      (11)   If the parade or open air meeting is designed to be held by, and
on behalf of or for, any person other than the applicant, the applicant for
such permit shall file a communication in writing from the person proposing to
hold the parade or open air meeting authorizing the applicant to apply for the
permit on his or her behalf;
      (12)   The name and address of a resident of the village who will act as
additional sponsor for said parade or open air meeting and who will be
responsible for the application fee and bond; and
      (13)   An agreement to pay for additional expenses incurred by the
village by reason of the issuance of said permit.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-3)
§ 93.004 PERMIT FEE.
   The fee for a parade or open air meeting permit shall be $100. This fee
shall be paid after approval by the President and Board of Trustees of the
issuance of said permit. In the case of hardship or other good cause shown, the
President and Board of Trustees may waive the permit fee.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-4)
§ 93.005 BOND REQUIREMENTS.
   There shall also be filed at the time the applicant secures his or her
parade or open air meeting permit, a bond in the sum of $1,000 to be executed
by two responsible citizens, one of whom shall be a resident of the village,
indemnifying the village for the additional costs and expenses incurred in
supplying additional police, fire and other municipal services for the parade
or open air meeting. In lieu of the individual bond, a bond from an insurance
company authorized to do business in the state may be supplied. The applicant
and surety shall agree to pay the additional costs and expenses of the village
incurred by reason of the issuance of the parade or open air meeting permit
within 30 days of receipt of the itemization of expenses from the village.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-5)
§ 93.006 PERMIT ISSUANCE; NOTICE TO OFFICIALS.
   (A)   The President and Board of Trustees shall issue a permit as provided
for hereunder when, from a consideration of the application and from such other
information as may otherwise be obtained, they find that:
      (1)   The conduct of the parade will not substantially interrupt the safe
and orderly movement of other traffic contiguous to its route;
      (2)   The conduct of the parade or open air meeting will not require the
diversion of so great a number of police officers of the village to properly
police the line of movement and the areas contiguous thereto as to prevent
normal police protection to the village;
      (3)   The conduct of such parade or open air meeting will not require the
diversion of so great a number of ambulances as to prevent normal ambulance
service to portions of the village other than that to be occupied by the
proposed line of march and areas contiguous thereto;
      (4)   The concentration of persons, animals and vehicles at the open air
meeting or assembly points of the parade will not unduly interfere with proper
fire and police protection of, or ambulance service to, areas contiguous to
such assembly areas;
      (5)   The conduct of such parade or open air meeting will not interfere
with the movement of firefighting equipment en route to a fire;
      (6)   The conduct of the parade or open air meeting is not reasonably
likely to cause injury to persons or property, to provoke disorderly conduct or
create a disturbance;
      (7)   The parade is scheduled to move from its point of origin to its
point of termination expeditiously and without unreasonable delays en route;
      (8)   The parade or open air meeting is not to be held for the sole
purpose of advertising any products, goods or event, and is not designed to be
held purely for private profit;
      (9)   The march, assembly, meeting or gathering is to be in not more than
one specific area of or location in the village on any given day;
      (10)   The march, assembly, meeting or gathering is limited to such
numbers as in the opinion of the President and Board of Trustees will not
obstruct pedestrian or vehicular traffic in an unreasonable manner. The permit
issued shall state the number of persons who may participate in the parade or
open air meeting if issued; and
      (11)   The parade is not to be held during any peak traffic period, as
defined in §
93.010 of this chapter.
   (B)   Immediately upon the issuance of a parade or open air meeting permit,
the Chief of Police shall send a copy thereof to the following:
      (1)   Village President;
      (2)   Village Attorney;
      (3)   Fire Chief;
      (4)   Superintendent of the Department of Public Works;
      (5)   Postmaster; and
      (6)   General manager or responsible head of each public transportation
utility, the regular routes of whose vehicles will be affected by the route of
the proposed parade.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-6)
§ 93.007 PERMIT REJECTION; ALTERNATE PERMIT.
   (A)   The President and Board of Trustees may disapprove the application
and, if disapproved, notice shall be mailed to the applicant stating the
reasons for the denial of the permit.
   (B)   The President and Board of Trustees, in denying an application for a
parade or open air meeting, shall be empowered to authorize the conduct of the
parade or open air meeting on a date, at a time or over a route or a place
different from that named by the applicant. An applicant desiring to accept an
alternate permit shall, within five days after notice of the action of the
President and Board of Trustees, file a written notice of acceptance with the
Village Clerk who shall immediately notify the President, each Trustee and the
Chief of Police of such acceptance. An alternate parade or open air meeting
permit shall conform to the requirements of, and shall have the effect of a
parade or open air meeting permit under this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-7)
§ 93.008 PERMIT CONTENTS.
   (A)   Parade permit. Each parade permit shall state the following
information:
      (1)   Starting time;
      (2)   Minimum speed;
      (3)   Maximum speed;
      (4)   Maximum interval of space to be maintained between the units of the
parade;
      (5)   The portions of the streets to be traversed that may be occupied by
the parade;
      (6)   The maximum length of the parade in miles or fractions thereof; and
      (7)   Such other information as the Chief of Police shall find necessary
to the enforcement of this chapter.
   (B)   Open air meeting permit. Each open air meeting permit shall state the
following:
      (1)   Starting time;
      (2)   Termination time;
      (3)   Place of meeting;
      (4)   Maximum number of persons authorized to attend; and
      (5)   Such other information as the Chief of Police shall find necessary
to the enforcement of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-8)
§ 93.009 CONFLICTING PERMIT APPLICATIONS.
   (A)   If the President and Board of Trustees shall receive more than one
application for a parade or open air meeting at the same time and the same
place, or on the same day, the application filed first in time shall take
precedence.
      (1)   An application shall be considered to be “at the same time” if the
event is scheduled to commence within two hours before or after the holding of
another event.
      (2)   An application shall be considered to be “at the same place” if the
requested parade route comes at any point within six blocks or any equivalent
distance from the route of another parade or if the open air meeting be
conducted within one-half mile of another open air meeting.
   (B)   If the President and Board of Trustees receives an application for
more than one parade or open air meeting in a single day, they may set a time
for the duration of each parade or open air meeting which time shall not,
without the consent of the group seeking the permit, be less than three hours.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-9)
§ 93.010 PERMIT CONDITIONS.
   (A)   Compliance with provisions. A permittee hereunder shall comply with
all permit directions and conditions and with all applicable laws and
ordinances.
   (B)   Possession of permit. The parade or open air meeting chairperson or
other person heading or leading such activity shall carry the permit upon his
or her person during the conduct of the parade or open air meeting.
   (C)   Hours parades or open air meetings to be conducted.
      (1)   Parades. All parades shall be held during daylight hours at times
other than peak traffic periods, Monday through Saturday, and not before 12:00
noon on Sundays.
      (2)   Open air meetings. All open air meetings shall conclude by 11:00
p.m. and shall not be held before 12:00 noon on Sunday.
   (D)   Peak traffic periods. Peak traffic periods for the purpose of this
section shall be 7:30 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.
   (E)   Exemption. The time limitation shall not apply on state or national
holidays.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-10) Penalty, see §
93.999
§ 93.011 PUBLIC CONDUCT.
   (A)   Interference. No person shall unreasonably hamper, obstruct or impede,
or interfere with any parade or parade assembly or with any person, vehicle or
animal participating or used in a parade or with any person in an open air
meeting.
   (B)   Driving through parades. No driver of a vehicle shall drive between
the vehicles or persons comprising a parade when such vehicles or persons are
in motion and are conspicuously designated as a parade.
   (C)   Parking on parade route. The Chief of Police shall have the authority
when reasonably necessary to prohibit or restrict the parking of vehicles along
a highway or part thereof constituting a part of the route of a parade. The
Chief of Police shall post signs to such effect, and it shall be unlawful for
any person to park or leave unattended any vehicle in violation thereof. No
person shall be liable for parking on a street unposted in violation of this
chapter.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-11) Penalty, see §
93.999
§ 93.012 PERMIT REVOCATION.
   The Chief of Police shall have the authority to revoke a parade or open air
meeting permit issued hereunder upon application of the standards for issuance
as herein set forth.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-12)
§ 93.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person who violates this chapter shall be fined not to exceed $500
for each offense.
   (B)   The violation of this chapter is hereby declared to be a public
nuisance to be abated in the manner provided by law.
(Prior Code, § 5-8-13)
CHAPTER 94: PUBLIC LIBRARY
Section
   
94.001   Use of library
   
94.002   Damage to library property
   
94.003   Library Fund
 
   
94.999   Penalty
§ 94.001 USE OF LIBRARY.
   The Dolton Public Library shall be free to the use of the inhabitants of the
village, subject to such reasonable rules and regulations as the village’s
Board of Trustees may adopt in order to render the use of the library of the
greatest benefit to the greatest number.
(Prior Code, § 7-3-1)
§ 94.002 DAMAGE TO LIBRARY PROPERTY.
   Any person who shall willfully or maliciously cut, write upon, injure,
deface, tear or destroy any book, newspaper, plate, picture, engraving or other
thing of value belonging to the Dolton Public Library, or shall willfully or
maliciously commit any injury upon the grounds, building, furniture, fixtures
or other property thereof, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and fined.
(Prior Code, § 7-3-2) Penalty, see §
94.999
§ 94.003 LIBRARY FUND.
   (A)   Custodian of Fund. The Village Treasurer shall be the custodian of the
Library Fund. The bond he or she executes as Village Treasurer shall be
conditioned for the faithful performance of his or her duty as Treasurer of the
Library Fund.
   (B)   Library tax; proceeds. The corporate authorities shall levy a tax for
library purposes of not to exceed 0.12% of the full, fair cash value of all the
taxable property in the village, as equalized or assessed by the Department of
Revenue. The library taxes provided for herein are in addition to all other
taxes or tax rates authorized to be levied and shall not be a part of the taxes
making up any rate prescribed as a limitation on the amount of taxes the
village may levy. The library taxes provided for in this division (B) shall be
levied and collected in like manner with other general taxes of the village and
the proceeds shall be deposited on a special fund which shall be known as the
Library Fund. The proceeds of any such tax shall be paid over to the Board of
Library Directors.
   (C)   Expenditures from Fund. Expenditures from the Library Fund shall be
under the direction of the Board of Library Directors.
(Prior Code, § 7-3-3)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 95.001 SMOKING.
   (A)   Smoking prohibited. Smoking, or the carrying of a lighted cigar, pipe
or cigarette is prohibited:
      (1)   In any retail store which has in its employ five or more full-time
employees engaged in work at the same time on the premises, except for areas
designated as smoking areas and except for areas set apart for serving food or
beverage, waiting and rest rooms, executive offices and rooms and areas where
merchandise is not exposed;
      (2)   In every theater, church, school or garage, except in rooms
designated as smoking rooms or smoking areas; and
      (3)   In every building or premises where the combustible nature and
quantity of contents are, in the opinion of the Chief of the Fire Department,
hazardous to life and property from fire.
   (B)   Smoking receptacles. All smoking rooms or smoking areas as permitted
in premises designated in division (A)(1) and (A)(2) above shall be provided
with smoking stands, ashtrays or sand jars and shall be cleaned daily and kept
in a sanitary condition at all times.
   (C)   No smoking signs. “NO SMOKING” signs shall be conspicuously posted in
every room, building or premises where smoking is prohibited. The words “NO
SMOKING” on a sign shall be in letters of at least one inch in size in a color
which shall be in contrast to the background color of said sign.
(Prior Code, § 4-3-1) Penalty, see §
95.999
§ 95.002 CLAY HOLES AND EXCAVATIONS TO BE FENCED.
   The owner, lessee or person in possession of any real estate within the
village upon which are located or situated any clay holes or other similar
excavations is hereby required to cause such clay holes or excavations to be
enclosed with wooden or wire fences of not less than six feet in height. When
such fences are of wire, only smooth or non-barbed wire shall be used below a
height of six feet above the established grade or about the ground where no
grade has been established, and such fence or fences shall consist of not less
than eight rows of wire, and such rows of wire shall not be more than nine
inches apart.
(Prior Code, § 4-3-2) Penalty, see §
95.999
NUISANCES GENERALLY
§ 95.015 COMMON LAW NUISANCES.
   In all cases where no provision is made defining what are nuisances and how
the same may be removed, abated or prevented, in addition to what may be
declared such herein, those offenses which are known to be the common law of
the land, the statutes of the state and other ordinances of the village may, in
case the same exists within the village limits, be treated as such and
proceeded against as provided in this subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 4-4-1)
§ 95.016 NUISANCES DEFINED.
   Whatever is dangerous to human health or renders ground, water, air or food
dangerous or injurious to human health, and the following specific acts,
conditions and things, each and all of them are hereby declared to constitute
nuisances:
   (A)   Offensive substances.
      (1)   The deposit or accumulation of any foul, decaying or putrescent
substance, or other offensive matter, in or upon any private or public place;
      (2)   The storage of any foul, decaying or putrescent matter in liquid or
solid form in any vault, cesspool or other receptacle; and/or
      (3)   The overflow of any foul liquid or the escape of any gases to such
an extent that the same shall become or be likely to become hazardous to health
or shall, by reason of offensive odors, become a source of discomfort to
persons living in or passing by the vicinity thereof.
   (B)   Animal carcasses; offal.
      (1)   To cause or suffer the carcass of any animal or any offal, filth or
noisome substance to be collected, deposited or to remain in any place to the
prejudice of others; and/or
      (2)   To throw or deposit any offal or other offensive matter, or the
carcass of any dead animal, in any watercourse, lake, pond, spring, well,
common sewer or public place.
   (C)   Water pollution. To corrupt or render unwholesome or impure the water
of any spring, river, stream, pond or lake to the injury or prejudice of
others;
   (D)   Obstructions and encroachments. To obstruct or encroach upon public
highways, private ways, streets, alleys, commons, landing places and ways to
burying places;
   (E)   Offensive businesses. To erect, continue or use any building or other
place for the exercise of any trade, employment or manufacture which by
occasioning noxious exhalations, offensive smells or otherwise, is offensive or
dangerous to the health of individuals or to the public;
   (F)   Unauthorized advertising. To advertise wares or occupation by painting
notices of the same on, or affixing them to fences or other private property,
or on rocks or other natural objects without the consent of the owner, or if on
the highway or other public place, without permission of the corporate
authorities;
   (G)   Improper building construction.
      (1)   A building or a portion of a building occupied as a dwelling which
is not lighted and ventilated by means of at least one window in each room,
said room opening to the outer air;
      (2)   A building, or dwelling unit in said building, which is not
provided with a plentiful supply of pure water; and/or
      (3)   A building, or dwelling unit in said building, which is not
provided with one sink for each family, said sink to be connected to the
sewerage system or a properly constructed cesspool if no sewer main is
available.
   (H)   Stagnant ponds. The accumulation of water in which mosquito larvae may
breed;
   (I)   Spitting in public. It shall be unlawful to spit or expectorate in or
on any public place, or in or on the premises of any store, theater, hall,
public vehicle or other place frequented by the public or to which the public
is invited;
   (J)   Improper fill.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful to fill any lot, parcel or piece of property
with garbage.
      (2)   Property which is filled with stones, concrete or other similar
material, excluding soil, shall be leveled and covered with a minimum of three
inches of soil.
      (3)   This division (J) shall not apply to the village garbage dump.
   (K)   Basketball playing in residential districts and planned senior/elderly
family dwelling districts. It shall be unlawful to engage in playing basketball
within residential districts and planned senior/elderly family dwelling
districts between the hours of 8:00 p.m. and 10:00 a.m.; and
   (L)   Portable basketball hoop.
      (1)   It is unlawful to use portable basketball hoops unless:
         (a)   Said portable basketball hoops are being used on private
property;
         (b)   The portable basketball hoops when in use are situated at least
20 feet from the public right-of-way; and
         (c)   The name and address of owner is permanently affixed to said
portable basketball hoops.
      (2)   (a)   It shall be unlawful to use portable basketball hoops on
public property, in public ways, public streets, rights-of-way or alleyways at
any time.
         (b)   A basketball hoop located within the public right-of-way shall
be presumed to have been placed with the knowledge and consent of the owner of
the abutting private property.
         (c)   Damage to the basketball hoop which occurs during the lawful,
non-negligent use of the public right-of-way shall be the responsibility of the
hoop owner.
         (d)   The village shall not be liable for any damage to the basketball
hoop or other property resulting from the non-negligent removal of the
basketball hoop when a basketball hoop has been removed due to a nuisance
condition.
      (3)   (a)   Portable basketball hoops which are found in the village on
public property, in public ways, public streets, rights-of-way or alleyways,
streets and rights-of-way and which items do not have identification as to
ownership of those items, shall be considered abandoned and subject to removal
by the Police Department and/or the Public Works Department.
         (b)   Abandoned portable basketball hoops (personal property)
confiscated by the village may be redeemed by the rightful owner upon payment
of a fee of $100. Said fee calculated to cover the village’s cost in removing
and storing the item. The village’s Police Department may issue citations for
violations of the provisions of this division (L) to the previously
unidentified owner of the portable basketball hoop at the time the owner seeks
to redeem the property, including, but not limited to, the failure to
permanently affix the name and address of the owner to said portable basketball
hoop. Any citizen or owner who desires to contest whether the item of personal
property was properly removed as abandoned property, may file a request for a
hearing with the village’s Police Department. Said hearing shall be held within
21 days of the request for a hearing.
      (4)   The village shall choose an officer or employee of the village to
serve as Hearing Officer (in no case shall that Hearing Officer be an
individual who was involved in the initial decision or removal of the portable
basketball hoop). The hearing shall be informal in nature, and the rules of
evidence shall not apply. The hearing will not be determinative of, or
adjudicate, any citation relative to any vehicle. After receiving all relevant
evidence, the Hearing Officer shall make a written decision based upon a
preponderance of the evidence as to whether the portable basketball hoop was
properly removed as abandoned property. The owner shall be provided a copy of
such hearing decision.
   (M)   Outdoor cooking in certain areas. It shall be unlawful for any person
to barbeque, grill or engage in any similar outdoor cooking activities in the
front yard, on the public sidewalk or in the front parkway of any residential
property.
(Prior Code, § 4-4-2) (Ord. 97-352, passed 12-15-1997; Ord. 06-362, passed 7-
17-2006; Ord. 17-019, passed 7-21-2017; Ord. 17-022, passed 8-3-2017) Penalty,
see §
95.999
§ 95.017 NUISANCES PROHIBITED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to permit or maintain the existence of
any nuisance in fact on any property under the control of said person, whether
such nuisance is specifically recognized by this subchapter or not.
(Prior Code, § 4-4-3) Penalty, see §
95.999
§ 95.018 NOTICE TO ABATE.
   (A)   When a nuisance is created, or in fact exists, notice of same shall be
given to the person who created or caused such nuisance.
   (B)   If such person is unknown, then notice shall be given to the person
occupying the land where said nuisance is located.
   (C)   Notice shall also be given to the person who is listed as the person
who is obligated to pay the general taxes on said property as disclosed by the
tax rolls in the County Collector’s office.
   (D)   (1)   The notice shall be in writing and delivered in person to the
person entitled to notice or sent by registered or certified mail.
      (2)   The notice shall contain a description of the nuisance location and
shall direct that the nuisance be abated within five days after the delivery of
said notice.
   (E)   If said nuisance is not abated within five days, then the Chief of
Police or the Building Commissioner may take the necessary step to abate the
nuisance.
(Prior Code, § 4-4-4)
§ 95.019 ABATEMENT BY VILLAGE.
   (A)   The Chief of Police and the Building Commissioner are hereby
authorized to abate any such nuisance after notice as provided above.
   (B)   In the event of any imminent danger to the health and safety of the
village and its citizens, the nuisance may be abated summarily by the Chief of
Police or the Building Commissioner.
(Prior Code, § 4-4-5)
PLANTS AND WEEDS
§ 95.030 NUISANCE DECLARED.
   Any weeds such as jimson, burdock, ragweed, thistle, cocklebur or other
weeds of a like kind found growing in any lot or tract of land in the village
are hereby declared to be a nuisance, and it shall be unlawful to permit any
such weeds to grow or remain in any such place.
(Prior Code, § 4-10-1) Penalty, see §
95.999
§ 95.031 HEIGHT RESTRICTIONS.
   It shall be unlawful for anyone to permit any weeds, plants or grass, other
than trees, bushes, flowers or other ornamental plants, to grow to a height
exceeding eight inches anywhere in the village; and such plants or weeds
exceeding such height are hereby declared to be a nuisance.
(Prior Code, § 4-10-2) Penalty, see §
95.999
§ 95.032 REMOVAL NOTICE.
   It shall be the duty of the Superintendent of Public Works to serve or cause
to be served a notice upon the owner or occupant of premises on which weeds or
plants are permitted to grow in violation of the provisions of this subchapter
and to demand the abatement of the nuisance within ten days.
(Prior Code, § 4-10-3)
§ 95.033 ABATEMENT; COSTS TO OWNER.
   If the person so served does not abate the nuisance within five days after
such notice, the Foreperson of the village may proceed to abate such nuisance,
keeping an account of the expense of the abatement and such expenses shall be
charged to and paid by such owner or occupant. After the abatement of the
nuisance provided for above, the Superintendent of Public Works shall notify
the owner of same by causing notice to be served upon the owner. Such notice
shall also inform the owner that the subject property shall thereafter be
placed upon a regularly scheduled maintenance program to ensure the continued
abatement of such nuisance and further informing the owner that such abatement
shall continue until the owner arranges to abate the nuisance by other means.
All costs for this maintenance schedule shall be assessed to the owner of the
premises and shall be a lien thereon.
(Prior Code, § 4-10-4) (Ord. 11-548, passed 12-19-2011)
§ 95.034 WEED CUTTING LIEN.
   (A)   Charges for weed cutting shall be a lien upon the premises as provided
by statute. Whenever a bill for weed cutting remains unpaid 60 days after it
has been rendered, the Village Clerk may file with the county’s Recorder of
Deeds a statement of lien claim. This statement shall contain the legal
description of the premises served, the amount of the unpaid bill, and a notice
that the village claims a lien for this amount. Notice of the bill for weed
cutting shall be mailed to the owner of the premises whenever such bill remains
unpaid for a period of 60 days after it has been rendered.
   (B)   The failure of the Village Clerk to record such lien claim or to mail
such notice or the failure of the owner to receive such notice shall not affect
the right to foreclose the lien for unpaid bills for weed cutting as provided
for in §
95.035 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 4-10-5)
§ 95.035 FORECLOSURE OF LIEN.
   (A)   Property subject to a lien for unpaid weed cutting charges shall be
sold for non-payment of the same and the proceeds of such sale shall be applied
to pay the charges, after deducting costs, as is the case in the foreclosure of
statutory liens.
   (B)   Such foreclosure shall be by bill in equity in the name of the
village.
   (C)   The Village Attorney is hereby authorized and directed to institute
such proceedings in the name of the village in any court having jurisdiction
over such matters against any property for which a bill for weed cutting has
remained unpaid 60 days after it has been rendered.
(Prior Code, § 4-10-6)

CHAPTER 96: SECURITY AND FIRE ALARM SYSTEMS
Section
   
96.001   Definitions
   
96.002   Permit requirement
   
96.003   General requirements and prohibitions
   
96.004   Service charges for false alarms
   
96.005   Suspension of alarm permits and disconnection of alarm systems
   
96.006   Limitation of village’s responsibility
   
96.007   Exemption of village buildings
 
   
96.999   Penalty
§ 96.001 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions apply unless the
context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ALARM SUBSCRIBER. The owner, tenant or other agents of the property where an
alarm system is installed.
   ALARM SYSTEM. Any equipment or device initiating a request for emergency
response.
   CENTRAL STATION. An independent alarm monitoring location which is regulated
by the state which relays requests for emergency response to the Police or Fire
Departments.
   FALSE ALARM. An activation of an alarm system due to mechanical failure,
malfunction, improper installation, improper operation or negligence of an
alarm subscriber which causes an alarm signal to be received and responded to
by either the Police or Fire Departments, other than a non-controllable alarm.
   LOCAL ALARM. Any alarm system that activates an audible or visual display
without transmitting the alarm to a central station or to the Police or Fire
Departments.
   NON-CONTROLLABLE ALARM. An activation of alarm system caused by adverse
weather conditions, telephone line problems or any other events over which the
alarm company and its subscribers have no control.
(Ord. 90-133, passed 10-16-1990)
§ 96.002 PERMIT REQUIREMENT.
   (A)   All alarm systems operating within the village must have an annual
alarm permit issued by the village.
   (B)   Application for initial, alarm permit shall be on the form prescribed
by the Chief of Police and Billing Department and shall include all information
deemed necessary for the administration of this chapter. A $25 processing fee
will be charged for the initial permit; a $10 annual renewal fee shall be
payable every May 1 thereafter. The annual renewal fee shall be waived for any
alarm subscriber upon presentation of a valid village business license paid for
the current year.
   (C)   Upon initial application, the proposed alarm system shall be inspected
by the Building Department and Electrical Inspector. In addition, to the alarm
permit fee, the applicant shall be responsible for any electrical inspection
permit fees.
   (D)   All properties in the village, which have alarm systems as of the
effective date of this chapter, shall have 180 days from the effective date
hereof within which to obtain inspection of their alarm systems.
   (E)   A new permit shall be required upon a change of owner or tenant of the
property within which the alarm system has been installed.
   (F)   Any change to the information listed on the original application for
alarm permit shall be reported in writing to the Police Department within five
working days.
(Ord. 90-133, passed 10-16-1990)
§ 96.003 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS AND PROHIBITIONS.
   (A)   All alarm system equipment must be approved by a nationally recognized
testing or certifying laboratory or agency.
   (B)   All alarm systems may be connected to a central station or, in the
case of commercial or bank alarms, may be connected directly to the Police
Department alarm board, or else they may function as a local alarm. Any alarm
system having an outside ringer, siren, buzzer or similar noise-making device
or any visual signal, either of which is designed to be detected by the public
outside of the structure where the alarm is installed, must be equipped with an
automatic shut-off device which will cause the alarm to shut off no later than
15 minutes after it activates. This restriction shall not apply to fire alarm
systems.
   (C)   No alarm system utilizing, signaling devices that automatically select
a telephone line of the Police or Fire Departments, and then reproduce any pre-
recorded message which initiates a request for emergency response from the
Police or Fire Departments, shall be permitted.
   (D)   No alarm system may utilize the emergency 9-1-1 telephone lines into
the Police and Fire Departments.
   (E)   No alarm shall be manually activated for reasons other than a robbery
or burglary in progress or having just occurred, a medical or fire emergency or
circumstances indicating a likelihood of death or great bodily harm.
(Ord. 90-133, passed 10-16-1990) Penalty, see §
96.999
§ 96.004 SERVICE CHARGES FOR FALSE ALARMS.
   (A)   Each alarm system shall be allowed three false alarms in the first
month after installation or upgrading without the levy of a service charge.
Thereafter, each alarm system will be allowed one false alarm per calendar
quarter without service charge.
   (B)   The owner of any system registering false alarms in excess of the
allowances listed above shall be assessed a $50 service fee payable to the
village.
(Ord. 90-133, passed 10-16-1990)
§ 96.005 SUSPENSION OF ALARM PERMITS AND DISCONNECTION OF ALARM SYSTEMS.
   (A)   The following constitute grounds for suspension of alarm permits:
      (1)   More than three false alarms in any calendar quarter;
      (2)   Installation, maintenance or operation of an alarm system in
violation of this chapter or any term or condition of the owner’s alarm permit;
      (3)   False information on the permit application; and/or
      (4)   Failure to pay alarm service charges assessed under the terms of
this chapter.
   (B)   (1)   When either the Chief of Police or the Chief of the Fire
Department determines that there are reasonable grounds for revocation of an
alarm permit, the Chief will have a notice of intent to revoke said permit sent
to the alarm subscriber via certified mail. The notice will include the
specific grounds for the intended revocation and will allow seven days to
correct the problem.
      (2)   If no corrective action has been taken by the alarm subscriber at
the end of the seven-day period, the Police or Fire Chief shall revoke the
alarm permit, and so notify the owner.
      (3)   Following the notice of revocation of an alarm permit, any
subscriber shall be entitled to request a hearing before a committee designated
by the Village President. Such committee may be comprised of the members of the
Police or Fire Committees of the Board of Trustees along with such other
members as the President deems appropriate. At such hearing, the subscriber may
present evidence and, upon conclusion of the presentations, the committee shall
sustain, reverse or modify the determination of the Fire or Police Chief. The
committee determination shall be final and binding on all parties.
   (C)   Upon revocation of an alarm permit, the alarm subscriber will
disconnect the alarm system within 24 hours after receipt of a written notice,
via certified mall, of revocation. Any alarm remaining operational after this
24-hour period would be deemed to be prima facie evidence of a violation of
this chapter and the permit holder subject to the penalties described in §
96.999 of this chapter.
(Ord. 90-133, passed 10-16-1990) Penalty, see §
96.999
§ 96.006 LIMITATION OF VILLAGE’S RESPONSIBILITY.
   Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as imposing any obligation or
responsibility on the village with respect to the functioning of any alarm
system. Nothing herein shall be construed as imposing on the village any
obligation to provide any particular level of police or fire protection service
to the owner of a system beyond that which the village provides for all of its
citizens.
(Ord. 90-133, passed 10-16-1990)
§ 96.007 EXEMPTION OF VILLAGE BUILDINGS.
   All buildings, locations and other installations owned or operated by the
municipal authorities of the village and equipped with security or fire alarm
systems shall be exempt from the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 90-133, passed 10-16-1990)
§ 96.999 PENALTY.
   Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall, upon
conviction thereof, be subject to a fine in accordance with the provisions of §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
(Ord. 90-133, passed 10-16-1990)
CHAPTER 97: LEAD-BEARING SUBSTANCES
