§ 97.001 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions apply unless the
context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CHILD CARE FACILITY. Any structure used by a child care provider, school or
other facility frequented by children.
   CHILDREN. Persons six years of age and younger.
   DEPARTMENT. The Village of Dolton Department of Housing.
   DWELLING. Any structure all or part of which is designed or used for human
habitation.
   EXPOSED SURFACE. Any interior or exterior surface of a child care facility,
school, dwelling or residential building.
   HOUSING DIRECTOR. The Village of Dolton Director of Housing or an
appropriate designee.
   LEAD HAZARD. A lead-bearing substance that poses a significant health hazard
to humans.
   LEAD POISONING. The condition of having blood lead levels in excess of those
considered safe under applicable regulations promulgated by the Housing
Director.
   LEAD-BEARING SUBSTANCE. Any dust on any surface or in furniture or other
non-permanent elements of the dwelling, child care facility or school and any
paint or other surface coating material containing more than the lead by weight
as established by state law or regulation, and/or that the Housing Director
determines, by regulation, may pose a significant health hazard to humans.
   OWNER. Any person, who alone, jointly or severally with others:
      (1)   Has legal title to or a beneficial interest in a land trust or
other entity having legal title to a child care facility, school, dwelling or
residential building with or without accompanying actual possession of the
child care facility, school, dwelling or residential building, and includes any
agent of the owner, or as executor, administrator, trustee or guardian of the
estate of the owner;
      (2)   Has charge, care or control of or responsibility for a child care
facility, school, dwelling or residential building; or
      (3)   Has an interest as a purchaser under a real estate installment
contract in a child care facility, dwelling or residential building.
   PERSON. Any one or more natural persons, legal entities, governmental bodies
or combination thereof.
   RESIDENTIAL BUILDING. Any room, group of rooms or other interior areas of a
structure designed or used for human habitation; common areas accessible by
inhabitants; and the surrounding property or structures.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)
§ 97.002 LEAD-BEARING SUBSTANCE USE.
   No person shall use or apply lead-bearing substances:
   (A)   In or upon any exposed surface of a dwelling or dwelling unit;
   (B)   In or around the exposed surfaces of a residential building, child
care facility, school or other structure frequented by children;
   (C)   In or upon any fixtures or other objects used, installed or located in
or upon any exposed surface of a dwelling or residential building, child care
facility, school or intended to be so used, installed or located and that, in
the ordinary course of use, are accessible to and chewable by children;
   (D)   In or upon any toys, furniture or other articles used by and chewable
by children; and/or
   (E)   Within or upon a residential building or dwelling, child care
facility, school, playground, park or recreational area, or other areas
regularly frequented by children.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004) Penalty, see §
97.999
§ 97.003 MAINTENANCE OF RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS.
   It is the duty of every owner of a residential building to maintain the
residential building in such a manner so as to prevent the existence of a lead
hazard.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004) Penalty, see §
97.999
§ 97.004 TOYS OR FURNITURE CONTAINING LEAD-BEARING SUBSTANCE; SALE.
   (A)   No person shall knowingly sell, have, offer for sale or transfer any
toy or furniture that contains a lead-bearing substance and that, in the
ordinary course of use, is accessible to and chewable by children.
   (B)   This section shall not apply to antique furniture and toys.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004) Penalty, see §
97.999
§ 97.005 OBJECTS CONTAINING LEAD-BEARING SUBSTANCE; SALE.
   No person shall sell or transfer or offer for sale or transfer any fixtures
or other objects intended to be used, installed or located in or upon any
surface of a dwelling or residential building, child care facility or school
that contains a lead-bearing substance and that, in the ordinary course of use,
are accessible to and chewable by children.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004) Penalty, see §
97.999
§ 97.006 WARNING STATEMENT.
   No person, firm or corporation shall have, offer for sale, sell or give away
any lead bearing substance that may be used by the general public unless it
bears the warning statement as prescribed by state law (410 ILCS 45/6) or
federal regulation, as follows:
 
Warning statement.
 
No person, firm or corporation shall have, offer for sale, sell or give away any lead
bearing substance that may be used by the general public unless it bears the warning
statement as prescribed by federal regulation. If no regulation is prescribed the
warning statement shall be as follows: “WARNING - CONTAINS LEAD. DRIED FILM OF THIS
SUBSTANCE MAY BE HARMFUL IF EATEN OR CHEWED. See other cautions on (side or back)
panel. Do not apply on toys, or other children’s articles, furniture or interior, or
exterior exposed surfaces of any residential building or facility that may be occupied
or used by children. KEEP OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN.”
 
(a)   The generic term of a product, such as “paint” may be substituted for the word
“substance” in the above labeling.
 
(b)   The placement, conspicuousness and contrast of the above labeling shall be in
accordance with § 191.101 of the regulations promulgated under the provisions of the
Federal Hazardous Substances Act (15 U.S.C. §§ 1261 et seq.).
 
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004) Penalty, see §
97.999
§ 97.007 CHILD CARE FACILITIES; BLOOD LEAD LEVEL SCREENING FOR ADMISSION.
   (A)   (1)   Each day care center, day care home, preschool, nursery school,
kindergarten or other child care facility licensed or approved by the state,
including such programs operated by a public school district, shall include a
requirement that each parent or legal guardian of a child between the ages of
six months through six years provide a statement from a physician or health
care provider that the child has been screened for lead poisoning.
      (2)   This statement must indicate that the screening of the child has
been performed in accordance with applicable criteria mandated by the state’s
Department of Health and/or the Housing Director. This statement shall be
provided prior to admission and subsequently in conjunction with required
physical examinations.
   (B)   Nothing in this section shall be construed to require any child to
undergo a blood lead level screening or test whose parent or guardian objects
on the grounds that the screening or test conflicts with his or her religious
beliefs.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004) Penalty, see §
97.999
§ 97.008 FEES.
   (A)   The Housing Department may establish fees according to a reasonable
fee structure to cover the cost of inspections and providing a testing service
for laboratory analysis of blood lead tests and any necessary follow-up.
   (B)   The Housing Director may promulgate rules and regulations for waiving
applicable fees for low-income persons.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)
§ 97.009 INSPECTION OF BUILDINGS.
   (A)   (1)   An authorized representative of the village charged with
enforcement of this chapter, upon presentation of the appropriate credentials
to the owner, occupant or his or her representative, may inspect child care
facilities, schools, dwellings and residential buildings at reasonable times,
for the purposes of ascertaining that all surfaces accessible to children are
intact and in good repair, and for purposes of ascertaining the existence of
lead-bearing substances. Such representative may remove samples or objects
necessary for laboratory analysis.
      (2)   If a person entitled to withhold consent to an inspection refuses
to allow inspection, a representative of the prosecuting attorney of the
village may apply for a warrant to permit entry.
   (B)   Annual rental inspections, annual business in sections of childcare
facilities, single- and multiple-family unit turn over inspections, and
inspections upon transfer of ownership, shall include a lead-based paint
inspection of the premises, and no water stamp or occupancy (rental and sale)
permit shall issue unless or until a determination has been made by the Housing
Director that no lead hazards exist and or existing lead-based hazards have
been abated.
   (C)   No work permit shall be issued for rehabilitation of single- and
multiple-family units and/or child care facilities unless a lead-based paint
inspection has been conducted, and a plan for lead abatement has been filed
with and approved by the Housing Department/Building Department (as
applicable), if any.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)
§ 97.010 PROCEDURES UPON DETERMINATION OF LEAD-BEARING SUBSTANCE.
   (A)   Upon determination that there is a lead-bearing substance in or upon
any child care facility, school, dwelling or residential building which could
reasonably be hazardous to children, or upon receipt of confirmation that an
individual has a level of lead in his or her blood indicative of lead
poisoning, the village shall, as soon as is practicable, give appropriate
notice to the owner of a child care facility, school, dwelling or dwelling
unit, of the existence and location of a lead hazard.
   (B)   In addition, regardless of whether there has been compliance with the
preceding sentence, the village shall take action as needed to enforce this
chapter, including, as the village or its authorized representative may
determine is appropriate:
      (1)   Providing the owner and occupants with suitable recommendations for
elimination of the problem areas;
      (2)   Notifying the other persons or entities with responsibility for a
child care facility, school, dwelling or dwelling unit of the existence and
location of such substances;
      (3)   Ordering that these substances shall be removed, replaced or
securely and permanently covered within a specified time period and in a manner
prescribed by the Department; and/or
      (4)   Pursuing the remedies provided for in §§
97.013 and
97.014 of this chapter.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)
§ 97.011 MANNER OF ABATEMENT OF LEAD HAZARDS.
   The removal of the lead-bearing substance from the dwelling, residential
building, child care facility or school shall be accomplished in a manner
consistent with all rules and regulations promulgated pursuant to this chapter
concerning acceptable and safe methods of lead hazard removal or abatement, and
in a manner which will not endanger the health or well-being of its occupants,
and will result in the safe removal from the premises, and the safe disposition
of flakes, chips, debris, dust and other potentially harmful materials.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)
§ 97.012 RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The Housing Department, in conjunction with the Building Inspector, is
authorized to promulgate reasonable rules and regulations for carrying out the
provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)
§ 97.013 EMERGENCY MEASURES.
   (A)   (1)   When the Housing Director finds that because of a violation of
this chapter, an emergency condition exists requiring immediate action to
protect the health of any person, the Housing Director may issue an emergency
order reciting the existence of the emergency condition and requiring that
necessary actions be taken to meet the emergency.
      (2)   (a)   An emergency order shall be effective immediately, and any
person to whom an emergency order is directed shall comply therewith within the
period of time specified in the order.
         (b)   Any such person shall receive a reasonably prompt notice of his
or her right to a prompt hearing conducted by an administrative law officer of
the Buildings Hearings Division of the Department of Administrative Hearings,
pursuant to the procedures established for such hearings.
      (3)   Pending the hearing, the Housing Director may take whatever steps
are necessary to execute the emergency order when necessary to protect the
health of any person.
   (B)   The entire cost of abatement and relocation actions taken or caused to
be taken by the village, pursuant to this section, shall be recoverable from
each of the persons of the persons responsible for correcting the violations or
giving rise to the emergency conditions by bringing an action in a court of
competent jurisdiction or pursuant to other applicable law.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)
§ 97.014 REMEDIES.
   (A)   The prosecuting attorney for the village may seek relief with respect
to any violation of this chapter by filing an appropriate action in a court of
competent jurisdiction or the Department of Administrative Hearings seeking
equitable relief or the penalties contained in §
97.999 of this chapter, or both.
   (B)   Upon determining that any person has not complied with an order
authorized pursuant to this chapter, the Housing Director/Building Inspector
shall issue a ticket and cause such person to appear for a hearing before the
appropriate court/administrative proceedings.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)
§ 97.015 ENFORCEMENT.
   Any department of the village may take appropriate action to enforce any of
the provisions of this chapter when a violation of any of the provisions comes
to its attention.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)
§ 97.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Violation of any section of this chapter and any failure to comply
with any order authorized pursuant to this chapter shall be punishable by
incarceration not to exceed six months and by a fine not less than $200, nor
more than $500, for each offense.
   (B)   Each day that such violation or non-compliance exists shall be
considered a separate offense.
(Ord. 04-272, passed 10-18-2004)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 110.001 PURPOSE AND JURISDICTION.
   Because each commercial, mercantile or industrial establishment located
within the limits of the village is a basic part of, and affects the physical
and economic well-being of the village which necessitates special services from
the village in the form of fire, health and police inspections and services,
and because the health and safety of residents who visit or attend such
commercial, mercantile or industrial establishments may be affected, and
because the health and safety of employees who are employed in these
establishments are affected, it is desirable and necessary that inspections of
these establishments be made in order to ensure full compliance with the
ordinances of the village and the statutes of the state relating to fire,
health, safety and building. This title is deemed to be regulatory in nature
and is designed to provide the means whereby the necessary inspections and
services may be made in order that the public health, safety and welfare of the
residents of the village may be effectively protected and to enable and effect
an accurate record of commercial, mercantile and factory establishments located
within the village.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-1)
§ 110.002 COMPLIANCE WITH STATE AND VILLAGE REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Each licensee shall be required to comply with each and all of the
ordinances of the village and of the statutes of the state and such licensee
shall certify to this in his or her application.
   (B)   No license for the operation of a commercial, mercantile or industrial
establishment shall be issued unless and until the following is determined:
      (1)   The building or premises of the commercial, mercantile or
industrial establishment complies with the provisions and terms of the Building
Code and ordinances relating to buildings;
      (2)   The buying or premises of the commercial, mercantile or industrial
establishment complies with the provisions and terms of the zoning ordinances;
      (3)   The building or premises of the commercial, mercantile or
industrial establishment complies with the fire ordinances and fire
regulations;
      (4)   The building or premises of the commercial, mercantile or
industrial establishment complies with the health ordinances and regulations;
      (5)   The applicant and/or his or her agent are of good business and
moral character;
      (6)   There is proper sanitation and ventilation of all mercantile
establishments where the public is invited so that they may be guarded against
personal injuries and disease;
      (7)   There is proper sanitation and ventilation of all places of
employment to guard against personal injuries and disease;
      (8)   There is proper arrangement and guarding of machinery and the
storing and placing of personal property to guard against personal injuries and
diseases to employees;
      (9)   There is proper preventive action to eliminate and reduce the
danger of personal injuries and diseases to the consumer public as well as to
employees by contact with any poisonous or deleterious materials, dust, vapors,
gases or fumes;
      (10)   All buildings are drained and plumbed in a manner conducive to
healthful and proper sanitary conditions;
      (11)   Adequate exits are provided and maintained;
      (12)   Suitable and proper sanitary washrooms are provided and
maintained;
      (13)   There is an adequate quantity of soap containing bland non-
irritating detergents which effectively can cleanse the skin where appropriate;
      (14)   There is an adequate supply of safe, clean and potable water
satisfactory for drinking purposes dispensed where appropriate and necessary;
      (15)   There is an adequate supply of safe, clean, hot and cold water
where appropriate and necessary;
      (16)   Adequate toilet facilities, properly enclosed are provided; and
      (17)   The premises are sufficiently heated during cold weather.
   (C)   Failure of any officer or employee to make such investigation or to
make a complete and proper investigation shall not be a basis for liability
against said employee or officer or against the village by a person for any
damage or injury since the obligation for compliance with all laws and
regulations rests upon the licensee.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-2)
§ 110.003 ENFORCEMENT.
   It shall be the duty of the President to enforce this title and to cause
visits and inspections to be made during reasonable hours and as often as
practicable of factories, mercantile establishments, mills, workshops and all
other industrial and commercial establishments in the village where goods,
wares or merchandise are manufactured and stored or purchased or sold at
wholesale or retail.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-3)
§ 110.004 APPLICATIONS FOR LICENSES AND PERMITS.
   Applications for all licenses and permits shall be made in writing on forms
to be prescribed and furnished by the Village Board and shall be submitted to
the office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services, unless express
provision to the contrary is made. All such applications shall state thereon
the name and address of the owner or owners and the street and number location
of the business to be licensed. A new application shall be necessary to renew
any license at its expiration. The office of Comptroller and Revenue
Administrative Services shall keep a record of all applications.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-4) (Ord. 02-189, passed 7-23-2002; Ord. 03-214, passed 4-21-
2003)
§ 110.005 INDEBTEDNESS TO THE VILLAGE.
   (A)   For the purpose of this section, the following definitions apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      DEBT. A specific indebtedness, whether known to the village or unknown,
owed to the village or for which the period granted for payment has expired,
including, but not limited to, any and all license fees, permit fees, water tax
fees and any and all other obligations, known or unknown, which are required to
be paid to the village, pursuant to the rules and regulations of municipal code
of the village.
      LICENSE FEE/PERMIT FEE. Those fees required to be paid under any and all
provisions of the municipal code of the village.
      OUTSTANDING PARKING VIOLATION COMPLAINT. A parking ticket, notice of
parking violation or parking violation complaint on which no payment has been
made or appearance filed in the Circuit Court of the county within the time
specified on the complaint.
      UNKNOWN OBLIGATIONS. Those obligations due the village, knowledge of
which is solely in the possession of the debtor/obligor.
      WATER TAX FEE. Those sums of money due pursuant to the provisions of the
municipal code of the village for water and sewer service.
   (B)   Every person applying for a license or permit shall file an affidavit
with the Village Clerk, or other appropriate village official, disclosing any
and all debts owed by the applicant to the village and any outstanding parking
violation complaints issued to any vehicle, owned by the applicant. (A copy of
said affidavit is attached to the ordinance codified herein and made a part
hereof.)
   (C)   No license or permit shall be issued to any person, corporate entity
or other business activity indebted to the village or has acquired any
outstanding parking violation complaints, unless and until such person,
corporate entity or other business activity pays to the village all
indebtedness then due from such person, corporate entity or other business and
either pays the fines for each parking violation or files an appearance with
the Circuit Court of the county to contest the parking violation alleged in
each complaint, or by authority of the village, discharges all such
indebtedness in accordance with the terms and conditions fixed by the Board of
Trustees.
   (D)   Notwithstanding the provisions of division (C) above, the village may
issue a license to a person, corporate entity or other business who owes a debt
to the village if the Village Clerk determines that:
      (1)   The applicant has entered into an agreement with the village or
other appropriate village representative, for the payment of all debts owed the
village and such applicant is in compliance with the agreement;
      (2)   The applicant is contesting liability for or the amount of debt in
a pending administrative or judicial proceedings; or
      (3)   The applicant has filed a petition in bankruptcy and the debts owed
to the village are dischargeable in bankruptcy.
(Ord. 91-158, passed 6-25-1991)
§ 110.006 BOND REQUIREMENTS.
   In case a bond is required for the issuance of any license, such bond must
be a surety company bond to be approved by the Village Attorney and must be
filed with the Village Clerk before the license is issued. The President may,
in any case, require a bond from the licensee where deemed necessary to protect
the village. Such bond shall in no event be less than the sum of $1,000.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-5)
§ 110.007 PAYMENT OF LICENSE AND PERMIT FEES; REFUNDS.
   (A)   The fees required for licenses and permits must be paid at the time
the application is made. Except as may be otherwise provided, all license fees
shall become a part of the Corporate Fund. Any new applicant who commences his
or her business or occupation after the first one-half of the fiscal year shall
pay one-half of the license fee to cover the balance of the fiscal year.
   (B)   In no event shall any rebate or refund be made of any license fee, or
part thereof, by reason of the death of the licensee, or by reason of non-use
of the license, or by reason of a change of location or occupation of such
licensee.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-6)
§ 110.008 DUPLICATE LICENSES; VEHICLE TAGS.
   (A)   Duplicate licenses. In case of the loss or destruction of any license
issued by the village, a duplicate thereof may be issued to the licensee by the
office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services upon satisfactory
evidence of such loss or destruction being filed with the office of Comptroller
and Revenue Administrative Services and the payment to the village of $1 for
such duplicate.
   (B)   Vehicle tags. Whenever the number of vehicles used is the basis of a
license fee, the office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services
shall furnish each licensee with a tag or sticker for each vehicle covered by
the license, and such tag or sticker shall be posted in a conspicuous place on
each such vehicle while it is in use.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-7) (Ord. 02-189, passed 7-23-2002; Ord. 03-214, passed 4-21-
2003)
§ 110.009 APPROVAL AND ISSUANCE OF LICENSE; SIGNATURE REQUIRED.
   Except as may otherwise be specifically provided, licenses shall be granted
and signed by the Village President and issued by the office of Comptroller and
Revenue Administrative Services. Any application may be ordered by the
President or the Village Board to be presented to and approved by such Board
before issuance or approval of the license, and the Board may overrule the
decision of the President in reference to any application for license.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-8) (Ord. 03-214, passed 4-21-2003)
§ 110.010 LICENSE TERM; NOTICE OF TERMINATION.
   (A)   All annual licenses shall terminate on the last day of the fiscal year
of the village where no provision to the contrary is made. The office of
Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services shall mail to all licensees of
the village a statement of the time of expiration of the license held by the
licensees, if an annual one, three weeks prior to the date of such expiration;
provided that, a failure to send out such notice or the failure of the licensee
to receive it shall not excuse the licensee from a failure to obtain a new
license or a renewal thereof, nor shall it be a defense in an action for
operation without a license.
   (B)   If a license is issued for a period in excess of one month, it shall
be the duty of the office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services
from ten to 20 days prior to the termination of the license period, to cause a
written notice to be mailed to each licensee, stating that the new license will
be required on the day following expiration of its existing license and stating
also the amount of the license fee and the penalty for failure to procure a
license in accordance with the provisions of the ordinances of the village
governing the issuance of such license; provided, however, that, failure on the
part of the office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services to cause
such notice to be mailed to any such licensee shall not waive the requirement
that a license be procured.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-9) (Ord. 02-189, passed 7-23-2002; Ord. 03-214, passed 4-21-
2003)
§ 110.011 TRANSFER OF LICENSE OR PERMIT; CHANGE OF LOCATION.
   (A)   No license or permit shall be transferred from one person to another.
   (B)   However, the location of any licensed business or occupation, or of
any permitted act, may be changed; provided, ten days’ notice thereof is given
to the office of Comptroller and Revenue Administrative Services in the absence
of any provision to the contrary and provided the building and zoning
requirements of the village are complied with.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-10) (Ord. 02-189, passed 7-23-2002; Ord. 03-214, passed 4-
21-2003)
§ 110.012 LICENSES TO BE POSTED.
   Every license granted for the purpose of conducting any business or
occupation required by ordinance to be licensed and which designates the
particular room, store or office, or place in which such business or license is
to be conducted shall be posted at all times in a conspicuous place so that the
same may easily be seen upon the wall of the principal room or office of the
store or place in which such licensed business or occupation is carried on;
and, when such license shall have expired, it shall be removed from such place
in which it has been posted and no license which is not in force and effect
shall be permitted to remain posted upon the wall or upon any part of any room,
store, office or place of business after the period of such license has
expired.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-11)
§ 110.013 NUISANCE BUSINESSES.
   No business shall be so conducted or operated as to amount to a nuisance in
fact.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-12) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 110.014 INSPECTIONS AND ANALYSES.
   (A)   Whenever inspections of the premises used for or in connection with
the operation of a licensed business or occupation is made, it shall be the
duty of the licensee or the person in charge of the premises to be inspected to
admit thereto for the purpose of making the inspection any officer or employee
of the village who is authorized or directed to make such inspection at any
reasonable time that admission is requested.
   (B)   Whenever an analysis of any commodity or material is reasonably
necessary to secure conformance with any ordinance provision or to detect
violations thereof, it shall be the duty of the licensee of the village whose
business is governed by such provision to give to any authorized officer or
employee of the village requesting the same, sufficient samples of such
material or commodity for such analysis upon request.
   (C)   In addition to any other penalty which may be provided, the President,
by and with the consent of the Board of Trustees, may revoke the license of any
licensed proprietor of any licensed business in the village who refuses to
permit any such officer or employee, while in the performance of his or her
duty, to make such inspection; provided that, no license shall be revoked for
such cause unless written demand is made upon the licensee or person in charge
of the premises, in the name of the village, stating that such inspection or
sample is desired at the time it is sought to make the inspection or obtain the
sample.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-13)
§ 110.015 REVOCATION OF LICENSE OR PERMIT.
   Any license or permit for a limited time may be revoked by the President and
Board of Trustees at any time during the life of such license or permit for any
violation by the licensee of the ordinance provisions relating to the license
or permit, the subject matter of the license or to the premises occupied. Such
revocation may be in addition to any fine imposed.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-14)
§ 110.016 GENERAL MERCHANDISE AND INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      EMPLOYEE. A person shall be considered an employee if he or she is
scheduled to work 20 or more hours per week and 20 or more weeks per year.
      GENERAL MERCHANDISE. Any established place of business where articles of
commerce are offered for sale at retail, such articles to include items of
hardware, auto accessories, camera supplies, clothing, drug items, small
electrical appliances, sporting goods, ceramics and to include those items
customarily sold in groceries or markets, as defined in this code. In the event
such a business establishment shall qualify as a bakery or florist, as defined
in this code, an additional fee as set forth in §
110.018(B) of this chapter shall be paid. Additional fees shall also be paid
for cigarettes, vending machines and alcoholic liquor sales as set forth in §
110.018(B) of this code or ordinances.
      INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS. Includes all manufacturing establishments,
factories, foundries, machine shops, fabricating or assembly shops, furnace
maintenance shops, paint spray shops, sheet metal shops and any place where
products or parts of products are manufactured, altered, processed or repaired.
   (B)   Licenses required. No person shall operate a general merchandise store
or an industrial establishment within the village without first having obtained
a license to do so from the Village Clerk.
   (C)   License fees. An annual license fee shall be paid by each applicant
based on the number of employees. The annual license fee for such businesses
shall be established by ordinance as set forth in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
   (D)   Additional provisions for industrial establishments.
      (1)   Sanitary and safety requirements.
         (a)   No owner, proprietor, lessee, manager or superintendent of any
industrial establishment where workers are employed for wages shall cause,
permit or allow the same or any portion of such industrial establishment to be
overcrowded or inadequate, faulty or insufficient in respect of light,
ventilation, heat or cleanliness.
         (b)   All such places shall be kept in a clean condition, free from
the effluvia of a sewer, drain or other nuisance; also free, as far as
practicable, from all gases, vapors, dust or other impurities generated by
manufacturing processes or otherwise which are injurious to health.
         (c)   Sufficient and separate water closets shall be provided for male
and female employees and such water closet compartments shall be properly
ventilated.
      (2)   Inspections. The President shall have the power to inspect or cause
to be inspected all such places of employment or service within the village as
often as he or she shall deem necessary to see that the provisions of this
section are complied with and, if such premises are found to be in an
unsanitary or unsafe condition, he or she shall require such alterations and
arrangements to be made as may be necessary for the health and safety of the
employees pursuant to the terms of this section and shall cause the Fire Chief
to direct the Bureau of Fire Prevention to see that an inspection of the
premises is made to determine whether the fire regulations of this code of
ordinances applicable thereto have been complied with, as well as other
provisions of this code of ordinances, and such laws as may be in force
concerning health and sanitary measures.
(Prior Code, § 3-1-15) (Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986)

PUBLIC SAFETY THREAT PREVENTION
§ 110.030 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly requires a different meaning.
   ACCEPTABLE NUISANCE ABATEMENT PLAN or NUISANCE ABATEMENT PLAN. Any conduct,
action, step or acceptance of conditions that is reasonably calculated to
prevent the reoccurrence of a public safety threat under this subchapter, as
agreed to by the licensee/owner and approved by the village’s Hearing Officer
in consultation with the Chief of Police. An ACCEPTABLE NUISANCE ABATEMENT PLAN
in response to any violent offenses, as defined herein, must include a security
plan with licensed aimed security guards being hired or contracted to perform
security services for the business.
   APPROPRIATE. To effect the summary closure or means of closure means a
police order, sign, lock or other barrier or device intended to seal, secure,
close or otherwise render an establishment or any pail thereof inaccessible to
a person.
   ESTABLISHMENT.
      (1)   Any premises or place of business licensed or required to be
licensed by law. The term ESTABLISHMENT includes adjacent property.
      (2)   As used in this definition, “adjacent property” means:
         (a)   Any public way located next to an establishment, if such public
way is used by the licensee/owner, patrons or employees of the establishment;
         (b)   Any private property that is located next to an establishment,
if such private property is owned, leased, rented or used by the licensee/
owner; or
         (c)   Any private property separated from an establishment by a public
way and located next to such public way, if such private property is owned,
leased, rented or used by the licensee/owner.
   ESTABLISHMENT’S OPERATING HOURS. Any time while the establishment is open
for business or within one hour or less of the time the establishment is opened
or closed for business.
   LICENSEE/OWNER. The licensee of an establishment licensed under this Code.
If an establishment is not licensed under this code, LICENSEE/OWNER means the
owner of record of the real property in or on which the establishment is
operating.
   PUBLIC SAFETY THREAT. The occurrence of all of the following:
      (1)   A violent offense occurs at an establishment during the
establishment’s operating hours;
      (2)   The violent offense involves acts of the licensee/owner, or its
employees, agents or patrons, or otherwise involves circumstances having a
nexus to the operation of the establishment; and
      (3)   The Chief of Police reasonably determines, based on data or
information in the Chief of Police’s possession, that continued operation of
the establishment presents a danger to the public.
   SUMMARY CLOSURE or SUMMARILY CLOSED. The immediate cessation of all business
activities at an establishment and closure of the establishment.
   VIOLENT OFFENSE. The illegal discharge of a firearm; the killing of a human
being by another; aggravated assault or aggravated battery; criminal sexual
assault; or any other conduct that causes a person to suffer unconsciousness,
severe bruising, severe bleeding, disability or disfigurement.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.031 UNLAWFUL ACTS.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate any establishment in a manner
that presents a public safety threat. For purposes of this subchapter, a public
safety threat is hereby declared to be a public nuisance subject to abatement
under this section. If a public safety threat occurs at an establishment, a
rebuttable presumption shall exist, for a period of six months after the date
on which the public safety threat occurred, that continued operation of the
establishment presents a danger to the public.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.032 SUMMARY CLOSURE ORDER.
   (A)   When authorized. If the Chief of Police determines that an
establishment presents a public safety threat, the Chief of Police may abate
the threat by ordering the summary closure of the establishment. Except as
otherwise provided in this section, such order shall remain in effect for an
aggregate period of six months as measured from the date on which the public
safety threat occurred; provided, however, that, any summary closure order
issued by the Chief of Police may be lifted by the Chief of Police and the
establishment shall be allowed to reopen, if:
      (1)   It is determined at a probable cause hearing or nuisance abatement
hearing that a public safety threat did not occur; or
      (2)   It is determined at a nuisance abatement hearing that continued
operation of the establishment no longer presents a danger to the public, as
may be evidenced by the submission and implementation of an acceptable nuisance
abatement plan.
   (B)   An acceptable nuisance abatement plan in response to any violent
offenses, as defined herein, must include a security plan with licensed armed
security guards being hired or contracted to perform security services for the
business; provided further that, no summary closure order shall be lifted by
the Chief of Police if the establishment is not properly licensed as required
by law.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.033 NOTICE OF SUMMARY CLOSURE; REQUIRED.
   (A)   Upon ordering the summary closure of an establishment, the Chief of
Police, or designee, shall cause a dated notice to be posted in a prominent
place on the establishment informing the licensee/owner of the following facts:
      (1)   The Chief of Police has issued an order requiring the immediate
cessation of all business activities at, and closure of, the establishment;
      (2)   The reason(s) for the summary closure;
      (3)   The licensee/owner’s right to request in writing, within three
business days after notice is posted, a probable cause hearing before the
village’s Hearing Officer to determine whether a public safety threat occurred;
      (4)   If requested in writing, a probable cause hearing shall be
commenced within three business days of receipt of such request;
      (5)   The licensee/owner’s right, at any time during the period of
closure, to seek to resume business activities at the establishment, by
requesting, in writing, a nuisance abatement hearing before the village’s
Hearing Officer to contest whether a public safety threat occurred or to rebut
the Chief of Police’s determination that continued operation of the
establishment presents a danger to the public;
      (6)   If requested in writing, a nuisance abatement hearing shall be
commenced by the village’s Hearing Officer within five business days of receipt
of such request;
      (7)   The name of the person and the address to which a written request
for each hearing should be directed;
      (8)   The consequences of not requesting a hearing; and
      (9)   The owner’s potential liability for three times the cost or expense
incurred by the village in abating a public safety threat under this section.
   (B)   (1)   If a person apparently in control of the establishment is
present at the time the notice is posted at the establishment, a copy of such
notice shall be personally served on such person at that time.
      (2)   In addition, a copy of such notice shall be mailed, by first class
mail to the licensee/owner. If the establishment identified in the notice is
licensed under this code, such copy shall be mailed to the licensee or, if
applicable, to the registered agent or other officer of the licensee, at the
licensee’s business address and, if available, at the licensee’s home address.
If the establishment identified in the notice is not licensed under this code,
such copy shall be mailed to the owner of record as listed with the Recorder of
Deeds, and to the taxpayer of record, of the real property in or on which the
establishment is operating.
      (3)   At the time the establishment is summarily closed, the Chief of
Police shall also post a sign at the establishment notifying the public of the
penalty which shall attach, as set forth in §
110.999 of this chapter, if the summary closure order is violated or if any
posted notice or means used to effect the closure is removed without
authorization.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.034 PROBABLE CAUSE HEARING.
   Within three business days after notice is posted under §
110.033 of this chapter, the licensee/owner of the establishment may request a
probable cause hearing before the village’s Hearing Officer to determine
whether a public safety threat occurred at such establishment. Such request
shall be in writing. Within three business days of receipt of a written request
for a probable cause hearing, the village’s Hearing Officer shall commence such
hearing to determine whether a public safety threat occurred. The decision and
order of the village’s Hearing Officer shall be announced no later than two
business days after the probable cause hearing is completed. If, after a
probable cause hearing, the village’s Hearing Officer determines, by a
preponderance of the evidence, that a public safety threat did occur, the
village’s Hearing Officer shall enter an order authorizing continued closure of
the establishment during the interim period prior to expiration of the
aggregate six month period. If, after the probable cause hearing, the village’s
Hearing Officer determines, by a preponderance of the evidence, that a public
safety threat did not occur, the village’s Hearing Officer shall enter an order
lifting the summary closure order and business operations at the establishment
shall be allowed to resume during the interim period prior to expiration of the
aggregate six-month period. If, after notice is given to the licensee/owner in
accordance with §
110.033 of this chapter, the licensee/owner fails to request a probable cause
hearing in a timely manner, or requests a probable cause hearing, but fails to
appear at the hearing, the village’s Hearing Officer shall enter a default
order in favor of the village authorizing continued closure of the
establishment during the interim period prior to expiration of the aggregate
six-month period. Upon entry of any order under this subsection, the village’s
Hearing Officer shall notify the Chief of Police, who shall take appropriate
steps to effect the village’s Hearing Officer’s order without delay.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.035 NUISANCE ABATEMENT HEARING.
   (A)   (1)   At any time during the interim period prior to expiration of the
aggregate six-month period, the licensee/owner may seek to have the summary
closure order lifted by the village’s Hearing Officer by:
         (a)   Requesting, in writing, a nuisance abatement hearing under this
section; and
         (b)   Showing, at such hearing, that there is reasonable cause to
believe that continued operation of the establishment no longer presents a
danger to the public, as may be evidenced by the submission and implementation
of an acceptable nuisance abatement plan.
      (2)   At such hearing, the licensee/owner may also contest whether a
public safety threat occurred at the establishment unless it was previously
determined at a probable cause hearing that such public safety threat did
occur.
   (B)   Within five business days of receipt of a written request for a
nuisance abatement hearing, the village’s Hearing Officer shall commence such
hearing. The decision and order of the village’s Hearing Officer shall be
announced no later than five business days after the nuisance abatement hearing
is completed. If, after the nuisance abatement hearing, the village’s Hearing
Officer determines, by a preponderance of the evidence, that a public safety
threat did occur and that continued operation of the establishment presents a
danger to the public, the village’s Hearing Officer shall enter an order
authorizing continued closure of the establishment during the interim period
prior to expiration of the aggregate six-month period. If, after the nuisance
abatement hearing, the village’s Hearing Officer determines, by a preponderance
of the evidence, that a public safety threat did not occur or that continued
operation of the establishment no longer presents a danger to the public, as
may be evidenced by the submission and implementation of an acceptable nuisance
abatement plan, the village’s Hearing Officer shall enter an order lifting the
summary closure order, in which case the establishment shall be allowed to
reopen prior to expiration of the aggregate six-month period.
   (C)   If, at any time after an acceptable nuisance abatement plan is
implemented at the establishment governed by such plan, the licensee/owner
fails to comply with the plan or any part thereof or another violent offense
occurs at the establishment, the Chief of Police may reinstate the summary
closure order in accordance with the notice and hearing requirements of this
section. In such case, the establishment shall remain closed for an additional
aggregate period of six months, as measured from the date that the village
acquired knowledge of the licensee’s noncompliance with the nuisance abatement
plan or any part thereof or from the date of the occurrence of another violent
offense, as applicable, unless:
      (1)   It is determined at a probable cause hearing or nuisance abatement
hearing that the licensee/owner was in full compliance with the nuisance
abatement plan and all parts thereof or that another violent offense did not
occur at the establishment, as applicable; or
      (2)   It is determined at a nuisance abatement hearing that continued
operation of the establishment does not present a danger to the public, as may
be evidenced by the submission of a modified nuisance abatement plan, approved
by the village’s Hearing Officer and implemented by the owner/licensee,
containing new or additional reasonable and warranted measures capable of
abating a nuisance under this section.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.036 EVIDENTIARY STANDARD.
   At any hearing conducted under this subchapter, any evidence on which a
reasonably prudent person would rely may be considered without regard to the
formal or technical rules of evidence, and the village’s Hearing Officer may
rely upon written official reports, affidavits and other business records
submitted by police officers or other authorized village officials or village
employees to determine whether a public safety threat occurred; provided,
however, that, only evidence reasonably necessary to demonstrate the existence
or absence of elements which must be considered when determining whether a
public safety threat occurred shall be heard.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.037 COST RECOVERY AUTHORIZED.
   An amount equal to three times the cost or expense incurred by the village
in abating a public safety threat under this subchapter may be recovered by the
village in an appropriate legal action.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.038 RIGHT OF REVIEW.
   Any order of the village’s Hearing Officer issued under this section may be
appealed to a court of competent jurisdiction or as otherwise provided by law.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.039 STAY PENDING REVIEW.
   No summary closure order issued by the Chief of Police under §
110.032 of this chapter, or order of closure issued by the village’s Hearing
Officer under §§
110.034 and
110.035 of this chapter, shall be considered to a be a suspension or revocation
of a liquor license subject to review by the License Appeal Commission under
the Liquor Control Act of 1934, being 235 ILCS 5/1-1 et seq. as now or
hereafter amended. Nor shall any such order be subject to the automatic stay
provision set forth in § 7-9 of the Liquor Control Act of 1934.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.040 CONSTRUCTION; EFFECT.
   Nothing in this section shall be construed to:
   (A)   Prohibit the village’s Hearing Officer from taking additional action
as allowed under the village code;
   (B)   Effect the status of any ongoing village prosecution or other action
involving such licensee or establishment, including, but not limited to, any
ongoing license suspension or revocation hearing under this code;
   (C)   Prevent the Chief of Police from closing any establishment for
purposes of conducting an investigation of a crime scene or for any other
reason authorized by law;
   (D)   Prevent the arrest and prosecution of any person for operating a
business or occupation without a license;
   (E)   Prevent the arrest and prosecution of any person for operating a
business or occupation in violation of any closure order;
   (F)   Constitute an act of possession, ownership or control by the village
over the closed premises; or
   (G)   Deny common law right to anyone to abate a nuisance.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.041 MANNER OF ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   The Chief of Police is authorized to use appropriate means io effect
the summary closure of an establishment. The summary closure authorized by this
section shall not be executed in a manner that prevents legally required
ingress to or egress from the residential occupancy portion of a building.
Access to the closed establishment by the licensee/owner and other persons able
to prove an interest in the establishment may be permitted for the purposes of
maintaining the establishment in safe and code-compliant condition, correcting
code violations, removing items from the closed establishment and any other
purpose authorized in accordance with rules and regulations promulgated by the
Chief of Police. Entry to the closed establishment by government inspectors and
investigators acting within the scope of their employment shall be permitted.
No means used to close an establishment pursuant to this subchapter shall be
removed by the Chief of Police unless the village’s Hearing Officer or a court
of competent jurisdiction orders the removal of such means.
   (B)   For purposes of this subchapter, any period of time during which the
means used to close an establishment are temporarily removed pursuant to a
court order shall not be included in the calculation of the required closure
period.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.042 PROHIBITION OF CONDUCTING BUSINESS.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to conduct any business activity at, or
to knowingly frequent, any establishment that has been summarily closed
pursuant to this subchapter.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.043 TAMPERING WITH MEANS OF CLOSURE PROHIBITED.
   Except as authorized pursuant to §
110.030 of this chapter, it shall be unlawful for any person to damage, tamper
with, destroy or remove, or to cause to be damaged, tampered with, destroyed or
removed, any means of closure used to summarily close an establishment pursuant
to §
110.030 of this chapter or any notice of summary closure or closure sign
affixed at such establishment pursuant to §
110.033 of this chapter.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)
§ 110.044 FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH APPROVED NUISANCE ABATEMENT PLAN.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to fail to comply with any nuisance
abatement plan or part thereof approved or subsequently modified under §
110.035 of this chapter.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   In addition to any other penalty provided by law, any person who
violates §
110.042 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $750 and may be subject to
further criminal or other prosecution. Each day that a violation continues
shall constitute a separate and distinct offense.
      (2)   In addition to any other penalty provided by law, any person who
violates §
110.043 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $750 and may be subject to
further criminal or other prosecution. Each day that a violation continues
shall constitute a separate and distinct offense.
      (3)   In addition to any other penalty provided by law, which may include
license suspension or revocation, any person who violates §
110.044 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $750. Each day that a
violation continues shall constitute a separate and distinct offense.
(Ord. 22-008, passed 11-7-2022)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 111.001 DEFINITIONS.
   Unless the context otherwise requires, the words and phrases as defined in
235 ILCS 5/1-3.01 through 5/1-3.38 as now or hereafter amended shall have the
meanings and construction in this chapter as is given in said paragraphs.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-1)
§ 111.002 LIQUOR CONTROL COMMISSIONER.
   The President of the Board of Trustees shall be Liquor Control Commissioner
and shall be charged with the administration of this chapter.
   (A)   Powers and duties.
      (1)   Said President, as Liquor Control Commissioner, shall have the
power:
         (a)   To grant and revoke for cause all licenses issued pursuant to
this chapter;
         (b)   To enter, or to authorize any law enforcing official to enter,
at any time upon any premises licensed hereunder to determine whether any of
the provisions of this chapter are being violated and at such time to examine
the premises of the licensee;
         (c)   To receive complaint from any citizen of the village that any of
the provisions of this chapter have been or are being violated and to take such
actions as to him or her shall seem necessary and advisable; and
         (d)   To receive license fees and pay the same forthwith to the
Village Treasurer.
      (2)   (a)   The President, as Liquor Control Commissioner, shall have the
right to examine, or cause to be examined, the books and records of any such
applicant or licensee; to hear testimony and take proof for his or her
information in the performance of his or her duties, and for such purpose to
issue subpoenas which shall be effective in any part of the state.
         (b)   For the purpose of obtaining any of the information desired by
the Liquor Control Commissioner under this section, he or she may authorize his
or her agent to act on his or her behalf.
   (B)   Assistants. The President, as Liquor Control Commissioner, may appoint
a person or persons to assist him or her in the exercise of the powers and the
performance of his or her duties as such Liquor Control Commissioner.
   (C)   Compensation. The Liquor Control Commissioner shall receive
compensation in the sum of $600 per year payable in 26 equal installments.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-2)
§ 111.003 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or offer for sale at retail any
alcoholic liquor in the village without first having procured a license
therefor as required by this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-3) Penalty, see §
111.999
§ 111.004 APPLICATION FOR LICENSE.
   Application for any license required by this chapter shall be made to the
President, as Liquor Control Commissioner, in writing, under oath, stating:
   (A)   The name, age and address of the applicant in the case of an
individual; if a partnership, the persons entitled to share in the profits
thereof; and, if a corporation or an incorporated club, the corporate name,
registered officer and agent, and the date of incorporation. A copy of the
articles of incorporation shall also be furnished with the application;
   (B)   The citizenship of the applicant, his or her place of birth and, if a
naturalized citizen, the date and place of his or her naturalization;
   (C)   The character of business of the applicant;
   (D)   The length of time that the applicant has been in business of such
character;
   (E)   The location and description of the premises which are to be operated
under such licenses;
   (F)   A statement as to whether applicant has made similar application for a
license required by this chapter for another location and the disposition of
such application;
   (G)   A statement that applicant has never been convicted of a felony;
   (H)   A statement as to whether a previous license issued by any state or
subdivision thereof, or by the Federal Government has been revoked and the
reasons therefor; and
   (I)   A statement that applicant will not violate any of the laws of the
state or of the United States or any ordinance of the village in the conduct of
his or her business.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-4) (Ord. 14-005, passed 4-7-2014)
§ 111.005 RESTRICTIONS ON ISSUANCE OF LICENSE.
   (A)   No license shall be issued under this chapter to:
      (1)   A person who is not of good character and reputation in the
community in which he or she resides;
      (2)   A person who is not a citizen of the United States;
      (3)   A person who has been convicted of a felony under any state or
federal law;
      (4)   A person who has been convicted of being a keeper of, or is
keeping, a house of ill fame;
      (5)   A person who has been convicted of pandering or other crime or
misdemeanor opposed to decency and morality;
      (6)   A person whose license issued pursuant to the Liquor Control Act,
being 235 ILCS 5/1-1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended, or this chapter has
been revoked for cause;
      (7)   A person, who at the time of application for renewal of any license
issued hereunder, would not be eligible for such license upon an original
application;
      (8)   A copartnership, unless all of the members of such copartnership
shall be qualified to obtain a license;
      (9)   A corporation, if any officer, director or manager thereof or any
stockholder or stockholders owning in the aggregate more than 5% of the stock
of such corporation, would not be eligible to receive a license hereunder for
any reason other than citizenship and residence within the village;
      (10)   A corporation, unless it is incorporated in the state, or unless
it is a foreign corporation which is qualified under the state’s Business
Corporation Act, being 805 ILCS 5/1.01 et seq. as now or hereafter amended, to
transact business in the state;
      (11)   A person whose place of business is conducted by a manager or
agent, unless such manager or agent possesses the same qualifications required
of the licensee;
      (12)   A person who has been convicted of a violation of any federal or
state saw concerning the manufacture, possession or sale of alcoholic liquor
subsequent to the effective date hereof or who has forfeited his or her bond to
appear in court to answer charges for any such violation;
      (13)   A person who does not own the premises for which a license is
sought or does not have a lease therefor for the full period for which the
license is to be issued;
      (14)   Any law enforcing public official or any village officer; and no
such official shall be interested in any way, either directly or indirectly, in
the manufacture, sale or distribution of alcoholic liquor;
      (15)   A person who is not a beneficial owner of the business to be
operated by the licensee; and
      (16)   A person who owes a indebtedness to the village or is in violation
of any village ordinance.
   (B)   The Local Liquor Commissioner shall cause the Chief of Police, the
Building Department and the Fire Chief to do an investigation of an application
for the issuance or renewal of a liquor license. If such departments find that
all applicable ordinances of the village have been complied with and the
applicant is eligible for issuance or renewal of the license, said application
or renewal shall be forwarded to the Commissioner. From time to time, the
Commissioner may cause such additional inspections or investigations as are
necessary to ensure the protection of the public health, safety and welfare and
to ensure full compliance by an applicant and licensee with the ordinances of
the village.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-5) (Ord. 98371, passed 6-1-1998; Ord. 98-379, passed 9-8-
1998; Ord. 14-005, passed 4-7-2014)
§ 111.006 CLASSIFICATION OF LICENSES; FEES.
   (A)   The licenses required by this chapter shall be classified as follows:
      (1)   Class “A” license. Shall authorize the sale at retail and
consumption of alcoholic liquor on the specified premises;
      (2)   Class “B” license. Shall authorize the sale at retail of alcoholic
liquor to be consumed within the established location of a club by the members
thereof;
      (3)   Class “C” license. Shall authorize the sale at retail of alcoholic
liquor on the specified premises, but shall not permit the consumption thereon
or adjacent thereof;
      (4)   Class “D” license. Shall authorize the sale at retail and
consumption of alcoholic liquor on the specified premises, only as an incident
to a business, other than the sale of alcoholic liquor which is regularly
licensed and operated as a business in chief or principal business of the
owner;
      (5)   Class “D/special” license. Shall authorize the sale at retail and
consumption of alcoholic liquor on the premises located at 15420 S. Harper in
the village for so long as a municipally-owned building shall occupy those
premises and only as an incident to a catering business conducted at that
location which is legally licensed and operated as the business in chief or
principal business of the caterer for the premises;
      (6)   Class “E” license. Shall authorize the sale at retail and
consumption of alcoholic liquor on the specified premises, only as an incident
to a business, other than the sale of alcoholic liquor, such as a hotel or
motel, which is regularly licensed and operated as a business in chief or
principal business of the owner;
      (7)   Class “F” license. Shall authorize the sale at retail and
consumption of alcoholic liquor as a separate and distinct business which is
located entirely within a hotel or motel which is regularly licensed by the
village;
      (8)   Class “G” license. Shall authorize the sale at retail and
consumption of beer on the specified premises;
      (9)   Class “H” license. Shall authorize the sale at retail and
consumption of alcoholic liquor on the specified premises for a period of time
not to exceed four days; and
      (10)   Class “I” license, special event. Shall authorize the sale at
retail and consumption of alcoholic liquor on the premises located at 142nd and
Chicago Avenue, in the Dolton Village Mall.
   (B)   The annual license fees for the above businesses shall be established
by ordinance as set forth in the license fee schedule of §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-6) (Ord. 87-132, passed - -1987; Ord. 88-144, passed 8-9-
1988; Ord. 91-159, passed 6-25-1991)

shall not exceed the following:
Class A license                                    7

apply for and secure a license, if otherwise eligible under the provisions of

   (B)   The holder of a liquor license authorizing retail sales for

   (C)   The holder of a Class C license may designate a limited area of the
licensed premises for the sale at retail and consumption of alcoholic liquor on
the licensed premises. Any Class C licensee seeking to avail itself of
designated area sale of alcohol for consumption on the premises shall make
application to the village. There shall be an additional annual license fee of
$500 over and above the then-current Class A license fee.
(Ord. 87-132, passed - -1987; Ord. 88-119, passed 5-10-1988; Ord. 90-136,
passed 10-16-1990; Ord. 91-159, passed 6-25-1991; Ord. 91-166, passed 11-12-
1991; Ord. 93-205, passed 4-13-1993; Ord. 93-210, passed 5-25-1993; Ord. 94-
242, passed 3-16-1994; Ord. 14-005, passed 4-7-2014; Ord. 15-012, passed 5-4-
2015; Ord. 19-012, passed 5-9-2019)
§ 111.008 TERM OF LICENSE.
   All licenses to be issued under this chapter shall be for a period of one
year and shall expire on April 30 of each year.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-8)
§ 111.009 PAYMENT AND DISPOSITION OF LICENSE FEES.
   All license fees required by this chapter shall be paid to the President, as
Liquor Control Commissioner, or to such other person as may be designated. Upon
such payment, the license fees shall be promptly turned over to the Village
Treasurer for deposit in the Corporate Fund. New licenses issued on or after
November 1 shall require payment of only one-half the annual license fee. There
shall be no refund of any fee paid for any unused portion of the license
period.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-9)
§ 111.010 RENEWAL OF LICENSES.
   Any licensee may renew his or her license at the expiration thereof;
provided, he or she is then qualified to receive a license and the premises for
which such renewal license is sought are suitable for such purpose; and,
provided further that, the renewal privilege herein provided for shall not be
construed as a vested right which shall in any case prevent the President and
Board of Trustees from decreasing the number of licenses to be issued within
its jurisdiction.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-10)
§ 111.011 TRANSFER OF LICENSE.
   A license shall be purely a personal privilege, good for not to exceed one
year after issuance, unless sooner revoked as in this chapter provided, and
shall not constitute property, nor shall it be subject to attachment,
garnishment or execution, nor shall it be alienable or transferable,
voluntarily or involuntarily, or subject to being encumbered or hypothecated.
Such license shall not descend by the laws of the state or intestate
devolution, but it shall cease upon the death of the licensee.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-11)
§ 111.012 BUILDING AND LOCATION RESTRICTIONS.
   (A)   Location restrictions. No license shall be issued for the sale at
retail of any alcoholic liquor within 100 feet of any church, school, hospital,
licensed nursing home or licensed care facility or home for veterans, their
wives or children, or any military or naval stations.
   (B)   View from street. On premises where the sale of alcoholic liquor for
consumption thereon is licensed, no screen, blind, curtain, partition, article
or thing shall be permitted in the windows, or upon the doors of such licensed
premises, nor inside such premises from the street, road or sidewalk at all
times, and no booth, screen, partition or other obstruction, nor any
arrangements of lights or lighting shall be permitted in or about the interior
of such licensed premises which shall prevent a full view of the entire
interior of such premises from the street, road or sidewalk, and said premises
must be so located that there shall be a full view of the entire interior of
such premises from the street, road or sidewalk. All rooms where liquor is sold
for consumption upon the premises shall be continuously lighted during business
hours by natural light or artificial white light so that all parts of the
interior of the premises shall be clearly visible. In case the view in any such
licensed premises required by the foregoing provision shall be willfully
obscured by the licensee or by him or her willfully suffered to be obscured or
in any manner obstructed, then such license shall be subject to revocation.
   (C)   Change of location. A retailer’s license shall permit the sale of
alcoholic liquor only on the premises described in the application and license,
and it shall be unlawful to sell alcoholic liquor at retail at any other place.
Such location may be changed only upon the written permit of the President as
Liquor Control Commissioner. No change of location shall be permitted unless
the proposed new location is a proper one for the sale at retail of alcoholic
liquor under this chapter or under any other ordinance of the village.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-12)
   (D)   Video surveillance cameras on premises. Each Licensee shall maintain
in working condition video surveillance cameras (the “cameras”) that are
sufficiently light-sensitive and provide sufficient image resolution to produce
easily discernable images that visually record activities on all entrances of
the licensed premises as well as any bar area and any parking lot under the
control of the licensee. The video recording must be made available to law
enforcement officers and maintained in compact disc electronic file or other
digital media. The cameras shall be operational during all hours when the
licensed premises is open and shall be preserved at least 30 days after
recording. Failure to comply with this requirement shall subject the licensee
as to any and all penalties set forth in the village code, including, but not
limited to, license suspension or revocation.
(Ord. 87-132, passed - -; Ord. 19-022, passed 12-2-2019) Penalty, see §
