§ 111.013 CONDITIONS OF LICENSE.
   (A)   License to be displayed. Every licensee shall cause his or her license
or licenses to be framed and hung in plain view in a conspicuous place on the
licensed premises.
   (B)   Closing hours. It shall be unlawful for any holder of any license
issued under this chapter to sell or to offer for sale at retail any alcoholic
liquor before the hour of 7:00 a.m., Monday through Saturday, and before 12:00
p.m. on Sundays. It shall also be unlawful for any holder of any license issued
under this chapter to sell or offer for sale at retail any alcoholic liquor
after the hour of 1:00 a.m., Monday through Friday, and after 2:00 a.m. on
Saturday and Sunday.
   (C)   Insurance requirements. Each licensee shall, at all times, maintain a
policy of dram shop insurance issued by a responsible insurance company
authorized and licensed to do business in the state insuring such licensee
against liability, which such licensee may incur under the provisions of the
state’s Dram Shop Act, being 235 ILCS 5/6-21 as now or hereafter amended, and
specifically designating the village as an additional insured. Evidence of the
insurance policy shall indicate that the term of insurance is of sufficient
length to encompass the period of the current license.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-13) (Ord. 14-005, passed 4-7-2014; Ord. 19-018, passed 11-4-
2019) Penalty, see §
111.999
§ 111.014 SANITARY CONDITIONS.
   (A)   Premises. All premises used for the sale at retail of alcoholic
liquor, including all wash and toilet rooms thereon, shall be kept in a clean
and sanitary condition.
   (B)   Employees. No licenses under this chapter shall employ any person who
is afflicted with or who is a carrier of any contagious, infectious or venereal
disease. It shall be unlawful for any person who is afflicted with or is a
carrier of any such disease to work in or about the licensed premises or to
engage in any way in the handling, preparation or sale of alcoholic liquor.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-14) Penalty, see §
111.999
§ 111.015 MINORS; SALE TO CERTAIN PERSONS.
   (A)   Application of provisions. Pursuant to the authority granted by § 6 of
Art. VII of the Constitution of Illinois, 1970, this section shall be
controlling within the village in regards to the sale, gift or delivery of all
alcoholic liquor, notwithstanding anything contrary contained in 235 ILCS 5 as
now or hereafter amended and all acts amendatory thereof and supplementary
thereto and any other law or laws of the state.
   (B)   Sale to minors, intoxicated persons, habitual drunkards and persons
fighting on the licensed premises.
      (1)   No licensee or any officer, associate, member, representative,
agent or employee of such licensee shall sell, give or deliver alcoholic liquor
to any person under the age of 21 years, or to any intoxicated person, or to
any person know by him or her to be an habitual drunkard, spendthrift, insane,
mentally ill, mentally deficient or in need of mental treatment, or to any
person known to the licensee, or officer, associate, member, representative,
agent or employee of the licensee, to have been involved in a fight at the
licensed premises within the immediately preceding 48-hour period.
      (2)   Nothing in this section shall prohibit any person under the age of
21 years, but at least 18 years of age from serving or delivering alcoholic
liquor at dining tables for consumption on the premises in those licensed
premises holding a retail license Class D, D/Special License and E pursuant to
this chapter. It shall be unlawful for any person under the age of 21 years to
draw, pour, mix or sell any alcoholic liquor to patrons of establishments
licensed pursuant to this chapter.
   (C)   Purchase for minors. No person, after purchasing or otherwise
obtaining alcoholic liquor, shall give, sell or deliver such alcoholic liquor
to another person under the age of 21 years.
   (D)   Purchase or acceptance by minors. Any person to whom the sale, gift or
delivery of any alcoholic liquor is prohibited because of age shall not
purchase or accept a gift of such alcoholic liquor or have alcoholic liquor in
his or her possession.
   (E)   Consumption by minors. The consumption of alcoholic liquor by any
person under 21 years of age is forbidden.
   (F)   Identification; misrepresentation of age.
      (1)   If a licensee or his or her agents or employees believes or has
reason to believe that a sale or delivery of any alcoholic liquor is prohibited
because of the non-age of the prospective recipient, he or she shall, before
making such sale or delivery, demand presentation of some form of positive
identification, containing proof of age, issued by a public officer in the
performance of his or her official duties.
      (2)   No person shall transfer, alter or deface such an identification
card; use the identification card of another; carry or use a false or forged
identification card; or obtain an identification card by means of false
information.
   (G)   Unlawful purchase, acceptance or possession. No person shall purchase,
accept delivery or have possession of alcoholic liquor in violation of this
section.
   (H)   Alcohol sales to minors compliance checks. The purpose of this section
is to establish policy and procedures for conducting compliance check
operations for the sale of alcohol to underage minors.
      (1)   Definitions. For the purpose of this division (H), the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
         COMPLIANCE CHECK MANAGER OFFICER. The village police officer who is
responsible for the supervising enforcement compliance checks operations for
alcohol and any other age restricted products.
         COMPLIANCE CHECK OPERATIONS. A controlled purchase operation conducted
using covert minors to ensure that age restricted products are being sold
within legal guidelines. COMPLIANCE CHECK OPERATIONS may also be referred to as
an INSPECTION.
         COMPLIANCE OFFICER(S). Village police officer(s) assigned to conduct
compliance check operation and supervise the covert minor(s) engaging in
controlled buys of age restricted alcohol liquor products.
         COVERT MINOR(S). A volunteer who is under the legal age to purchase
the age restricted product and who, while under police supervision, assists the
Police Department in controlled purchase operations.
         IDENTIFICATION. A government issued driver’s license, state
identification card, active duty military identification card or passport
lawfully issued to the covert minor for the purposes of establishing identity.
         LICENSEE. In the case of alcohol, the business, licensed by the
village and state, to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on or off
premises.
         OBSERVERS. Adult volunteers who assist supervising officer(s) in the
conducting of compliance check operations.
         PRODUCT. Any alcohol purchased by a covert minor in the course of
conducting a compliance check operation.
         SELLER(S). Persons who are responsible for and involved in the sale or
refusal of sale of the age restricted product.
      (2)   Procedures.
         (a)   Scheduling.
            1.   The compliance check manager will be responsible for creating
a schedule of alcohol compliance check operations. The number of alcohol
focused operations to be scheduled will be established by the count of licensed
liquor establishments eligible to be checked multiplied by the number of base
checks to be conducted per licensed establishment and then divided by the
number of locations to be checked during a single compliance check operation.
For alcohol based operations, the Liquor Commissioner will determine the number
of base checks to be conducted.
            2.   When an alcohol licensee has a compliance check failure, that
licensee will be scheduled to have two additional compliance check operations.
The follow-up compliance check operation will not occur within the first 30
days to allow for a review of the failure and suggestions for improvement. A
priority will be placed on completing the follow-up inspections.
            3.   The schedule for alcohol compliance check operations will be
subject to the approval of the Police Chief and shall be reported to the
village’s Police Trustee.
            4.   Upon the receiving of a complaint of underage access to a
alcohol product, the compliance check manager will schedule a compliance check
operation within 30 days of the complaint. The business alleged to be in
violation may be inspected as part of a regularly scheduled compliance check
operation.
         (b)   Officer assignments.
            1.   For pre-scheduled compliance check operations, the compliance
check manager will notify all eligible officers of the opportunity to conduct
compliance check operations. To ensure fairness in assignments, officers will
be given a period of time to sign up for the operations on a first come first
serve basis with a limitation on how many operations the individual officer may
sign up for. Once the sign-up period has lapsed, the compliance check manager
will re-open the schedule for a second round of sign ups to include officers
who previously sign up, again with limitations on the number they are allowed
to sign up for. If dates are still available following the second round, the
schedule will be opened up for general sign up with no limitations.
            2.   Officers who fail to report to scheduled assignments on two
consecutive dates may be required to forfeit upcoming dates or be denied the
opportunity to sign up during the next scheduling period.
         (c)   Covert minors. The compliance check operations manager is
responsible for the recruiting and scheduling of covert minors. Covert minors
will be selected using the following criteria.
            1.   Actual age of minors.
               a.   Covert minors assigned to alcohol compliance checks must be
at least 18 years of age and no more than 20 years of age.
               b.   Minors who are 16 years of age or minors who reside with
parent year round and have not reached the age of 19 years must have a parent
permission slip signed authorizing the involvement in compliance check
operations. The parent permission will outline the role the minor will take in
compliance check operations.
               c.   Under no circumstances will a covert minor be allowed to
participate in compliance check operations if he or she is within two months of
his or her birth date that would make them legal to purchase the age restricted
product.
            2.   Appearance of minors.
               a.   Minors should be “youthful” in appearance. No minor will
use excessive makeup to enhance their appearance, nor will males be allowed to
have facial hair (i.e., beard or mustache).
               b.   Minors will not be allowed to participate in a compliance
check operation if not appropriately dressed. Minors will not wear clothing
that would aid the determining of age (i.e., letter jackets and t-shirts that
provide class information).
               c.   Minors at the direction of the compliance check manager may
be required to participate in an age verification study.
               d.   To complete an age verification study, minors will be taken
to an area with high levels of pedestrian traffic. Officers will conduct the
study by requesting a variety of pedestrians to evaluate the minor and estimate
the minors age. Officers will request this input from 12 people who would be
eligible to sit on a jury.
               e.   Upon completing of the age verification study, the officers
conducting the study will turn the documentation over to the compliance check
manager for inclusion in the minor’s file.
            3.   Background review.
               a.   Minors should be of good character. A background check
shall be conducted by the compliance check manager. This background check will
include a criminal history check and a check of ARMS.
               b.   Minors will be disqualified from participation if they have
any felony or misdemeanor convictions or been charged with DUI or similar
violation from another state. Minors with a single violation of minors in
possession may be allowed to participate in the program with the authorization
of the Legal Department and the compliance check manager.
            4.   Selected covert minors.
               a.   Minors who are selected as a covert minor will compete a
covert minor information sheet. The information sheet will contain basic
information on the covert minor, contact information, medical information and
emergency contact information.
               b.   The compliance check manager will review the statement of
understanding (included on the covert minor information sheet) with the covert
minor. The statement of understanding outlines the rules for the covert minors
and the goal and direction of the compliance check program. They will also
agree to participate in any additional follow up investigations, case review
and preparation, trials being held to prosecute the seller and administrative
hearings against the licensee.
               c.   The compliance check manager will maintain a file on each
minor which include the covert minor information sheet, a copy of the covert
minor’s driver’s license, a completed background investigation and a photograph
of the covert minor. If the minor is working as part of fine reduction
arrangements, the file will also include the original documentation of the
violation.
               d.   Covert minors will not be evaluated on their ability to
purchase alcohol from a licensee. The evaluation of the covert minor will be
based on the minor conducting a fair test. Minors will be removed from the
program if they are found to be alerting businesses of the up coming compliance
check or tipping of an employee of an establishment while conducting the
compliance check. Officers observing or learning of the above behavior will
immediately notify the compliance check manager.
            5.   Covert minor compensation.
               a.   Minors working through an agreement for compensation will
be compensated at a rate of $10 per hour and figured to the nearest half hour.
This compensation will be issued through the supervising officer(s).
Compensation in this case does not imply employment but is a stipend given in
consideration for the voluntary activity of the covert minor.
               b.   Covert minors working through arrangements for fine
reduction will be scheduled for one compliance operation per $50 in fines
issued. No partial consideration will be made. When a covert minor agrees to
participate in this program, the minor will be assigned to the number of
details necessary to cover the entire fine amount. If the minor fails to
complete the program as agreed to.
            6.   Covert minor scheduling.
               a.   The compliance check manager is responsible for the
scheduling of covert minors. Two to three covert minors will be scheduled per
detail. If possible, a covert minor will not be scheduled for more than two
compliance check details in a month. Minor are required to notify the
compliance check manager if the covert minor is unable to complete an
assignment as scheduled.
               b.   Covert minors working as part of an agreement for fine
reduction will be given credit for working the compliance check operation if
the department is required to cancel the operation on short notice.
         (d)   Operational funds.
            1.   The compliance check manager will maintain and manage funds to
conduct compliance check operations. Funds will be requested from the Village
Treasurer’s office in $500 increments. The compliance check manager will keep
these funds secured in his or her office. A fund log will be maintained that
will show the distribution of these funds and the returning of funds not used
during the compliance check operations.
            2.   On each occasion that compliance check funds are to be used,
the compliance check manager will determine funds necessary to complete the
operation. The compliance check manager will log those funds out of the account
and issue them to the supervising officer(s). A covert fund tracking sheet will
be completed and one of the supervising officer(s) will verify and sign for
funds received.
            3.   Upon the conclusion of the compliance check operation the
supervising officer(s) will do an accounting of all expenditures and reconcile
the funds on the covert detail sheet. This reconciliation shall be reported to
the Village Treasurer timely. If discrepancies are found the supervising
officer(s) will provide a memo outlining what the discrepancies were and what
actions are needed to reconcile the account. Said funds shall be audited
annually by the Village Auditor.
            4.   If minors used in the compliance check operations are working
through an agreement for compensation, said agreement is subject to the
approval of the Chief of Staff/Village Administrator, the supervising officer
(s) will provide to the minor(s) appropriate funds as per the agreement with
the minor. The minors receiving compensation will sign for the funds received
on the covert fund tracking sheet.
            5.   The supervising officer(s) will return the unused funds to the
compliance check manager. The compliance check manager will review the
expenditure and ensure that the accounting was true and correct. If
discrepancies are found the compliance check manager will note the discrepancy
and request a memo from the supervising officer(s) regarding the discrepancy. A
copy of the discrepancy report shall be timely filed with the Village Treasurer
and the Chief of Staff/Village Administrator.
            6.   Funds will then be placed back into the covert funds account
and the return of unused funds will be documented on the covert fund log by the
compliance check manager.
            7.   Covert funds will be subject to periodic audits by the Police
Department and the Village Treasurer’s accounting staff and shall be audited
annual by the village duly appointed Auditor. The compliance check manager will
ensure that the covert funds logs kept up to date and reconciled on a monthly
basis. Said monthly reconciliations shall be reported to the Chief of Staff/
Village Administrator and the Village Treasurer.
         (e)   Operation procedures; assignment of businesses to be inspected.
            1.   For alcohol compliance check operations, the compliance check
manager will review the history of compliance checks completed and determine
which licensees need an inspection. The compliance check manager will then
prepare a compliance check detail sheet that provides information on
supervising officer(s) and covert minors along with a listing of locations to
be checked.
            2.   The types of licensees to be inspected on a single detail will
be left to the discretion of the compliance check manager. Typically, these
inspections should include one or two Class P licensees, a Class R licensee
that does not have a lounge area and the remaining slots are comprised of Class
As, Rs and other types of licenses which are publicly accessible. A minimum of
five licensees and a maximum of eight licensees will be inspected during a
compliance check operation.
            3.   The compliance check manager will, upon determining what
locations are to be inspected, calculate the amount of funds necessary to
complete the operation and issue those to the supervising officer(s) as
outlined above. The supervising officer(s) will be provided a kit that will
include the compliance check detail sheet and sufficient paperwork to handle
the detail. The compliance check manager will also provide any special
instructions to the supervising officer(s).
         (f)   Pre-operational briefing.
            1.   The supervising officer(s) will conduct a pre-operation
briefing. During this briefing, the supervising officer(s) will ensure that the
covert minors appearance follows the standards as outlined in this policy. If
their appearance does not meet those standards the supervising officer(s) will
take necessary action to get the covert minor into compliance If the
supervising officer(s) are unable to get the covert minor into compliance, the
covert minor shall not be allowed to perform duties on this occasion. The
supervising officer(s) will also notify the compliance check manager of the
issues related to the appearance of the minor.
            2.   The supervising officer(s) will then review the list of
businesses to be inspected with the covert minor. During this review, the
supervising officer(s) will determine which minors will be involved in checking
specific businesses. If the minor is aware of individuals employed by the
business to be checked, the covert minor should not be used at that location.
            3.   The supervising officer(s) should review with the covert
minors the procedures for conducting compliance operations, what products are
to be purchased and what things should be said by the covert minors. The
supervising officer(s) will discuss entrapment and what behaviors and
statements the minors should avoid to prevent entrapment from being an issue.
         (g)   Compliance check operation.
            1.   The supervising officer(s) will use a departmental vehicle in
conducting the compliance check operation. Only with advanced approval from the
Chief of Police will an officer’s personally-owned vehicle be used during a
compliance check operation. All participants in the compliance check operation
will conduct the operation out of the same vehicle. Covert minors will not be
allowed to use their own vehicles.
            2.   Supervising officer(s) will determine the order in which the
compliance checks should be conducted. When conducting these inspections,
officers should make every effort to avoid detection by the businesses being
inspected.
            3.   When conducting the actual compliance check operation, the
supervising officer(s) shall be in a position to see and, if possible, hear the
transaction. When practical, this observation should occur within the
establishment.
            4.   At a minimum, the supervising officer(s) should scan the
business to ensure that the minor is not entering into a dangerous situation.
If the supervising officer(s) are going to enter the establishment, they should
do so before the minor enters. This is done to further ensure the safety of the
covert minor.
            5.   The supervising officer(s) may send any combination of minors
into the establishment to aid in the natural appearance of the minors for the
business they are entering. Supervising officer(s) should avoid, as is
reasonably possible, giving the appearance that the supervising officer(s) are
with the covert minors. When using multiple covert minors, only one will be
directed to make the purchase of the product.
            6.   The supervising officer(s) will issue sufficient covert funds
needed to complete a transaction to the covert minor(s) prior to their entering
a specific location. Upon conclusion of the compliance check, the supervising
officer(s) will recover from the covert minor(s) funds not used in that check.
The supervising officer will then record the expenses related to that
compliance check of the covert detail sheet.
            7.   During the compliance check operation, the covert minor(s)
will be expected to be a good witness. They will be required to identify the
seller by name, number or description to the supervising officer(s) and provide
a statement regarding the conversation conducted between the seller and the
covert minor(s).
         (h)   Attempts to purchase/off-premises use products.
            1.   For purchases of products that are sold for off-premises use,
the covert minor will enter the establishment and locate the product to be
purchased. The covert minor will take the product immediately to the counter
for purchase. The quantity of product purchased will be limited to single-
serve containers, packs or a single. If the seller asks for identification, the
covert minor will indicate that he or she does not have his or her
identification on his or her person. If the covert minor is asked to provide an
age or a birth date, he or she will provide information that will put his or
her age over the purchase age for that product. During the actual attempt to
purchase, the covert minor will avoid excessive conversation and any actions
that would coerce, entice or compel the seller to agree to the purpose.
            2.   After the attempt to purchase occurs, the covert minor will
immediately leave the store with the product (if purchase is made) and return
to a previously agreed upon meeting location. He or she will meet with the
supervising officer(s), turn the product over to them and review the facts of
the case.
            3.   Following the compliance check, the covert minor(s) and
supervising officer(s) will then leave the premises and meet at the prearranged
location. A review of the check will be completed and the seller identified.
         (i)   Supervising officer(s) actions.
            1.   The primary responsibility of the supervising officer(s) is
the protection of the covert minor(s). The supervising officer(s) will make
every effort necessary to ensure the covert minor(s) are protected. At no time
will the supervising officer(s) make the covert minor(s) available to the
seller or business manager or other business staff.
            2.   While conducting a compliance check, the supervising officer
(s) will be observant of other violations occurring in the establishment. As
violations are noted, the supervising officer(s) will document violations and
notify the compliance check manager. When violations of a more serious nature
(i.e., employee consumption on duty) are found, the supervising officer(s) will
immediately notify the compliance check manager of their observations.
            3.   During the course of compliance check operations, the
supervising officer(s) may feel that it is necessary to purchase alcohol in
order to avoid detection. Supervising officer(s)in this case may purchase
alcohol and give the appearance of consumption. Supervising officer(s) should
make every effort not to consume alcohol during the operation. Under no
circumstance should supervising officer(s) consume more than two ounces of
alcohol during the compliance check detail.
         (j)   Completed inspections. Upon the completion of an individual
compliance check, the supervising officer(s) will meet with the covert minor(s)
and review the check. A determination will be made as to what if any violations
have occurred.
         (k)   Violations found.
            1.   In cases where violations are found, the supervising officer
(s) will notify TEP of the violations and request a report number. Preliminary
paperwork will be completed prior to re-entering the establishment.
            2.   The supervising officer(s) will wait for a reasonable period
of time. The purpose of this waiting period is to provide some distance between
the purchase and the notification of violation. The recommend waiting period is
a minimum of five minutes. In no case should the supervising officer(s)
continue to another compliance check location without first completing the
notification and issuance of a notice to appear.
            3.   Upon re-entering the business the supervising officer(s) will
request to speak to a manager or employee in charge. While this is occurring
efforts should also be made to locate the employee involved in the violation.
The business should be given a reasonable period of time to adjust business
operations to allow for enforcement action to occur.
            4.   The supervising officer(s) will provide notification to the
offending employee. During that notification, the supervising officers should
note any spontaneous statements made by the offending employee or business
representative and include those statements in the police report. Supervising
officer(s) should also make note of the conditions of the business with respect
to signage and other warnings or procedures specific to the control of the sale
of the product.
            5.   In the event that a demand to see the covert minor(s) is made
by the offending employee or business representative, the supervising officer
(s) will advise the requestor that it is not possible and that they should
contact the compliance check manager. Under no circumstance will the covert
minor be brought forward for viewing by the requestor.
            6.   Unless circumstances dictate otherwise, the offender will be
issued a notice to appear for the ordinance violation(s) as per standard
procedures. The supervising officer(s) will issue the notice of violation to
the business manager or representative. They will also encourage the business
manager or representative to contact the compliance check manager for a case
review and suggestions for improvement. A copy of the failure letter will be
included in the report.
            7.   Violation reports will include a detailed narrative of facts
of the violation. The report will also include the name and date of birth of
the covert minor(s). Addresses and phone numbers for the covert minor(s) shall
not be included in the report. The Police Department address and compliance
check manager’s phone number should be used as the address and phone number for
the covert minor(s).
         (l)   No violations found. When a business successfully passes an
inspection, a letter of congratulations will be prepared. The pass letter will
identify the seller by name or number. Upon completion of the compliance check
operation and after the covert minor(s) have been released, the supervising
officers will return to those businesses that successfully handled an
inspection and issue the pass letter to the manager or representative. The pass
letter will also note who the letter was served to.
         (m)   Compliance check operation wrap-up.
            1.   At the conclusion of the compliance check operation, the
supervising officer(s) will return the covert minor(s) to the Department or
other requested location. Any minors who are to receive compensation for
services will be paid at that time.
            2.   The supervising officer(s) will ensure that any issued funds
not used in the detail are returned to the supervising officer and accounted
for. The accounting section of the compliance check detail sheet will be
completed and the supervising officer(s) will sign for the return of covert
funds.
            3.   The compliance check detail sheet will be completed in full.
Supervising officer(s) must ensure that the outcome of each individual
inspection is noted along with which covert minor(s) were assigned to the
specific inspection. Both pass and failure letters will be attached to the
compliance check detail sheet.
            4.   Any reports of compliance check failures will be completed
immediately by the supervising officer(s) following the actual operation unless
delayed reporting is authorized by the compliance check manager. Completed
reports will be attached to the compliance check detail sheet and all paperwork
and the issued kit will be returned to the compliance check manager.
            5.   Upon receipt of the compliance check paperwork and kit the
compliance check manager will reconcile the funds issued and return them to the
fund.
            6.   Following the cities administrative policy on alcohol
violations, the compliance check manager will process all reports of
violations. The information from the completed compliance check operation will
be entered into a data base. Businesses with violations will be flagged for
additional inspections.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-15) (Ord. passed 3-4-1975; Ord. 10-511, passed 11-1-2010;

§ 111.016 POSSESSION OF LIQUOR IN PUBLIC PLACES.
   It shall be a violation for any person to carry or possess alcoholic liquor
in a public place, parking lot, on any highway or in or about any motor vehicle
upon a highway or public place within the village, except in the original
container and with the seal unbroken.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-16) (Ord. 86-137, passed 10-14-1986) Penalty, see §
111.999
§ 111.017 REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION OF LICENSES; APPEALS; FINES.
   (A)   The Commissioner may revoke or suspend any license and impose a fine,
if he or she determines that the licensee has violated any of the provisions of
this code or state or federal law or any other ordinances or resolutions of the
village or any applicable rules or regulations established by the state’s
Liquor Control Commission. No license may be suspended or revoked and no fines
levied, except after a public hearing with a three-day written notice to the
licensee. Monetary fines may be imposed for each violation; each day on which a
violation continues shall constitute a separate violation. Proceeds from such
fines shall be paid into the village’s General Corporate Fund.
   (B)   If the Commissioner has a reason to believe that any continued
operation of a particular licensed premises will immediately threaten the
welfare of the village, he or she may, upon the issuance of a written order
stating the reason for such conclusion and without notice or hearing, order the
licensed premises closed for not more than seven days, giving the licensee an
opportunity to be heard during that period; except that, if the licensee is
engaged in the conduct of another business on the licensed premises such order
shall not be applicable to such other business.
   (C)   Upon complaint being made of violation of this chapter or the state’s
statutes or the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder, the Commissioner
shall set the matter for hearing and shall serve notice upon the licensee of
the time and place of such hearing and the particular charge.
   (D)   Notice of such hearing shall be served by registered or certified
mail, prepaid, return receipt requested, or by leaving a copy of said notice
with the licensee or with a person at the said licensed place of business at
least three days prior to the hearing. The notice shall also include a copy of
this section.
   (E)   All evidence received at the hearing shall be reduced to writing and
an official record of the proceedings shall be maintained. Within five days of
the conclusion of the hearing, the Commissioner shall determine if the license
should be revoked or suspended or that the licensee should be fined, and state
the reasons for such determination in a written order, and either the amount of
the fine, the period of suspension or that the license has been revoked, and
shall serve a copy of the order within five days upon the licensee.
   (F)   Pursuant to 235 ILCS 5/7-9, any appeal from a decision of the
Commissioner to the state’s Commission shall be limited to a review of the
official proceedings of the Commissioner. A certified copy of the record of the
proceedings taken and prepared by a certified court reporter or certified
shorthand reporter shall be filed by the Commissioner within five days after
notice of the filing of such an appeal, if the appellant licensee pays the cost
of the transcript.
   (G)   When any license shall have been revoked for any cause, no license
shall be granted to any person for the period of one year thereafter for the
conduct of selling alcoholic liquor in the premises described in such revoked
license.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-17) (Ord. passed 2-18-1975; Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012;
Ord. 14-005, passed 4-7-2014)
§ 111.018 RECORD OF LICENSES AND REVOCATIONS.
   (A)   The President, as Liquor Control Commissioner, shall keep or cause to
be kept a complete record of all licenses issued hereunder and shall furnish
the Clerk, Treasurer and Chief of Police with copies thereof.
   (B)   Upon the issuance of any new license or the revocation of any existing
license, the President, as Liquor Control Commissioner, shall give written
notice of such action to the Clerk, Treasurer and Chief of Police as promptly
as possible.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-18)
§ 111.019 BASSET PROGRAM.
   (A)   For the purpose of this section, the following definitions apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      BASSET. Beverage Alcohol Sellers and Servers Education and Training.
      PERSONNEL. The owner, all management personnel, anyone whose job
description entails pouring, mixing or dispensing alcoholic liquor, all persons
who sell or serve alcoholic beverages and anyone whose job description entails
checking identification in connection with purchasing alcoholic beverages.
      STATE CERTIFIED BASSET PROGRAM. A BASSET program licensed by the state’s
Liquor Control Commission as required by §§ 3-12(a)(11.1) and 6-27 of the
Liquor Control Act of 1934 (235 ILCS 5/3-12(a)(11.1), 5/6-27) and 77 Illinois
Adm. Code part 3500.
   (B)   (1)   For liquor licenses issued prior to 1-1-2013, compliance with
this section shall be completed on or before 5-1-2013 and proof of said
training must be filed with the village’s Liquor Commission or its prior to 5-
1-2013.
      (2)   For all original or renewal liquor licenses issued pursuant to this
section on or after 5-1-2013, the licensee shall cause all personnel to
complete the state’s Beverage Sellers and Servers Education and Training
(BASSET) program prior to the issuance or renewal of said liquor license by the
village’s Liquor Commissioner.
   (C)   Any new personnel requiring BASSET training shall, within 90 days from
the commencement of their employment with a licensee, complete a BASSET
approved seller/server training program and shall, until completion of the
BASSET program, work under the direct supervision of a person who has completed
BASSET training.
   (D)   The licensee shall on maintain photocopies of all licenses and
certificates of completion of the BASSET Program for all personnel and such
photocopies shall be available for immediate inspection upon demand, by the
village’s Liquor Commissioner or any designee of the village’s Liquor
Commissioner.
   (E)   All cost associated with the licensee’s compliance with the BASSET
training required under this section shall be paid by the licensee.
   (F)   Any licensee found to be in violation of this section shall be subject
to suspension or revocation of any license issued under this chapter.
(Ord. 12-785, passed 12-17-2012)
§ 111.020 PARENTAL RESPONSIBILITY.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person knowingly to allow or permit any
minor child of whom he or she is the parent or guardian to violate any
provision of this chapter.
   (B)   Notwithstanding the foregoing, the possession, dispensing and/or
consumption, by a person under the age of 21 years, of alcoholic liquor in the
performance of religious service or ceremony, or the possession and delivery of
alcoholic liquors in pursuance of a person’s employment by a licensee under
this chapter as allowed in §
111.005 of this chapter is not prohibited.
(Ord. 12-785, passed 12-17-2012) Penalty, see §
111.999
§ 111.021 NOTICES; SIGNAGE.
   All licensees shall cause an underage purchase/consumption printed card
approximately eight inches by ten inches to be framed and displayed at all
times on the licensed premises in a conspicuous location, prominently visible
to all patrons, and shall read substantially as follows:
 
UNDERAGE DRINKING
 
If you are under 21, you are subject to a mandatory fine of up to $750 if you
purchase and/or consume any alcoholic liquor on these premises. If you buy for
or deliver an alcoholic beverage to an underage person, you will be subject to
a fine of up to $750.
 
(Ord. 12-785, passed 12-17-2012)
§ 111.022 SPECIAL EVENT LIQUOR LICENSE.
   (A)   A Class I special event liquor license may be issued at the direction
of the Liquor Control Commissioner, with payment of fees for same as follows:
      (1)   Twelve-month Class I licenses: $2,400 each;
      (2)   A person or entity not currently licensed in the village, but in
“good standing” with no outstanding indebtedness due and owing the village:
$250 per day; and
      (3)   A person or entity already issued a valid liquor license and in
“good standing” with no indebtedness due and owing the village: $35 per day.
   (B)   Any special event license so issued will be in full compliance with
all provisions of this chapter, concerning application and issuance of liquor
licenses.
(Ord. 91-159, passed 6-25-1991)
BRING YOUR OWN ALCOHOL ESTABLISHMENTS
§ 111.035 DEFINITION.
   BRING YOUR OWN ALCOHOL ESTABLISHMENTS shall mean any establishment, place of
business and/or private club which is open to the public generally or to its
members and guests which permits members, guests, customers or patrons to bring
alcoholic beverages purchased elsewhere to the premises and consume the same on
the premises. The term BRING YOUR OWN ALCOHOL ESTABLISHMENTS shall not include
a private home where any of the activities described in above occur unless the
person owning or possessing the premises is paid and/or otherwise compensated.
(Ord. 08-435, passed 5-5-2008)
§ 111.036 PROHIBITION.
   No person may own or operate a “bring your own alcohol establishment” in the
village.
(Ord. 08-435, passed 5-5-2008) Penalty, see §
111.999
§ 111.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §§
111.001 through
111.018 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $5, nor more than $500,
for each offense, and a separate offense shall be deemed committed on each day
during or on which a violation occurs or continues. The revocation of a license
issued hereunder shall not preclude the assessment of any such fine for a
violation of any provision of §§
111.001 through
111.018 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 3-3-19)
   (C)   Any person who violates the provisions of §
111.036 of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, is
subject to a fine not exceeding $500 and/or incarceration not exceeding 90
days. Each day of violation shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 08-435, passed 5-5-2008)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 112.001 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning. Any terms not
defined herein shall have the meaning ascribed to it in other ordinances of the
municipality and, if not defined in any other municipal ordinances, it shall
have the meaning ascribed in state statutes.
   AMUSEMENT.
      (1)   Any exhibition, performance, presentation or show for entertainment
purposes, whether viewed within or outside the home, including, but not limited
to, any theatrical, dramatic, musical or spectacular performance, promotional
show, motion picture show, flower, poultry or animal show, animal act, circus,
rodeo, athletic contest, sport, game or similar exhibition such as boxing,
wrestling, skating, dancing, swimming, racing or riding on animals or vehicles,
baseball, basketball, softball, football, tennis, golf, hockey, track and field
games, bowling or billiard and pool games;
      (2)   Any entertainment or recreational activity offered for public
participation or on a membership or other basis including, but not limited to,
carnivals, amusement park rides and games, bowling, billiards and pool games,
dancing, tennis, racquetball, swimming, weightlifting, body building or similar
activities; or
      (3)   Any paid television programming, whether transmitted by wire,
cable, fiber optics, laser, microwave, radio, satellite or similar means.
   ARCADE. A place of amusement that includes four or more automatic amusement
devices; provided, however, that, when calculating the number of automatic
amusement devices, jukeboxes shall not be counted.
   LEGAL VOTER. A person who has registered to vote and whose name appears on a
poll sheet from the last preceding election regardless of whether primary,
general or special.
   LIVE THEATRICAL, LIVE MUSICAL OR OTHER LIVE CULTURAL PERFORMANCE. A live
performance in any of the disciplines which are commonly regarded as part of
the fine arts, such as live theater, music, opera, drama, comedy, ballet,
modern or traditional dance, and book or poetry readings. The term does not
include such amusements as athletic events, races or performances conducted at
adult entertainment cabarets.
   MAXIMUM CAPACITY. The number of persons that an auditorium, theater or other
space may accommodate as determined by the Building Commissioner or the
Executive Director of the Department of Construction and Permits or by any
other appropriate government official; provided, however, that, MAXIMUM
CAPACITY shall not exceed the maximum number of tickets or admissions that may
be made available for sale to a performance as stated in any binding written
agreement relating to that performance. If the number of tickets or admissions
actually sold to a performance exceeds the legally permissible limit, for
purposes of determining the applicable tax, MAXIMUM CAPACITY shall mean such
greater number.
   OWNER.
      (1)   With respect to the owner of a place where an amusement is being
held, any person with an ownership or leasehold interest in a building,
structure, vehicle, boat, area or other place who presents, conducts or
operates an amusement in such place or who allows, by agreement or otherwise,
another person to present, conduct or operate an amusement in such place;
      (2)   With respect to the owner of an amusement, any person who has an
ownership or leasehold interest in such amusement or any person who has a
proprietary interest in the amusement so as to entitle such person to all or a
portion of the proceeds, after payment of reasonable expenses, from the
operation, conduct or presentation of such amusement, excluding proceeds from
non-amusement services and from sales of tangible personal property; and
      (3)   With respect to paid television programming, any person operating a
community antenna television system or wireless cable television system, or any
person receiving consideration from the patron for furnishing, transmitting, or
otherwise providing access to paid television programming.
   PAID TELEVISION. Programming that can be viewed on a television or other
screen, and is transmitted by cable, fiber optics, laser, microwave, radio,
satellite or similar means to members of the public for consideration.
   PERSON. Any natural individual, firm, society, foundation, institution,
partnership, limited liability company, association, joint stock company, joint
venture, public or private corporation, receiver, executor, trustee or other
representative appointed by the order of any court, or any other entity
recognized by law.
   SPECIAL SEATING AREA.
      (1)   An enclosed or substantially enclosed apartment-style room
containing or making available amenities for the exclusive use of the patrons
thereof whether denominated as luxury or super suites or skyboxes or by other
similar terms.
      (2)   Such amenities may include, but are not necessarily limited to,
television (including closed-circuit capacity), bathroom, refrigerator,
telephone service, storage sink, living room or lounge furniture, special
spectator seating, food, heat, air conditioning and parking.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.002 TAX IMPOSED.
   (A)   Except as otherwise provided by this chapter, an amusement tax is
imposed upon the patrons of every amusement within the village. The rate of the
tax shall be equal to 8% of the admission fees or other charges paid for the
privilege to enter, to witness, to view or to participate in such amusement,
unless division (E) below provides for a lower rate.
   (B)   The tax imposed by division (A) above shall not apply to the following
persons or privileges:
      (1)   Patrons of automatic amusement machines, as defined in §§
112.020 through
112.027 of this chapter;
      (2)   The privilege of witnessing or participating in any stock show or
business show that is not open to the general public;
      (3)   The privilege of hiring a horse-drawn carriage licensed under this
code of ordinances;
      (4)   The privilege of witnessing or participating in any amateur
production or activity, such as amateur musicals, plays and athletic events,
conducted by a not-for-profit organization operated exclusively for charitable,
educational or religious purposes; or
      (5)   Subject to satisfying the requirement contained in division (C)
below, the privilege of witnessing or participating in any amusement sponsored
or conducted by and the proceeds of which, after payment of reasonable
expenses, inure exclusively to the benefit of:
         (a)   Religious, educational and charitable institutions, societies or
organizations;
         (b)   Societies or organizations for the prevention of cruelty to
children or animals;
         (c)   Societies or organizations conducted and maintained for the
purpose of civic improvement;
         (d)   Fraternal organizations, legion posts, social and political
groups which conduct amusements, sponsored occasionally but not more often than
twice yearly; provided, however, that, the entities described in divisions (B)
(5)(a) through (B)(5)(d) herein are not-for-profit institutions, organizations,
groups or societies, where no part of the net earnings inure to the benefit of
any private shareholder or person;
         (e)   Organizations or persons in the armed services of the United
States, or National Guard organizations, reserve officers’ associations or
organizations or posts of war veterans, or auxiliary units or societies of such
posts or organizations, if such posts, organizations, units or societies are
organized in the state and if no part of their earnings inure to the benefit of
any private shareholder or person;
         (f)   Organizations or associations created and maintained for the
purpose of benefitting the members, or dependents or heirs of members of the
police or Fire Departments of any political subdivision of the state; provided
that, the exemptions contained in divisions (B)(5)(a) through (B)(5)(f) hereof
shall apply only to benefits or other fundraising events and shall not apply to
more than two events per calendar year which shall not exceed a total of 14
calendar days;
         (g)   1.   Societies or organizations conducted for the sole purpose
of maintaining symphony orchestras, opera performances and artistic
presentations, including, but not limited to, musical presentations artistic
societies or organizations, if the artistic society or organization:
               a.   Receives substantial support from voluntary contributions;
               b.   Is a not-for-profit institution where no part of the net
earnings inure to the benefit of any private shareholder or person; and
               c.   Either:
                  i.   Bears all risk of financial loss from its presentation
of the amusement and the amusement is limited to an engagement of not more than
eight calendar days over the course of a calendar year; or
                  ii.   Is substantially and materially involved in the
production and performance of the amusement.
            2.   Where an amusement is sponsored or conducted by two or more
artistic societies or organizations, the requirements of divisions (B)(5)
(g)1.a. and (B)(5)(g)1.b. above must be met by each of such artistic societies
or organizations, but the requirements of division (B)(5)(g)1.c. above may be
met by any of such artistic societies or organizations, individually or in
combination.
   (C)   (1)   None of the exemptions contained in division (B)(5) above shall
apply to a person or privilege unless a written notice of the amusement is
filed with the Department of Revenue at least 30 calendar days prior to the
amusement or 15 calendar days prior to the date that admission tickets to the
amusement are first made available for sale, whichever is earlier. The notice
shall be on a form prescribed by the Director of Revenue, and shall contain all
information and materials necessary to permit the Department to consider
whether the exemption claimed by the applicant is applicable.
      (2)   Upon the request of the person filing the notice, the Department
shall indicate within 14 calendar days after receiving the notice whether the
claimed exemption does or does not apply, or whether additional information is
necessary to make a determination.
   (D)   (1)   The tax imposed in division (A) above shall not apply to or be
imposed upon the admission fees to witness in person live theatrical, live
musical or other live cultural performances that take place in any auditorium,
theater or other space in the village whose maximum capacity, including all
balconies and other sections, is not more than 750 persons.
      (2)   Initiation fees and membership dues paid to a health club,
racquetball club, tennis club or a similar club or organization, when such club
or organization is organized and operated on a membership basis and for the
recreational purposes of its members and its members’ guests, shall be exempt
from the tax imposed in division (A) above. This exemption shall not be
construed to apply to any fees paid or based upon, in any way whatsoever, a
per-event or a per-admission basis.
   (E)   The rate of the tax imposed in division (A) above shall be 4% of the
admission fees or other charges to witness in person live theatrical, live
musical or other live cultural performances that take place in any auditorium,
theater or other space in the village whose maximum capacity, including all
balconies and other sections, is more than 750 persons.
   (F)   The tax imposed in division (A) above shall apply to and be imposed
upon 60% of the admission fees or other charges (including, but not limited to,
the gross, lease or rental amount) paid for the privilege of using special
seating areas to witness or to view an amusement.
   (G)   It shall be presumed that all amusements are subject to tax under this
chapter until the contrary is established by books, records or other
documentary evidence.
   (H)   For the purpose of determining the amount of the amusement tax due
under this section, admission fees or other charges shall be computed exclusive
of this tax, any federal, state or county taxes imposed upon the amusement
patron and any separately stated charges for non-amusement services or for
sales of tangible personal property.
   (I)   It is unlawful for any person to produce, present, conduct or resell
tickets to any amusement without collection of the tax, except as provided in
this chapter.
   (J)   Notwithstanding division (A) above, if an owner, manager or operator
of an amusement or of a place where an amusement is being held, or if a
reseller of tickets to an amusement, is a party to a franchise agreement or any
other agreement with the village pursuant to which the owner, manager, operator
or reseller compensates the village for the right to use the public way or to
do business in the village, liability under the tax imposed by division (A)
above shall be reduced by 95% of the amount paid to the village pursuant to the
agreement.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.003 COLLECTIONS, PAYMENT AND ACCOUNTING.
   (A)   It shall be the joint and several duty of every owner, manager or
operator of an amusement or of a place where an amusement is being held, and of
every reseller of tickets to an amusement, to secure from each patron the tax
imposed by §
112.002 of this chapter and to remit the tax to the Department of Revenue not
later than the last day of each calendar month for all admission fees or other
charges received during the immediately preceding calendar month; provided,
however, that, a reseller of tickets shall be required to collect and remit tax
to the Department only on that portion of the ticket price that exceeds the
original or face amount of the tickets. A verified statement of admission fees
or charges in a form prescribed by the Director of Revenue shall accompany each
remittance. Acceptance by the village of any amount tendered in payment of the
tax shall be without prejudice to any claim, demand or right on account of any
deficiency. Effective 7-1-2006, each owner, manager, operator or reseller that
collects and remits taxes in accordance with this section may retain 1% of the
taxes it collects under this chapter to reimburse itself for expenses incurred
in connection with accounting for and remitting the taxes to the Department;
provided that, this service fee shall not be allowed for taxes not timely
remitted to the Department; and, provided further that, this service fee shall
not apply to any taxes that are collected and remitted pursuant to the terms of
a contract between the operator and the village.
   (B)   Every person required to collect and remit the tax imposed by §
112.002 of this chapter, or pay the tax directly to the Department, shall keep
accurate books and records of its business or activity, including original
source documents and books of entry denoting the transaction that gave rise, or
may have given rise, to the tax liability or any exemption that may be claimed.
All such books, records and accounts shall be available for inspection by the
Department at all reasonable times during business hours of the day.
   (C)   Every owner, manager, operator or reseller of tickets, who is required
to collect the tax imposed by §
112.002 of this chapter shall be considered a Tax Collector for the village.
All amusement tax collected shall be held by such Tax Collector as trustee for
and on behalf of the village. The failure of the Tax Collector to collect the
tax shall not excuse or release the patron from the obligation to pay the tax.
   (D)   Notwithstanding any other provision of this code, in order to permit
sound fiscal planning and budgeting by the village, no person shall be entitled
to a refund of, or credit for, either tax imposed by this chapter unless the
person files a claim for refund or credit within one year after the date on
which the tax was paid or remitted to the Department. This provision shall
apply to any claim for credit or refund for which the Director has not issued a
final determination as of the effective date of this division (D).
   (E)   Notwithstanding division (A) above, a reseller of tickets shall not be
required to collect the tax imposed by §
112.002 of this chapter, and remit the tax to the Department of Revenue, if the
purchaser of such tickets will in turn act as a reseller of the same tickets;
provided that, the purchaser supplies to the reseller:
      (1)   A written verification that the purchaser intends to resell the
tickets; and
      (2)   The tax registration number issued to the purchaser by the
Department of Revenue.
   (F)   Notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter, for all periods
beginning on or after 7-1-2006:
      (1)   All tax returns shall be filed with the Department on an annual
basis on or August 15 of each year;
      (2)   All tax payments and remittances shall be made in accordance with
the protocol established for the payment of actual tax liabilities or estimated
taxes given in this code; and
      (3)   The provisions outlined as duties of the taxpayer and the Tax
Collector shall control over any contrary provisions in this chapter regarding
the subjects covered by those sections.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.004 RATE OF TAX.
   (A)   (1)   In addition to the tax imposed by §
112.002 of this chapter, a tax is imposed upon persons that sell tickets in the
village for theatricals, shows, exhibitions, athletic events and other
amusements within the village at a place other than the theater or location
where the amusement is given or exhibited.
      (2)   The rate of this tax shall be 8% of any service fees or similar
charges received by the seller in connection with the sale of such tickets in
the village, as distinguished from the admission fees or other charges paid for
the privilege to enter, to witness, to view or to participate in such
amusements.
      (3)   This tax shall not apply if the theatrical, show, exhibition,
athletic event or other amusement is exempt or otherwise not subject to the tax
imposed by §
112.002 of this chapter.
   (B)   To prevent multiple taxation, upon proof that a taxpayer has paid a
similar tax in another state or municipality with respect to the service fee or
similar charge received by a seller in connection with the sale of tickets in
the village, the taxpayer shall be allowed a credit against the tax authorized
by division (A) above to the extent of the amount of such tax properly due and
paid in such other state or municipality.
   (C)   (1)   Sellers of tickets shall pay the tax imposed by this section to
the Department of Revenue not later than the last day of the calendar month
following the month they receive the service fees or similar charges. A return
prescribed by the Director of Revenue shall accompany each tax payment.
      (2)   Such sellers of tickets shall keep accurate books and records of
their business, including original source documents and books of entry, which
shall be made available for inspection by the department at all times during
business hours of the day.
   (D)   Notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter, for all periods
beginning on or after 7-1-2006:
      (1)   All tax returns shall be filed with the Department on an annual
basis on or August 15 of each year;
      (2)   All tax payments and remittances shall be made in accordance with
the protocol established for the payment of actual tax liabilities or estimated
taxes given in this code; and
      (3)   The provisions outlined as duties of the taxpayer and the Tax
Collector shall control over any contrary provisions in this chapter regarding
the subjects covered by those sections.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.005 RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The Director of Revenue is authorized to adopt, promulgate and enforce rules
and regulations pertaining to the interpretation, administration and
enforcement of this chapter, including, but not limited to, the meaning and
scope of the exemptions contained in §
112.002 of this chapter.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)

this chapter is silent, the provisions of the Revenue Ordinance for procedures
for the village, as amended, shall apply and supplement this chapter.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.007 RAFFLES.
   (A)   Terms defined. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      ACT. An act to provide for licensing and regulating certain games of
chance as provided in governing state statutes, as may be amended from time to
time.
      RAFFLE, RELIGIOUS, CHARITABLE, LABOR, FRATERNAL, EDUCATIONAL and
VETERANS. The respective meanings specified in §
112.125 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Licenses; issuance by Revenue Department. The Revenue Director shall
have the authority to issue licenses for raffles, as defined in the act,
subject to the limitations stated in §
112.126 of this chapter.
   (C)   Licenses; requirements. See §
112.126(B) in this chapter for eligibility requirements for license.
   (D)   Separate licenses; fee; term. Each raffles must be authorized by a
separate license. Each application for a license shall be accompanied by
payment of a fee of $500. The license shall be valid for the duration of one
year.
   (E)   Raffle tickets. Each raffle ticket, chance or other raffle token shall
state on its face, the name and address of the licensee, the date or dates of
the drawing and the prize or prizes to be awarded; provided, however, that,
this requirement shall not apply to any raffle in which prizes in aggregate
value under $50 are awarded. No such ticket, chance or token shall be sold or
issued more than 364 days before the determination of the winning chance or
chances.
   (F)   Prizes; fees. The maximum cash prize awarded in any raffle, the
maximum retail value of a non-cash prize awarded in any raffle, and the
aggregate value of all prizes awarded in any raffle shall be as set forth in §
112.126(D) of this chapter. The maximum fee for any chance shall be shall be as
set forth in §
112.126(E) of this chapter. All such fees shall be paid in currency or by
check.
   (G)   Publication of rules and regulations. The Director of Revenue, or his
or her designated agent, shall publish rules and regulations not inconsistent
with this chapter or the act governing the conduct of raffles licensed
hereunder.
   (H)   Fee exemption conditions. Notwithstanding any provision of division
(D) above, no license fee shall be charged for any other raffle conducted by
qualifying organization in the same calendar year during which such
organization has paid a raffle license fee and conducted the licensed raffle.
   (I)   Auxiliaries and affiliates of organizations. Whenever used in this
chapter, the word ORGANIZATION shall include an auxiliary or affiliate of a
licensee.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006; Ord. 09-468, passed 3-2-2009)
AUTOMATIC AMUSEMENT DEVICES
§ 112.020 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning. Any terms not
defined herein shall have the meaning ascribed to it in other ordinances of the
municipality and, if not defined in any other municipal ordinances, it shall
have the meaning ascribed in the state statutes.
   A COUNT OF PAYOFFS OF THE NUMBER OF TIMES PLAYER HAS WON A GAME PLANE ON THE
DEVICE. A tally, whether on paper, mechanical or electronic, and regardless of
whether maintained inside, on or outside the automatic amusement device. The
phrase is not intended to include a record of scores, accessible to players of
the device, and linked to previous players’ names, nicknames, initials or other
identifiers, for purposes of comparison and competition.
   AUTOMATIC AMUSEMENT DEVICE.
      (1)   Any machine, which, upon the insertion of a coin, slug, token, card
or similar object, or upon any other payment method, may be operated by the
public generally for use as a game, entertainment or amusement, whether or not
registering a score, and includes, but is not limited to, such devices as
jukeboxes, marble machines, pinball machines, movie and video booths or stands
and all games, operations or transactions similar thereto under whatever name
by which they may be indicated. Bingo devices are deemed gambling devices and
are therefore prohibited from use, except as provided by state law.
      (2)   If a machine consists of more than one game monitor which permits
individuals to play separate games simultaneously, each separate game monitor
shall be deemed an AUTOMATIC AMUSEMENT DEVICE.
   ILLEGAL AMUSEMENT DEVICE.
      (1)   An automatic amusement device that: includes a knock-off circuit;
or allows more than ten replays or free games, or maintains a count of payoffs
or the number of times a person has won a game played on the device; or
maintains a tally of players’ scores other than the tally displayed to players;
or fails to display in the required manner a tax emblem required by chapter; or
has been used for illegal gambling.
      (2)   ILLEGAL AMUSEMENT DEVICE does not include a device that properly
displays a required tax emblem, that is not used for illegal gambling and that
qualifies either as a crane game or as a redemption machine as defined in the
Criminal Code of 2012, being 720 ILCS 5/1-1 et seq. as now or hereafter
amended.
      (3)   An automatic amusement device shall not be deemed an ILLEGAL
AUTOMATIC AMUSEMENT DEVICE because of internal diagnostic devices or
capabilities that are able to record and maintain statistical data such as the
number of coins or tokens deposited, the number of games played or the number
of games won, if such diagnostic devices or capabilities are intended and used
exclusively for auditing of game performance.
   KNOCK-OFF CIRCUIT. Any mechanical or electrical device, circuitry or
modification on an automatic amusement device, whereby free games shown on an
externally visible indicator are released, while a record of games so released
is maintained on a second indicator, meter or counter, either inside or outside
the device. A reset button installed by the manufacturer of the automatic
amusement device shall not, without more, constitute a KNOCK-OFF CIRCUIT.
   MORE THAN 10 REPLAYS OR FREE GAMES. More than ten replays or free games at
one time. Free game or replay does not include an extension of a game awarded
as a result of the player’s skill, such as an extra ball in a pinball game or
extended playing time in a video game.
   PAYOFF. The giving of money or other thing of value in exchange for a
player’s accumulated points or free games or replays.
   TALLY OF PLAYERS’ SCORES OTHER THAN THE TALLY DISPLAYED TO PLAYERS. Does not
include a record of scores, accessible to players of the device, and linked to
previous players’ names, nicknames, initials or other identifiers, for purposes
of comparison and competition.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.021 TAX IMPOSED.
   An annual tax in the amount of $150 for non-gambling-type automatic
amusement devices and $225 for gambling-type automatic amusement devices for
each calendar year is imposed upon all automatic amusement devices operated for
gain or profit per device.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.022 TAX EMBLEM.
   (A)   The automatic amusement device tax shall be paid by the owner of such
device to the Department of Revenue and Administrative Services.
   (B)   The Revenue Director shall issue as evidence of the payment of the tax
a self-voiding adhesive tax emblem to be placed on each device. Such emblem
shall bear the words “Village of Dolton Amusement Device Tax”, the names of the
Mayor and Village Clerk and such other wording as may be prescribed by the
Mayor.
   (C)   It shall be unlawful for any person to mutilate said tax emblem during
the year for which it was issued.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.023 INSTALLATION PREREQUISITES.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for the owner or lessee of any premises or person
in control of such premises to permit the installation or use of an automatic
amusement device within the village for gain or profit unless the tax has been
paid and is evidenced by a tax emblem affixed to the automatic amusement
device. Each such device shall be plainly labeled with the name, address and
telephone number of its owner.
   (B)   No person shall remove, alter or deface the tax emblem or label
required by this section, or allow use of an automatic amusement machine if the
tax emblem or label has been removed, altered, defaced or become illegible.
   (C)   The owner or lessee of the premises where the device is placed for
operation by the public and every person responsible for the premises shall be
jointly and severally liable for a violation of this section.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.024 SEIZURE FOR UNLAWFUL USE.
   (A)   If the Mayor, Police Chief or Revenue Director, or their duly
authorized enforcement officer, shall have a reasonable basis for believing any
amusement device is an illegal amusement device, said device or any part or
contents thereof may be seized by any duly authorized enforcement official,
followed by an administrative hearing with notice to the owner within seven
days of such seizure for the purpose of reviewing the appropriateness of the
seizure, and held until such time as the owner of such device pays the
delinquent tax, reimburses the Police Department for actual cartage cost
incurred in the seizure and pays to the Department of Revenue $20 for each day
or part of day said device has been in storage.
   (B)   If criminal charges involving the use or condition of the device are
pending, the device shall be held until disposition of the criminal charges. If
it is determined at the hearing, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the
seized device is not an illegal amusement device, it shall be returned to the
owner without charge.
   (C)   If it is determined at the hearing that the automatic amusement device
was used for illegal gambling, it shall be destroyed by the village, and all
money found within the device at the time of confiscation shall become the
property of the village, and shall be used to defray the costs of cartage,
notice, storage and hearings.
   (D)   If the owner of the device does not claim the automatic amusement
device within 14 days after the mailing of the notice, the device and its
contents will be treated as abandoned property and the device will be
destroyed.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.025 LICENSING PROVISIONS.
   (A)   License required. See §
112.101 of this chapter for eligibility requirements for license.
   (B)   License application; examination of records.
      (1)   An application for an automatic amusement device operator’s license
shall be made in conformity with the general requirements of this chapter
relating to application for license.
      (2)   The Department of Revenue, upon reasonable notice, shall have the
authority to examine all books and records of automatic amusement device

      (3)   The license fee for an automatic amusement device operator’s
license shall be as set forth in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
   (C)   Application; investigation. See §
112.104 of this chapter for application investigation and inspection.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)

arcade unless the person in control of such place has first obtained a public
place of amusement license.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
