§ 112.027 RESTRICTIONS ON USE BY MINORS.
   (A)   No person, firm, corporation, organization or other legal entity shall
permit, and it shall be unlawful for, any person under 17 years of age, who is
not accompanied by a parent or guardian, to operate any automatic amusement
device, except upon the premises of the village airports, between the hours of
8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. on days in which the village’s public schools are in
session.
   (B)   No person, firm, corporation, organization or other legal entity shall
permit, and it shall be unlawful for, any person under the age of 21 to play an
automatic amusement device located at an establishment which sells alcoholic
liquor for consumption on the premises. The prohibition described in this
division (B) shall not prohibit any person or legal entity to permit any person
under the age of 21 to play an automatic amusement device located at an
establishment which sells alcoholic liquor for consumption on the premises, if:
      (1)   The minor is accompanied by a parent or guardian; and/or
      (2)   The establishment is a restaurant holding a valid license issued
under §§
120.40 through
120.50 of this code of ordinances.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
PUBLIC PLACES OF AMUSEMENT
§ 112.040 DEFINITION.
   A PUBLIC PLACE OF AMUSEMENT means any building or part of a building, park
or other grounds used or intended to be used for any amusement, as defined in §
112.001 of this chapter.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.041 LICENSING PROVISIONS.
   (A)   License required.
      (1)   (a)   Unless specifically exempted in division (B) below, it shall
be unlawful for the owner, lessee or manager of any property, or for any other
person, to produce, present or conduct thereon, for gain or profit, any
amusement unless the owner, lessee or manager of such property has first
obtained a public place of amusement license.
         (b)   If an amusement is produced presented or conducted for gain or
profit on any property without a valid public place of amusement license first
having been obtained, and unless division (B) below applies, all of the
following persons shall be in violation of this division (A)(1)(b):
            1.   The owner of the property;
            2.   The lessee of the property;
            3.   The manager of the property;
            4.   The producer of the amusement;
            5.   The presenter of the amusement; and
            6.   The person conducting the amusement.
      (2)   If any part of the property is used or intended for use for any
amusement, a public place of amusement license shall be required, regardless of
whether the use is incidental to the property’s principal use.
      (3)   If more than one amusement is produced, presented or conducted at
any single place or premises as part of a single business, only one public
place of amusement license shall be required.
      (4)   A special class of public place of amusement license shall be
required for any public resort which is designed, used or intended to be used
primarily for participation by minors in entertainment or amusement primarily
involving music, music videos and dancing. Examples of such resorts include,
but are not limited to, a dry dance hall, non-alcohol bar, dry cabaret, juice
bar or teenage cabaret This class of license shall be known as a juice bar
license. No juice bar licensee may operate between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and
11:00 a.m. No premises requiring a juice bar license shall be eligible for a
retail liquor license.
      (5)   Any person who owns, operates or manages an establishment requiring
a juice bar license without first obtaining such license shall be subject to
revocation of all village licenses pertaining to that establishment.
   (B)   License exceptions. No public place of amusement license shall be
required, if the only amusement to be produced, presented or conducted is one
or more of the following:
      (1)   A single pool or billiard table regardless of whether players must
pay to use the pool or billiard table;
      (2)   Less than four automatic amusement devices; provided, however,
that, when calculating the number of automatic amusement devices, jukeboxes
shall not be counted. A pool or billiard table shall be included when
calculating the number of automatic amusement devices for purposes of this
division (B)(2) if players must pay to use the pool or billiard table; provided
that, in no case shall this division (B)(2) create an exemption for
establishments which contain more than one pool or billiard table regardless of
whether any payment is required;
      (3)   Music, dancing or other amusement, if:
         (a)   It is offered in a venue with a capacity of less than 100
persons; and
         (b)   No admission fee, minimum purchase requirement, membership fee
or other fee or charge is imposed for the privilege of entering the premises or
the portion of premises where the music, dancing or other amusement is provided
or permitted.
      (4)   Live or recorded music and dancing in a banquet hall, restaurant or
similar establishment if:
         (a)   The owner of the establishment possesses the necessary retail
food establishment license;
         (b)   The music and dancing is being presented in connection with an
event which is not open or advertised to the general public, including a
wedding, graduation or religious celebration; and
         (c)   No admission fee, minimum purchase requirement, membership fee
or other fee or charge is imposed for the privilege of entering the premises or
the portion of premises where the music and dancing is provided or permitted.
      (5)   Live or recorded readings from books or other publications
available for sale within the premises of a retail seller of books or other
publications, and the presentation of live or recorded music within the
premises of a retail seller of printed or recorded music, if:
         (a)   The owner of the establishment possesses the necessary retail
establishment license;
         (b)   The retail activity conducted on the premises is not the sale of
alcoholic liquor; and
         (c)   No admission fee, minimum purchase requirement or other fee or
charge is imposed for the privilege of entering the premises or the portion of
premises where the reading or musical presentation takes place.
      (6)   Instrumental music by an orchestra of not more than eight pieces in
a hotel, restaurant or retail establishment if:
         (a)   No dancing or other entertainment is permitted; and
         (b)   No admission fee, minimum purchase requirement, membership fee
or other fee or charge is imposed for the privilege of entering the premises or
the portion of premises where the music is provided or permitted.
      (7)   (a)   Any amusement produced, presented or conducted on the
premises owned or leased, for a minimum lease term of one year, by a private
club or lodge that is produced, presented or conducted either:
            1.   Solely for its members and their guests; or
            2.   As part of a program to augment the support of the fine or
performing arts by a club that has been in continuous existence for more than
50 years.
         (b)   For purposes of this division (B)(7), PRIVATE CLUB OR LODGE
means any not-for-profit association that:
            1.   Has been in active and continuous existence for at least three
years; and
            2.   Has a membership role of more than 50 bona fide members who
pay membership dues on an annual or other periodic basis.
         (c)   For purposes of this division (B)(7), BONA FIDE MEMBERS do not
include members who pay membership dues at the time of an amusement produced,
presented or conducted by the club or lodge or in conjunction with contracting
for production, presentation or conduct of an amusement by the club, as a
condition to entering the premises where the amusement is produced, presented
or conducted.
         (d)   For purposes of division (B)(7)(c) above, a private club’s
program of supporting the fine or performing arts must include offering
residential facilities to performers or artists; offering a venue for practice
and performances; and availability of facilities for the discussion, promotion
and development of skills and interests in the fine or performing arts. A
private club or lodge, at the request of the Department of Revenue or the
Department of Police, shall make available for inspection records and documents
that provide evidence of its not-for-profit status and membership roles.
      (8)   Paid television programming; or a health club, racquetball club,
tennis club or a similar club or organization when such club or organization is
organized and operated on a membership basis and for the recreational purposes
of its members and its members’ guests. For purposes of this division (B)(8),
when determining whether a venue has a capacity of more than 100 persons, the
total occupancy of all rooms or other occupancy areas of the premises of the
business operating the amusement shall be calculated.
   (C)   License application; contents.
      (1)   An application for said license shall be made in conformity with
the general requirements of this code of ordinances relating to applications
for licenses. Said application shall be signed under oath by the owner of the
business for which a license is sought. If the owner is a corporation, the
application shall be signed by an authorized officer of the corporation. If the
owner is a partnership, the application shall be signed by a partner. If the
owner is a limited liability company that is managed by managers, the
application shall be signed by a manager. If the owner is a limited liability
company managed by members, the application shall be signed by a member.
      (2)   The application shall set forth the location and a description of
the property used or intended for use as a public place of amusement,
indicating the seating capacity and the floor area or ground area of the place,
the types of amusements which the applicant intends to conduct on the property,
and shall include the following:
         (a)   The name, residence address, current telephone number and Social
Security number of the applicant in the case of an individual; in the case of a
partnership, the names, residence addresses, Social Security numbers and
percentage of interest therein of the three members who own the highest
percentage interest in such partnership and of any other member who holds a 25%
or more interest therein; in the case of a limited partnership, the names,
residence addresses, Social Security numbers, and percentage interest therein
of each general partner thereof; in the case of a corporation, the date of
incorporation, the objects for which it was organized, a summary of its
activities during the past year, and the names, residence addresses and Social
Security numbers of its principal officers, those stockholders who own 25% or
more of its voting shares; in the case of a limited liability company, the date
of its formation, the objects for which it was organized, a summary of its
activities during the past year and the names, residence addresses, Social
Security numbers and percentage of interest of the three members who own the
highest percentage interests in such limited liability company, of any other
member who holds a 25% or more interest therein and, if the limited liability
company is manager-managed, the names, residence addresses and Social Security
numbers of all managers; and in the case of a club, the date of its
incorporation, the objects for which it was organized, a summary of its
activities during the past year and the names, residence addresses and Social
Security numbers of the officers and directors. If the applicant is a
partnership, limited partnership, corporation, limited liability company or
club, the applicant shall also provide the current telephone number of its
authorized agent;
         (b)   The name and address of the owner of the premises. If the
premises are leased:
            1.   A copy of the lease, unless the applicant already has a lease
for premises on file with the Department of Revenue and no changes have been
made to the lease since it was filed;
            2.   The name, address and telephone number of the owner of the
premises, including the name and address of the beneficiary if title to the
premises is held by a person as trustee and if known to the applicant; and
            3.   The name, address, Social Security number and telephone number
of the manager of the premises.
         (c)   A copy of each agreement for management of the licensed
business; and
         (d)   A statement as to whether the applicant has made application for
a similar license on premises other than that described in the application and
the disposition of such application.
      (3)   If a change in any information required in this division (C) occurs
at any time during a license period, the licensee shall file a statement,
executed in the same manner as an application, indicating the nature and
effective date of the change. The supplemental statement shall be filed within
ten days after the change takes effect. The Department of Revenue shall take
measures to prevent disclosure of confidential information required under this
division (C) and not subject to disclosure under the state’s Freedom of
Information Act, being 5 ILCS 140/1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended, to
persons outside the government.
   (D)   License application; approval conditions.
      (1)   Each application and all information required to be furnished in
connection therewith or a copy thereof shall be referred for approval to the
Building Commissioner, the Zoning Administrator, the person designated as the
Director in charge of the Bureau of Fire Prevention and Police Chief. The
Police Chief shall require the following individuals to submit to
fingerprinting in order to determine whether the issuance of the license is
prohibited pursuant to division (E) below: the individual applicant; all
officers of an applicant corporation; the three members who own the highest
percentage interests of an applicant partnership; the general partners of an
applicant limited partnership; the three members who own the highest percentage
interests and, in the case of a member-managed limited liability company, the
manager of an applicant limited liability company, unless the above listed
individuals are already named on a valid liquor license or are named in a
liquor license application that has been filed and is being processed for the
same premises for which the public place of amusement license is sought. Within
21 days after receipt of the application of copy thereof, and all other
information requested of the applicant by any department whose approval is
necessary, each department shall certify to the Mayor whether or not the place
and the applicant complies in every respect with the applicable provisions of
this code of ordinances relating to that department. No license shall be issued
without approval by the Mayor.
      (2)   The Mayor shall review the application and the reports of the
departments and shall determine within 14 days after receipt thereof whether or
not the subject property complies with the applicable provisions of the code;
provided, however, that, the Mayor may extend the period of such review for an
additional 15 days to allow completion of the review, if necessary. If the
Mayor finds that either subject property or the applicant does not comply with
applicable provisions of this municipal code, he or she shall disapprove the
application, and the requirements of §
30.04(D) of this code of ordinances relating to disapproval of license
applications shall apply.
   (E)   License issuance prohibited. No public place of amusement license
shall be issued to:
      (1)   A person who has been convicted of a felony, within the past ten
years, under any federal or state law;
      (2)   A person who knowingly files false or incomplete information on an
application for a public place of amusement license or any other document
required by this chapter.
      (3)   A person whose license, issued by the village under any chapter of
this municipal code, has been revoked for cause within the past five years;
      (4)   A person who at the time of application for renewal of a public
place of amusement license would not be eligible for such license upon a first
application;
      (5)   A corporation, partnership, limited partnership or limited
liability company, if any of the officers, substantial owners, members or other
individuals required to be identified in the initial license application by
division (C)(1) above would not be eligible to receive a license hereunder;
      (6)   A corporation unless it is incorporated in the state, or unless it
is a foreign corporation which is qualified under the Business Corporation Act
of 1983 to transact business in the state; provided that, the corporation is
not dissolved and is in good standing under the laws of the state;
      (7)   A person who is not a beneficial owner of the business for which a
license is sought;
      (8)   A person whose place of business is conducted by a manager or agent
unless the person demonstrates that the manager or agent possesses the
qualifications required to obtain a license hereunder; or
      (9)   A person whose public place of amusement license has not undergone
and passed a building inspection as required by this code of ordinances within
the 90 days preceding the date of submission of an annual renewal license
application.
   (F)   License annual fees.
      (1)   The annual license fee for each public place of amusement shall be
as set forth as follows: the fee for each public place of amusement license
shall be graded according to the capacity in accordance with the following
schedule:
Maximum Capacity Fee
Maximum Capacity Fee
1 - 350          $385
351 - 500        $550
501 - 750        $750
751 - 1,000      $1,100
1,001 - 2,000    $1,650
2,001 - 3,000    $2,200
3,001 - 4,000    $3,300
Over 4,000       $6,600
 
      (2)   Notwithstanding the foregoing, the annual license fee for a
performing arts venue with an aggregate maximum occupancy of all performance
spaces within the building of less than 500 persons shall be $55 and the annual
license fee for all other performing arts venues shall be equal to $1
multiplied by the total occupancy of all performance spaces within the
building.
      (3)   When computing the capacity of a public place of amusement, other
than a performing arts venue, the total occupancy of all rooms or other
occupancy areas of the premises of the business operating the amusement shall
be calculated.
   (G)   Term of license. The term shall be May 1 through April 30, annually.
   (H)   Statement of conditions. Every license shall contain apt words
indicating that it is issued and accepted subject to the representations made
in the application and to all laws, ordinances and regulations governing the
conduct of the licensed premises now in effect or which may hereafter be
adopted.
   (I)   License restrictions. No public place of amusement license shall be
granted to any establishment if there already exists a public place of
amusement license in the same area, except for establishments designated for
motion pictures, motor vehicle repair or motor vehicle washes.
   (J)   License revocation.
      (1)   The Mayor may revoke any license for default in the payment or
performance of any obligation to the village under the provisions of this
chapter or for the violation of any provisions in this code of ordinances or
the laws of the state, applicable to the licensee or the licensed premises.
      (2)   A license issued or renewed after the effective date of this
division (J) shall be subject to suspension or revocation if the licensee’s
business becomes or creates a nuisance. A licensed business is or creates a
nuisance if within any consecutive 12 months not less than five separate
incidents occur on the licensed premises, involving acts that violate any
federal or state law defining a felony or any federal or state law or municipal
ordinance regulating narcotics, controlled substances or weapons. It is not a
defense to a charge of violating this division (J) that the licensee or the
licensee’s employees or agents were not personally involved in the commission
of the illegal acts.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.042 NOTICE REQUIREMENTS; OBJECTIONS.
   (A)   Within five days of receipt of an application for a public place of
amusement license, the Department of Revenue shall cause a written notice to be
sent to the alderman of the ward in which the premises described in the
application is located, providing the information specified in §
112.041(C) of this chapter and the current telephone number of the applicant.
   (B)   Within five days of receiving an application, the Department of
Revenue shall serve written notice by first class, registered or certified mail
on all legal voters residing within 250 feet of the location for which the
license is sought. The measurement of such area shall be made from the
boundaries of the premises described in the application for which the license
is sought, to a radius of 250 feet away. The notice shall identify the license
being sought and shall state the name and residence address of the applicant,
the street number and location of the premises for which the license is sought
and the date on which the application will be filed. The notice shall include
the language of division (D)(1) below.
   (C)   Within five days after filing an application, the applicant shall
cause to be posted at the location of the premises for which the license is
sought, in a place clearly visible from the public way, a notice stating that
an application has been made for a public place of amusement license, the date
the application was filed, the name and residence address of the applicant and
the street number and location of the premises covered by the application. The
notice shall also include the language of division (D)(1) below.
   (D)   (1)   (a)   Within 30 days of the filing of an application for a
public place of amusement license, no less than a majority of the legal voters
residing within 250 feet of the location for which the license is sought may
file a petition with the Department of Revenue requesting the Department to
deny the license on the grounds that:
            1.   The license would cause substantial injury to the value of the
property in the neighborhood in which it is to be located;
            2.   The license would have an adverse effect on other commercial
or industrial enterprises in the surrounding area;
            3.   The license would have an adverse effect on traffic-flow or
parking within the surrounding area; or
            4.   The license would have an adverse effect on the character of
the surrounding neighborhood because of the hours of operation of use.
         (b)   To be considered the petition shall be delivered no later than
30 days after the date on which the application for the license was filed and
shall include the residence address of each person whose signature appears on
the petition.
      (2)   After the petition signatures have been validated, the Revenue
Director shall set a hearing date and shall provide notice of the hearing to
the license applicant, to the voters listed on the petition and to the Alderman
of the ward in which the premises sought to be licensed is located. Notice
shall be sent by first class, registered or certified mail. The Revenue
Director shall cause to be published, in a daily newspaper of general
circulation in the village, a notice stating that a public hearing has been
scheduled regarding the application for a public place of amusement license
setting forth the address of the premises sought to be licensed and the date,
time and location of the hearing. The hearing shall be commenced no later than
30 days after validated signatures have been received by the Department of
Revenue. The Revenue Director or his or her designee may deny the license, upon
a showing of due cause, for any of the grounds listed in divisions (D)(1)(a)1.
through (D)(1)(a)4. above. A decision denying the application for a license may
be appealed by the applicant to the Department of Revenue’s Adjudication
Division.
      (3)   This section shall not limit the authority of the village or a
department or agency of the village to seek denial of an application on the
basis of other applicable law.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.043 LOCATION RESTRICTIONS.
   (A)   (1)   No license shall be issued for any place within 200 feet of any
church, hospital or building used exclusively for educational purposes, unless
the place to be licensed has been established as a public place of amusement
before the establishment of the church, hospital or educational institution.
Said distance shall be measured from the nearest point of the premises for
which application for license has been made and the nearest point of the
church, hospital or educational institution.
      (2)   This prohibition shall not apply to a performing arts venue, as
defined in §
112.065 of this chapter.
   (B)   The restrictions described in division (A) above shall not prohibit
the issuance of a license to operate a public place of amusement within a
licensed hotel having accommodations for more than 150 guests, or within a
restaurant with an occupancy of more than 100 persons, if the building in which
the public place of amusement is to be located is at least ten stories in
height, and if neither the public place of amusement, nor the sale of alcoholic
liquor for consumption on the premises is the principal business conducted
within the licensed premises.
   (C)   (1)   No public place of amusement license shall be granted to any
establishment that is located within 125 feet of any R1, R2 or R3 Zoning
District, as defined in Ch. 159 of this code of ordinances, except for a
renewal license for property that was duly licensed as a public place of
amusement on the effective date of this division (C), if any, and except as
permitted as an authorized variation.
      (2)   The 125-foot distance shall be measured from the nearest property
line of the public place of amusement to the nearest property line of the R1,
R2 or R3 Zoning District. The restriction imposed by this division (C) shall
not apply to a performing arts venue, as defined in §
112.065 of this chapter.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.044 WRITTEN GUARANTY REQUIRED.
   Before any license is issued, the applicant shall execute a written
undertaking conditioned that the taxes imposed upon any amusement at the
licensed premises will be paid in the manner and at the times provided in §
112.002 of this chapter.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.045 OCCUPANCY ENFORCEMENT.
   No public place of amusement license shall be issued unless the applicant
certifies that, since the issuance of the most recent license and the most
recent occupancy sign required to be posted on the licensed premises pursuant
to the appropriate fire codes (as adopted by the village as the official Fire
Code), neither the applicant nor any other person has made any modifications or
alterations affecting the layout, floor plan, doorways, stairways, interior
separations or other features of the subject premises that may affect occupancy
limits.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.046 EXIT DIAGRAM.
   The licensee of every public place of amusement shall post diagrams, drawn
to scale, showing the locations of the exits. For every public place of
amusement that is located in a building or part of a building, the diagrams
shall be posted in the same locations as the occupancy signs required under
this section. For any public place of amusement that is a park or other outdoor
venue that is enclosed by a fence or other enclosure, the diagrams shall be
conspicuously posted in the entrance to the park or outdoor venue.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.047 TICKET SALES.
   It is unlawful for any licensee to sell or permit any person to sell any
ticket of admission to the licensed premises unless it has conspicuously
printed upon its face the price of admission.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.048 SPECIFIC BUSINESSES.
   (A)   It shall be the duty of the licensee of any motion picture theater to
exhibit on a billboard, placed in front of the building or other structure in
which such show is given and such motion pictures are exhibited, the title to
the pictures, which title shall either be full enough to describe in general
terms the nature and character of the picture or pictures to be shown, or shall
be accompanied by other explanatory wording, pictures or other advertising
matter so as to describe the said picture or pictures.
   (B)   No such licensee shall place, maintain or allow to be placed or
maintained in front of or in connection with any such place any sign, picture
or other announcement which in any manner misstates or misrepresents the
picture or other amusements which are being shown in said place, or which
announces a picture or other form of amusement or entertainment which is not,
at the time such announcement is displayed, being shown and exhibited in said
place.
   (C)   See §
112.126(B) of this chapter for provisions pertaining to minors and hours of
operation.
   (D)   (1)   It shall be unlawful for any licensee to conduct or permit any
person to conduct any exhibition where the intent or outcome of the exhibition
or match is to injure or harm one of the contestants and the exhibition is
unregulated by the state. The terms of the section may be enforced by the
Village Prosecuting Attorney through injunction or any other suit, action or
proceeding at law or in equity.
      (2)   It is unlawful for any licensee to conduct or permit any person to
conduct any raffle, lottery or chance distribution of money, or article of
value, or any gilt enterprise or any form of gambling upon the licensed
premises.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.049 LIABILITY FOR CERTAIN ADDITIONAL VILLAGE SERVICES.
   (A)   The business entity benefitting from the traffic management services
provided by the village in connection with an event presented at a conference
or exhibition facility shall pay to the village an amount equal to the sum of
100% of the non-overtime hourly rate for village police officers, for each hour
of time worked by a police officer in providing traffic management services
related to the event.
   (B)   No later than 30 days before an event to be held in a conference or
exhibition facility, the business entity benefitting from traffic management
services shall notify the Police Chief and the Director of the Emergency
Services and Disaster Agency (ESDA) of the date, time and nature of the event,
and the teams or other entities participating in the event.
   (C)   The Police Department and ESDA shall maintain a record of the hours
worked by police officers in providing traffic management services related to
an event at a qualifying exhibition facility. The records shall indicate the
date, location and nature of each event; the number of police officers, if any,
providing traffic management services related to the event and the total number
of hours worked by those police officers. At the end of each calendar quarter,
the records shall be delivered to the Department of Revenue, which shall issue
separate bills to each business entity benefitting from traffic services. The
business entity shall pay the amount billed no later than 30 days after the
date of mailing indicated on the bill. Amounts due under this section shall
constitute a debt due and owing the village.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.050 SPECIAL EVENT ALLOWANCE.
   An establishment may host up to six special events in a 12-month period
before a public place of amusement license is required. The event organizers
must be a recognized not-for-profit corporation and must obtain all necessary
food, liquor and special event licenses from the Department of Revenue. The
establishment must have passed an inspection from the Department of Buildings
and the Bureau of Fire Prevention. Private events where no admission fee,
minimum purchase requirement, membership fee or other fee or charge is imposed
for the privilege of entering the premises or the portion of premises where the
event is held and that are not advertised to the public shall not constitute as
special event for purposes of this section.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.051 SUBJECT TO TAXATION.
   Nothing in this subchapter shall be construed to impose a tax upon any
person, business or activity which, under the Constitutions of the United
States or the state, may not be made the subject of taxation by the village.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
PERFORMING ARTS
§ 112.065 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning. Any terms not
defined herein shall have the meaning ascribed to it in other ordinances of the
municipality, and if not defined in any other municipal ordinances, it shall
have the meaning ascribed in the state statutes.
   PERFORMANCE SPACE. The portion of the premises where the live theatrical or
other live cultural performance is provided or permitted, and does not include
any hallway, lobby or public restroom.
   PERFORMING ARTS VENUE. A building or portion thereof in which the aggregate
maximum occupancy of all performance spaces within the building is less than
500 persons and which is used by an organization for live theatrical and other
live cultural performances. If the organization is operating as an incidental
use in a building that is primarily used in the conduct of activities of a
religious, philanthropic, educational, eleemosynary or other not-for-profit
organization, the aggregate maximum occupancy of all performance spaces within
the building shall be less than 1,000 persons.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
§ 112.066 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for the owner, lessee or manager of any property,
or for any other person, to produce, present or conduct thereon, any amusement
within a performing arts venue unless the owner, lessee or manager of such
property has first obtained a performing arts venue license. Such license shall
be known as an “arts venue license”.
   (B)   (1)   The arts venue license shall be a special class of public place
of amusement license and shall be subject to the same restrictions and
requirements as a public place of amusement license, except as set forth in
this subchapter.
      (2)   In the event of a conflict between the general public place of
amusement license provisions and the provisions of this subchapter, the
provisions of this subchapter shall apply.
   (C)   (1)   No arts venue license shall be required if the only amusement to
be produced, presented or conducted is:
         (a)   Offered in a performance space with a capacity of less than 100
persons; and
         (b)   No admission fee, minimum purchase requirement, membership fee
or other fee or charge is imposed for the privilege of entering the premises or
the portion of premises where the amusement is provided or permitted.
      (2)   (a)   Donations that are solicited strictly on a voluntary basis
may be accepted by a venue under this division (C) only if the venue posts a
sign, no less than eight and one-half inches by eleven inches, in a conspicuous
place near the entrance of the venue stating.
         (b)   Under this section, this performing arts venue may not charge an
admission fee, minimum purchase requirement, membership fee or other fee or
charge imposed for the privilege of entering the premises.
         (c)   Any donations are purely voluntary.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.067 LICENSE APPLICATION; CONTENTS.
   (A)   (1)   An application for an arts venue license shall be made in
conformity with the general requirements of this chapter relating to
applications for licenses. Said application shall be signed under oath by the
owner of the business for which a license is sought.
      (2)   If the owner is a corporation, the application shall be signed by
an authorized officer of the corporation. If the owner is a limited liability
company managed by managers, the application shall be signed by a manager. If
the owner is a limited liability company managed by members, the application
shall be signed by a member.
   (B)   The application shall set forth the location and a description of the
property used or intended for use as a performing arts venue, indicating the
estimated occupancy, the estimated seating capacity and the floor area or
ground area of the place, the types of amusements which the applicant intends
to conduct on the property, and shall include the following:
      (1)   The name, residence address and current telephone number of the
applicant in the case of an individual; in the case of a partnership, the
names, residence addresses and percentage of interest therein of the three
members who own the highest percentage interest in such partnership and of any
other member who holds a 25% or more interest therein; in the case of a limited
partnership, the names, residence addresses and percentage interest therein of
each general partner thereof, in the case of a corporation, the date of
incorporation, the objects for which it was organized, a summary of its
activities during the past year, and the names, and residences addresses of its
principal officers, those stockholders who own 25% or more of its voting
shares; in the case of a limited liability company, the date of its formation,
the objects for which it was organized, a summary of its activities during the
past year and the names, residence addresses and percentage of interest of the
three members who own the highest percentage interests in such limited
liability company, of any other member who holds a 25% or more interest therein
and, if the limited liability company is manager-managed, the names and
residence addresses of all managers. If the applicant is a partnership, limited
partnership, corporation or limited liability company, the applicant shall also
provide the current telephone number of its authorized agent;
      (2)   The name and address of the owner of the premises. If the premises
are leased:
         (a)   A copy of the current lease, unless the applicant already has a
lease for premises on file with the Department of Revenue and no changes have
been made to the lease since it was filed;
         (b)   The name, address and telephone number of the owner of the
premises, including the name and address of the beneficiary if title to the
premises is held by a person as trustee and if known to the applicant;
         (c)   The name, address and telephone number of the manager of the
premises; and
         (d) A statement as to whether the applicant has made application for a
similar license on premises other than that described in the application and
the disposition of such application.
      (3)   If a change in any information required in this section occurs at
any time during a license period, the licensee shall file a statement, executed
in the same manner as an application, indicating the nature and effective date
of the change. The supplemental statement shall be filed within 60 days after
the change takes effect. The Revenue Director shall take measures to prevent
disclosure of confidential information required under this section and not
subject to disclosure under the state’s Freedom of Information Act to persons
outside the government.
(Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006)
SWEEPSTAKES KIOSKS
§ 112.080 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   BONA FIDE PRODUCT. Any item of real value, which may include vouchers or
coupons, to be used for or towards the purchase of a retail item. BONA FIDE
PRODUCT does not include Internet access, a telephone card, a calling card or a
phone card.
   INSTANT REVEAL. The results of the outcome of a prize offer or reward are
immediately displayed.
   INTERNET ACCESS. A connection of individual computer terminals, computers,
mobile devices and computer services, such as email and the world wide web.
   NET REVENUES. Revenues derived from a sweepstakes kiosk minus the cost of
prizes paid to participants.
   PERSON. Any individual, firm, corporation or other entity doing business in
the village.
   SWEEPSTAKES. The promotion of products whether through a written or
electronic manner.
   SWEEPSTAKES KIOSKS or ELECTRONIC PRODUCT PROMOTIONS SWEEPSTAKE KIOSK. Any
electronic video machine which, upon the insertion of payment, is used to
purchase a bona fide product from a sponsor and offers or awards a prize as a
means to promote that sponsor and is otherwise consistent with the Act, para.
(13) of subs. (b) of § 28-1 of the Criminal Code of 2012, being 720 ILCS 5/28-
1 as now or hereafter amended, and the Video Gaming Act, being 230 ILCS 40/1 et
seq. as now or hereafter amended, and is not capable of connecting directly or
indirectly to the Internet, either by hardwire or wireless connection, or to a
set of interconnected networked devices.
   TELEPHONE CARD, CALLING CARD or PHONE CARD. Any stored-value system capable
of being discarded when depleted or recharged for reuse and utilized to place a
telephone call.
(Ord. 15-023, passed 7-6-2015)
§ 112.081 REGULATION; LICENSE REQUIRED.
   It is unlawful for a person to operate sweepstakes kiosks without first
obtaining a license from the village.
(Ord. 15-023, passed 7-6-2015) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.082 ELIGIBILITY.
   Only persons holding a valid liquor license from the village are eligible
for the issuance of a license under this subchapter.
(Ord. 15-023, passed 7-6-2015)
§ 112.083 ANNUAL FEE; TAX.
   (A)   The annual license fee for each electronic product promotion
sweepstakes kiosk is $500.
   (B)   A monthly tax of 5% of net revenues from each electronic product
promotion sweepstakes kiosk is hereby assessed.
(Ord. 15-023, passed 7-6-2015; Ord. 17-034, passed 10-2-2017)
§ 112.084 ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS.
   (A)   It is unlawful for a person to operate on any premises more than five
electronic product promotion sweepstakes kiosks at any one time.
   (B)   No electronic product promotion sweepstakes kiosk shall be capable of
connecting directly to the Internet, either by hardwire or wireless connection,
or to a set of interconnected networked devices, and nothing in this subchapter
may be construed to permit any person to knowingly establish, maintain, or
operate an Internet site that permits a person to play a game of chance or
skill for money or other thing of value by means of the Internet or to make a
wager upon the result of any game, contest, political nomination, appointment
or election by means of the Internet in violation of item (12) of subs. (a) of
§ 28-1 of the Criminal Code of 2012, being 720 ILCS 5/28-1 as now or hereafter
amended.
   (C)   It is unlawful for any person to operate an electronic product
promotion sweepstakes kiosk where the sale of a product is subterfuge for
gambling. A subterfuge shall be the sale of Internet access, a telephone card,
a calling card or a phone card.
   (D)   Electronic product promotion sweepstakes kiosks shall provide the
option of an instant reveal of the outcome of any prize offer or award.
(Ord. 15-023, passed 7-6-2015) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.085 ILLEGAL GAMBLING DEVICES PROHIBITED.
   Nothing in this subchapter shall in any way be construed to authorize,
license or permit any gambling devices whatsoever or any mechanism that has
been judicially determined to be a gambling device or in any way contrary to
law or that may be contrary to any future laws of the village and the state.
(Ord. 15-023, passed 7-6-2015)
MECHANICAL AMUSEMENT DEVICES AND VIDEO GAMBLING TERMINALS
§ 112.100 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   MECHANICAL AMUSEMENT DEVICE. Any machine which, upon the insertion of a
coin, slug, token, plate or disc, or payment of a fee, may be operated by the
public generally for use as a game, entertainment or amusement, whether or not
registering a score. It shall include such devices as marble machines, pinball
machines, foosball, skill ball, mechanical grab machines and all games,
operations or transactions similar thereto under whatever name they may be
indicated.
   VIDEO GAMBLING TERMINAL. The same meaning as “video gaming terminal”, as set
forth in the Video Gaming Act, 230 ILCS 40/1 et seq., as amended. For purposes
of this subchapter, all other definitions and requirements of the Video Gaming
Act as in force and effect in the state are hereby incorporated into this
section by reference.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 112.101 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   Any person who owns a video gaming terminal for use in the village
shall obtain a video gambling terminal operator’s license.
   (B)   Any person who owns any place of business in which a video gambling
terminal is located shall obtain a video gambling terminal establishment
license.
   (C)   Any person located in the village who manufactures, distributes or
supplies video gambling terminals who does not have a video gambling terminal’s
operator’s license shall obtain a video gambling terminal supplier’s license.
   (D)   Any person displaying for public patronage or keeping for operation
any mechanical amusement device or video gambling terminal, as herein defined
by §
112.100 of this chapter, shall before such person displays such device or
terminal, file with the Department of Administrative Services of the village an
application for a license for each such device or terminal and be required to
obtain a license from the village, upon payment of a license fee. Any person
who displays any video gambling terminal to be played or operated by the public
shall as a prerequisite to receiving any license from the village have a valid
license from the state for each such terminal, and the loss or suspension of
any such license by the state shall automatically result in the same status
from the license issued hereunder without a refund of any license fee.
   (E)   For each video gambling terminal to be located in the village, an
application for license shall be filed by the following, as may be applicable:
      (1)   The holder of the liquor license for the premises of a licensed
establishment. A licensed establishment is any licensed retail establishment
where alcoholic liquor is served for consumption on the premises;
      (2)   An authorized representative of the licensed truck stop. A licensed
truck stop establishment is a facility of at least three acres with a
convenience store, separate diesel islands for fueling commercial motor
vehicles and parking spaces for commercial vehicles;
      (3)   An authorized representative of the licensed fraternal
organization. A licensed fraternal establishment is a location where a
fraternal organization that derives its charter from its national parent
organization regularly meets; and
      (4)   An authorized representative of the licensed veteran’s
organization. A licensed veteran’s establishment is a location where a
qualified veteran’s organization that holds a charter from its national parent
organization regularly meets.
   (F)   There is hereby imposed, on the privilege of operating every video
gambling terminal in the village, an annual license requirement and fee:
      (1)   Video gambling terminal operator’s license;
      (2)   Video gambling terminal supplier’s license;
      (3)   A video gambling terminal establishment license; and
      (4)   A video gambling terminal license for each video gambling terminal.
   (G)   Not more than one mechanical amusement device or video gambling
terminal shall be operated under one amusement device or video gambling
terminal license and the applicant or licensee shall be required to secure a
license for each and every machine displayed or operated by him or her.
   (H)   The approving authority shall be the Mayor.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.102 LICENSE APPLICATION; LIMITATIONS ON VIDEO GAMBLING TERMINALS.
   (A)   Application by any persons desiring to display in the village any
amusement machine or device or video gambling terminal shall make application
for such appropriate license to the Department of Administrative Services upon
a form to be supplied by the Department of Administrative Services for that
purpose.
   (B)   The application for such license shall be accompanied by the required
license fee and/or tax and shall contain the following:
      (1)   Name and address, age, date and place of birth of applicant;
      (2)   Place where machine or device is to be displayed or operated and
the business conducted at that place;
      (3)   Description of amusement machine or device, or video gambling
terminal to be displayed on the premises where such amusement device or video
gambling terminal will be located, the mechanical features, name of
manufacturer and serial number and such other data or information as the
village may require;
      (4)   The applicant shall include a copy of the license from the state
for each video gambling terminal on the premises; and
      (5)   Video gambling terminals may not be operated or played during the
hours alcoholic liquor sales are prohibited by village ordinance.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 112.103 RESTRICTIONS ON ISSUANCE OF LICENSE.
   (A)   No license shall be issued to any applicant unless he or she shall be
over 21 years of age and a citizen of the United States.
   (B)   Every establishment licensed to sell alcoholic liquor shall comply
with all provisions of the state’s Video Gaming Act, 230 ILCS 40/1 et seq., and
all rules, regulations and restrictions imposed by the state’s Gaming Board.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 112.104 INVESTIGATIONS; INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   (1)   A copy of the application for license shall be made out in
duplicate, one copy being referred to the village’s Police Department and the
other copy to the village’s Building Inspection Department.
      (2)   The Police Department and the Building Department shall investigate
the location wherein it is proposed to operate such machine, ascertain if the
applicant is a good person or good moral character and either approve or
disapprove the application.
      (3)   The Building Department shall inspect all wiring connections to the
machine, determine if the same complies with the Electrical Code of the
village, and shall either approve or disapprove the application.
   (B)   No license shall be submitted to the Mayor for issuance to any
applicant unless first approved by the Police Department and the Building
Department.
   (C)   Upon receipt of the proper application, upon approval from the
appropriate departments, and upon the payment of license fee(s) as herein
provided, the Mayor shall issue the appropriate license for each such device or
terminal, which license shall be issued for a period of one year from May 1 to
April 30 in the ensuing year.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 112.105 LICENSE FEES.
   Every applicant, before being granted an amusement device or video gambling
terminal license, shall pay an annual license fee as provided in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances for the privilege of operating or
maintaining for operation each mechanical amusement device or video gambling
terminal, as defined in §
112.100 of this chapter.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 112.106 NUMBER OF LICENSES ISSUED.
   (A)   Amusement device. The Mayor shall be authorized to issue a license for
a mechanical amusement device, if the applicant otherwise qualifies as provided
in this code, in accordance with the following schedule:
      (1)   One license for the first 2,000 square feet of floor area in the
premises in which the mechanical device is located or fraction thereof; and
      (2)   One additional license for each 1,500 square feet of floor area
over and above 2,000 square feet.
   (B)   Video gambling terminal. The Mayor shall be authorized to issue a
license/permit for establishments licensed to sell alcoholic liquor and
licensed to operate a video gambling terminal by the state’s Gaming Board
pursuant to the provisions of the state’s Video Gaming Act, 230 ILCS 40/1 et
seq., for each video gambling terminal, if the applicant otherwise qualifies as
provided in this code, as follows: no more than five video gambling terminals
may be located on any premises licensed to sell alcoholic liquors. No more than
six video gambling terminals may be located on any premises licensed to sell
alcoholic liquors. In the event that any of the licensed premises shall no
longer display video gambling terminal license to be played or operated by the
public for any video gambling terminal, for any reason, the number of licensed
video gambling terminals authorized to be played or operated by the public on
those premises shall automatically and immediately be reduced by one. The
licensee shall immediately notify the village if for any reason the licensee is
no longer displaying a license for a video gambling terminal.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012; Ord. 20-004, passed 3-2-2020)
§ 112.107 LICENSE TRANSFER.
   (A)   Amusement device. Such license may be transferred from one machine or
device to another similar machine located on the same premises and owned by the
same applicant upon application to the Department of Administrative Services to
such effect and giving of a description and the serial number of the new
machine or amusement device; provided that, any and all such amusement devices
so displayed at any one time on such premises shall be licensed as provided
herein.
   (B)   Video gambling terminal. A video gambling terminal license is not
transferable.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 112.108 DISPLAY OF LICENSE.
   (A)   The license for each amusement device or video gambling terminal shall
be in the form of a gummed sticker, which shall be serially numbered and shall
be securely affixed in plain view to the device for which it is issued.
   (B)   It shall be unlawful to operate a video gambling terminal in the
village without a valid video gambling sticker affixed thereon.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.109 GAMBLING DEVICES PROHIBITED.
   (A)   Nothing in this subchapter shall in any way be construed to authorize,
license or permit any gambling devices whatsoever, or any mechanism that has
been judicially determined to be a gambling device, or in any way contrary to
law, or that may be contrary to any future laws of the village and the state,
except for devices and equipment licensed and operated in accordance with the
Video Gaming Act, 230 ILCS 40/1 et seq.
   (B)   (1)   No license shall be issued for any amusement device or video
gambling terminal which violates the laws of the state or the ordinances of the
village.
      (2)   All amusement devices and/or video gambling terminals shall be
available for inspection by the proper village authorities for the purpose of
ascertaining and declaring whether such laws are being complied with.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 112.110 LICENSE REVOCATION.
   (A)   Every license issued under this subchapter is subject to the right,
which is hereby expressly reserved, of revocation of the same should the
licensee, directly or indirectly, permit the operation of any mechanical
amusement device or video gambling terminal contrary to the provisions of this
section, the ordinances of the village or the law of the state.
   (B)   Said license may be revoked by the Mayor and Board of Trustees after
written notice to the licensee, which notice shall specify the ordinance or law
violations with which the licensee is charged, if, after a hearing, the
licensee is found to be guilty of such violations.
   (C)   Ten days’ notice of the hearing shall be given the licensee.
   (D)   At such hearing, the licensee and his or her attorney may be present
and submit evidence of witnesses in his or her defense.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 112.111 ALLOWING TO FREQUENT OR REMAIN IN PUBLIC AREAS OF ESTABLISHMENTS WITH
VIDEO GAMBLING TERMINALS.
   (A)   Video gambling shall be located in an area that is restricted to
persons over 21 years of age.
   (B)   Notwithstanding any provisions of this subchapter, no licensee of a
mechanical amusement device or video gambling establishment or terminal shall
permit or allow any person under 21 years of age to frequent or remain in any
area within the licensee’s place of business which is open to the general
public.
(Ord. 12-566, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 112.112 BAGATELLE AND PIGEONHOLE.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      BAGATELLE or PIGEONHOLE. A game played with any number of balls or
spheres upon a table or board having holes, pickets or cups into which such
balls or spheres may drop or become lodged and having arches, pins and springs,
or any of them, to control, deflect or impede the direction or speed of the
balls or spheres put in motion by the player, and shall include the modern
variety of bagatelle or pigeonhole commonly known as PIN GAMES.
      PLACE OF PUBLIC RESORT. Any premises wherein any service or merchandise
is offered for sale to the public or where tables or implements for playing the
game of bagatelle or pigeonhole are kept for gain or profit, or any premises
used as a clubhouse or clubrooms.
   (B)   Use in public places prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person
to keep or use in any place of public resort within the village any tables or
implements for any game of bagatelle or pigeonhole.
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-2) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.113 COIN-OPERATED MUSIC DEVICES.
   (A)   License required. It shall be unlawful for any person to locate,
install, keep, maintain or use, or permit the location, installation,
maintenance or use upon his or her premises of any automatic or coin-controlled
or coin-operated music box or device which furnishes what is commonly called
“canned music” without first having obtained a license therefor.
   (B)   Application for license. The application shall state the location of
the place where such music box or device is located and the number of such
boxes at such location.
   (C)   License fee. A license shall be obtained for each such music box or
device operated and the annual license, fee for such businesses shall be
established by ordinance as set forth in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
   (D)   Unlawful use of device. It shall be unlawful to use such coin-
controlled musical devices in a manner which interferes with the health, peace
and comfort of any person in the neighborhood thereof; such use is hereby
declared to be a nuisance.
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-3) (Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986) Penalty, see §
112.999
RAFFLES
§ 112.125 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CHARITABLE. An organization or institution organized and operated to benefit
an indefinite number of the public. The service rendered to those eligible for
benefits must also confer some benefit on the public.
   EDUCATIONAL. An organization or institution which is organized and operated
to provide systematic instruction in useful branches of learning by methods
common to schools and institutions of learning which compare favorably in their
scope and intensity with the course of study presented in tax-supported
schools.
   FRATERNAL. An organization of persons having a common interest, the primary
interest of which is both to promote the welfare of its members and to provide
assistance to the general public in such a way as to lessen the burdens of
government by caring for those that otherwise would be cared for by the
government.
   LABOR. An organization composed of workers organized with the objective of
betterment of the conditions of those engaged in such pursuit and the
development of a higher degree of efficiency in their respective occupations.
   NET PROCEEDS. Gross receipts from the conduct of raffles, less reasonable
sums expended for prizes, local license fees and other reasonable operating
expenses incurred as a result of operating a raffle.
   NON-PROFIT. An organization or institution organized and conducted on a not-
for-profit basis with no personal profit inuring to any one as a result of the
operation.
   RAFFLES. A form of lottery, as defined in § 28-2(b) of the Illinois Criminal
Code of 1961, being 720 ILCS 5/28-2(b) as now or hereafter amended, conducted
by an organization licensed under this subchapter in which:
      (1)   The player pays or agrees to pay something of value for a chance,
represented and differentiated by a number or by a combination of numbers or by
some other medium, one or more of which chances is to be designated the winning
chance; and
      (2)   The winning chance is to be determined through a drawing or by some
other method based on an element of chance by an act or set of acts on the part
of persons conducting or connected with the lottery; except that, the winning
chance shall not be determined by the outcome of a publicly exhibited sporting
contest.
   RELIGIOUS. Any church, congregation, society or organization founded for the
purpose of religious worship.
   VETERANS. An organization or association comprised of members of which
substantially all are individuals who are veterans or spouses, widows or
widowers of veterans, the primary purpose of which is to promote the welfare of
its members and to provide assistance to the general public in such a way as to
confer a public benefit.
(Prior Code, § 3-21-1)
§ 112.126 LICENSING.
   (A)   Location. Sales of raffle chances shall be only at locations
designated in the license application and which are within the borders of the
village.
   (B)   Eligibility for license. Licenses shall be issued only to bona fide
religious, charitable, labor, fraternal, educational or veterans organizations
that operate without profit to their members and which have been in existence
continuously for a period of five years immediately before making application
for a license and which have had, during that entire four-year period, a bona
fide membership engaged in carrying out their objectives.
   (C)   Duration of license. Licenses shall permit the applicant to issue or
sell raffle chances only for those dates stated in the license application, but
in no event shall the period of sales exceed 180 days. Each license is valid
for one raffle only.
   (D)   Maximum value of prizes.
      (1)   The aggregate retail value of all prizes or merchandise awarded by
a licensee in a single raffle shall not exceed $150,000.
      (2)   The retail value of each individual prize awarded by a licensee in
a single raffle shall not exceed $150,000.
   (E)   Price of chances. The price charged for each raffle chance sold or
issued shall not exceed $250.
(Prior Code, § 3-21-2)
§ 112.127 LICENSE; APPLICATION; RESTRICTIONS.
   (A)   No person shall conduct a raffle without having first obtained a
license therefor.
   (B)   Each application for a licence shall be in writing upon forms provided
by the village and shall contain the following:
      (1)   Name and address of individual making application;
      (2)   Name and address of organization applying for a license;
      (3)   Approximate number of members of the organization that reside in
the village and the length of existence of the organization;
      (4)   Name and address of the raffle manager;
      (5)   The location(s) at which raffle chances are to be sold or issued;
      (6)   The time period during which raffle chances will be sold or issued;
      (7)   The maximum number of raffle chances to be sold;
      (8)   The time of determination of winning chances;
      (9)   The location(s) at which winning chances will be determined;
      (10)   A sworn statement signed by the presiding officer and secretary,
if there is one, of the organization attesting to the not-for-profit character
of the organization, and attesting to the fact the organization is not
otherwise ineligible to receive a license; and
      (11)   Such other information as the village may require.
   (C)   Each application for a license shall be accompanied by payment of a
fee of $10.
   (D)   Application for licenses shall be submitted to the village. The
village shall act to either issue or deny the license within 30 days.
(Prior Code, § 3-21-3) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.128 INELIGIBILITY.
   The following are ineligible for any license under this chapter:
   (A)   Any person who has been convicted of a felony;
   (B)   Any person who is or has been a professional gambler or gambling
promoter;
   (C)   Any person who is not of good moral character;
   (D)   Any firm or corporation in which a person defined in divisions (A),
(B) or (C) above has a proprietary, equitable or credit interest or in which
such a person is active or employed;
   (E)   Any organization in which a person defined in divisions (A), (B) or
(C) above is an officer, director or employee, whether compensated or not; and
   (F)   Any organization in which a person defined in divisions (A), (B) or
(C) above is to participate in the management or operation of a raffle.
(Prior Code, § 3-21-4)
§ 112.129 CONDUCT OF RAFFLES.
   The conducting of raffles is subject to the following restrictions.
   (A)   The entire net proceeds of any raffle must be exclusively devoted to
the lawful purposes of the organization permitted to conduct that game.
   (B)   No person, except a bona fide member of the sponsoring organization,
may participate in the management or operation of the raffle.
   (C)   No person may receive any remuneration or profit for participating in
the management or operation of the raffle.
   (D)   A licensee may rent a premises on which to determine the winning
chance or chances in a raffle only from an organization which is also licensed
under this subchapter.
   (E)   Raffle chances may be sold or issued only at the locations specified
on the license and winning chances may be determined only at those locations
specified on the license.
   (F)   No person under the age of 18 years may participate in the conducting
of raffles or chances. A person under the age of 18 years may be within the
area where winning chances are being determined only when accompanied by his or
her parent or guardian.
(Prior Code, § 3-21-5) Penalty, see §
112.999
§ 112.130 RECORDS AND REPORTS.
   (A)   Each organization licensed to conduct raffles shall keep records of
its gross receipts, expenses and net proceeds for each single gathering or
occasion at which winning chances are determined. All deductions from gross
receipts for each single gathering or occasion shall be documented with
receipts or other records indicating the amount, a description of the purchased
item or service or other reason for the deduction and the recipient. The
distribution of net proceeds shall be itemized as to payee, purpose, amount and
date of payment.
   (B)   Gross receipts from the operation of raffles programs shall be
segregated from other revenues of the organization, including bingo gross
receipts, if bingo games are also conducted by the same non-profit organization
pursuant to license therefor issued by the Department of Revenue of the state
and placed in a separate account. Each organization should have separate
records for its raffles. The person who accounts for gross receipts, expenses
and net proceeds from the operation of raffles should not be the same person
who accounts for other revenues of the organization.
   (C)   Each organization licensed to-conduct raffles shall report monthly to
its membership, and to the village, its gross receipts, expenses and net
proceeds from raffles and the distribution of net proceeds itemized as required
by this section.
   (D)   Records required by this section shall be preserved for three years,
and organizations shall make available their records relating to operation of
raffles for public inspection at reasonable times and places.
(Prior Code, § 3-21-6)
§ 112.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
112.007 of this chapter shall be fined as stated in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances. Every day such violation continues shall
constitute a separate and distinct offense.
   (C)   (1)   The owner, manager, licensee or person in control of premises
where an automatic amusement device, as per §§
112.020 through
112.027 of this chapter, is used for illegal gambling shall be subject to a
fine of $5,000 for each device so used. Any person violating any other
provision of §§
112.020 through
112.027 of this chapter, by possession or use of an illegal amusement device,
shall be fined not less than $500, nor more than $1,000, for each offense.
Every day such violation continues shall constitute a separate and distinct
offense. Fines under this division (C) shall be in addition to suspension or
revocation of business licenses issued under this code or ordinances and, in
addition, to confiscation and destruction of illegal amusement devices.
      (2)   Upon a third violation of the provisions of §§
112.020 through
112.027 of this chapter, relating to possession or use of an illegal amusement
device occurring on the same premises for a period of five years, all village
licenses issued for business activity on those premises shall be revoked, and
no automatic amusement device may be placed on the premises for a period of one
year from the date of revocation. Nothing in this division (C) limits the
authority of the Mayor to revoke a license on a licensee’s first or second
violation during such period. For purposes of this division (C)(2), “licensee”
includes an “employee or agent of a licensee”.
   (D)   (1)   Any person violating any provision of §§
112.040 through
112.051 of this chapter for which no other penalty is specified shall be fined
not less than $200, nor more than $500, for each offense. Every day such
violation shall continue shall be regarded as a separate and distinct offense.
      (2)   Each person found in violation of §
112.041(A) of this chapter shall be subject to a fine of up to $10,000.
   (E)   (1)   Any person convicted of the offense of violating any of the
provisions of §§
112.100 through
112.111 of this chapter, in addition to the revocation of his or her or its
license, shall be liable to a fine or penalty according to the provisions of §
10.999 of this code of ordinances for violation not less than $250, nor more
than $750. Each day an offense occurs or continues shall be considered a new
offense.
      (2)   In the event of a revocation or denial of any license under §§
112.100 through
112.111 of this chapter, such person shall not be issued any license provided
for in §§
112.100 through
112.111 of this chapter for one calendar year following the date of revocation
or any appeal thereof.
   (F)   It is hereby made the duty of every police officer to seize any table
or implement kept or used in violation of §
112.112 of this chapter and, upon conviction of the keeper thereof, such table
or implement so seized shall be destroyed. Any person violating §
112.112 of this chapter shall be fined according to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-4A-2)
   (G)   Any person that violates any provision of §§
112.125 through
112.130 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $100, nor more than $500.
(Prior Code, § 3-21-7)
(Ord. 90-103, passed 1-30-1990; Ord. 06-342, passed 5-15-2006; Ord. 09-468,
passed 3-2-2009)

§ 113.001 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   All sales of real and personal property at public auction within the
village, except such as are made under and by virtue of legal process, shall be
made by a person who shall first obtain a license for such purpose as provided
herein.
(Prior Code, § 3-5-1)
§ 113.002 LICENSE APPLICATION; FEE.
   (A)   Every person desiring to obtain a license for the sale of real and
personal property at public auction shall set forth in the application the
location of his or her proposed place of business and the names of the surety.
   (B)   The fee for such license shall be as provided in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-5-2)
§ 113.003 BOND.
   Any person may become an auctioneer and be licensed to sell real and
personal property at public auction at a place to be named in the license upon
paying to the Village Clerk the fee required by this chapter and executing a
bond to the village with two sureties to be approved by the Village President
in the penal sum of $1,000 conditioned for the observance of this chapter and
the other provisions of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-5-3)
§ 113.004 LICENSE TRANSFER; CHANGE OF LOCATION.
   In no case shall the license for the sale of real or personal property at
public auction within the village be transferable or the place of business
changed without the consent in writing of the Village Clerk.
(Prior Code, § 3-5-4) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 113.005 LOCATIONS OF AUCTIONS.
   (A)   No goods, wares, merchandise or any other thing whatever shall be sold
or exposed for sale at auction in any street, avenue, alley or public place in
the village.
   (B)   All auctions shall be held or conducted in the store, warehouse or
other proper place which shall be so arranged and none of the bidders or
bystanders will be compelled to or required to stand or remain on the street or
sidewalk in front of such warehouse, store or other place in such a manner to
obstruct free travel.
(Prior Code, § 3-5-5) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 113.006 PROHIBITED ACTS AND CONDITIONS.
   (A)   Devices for attracting attention. No bellman or cryer, nor any drum or
other instrument of music, nor any show, signal or means of attracting
attention of passers, other than a sign or flag, shall be employed or permitted
to be used at any place of sale or at any auction room or near any auction
whatsoever.
   (B)   False representation. Any auctioneer or person present when any
article is offered for sale who shall knowingly, with the intent to induce any
person to purchase the same or any part thereof, make any false representation
or statement as to the ownership of or the character or quality of the article
offered for sale, or as to the poverty or circumstances of the owner or
pretended owner of such article shall, on conviction, be punished by a fine as
set forth in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances, and his or her license shall be forfeited.
   (C)   Substitution of articles. Any auctioneer who shall exhibit and offer
for sale at auction any article and induce its purchase by any bidder and who
shall afterwards substitute any article in lieu of that offered to and
purchased by the bidder shall forfeit his or her license and be punished by a
fine as set forth in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances and the license of such auctioneer shall be
revoked.
   (D)   False bids. Any auctioneer who shall procure any person to make a
fictitious bid at any auction sale of real or personal property, or who shall
conspire with any person to make a fictitious bid at any such auction sale, or
who shall knowingly permit any person to make a fictitious bid at any such
auction sale, or any auctioneer who shall himself or herself fictitiously raise
any bid at any such auction sale shall be punished by a fine as set forth in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances, and the license of such auctioneer shall be
revoked.
(Prior Code, § 3-5-6) Penalty, see §
10.999
