FLEA MARKETS
§ 114.001 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   FLEA MARKET. A market, indoors or out of doors, where new or used items are
traded or sold from individual locations (stands, booths), with each location
being operated independently from other locations. Items sold include, but are
not limited to, household items, antiques, rare items, decorations, used books,
used magazines and prepackaged food items in sealed containers and not for
consumption at the market.
   FLEA MARKET SELLER. A person, firm or corporation selling items or offering
items for sale at flea market.
   PRIVATE FLEA MARKET. A flea market operated by a private person, firm or
corporation operating a flea market on non-residentially zoned private
property.
   PUBLIC FLEA MARKET. A flea market operated by the village on public
property.
(Ord. 15-032, passed 8-3-2015)
§ 114.002 PRIVATE FLEA MARKETS; PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (A)   Times. Private flea markets may be held from January 1 through
December 31. No flea market may be held on residentially-zoned property.
   (B)   Permit required. No person, firm or corporation shall operate the
business of renting space or allocating space to flea market sellers without
first obtaining a permit from the Village Clerk. Only one license shall be
required for each flea market location, and the individual flea market sellers
shall not be required to obtain a permit to lease/rent a space at said flea
market. The permit shall be good for one fiscal year, May 1 through April 30,
at any given location and shall set forth and restrict the time and location of
such flea market.
   (C)   Permit application. Each application for a permit shall be in writing
upon a form provided by the Village Clerk and filed in person with the Village
Clerk. The application shall contain the following information:
      (1)   Name, address, daytime telephone number and e-mail address of
person, firm, group, corporation, association or organization of the applicant;
      (2)   Name of owner of the property on which the flea market is to be
conducted, and consent of owner if applicant is other than the owner;
      (3)   Name, address, daytime telephone number and e-mail address of the
person supervising the flea market;
      (4)   Location where flea market is to be held;
      (5)   Date and nature of any past flea market;
      (6)   Evidence that applicant has satisfactory liability insurance issued
by a responsible insurance company authorized and licensed to do business in
the state, insuring such applicant against liability which such applicant may
incur in the operation of a flea market, and specifically designating the
village as an additional insured. The evidence of the insurance policy shall
indicate that the term of the insurance encompasses the period of the permit
sought;
      (7)   Relationship or connection applicant may have had with any other
person, form, group, organization, association or corporation conducting said
flea market and the date of such flea market; and
      (8)   Sworn statement or affirmation by the person signing the
application that the information therein given is full and true and known to
him or her to be so.
   (D)   Permit fee. The annual fee for a permit is $500 and shall be paid at
the time the application is filed with the Village Clerk.
   (E)   Separate permit for each location. A permit shall apply only to the
location described in the application and only one location shall be so
described in each permit. Permits are non-transferable.
   (F)   Posting of permits. The flea market permit shall be displayed in a
conspicuous place on the premises of the flea market where it can be readily
and distinctly seen by the public, the village inspector and the village
police.
   (G)   Records to be kept by permittee. Each person, firm or corporation
issued a permit under this subchapter shall keep accurate records of the names
and addresses of each flea market seller, together with a brief description of
the type or types of merchandise offered for sale by that seller. Such records
shall be made available to the village for inspection during regular business
hours.
(Ord. 15-032, passed 8-3-2015)
§ 114.003 CONDUCT OF SALE.
   (A)   Generally. The applicant and the owner or tenant of the location where
the flea market is conducted shall be jointly and severally responsible for the
maintenance of good order and decorum on the premises during all hours of such
flea market. Loud or boisterous conduct shall not be permitted and vehicles
shall not impede the passage of traffic on any roads or streets in the area of
the flea market. Reasonable orders of any member of the Village Police or Fire
Departments to maintain the public health, safety and welfare shall be obeyed.
   (B)   Unlawful transactions. It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or
offer for sale, any of the following:
      (1)   Any type of drugs, drug paraphernalia, tobacco products of any kind
or pharmaceuticals, legal or otherwise, and alcohol;
      (2)   Firearms, working or not, ammunition or explosive devices, weapons
of any kind;
      (3)   Knives, dirks, daggers, folding knives with locking blades;
      (4)   Stolen merchandise;
      (5)   Live animals: no dogs or other live pets are allowed on the
premises, unless such animals are service animals;
      (6)   Videos, cassettes, DVDs, blue-rays and the like, which are pirated,
dubbed or in violation of copyright law;
      (7)   X-rated, pornographic materials, including, but not limited to,
printed materials, pictures, magazines and movies;
      (8)   Items that by sale, possession or use are in violation of village,
county, state or federal laws and any item that is misrepresented by the seller
in any way; and
      (9)   No food products shall be sold without a health permit or any types
of products such as pills of any kind, toothpaste, mouthwash, prepared food
products, beverages or alcoholic beverages. The village reserves the right to
approve all food vendors.
   (C)   Purchases from children. No flea market seller shall purchase any used
household item, antique or used article whatsoever from any person under the
age of 18, unless such person is accompanied by the person’s parent or
guardian.
   (D)   Hours of operation. Flea markets may remain open for business between
the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m., unless otherwise specified on the permit
at the time of issuance.
   (E)   Signs and advertisements. All signs and advertisements shall be
conducted and posted in compliance with all applicable village laws and
ordinances. The Police Department may enforce such temporary controls to
alleviate any special hazards and/or congestion created by any flea market.
   (F)   Parking regulations. All parking of vehicles shall be conducted in
compliance with all applicable village laws and ordinances. The Police
Department may enforce such temporary controls to alleviate any special hazards
and/or congestion created by any flea market.
(Ord. 15-032, passed 8-3-2015) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.004 PERMIT REVOCATION AND REFUSAL.
   (A)   Any permit issued under this subchapter may be revoked or any
application for issuance of a permit may be refused by the village of the
application submitted by the applicant or permit holder contains any false,
fraudulent or misleading statements.
   (B)   If any individual, firm or corporation is convicted of an offense
under this subchapter, the existing flea market permit held by such individual,
firm or corporation shall be revoked and such individual, firm or corporation
shall not be issued a flea market permit for a period of two years from the
time of conviction.
(Ord. 15-032, passed 8-3-2015)
§ 114.005 PUBLIC FLEA MARKETS.
   The village may hold flea markets on public property at the Village Board’s
discretion. The fee for a flea market seller to operate a stall at any such
flea market shall be determined by the Village Board, at its discretion.
(Ord. 15-032, passed 8-3-2015)
LANDSCAPE AND LAWN CARE PROFESSIONALS
§ 114.020 DEFINITIONS.
   (A)   The language in the text of this subchapter shall be interpreted in
accordance with the following rules of construction.
      (1)   The singular number includes the plural number, and the plural the
singular.
      (2)   The word “shall” is mandatory; the word “may” is permissive.
      (3)   The masculine gender includes the feminine and neuter.
   (B)   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      LANDSCAPE AND LAWN CARE PROFESSIONALS. Any person that employs one or
more individuals for the purpose of providing landscape maintenance for
clients, including, without limitation, the cultivating or beautifying of
gardens; the trimming of hedges, plants or grass; or the raking or sweeping of
debris and leaves.
      LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE. The improvement and/or maintenance of the
appearance of an area of land by planting and/or maintaining trees, shrubs,
grass or other plants and lawn ornaments; or by altering the contour of the
ground.
      LEAF BLOWER. A machine that blows air supplying forced drafts,
supercharging the air in order to move non-growing fallen leaves, foliage and/
or debris.
      LICENSEE. A holder of a landscape and lawn care professional’s license
issued by the village. In the operation of landscape maintenance, the term
LICENSEE shall include agents and employees of a licensee.
      PERSON. Any individual, partnership, firm or corporation.
      VEHICLE. Any motor-driven vehicle used by the licensee to transport a
work crew, equipment, yard waste and/or debris.
      VILLAGE. The Village of Dolton, Cook County, Illinois.
      YARD WASTE. Leaves with twig stems no longer than four inches, grass
clippings and similar garden debris and waste, tree branches, limbs and other
similar wood materials; unusable or unwanted substances of organic garden or
yard material.
(Ord. 03-219, passed 4-21-2003)
§ 114.021 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No landscape and lawn care professional shall engage in the business of the
care of lawns, shrubs, trees and any other occupation pertaining to landscape
maintenance without first securing a license from the village.
   (A)   General. Application for the license shall be made to administrative
services in Village Hall on forms provided by the village and shall contain the
following information:
      (1)   Name and address of the applicant; if the applicant is a
partnership, the application shall show for each partner his or her name and
address and interest, and all information required by divisions (A)(2) and (A)
(7) below. If the applicant is a corporation, the application shall show the
name and address of the registered agent, and with respect to each director,
and each shareholder owning 5% or more of the corporation’s shares his or her
name and address, together with the information required by division (A)(2)
below;
      (2)   The criminal record, if any, of the applicant;
      (3)   The number and kind of vehicles owned and controlled by the
applicant;
      (4)   The location of the applicant’s office and garage;
      (5)   The color scheme, insignia, trade name and telephone number located
upon and used to designate the vehicles of the applicant;
      (6)   A complete description of each vehicle including the year, make,
model and motor or factory number (“VIN”) of the vehicle;
      (7)   A statement that the applicant has received copies of, reviewed and
understands the applicable ordinances of the village and will promulgate same
and educate his or her employees thereof; and
      (8)   Such other information as the Board of Trustees of the village may
require from time to time.
   (B)   Required license of landscape and lawn care professionals. The fee for
the license shall be $75, non-refundable, per calendar year or fraction
thereof, and shall accompany the application therefore. The application fee
includes the cost of one landscape/lawn care vehicle sticker. There shall be a
$5 fee for each additional sticker and/or each transfer of vehicle stickers.
   (C)   Insurance. Evidence that the applicant is covered by a policy of
comprehensive general liability insurance, including bodily injury and property
damage. The applicant shall also submit proof to the village that it carries
adequate worker’s compensation and vehicle insurance; provided, however, that,
the village may waive this requirement if the landscape and lawn care
professional employs no more than two employees, including the landscape and
lawn care professional, and the village is otherwise satisfied with the
application. Proof of insurance will be periodically reviewed by the village
staff.
   (D)   Vehicle identification. Each vehicle operated by the licensee shall at
all times display:
      (1)   The information required by division (A)(5) above; and
      (2)   The landscape and lawn care professionals vehicle sticker issued by
the village at the time a license is granted pursuant to this subchapter, which
vehicle sticker shall be placed in the front driver’s side window of the
vehicle.
   (E)   Conditions. The landscape and lawn care professionals shall either:
      (1)   Remove all yard waste from the premises at the conclusion of each
work day; or
      (2)   Bag all yard waste in brown paper yard waste bags and place said
waste bags in rear of premises. Under no circumstances shall yard waste be left
on the premises in plastic garbage or plastic waste bags.
   (F)   Clientele list. The landscaping or lawn care professionals shall file
with the village on May 1, June 1, July 1, August 1, September 1 and October 1
of each year, a complete clientele list for all properties located within the
village corporate limits and receipts evidencing the proper disposal of yard
waste, if applicable. The village or any person certified by the Mayor, may
require inspection and examination of books and records in order to verify
information provided and for enforcement of this subchapter and collection of
any moneys due and owing to the village.
   (G)   Expiration. Each license shall expire on April 30 unless sooner
revoked as hereinafter provided.
(Ord. 03-219, passed 4-21-2003; Ord. 03-223, passed 6-2-2003)
§ 114.022 LICENSE DENIAL, SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION.
   (A)   The village may refuse to issue or renew, may suspend or revoke a
landscape and lawn care professional’s license or fine a licensee for any one
or more of the following reasons, including, but not limited to:
      (1)   Engaging in the business of the care of lawns, shrubs, trees and
any other occupation pertaining to landscape maintenance without first securing
a landscape and lawn care professional’s license from the village;
      (2)   Failing to either remove yard waste from the premises upon the
conclusion of each work day, or failing to leave the yard waste in brown paper
yard waste bags in the rear of the premises;
      (3)   Leaving or blowing any form of debris, leaves, loose paper or yard
waste from landscaping or lawn care services from the subject yard or parkway,
onto the parkway, in the street, in the alley or on neighboring property;
      (4)   Violation of other village ordinances by the licensee concerning:
         (a)   Unauthorized dumping of debris;
         (b)   Use of back-pack leaf blowers between May 15 and October 1; and
         (c)   Any other ordinance pertaining to landscape maintenance.
      (5)   Inaccurate, false or misleading statements having been made by the
licensee in any application for any such license;
      (6)   The licensee having made substantial misrepresentation or false
promise of a character likely to influence or induce another in connection with
the business of landscaping; and/or
      (7)   Pursuit by the licensee of a continued course of making false
promises through advertising, salespersons and/or agents or making other
misrepresentations in connection with the business of landscaping.
   (B)   In the event the village suspends, revokes or fines any such licensee,
such licensee shall also forfeit his or her bond. The village shall not assess
a fine in excess of $500. No person whose license has been revoked may apply
for re-issuance of such license for a period of one year following the date of
such revocation.
(Ord. 03-219, passed 4-21-2003; Ord. 11-545, passed 12-5-2011)
TOBACCO
§ 114.035 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   DISTRIBUTE. To give, sell, deliver, dispense or issue or offer to give,
sell, deliver, dispense or issue, or cause to hire any person to give, sell,
deliver, dispense, issue or offer to give, sell, deliver, dispense or issue.
   INDIVIDUALLY PACKAGED. The practice of selling any tobacco or tobacco
product wrapped individually for sale. INDIVIDUALLY WRAPPED TOBACCO AND TOBACCO
PRODUCTS shall include, but not be limited to, manufacturer-sealed cigarette
packs, single bags or cans of loose tobacco in any form, and single form, and
single cans or other packaging of snuff or chewing tobacco. Cartons or other
packaging containing more than a single pack or other container as described in
this definition shall not be considered INDIVIDUALLY PACKAGED.
   LICENSEE. Any person who obtains a tobacco product retailer’s license under
this subchapter.
   LOOSIES. The common term used to refer to a single or individually packaged
cigarette or any other tobacco product that has been removed from its packaging
and sold individually. The term LOOSIES does not include individual cigars with
a retail price, before any sales taxes, stamped on the package.
   MINOR. Any person who is under the age of 18 years.
   PERSON. Any individual, firm, partnership, corporation, association, joint
venture, personal representative, receiver, estate, trust, trustee, assignee,
any other group or combination acting as a unit, or any other legal entity,
except the federal government, the state and any political subdivision thereof.
   PHOTOGRAPHIC IDENTIFICATION. An officially issued card containing the
bearer’s date of birth and photograph that is accepted as proof of age under
state law.
   POINT-OF-SALE. A store, stand, building, vending machine or any other
separate place of business maintained by a seller from which tobacco products
are made available for sale or distribution to consumers. POINT-OF-SALE does
not include separate cash registers or service counters within a store or other
place of business.
   PUBLIC PLACE. Any area to which the public is invited or permitted.
   RETAIL ESTABLISHMENT. Any place of business where tobacco, tobacco products
or tobacco-related devices are available for sale to the general public. The
phrase shall include, but not be limited to, tobacco shops, grocery stores,
convenience stores, restaurants, gasoline stations and drug stores.
   RETAILER. Any person who sells tobacco products to individuals for personal
consumption, or who operates a facility containing self-service displays of
tobacco products in the village.
   SELF-SERVICE MERCHANDISING. Open displays of tobacco, tobacco products and
point-of- sale tobacco products that the public has access to, without the
intervention of the licensee or the licensee’s employee or other personnel. The
assistance or intervention shall entail the actual physical exchange of tobacco
and tobacco products between an individual and the licensee or employee. SELF-
SERVICE SALES are interpreted as being any sale where there is not an actual
physical exchange of the product between the clerk and the customer.
   TAVERN. An enclosed place of business kept, used, maintained, advertised and
held out to the public as a place that primarily serves alcoholic beverages for
consumption on the premises and in which providing entertainment or the serving
of food is incidental or secondary to the sale of alcoholic beverages for
immediate consumption. Examples of businesses not deemed to be TAVERNS within
this definition include, but are not limited to, restaurants, catering halls,
bowling alleys, billiard parlors, dance halls, theaters and arenas.
   TOBACCO PRODUCT. Any tobacco cigarette, cigar, pipe tobacco, smokeless
tobacco, snuff or any other product that contains tobacco leaf which may be
utilized for smoking, chewing, inhalation or other manner of ingestion.
   TOBACCO PRODUCT SAMPLE. Any tobacco product distributed to members of the
general public at no cost or nominal cost for the purpose of promoting the
product.
   TOBACCO SHOP. A tobacco retailer whose business exclusively or primarily
involves the sale of tobacco products and related goods.
   VENDING ASSISTED. Any mechanical, electronic, automated or self-service
device which, upon insertion of money, tokens or any other form of payment,
dispenses cigarettes or any other tobacco product.
   VENDING MACHINE. Any mechanical, electronic, automated or self-service
device which, upon the assertion of money, tokens or other form of payment,
dispenses cigarettes or any other tobacco product.
(Ord. 16-005, passed 3-7-2016)
§ 114.036 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   License required. No person shall engage in the sale at retail of
cigarettes, cigars, tobacco in any form, tobacco products or tobacco-related
devices, without first obtaining a state license and a village license as
provided in this subchapter, or is an agent or employee of a person who has a
current valid license. A separate license must be obtained for each point-of-
sale maintained by the retailer.
   (B)   Application. An application for a license to sell tobacco, tobacco
products and tobacco-related devices shall be made on a form provided by the
village’s Permit and License Department (“Department”). The application shall
contain the full name of the applicant; the applicant’s residential address;
business address to be licensed; telephone numbers; the name of the business
for which the license is sought; a copy of a valid state license for the
premises sought to be licensed; the name, address and telephone number of the
person authorized to receive notices issued pursuant to this subchapter; and
any additional information the village deems necessary. Upon receipt of a
completed application, the Department shall cause an investigation be made of
the character of the applicant. If the Department determines that an
application is incomplete, the application shall be returned to the applicant
with notice of the information necessary to make the application complete. No
such license shall be issued to any person who is not a person of good
character.
      (1)   If the applicant is a corporation or limited liability corporation,
the corporate name, title, address and telephone number of the principal place
of business; the date and state of incorporation; the names of the corporate
officers and the name, address and telephone number of the person authorized to
receive notices issued pursuant to this subchapter.
      (2)   If the applicant is a partnership, the name, address and telephone
number of the principal place of business; the names of all partners; and the
name, address and telephone number of a person authorized to receive notices
issued pursuant to this subchapter.
   (C)   Action. The Department may either approve or deny the license, or may
delay the action for a reasonable period of time as necessary to complete any
investigation of the application or the applicant it deems necessary. If the
application is approved, the Department shall issue the license to the
applicant. If the application is denied, notice of the denial shall be given to
the applicant along with notice of the applicant’s right to appeal the decision
to the Village President.
   (D)   Fees. No license shall be issued under this subchapter until the
appropriate license fee is paid in full. The annual license fee for such
business shall be established by ordinance as set forth in the license fee
schedule of §
110.018(A) of this code of ordinances.
   (E)   Term. All licenses issued under this subchapter shall be valid for one
calendar year from the date of issuance.
   (F)   Revocation or suspension. Any license issued under this subchapter may
be revoked or suspended as provided in §
114.999 of this chapter. Any retailer whose license is revoked for violating
any of the provisions of this subchapter shall be prohibited from obtaining a
tobacco retailer’s license for one year.
   (G)   Transfers. All licenses issued under this subchapter shall be valid
only for the premises for which the license was issued and only for the person
to whom the license was issued. No transfer of any license to another location
or person shall be valid without the prior written approval of the Department.
   (H)   Display. All licenses shall be posted and displayed in plain view of
the general public on the licensed premises.
   (I)   Renewals. The renewal of a license issued under this subchapter shall
be handled in the same manner as the original application. The request for a
renewal shall be made at least 30 days, but no more than 60 days, before the
expiration of the current license.
   (J)   Smoking prohibited. Smoking shall not be permitted and no person shall
smoke indoors at any location with a tobacco retailer license. Smoking for the
purposes of sampling tobacco, tobacco-related products, plant products or
electronic delivery devices shall be prohibited.
   (K)   Issuance is a privilege and not a right. The issuance of a license
issued under this subchapter shall be considered a privilege and not an
absolute right of the applicant and shall not entitle the holder to an
automatic renewal of the license.
   (L)   Minimum clerk age. An individual must be at least 18 years of age to
sell tobacco products, tobacco-related devices or electronic delivery devices
on behalf of a person licensed under this subchapter.
   (M)   Product placement. A license holder must have all tobacco products or
tobacco-related devices located behind the service counter.
   (N)   License for tobacco product vending machine.
      (1)   Every tobacco product vending machine must be licensed by the
License and Permit Department. The Department shall issue an adhesive self-
voiding license emblem to be placed on each licensed tobacco product vending
machine. The license emblem shall be coded to identify the retailer who has
control over the vending machine. The license emblem shall bear the words:
“Village of Dolton Tobacco Product Vending Machine”. The license shall
designate the period of time for which the license is valid; shall contain a
reproduction of the village seal, along with the name of the Village President;
shall contain a space for a brief description of the name, style and type of
vending machine to be licensed; the location of the vending machine; and such
other language as may be prescribed by the Village President. A replacement
license emblem shall not be issued unless the application for such replacement
is accompanied by a village police report of the incident in which the emblem
to be replaced was lost, stolen or mutilated, or unless the remnants of the
emblem being replaced are submitted with the replacement application.
      (2)   The annual license fee for a vending machine shall be established
by ordinance as set forth in the license fee schedule of §
110.018(A) of this chapter. Each additional vending machine operated by a
licensee shall be subject to an additional fee as set forth in the fee schedule
of §
110.018(A) of this code of ordinances.
(Ord. 16-005, passed 3-7-2016) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.037 BASIS FOR DENIAL OF LICENSE.
   (A)   Grounds for denying the issuance of a license under this subchapter
include, but are not limited to, the following:
      (1)   The applicant is under the age of 18 years;
      (2)   The applicant has been convicted within the past five years of any
violation of a federal, state or local law or ordinance, or other regulation
relating to tobacco, tobacco products or tobacco- related devices;
      (3)   The applicant had a tobacco license revoked within the preceding 12
months of the date of application;
      (4)   The applicant fails to provide any information required on the
application or provides false or misleading information; and
      (5)   The applicant is prohibited by federal, state or other local law or
ordinance, or other regulation from holding a license.
   (B)   If a license is mistakenly issued or renewed to a person, it shall be
revoked upon the discovery that the person was ineligible for the license under
this subchapter.
(Ord. 16-005, passed 3-7-2016)
§ 114.038 ENFORCEMENT AND ADMINISTRATION.
   (A)   The Permit and License Department shall be responsible for the
enforcement and administration of this subchapter.
   (B)   Such duties include, but are not limited to:
      (1)   Conducting random, unannounced inspections at locations where
tobacco products are sold, including tobacco vending machines;
      (2)   Promulgating rules and regulations consistent with this subchapter
to provide the enforcement and administration of the provisions of this
subchapter. The rules and regulations shall establish procedures for
administrative action against violators, including the adjudication of the
violations pursuant to the village’s administrative adjudication hearing
process; and
      (3)   Any rules and regulations promulgated under this subchapter shall
be filed in the Department’s office and shall be made available upon request
and payment of all reasonable fees as determined by the Department to cover the
cost of providing such copies.
(Ord. 16-005, passed 3-7-2016)
§ 114.039 PROHIBITED SALES AND DISTRIBUTION.
   (A)   It shall be a violation of this subchapter for any person to sell,
distribute or offer to sell or distribute any tobacco, tobacco product,
tobacco-related device or electronic delivery device:
      (1)   To any person under the age of 18 years. Every retailer shall
request and examine the photographic identification of any person purchasing
tobacco products to verify that the purchaser is over 18 years of age. No such
verification shall be required for any person, who appears, without reasonable
doubt, to be 35 years and older;
      (2)   By means of any type of vending machine, unless such vending
machines are located in factories, businesses, offices, private clubs and other
places not open to the public, or in taverns. Tobacco products may only be sold
or distributed by a vending machine located in a tavern subject to the
following:
         (a)   The vending machine must be placed at least 25 feet from any
entrance or exit to the premises; and
         (b)   The vending machine must be directly visible to the owner or
lessee of the premises, or his or her employees or agents during the tavern’s
hours of operation.
      (3)   By means of self-service methods whereby a customer does not need
to make a verbal or written request to an employee of the licensed premises in
order to receive the tobacco, tobacco product or tobacco-related device and
whereby there is no physical exchange of the tobacco, tobacco product, tobacco-
related device or electronic delivery device between the licensee, or the
licensee’s employee, and the customer. All tobacco, tobacco products, tobacco-
related devices and electronic delivery devices shall either be stored behind a
counter or other area not freely accessible to customers, or in a case or other
storage unit not left open and accessible to the general public;
      (4)   By means of single or loose (“loosies”) cigarettes. No retailer
shall break or otherwise open any cigarette or smokeless tobacco package to
sell or distribute individual cigarettes or a number of unpacked cigarettes or
any quantity of cigarette tobacco or smokeless tobacco that is not in the
manufacturer’s original sealed and stamped packaging;
      (5)   By any other means, to any other person, in any manner or form
prohibited by federal, state or local law or ordinance, or other regulation;
      (6)   By giving away, bartering, exchanging, distributing or in any way
dispensing free of charge, or at nominal cost, any tobacco product samples and/
or coupons redeemable for any tobacco product, on any public street, alley,
sidewalk or in any public park, grounds or playground, or in areas open to the
public in any publicly owned or operated building, or at place located within
500 feet of any building or other location used primarily as a school, child
care facility or for the education or recreation of children under 18 years of
age; and
      (7)   Any cigarette or tobacco product which is not properly licensed by
the state.
   (B)   No retailer shall sell or distribute tobacco products at any place
located within 500 feet of any building or other location used primarily as a
school, child care facility, or for the education or recreation of children
under the age of 18 years of age. This prohibition shall not apply to those
businesses engaged in the retail sale of tobacco products at a location that
would otherwise be prohibited under this subchapter prior to 11-1-2010 and any
new owner that acquired the place of business subsequent to 11-1-2010, at the
same location and providing the same service.
(Ord. 16-005, passed 3-7-2016; Ord. 19-002, passed 4-1-2019) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.040 RESPONSIBILITY.
   All licensees under this subchapter shall be responsible for the actions of
their employees in regard to the sale of tobacco, tobacco products, tobacco-
related devices and electronic delivery devices on the licensed premises and
the sale of an item by an employee shall be considered a sale by the license
holder. Nothing in this section shall be construed as prohibiting the village
from also subjecting the employee to whatever penalties are appropriate under
this subchapter, state or federal law or other applicable law or regulation.
(Ord. 16-005, passed 3-7-2016)
§ 114.041 OTHER ILLEGAL ACTS.
   Unless otherwise provided, the following acts shall be a violation of this
subchapter.
   (A)   Illegal sales. It shall be a violation for any person to sell or
otherwise provide any tobacco, tobacco product, tobacco-related device or
electronic delivery device to any minor.
   (B)   Illegal possession. It shall be a violation for any minor to have in
his or her possession any tobacco, tobacco product, tobacco-related device or
electronic delivery device.
   (C)   Illegal use. It shall be a violation for any minor to smoke, chew,
sniff or otherwise use any tobacco, tobacco product, tobacco-related device or
electronic delivery device.
   (D)   Illegal procurement. It shall be a violation for any minor to purchase
or attempt to purchase or otherwise obtain any tobacco, tobacco product,
tobacco-related device or electronic delivery device, and it shall be a
violation for any person to purchase or otherwise obtain these items on behalf
of a minor. It shall further be a violation for any person to coerce or attempt
to coerce a minor to illegally purchase or otherwise obtain or use any tobacco,
tobacco product, tobacco-related device or electronic delivery device.
   (E)   Use false identification. It shall be a violation for any minor to
attempt to disguise his or her true age by use of a false form of
identification, whether the identification is that of another person or one on
which the age of the person has been modified or tampered with to represent an
age older than the actual age of the person.
(Ord. 16-005, passed 3-7-2016) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.042 COMPLIANCE CHECKS AND OPERATIONS.
   (A)   Purpose. The purpose of this section is to establish procedures for
conducting compliance checks and operations of the sale of age restricted
tobacco products.
   (B)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      COMPLIANCE CHECK MANAGER. A village police officer who is responsible for
supervising enforcement compliance check operations for tobacco and any other
age-restricted products.
      COMPLIANCE CHECK OPERATIONS. A controlled purchase operation conducted
with the use of covert minors to ensure that age-restricted tobacco products
are being sold in accordance with this section. A COMPLIANCE CHECK OPERATION
may also be referred to as an INSPECTION.
      COMPLIANCE OFFICER. A village police officer assigned to conduct
compliance check operations and supervise the covert minor(s) engaging in
controlled buys of age-restricted tobacco products.
      COVERT MINOR. A volunteer who is under 18 years of age and who, while
under village police supervision, assists the Police Department in controlled
purchase operations.
      IDENTIFICATION. A government issued driver’s license, state
identification card, active duty military identification card or passport
lawfully issued to the covert minor for the purposes of establishing identity.
      LICENSEE. The person who is licensed by the state and the village to sell
alcoholic beverages and/or tobacco products.
      OBSERVERS. Adult volunteers who assist supervising officers in conducting
compliance check operations.
      PRODUCT. Any age-restricted tobacco product purchased by a covert minor
in the course of conducting a compliance check operation.
      SELLER. A person who is responsible for and involved in the sale or
refusal to sell age-restricted products.
   (C)   Compliance check procedures.
      (1)   Scheduling. Tobacco compliance operations will be scheduled based
on the results from civilian-based tobacco compliance check operations
conducted through the state’s Liquor Control Commission. The state’s Liquor
Control Commission will provide the compliance check manager a list of
locations within the village that failed their most recent state tobacco
compliance check. Based on the number of businesses that failed, the compliance
check manager will determine the number of operations needed to complete
follow-up inspections.
         (a)   The schedule for alcohol and tobacco compliance check operations
will be subject to the approval of the village’s Police Chief and shall be
reported to the police liaison trustee.
         (b)   Upon receipt of a complaint of underage access to a tobacco
product, the compliance check manager will schedule a compliance check
operation within 30 days of the receipt of the complaint. The business alleged
to be in violation may be inspected as part of a regularly scheduled compliance
check operation.
      (2)   Officer assignments.
         (a)   For pre-scheduled compliance check operations, the compliance
check manager will notify all eligible officers of the opportunity to conduct
compliance check operations. To ensure fairness in assignments, officers will
be given a period of time to sign up for the operations on a first come, first
serve basis, with a limitation on how many operations an individual officer may
sign up for. Once the sign-up period has lapsed, the compliance check manager
will re-open the schedule for a second round of sign-ups to include officers
who previously signed up, again with limitations on the number an individual
officer may sign up for. If dates are available following a second round, the
schedule will be opened up for general sign up with no limitations.
         (b)   Officers who fail to report to scheduled assignments on two
consecutive dates may be required to forfeit upcoming dates or be denied the
opportunity to sign up during the next scheduling period.
      (3)   Covert minors. The compliance check manager is responsible for
recruiting and scheduling covert minors. Covert minors will be selected using
the following criteria.
         (a)   Covert minors assigned to tobacco compliance checks must be at
least 16 years of age and no more than 17 years of age.
         (b)   Minors who are 16 years of age or who reside with a parent year
round and have not reached the age of 19, must have a permission slip, provided
by the compliance check manager, signed by a parent, authorizing the
involvement in compliance check operations. The parent permission slip will
outline the role the minor will take in compliance check operations.
         (c)   No covert minors will be allowed to participate in compliance
check operations if they are within two months of their birthday that would
allow them to legally purchase age-restricted products.
      (4)   Appearance of minors.
         (a)   Minors should be “youthful” in appearance. No minor will use
excessive makeup to enhance his or her appearance. Males will not be allowed to
have facial hair (i.e., beards or mustaches).
         (b)   Minors must dress appropriately in order to participate in a
compliance check operation. Minors will not wear clothing that would aid in the
determination of age (i.e., letter jackets and t-shirts that provide class
information).
         (c)   Minors, at the direction of the compliance check manager, may be
required to participate in an age verification study provided by the compliance
check manager.
            1.   To complete the age verification study, a minor will be taken
to an area with high levels of pedestrian traffic. Officers will conduct the
study by requesting a variety of pedestrians to evaluate the minor and estimate
the minor’s age. Officers will request this input from 12 individuals who would
be eligible to sit on a jury.
            2.   Upon completion of the age verification study, the officers
conducting the study, will submit the documentation to the compliance check
manager for inclusion in the minor’s file.
      (5)   Background review.
         (a)   Minors should be of good character. A background check shall be
conducted by the compliance check manager. The background check will include a
criminal history check and an ARMS check.
         (b)   Minors will be disqualified from participation if they have any
felony or misdemeanor convictions or have been charged with a DUI or similar
violation from another state. Minors with a single violation of minors in
possession of alcohol/tobacco-related products may be allowed to participate in
the program with authorization from the Village Attorney and approval of the
compliance check manager.
      (6)   Selected covert minors.
         (a)   Minors who are selected as a covet minor will complete a covert
minor information sheet provided by the compliance check manager. The
information sheet will contain basic information on the covert minor, contact
information, medical information and emergency information.
         (b)   The compliance check manager will review the statement of
understanding (included with the covert minor information sheet), which
outlines the rules for the covert minor and the goals and directions of the
compliance check operation with the covert minor. The covert minor must also
agree to participate in any additional follow-up investigations, case review
and preparation, trials involving the seller and administrative review hearings
against a licensee.
         (c)   The compliance check manager will maintain a file on each covert
minor. The file will contain the covert minor information sheet, a copy of the
minor’s driver’s license, a completed background investigation and a photograph
of the minor. If the minor is working as part of a fine reduction arrangement,
the file will also include the original document of the minor’s violation.
      (7)   Evaluation of a covert minor. A covet minor will not be evaluated
on his or her ability to purchase alcohol from a licensee. Rather, the minor
will be evaluated based on the minor being able to conduct a fair test. Minors
will be removed from the program if they are found to be alerting businesses of
upcoming compliance checks or tipping employees of establishments while
conducting the compliance check. Officers observing or learning of such
behavior will immediately notify the compliance check manager.
      (8)   Covert minor compensation.
         (a)   Minors working through an agreement for compensation will be
compensated at a rate of $10 per hour, figured to the nearest half hour. This
compensation will be issued through a supervising officer assigned to the
operation. Compensation under this division (C)(8) does not imply employment
with the village, but is a stipend given in consideration for the voluntary
activity of the minor.
         (b)   Covert minors working through arrangements for fine reductions
will be scheduled for one compliance operation per $50 in fines issued to the
minor. No partial consideration will be made. When a covert minor agrees to
participate in this program, the minor will be assigned to the number of
details necessary to cover the entire fine amount. If the minor fails to
complete the program as agreed to, he or she will be responsible for the amount
of fines not covered by his or her participation in the program.
         (c)   Covet minors working as part of an agreement for fine reduction
will be given credit for working the compliance check operation if the Police
Department cancels the operation on short notice.
      (9)   Covert minor scheduling. The compliance check manager is
responsible for the scheduling of covert minors. Two to three minors will be
scheduled for each detail. If possible, a minor will not be scheduled for more
than two compliance check details in one month. The minor is required to notify
the compliance check manager if he or she is unable to complete an assignment
as scheduled.
   (D)   Operational funds.
      (1)   The compliance check manager will maintain and manage funds to
conduct compliance check operations. Funds will be requested from the Village
Administrator in $500 increments. The compliance check manager will keep these
funds secured in his or her office. A fund log will be maintained that shows
the distribution of these funds and the return of funds not used during the
compliance check operation.
      (2)   On each occasion that compliance check funds are to be used, the
compliance check manager will determine the amount of funds necessary to
complete the operation. The compliance check manager will log such funds out of
the account and issue them to the supervising officer(s). A covert fund
tracking sheet provided by the compliance check manager will be completed,
verified and signed by a supervising officer assigned to the operation.
      (3)   Upon the conclusion of the compliance check operation, a
supervising officer assigned to the operation will conduct an accounting of all
expenditures and will reconcile the funds on the covert detail sheet. This
reconciliation shall be reported to the Village Administrator in a timely
manner. If discrepancies are found, the supervising officer will provide a memo
outlining what the discrepancies are and what actions are needed to reconcile
the account. Said funds shall be audited annually by the Village Auditor.
      (4)   If minors used in the compliance check operation are working
through an agreement for compensation, said agreement is subject to approval of
the Village Administrator. A supervising officer assigned to the operation will
provide the minor the appropriate funds as per the agreement. A minor receiving
compensation must sign the covert fund tracking sheet for the funds received.
      (5)   A supervising officer assigned to the operation will return the
unused funds to the compliance check manager. The compliance check manager will
review the expenditures and ensure that the accounting is true and correct. If
discrepancies are found, the compliance check manager will note the discrepancy
and request a memo from the supervising officer regarding the discrepancy. A
copy of the discrepancy report shall be timely filed with the Village
Administrator. The funds will then be placed back into the covert funds account
and the return of unused funds will be documented on the covert fund log by the
compliance check manager.
      (6)   Covert funds will be subject to periodic audits by the Police
Department and the Village Administrator and shall be audited annually by the
Village Auditor. The compliance check manager will ensure that the covert funds
log is kept current and reconciled on a monthly basis. Said monthly
reconciliations shall be reported to the Police Chief and the Village
Administrator.
   (E)   Operation procedures.
      (1)   Upon receipt from the state’s Liquor Control Commission of the
number of businesses located in the village that failed a Commission compliance
check operation, the compliance check manager will determine the number of
compliance check operations to be conducted. The compliance check manager will
then assign the appropriate number of officers and covert minors needed, and
will set the date on which the inspections are to be completed.
      (2)   The compliance check manager will, upon determining which locations
are to be inspected, calculate the amount of funds necessary to complete the
operation. The funds will then be issued to the supervising officer(s) as
provided in division (C) above. The supervising officer(s) will be provided a
kit, to include the compliance check detail sheet and the appropriate paperwork
to handle the detail. The compliance check manager will also provide any
special instructions to the supervising officer(s).
      (3)   The supervising officer(s) will conduct a pre-operation briefing.
During the briefing, the supervising officer(s) will ensure that the covert
minors appearance follows the standards set forth in division (B)(4) above. If
their appearance does not meet those standards, the supervising officer(s) will
take any necessary action to have the minors come into compliance with the
standards. If a minor is unable to meet the standards, the minor shall not be
allowed to participate in the operation. The supervising officer(s) will notify
the compliance check manager of the issues related to the appearance of a
minor.
         (a)   The supervising officer(s) will review the list of businesses to
be inspected with the covert minors. During this review, the supervising
officer(s) will determine which minors will be involved in checking specific
businesses. If the minor knows the individuals employed by the business to be
checked, the minor will not be used at that location.
         (b)   The supervising officer(s) shall review with the covert minor(s)
the procedures for conducting compliance operations, which products are to be
purchased, and what things should be said by the minor(s). The supervising
officer(s) shall also discuss entrapment and what behaviors and statements the
minor(s) should avoid to prevent entrapment from being an issue for prosecution
of a violation.
   (F)   Compliance check operations.
      (1)   The supervising officer(s) will use a Police Department vehicle in
conducting the compliance check operation. Only with advanced approval from the
Police Chief will an officer’s personally owned vehicle be used during a
compliance check operation. All participants in the operation will conduct the
operation out of the same vehicle. Covert minors will not be allowed to use
their own vehicles.
      (2)   The supervising officer(s) will determine the order in which the
compliance checks should be conducted. When conducting the inspections, the
officers should make every effort to avoid detection by the businesses being
inspected.
      (3)   When conducting the actual compliance check operation, the
supervising officer(s) shall be in a position to see and, if possible, to hear,
the transaction. When practical, this observation should take place within the
establishment.
      (4)   At a minimum, the supervising officer(s) should scan the business
to ensure that the minor is not entering into a dangerous situation. If the
supervising officer(s) are going to enter the establishment, they should do so
before the minor enters, to ensure the safety of the minor.
      (5)   The supervising officer(s) may send any combination of minors into
the establishment to aid in the natural appearance of the minors for the
business they are entering. Supervising officer(s) should avoid, as is
reasonably possible, giving the appearance that they are with the covert
minors. When using more than one minor, only one will be directed to make the
purchase of the product.
      (6)   The supervising officer(s) will issue covert funds needed to
complete a transaction to the covert minor(s) prior to their entering a
specific location. Upon conclusion of the compliance check, the supervising
officer(s) will recover from the minor(s) the funds not used in that check. The
supervising officer(s) will then record the expenses related to that compliance
check on the covert detail sheet
      (7)   During the compliance check operation, a covert minor is expected
to be a good witness. The minor will be required to identify the seller by
name, number or description to the supervising officer(s) and provide a
statement regarding the conversation conducted between the seller and the
minor.
   (G)   Attempts to purchase products.
      (1)   For purchases of products that are sold for off-premises use, the
covert minor will enter the establishment and locate the product to be
purchased. The covert minor will take the product immediately to the counter
for purchase. The quantity of the product purchased will be limited to single
serve containers, six-packs or a single item.
      (2)   If the seller asks for identification, the covert minor will
indicate that he or she does not have identification on his or her person. If
the minor is asked to provide an age or birth date, he or she will provide
information that will put his or her age over the purchase age for that
product.
      (3)   During the actual attempt to purchase, the covert minor will avoid
excessive conversation and any actions that would coerce, entice or compel the
seller to agree to the purchase.
      (4)   (a)   After the attempt to purchase occurs, the covert minor will
immediately leave the store with the product (if a purchase is made) and return
to a previously agreed upon meeting location. The minor(s) will meet with the
supervising officer(s), turn the product over to the officer(s), and review the
facts of the case.
         (b)   A review of the check will be completed and the seller
identified.
   (H)   Supervising officer’s responsibilities.
      (1)   The primary responsibility of a supervising officer is the
protection of the covert minor(s). A supervising officer will make every effort
necessary to ensure that a covert minor is protected. At no time will a
supervising officer make a covert minor available to the seller, business
manager or other business staff.
      (2)   While conducting a compliance check, a supervising officer will be
observant of other violations occurring in the establishment. As violations are
noted, the supervising officer(s) will document the violations and notify the
compliance check manager. When violations of a more serious nature (i.e.,
employee consumption of alcohol or drugs on duty) are found, the supervising
officer(s) will immediately notify the compliance check manager of such
observations.
   (I)   Completed inspection. Upon completion of an individual compliance
check, the supervising officer(s) will meet with the covert minor(s) and review
the check to determine if any violations have occurred.
   (J)   Compliance check wrap-up.
      (1)   At the conclusion of the compliance check operation, the
supervising officer(s) will return the covert minor(s) to the Police Department
or other requested location. Any minors who are to receive compensation for
services will be paid at that time.
      (2)   The supervising officer(s) will ensure that any issued funds not
used in the individual inspection are returned to the supervising officer(s)
and accounted for. The accounting section of the compliance check detail sheet
must be completed and a supervising officer shall sign for the return of covert
funds.
      (3)   The compliance check detail sheet shall be completed in full.
Supervising officer(s) must ensure that the outcome of each individual
inspection is noted, along with which covert minor was assigned to the specific
inspection. Pass and fail letter will be attached to the compliance check
detail sheet.
      (4)   (a)   Any reports of compliance check failures shall be completed
immediately by the supervising officer(s) following the actual operation unless
delayed reporting is authorized by the compliance check manager.
         (b)   Completed reports will be attached to the compliance check
detail sheet and all paperwork and the issued kit will be returned to the
compliance check manager.
      (5)   Upon receipt of the compliance check paperwork and kit, the
compliance check manager will reconcile the funds issued and return them to the
operations fund.
   (K)   Violations.
      (1)   Violations found.
         (a)   In cases where violations are found, the supervising officer(s)
will notify TEP and request a report number. Preliminary paperwork will be
completed prior to re-entering the establishment.
         (b)   The supervising officer(s) will wait a reasonable period of time
before re-entering the establishment, in order to provide some distance between
the purchase and notification of the violation(s). The recommended waiting
period is a minimum of five minutes. In no case should the supervising office
(s) continue to another compliance check location without first completing the
notification and issuance of a notice to appear.
         (c)   Upon re-entering the establishment, the supervising officer(s)
will request to speak to the owner, manager or employee in charge.
Additionally, efforts should be made to locate the employee(s) involved in the
violation(s). The establishment should be given a reasonable period of time to
adjust business operations to allow for the enforcement action to occur.
         (d)   The supervising officer(s) shall provide notification to the
offending employee(s). During said notification, the supervising officer(s)
should note any spontaneous statements made by the offending employee(s) and/or
the business representative and include those statements in the police report.
Supervising officer(s) should also make note of the conditions of the
establishment with respect to signage and other warnings or procedures specific
to the control of the sale of the products.
         (e)   In the event that a demand is made by the offending employee(s)
or business representative to see the covert minor(s), the supervising officer
(s) shall advise the requestor(s) that it is not possible and that such request
should be made to the compliance check manager. Under no circumstances shall
the requestor be allowed to see covert minor(s).
         (f)   Unless circumstances dictate otherwise, the offender(s) will be
issued a notice to appear for the ordinance violation(s) as provided in §
114.999 of this chapter. The supervising officer(s) will issue the notice of
violation (i.e., “failure letter”) to the owner, business manager or
representative. They will also encourage the owner, business manager or
representative to contact the compliance check manager for a case review and
suggestions for improvement. A copy of the failure letter will be included in
the report.
         (g)   Violation reports will include a detailed narrative of the
violation. The report will also include the name and date of birth of the
covert minor(s). Addresses and phone numbers for the covert minor(s) shall not
be included in the report. The address of the Police Department and the
compliance check manager’s business telephone number are to be used as the
address and phone number for the covert minor(s).
      (2)   No violations found.
         (a)   When an establishment successfully passes an inspection, a
letter of congratulations (i.e., “pass letter”) will be prepared. The pass
letter will identify the seller by name or number.
         (b)   Upon completion of the compliance check operation, and after the
covert minor(s) have been released, the supervising officer(s) will return to
those establishments that successfully passed inspection and issue the letter
to the owner, manager or representative. The pass letter will note who the
letter was served to.
(Ord. 16-005, passed 3-7-2016) Penalty, see §
114.999
JUNK DEALERS AND JUNKYARDS
§ 114.055 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful to purchase, sell or deal in junk, rags, old
rope, paper, bagging, old iron, brass, copper, tin, lead, empty bottles or
similar articles or to operate or carry on the business of keeper of a junk
shop, store or place for the purchase, sale or dealing in any of said articles
without first having obtained a license therefor.
   (B)   Such articles shall include the purchase and sale of junked
automobiles or parts thereof.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-1) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.056 LICENSE APPLICATION; APPROVAL.
   (A)   Application for such license shall set forth the name and address of
the applicant, the description of his or her business, the place where such
junk shop, store or place is to be operated and the area of said junkyard.
   (B)   Such application shall be subject to approval by the Board of
Trustees.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-2)
§ 114.057 LICENSE FEES.
   The annual license fee for such business and each vehicle used in the
conduct of said business shall be established by ordinance as set forth in the
license fee schedule of §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-3) (Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986)
§ 114.058 PREMISES REQUIREMENT; AREA LIMITATION.
   No junkyard shall be maintained in a greater area than 20,000 square feet
and the Board may, at its discretion, in the best interest of the public, limit
and restrict the number of licenses to be issued therein.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-4) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.059 LICENSE CONDITIONS.
   (A)   Conduct of business. In every case where a license is issued under the
provisions of this chapter, the licensee shall maintain and operate his or her
business and, in particular, his or her junkyard, in event a junkyard is
operated, in such a manner as to not be a nuisance, and such licensee shall at
all times keep his or her junkyard clear of unnecessary rubbish and clear away
rubbish as may be directed by the Police Department from time to time, and if
in event such licensee shall not operate said junkyard in conformity with
regulations of the Police Department, the village shall in all cases reserve
the right to declare such junkyard a nuisance and abate same as such; and all
licenses issued to junk dealers shall particularly specify therein that same is
taken subject to provisions herein contained to which the licensee consents.
   (B)   Vehicles. Every vehicle used by a junk dealer in the conduct of his or
her business shall bear thereon in legible characters the name and address of
the owner and proprietor thereof.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-5) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.060 STOLEN GOODS.
   (A)   Each keeper of a junk shop or junkyard who shall receive or be in
possession of any goods, articles or things of value which may have been stolen
shall, upon demand, produce such articles or things to any member of the Police
Department for examination.
   (B)   No keeper of a junk shop or a junkyard shall purchase, take or receive
from any person any catalytic converter that is not attached to a motor vehicle
or any portion of a dismantled catalytic converter that is reasonably
identifiable as such.
(Prior Code, § 3-6-6) (Ord. 15-027, passed 7-6-2015) Penalty, see §
114.999
SECONDHAND STORES
§ 114.075 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall operate or conduct a secondhand store without having first
obtained a license therefor.
(Prior Code, § 3-7-1) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.076 LICENSE APPLICATION; INVESTIGATION.
   Applications for such licenses shall state the location intended to be
occupied. Upon receipt of such application, the Chief of Police shall cause to
have investigated the character of the applicant. No license shall be issued to
anyone who is not a person of good character nor to any person who shall have
been convicted of burglary, robbery or of receiving stolen goods.
(Prior Code, § 3-7-2)
§ 114.077 LICENSE FEES.
   The annual license fee for a secondhand store shall be based on the number
of employees as provided in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-7-3)
§ 114.078 RECORDS KEPT.
   Every person operating a secondhand store shall keep a record of every
article purchased by or sold to him or her stating the name and address of the
person from whom such purchase was made, an accurate description of the
article, the time of such purchase and the price paid therefor and this record
shall be open to inspection by any police officer at any time.
(Prior Code, § 3-7-4) Penalty, see §
114.999
LEASING AND/OR MANAGEMENT AGENTS
§ 114.090 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   AGENT. An individual or firm authorized to act on behalf of another.
   LEASING AGENT. The person, business, association, corporation or
organization contracting on behalf of the owner for the use or occupancy of
real property under terms of a lease, regardless of whether verbal or written.
   MANAGEMENT AGENT. The person, business or organization handling,
supervising, controlling or directing the use or occupancy or business affairs
of real property on behalf of the owner.
   REAL ESTATE. An identified parcel or tract of land, including improvements
if any, a piece of land, including the air above it and the ground below it and
any buildings or structures on it.
   REAL ESTATE AGENT. A licensed salesperson working for a real estate broker.
REAL ESTATE BROKER or REAL ESTATE SALESPERSON means a person licensed to
arrange the buying and selling of real estate for a fee.
   REAL PROPERTY. The interest, benefits, and rights inherent in the ownership
of real estate.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.091 REGISTRATION AND BUSINESS LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   No person shall engage in the business of soliciting for the purchase,
sale or lease of any real estate or property within the village without first
having been registered with the Village Collector or such other person so
designated by the President and Board of Trustees, and it shall be unlawful to
engage in business in the village as a leasing or management agent for rental
property, either directly or through an authorized designee, without first
having obtained a business license therefor from the village, paying the
applicable business license fee as hereafter required.
   (B)   No person shall engage in the business of actively participating in
the real estate sales or leasing process (e.g., informing potential purchasers
or lessees of current listings), meeting with property owners or property
managers for the purpose of acquiring a listing on the property or facilitating
the lease of real estate or property, conducting viewings of listed property,
procurement of an interested party to a real estate transaction or lease and/or
arranging for preliminary options, without first having been registered with
the Village Collector or such other person so designated by the President and
the Board of Trustees.
   (C)   It shall be unlawful to actively participate or engage in the leasing
process in the village or to conduct business in the village as a leasing and/
or rental management agent broker or real estate salesperson, either directly
or through an authorized designee, without first having obtained a business
license therefor from the village, paying the applicable business license fee
as hereafter required.
   (D)   Where an employee, agent, licensed individual or an unlicensed
individual, association or corporation renders its services directly to a
licensed salesperson leasing and/or rental management agent, to the extent
allowable by law, said person shall not be required to obtain a business
license.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.092 APPLICATION OF PROVISIONS.
   (A)   (1)   This chapter shall apply to all leasing and/or rental management
agents conducting business within the village whether their place of business
is located within or without the corporate limits of the village.
      (2)   The annual business license fee for registering as a real estate
broker or leasing or rental management agent shall be established by ordinance
as set forth in the business license fee schedule of §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   All provisions of §
110.001 of this code of ordinances are applicable and are incorporated herein
as if fully set forth.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.093 APPLICATION FOR BUSINESS LICENSE.
   Application for any business licenses required by this subchapter shall be
made to the Village Collector or such other person so designated by the
President and Board of Trustees, in writing, under oath, stating:
   (A)   The name and address of the applicant in the case of an individual; if
a partnership, the persons entitled to share in the profits thereof; and, if a
firm, corporation or limited liability corporation, the corporate name,
registered office and agent, and the date of incorporation or license to do
business under an assumed name;
   (B)   A copy of the required license, if any, issued by the state; and
   (C)   A statement that applicant will not violate any of the laws of the
state or the United States or any ordinance of the village in the conduct of
business.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.094 RESTRICTION ON ISSUANCE OF BUSINESS LICENSE.
   No business license shall be issued under this subchapter to:
   (A)   A person, partnership, firm, corporation or limited liability
corporation, who at the time of application for renewal of any business license
issued hereunder, would not be eligible for such business license upon an
original application;
   (B)   A corporation or limited liability corporation, unless it is
incorporated in the state, or unless it is a foreign corporation which is
qualified under the state’s Business Corporation Act, being 805 ILCS 5/1.01 et
seq. as now or hereafter amended, to transact business in the state, including
the act commonly known as “blockbusting”;
   (C)   A copartnership, unless all of the members of such copartnership shall
be qualified to obtain a business license; and
   (D)   A person, partnership, firm, corporation or limited liability
corporation who provides false or incorrect information or misrepresentation of
any material facts in the business license application.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.095 TERM OF BUSINESS LICENSE.
   All business licenses to be issued under this subchapter shall be for a
period of one year and shall expire on April 30 of each year.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.096 PAYMENT AND DISPOSITION OF BUSINESS LICENSE FEES.
   All business license fees required by this subchapter shall be paid to the
Village Collector or to such other person as may be designated. Upon such
payment, the business license fees shall be promptly turned over to the Village
Treasurer for deposit in the Corporate Fund. New business licenses issued on or
after November 1 shall require payment of only one-half the annual business
license fee. There shall be no refund of any fee paid for any unused portion of
the license period.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.097 RENEWAL OF BUSINESS LICENSES.
   Any licensee failing to apply for the renewal of said business license in a
timely manner shall be subject to the late filing penalties provided for in §
114.999 of this chapter.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.098 TRANSFER OF BUSINESS LICENSE.
   A business license shall be purely a personal privilege, good for not to
exceed one year after issuance, unless sooner revoked as in this subchapter
provided, and shall not constitute property, nor shall it be subject to
attachment, garnishment or execution, nor shall it be transferable, voluntarily
or involuntarily, or subject to being encumbered.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.099 REVOCATION OF BUSINESS LICENSE.
   (A)   The Village Collector, or other person so designated by the President
and the Board of Trustees, shall have the authority to suspend for a period of
up to one year for cause, or revoke, for cause, any business license issued
pursuant to this subchapter.
   (B)   FOR CAUSE shall mean any violation of any provision hereof, or for any
misrepresentation of any material facts set forth in the application for the
business license, or for the violation of any state law or village ordinance,
pertaining to the purchase, sale or lease of any real estate or property.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.100 RECORD OF BUSINESS LICENSES AND REVOCATIONS.
   The Village Collector, or other person so designated by the President and
the Board of Trustees, shall keep or cause to be kept a complete record of all
business licenses issued or revocations hereunder.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)
§ 114.101 RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   (A)   The Village Collector, or such other person so designated by the
President and the Board of Trustees, shall promulgate due process rules and
regulations for any charges brought pursuant to §
114.096 of this chapter.
   (B)   Said rules and regulations shall be approved by the President and the
Board of Trustees prior to becoming effective.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000)

§ 114.115 DEFINITIONS.
   The terms BARBER SHOP and BEAUTY SHOP, as used in this subchapter, shall be
construed to mean a place where the hair is cut, cleansed, treated or dressed,
or the face is shaved or the beard trimmed, for hire, and where also, manicure,
chiropody or massage treatments are sometimes furnished for hire, and shall
also be deemed to include hair dressing establishments which are commonly
patronized by women.
(Prior Code, § 3-11-1)

114.999

in the establishment.
(Prior Code, § 3-11-3)

   The annual license fee for such business shall be established by ordinance

110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.

§ 114.119 SANITARY CONDITIONS AND REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Premises. Premises used for barber shop or beauty shop shall be kept
in a clean and sanitary condition and it shall be unlawful to permit waste
materials of any kind to accumulate therein.
   (B)   Employees. It shall be unlawful to employ in such establishment any
persons afflicted with a venereal or contagious disease.
   (C)   Equipment and supplies. It shall be unlawful to use in any
establishment used as a barber shop or beauty shop any implements or tools upon
any person after the same have been used upon a person afflicted with any skin
disease without sterilizing the tool or implement afterwards and it shall be
unlawful to use any towel on any customer after the same has been used without
having such towel sterilized and cleaned prior to such second usage.
   (D)   Customers. No person infected with any disease of the face or head
shall have the same barbered or treated in any manner in a barber shop or hair
dressing establishment in the village, nor shall any person with hand disease
be manicured therein.
(Prior Code, § 3-11-5) Penalty, see §
114.999

   (B)   Fire hazards. The Chief of the Fire Department shall have the right to
