COIN-OPERATED DRY CLEANING MACHINE PLANTS
§ 114.180 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a coin-operated dry cleaning
machine plant in the village who does not possess a license from the village.
(Prior Code, § 3-15B-2-1) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.181 LICENSE FEE.
   The license fee for a coin-operated dry cleaning machine plant shall apply
for each calendar year or any portion thereof. This fee shall be as provided in
§
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-15B-2-2)
§ 114.182 INSPECTIONS.
   Operation of such a plant shall not begin prior to inspection and approval
by the Building Commissioner and Fire Chief.
(Prior Code, § 3-15B-2-3)
§ 114.183 REQUIREMENTS AND REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Building requirements.
      (1)   Such structures shall be single-story with concrete floors in good
condition.
      (2)   Machines shall not be installed in buildings used in whole or in
part as dwellings.
      (3)   Maintenance areas shall be separate from customer service areas.
   (B)   Sanitation requirements.
      (1)   Every room or place of a plant shall at all times be kept in good
repair and in a clean and sanitary condition.
      (2)   Separate toilet facilities for men and women shall be provided.
   (C)   Plant and machine operation requirements.
      (1)   An attendant shall be on duty and present at all hours the plant is
open for business.
      (2)   Customers shall not be permitted in maintenance service areas. The
doors of any such areas shall be kept locked to the public.
      (3)   Complete step-by-step operating instructions shall be posted near
the machines in the customer service area. The instructions shall also include
the statements, as follows: notify attendant if any odor of solvent remains in
garment or material, and garment or materials bearing the odor of solvent are
dangerous if enclosed in an automobile or other enclosed places.
      (4)   Warning signs shall be posted requiring the evacuation of the plant
in the presence of noticeable vapor odor or in the presence of such symptoms as
irritation of the eyes, nose or throat, lacrimation or dizziness. The attendant
shall enforce such evacuation.
      (5)   The attendant shall take all reasonable precautions to see that
materials that cannot be properly cleaned shall not be placed in machines.
      (6)   All machines shall be inspected by plant personnel daily and any
machine found to be operating improperly or found to be unsafe shall not be
placed in service and shall be clearly marked “Out of Order - Do Not Use”.
      (7)   All pipes, connections and transfer pumps carrying the cleaning
solvent shall be maintained tight and free from leaks.
      (8)   Servicing of machines shall be done only during the operation of
exhaust ventilation.
      (9)   The dry cleaning solvent shall be stored in tightly closed
containers and shall be transferred from the containers by means of a closed
system. All solvent storage containers, external from machine tanks, must be
adequately and properly labeled and stored in a maintenance or storage area of
the plant.
      (10)   Filter residue and other residues containing dry cleaning solvent
shall be stored in tightly covered metal containers outside of the plant in an
area not accessible to the public and shall be collected by a scavenger
according to the terms of this code of ordinances.
      (11)   Spotting of materials shall be done with no solvent other than
water.
   (D)   Safety and testing equipment requirements.
      (1)   Respiratory protective equipment, approved for use in the plant by
the Fire Chief, shall be provided for attendants and maintenance personnel and
shall be kept in good repair and available for immediate use.
      (2)   Utility fire extinguishers shall be provided. The type, capacity,
number and location of extinguishers shall be designated by the Fire Chief.
Such extinguishers shall be maintained properly.
      (3)   Safety goggles, rubber gloves and rubber safety aprons shall be
provided for service personnel.
      (4)   (a)   A device for testing concentration of solvent vapors in the
plant atmosphere shall be provided by the licensee.
         (b)   Such device shall be a Kitagawa Precision Gas Detector, Unico
Model No. 400 or equivalent, and maintained with no fewer than ten gas detector
tubes of the appropriate type.
         (c)   Such equipment shall be kept at the plant and made available for
on-site inspection services by the Building Commissioner and Fire Chief.
      (5)   A telephone of the non-pay type shall be available at the plant for
emergency use. Village fire and police numbers shall be posted conspicuously at
the phone.
   (E)   Compliance with other provisions. The building shall in all other
respects comply with the building, light and ventilation requirements of this
code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-15B-2-4) Penalty, see §
114.999

§ 114.227 INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   Fire safety. Every warehouse operated or maintained in the village
shall be inspected under and by the authority of the Fire Prevention Bureau at

CABLE TELEVISION
§ 114.240 ADOPTING RULES AND REGULATIONS OF FCC.
   (A)   The Mayor and Board of Trustees of the village do hereby adopt the
rules and regulations set forth by the Federal Communications Commission
pursuant to § 623(b) of the Cable Televisions Consumer Protection and
Competition Act of 1992 (47 U.S.C. § 543(b)) for the review of the basic
service tier of cable television services and equipment necessary for the
provision of such service tier.
   (B)   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      BASIC SERVICE TIER OF CABLE TELEVISION SERVICES. A separately available
service tier to which subscription is required for access to any other tier of
service, including as a minimum, but not limited to, all signals of domestic
television broadcast stations provided to any subscriber, (except a signal
secondarily transmitted by satellite carrier beyond the local service area of
such station, regardless of how such signal is ultimately received by the cable
system) any public, education and governmental programming required by the
franchise to be carried on the basic tier, and any additional video programming
signals or service added to the basic tier by the cable operator.
      EQUIPMENT NECESSARY TO PROVIDE SAID BASIC TIER OF SERVICE. Those items of
associated equipment necessary for the reception of basic cable service by a
subscriber, including, but not limited to, converter boxes, remote control
units, additional outlets and installations.
(Ord. 94-237, passed 1-25-1994)
§ 114.241 PUBLIC HEARING; NOTIFICATION.
   (A)   The village shall provide the grantee of the cable television
franchise, the public and interested parties with an opportunity to be heard at
a public hearing before the Mayor and the Board of Trustees, upon 14 days’
written notice to the grantee of the cable television franchise of the time and
place of the public hearing; provided further that, said notice shall indicate
that the purpose of the public hearing is to receive the views of the grantee
and interested parties on issues pertaining to regulation of the basic service
tier of cable television services and equipment necessary to provide said basic
tier of service; and, provided further that, notice of said public hearing
shall be published in a local newspaper of general circulation at least ten
days before the date of this hearing and provided further, that an agenda for
said public hearing shall be posed in a public place at the Village Hall at
least seven days prior to said public hearing.
   (B)   Upon the adoption of this subchapter and the certification of the
village by the Federal Communications Commission, the village shall immediately
notify the cable operator by certified mail, return receipt requested, that the
village intends to regulate subscriber rates charged for the basic service tier
and associated equipment as authorized by the Cable Television Consumer
Protection and Competition Act of 1992, being Pub. Law No. 102-385 as now or
hereafter amended. Upon receipt of said notice by the village, the cable
operator shall, within 30 days, file with the village its current rates for the
basic service tier and associated equipment along with any additional
documentation justifying the reasonableness of its rates.
(Ord. 94-237, passed 1-25-1994)
§ 114.242 REVIEW OF RATES.
   (A)   The village shall establish that the period for review of rates of the
basic service tier of cable television services and the equipment necessary to
provide said basic tier of services shall be 30 days from the submission by the
grantee of the cable television franchise of Federal Communications Commission
Form 393. If the Mayor and the Board of Trustees of the village take no action
within 30 days from the date the cable operator files its basic cable rate with
the town, the proposed rates will continue in effect.
   (B)   In the event that additional time for review of the Federal
Communications Commission Form 393 submitted by grantee is necessary, the Mayor
and the Board of Trustees of the village or their designee shall issue a brief
written order prior to the end of the 30-day review period, with a copy of said
order to be sent by certified United States mail to the grantee, providing for
an additional 90-day period for review of rates of the basic service tier and
the equipment necessary to provide said basic tier of service. During the
extended review period and before taking action on the proposed rate, the Mayor
and the Board of Trustees of the village shall hold at least one public hearing
in which interested citizens may express their views and record objections.
(Ord. 94-237, passed 1-25-1994)
§ 114.243 REVIEW OF SERVICE.
   (A)   The village shall establish that the period for review of the basic
service tier of cable television services and the equipment necessary to
provide said basic tier of services shall be 90 days from the submission by the
grantee of information and forms prescribed by the Federal Communications
Commission for a showing of cost-of-service, as defined by the Federal
Communications Commission.
   (B)   In the event that the additional time for review of the cost-of-
service showing submitted by the grantee is necessary, the Mayor and the Board
of Trustees or their designee shall issue a brief written order prior to the
end of the 90-day review period with a copy of said order to be sent by
certified U.S. mail to the grantee, providing for an additional 150-day period
for review of rates of the basic service tier and the equipment necessary to
provide said basic tier of service. During the extended review period and
before taking action on the proposed rate, the Mayor and the Board of Trustees
of the village shall hold at least one public hearing in which interested
citizens may express their views and record objections.
(Ord. 94-237, passed 1-25-1994)
§ 114.244 FORMAL RESOLUTION.
   (A)   (1)   Upon completion of its review of the proposed rates for the
basic service tier of cable television services and the equipment necessary to
provide said basic tier of service, the Mayor and the Board of Trustees of the
village shall adopt its decision by formal resolution. Said resolution shall
indicate the reasons for the decision.
      (2)   Upon passage of the resolution, the Mayor and the Board of Trustees
shall publish the resolution in pamphlet form.
   (B)   In the event that the cable operator’s proposed rates exceed the
reasonable rate standard as established by the FCC in its rules and regulations
attached to the ordinance codified herein, the Mayor and the Mayor and the
Board of Trustees may order the rates reduced by rollbacks or refunds to
subscribers, in the byline FCC.
(Ord. 94-237, passed 1-25-1994)
§ 114.245 AUTHORIZATION.
   The Mayor or appropriate designee, is authorized to execute on behalf of the
village and file with the FCC, such certification forms or other instruments as
are now or may hereafter be required by the FCC rate regulations in order to
enable the village to regulate basic service rates and charges.
(Ord. 94-237, passed 1-25-1994)
§ 114.246 REFUND OF RATES.
   The Mayor and the Board of Trustees of the village may order the cable
operator to refund to subscribers a portion of previously paid rates under the
following circumstances:
   (A)   A portion of the previously paid rates have been determined to be in
excess of the permitted basic cable service tier charge or above the actual
cost of equipment; or
   (B)   The cable operator has failed to comply with a valid rate order issued
by the town.
(Ord. 94-237, passed 1-25-1994)
§ 114.247 VIOLATION.
   Failure by the cable operator to comply with the terms and conditions
established by this subchapter, including the codified ordinance’s attachment,
shall constitute a violation of the Cable Television Franchise Ordinance
originally enacted by the Board of Trustees on 8-18-1981 and amended and
extended on 2-2-1993. Penalties for such violation are subject to the
provisions of the municipal code of the village.
(Ord. 94-237, passed 1-25-1994)
UNATTENDED COLLECTION BOXES
§ 114.260 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly requires a different meaning.
   OPERATOR. A entity, association or organization who places, maintains or
operates unattended collection box(es) to solicit donations of salvageable
personal property.
   PERMITTEE. The operator who is issued a permit (with written authorization
of the property owner) for placement of an unattended collection box.
   PROPERTY OWNER. Person, entity, association, business or organization who
owns the real property where the unattended collection box(es) are or are
proposed to be located.
   RESIDENTIAL DISTRICT. Includes residential zoning districts.
   UNATTENDED COLLECTION BOX. Any unattended container, receptacle, box or
similar device that is located on any property within the village and used for
soliciting and collecting clothing or other salvageable personal property.
(Ord. 16-023, passed 11-7-2016)
§ 114.261 PERMITS.
   (A)   Unless otherwise exempt, it shall be unlawful and a public nuisance to
place, operate, maintain or allow unattended collection boxes on real property
without first obtaining a permit pursuant to this subchapter and the unattended
collection box is placed, operated and maintained in association with all
provisions in this subchapter.
   (B)   The permit application shall be made on a form provided by the village
and shall contain the following information:
      (1)   The name, address, email, website (if applicable) and telephone
number of the applicant;
      (2)   The address of the subject real property; a drawing/site plan
sufficient to indicate the proposed location of the unattended collection box
on the subject real property (must be accessory to a principal structure
located on the lot);
      (3)   The size of the proposed unattended collection box (maximum four
feet by five feet by six and one-half feet);
      (4)   The distance of the unattended collection box to any existing
unattended collection boxes;
      (5)   The proposed material of the collection box (metal or resin only);
      (6)   The text of the disclosure to be attached to the collection box, as
required by this subchapter; and
      (7)   Proof of non-profit status.
   (C)   Each application shall include a non-refundable fee of $250. This fee
shall be in addition to any fee or tax imposed by the village pursuant to any
other provision of this code.
   (D)   Permits will only be issued to non-profit organizations.
   (E)   Applications shall be filed with the Village Clerk.
   (F)   The Village Clerk shall issue a permit within 30 days of receiving the
application or the application will be deemed denied.
   (G)   The Village Clerk shall not issue a permit unless:
      (1)   The applicant has submitted a complete and accurate application
accompanied by the applicable fee;
      (2)   The site has been pre-approved by the village;
      (3)   The proposed location and placement of the unattended collection
box on the subject real property is in compliance with all applicable laws and
will not impede pedestrian, bicycle, site distances onto adjacent streets or
vehicular traffic;
      (4)   The proposed unattended collection box is located a minimum of 400
feet from the nearest property line of any lot which serves as the location of
an existing unattended collection box; and
      (5)   The applicant organization is a non-profit.
   (H)   Permits issued hereunder shall be valid for one unattended collection
box. Each unattended collection box shall have its own individual permit with a
maximum of two collection boxes per lot.
   (I)   The permit expires one year from the date of issuance.
   (J)   No operator to whom a permit has been issued shall transfer, assign or
convey such permit to another person, organization or operator.
   (K)   A permit holder may surrender the permit by notifying the Village
Clerk in writing of the intent to surrender. The permit shall be void upon the
Village Clerk’s receipt of a written notice of intent to surrender.
   (L)   The permit holder may renew a valid current permit by submitting to
the Village Clerk a timely renewal application and pay a renewal fee in the
amount of $250.
   (M)   There shall be no more than four permits issued at any one time.
(Ord. 16-023, passed 11-7-2016) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.262 REQUIREMENTS AND MAINTENANCE.
   (A)   A permittee shall operate and maintain or cause to be operated and
maintained all unattended collection boxes located in the city as follows.
      (1)   Unattended collection boxes shall be in good condition with no
structural damage, holes or visible rust and shall be free of any graffiti.
      (2)   Unattended collection boxes shall be locked or otherwise secured.
      (3)   Unattended collection boxes should have the following information
in two-inch type visible on the front of each box:
         (a)   Name of the permittee;
         (b)   Address of the permittee;
         (c)   Phone number of the permittee; and
         (d)   Email of the permittee.
      (4)   Unattended collection boxes shall be serviced and emptied at least
once per month or within five business days of a request by the village.
   (B)   A permittee shall maintain the area surrounding the unattended
collection box and keep it free of any junk, garbage, trash, debris or other
refuse material.
   (C)   The permittee shall be individually and severally responsible for
abating and removing all junk, garbage, trash, debris and other refuse material
from the area surrounding the unattended collection box within 24 hours of
written or verbal notice from the village.
   (D)   The permittee shall be individually and severally responsible to the
extent provided by law for all the village’s costs to abate and remove any
nuisance including junk, garbage, trash, debris and other refuse material from
the area surrounding the unattended collection boxes.
   (E)   No collection box may be permitted on any unimproved land or parcel of
land, nor where the principal use of the land has been closed, abandoned or
unoccupied for more than 30 days.
   (F)   An unattended collection box shall not be placed closer than ten feet
from:
      (1)   A public or private sidewalk;
      (2)   A public right-of-way;
      (3)   A driveway; or
      (4)   A side or rear property line of adjacent property used for
residential purposes.
   (G)   A unattended collection box shall not:
      (1)   Encroach upon or obstruct a designated fire lane or building exit;
      (2)   Interfere with an access drive, off-street parking lot maneuvering
lane and/or required off-street parking space to an extent which would cause
safety hazards and/or unnecessary inconvenience to the vehicular or pedestrian
traffic; and/or
      (3)   Encroach upon an access drive, off-street parking lot maneuvering
lane and/or required off-street parking space.
   (H)   Unattended collection boxes shall be placed on a level, hard (asphalt
or concrete) paved, dust-free surface.
(Ord. 16-023, passed 11-7-2016) Penalty, see §
114.999
§ 114.263 PERMIT REVOCATION; REMOVAL; LIABILITY.
   The village shall have the right to revoke any permit issued hereunder. Upon
revocation, a permittee shall be prohibited from applying for a permit under
this subchapter for one year.
(Ord. 16-023, passed 11-7-2016)
§ 114.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   Inspections; entry and arrest powers. A police officer or any
other official designated by the village to make inspections shall have the
right to enter any premises showing evidence of a flea market for the purpose
of enforcement or inspection and may close the flea market and/or arrest any
individual who violates the provisions of §§
114.001 through
114.005 of this chapter.
      (2)   Penalty. Any person, firm or corporation found guilty of violating
the provisions of §§
114.001 through
114.005 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $100, nor more than $750.
Every article sold and every day a sale is conducted in violation of §§
114.001 through
114.005 of this chapter shall constitute a separate offense.
   (C)   (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to:
         (a)   Engaging in the business of the care of lawns, shrubs, trees and
any other occupation pertaining to landscape maintenance without first securing
a landscape and lawn care professional’s license from the village;
         (b)   Failing to either remove yard waste from the premises upon the
conclusion of each work day, or failing to leave the yard waste in brown paper
yard waste bags in the rear of the premises;
         (c)   Leaving debris or yard waste from landscaping or lawn care
services on the parkway;
         (d)   Violation of other village ordinances by the licensee
concerning:
            1.   Unauthorized dumping of debris;
            2.   Use of back-pack leaf blowers between May 15 and October 1;
and/or
            3.   Any other ordinance pertaining to landscape maintenance.
         (e)   Make inaccurate, false or misleading statements in any
application for any such license;
         (f)   Make substantial misrepresentation or false promise of a
character likely to influence or induce another in connection with the business
of landscaping; and/or
         (g)   Pursue a continued course of misrepresentations or making false
promises through advertising, salesperson, agents or otherwise in connection
with the business of landscaping.
      (2)   Any person found guilty of violating any terms of §§
114.020 through
144.022 of this chapter shall be found guilty of a misdemeanor and shall, upon
conviction thereof, be fined in an amount not less than $100, nor more than
$1,000, for each offense. Every day that a violation exists constitutes a
separate offense.
   (D)   (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person who owns, manages, operates
or otherwise controls the use of any premises licensed under §§
114.035 through
114.042 of this chapter to fail to comply with any of its provisions.
      (2)   (a)   Other than violations of §
114.039(A)(4) or (A)(7) of this chapter, any licensee found to have violated §§
114.035 through
114.042 of this chapter, or whose employee shall have violated this §§
114.035 through
114.042 of this chapter shall be deemed guilty and punishable by:
            1.   First violation: a fine of $5,000; and
            2.   Second violation, within 12 months after first conviction: a
fine of $5,000 and a 60-day license suspension.
         (b)   Any licensee found to have violated §
114.039(A)(4) or (A)(7) of this chapter shall be deemed guilty and punishable
by:
            1.   First violation: a fine of $5,000 and a 30-day license
suspension;
            2.   Second violation, within 12 months: a fine of $5,000 and be
subject to revocation of the license; and
            3.   Third violation, within five years of first conviction: a fine
of $25,000 and license revocation.
         (c)   Any licensee who has received an order of suspension or order of
revocation shall comply with the order immediately unless a timely appeal is
filed. The licensee may obtain a post-suspension or post-revocation hearing
before the Mayor or a hearing officer appointed by the Mayor. The request for a
hearing must be made in writing within five calendar days of the effective date
of the suspension or revocation. A due process hearing will be scheduled within
21 days of the date of request for hearing. The decision of the Mayor will be
final.
      (3)   Other individuals, other than minors, found to have violated §§
114.035 through
114.042 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $100, nor more than $750.
      (4)   Minors found in unlawful possession of, or who unlawfully purchased
or attempted to purchase, tobacco, tobacco products, tobacco-related devices or
electronic delivery devices, shall be subject to a fine not less than $100, nor
more than $750, or may be subject to tobacco-related education classes,
diversion programs, community services or both.
      (5)   Any violation of any provision of §§
114.035 through
114.042 of this chapter, unless otherwise provided for, may be enforced
pursuant to §§
10.30 through
10.43 of this code of ordinances, and as amended from time to time, which
provides for the administrative adjudication of certain ordinance violations.
The Village Administrator may also direct the Village Prosecutor or the Village
Attorney to proceed before any court having competent jurisdiction to enforce
the provisions of §§
114.035 through
114.042 of this chapter, including injunctive relief.
   (E)   Any person violating the provisions of §
114.060 of this chapter shall be subject to a fine of not less than $500.
   (F)   (1)   A penalty of $20 per day, to a maximum of 30 days for each day a
leasing and/or rental management agent is late in relation to the date upon
which it should have been filed is set for violation of §§
114.090 through
114.101 of this chapter.
      (2)   During such period of delinquency, commencing immediately after the
date upon which the renewal application was required to be filed, and until all
such fees and penalties are paid in conjunction with the filing of the renewal
application and its issuance, the individual, partnership, corporation or
limited liability corporation shall cease all operations relative to the
purchase, sale or lease of real estate or property.
   (G)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §§
114.180 through
114.183 of this chapter shall be fined according to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances, and every day that the violation shall
continue, after notice of same, shall be held to constitute a separate and
distinct offense.
(Prior Code, § 3-15B-2-5)
   (H)   (1)   Any condition caused or permitted to exist in violation of the
provisions of §§
114.260 through 114.264 of this chapter shall be deemed a new and separate
offense for each day that the condition continues to exist.
      (2)   The village shall assess a fine of $500 per unattended collection
box for each violation of §§
114.260 through 114.264 of this chapter.
      (3)   Nothing in §§
114.260 through 114.264 of this chapter shall prevent the village from pursuing
any other remedy provided by law in conjunction with or in lieu of prosecuting
persons under this division (H) for violation of §§
114.260 through 114.264 of this chapter.
(Ord. 00-136, passed 1-3-2000; Ord. 03-219, passed 4-21-2003; Ord. 15-027,
passed 7-6-2015; Ord. 15-032, passed 8-3-2015; Ord. 16-005, passed 3-7-2016;
Ord. 16-023, passed 11-7-2016; Ord. 19-002, passed 4-1-2019)

ESTATE SALES
§ 115.001 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ESTATE SALE. A type of garage sale, yard sale or auction to dispose of the
majority of the materials or personal property owned by a deceased person.
ESTATE SALES are usually conducted, for a percentage of the take, by
specialists and may last several days.
   PERSONAL PROPERTY. Property, which is owned, utilized and maintained by an
individual or members of his or her residence and acquired, in the normal
course of living in or maintaining a residence. It does not include
merchandise, which was purchased for resale or obtained on consignment.
   REAL PROPERTY. Land and anything permanently affixed to it, including
buildings.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007)
§ 115.002 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (A)   No estate sale shall be conducted unless and until the individuals
desiring to conduct such sale shall obtain a permit therefore from the village.
Members of more than one residence may not join in obtaining a permit for an
estate sale. No real estate shall be sold at an estate sale.
   (B)   The permit shall set forth and restrict the time and location of such
estate sale.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007) Penalty, see §
115.999
§ 115.003 CONTENTS OF APPLICATION.
   Prior to issuance of any estate sale permit, the individuals conducting such
sale shall file a written statement with the village at least five days in
advance of the proposed sale (mailed applications must be postmarked at least
seven days in advance of the sale) setting forth the following information:
   (A)   Full name, address, daytime telephone number and email address of
applicant;
   (B)   The location at which the proposed estate sale is to be held;
   (C)   The date or dates upon which the sale shall be held;
   (D)   The date or dates of any other estate sales within the current
calendar year; and
   (E)   An affirmative statement that the property to be sold was owned by the
estate and was neither acquired, nor consigned for the purpose of resale.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007)
§ 115.004 PERMIT FEE.
   There shall be an administrative processing fee of $25 for the issuance of
such permit.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007)
§ 115.005 INVESTIGATION OF APPLICANT.
   Before issuing a permit, the village’s Revenue Department may conduct an
investigation as may reasonably be necessary to determine if there is
compliance with this subchapter.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007)
§ 115.006 NUMBER OF PERMITS RESTRICTED; EXCEPTIONS.
   (A)   No more than three such permits may be issued to one residence and/or
family household during any calendar year.
   (B)   If an estate sale is not held on the dates for which the permit is
issued or is terminated during the first day of the sale because of inclement
weather conditions and an affidavit by the permit holder to this effect is
submitted, the village may issue another permit to the applicant for an estate
sale to be conducted at the same location within 30 days from the date when the
first sale was to be held. No additional permit fee is required.
   (C)   A fourth estate sale shall be permitted in a calendar year if
satisfactory proof of a bona fide change in ownership of the real property is
first presented to the village designated representative.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007)
§ 115.007 PERMIT TO BE POSTED.
   Any permit in possession of the holder or holders of an estate sale shall be
posted on the premises in a conspicuous place so as to be seen by the public
and the village inspector or village police.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007)
§ 115.008 CONDUCT OF SALE.
   (A)   Generally. The individual to whom such permit is issued and the owner
or tenant of the premises on which such sale or activity is conducted shall be
jointly and severally responsible for the maintenance of good order and decorum
on the premises during all hours of such sale or activity. No such individual
shall permit any loud or boisterous conduct on said premises nor permit
vehicles to impede the passage of traffic on any roads or streets in the area
of such premises. All such individuals shall obey the reasonable orders of any
member of the Police or Fire Departments of the village in order to maintain
the public health, safety and welfare.
   (B)   Property permitted to be sold. It shall be unlawful for any individual
to sell or offer for sale, under authority granted by this subchapter, property
other than personal property.
   (C)   Hours of operation. Estate sales shall be limited in time to no more
than the daylight hours of three consecutive days or two consecutive weekends
(Monday through Saturday).
   (D)   Display of sale property.
      (1)   Personal property offered for sale may be displayed within the
residence, in a garage, carport and/or in a rear yard, but only in such areas.
      (2)   No personal property offered for sale at an estate sale shall be
displayed in the front or side yard areas of any such premises or in any public
right-of-way.
      (3)   However, a vehicle offered for sale may be displayed on a
permanently constructed driveway within such front or side yards.
   (E)   Signs and advertisements.
      (1)   Signs permitted. Only the following specified signs may be
displayed in relation to the a pending estate sale:
         (a)   Two signs of not more than four square feet shall be permitted
to be displayed on the property of the residence where the estate sale is being
conducted; or
         (b)   Two or not more than two square feet are permitted; provided
that, the premises upon which the estate sale is conducted is not on a major
thoroughfare and written permission to erect said signs is received from the
property owners upon whose property such signs are to be placed.
      (2)   Time limitations. No sign or other form of advertisement shall be
exhibited for more than two days prior to the day such sale to commence.
      (3)   Removal of signs. Signs must be removed each day at the close of
the estate sale activities or by the end of daylight, whichever occurs first.
   (F)   Parking regulations.
      (1)   All parking of vehicles shall be conducted in compliance with all
applicable laws and ordinances.
      (2)   Further, the village’s Police Department may enforce such temporary
controls to alleviate any special hazards and/or congestion created by any
estate sale.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007) Penalty, see §
115.999
§ 115.009 REVOCATION AND REFUSAL OF PERMIT.
   (A)   Any permit issued under this subchapter may be revoked or any
application for issuance of a permit may be refused by the village if the
application submitted by the applicant or permit holder contains any false,
fraudulent or misleading statement.
   (B)   If any individual is convicted of an offense under this subchapter,
the Village Clerk is instructed to cancel any existing estate sale permit held
by the individual convicted and not to issue such individual another estate
sale permit for a period of two years from the time of conviction.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007)
§ 115.010 PERMIT EXEMPTIONS.
   The provisions of this subchapter shall not apply to or affect the
following:
   (A)   Persons selling goods pursuant to an order or process of a court of
competent jurisdiction;
   (B)   Persons acting in accordance with their powers and duties as public
officials;
   (C)   Any sale conducted by any merchant or mercantile or other business
establishment from or at a place of business wherein such sale would be
permitted by the zoning regulations of the village or under the protection of
the non-conforming use section thereof or any other sale conducted by a
manufacturer, dealer or vendor and which sale would be conducted from properly
zoned premises and not otherwise prohibited in other ordinances; and/or
   (D)   Any governmental institution or organization when the proceeds from
the sale are used directly for the institution’s purposes.
(Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007)
GARAGE SALES
§ 115.025 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   GARAGE SALE. All general sales open to the public conducted from or on a
residential premises in any residential zone, as defined by the Zoning
Ordinance, for the purpose of disposing of personal property including, but not
limited to, all sales entitled “garage”, “lawn”, “yard”, “attic”, “porch”,
“room”, “back yard”, “patio”, “flea market” or “rummage” sale. This definition
shall not include a situation where no more than five specific items are held
out for sale and all advertisement of such sale specifically names those items
to be sold.
   PERSONAL PROPERTY. Property which is owned, utilized and maintained by an
individual or members of his or her residence and acquired in the normal course
of living in or maintaining a residence. It does not include merchandise which
was purchased for resale or obtained on consignment.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-1)
§ 115.026 PERMIT REQUIRED; CONTENTS.
   (A)   No garage sale shall be conducted unless and until the individuals
desiring to conduct such sale shall obtain a permit therefor from the Village
Clerk. Members of more than one residence may join in obtaining a permit for a
garage sale to be conducted at the residence of one of them.
   (B)   The permit shall set forth and restrict the time and location of such
garage sale.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-2) Penalty, see §
115.999
§ 115.027 APPLICATION FOR PERMIT.
   Prior to issuance of any garage sale permit, the individuals conducting such
sale shall file a written statement with the Village Clerk at least five days
in advance of the proposed sale (mailed applications must be postmarked at
least seven days in advance of the sale) setting forth the following
information:
   (A)   Full name and address of applicant;
   (B)   The location at which the proposed garage sale is to be held;
   (C)   The date or dates upon which the sale shall be held;
   (D)   The date or dates of any other garage sales within the current
calendar year; and
   (E)   An affirmative statement that the property to be sold was owned by the
applicant as his or her own personal property and was neither acquired nor
consigned for the purposes of resale.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-3)
§ 115.028 PERMIT FEES.
   There shall be an administrative processing fee of $3 for the issuance of
such permit.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-4)
§ 115.029 INVESTIGATION OF APPLICANT.
   Before issuing a permit, the Village Clerk may conduct an investigation as
may reasonably be necessary to determine if there is compliance with this
subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-5)
§ 115.030 NUMBER OF PERMITS RESTRICTED; EXCEPTIONS.
   (A)   No more than three such permits may be issued to one residence and/or
family household during any calendar year. If members of more than one
residence join in requesting a permit, then such permit shall be considered as
having been issued for each and all of such residences.
   (B)   If a garage sale is not held on the dates for which the permit is
issued or is terminated during the first day of the sale because of inclement
weather conditions and an affidavit by the permit holder to this effect is
submitted, the Village Clerk may issue another permit to the applicant for a
garage sale to be conducted at the same location within 30 days from the date
when the first sale was to be held. No additional permit fee is required.
   (C)   A fourth garage sale shall be permitted in a calendar year if
satisfactory proof of a bona fide change in ownership of the real property is
first presented to the Village Clerk or his or her duly authorized
representative.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-6)
§ 115.031 PERMIT TO BE POSTED.
   Any permit in possession of the holder or holders of a garage sale shall be
posted on the premises in a conspicuous place so as to be seen by the public
and the Village Inspector or village police.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-7)
§ 115.032 CONDUCT OF SALE.
   (A)   Generally. The individual to whom such permit is issued and the owner
or tenant of the premises on which such sale or activity is conducted shall be
jointly and severally responsible for the maintenance of good order and decorum
on the premises during all hours of such sale or activity. No such individual
shall permit any loud or boisterous conduct on said premises nor permit
vehicles to impede the passage of traffic on any roads or streets in the area
of such premises. All such individuals shall obey the reasonable orders of any
member of the Police or Fire Departments of the village in order to maintain
the public health, safety and welfare.
   (B)   Property permitted to be sold. It shall be unlawful for any individual
to sell or offer for sale, under authority granted by this subchapter, property
other than personal property.
   (C)   Hours of operation. Garage sales shall be limited in time to no more
than the daylight hours of three consecutive days or two consecutive weekends
(Saturday and Sunday).
   (D)   Display of sale property. Personal property offered for sale may be
displayed within the residence, in a garage, carport and/or in a rear yard, but
only in such areas. No personal property offered for sate at a garage sale
shall be displayed in the front or side yard areas of any such premises or in
any public right-of-way. However, a vehicle offered for sale may be displayed
on a permanently constructed driveway within such front or side yards.
   (E)   Signs and advertisements.
      (1)   Signs permitted. Only the following specified signs may be
displayed in relation to a pending garage sale:
         (a)   Two signs of not more than four square feet shall be permitted
to be displayed on the property of the residence where the garage sale is being
conducted; and
         (b)   Two signs of not more than two square feet each are permitted;
provided that, the premises upon which the garage sale is conducted is not on a
major thoroughfare and written permission to erect said signs is received from
the property owners upon whose property such signs are to be placed.
      (2)   Time limitations. No sign or other form of advertisement shall be
exhibited for more than two days prior to the day such sale is to commence.
      (3)   Removal of signs. Signs must be removed each day at the close of
the garage sale activities or by the end of daylight, whichever first occurs.
   (F)   Parking regulations. All parking of vehicles shall be conducted in
compliance with all applicable laws and ordinances. Further, the Police
Department may enforce such temporary controls to alleviate any special hazards
and/or congestion created by any garage sale.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-8) Penalty, see §
115.999
§ 115.033 REVOCATION AND REFUSAL OF PERMIT.
   (A)   Any permit issued under this subchapter may be revoked or any
application for issuance of a permit may be refused by the Village Clerk if the
application submitted by the applicant or permit holder contains any false,
fraudulent or misleading statement.
   (B)   If any individual is convicted of an offense under this subchapter,
the Village Clerk is instructed to cancel any existing garage sale permit held
by the individual convicted and not to issue such individual another garage
sale permit for a period of two years from the time of conviction.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-9)
§ 115.034 EXEMPTIONS FROM PROVISIONS.
   The provisions of this subchapter shall not apply to or affect the
following:
   (A)   Persons selling goods pursuant to an order or process of a court of
competent jurisdiction;
   (B)   Persons acting in accordance with their powers and duties as public
officials;
   (C)   Any sale conducted by any merchant or mercantile or other business
establishment from or at a place of business wherein such sale would be
permitted by the zoning regulations of the village or under the protection of
the non-conforming use section thereof or any other sale conducted by a
manufacturer, dealer or vendor and which sale would be conducted from properly
zoned premises and not otherwise prohibited in other ordinances; or
   (D)   Any bona fide charitable, eleemosynary, educational, cultural or
governmental institution or organization when the proceeds from the sale are
used directly for the institution’s or organization’s charitable purposes and
the goods or articles are not sold on a consignment basis.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-10)
§ 115.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   Inspections; entry and arrest powers. A police officer, or any
other official designated by any village ordinance to make inspections under
the licensing or regulating ordinance or to enforce the same, shall have the
right of entry to any premises showing evidence of a estate sale for the
purpose of enforcement or inspection and may close the premises from such a
sale or arrest any individual who violates the provisions of §§
115.001 through
115.010 of this chapter.
      (2)   Penalties. Any person found guilty of violating the terms of §§
115.001 through
115.010 of this chapter shall be fined as set forth in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances. Every article sold and every day a sale is
conducted in violation of §§
115.001 through
115.010 of this chapter shall constitute a separate offense.
   (C)   (1)   Inspections; entry and arrest powers. A police officer, or any
other official designated by any village ordinance to make inspections under
the licensing or regulating ordinance or to enforce the same, shall have the
right of entry to any premises showing evidence of a garage sale for the
purpose of enforcement or inspection and may close the premises from such a
sale or arrest any individual who violates the provisions of §§
115.025 through
115.034 of this chapter.
      (2)   Penalties. Any person found guilty of violating the terms of §§
115.025 through
115.034 of this chapter shall be fined as set forth in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances. Every article sold and every day a sale is
conducted in violation of §§
115.025 through
115.034 of this chapter shall constitute a separate offense.
(Prior Code, § 3-8-11)
(Ord. passed 9-20-1977; Ord. 07-397, passed 5-7-2007)

TOWING BUSINESSES
§ 116.001 DEFINITIONS.
   Unless the context otherwise requires, the words and phrases as defined in
the 625 ILCS 5/18c-1104, as amended, shall have the meanings and construction
in this subchapter as is given in said 625 ILCS 5/18c-1104, as amended.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.002 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   It shall be unlawful for any persons, partnership, corporation or other
entity to operate or cause to be operated within the village a motor vehicles
towing service (hereinafter “towing service”) without having first obtained a
license therefor as required by this subchapter.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.003 LICENSE APPLICATION.
   Applications for such license shall be submitted to the Village Clerk or to
such other person as may be designated.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.004 LICENSE FEE.
   The annual license fee for businesses providing towing of motor vehicles
services shall be $170. Said annual license fee shall be paid to the Village
Clerk or such other person as may be designated. Upon such payment, the
business license fee shall be turned over to the Village Treasurer for deposit
in the Corporate Fund. New licenses issued on or after November 1 shall require
payment of only one- half the annual license fee. There shall be no refund of
any fee paid of for any unused portion of the license period.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.005 LICENSE RENEWAL.
   (A)   Any licensee failing to apply for the renewal of said license in a
timely manner shall be subject to the late filing penalties of $50 per day, to
a maximum of 30 days for each day a renewal application is late in relation to
the date upon which it should have been filed.
   (B)   During such period of delinquency, commencing immediately after the
date upon which the renewal application was required to be filed, and until
such fees and penalties are paid in conjunction with the filing of the renewal
application and its issuance, the individual or establishment shall cease all
operations relative to the towing of motor vehicles.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.006 LICENSE TRANSFER.
   A license shall be purely a personal privilege, good for not to exceed one
year after issuance, unless sooner revoked as in this subchapter provided, and
shall not be alienable or transferable, voluntarily or involuntarily.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.007 TOW ORDERS.
   (A)   (1)   Any motor vehicle or any part thereof removed from public
property shall be authorized for removal by a tow order duly executed by a law
enforcement agency having jurisdiction prior to the removal or tow of said
motor vehicle or part thereof.
      (2)   Any motor vehicle or any part thereof removed from privately owned
property shall be authorized for removal by a tow order duly executed by the
owner or lessee of the private property from which the motor vehicle or part
thereof is being towed prior to the removal or tow of said motor vehicle or
part thereof.
   (B)   Tow orders issued for removal of a motor vehicle or any part thereof
from public or privately owned property shall not be executed by the towing
service owner, operator, employee, agent or designee.
   (C)   It shall be unlawful to violate the provisions of this section.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.008 BOOKS AND RECORDS; EXAMINATION.
   The towing service shall keep or cause to be kept a complete record of all
towing orders issued hereunder and shall furnish the village’s Chief of Police
or the Department of Revenue with copies thereof upon request.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.009 ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITY.
   The Department of Revenue, its employees, agents or designees, shall be
charged with the administration of this subchapter, as follows:
   (A)   To grant, suspend for a period of up to one year for cause and/or
revoke for cause, all licensees issued pursuant to this subchapter;
   (B)   To enter, or authorize any designee to enter at any time upon any
premises licensed hereunder to determine whether any of the provisions of this
subchapter are being violated and at such time to examine the premises of the
licensees;
   (C)   To receive complaint(s) from any citizen of the village that any of
the provisions of this subchapter have been or are being violated and to take
such actions as shall be deemed necessary and advisable;
   (D)   (1)   To enter the premises of any towing service subject to the
provisions of this subchapter for inspection and examination of books and
records in order to effectuate the proper administration and enforcement of
this subchapter.
      (2)   It shall be unlawful for any person to prevent, hinder or interfere
with any person so designated in the discharge of the duties in the performance
of this subchapter. It shall be the duty of every towing service business
subject to the provisions of this subchapter to keep accurate records and
complete books and records to which the Department of Revenue or any deputies,
representatives, employees, agents or designees thereof, shall at all times
have full access.
   (E)   (1)   To promulgate rules and regulations as deemed necessary, to
conduct hearings, to hear testimony and take proof of information in the
enforcement of this subchapter, and for such purpose to issue subpoenas which
shall be effective in any part of the state.
      (2)   For purpose of obtaining any of the information desired by the
Department of Revenue under this subchapter, a designee may be appointed.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.010 APPLICABILITY OF BUSINESS LICENSE, PERMIT PROVISIONS.
   All provisions of §
110.001 of this code of ordinances are applicable and are incorporated herein
as if full set forth.
(Ord. 99-126, passed 10-18-1999)
MOTOR VEHICLE STORAGE
§ 116.025 DEFINITIONS.
   Unless the context otherwise requires, the words and phrases as defined in
the 625 ILCS 5/18c-1104, as amended, shall have the meanings and construction
in this subchapter as is given in said 625 ILCS 5/18c-1104, as amended.
(Ord. 99-127, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.026 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   It shall be unlawful for any persons, partnership, corporation or other
entity to operate or cause to be operated within the village a motor vehicle
storage facility without having first obtained a license therefor as required
by this subchapter.
(Ord. 99-127, passed 10-18-1999) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.027 LICENSE APPLICATION.
   Applications for such license shall be submitted to the Village Clerk or to
such other person as may be designated and said application.
(Ord. 99-127, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.028 LICENSE FEE.
   (A)   The annual license fee for businesses with storing motor vehicles that
have the capacity to store:
 
10 motor vehicles                             $350
More than 10 motor vehicles, but less than 25 $750
More than 25 motor vehicles, but less than 50 $1,000
50 or more motor vehicles                     $1,200
 
   (B)   Said annual license fee shall be paid to the Village Clerk or such
other person as may be designated. Upon such payment, the business license fee
shall be turned over to the Village Treasurer for deposit in the Corporate
Fund. New licenses issued on or after November 1 shall require payment of only
one-half the annual license fee. There shall be no refund of any fee paid of
for any unused portion of the license period.
(Ord. 99-127, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.029 LICENSE RENEWAL.
   (A)   Any licensee failing to apply for the renewal of said license in a
timely manner shall be subject to the late filing penalties of $50 per day, to
a maximum of 30 days for each day a renewal application is late in relation to
the date upon which it should have been filed.
   (B)   During such period of delinquency, commencing immediately after the
date upon which the renewal application was required to be filed, and until
such fees and penalties are paid in conjunction with the filing of the renewal
application and its issuance, the individual or establishment shall cease all
operations relative to the storing of motor vehicles.
(Ord. 99-127, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.030 LICENSE TRANSFER.
   A license shall be purely a personal privilege, good for not to exceed one
year after issuance, unless sooner revoked as in this subchapter provided, and
shall not be alienable or transferable, voluntarily or involuntarily.
(Ord. 99-127, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.031 RESTRICTIONS ON ISSUANCE OR RENEWAL OF LICENSE.
   (A)   All current employees of a business operating a motor vehicle storage
facility shall, within 60 days of enactment of this subchapter, and all future
employees of a business operating a motor vehicle storage facility, shall be
fingerprinted and subject to a background check.
   (B)   No motor vehicle storing company or facility shall employ or hire any
person(s):
      (1)   Who is not of good character and reputation in the community in
which he or she resides;
      (2)   Who has been convicted of a felony under any state or federal law;
or
      (3)   Who has been convicted of a crime or misdemeanor opposed to decency
and morality.
(Ord. 99-127, passed 10-18-1999) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.032 ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITY.
   The Department of Revenue, its employees, agents or designees, shall be
charged with the administration of this subchapter, as follows:
   (A)   To grant, suspend for a period of up to one year for cause and/or
revoke for cause, all licensees issued pursuant to this subchapter;
   (B)   To enter, or authorize any designee to enter at any time upon any
premises licensed hereunder to determine whether any of the provisions of this
subchapter are being violated and at such time to examine the premises of the
licensees or any vehicles thereof;
   (C)   To receive complaint(s) from any citizen of the village that any of
the provisions of this subchapter have been or are being violated and to take
such actions as shall be deemed necessary and advisable;
   (D)   To enter the premises of any motor vehicle storing business subject to
the provisions of this subchapter for inspection and examination of books and
records in order to effectuate the proper administration and enforcement of
this subchapter. It shall be unlawful for any person to prevent, hinder or
interfere with any person so designated in the discharge of the duties in the
performance of this subchapter. It shall be the duty of every such business
subject to the provisions of this subchapter to keep accurate records and
complete books and records to which the Department of Revenue or any deputies,
representatives, employees, agents or designees thereof, shall at all times
have full access; and
   (E)   To promulgate rules and regulations as deemed necessary, to conduct
hearings, to hear testimony and take proof of information in the enforcement of
this subchapter, and for such purpose to issue subpoenas which shall be
effective in any part of the state. For purpose of obtaining any of the
information desired by the Department of Revenue under this subchapter, a
designee may be appointed.
(Ord. 99-127, passed 10-18-1999)
§ 116.033 APPLICABILITY OF BUSINESS LICENSE, PERMIT PROVISIONS.
   All provisions of §
110.001 of this code of ordinances are applicable and are incorporated herein
as if fully set forth:
   (A)   Suspension of business license for a period up to one year; or
   (B)   Revocation of business license.
(Ord. 99-127, passed 10-18-1999)
GASOLINE SERVICE STATIONS AND STORAGE PLANTS
§ 116.045 DEFINITION.
   SERVICE STATION is any place of business where gasoline or any highly
volatile fuels for motor vehicles or internal combustion engines are sold or
offered for sale at retail and dispensed into fuel tanks of such motor
vehicles. This definition shall include any private storage and dispensing of
such products for the same purpose as those served by a service station,
whether the storage is maintained for the use or benefit of the owner, lessee,
agents or employees of either, or of any others.
(Prior Code, § 3-18A-1)
§ 116.046 LICENSE REQUIRED; RESTRICTIONS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful to conduct or operate a service station in the
village without having first obtained a license therefor.
   (B)   No such license shall be issued unless the location and equipment to
be used fully comply with this village code.
(Prior Code, § 3-18A-2) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.047 LICENSE FEE.
   The annual license fee for such business shall be established by ordinance
as set forth in the license fee schedule of §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-18A-3) (Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986)
§ 116.048 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS.
   No license for a gasoline service station shall be issued unless all of the
requirements of the Building Code adopted by reference in this village code are
fully complied with.
(Prior Code, § 3-18A-4)
§ 116.049 APPLICATION OF PROVISIONS TO STORAGE PLANTS.
   The requirements covering service stations shall also govern underground
storage maintained at general storage plants and places other than service
stations, so far as possible.
(Prior Code, § 3-18A-5)
PUBLIC GARAGES
§ 116.060 DEFINITION.
   A PUBLIC GARAGE is any building or premises used or held out or advertised
to the public by the owner or person occupying or maintaining the same for the
renting, sale, storage or repair of automobiles or other motor vehicles, except
motorcycles.
(Prior Code, § 3-18B-1)
§ 116.061 LICENSE REQUIRED; APPLICATION.
   (A)   No person shall operate or maintain a public garage in the village
without first having obtained a license therefor.
   (B)   Applications for such licenses shall state thereon the location of the
garage and the number of cars which can be accommodated therein.
(Prior Code, § 3-18B-2) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.062 LICENSE FEES.
   The annual license fee for a public garage maintained for the repair or
storage only of automobiles; for a public garage maintained for the renting,
sale, storage or repair of automobiles, which shall include the sale of used
automobiles on the same premises or at one location other than the same
premises and for the sale of used automobiles only, shall be established by
ordinance as set forth in the license fee schedule of §
110.018(A) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-18B-3) (Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986)
§ 116.063 BUILDING AND PREMISES REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful to maintain or operate any public garage in a
frame or wooden building, or in any building or structure used for church,
school or theater purposes or in any building which does not conform to the
requirements of this subchapter or any provisions of this code of ordinances
relating thereto.
   (B)   The premises of every garage must be kept clean and free from
inflammable waste material.
(Prior Code, § 3-18B-4) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.064 FIRE SAFETY REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Smoking. It shall be unlawful for any person to smoke or light a
cigarette, pipe or cigar in any public garage, except in such portion thereof
as may be separated from the remainder of the premises by a partition and used
only for office purposes or outside the building.
   (B)   Fire extinguishers. There shall be kept in each public garage, fire
extinguishers approved by the Fire Chief.
(Prior Code, § 3-18B-5) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.065 PROHIBITED ACT; CHANGING VEHICLE IDENTIFICATION.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to change the identification marks on
the engine of any car or automobile in any public garage, and it shall be
unlawful to change the license tags on such cars, except pursuant to law.
(Prior Code, § 3-18B-6) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.066 INSPECTIONS.
   It shall be the duty of the Chief of Police and the Fire Chief to make or
cause to be made such inspections of public garages as may be necessary to
ensure compliance with the provisions of this code of ordinances. Any police
officer shall be permitted at any reasonable hour to view every car stored or
kept in any public garage as may be necessary to ensure compliance with the
provisions of this code of ordinances, and it shall be unlawful to hinder any
such inspection or to conceal any car or motor vehicle from such officer.
(Prior Code, § 3-18B-7) Penalty, see §
116.999
PARKING LOTS
§ 116.080 DEFINITION.
   The term PARKING LOT, as used in this subchapter, shall be construed to mean
and include any premises, enclosures or other places (other than a licensed
public garage) where four or more automobiles may be stored or parked and where
rent is paid or compensation is paid to the owner, manager or lessee of such
premises for the storing or parking of such vehicles.
(Prior Code, § 3-18C-1)
§ 116.081 LICENSE REQUIRED; FEE.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful to operate a parking lot without having first
obtained a license therefor.
   (B)   The annual fee for such license shall be as provided in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-18C-2) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.082 PROHIBITED ACTS.
   (A)   Parking or storing disabled vehicles. It shall be unlawful to park or
store in any parking lot any vehicle which is not in condition and ready for
use, or to permit the parking of any abandoned, junked or partially dismantled
vehicle in any such lot.
   (B)   Display of vehicles for sale; use of lot as an automobile repair shop.
It shall be unlawful to use any parking lot for storage or parking of any
vehicle for the purpose of displaying it for sale, or to use any parking lot or
portion thereof as an automobile repair shop.
(Prior Code, § 3-18C-3) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.083 ENTERING AND EXITING FROM LOTS.
   No person operating a parking lot shall invite or permit any person to drive
into such lot over any sidewalk, curb or parkway at any place other than a
permanent driveway, or in any way in violation of any provision of this code of
ordinances. Vehicles driving into or out of such parking lot shall be driven
with due respect to traffic conditions and in accordance with police
regulations.
(Prior Code, § 3-18C-4) Penalty, see §
116.999
TAXICABS; VEHICLES FOR HIRE
§ 116.095 DEFINITION.
   The term PUBLIC VEHICLE, when used in this subchapter, shall be construed to
include and to mean any taxicab, bus, automobile or other similar vehicle used
in the business of carrying persons for hire upon the public streets of the
village.
(Prior Code, § 3-18D-1)
§ 116.096 LICENSE REQUIRED; ISSUANCE.
   (A)   A license shall be required to operate taxicabs or other public
vehicles on the public streets, to occupy cabstands and to pick up and
discharge passengers with the village. It shall be unlawful to operate a public
vehicle as aforesaid without a license.
   (B)   The Village Clerk shall issue licenses to qualified applicants as
designated from time to time by resolution of the President and Board of
Trustees.
(Prior Code, § 3-18D-2) Penalty, see §
116.999

and drivers licensed by the village.

§ 116.099 NUMBER OF LICENSES ISSUED.

Licenses may be issued to one or more qualified taxicab companies approved by

(Prior Code, § 3-18D-5)
§ 116.100 CONDUCT OF BUSINESS.
   (A)   Generally. Licensees shall be entitled to occupy cab stands where
permitted within the village and to pick up and deliver passengers within the
village limits.
   (B)   Fare required. No public vehicle, whether licensed or not by the
village, shall carry passengers on the village streets without charging a fee
therefor.
   (C)   Soliciting trade. It shall be unlawful for the owner or driver of any
such vehicle to solicit by word, gesture or otherwise, the patronage of any
person at any railroad station or upon any public place in the village.
(Prior Code, § 3-18D-6) Penalty, see §
116.999
§ 116.101 OPERATION OF TAXICABS.
   Taxicab operating rules and regulations may be established by resolution of
the Board from time to time. Failure to comply with these rules and regulations
shall constitute just cause for license revocation.
(Prior Code, § 3-18D-7)
§ 116.102 REVOCATION OF LICENSE; APPEALS.
   Licenses may be revoked at any time by the President for failure to maintain
the standards as described in §
116.097 of this chapter or for any other cause. License revocations may be
appealed to the Board of Trustees in writing within ten days after receipt of
the revocation notice. After suitable inquiry, the Village Board may sustain or
reverse the revocation.
(Prior Code, § 3-18D-8)
§ 116.103 FOREIGN CAB COMPANIES.
   Foreign cab companies licensed in another municipality or meeting the
statutory requirements for public carriers shall be permitted to deliver
passengers picked up outside of the village to a destination in the village and
shall be permitted to pick up passengers who arrange for service within the
village limits for delivery to a location outside the village limits without a
license.
(Prior Code, § 3-18D-9)

operation primarily used to transfer trailers or containers for the shipping of

Prevention Codes. Additionally, the village may enter upon the premises to
verify compliance with all such codes and to ascertain the actual number of

   (A)   Stolen property prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any drayman,

   (B)   Vehicle identification. Every vehicle used for such business shall

(Prior Code, § 3-19-3) Penalty, see §

§ 116.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   (1)   The village’s Police Department is hereby authorized to
immediately impound any towing vehicle utilized for the removal and towing of a
motor vehicle or part thereof that was used in the towing of a motor vehicle
without first having obtained a duly and properly executed tow order as set
forth in §§
116.001 through
116.010 of this chapter. The fine and penalty for release of said impounded
towing vehicle shall be $500.
      (2)   A towing service, and any of its officer or employees, that removes
or tows a motor vehicle or any part thereof without having first obtained a
duly and properly signed towing order shall be guilty of a Class C misdemeanor
and shall be subject to:

imprisonment for a period up to six months;
         (b)   Imprisonment for a period up to, but not in excess of, six
months;
         (c)   Suspension of business license for a period up to one year; and/
or
         (d)   Revocation of business license.

CONTRACTORS
§ 117.001 DEFINITION.
   Any of the following shall be deemed a CONTRACTOR for the purpose of this
chapter and are defined as follows.
   BUILDING CONTRACTOR. Any person, firm or corporation who procures a building
permit, who may or may not perform any direct work, but who must sublet all of
the work to licensed specialty contractors and including anyone engaged in
rehabilitation of property (rehabers).
   CONTRACTOR. Also includes, but is not limited to, the specific occupations
listed in §
117.006(A) of this chapter.
   GENERAL CONTRACTOR. Any person, firm or corporation who has the entire or
major portion of a contract, and who employs the basic trades directly to
perform building work and sublets to licensed specialty contractors.
   SPECIALTY CONTRACTOR. Any person, firm or corporation whose operations are
the performance of building work requiring special skills and whose principal
contracting business involves the use of a specialized building trade or craft.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-1)
§ 117.002 APPLICATION OF PROVISIONS.
   This subchapter shall apply to all contractors doing business within the
village whether their place of business is located within or without the
corporate limits of the village.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-2)
§ 117.003 REGISTRATION AND LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall engage in the business of contractor for the erection,
construction, repair or alteration of any building or structure within the
village without first having registered with the Village Clerk, and it shall be
unlawful to engage in business in the village as a contractor without first
having obtained a license therefor, paying the applicable license fee and
filing the bond as hereinafter required.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-3) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 117.004 LICENSE APPLICATION.
   Each application shall state the name of the applicant, applicant’s address,
number of persons to be operating under such license, type of license requested
and a statement that the applicant agrees to comply with all provisions of this
village code.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-4)
§ 117.005 REGISTRATION FEE; PENALTY.
   (A)   The annual fee for registering as a contractor shall be established by
ordinance as set forth in the license fee schedule of §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-5)
   (B)   In addition to other authorized penalties, any contractor, as defined
in this subchapter, that fails to register as required prior to commencing work
within the village shall be liable for an additional registration fee penalty
in the amount of 50% of the registration fee otherwise payable.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-5-1)
(Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986; Ord. 88-104, passed 1-26-1988)
§ 117.006 BOND AND INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Bond.
      (1)   Every applicant for a certificate of registration and a license as
a contractor shall execute and file with the Village Clerk a bond with good and
sufficient sureties to be approved by the Village President in the following
penal sums hereinafter shown as applicable to said contractor specialty.
         (a)   Five thousand dollar bond.
            1.   Decorating;
            2.   Painting;
            3.   Fence;
            4.   Roofing insulation;
            5.   Tile, marble or mosaic;
            6.   Air conditioning;
            7.   Awning or storm windows;
            8.   Doors carpenter;
            9.   Cement and concrete;
            10.   Drywall;
            11.   Electrical;
            12.   Excavating;
            13.   Furnace installer, cleaner or repairer;
            14.   Gas main;
            15.   Landscaper;
            16.   Lathing;

            18.   Paving;
            19.   Plastering;
            20.   Sign painter;
            21.   Sheet metal, including signs;
            22.   Steel erector, including signs;
            23.   Tuckpointing, building cleaning;
            24.   Water;
            25.   General building contractor, including: carpentry, drywall
and floor tile and insulation;
            26.   Glass installer; and
            27.   Heating.
         (b)   Ten thousand dollar bond.
            1.   Catch basin cleaner;
            2.   Sewer plumber; and
            3.   Sign installer.
         (c)   Twenty thousand dollar bond. House wrecker.
      (2)   The bond shall be payable to the village for the use of any persons
with whom such applicant shall thereafter contract to do work to indemnify any
such persons for damages sustained on account of the failure of such contractor
to perform work so contracted for or on account of the failure of such
contractor to perform the work so contracted for in accordance with any of the
provisions of this code of ordinances or on account of the failure of such
contractor to perform the work so contracted for in a good and workmanlike
manner.
   (B)   Insurance.
      (1)   No contractor shall be licensed to engage in business as provided
for in this subchapter unless such contractor shall provide, in addition to all
other requirements imposed by this subchapter, a certificate of insurance
verifying the existence of a current public liability policy in the name of the
contractor.
      (2)   Said insurance policy shall include coverage for personal injury in
an amount not less than $100,000 and property damage in an amount not less than
$50,000. The contractor shall be required to furnish the village with a new
certificate upon expiration, lapse, cancellation or other change or
interruption in coverage and the Building Commissioner shall be empowered to
suspend the license of any contractor found to be in violation of this division
(B). Proof of current insurance may be demanded at any time of a contractor
engaged in business in the village by the Building Commissioner, the Building
Inspector or their lawful designees.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-6) (Ord. 85-104, passed 5-5-1985; Ord. 07-410, passed 8-6-
2007)
§ 117.007 DUTIES OF CONTRACTORS.
   It shall be the duty of all contractors licensed hereunder to comply with
all provisions of this code of ordinances relating to or regulating the
activities engaged in and, in addition thereto, to at least once a week remove
or cause to be removed from the site of contractors’ activities all trash,
refuse and waste materials. Contractors shall at all times keep the site of
activities in an orderly condition, free from standing water, unguarded,
dangerous implements and health and safety hazards, and contractors shall not
obstruct traffic on streets or sidewalks or permit dirt or waste materials to
fall or be carried onto such public ways.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-7) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 117.008 SUBCONTRACTORS.
   (A)   License required. Any person doing business as a subcontractor shall
be construed as engaged in the business of a contractor for which a license is
required by this subchapter.
   (B)   Bond requirements. The provisions relating to a bond to be filed by
each contractor shall not apply in the event the developer, general contractor
or building contractor shall elect to file a bond in the penal amount equal to
the sum of the contract price for the construction work agreed upon, which bond
shall cover the acts and work of each and every contractor or subcontractor
engaged in the construction work agreed upon, and which bond shall be payable
to the village for the use of any person or persons, with whom such developer,
general contractor or building contractor shall contract to do work, to
indemnify any such person or persons for damages sustained on account of the
failure of such developer, general contractor or building contractor or any
subcontractor employed thereon to perform work so contracted for, in accordance
with any of the provisions of this code of ordinances, or on account of the
failure of such developer, general contractor or builder, or any subcontractor
employed thereon, to perform the work so contracted for in a good and
workmanlike manner; provided, however, that, each contractor so engaged by said
developer, general contractor or building contractor must pay the registration
or license fee. Such bond filed by any contractor or developer shall be
conditioned to indemnify, keep and save harmless the village and its officers
and employees against any loss, cost, damage, judgment or liability of any kind
whatsoever which the village may suffer or be part to, or which may accrue
against, be charged to or be recovered from the village or any of its employees
or officials by reason of any act or thing done or neglected to be done under
or by virtue of the authority given in such license.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-8)
§ 117.009 INSPECTION.
   The provisions of this subchapter are declared to be of a regulatory nature
and it shall at all times be the duty of the Police Department, the Health
Department, the Fire Department and the Building Commissioner regularly to
inspect the site of contractors’ activities to see that the same are being
conducted and operated in accordance with the requirements of all provisions of
this code of ordinances relating thereto.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-9)
§ 117.010 COMPLIANCE WITH CODE PROVISIONS.
   It shall be the duty of all contractors to comply with all provisions of
this code of ordinances relating to the erection, construction, alteration,
installation, repair or maintenance of any building or structures, to the
construction of streets, sidewalks or pavements, and all provisions pertaining
to or regulating the activities engaged in.
(Prior Code, § 3-20-10) Penalty, see §
10.999
