CHAPTER 118: PEDDLERS, ITINERANT MERCHANTS AND SOLICITORS
Section
   
118.01   Definitions
   
118.02   License requirement
   
118.03   Application procedure
   
118.04   Standards for issuance
   
118.05   Revocation procedure
   
118.06   Standards for revocation
   
118.07   Appeal procedure
   
118.08   Exhibition of identification
   
118.09   Village policy on soliciting
   
118.10   Notice regulating soliciting
   
118.11   Duty of solicitors
   
118.12   Uninvited soliciting prohibited
   
118.13   Time limit on soliciting
 
   
118.99   Penalty
Statutory reference:
   Authority of village to license, tax, regulate or prohibit peddlers,
itinerant merchants or transient vendors, see 65 ILCS 5/11-42-5
§ 118.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   BUSINESS. The business carried on by any person who is an itinerant
merchant, peddler or solicitor as defined in this section.
   GOODS. Merchandise of any description whatsoever, and includes but is not
restricted to wares and foodstuffs.
   ITINERANT MERCHANT. Any person, whether as owner, agent or consignee, who
engages in a temporary business of selling goods within the village and who, in
the furtherance of that business, uses any building, structure, vehicle or any
place within the village.
   PEDDLER. Any person not an itinerant merchant who:
      (1)   Travels from place to place by any means carrying goods for sale or
making sales or making deliveries; or
      (2)   Without traveling from place to place, sells or offers goods for
sale from any public place within the village.
   SOLICITOR. Any person who travels by any means from place to place, taking
or attempting to take orders for sale of goods to be delivered in the future or
for services to be performed in the future. A person who is a SOLICITOR is not
a peddler.
§ 118.02 LICENSE REQUIREMENT.
   (A)   Any person who is an itinerant merchant, peddler or solicitor shall
obtain a license before engaging in this activity within the village.
   (B)   The fee for the license required by this chapter shall be as set from
time to time by the Board of Trustees and set forth by ordinance or resolution.
   (C)   No license issued under this chapter shall be transferable.
   (D)   All licenses issued under this chapter shall expire 90 days after the
date of issuance thereof.
Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.03 APPLICATION PROCEDURE.
   (A)   All applicants for licenses required by this chapter shall file an
application with the Clerk. This application shall be signed by the applicant
if an individual, or by all partners if a partnership, or by the president if a
corporation. The applicant may be requested to provide information concerning
the following items:
      (1)   The name and address of the applicant;
      (2)   (a)   The name of the individual having management authority or
supervision of the applicant’s business during the time that it is proposed to
be carried on in the village;
         (b)   The local address of the individual;
         (c)   The permanent address of the individual; and
         (d)   The capacity in which the individual will act.
      (3)   The name and address of the person, if any, for whose purpose the
business will be carried on, and if a corporation, the state of incorporation;
      (4)   The time period or periods during which it is proposed to carry on
the applicant’s business;
      (5)   (a)   The nature, character and quality of the goods or services to
be offered for sale or delivered;
         (b)   If goods, their invoice value and whether they are to be sold by
sample as well as from stock; and
         (c)   If goods, where and by whom the goods are manufactured or grown,
and where the goods are at the time of application.
      (6)   The nature of the advertising proposed to be done for the business;
and
      (7)   Whether or not the applicant, or the individual identified in
division (A)(2)(a) above, or the person identified in division (A)(3) above,
has been convicted of any crime or misdemeanor, and if so, the nature of each
offense and the penalty assessed for each offense.
   (B)   Applicants for peddler or solicitor licenses may be required to
provide further information concerning the following items in addition to that
requested under division (A) above:
      (1)   A description of the applicant; and
      (2)   A description of any vehicle proposed to be used in the business,
including its registration number, if any.
   (C)   All applicants for licenses required by this chapter shall attach to
their application, if required by the village, credentials from the person, if
any, for which the applicant proposes to do business, authorizing the applicant
to act as the representative.
   (D)   Applicants who propose to handle foodstuffs shall also attach to their
application, in addition to any attachments required under division (C) above,
a statement from a licensed physician, dated not more than ten days prior to
the date of application, certifying the applicant to be free of contagious or
communicable disease.
Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.04 STANDARDS FOR ISSUANCE.
   (A)   Upon receipt of an application, an investigation of the applicant’s
business reputation and moral character shall be made.
   (B)   The application shall be approved unless the investigation discloses
tangible evidence that the conduct of the applicant’s business would pose a
substantial threat to the public health, safety, morals or general welfare. In
particular, tangible evidence that the applicant has committed the following
will constitute valid reasons for disapproval of an application:
      (1)   Has been convicted of a crime of moral turpitude;
      (2)   Has made willful misstatements in the application;
      (3)   Has committed prior violations of ordinances pertaining to
itinerant merchants, peddlers, solicitors and the like;
      (4)   Has committed prior fraudulent acts; or
      (5)   Has a record of continual breaches of solicited contracts.
§ 118.05 REVOCATION PROCEDURE.
   Any license or permit granted under this chapter may be revoked by the Clerk
after notice and hearing pursuant to the standards in §
118.06. Notice of hearing for revocation shall be given in writing, setting
forth specifically the grounds of the complaint and the time and place of the
hearing. This notice shall be mailed to the licensee at his or her last known
address at least ten days prior to the date set for the hearing.
§ 118.06 STANDARDS FOR REVOCATION.
   A license granted under this chapter may be revoked for any of the following
reasons:
   (A)   Any fraud or misrepresentation contained in the license application;
   (B)   Any fraud, misrepresentation or false statement made in connection
with the business being conducted under the license;
   (C)   Any violation of this chapter;
   (D)   Conviction of the licensee of any felony, or conviction of the
licensee of any misdemeanor involving moral turpitude; or
   (E)   Conducting the business licensed in an unlawful manner or in such a
way as to constitute a menace to the health, safety, morals or general welfare
of the public.
§ 118.07 APPEAL PROCEDURE.
   (A)   (1)   (a)   Any person aggrieved by a decision under §§
118.04 or
118.06 shall have the right to appeal to the Board of Trustees.
         (b) The appeal shall be taken by filing with the Board of Trustees,
within 14 days after notice of the decision has been mailed to the person’s
last known address, a written statement setting forth the grounds for appeal.
      (2)   The Board of Trustees shall set the time and place for a hearing,
and notice for the hearing shall be given to the person in the same manner as
provided in §
118.05.
   (B)   The order of the Board of Trustees after the hearing shall be final.
§ 118.08 EXHIBITION OF IDENTIFICATION.
   (A)   Any license issued to an itinerant merchant under this chapter shall
be posted conspicuously in or at the place named therein. In the event more
than one place within the village shall be used to conduct the business
licensed, separate licenses shall be issued for each place.
   (B)   (1)   The Clerk shall issue a license to each peddler or solicitor
licensed under this chapter.
      (2)   The license shall contain the words “Licensed Peddler” or “Licensed
Solicitor”, the expiration date of the license and the number of the license.
      (3)   The license shall be kept with the licensee during the time that he
or she is engaged in the business licensed.
Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.09 VILLAGE POLICY ON SOLICITING.
   It is hereby declared to be the policy of the village that the occupants of
the residences in the village shall make the determination of whether
solicitors shall be, or shall not be, invited to their respective residences.
§ 118.10 NOTICE REGULATING SOLICITING.
   (A)   Notice of the refusal of invitation to solicitors to any residence
shall be given on a weatherproof card, approximately three inches by four
inches in size, exhibited upon or near the main entrance door to the residence,
indicating the determination by the occupant, containing the applicable words
as follows:
   “NO SOLICITORS INVITED”
   (B)   The letters shall be at least one-third inch in height. For the
purpose of uniformity, the cards shall be provided by the Chief of Police to
persons requesting, at the cost thereof.
   (C)   The card so exhibited shall constitute sufficient notice to any
solicitor of the determination by the occupant of the residence of the
information contained thereon.
§ 118.11 DUTY OF SOLICITORS.
   (A)   It shall be the duty of every solicitor upon going onto any premises
in the village upon which a residence is located to first examine the notice
provided for in §
118.10, if any is attached, and be governed by the statement contained on the
notice. If the notice states “NO SOLICITORS INVITED”, then the solicitor,
whether registered or not, shall immediately and peacefully depart from the
premises.
   (B)   Any solicitor who has gained entrance to any residence, whether
invited or not, shall immediately and peacefully depart from the premises when
requested to do so by the occupant.
Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.12 UNINVITED SOLICITING PROHIBITED.
   It is hereby declared to be unlawful and shall constitute a nuisance for any
person to go upon any premises and ring the doorbell upon or near any door, or
create any sound in any manner calculated to attract the attention of the
occupant of the residence, for the purpose of securing an audience with the
occupant thereof and engage in soliciting in defiance of the notice exhibited
at the residence in accordance with the provisions of §
118.10.
Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.13 TIME LIMIT ON SOLICITING.
   It is hereby declared to be unlawful and shall constitute a nuisance for any
person to go upon any premises and ring the doorbell upon or near any door of a
residence located thereon, or rap or knock upon any door, or create any sound
in any other manner calculated to attract the attention of the occupant of the
residence, for the purpose of securing an audience with the occupant thereof
and engage in soliciting prior to 9:00 a.m. or after 9:00 p.m. of any weekday
or Saturday, or at any time on a Sunday or on a state or national holiday.
Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any provision of this chapter shall be fined not more than
$750. Each day’s violation shall constitute a separate offense.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 119.001 ADVERTISEMENTS ON PUBLIC OR PRIVATE PROPERTY; CONSENT REQUIRED.
   (A)   Public property. No person shall place or cause to be placed any
advertisement on village property without the express consent of the corporate
authorities.
   (B)   Private property. No person shall place or cause to be placed any
advertisement on any private structure or building, unless he or she is the
owner thereof, without the consent in writing of the owner.
   (C)   Village property.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to affix
any handbill, sign, poster, advertisement or notice of any kind on any
telephone pole, electric pole, telegraph pole, light pole, utility pole,
traffic light pole, traffic sign pole or upon any village property, or upon
private property without consent of the owner.
      (2)   Nothing herein contained shall be deemed to prohibit the village
from posting notices.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-3) Penalty, see §
119.999
OUTDOOR ADVERTISERS AND BILLPOSTERS
§ 119.015 DEFINITIONS.
   (A)   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      ADVERTISER. Any person engaged in the business of placing, posting or
painting any advertisements, notices or displays in or on any place for the
purpose of outdoor advertising so that the resultant display is visible from
any public place.
      BILLBOARDS or SIGNBOARDS. All outdoor structures used for the public
display of advertising material; except that, such terms shall not include
signs erected or maintained on roofs, or signs attached to or painted upon the
walls of buildings.
      SIGN. Includes all advertising structures having a face similar to a
billboard or signboard, but which are erected and maintained on the roofs, or
attached to the walls of buildings.
   (B)   The terms “billboards”, “signboard” or “sign”, as herein used, shall
not be held to include any board, sign or surface used to display official
notices issued by any court or public office, or to include any board or sign
having an area of less than 25 square feet.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-1-1)
§ 119.016 LICENSES REQUIRED.
   (A)   Billposters and sign painters. No person shall do any billposting or
sign painting within the limits of the village without first having procured a
license for so doing.
   (B)   Outdoor advertisers. It is unlawful for any outdoor advertiser to do
business in the village without first having secured a license therefor as
required herein.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-1-2) Penalty, see §
119.999
§ 119.017 LICENSE APPLICATION; APPROVAL.
   (A)   Applications for licenses required in the preceding section shall be
accompanied by a list of all places on which it is intended to place signs or
advertisements.
   (B)   This list may be added to from time to time by the licensee, who shall
have the right to post or place advertisements or signs on additional places as
acquired; provided that, the Village Clerk is first notified of such place.
   (C)   No such license shall be issued and no location shall be approved,
except upon favorable action of the President and Board of Trustees.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-1-3)
§ 119.018 LICENSE FEES.
   (A)   Billposters and sign painters. The annual license fee for billposters
and sign painters shall be as provided in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Outdoor advertisers. The annual fee for the license required by §
119.016(B) of this chapter shall be as provided in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances. In addition to such license fee, there
shall be paid the fees required by §
151.192 of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-1-4)
§ 119.019 BOND REQUIREMENTS.
   Every person engaged in the business of constructing, erecting and
maintaining billboards, signboards or signs in the village shall file with the
Village Clerk a bond, with sureties to be approved by the Village President, in
the sum of $10,000, conditioned that such person shall faithfully comply with
the provisions of this subchapter and §§
151.190 through
151.199 of this code of ordinances with reference to the construction,
alteration, maintenance and safety of such billboards, signboards and signs,
and for payment of such fees as are provided to be paid, and further, to save
and keep harmless the village and its officials from all damages, liability,
losses or judgments which may be claimed or recovered by any person against the
village by reason of the erection, maintenance, removal or repair of any such
billboard, signboard or sign.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-1-5)
HANDBILL AND SAMPLES DISTRIBUTORS
§ 119.030 LICENSE APPLICATION; INVESTIGATION.
   (A)   Applications for such licenses shall contain a statement of the nature
of the article, cards or advertisement to be distributed, the name of the
applicant and the name of the manufacturer or distributor of such article or
service advertised.
   (B)   No such license shall be issued to any but a person of good character.
The Chief of Police shall make or cause to be made an investigation into the
character of each applicant and shall report the results thereof to the
President before any such license shall be issued.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-2-1)
§ 119.031 LICENSE FEE.
   The fee for such licenses shall be as provided in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-2-2)
§ 119.032 DISTRIBUTION TO THE PUBLIC PROHIBITED; EXCEPTIONS.
   It shall be unlawful to distribute or to cause to be distributed to the
public, any cards, circulars, handbills, samples of merchandise or medicinal
preparations, or any advertising matter whatsoever, on any public place in the
village, or by leaving the same at stores, offices, houses or residences in the
village, except as provided in the following exceptions or qualifications.
   (A)   Notices or programs of public meetings or public celebrations or other
matters pertaining to the public welfare of the village may be so distributed
upon application to and approval of the President and Board of Trustees.
   (B)   Circulars, programs or other advertising matter relating solely to
plays, festivals, celebrations or other forms of entertainment which the public
is invited to attend or participate, with or without admission charges, when
sponsored by or promoted for the benefit of organized groups of individuals,
associations, corporations or institutions of an education, fraternal,
charitable, philanthropic or religious character may be so distributed upon
application and approval of the President and Board of Trustees.
   (C)   Advertising matter of publications, but not including free samples of
merchandise, that is printed or published at more or less regular intervals,
and to be delivered without charge or subscription fee only to residences or
places of business where the owners or occupants thereof have previously signed
a standard form card requesting such delivery, may be so distributed only to
those requesting same upon application to and approval of the President and
Board of Trustees; provided that, such signed cards are to be presented for
inspection by any police office or official of the village on request at any
time during business hours.
   (D)   Cards, circulars, dodgers, letters or notices relating solely to the
qualifications, political platform or policies of candidates for public office,
or to the platform or policies of political parties, or to any propositions
submitted for public referendum, or specimen ballots, may be so distributed
without approval of the President and Board of Trustees.
   (E)   Articles or merchandise sold or delivered by licensed peddlers,
whether or not accompanied by advertising matter, may be so distributed under
the provisions of this subchapter.
   (F)   Publications containing advertising matter, when such publications are
delivered upon a paid subscription or to members of an organization by virtue
of their membership therein, such delivery to be by carrier, may be so
distributed without approval of the President and Board of Trustees.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-2-3)
§ 119.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Any person found guilty of violating any of the provisions of §
119.001 of this chapter shall be punished by a fine as set forth in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances. Each day any violation hereof shall continue
shall constitute a separate offense.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-3)
   (C)   Any person found guilty of violating any of the provisions of §§
119.015 through
119.019 of this chapter shall be punished by a fine as set forth in §
10.999 of this code of ordinances. Each day any violation of any provision of
§§
119.015 through
119.019 of this chapter shall continue shall constitute a separate offense.
(Prior Code, § 3-13-1-6)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 120.001 FOOD SALES RESTRICTED.
   No article of food or drink intended for human use or consumption, and no
articles of such food or drink, or article which may be used in the composition
or preparation of such food or drink which is not then healthy, fresh, sound
and wholesome, fit and safe for such use; and no animal or fish that died by
disease or accident, and no carcass of any calf, pig or lamb which at the time
of its death was less than four weeks old, and no meat therefrom, shall be
brought within the limits of the village and offered or held for sale as food
anywhere in said village.
(Prior Code, § 4-7-1) Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.002 GROCERY STORES AND MARKETS.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      EMPLOYEE. A person shall be considered an EMPLOYEE if he or she is
scheduled to work 20 or more hours per week and 20 or more weeks per year.
      GROCERY or MARKET. An established place of business offering for sale at
retail and for consumption off the premises any fruit, vegetables, ice cream,
milk and milk products, meat, poultry, fish, seafood or other food product
whether fresh, frozen or sold in cans, bottles, boxes, cartons or other
containers, but shall not include those establishments commonly known as
confectionery stores selling ice cream, drinks, candy or bakeries. In the event
the applicant shall qualify as a bakery or florist, an additional fee as set
forth in those provisions shall be paid and additional fees shall be paid for
cigarettes, vending machines and alcoholic liquor sales as set forth in those
provisions.
(Prior Code, § 4-7B-1)
   (B)   License required. No person shall operate a grocery or market within
the village without first having obtained a license to do so from the Village
Clerk. Application for such license shall be made pursuant to §
110.004 of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 4-7B-2)
   (C)   License fees. An annual license fee shall be paid by each applicant
based on the number of employees as provided in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 4-7B-3)
Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.003 BAKERIES.
   (A)   Definition. Any place or establishment used for any process of mixing,
compounding or baking for sale or the purpose of a restaurant, bakery or hotel,
any bread, biscuits, pretzels, crackers, buns, rolls, macaroni, cake, pies or
any food product of which flour or meal is the principal ingredient shall be
deemed a BAKERY for the purpose of this section; provided that, restaurants in
which any of the foregoing food products are mixed and baked, for consumption
in said restaurants only, shall not be considered to be bakeries.
(Prior Code, § 4-7C-1)
   (B)   License required; fee.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful to conduct or operate a bakery in the village
without having first obtained a license therefor.
      (2)   The annual license fee for such business shall be established by
ordinance as set forth in the license fee schedule in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 4-7C-2)
   (C)   Health and sanitation regulations.
      (1)   Generally. Every place used as a bakery shall be kept in a clean
and sanitary condition.
      (2)   Light and ventilation. All parts of the bakery shall be adequately
lighted at all times and shall be ventilated by means of windows or skylights
or airshafts or ducts or mechanical apparatus if necessary, to ensure a free
circulation of fresh air at all times. Such ventilation construction and
equipment shall be of such character that a complete change of air in all parts
of the bakery must be made at least four times each hour; provided, however,
that, it shall not be necessary to ventilate at such times or in such manner
that the process of mixing or raising dough shall of necessity be interfered
with or prevented.
      (3)   Floors. The floor of every place used as a bakery, if below street
level, shall be constructed of concrete, cement, asphalt or other impervious
material, or of tile laid on cement. Such floors may, if desired, be covered
with a hardwood floor having tight joints or may be of any impervious material
as above provided.
      (4)   Flies, rodents and vermin. Every place used as a bakery shall be
kept free from flies, rodents and vermin of all kinds.
      (5)   Sleeping facilities. No person shall sleep, and no sleeping
accommodations shall be maintained, in any bakery or in the rooms where flour
and meal used in connection therewith or the food products made therein are
handled or stored.
      (6)   Storage of materials. All rooms for the storage of flour or meal
for use in connection with any bakery shall be dry and well ventilated, and
every bakery and room used for storage of materials and food products in
connection therewith shall be so arranged that the shelves, cupboards, trays,
troughs, bins and cases can be easily removed and cleaned.
      (7)   Use of tobacco. The use of tobacco in any form in a bakery is
hereby prohibited. Notices to this effect shall be placed in a prominent place
in every bakery by the proprietor thereof; but the absence of such notice shall
not excuse any person for any violation of this provision.
      (8)   Wearing apparel. All workers and employees, while engaged in the
manufacturing or handling of bakery products in a bakery, shall provide
themselves with slippers or shoes and a suit of washable material which shall
be used for that purpose only. These garments shall be kept clean at all times.
(Prior Code, § 4-7C-3)
   (D)   Inspections. It shall be the duty of the President to make, or cause
to be made, such inspections as may be necessary to see to it that the
provisions of this section are fully complied with.
(Prior Code, § 4-7C-4)
Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.004 ICE CREAM, CONFECTIONS AND BEVERAGES.
   (A)   License required. It shall be unlawful to engage in the business of
the manufacture or wholesale distribution of candy, ice cream, non-alcoholic
carbonated beverages or other confections other than bakery goods without first
having obtained a license therefor as is herein provided.
(Prior Code, § 4-7D-1)
   (B)   License fee. The annual license fee for such business shall be
established by ordinance as set forth in the license fee schedule in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 4-7D-2)
   (C)   Sanitary conditions.
      (1)   Premises. All premises used for such manufacture shall be kept in a
clean and sanitary condition.
      (2)   Employees.
         (a)   All employees therein shall keep themselves clean both as to
person and clothing where their duties bring them in contact with food and
materials used in the manufacture of the confection.
         (b)   It shall be unlawful to employ anyone in any such establishment
afflicted with a contagious or venereal disease.
(Prior Code, § 4-7D-3)
   (D)   Wholesomeness of materials.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful to use in such business any material which, as
a part of the product, may be harmful to health, or any material which is
adulterated in violation of state or federal statutes.
      (2)   All milk used in the manufacture of ice cream shall be of a
standard which may be sold at retail under the provisions of this code of
ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 4-7D-4)
   (E)   Inspections. The President shall cause to be made such inspections as
may be necessary under the provisions of this section for its enforcement.
(Prior Code, § 4-7D-5)
(Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986) Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.005 FOOD VENDING MACHINES.
   (A)   License required. It shall be unlawful for any coin-controlled or
coin-operated machine, commonly known as a vending machine, for the sale or
dispensing of merchandise of any kind, including, but not limited to food,
candy, nuts, gum and non-alcoholic beverages, to be installed on any premises
without first having obtained a license.
(Prior Code, § 4-7E-1)
   (B)   Application for license. Any person desiring a license for any coin-
controlled or coin-operated vending machine shall set forth the name of the
applicant, the address at which he or she conducts business, the address of the
place where such machines are located, the number of such vending machines and
the coin denomination required for each such machine.
(Prior Code, § 4-7E-2)
   (C)   License fee. The annual license fee for such business and each machine
shall be established by ordinance as set forth in §
110.018(A) of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 4-7E-3)
   (D)   Sanitary conditions; wholesomeness of merchandise.
      (1)   All food vending machines shall be kept and maintained in a clean
and sanitary condition, and the food and beverages sold and dispensed therefrom
shall be pure and wholesome.
      (2)   The operation of any machine found to be in an unsanitary condition
or containing impure or unwholesome food or beverages shall be stopped until
said machine has been cleaned or the impure or unwholesome food or beverages
removed and replaced with pure and wholesome food or beverages.
(Prior Code, § 4-7E-4)
   (E)   Inspections and analyses. The President shall be authorized and
empowered to make or cause to be made inspections from time to time of said
machines to determine whether said machines are in a sanitary condition and
whether the merchandise thereby offered for sale is pure and wholesome. Any
licensee hereunder shall, upon demand of the President, furnish him or her for
his or her inspection samples of any such food sold through said machines. A
record of the analysis of the contents of such machine or machines shall be
kept in the office of the President. If any analysis shows that any licensee is
selling or offering for sale food which is impure or unwholesome, or that said
machines are kept in an unsanitary condition, the President, after affording
such licensee an opportunity to be heard with respect to the findings and
analyses of the President may, if the facts warrant, revoke the license of such
person.
(Prior Code, § 4-7E-5)
   (F)   Revocation of license. Any license granted under the terms of this
section may be revoked by the President by notice in writing to the licensee
whenever it shall appear to his or her satisfaction that the person so licensed
shall have violated any of the provisions of this section.
(Prior Code, § 4-7E-6)
(Ord. passed 5-1-1973; Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986) Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.006 FOOD DELIVERY VEHICLES.
   (A)   License required; compliance with provisions. It shall be unlawful to
use or permit the use of any vehicle, including vehicles propelled by human
power, for the storage or carrying of any food or beverage or any other
provisions intended for human consumption, for the purpose of delivering any
such food or beverage for the use and consumption or for resale unless a
license for such vehicles is first secured and the provisions of this section
fully complied with.
(Prior Code, § 4-7F-1)
   (B)   Application for license; fees.
      (1)   Applications for such licenses shall recite the name and address of
the owner of the vehicle, the name or names of the persons for whom such
deliveries are made and the nature of the goods carried.
      (2)   The annual fee for a non-motorized vehicle and the annual fee for a
motorized vehicle shall be as provided in §
110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 4-7F-2)
   (C)   Sanitary conditions.
      (1)   All such vehicles shall be kept in a clean and sanitary condition
and shall be thoroughly cleaned each day they are so used. It shall be unlawful
to permit stale food, decaying matter or any other waste or material to
accumulate in or on any such vehicle while it is so used.
      (2)   If unwrapped food and beverages are transported in any vehicle,
such goods shall be carried in a portion or compartment of the vehicle which is
screened and protected against dust and insects.
(Prior Code, § 4-7F-3)
Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.007 ICE DEALERS.
   (A)   License required. It shall be unlawful to engage in the business of

(Prior Code, § 4-8-1)
   (B)   Application for license. Application for such license shall contain

(Prior Code, § 4-8-2)
   (C)   License fees. The annual fee for such ice dealer’s license shall be as

110.018(B) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 4-8-3)
   (D)   Ice standards. All ice sold or offered for sale shall be free from

(Prior Code, § 4-8-4)
Penalty, see §

FISH AND SHELLFISH
§ 120.020 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   COVERED COMMODITY.
      (1)   In general:
         (a)   Farm-raised fish; and
         (b)   Wild fish.
      (2)   The term COVERED COMMODITY does not include an item described in
division (1) above if the item is an ingredient in a processed food item.
   FARM-RAISED FISH. Includes:
      (1)   Farm-raised shellfish; and
      (2)   Fillets, steaks, nuggets and any other flesh from a farm-raised
fish or shellfish.
   FOOD SERVICE ESTABLISHMENTS.
      (1)   Restaurants, food stands, taverns, saloons, bars, lounge or other
similarly facility operated as an enterprise engaged in the business of selling
food to the public including salad bars and delicatessens and other food
enterprises located within retail establishments that provide ready-to-eat
foods.
      (2)   This subchapter shall not apply to schools or school breakfast and
lunch programs.
   WILD FISH. Naturally-born or hatchery-raised fish and shellfish harvested in
the wild; inclusions include a fillet, steak, nugget and any other flesh from
wild or shellfish; excluding net-pen aquacultural or other farm-raised fish.
(Ord. 07-425, passed 11-19-2007)
§ 120.021 NOTICE OF COUNTRY OF ORIGIN.
   (A)   Notice requirement. Except as provided in division (B) below, a
retailer of a covered commodity shall inform consumers, at the final point-of-
sale of the covered commodity to consumers, of the country of origin of the
covered commodity.
   (B)   United States country of origin. A retailer of a covered commodity may
designate the covered commodity as having a United States country of origin
only if, in the case of wild fish:
      (1)   It is harvested in waters of the United States, a territory of the
United States or a state; and
      (2)   It is processed in the United States, a territory of the United
States or a state, including waters thereof.
   (C)   Wild fish and farm-raised fish. The notice of country of origin for
wild fish and farm-raised fish shall distinguish between wild fish and farm-
raised fish.
(Ord. 07-425, passed 11-19-2007)
§ 120.022 INCLUSION OF FOOD SERVICE ESTABLISHMENTS.
   This subchapter shall apply to all fish and shellfish:
   (A)   Prepared or served in a food service establishment;
   (B)   Offered for sale or sold at the food service establishment in normal
retail quantities; or
   (C)   Served to consumers at the food service establishment.
(Ord. 07-425, passed 11-19-2007)
§ 120.023 METHOD OF NOTIFICATION.
   The information required by §
120.021 of this chapter, notice of country of origin, may be provided to
consumers, in a clear and visible manner, by a means of a inclusion of said
information on the paper or Markey menu, or by posting of a sign in a clear and
visible place and manner upon entry to the establishment, serving area or
tables and/or such other method that the village’s Health Inspector deems
reasonable and appropriate. If the fish or shellfish is already individually
labeled for retail sale regarding country of origin, that the fish or shellfish
is being sold or served with said label affixed, then the retailer shall not be
required to provide any additional information to comply with this section.
(Ord. 07-425, passed 11-19-2007)
§ 120.024 AUDIT VERIFICATION SYSTEM.
   (A)   The Health Inspector may require that any person that prepares,
stores, handles or distributes a covered commodity for retail sale maintain a
verifiable recordkeeping audit trail that will permit the Health Inspector to
verify compliance with the provisions of this subchapter. The Health Inspector
shall develop and publish rules and regulations regarding the nature and
content of records to be kept for audit purposes.
   (B)   Any person engaged in the business of supplying fish or shellfish to a
retailer shall provide information to the retailer indicating the country of
origin of the fish and/or shellfish.
(Ord. 07-425, passed 11-19-2007) Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.025 ENFORCEMENT.
   If the village’s Health Inspector determines that a retailer is in violation
of this subchapter, the Health Inspector shall:
   (A)   Notify the retailer of the determination by the Health Inspector; and
   (B)   Provide the retailer a 30-day period, beginning on the date on which
the retailer receives the notice under division (A) above from the Health
Inspector, during which the retailer may take necessary steps to comply with

RESTAURANTS
§ 120.040 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   APPROVED. Approved by the Hearth Inspector.
   BACTERICIDAL TREATMENT. The application of any method or substance for the
destruction of pathogens and all other organisms, so far as practicable, and
which, in the opinion of the Health Inspector, is effective and does not
adversely affect the food, drink or equipment with which it comes in contact,
or the health of the consumer of such food or drink.
   DRIVE-IN RESTAURANT. Any establishment where food and beverage is sold to
the consumer, and where motor vehicle parking space is provided, and where such
food and beverage is intended to be consumed in the motor vehicle upon the
premises or anywhere on the premises outside the building.
   EMPLOYEE. Any person working in a restaurant establishment, including the
proprietor, who handles food or drink during the preparation of serving, or who
comes in contact with any eating or cooking utensils, or who is employed in a
room in which food or drink is prepared or served.
   HEALTH INSPECTOR. The person so appointed by the Village President, with the
advice and consent of the Village Board; his or her compensation to be set by
ordinance.
   ITINERANT RESTAURANT. One operating for a temporary period in connection
with a fair, carnival, circus, public exhibition or other similar gathering.
   RESTAURANT. Any place that keeps for sale, sells and serves to the general
public, for consumption on the premises, any article of food or drink for human
consumption. Restaurants, ordinaries, coffee houses, ice cream parlors,
lunchrooms, tea rooms, lunch stand, box lunch deliveries, luncheonettes,
caféterias, taverns and retail liquor stores and drugstores serving sandwiches
or lunches and drinks, caterers and industrial food servers dispensing food or
drink to office personnel or employees of an industrial plant and any other
eating or drinking establishment, organization, club or guest house, whether
public or private, which sells or offers for sale food to the public, guests,
employees or patrons shall be included under the term RESTAURANT.
   SERVICE ACCOMMODATION. In the case of a restaurant is a seating place where
one patron or customer to be served can be seated and, in the case of a drive-
in restaurant, is a place provided on the premises for the parking of a
patron’s or customer’s motor vehicle.
   TAKE OUT RESTAURANT. Any establishment where food and beverage is prepared
for sale elsewhere or for consumption off the premises and shall include
catering functions.
   UTENSILS. Includes any kitchenware, tableware, glassware, cutlery, utensils,
containers or other equipment with which food or drink comes in contact during
storage, preparation or serving.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-1)
§ 120.041 LICENSES REQUIRED; COMPLIANCE WITH PROVISIONS.
   (A)   Restaurants and drive-ins. It shall be unlawful for any person to
operate a restaurant or drive-in, as defined herein, in the village without a
valid license.
   (B)   Itinerant restaurants. Any person conducting an itinerant restaurant
shall be required to secure a license. Only persons who comply with the
requirements of this subchapter shall be entitled to receive and retain such a
license.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-2) Penalty, see §

general requirements relating to applications for licenses. Such application
shall contain such further information as may be required by the Health
Inspector in order to inform him or her fully as to the size and nature of the
place to be used for the purposes of the business and the conditions, equipment
and facilities for conducting the business therein, the health of persons to be
employed, and the regulations and facilities provided for them.

§ 120.044 INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   (1)   Before any license shall be issued, the Health Inspector shall
cause an inspection to be made of the premises to be occupied by the applicant
as a restaurant, the equipment contained therein, the persons to be employed
therein, the sanitary and hygienic features and conditions and all other
matters relating to the business which he or she considers necessary or proper
to inquire into from the standpoint of health and sanitation.
      (2)   Before any such license shall be issued for a restaurant
establishment having service accommodations in excess of 15, the Building
Commissioner of the village shall cause an inspection to be made of the
premises to see that all building provisions of the village are complied with.
   (B)   (1)   At least once every four months, the Health Inspector shall
inspect every restaurant located within the village. In case the Health
Inspector discovers the violation of any item of sanitation, he or she shall
make a second inspection after the lapse of such time as he or she deems
necessary for the defect to be remedied, and the second inspection shall be
used in determining compliance with the requirements of this subchapter. Any
violation of the same item of this subchapter on such second inspection shall
call for the immediate suspension of the permit.
      (2)   (a)   One copy of the inspection report shall be posted by the
Health Inspector upon an inside wall of the restaurant and the inspection
report shall not be defaced or removed by any person, except the Health
Inspector.
         (b)   Another copy of the inspection report shall be filed with the
records of the Health Department.
      (3)   The person operating the restaurant, upon request of the Health
Inspector, shall permit access to all parts of the establishment and shall
permit the copying of any or all records of food purchased.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-5)
§ 120.045 LICENSE ISSUANCE; TERM; NON-TRANSFERABILITY; LICENSE TO BE POSTED.
   (A)   The license shall be issued annually for the fiscal year to the person
named in the application and for the premises stated in the application and
shall state the type of restaurant for which it is issued.
   (B)   Said license shall not be transferable and shall be posted in a
conspicuous place to the patrons.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-6)
§ 120.046 HOURS OF OPERATION.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful to keep open any premises licensed in this
subchapter or to sell or give away upon the premises any food or drink for
human consumption between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m.
   (B)   In the event that the operator of any premises shall furnish proof of
convenience and necessity requiring such premises to service public needs
during the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m., such operator may, on application,
be allowed a special license for such purpose; provided, however, that, no such
license shall be issued, except upon approval by the President and Board of
Trustees.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-7) Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.047 GRADE A RESTAURANT STANDARDS.
   (A)   No restaurant shall be operated within the village or its police
jurisdiction unless it conforms with the Grade A or approved itinerant
restaurant requirements as determined by the Health Inspector.
   (B)   Grade A restaurants shall comply with all of the following items of
sanitation and disease control.
      (1)   Sanitary conditions.
         (a)   Premises.
            1.   All restaurants shall be kept in a clean and wholesome
condition, dry and adequately ventilated so as to ensure a free circulation of
fresh air at all times.
            2.   Such places shall be kept free from rats, mice, flies and
other insects and vermin.
            3.   No domestic animal shall be permitted in any such place where
flour or meal or other foodstuffs are kept or prepared.
            4.   The premises of all food establishments shall be kept clean
and free of litter or rubbish.
            5.   Adequate lockers or dressing room shall be provided outside of
the kitchen or other food-processing rooms for employee’s clothing. Soiled
linens, coats and aprons shall be kept in containers provided for this purpose
in the lockers or dressing room.
            6.   None of the operations connected with a restaurant shall be
conducted in any room used as living or sleeping quarters.
         (b)   Employees.
            1.   All employees shall be clean in person, and no individual
having an infectious disease in a communicable form or who is a carrier of
infectious disease or who has diarrhea, sore throat or a discharging or
apparently infected wound shall be employed in, or remain in a restaurant
establishment in any capacity which will require him or her to handle food or
handle dishes or other receptacles in which food is sold or served.
            2.   Employees preparing and handling foods shall be required to
wear clean outer garments and use hairnets, headbands or caps. Employees shall
not expectorate or use tobacco in any form in any room in which food is
prepared or served. The hands of all persons shall be kept clean while such
persons are engaged in the handling of food, drink, utensils or equipment;
provided, however, that, an employee who does not prepare or serve food shall
not be required to wear a cap or other hair confiner.
      (2)   Floors. The floors of all rooms in which food or drink is stored or
prepared, or in which utensils are washed, shall be smooth and have such
construction as to be easily cleaned, and shall be kept clean and in good
repair. If floor drains are used, the floor shall be graded to the drain and
such drain shall be provided with proper traps so constructed as to minimize
clogging. All floors shall be kept free and clean from litter. Dustless methods
of floor cleaning shall be used, or dust-arresting sweeping compounds and
pushbrooms shall be employed; and all except emergency floor cleaning shall be
done during those periods when the least amount of food and drink is exposed.
      (3)   Walls and ceilings. Walls and ceilings of all rooms in which food
or drink is prepared or stored shall be painted or finished in light color, and
shall be refinished as often as necessary in a manner approved by the Health
Inspector. Nothing in this division (B)(3) shall prohibit the use of tiled or
varnished wood walls. The walls of all kitchens, sculleries and other rooms
where food is stored, prepared or mixed shall have a smooth, washable surface
up to the level reached by splash or spray from cooking, dishwashing or other
equipment used in the operation of such establishments. Walls shall have a cove
base at the floor.
      (4)   Screened doors and windows. When flies and other insects are
prevalent, all openings to the outer air shall be effectively screened with not
less than 16-mesh wire or plastic cloth. All doors shall be self-closing and
screen doors to the outer air shall open outward or fans of sufficient power to
prevent the entrance of flies and other flying insects shall be in use at all
otherwise ineffectively protected openings. Windows and door screens shall be
tight-fitting and free of holes; this shall include screens for skylights and
transoms.
      (5)   Lighting. Artificial light sources shall be provided which furnish
20 foot-candles on all working surfaces in the room in which food or drink is
prepared or in which utensils are washed, as measured by a suitable light
meter, and shall be in use, except when equivalent natural light is present.
This intensity of light does not apply to the dining room. Storage rooms shall
be considered to be sufficiently well lighted if approximately four foot-
candles are provided at a distance of 30 inches from the floor.
      (6)   Ventilation. All rooms in which food or drink is stored, prepared
or served, or in which utensils are washed, shall be adequately ventilated so
as to be reasonably free of disagreeable odors and condensation. Ventilation
equipment supplementary to windows and doors, such as adequate exhaust fans or
stove hoods, shall be provided if necessary. This requirement shall not apply
to cold storage rooms.
      (7)   Toilet and lavatory facilities. Adequate and convenient washing and
toilet facilities shall be provided for employees and customers in all
restaurant establishments, and the location of the same with reference to their
proximity to the place where the business of the establishment is carried on,
and to the place where foods are kept, stored or served shall be subject to the
approval of the Health Inspector.
         (a)   1.   In all such places where foods are dispensed for
consumption on the premises, such facilities shall include hot, running water
and a sign shall be placed by the licensee in compartments containing any
urinal or water closet directing employees to wash their hands before returning
to work after visiting such compartments or using such toilet facilities. Such
sign shall be of a permanent nature, printed, engraved or stamped on
waterproof, non-fragile material, and shall be printed in letters not less than
one inch in height. A sign shall be posted in each water closet compartment,
kitchen or employee’s locker room reading as follows:
 
No person who is affected with any disease in a communicable form or is a
carrier of such disease, or who has a gastrointestinal disturbance, sore throat
or a discharging or infected wound, sore or lesion shall handle food, drink,
utensils or equipment.
 
            2.   Toilet rooms shall be so lighted as to yield at least ten
foot-candles of tight by standard illuminometer test at a height 30 inches
above the floor.
         (b)   In establishments which may be hereafter constructed where food
or drink is served, there shall be an intervening room or vestibule between any
toilet room and any room in which food or drink is prepared, served or stored,
or where any food utensils are handled or stored. This intervening room or
vestibule shall be equipped with tight-fitting, self-closing doors, and shall
be of such dimensions as to prevent both doors being opened simultaneously by
the same person. Toilet room doors shall be equipped with self-closing devices.
         (c)   Toilet rooms and fixtures shall be kept clean and in good repair
and free from flies.
         (d)   Adequate and convenient hand-washing facilities shall be
provided and shall be kept clean. Hot and cold running water and individual
approved sanitary towels or efficiently operated blower shall be provided. The
use of a common towel is prohibited. No employee shall resume work after using
a toilet room without first washing his or her hands. Sinks used for the
washing of dishes or equipment shall not be used for hand-washing. Soap shall
be provided at all hand-washing sinks.
      (8)   Kitchen. The kitchen in all restaurant establishments shall have
adequate light and ventilation and the air flow shall always be from the dining
room through the kitchen. The discharge from kitchen fans shall always be
through a duct to a point above the roof line to protect the occupants of the
building in which the establishment is located or of adjoining buildings from
nuisance. Ranges, refrigerators and other bulky equipment shall be so arranged
as not to obstruct the light and ventilation, and tables for clean and dirty
dishes and food shall be so arranged that the dirty dishes will be as far
removed from the food rack and clean dishes as may be possible. Ranges shall be
hooded so that the cooking odors may be effectively carried off by a stack, an
exhaust fan or a skylight immediately above. The walls and ceilings shall be in
good repair and easily cleaned and the floors and walls should be proofed
against rats and vermin. Ranges, steam tables, shelves, racks, blocks, tables
or other machinery or furniture used in mixing, cutting, grinding, cooking or
otherwise preparing the foods for service shall be of such material and
construction that they may be kept scrupulously clean at all times.
      (9)   Utensils and equipment.
         (a)   Construction.
            1.   All multi-use utensils, all show and display cases or windows,
counters, shelves, tables, refrigerating equipment, sink and other equipment
used in connection with the operation of such establishment shall be so
constructed and located as to be easily cleaned and shall be kept in good
repair. Utensils made of or plated with cadmium or lead shall not be used,
however, solder containing lead may be used for jointing.
            2.   All surfaces of utensils coming in contact with food or drink
shall be of smooth construction, shall be made of not readily corrodible
material and shall be free of breaks, corrosion, open seams, cracks or chipped
surfaces. This requirement precludes the use of any type of equipment so
designed as to permit food or drink to come in contact with V-type threaded
surfaces. The point between the moving and stationary surfaces of food
equipment shall be close fitting. All surfaces of equipment and utensils with
which food or drink comes in contact shall be easily accessible for cleaning.
Tanks, kettles, large containers and other equipment used for the storage or
preparation of liquid or semi-liquid food shall be self-draining. All piping
used for the conveyance of food shall be so constructed as to be easily
dismounted for cleaning, and all surfaces of equipment used for the
preparation, storage or conservation of food and drink shall be accessible to
sight or touch for the purpose of cleaning. No new mechanical equipment
designed to meet the requirements of this subchapter or equipment having valves
or pipes shall be installed unless the same or complete drawings thereof shall
have been submitted to the Health Inspector for approval prior to installation.
         (b)   Cleaning and bactericidal treatment.
            1.   All equipment including display cases, counters, shelves,
tables, meat blocks, refrigerators, stoves and hoods shall be kept clean and
free from dust, dirt, insects and other contaminating material.
            2.   All tablecloths, napkins and cloths used by waiters, chefs and
other employees shall be clean.
            3.   Single-service articles such as paper cups, plates, straws and
milk bottle caps shall be used once only.
            4.   All multi-service eating and drinking utensils shall be
thoroughly cleaned after each usage, and all multi-use utensils used in the
preparation or serving of food and drink shall be thoroughly cleaned
immediately following the day’s operation in such manner as to be clean to the
sight and touch. A suitable detergent shall be used. The cleaning shall be
accomplished by the use of warm water, 110°F to 120°F, containing an adequate
amount of an effective soap or detergent to remove grease and solids. The soapy
wash water shall be changed at sufficiently frequent intervals to keep it
reasonably clean. In machine washing, dishes should be stacked in the racks or
trays so as to avoid overcrowding and so as to permit the wash and rinse waters
to reach all surfaces of each article.
            5.   After cleaning, all utensils shall be effectively subjected to
one or more of the following or other equivalent bactericidal processes:
               a.   i.   Immersion for at least two minutes in clean, hot water
at a temperature of at least 170°F or for one-half minute in boiling water.
Unless actually boiling water is used, a thermometer shall be available
convenient to the vat. The pouring of scalding water over washed utensils shall
not be accepted as satisfactory compliance.
                  ii.   Wherever practicable, bactericidal treatment shall be
obtained through the use of hot water in the manner above described. For this
method of bactericidal treatment, two adjacent deep sinks shall be provided and
fitted with a porcelain, metal or other impervious drainboard. After washing in
the first sink, the glasses, dishes and the like should be placed in metal
baskets and immersed in the hot water in the second sink for the required
period of time. Baskets may be lined with wooden strips to prevent marking of
the chinaware. Upon removal from the hot water, they should remain in the
baskets until dry and then be stored in such manner as not to become
contaminated before again being used.
                  iii.   Where hot water is used for bactericidal treatment,
there shall be provided a hot water heater (preferably controlled by a
thermostat) capable of maintaining a water temperature of at least 170°F in the
vat at all times during work hours, and water at such temperature shall be
available at all times while utensils are being washed and given bactericidal
treatment. The heating device may be integral with the immersion vat. Provision
should be made for compensating for heat loss to the utensils, especially when
large numbers are submerged at any time.
                  iv.   Equipment that is too large to immerse may be treated:
                     (A)   With live steam from a hose, in the case of
equipment in which steam can be confined;
                     (B)   By boiling water rinse; or
                     (C)   By spraying or swabbing with chlorine solution of at
least 50 parts per 1,000,000 strength.
               b.   i.   Immersion for at least two minutes in a lukewarm
chlorine bath containing at least 50 parts per 1,000,000 of available chlorine.
The bath should be made up at a strength of 100 parts per 1,000,000 or more and
shall not be used after its strength has been reduced to 50 parts per
1,000,000.
                  ii.   A test kit or test papers for checking concentration of
the chlorine solution shall be provided for use of the employees.
                  iii.   Where chlorine or other chemical treatment is used, a
three-compartment vat shall be required, the first compartment to be used for
washing, the second for plain rinsing and the third for chlorine or other
chemical immersion; provided that, for existing installations, the second or
rinsing compartment may be omitted if a satisfactory rinsing or spraying device
is substituted. The first basket of utensils will remain in the chlorine bath
for at least two minutes while the second basket is in the plain rinse and the
third basket is being washed. Upon removal from the chlorine bath, the utensils
may be rinsed in safe running water if desired and allowed to dry either in the
basket or inverted on a drain shelf or tray.
                  iv.   Silver and silver-plated tableware should not be
treated with chlorine for silver chlorides are formed which blacken the silver.
               c.   Other chemical bactericides shall be applied in a manner
similar to that of chlorine in division (B)(9)(b)5.b.ii. above.
            6.   a.   In dishwashing machines the washing period shall be at
least 40 seconds with the wash water temperature 120°F to 140°F and the rinse
period shall be at least 20 seconds with the rinse water temperature at 170°F
or higher.
               b.   Dishwashing machines must be kept clean. The pumps and the
wash and rinse sprays or jets, if any, should be so designed that a forceful
stream of water will reach all of the utensils when they are properly racked.
Periodic inspection and cleaning of wash and rinse sprays are essential to
continue satisfactory operation, and these parts of the machine should
therefore be readily accessible for inspection and cleaning. The wash tank
water should be changed during operation as often as is found necessary to keep
it reasonably clean. An effective concentration of detergent should be
maintained at all times.
               c.   New dishwashing machines should be provided with properly
operating automatic detergent dispensers, thermostat control of the temperature
of the wash water as well as that of the rinse water, and thermometers in both
the wash and rinse water lines and in such a location as to be readily visible.
Adequate hot water heating and storage facilities are essential. These
specifications are not intended to be mandatory, but to serve as a guide.
            7.   Drying cloths, if used, shall be clean and shall be used for
no other purpose. It is recommended that whenever possible utensils be
permitted to drain dry without the use of drying cloths.
            8.   No article, polish or other substance containing any cyanide
preparation or other poisonous material shall be used for the cleaning or
polishing of utensils.
         (c)   Storage and handling.
            1.   All containers and utensils shall be stored above the floor in
a clean, dry place protected from flies, splash, dust, overhead leakage,
condensation and other contamination. Wherever practicable, containers and
utensils shall be covered or inverted.
            2.   Drain racks, trays and shelves shall be made of not readily
corrodible material and shall be kept clean.
            3.   Containers and utensils shall not be handled by the surfaces
which come in contact with food or drink. Fingers should not touch the inside
surfaces of glasses, cups, dishes and the like, nor the bowls of spoons, the
tines of forks or the blades of knives.
            4.   Paper cups, plates, straws, spoons, forks and other single-
service containers and utensils shall be purchased in sanitary cartons and
stored therein in a clean, dry place until used, and after removal from the
cartons, these articles shall be handled in a sanitary manner. Laundered cloths
and napkins shall be stored in a clean place until used.
            5.   Spoons, spatulas, dippers, scoops and the like used for
dispensing frozen desserts shall be, when not in use, kept either in water
maintained at 170°F or in safe, running water.
      (10)   Water supply. Continuous, running hot and cold water under
pressure shall be easily accessible to all rooms in which food is prepared or
utensils are washed, and the water supply shall be of a safe, sanitary quality
and ample in quantity for all cleaning purposes.
      (11)   Waste disposal.
         (a)   Every person owning or controlling any restaurant establishment
shall cause all offal, table refuse, shells and animal or vegetable matter,
commonly known and described as garbage to be placed in proper metallic cans
which shall be practically air- and water-tight and easily washable and which
should be covered with close-fitting lids at all times, except when opened for
deposit or removal of garbage, and shall cause all such substances deposited in
such cans or receptacles to be removed daily from his or her premises and to be
disposed of either by burning in a properly constructed crematory which shall
have been approved by the Health Inspector or by dumping the same at any
dumping ground or place where garbage is dumped or disposed of by the village.
The removal and disposition of such substances shall be done by such person at
his or her own expense solely and in accordance with the provisions of village
ordinances and the directions or rules of the Health Inspector relating to the
disposition and removal of such substances.
         (b)   All garbage receptacles shall be washed when empty and if
necessary, treated with a disinfectant.
      (12)   Refrigeration.
         (a)   All readily perishable food or drink shall be kept at or below
50°F, except when being prepared or served. This shall include all custard-
filled and cream-filled pastries, milk and milk products, egg products, meat,
fish, shellfish, gravy, poultry stuffing, sauces, dressings and salads
containing meat, fish, eggs or milk or milk products. Raw meats should be
stored at or below 40°F.
         (b)   All ice shall be of safe, sanitary quality and stored and
handled in such a manner as to prevent contamination. Water used to wash ice
shall comply with the safety standards hereof.
         (c)   To prevent contamination of the refrigerator contents by
possible sewage backflow, all wastewater from refrigeration equipment shall
drain into an open sink or drain, properly trapped and sewer connected;
provided that, where sewer connections are not available, clean, adequate,
water-tight drip pans may be used, or the drainage disposed of in an approved
manner.
      (13)   Wholesomeness of food and drink. It shall be unlawful for any
person to use in any restaurant establishment, or to bring into or keep in the
same with the intention of selling, any food, condiment, confection or drink
which is unclean, unwholesome, tainted, putrid, decayed, adulterated, poisoned,
infected or in any other manner rendered unsafe or unwholesome for human food.
For the purposes of this subchapter, such food products shall be deemed
unwholesome for human food if the same have been contaminated by flies or other
insects, vermin, dust, dirt or other foreign contamination; if they contain any
poisonous or deleterious or injurious ingredients in kind and quantities so as
to render such articles injurious or detrimental to health; or if they contain
the whole or part of any uninspected and unpassed meat or meat-food products;
or if such articles are or have been submerged in brine or other solutions
which are unclean, sour, putrid, spoiled or contaminated.
         (a)   Custard-filled products. All custard-filled and custard cream-
filled pastries shall be rebaked after filling at an oven temperature of at
least 425°F for at least 20 minutes and cooled to 50°F or less within one hour
thereafter, or the filling shall be heated before the pastry shells are filled
so that every particle of the custard or custard-cream mix is held at a
temperature of at least 190°F for at least ten minutes and cooled either before
or after filling the pastry shells to 50°F or less within one hour after
heating, and shall be maintained at that temperature until served or sold.
         (b)   Milk products.
            1.   All milk, fluid milk products, ice cream, frozen custard,
sherbet, ices and similar frozen desserts served shall be obtained from sources
approved by the Health Inspector. Only Grade A pasteurized milk and milk
products shall be used.
            2.   In the case of milk drinks prepared, served or sold, the milk
used shall include the entire contents of the original container or shall be
from an approved bulk dispenser. All milk drinks shall be mixed in a sanitary
manner.
            3.   All milk and fluid milk products shall be served in the
individual, original containers in which they were received from the
distributor, or from a bulk container equipped with an approved dispensing
device complying with the following specifications.
               a.   It shall comply with the requirements of division (B)(11)
above pertaining to the construction of utensils and equipment.
               b.   No surfaces with which milk or milk products come in
contact, except the delivery office, while the dispenser is in use, shall be
accessible to manual contact, droplet infection, dust or flies.
               c.   All parts of the dispenser with which milk comes in
contact, including any measuring device, shall be cleaned and subjected to a
bactericidal treatment at the milk plant where filled and not at the restaurant
establishment.
               d.   The dispenser shall be filled and sealed with two seals at
the milk plant in such a manner as to make it impossible to withdraw any of its
contents without breaking one seal and impossible to replace any of its
contents without breaking the other.
               e.   The dispensing device shall be so constructed as to
automatically mix the milk and cream thoroughly with each dispensing operation,
except in the case of milk products which remain homogeneous without mixing.
All milk and milk products and cream served from dispensers shall be kept at a
temperature of 50°F or less until served. In the enforcement of this
requirement, the Health Inspector may make an exception in the case of cream
served with coffee, cereals and the like. The Health Inspector may permit the
serving of cream from the original container or from a dispenser which complies
with divisions (B)(13)(b)3.a. and (B)(13)(b)3.b. above and which can be filled
in a sanitary manner, kept clean and frequently subjected to bactericidal
treatment complying with the requirements of division (B)(12) above.
         (c)   Shellfish. Oysters, clams and mussels shall be obtained from a
source approved by the U.S. Public Health Service. Shucked shellfish shall be
kept, until sold, served or used, in the containers in which they were placed
in the shucking plant.
         (d)   Pork. All food products which, in whole or in part, shall
contain raw pork shall be deemed unwholesome if they have not been thoroughly
cooked or otherwise treated by the method approved by the Health Inspector to
ensure the destruction of trichinae.
      (14)   Storage, display and serving of food and drink.
         (a)   All food and drink shall be stored and displayed in such a
manner as to be protected from dust, flies, vermin, unnecessary handling,
droplet infection, overhead leakage and condensation, sewage backflow and other
contamination. Evidence of the presence of rodents, roaches, ants or other
vermin shall be considered a violation of this division (B)(14)(a). Food or
drink shall not be stored or prepared beneath overhead sewer or drain pipes
unless such pipes are provided with suitable means to carry off possible
leakage or condensation. Food or drink shall not be stored directly on floors
which are subject to flooding from sewage backflow. The pouring lips of bottles
containing milk or other beverages in non-leakproof containers shall not be
submerged in water for cooling.
         (b)   All food and drink shall be handled, prepared and served in such
a manner as to minimize the opportunities for contamination. Serving of sliced
butter and cracked ice shall not be by direct contact with fingers or hands and
manual contact with all food or drink shall be avoided insofar as possible.
         (c)   All unwrapped or unenclosed food and drink on display shall be
protected by glass or otherwise from public handling or other contamination;
except that, approved hand opening for self- service may be permitted on
counter fronts. Breads, pies, cakes or other like articles of food shall not be
carried or transported through any public or private way unless such articles
of food are carried or transported in a fly-proof and dust-proof receptacle.
         (d)   No animals or fowl shall be kept or allowed in any room in which
food or drink is prepared or stored.
         (e)   All enclosed spaces within double walls, between ceilings and
floors, beneath floors and in fixtures and equipment which provide harborage
and potential breeding places for rodents shall be eliminated by the removal of
the sheeting or interior walls which form the enclosed spaces, or all exposed
edges of such walls, floors and sheetings shall be protected against gnawing by
rats by the installation of approved rat-proof material; and all openings in
walls, floors and ceilings through which pipes, electric cables and other
conduits pass shall be properly sealed with snuggly-fitting collars of metal or
other approved rat-proof material securely fastened in place and so maintained;
and propagation of rats and invasion and infestation of the premises by them
shall be permanently prevented.
         (f)   All supplementary means necessary for the elimination of flies,
roaches and rodents shall be employed. For the elimination of flies, fly
repellent fans, flypaper, fly traps or fly-killing sprays or powders may be
used. All poisonous compounds used in the extermination of rodents or insects
shall be so colored as to be easily identified; however, poisonous substances
should be used with extreme caution and compounds harmless to humans should be
substituted wherever possible. Poisonous compounds shall not be stored in
kitchens or food preparation rooms.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-8) Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.048 DISEASED EMPLOYEES.
   (A)   Prohibited. No person who is affected with any disease in a
communicable form or is a carrier of such disease shall work in any restaurant.
No restaurant shall employ any such person or any persons suspected of being
affected with any disease in a communicable form or of being a carrier of such
disease. If the person in charge of any restaurant suspects that any employee
has contracted any disease in a communicable form or has become a carrier of
such disease, he or she shall notify the Health Inspector immediately.
   (B)   Infection suspected; procedure. When suspicion arises as to
probability of transmission of infection from any restaurant employee, the
Health Inspector is authorized to require the following measures:
      (1)   The immediate exclusion of the employee from all restaurants;
      (2)   The immediate closing of the restaurant concerned until no further
danger of diseased outbreak exists, in the opinion of the Health Inspector; and
      (3)   Adequate medical examination of the employee and of his or her
associates with such laboratory examinations as may be deemed necessary under
the circumstances.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-9) Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.049 ICE CREAM VENDORS.
   It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to sell, dispense
or distribute for profit in any manner, any ice cream or other frozen
confections produced for human consumption upon a public highway or right-of-
way in the village, except or unless such selling, dispensing or distributing
shall be made from a non-moving vehicle which has been licensed by the village
to sell from a designated or specific site. As used herein, the word NON-MOVING
VEHICLE shall not include a vehicle which uses wheels for the sole purpose of
reaching or moving to the site from which selling, dispensing and distributing
is authorized.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-10) (Ord. 93-216, passed 7-20-1993) Penalty, see §
120.999
§ 120.050 LICENSE SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION; REINSTATEMENT.
   (A)   Any license issued may be temporarily suspended by the Health
Inspector upon the violation by the holder of any of the terms of this
subchapter, or revoked, after an opportunity for a hearing by the Health
Inspector, upon serious or repeated violation.
   (B)   Any restaurant, the permit of which has been suspended, may at any
time make application for the reinstatement of the permit. Within one week
after the receipt of a satisfactory application, accompanied by a statement
signed by the applicant to the effect that the violated provision or provisions
of this subchapter have been conformed with, the Health Inspector shall make a
reinspection and, thereafter, as many additional reinspections as he or she may
deem necessary to assure himself or herself that the applicant is again
complying with all requirements and, in case the finding indicates compliance,
shall reinstate the permit.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-11)
§ 120.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   If, on completion of the 30-day period described in §
120.025 of this chapter, the Health Inspector determines that the retailer has
willfully violated §§
120.020 through
120.026 of this chapter, after providing notice and an opportunity for a
hearing before the Health Inspector with respect to the violation, the Health
Inspector may fine the retailer in an amount not more than $1,000 for each
violation.
   (C)   Any person, firm or corporation who violates, disobeys, omits,
neglects or refuses to comply with or who resists the enforcement of any of the
provisions of §§
120.040 through
120.050 of this chapter shall, upon conviction, be deemed guilty of a
misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not more than $500 for each offense and may
be committed to the county jail or to any place provided by ordinance for the
incarceration of offenders until the fine, penalty and cost are fully paid. No
imprisonment, however, shall exceed six months for any offense. Each day that a
violation is permitted to exist shall constitute a separate offense.
(Prior Code, § 4-7A-12)
(Ord. 93-216, passed 7-20-1993; Ord. 07-425, passed 11-19-2007)
