NURSING, CONVALESCENT AND SENIOR CITIZEN HOMES
§ 121.001 DEFINITION.
   A NURSING, CONVALESCENT OR SENIOR CITIZEN HOME shall mean a building or
buildings used for the lodging, boarding or nursing care on a 24-hour basis of
four or more infants or children, convalescents or aged persons, but shall not
include hospitals and mental or correctional institutions.
(Prior Code, § 4-2A-1)
§ 121.002 LICENSE REQUIRED; TERM; REVOCATION.
   (A)   No nursing, convalescent or senior citizen homes, as defined in §
121.001 of this chapter, shall be operated, except under a license from the
village.
   (B)   Such license shall expire on April 30 of each year and shall be
revocable for cause.
(Prior Code, § 4-2A-2) (Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 121.003 LICENSE APPLICATION.
   Application for such license shall conform to the general provisions
relating to applications for licenses and shall state:
   (A)   The location or proposed location of the home;
   (B)   The purpose for which it is to be opened, conducted, maintained or
operated;
   (C)   The accommodations for the residents thereof;
   (D)   The nature and kind of care, instruction or benefits given or proposed
to be given therein;
   (E)   The name and address of the officials, or board of officials,
conducting, managing, maintaining or operating said home;
   (F)   The name of the superintendent or person in charge of said home; and
   (G)   The name and address of the chief physician, surgeon or attending
physician.
(Prior Code, § 4-2A-3)
§ 121.004 LICENSE FEE.
   The annual license fee for such business shall be established by ordinance
as set forth in the license fee schedule of §
110.018(A) of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 4-2A-4)
§ 121.005 COMPLIANCE WITH VILLAGE AND STATE RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Building regulations. Nursing, convalescent or senior citizen homes
shall be constructed so as to conform to the Building Code of the village; and
the minimum standards set forth in the most current version of the Nursing Home
Care Act (210 ILCS 45) and the state’s Department of Public Health’s (IDPH)
Minimum Standards for Long-Term Care Facilities, being 77 Ill. Adm. Code §
300.110 et seq. as now or hereafter amended.
   (B)   Minimum standards of care. Each nursing, convalescent or senior
citizen home operated in the village shall furnish such care and services for
its occupants as shall conform and meet the standards and requirements set
forth in the most current version of the Nursing Home Care Act (210 ILCS 45)
and the state’s Department of Public Health’s (IDPH) Minimum Standards for
Long-Term Care Facilities, being 77 Ill. Adm. Code § 300.110 et seq. as now or
hereafter amended.
   (C)   Copies. Three copies of said rules and regulations were filed in the
office of the Village Clerk for public inspection in accordance with the
statutes of the state in such case made and provided.
(Prior Code, § 4-2A-5) (Ord. 86-114, passed 4-15-1986) Penalty, see §
10.999
AMBULANCES AND MOBILE INTENSIVE CARE UNITS
§ 121.020 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   No person shall operate or maintain any ambulance or mobile intensive care
unit or ambulance service or mobile intensive care unit service without first
obtaining a license therefor.
(Prior Code, § 4-2B-1) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 121.021 INVESTIGATION OF LICENSE APPLICANT.
   In case the license applicant is, at the time of such application, operating
or maintaining an ambulance or mobile intensive care unit, the village’s Health
Inspector shall cause an investigation to be made to determine whether or not
the applicant has complied with all applicable laws relating to health,
sanitation and safety.
(Prior Code, § 4-2B-2)
§ 121.022 INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS; SUITS.
   (A)   Insurance required.
      (1)   Every ambulance or mobile intensive care unit owner shall carry
public liability and property damage insurance and worker’s compensation
insurance for his or her employees with solvent and responsible insurers
authorized to transact such insurance business in the state and qualified to
assume the risks for amounts hereinafter set forth to secure payment of any
loss or damage resulting from any occurrence arising out of or caused by the
operation or use of any of the ambulance or mobile intensive care units
belonging to the licensee.
      (2)   The public liability insurance policy or contract may cover one or
more vehicles, but each ambulance or mobile intensive care unit shall be
insured for the sum of at least $250,000 for bodily injury or death to one
person, $500,000 for bodily injury or death in one occurrence and for the sum
of $100,000 for property damage. Every insurance policy or contract for such
insurance shall provide for the payment and satisfaction of any final judgment
rendered against the owner or any person driving any insured vehicle.
   (B)   Suit for claims. Suit may be brought in any court of competent
jurisdiction upon such policy or contract by any person having claims arising
from the operation or use of ambulances or mobile intensive care units. It
shall contain a description of each ambulance or mobile intensive care vehicle
insured, manufacturer’s name and serial number and the ambulance or mobile
intensive care unit license number.
(Prior Code, § 4-2B-3) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 121.023 STANDARDS FOR EQUIPMENT AND PERSONNEL.
   (A)   Generally. Each ambulance or mobile intensive care unit shall, at all
times, when in use as such:
      (1)   Be suitable for the transportation of patients from the standpoint
of health, sanitation and safety;
      (2)   Be maintained in suitable premises;
      (3)   Contain equipment conforming with the standards, requirements and
regulations provided for herein, which equipment shall be in proper and good
condition for such use; and
      (4)   Comply with all applicable statutes and ordinances relating to
health, sanitation and safety.
   (B)   Vehicles.
      (1)   Without any limitation on the foregoing provisions, each vehicle
shall comply with the requirements of the state’s Department of Transportation,
both as to design and equipment.
      (2)   Radio and communications equipment must be approved and licensed by
the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and all hospital equipment must be
approved by the FCC and the state’s Department of Public Health.
(Prior Code, § 4-2B-4) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 121.024 CONSENT OF SICK OR INJURED PERSON.
   No physically sick or injured person shall be conveyed against his or her
will by any private ambulance service or mobile intensive care service from the
place where he or she was overcome by sickness or from the scene of an
accident, nor having been placed in an ambulance or mobile intensive care unit,
shall he or she be conveyed to a place to which he or she is unwilling to go;
provided, however, that, if such sick or injured person is unable to give any
direction in his or her own behalf and there is no immediate relative present
to direct where he or she shall be taken, such sick or injured person shall be
conveyed to the nearest emergency medical facility; provided, further, that,
the requirement contained herein regarding transportation to the nearest
medical facility shall not apply when the ambulance or mobile intensive care
unit attendants are directed by a licensed physician, registered nurse or other
properly authorized representative of a hospital participating in the South
Cook County Mobile Intensive Care System, to transport the sick or injured
person to an emergency medical facility other than the nearest such facility.
(Prior Code, § 4-2B-5) Penalty, see §
10.999
§ 121.025 INSPECTIONS.
   No vehicle shall be licensed as an ambulance or mobile intensive care unit
until it has been inspected under the direction of the village’s Health
Inspector and found to be in safe operating condition. Further, the village’s
Health Inspector shall cause an inspection of the premises and vehicle or
vehicles named and described in the license application for the purpose of
determining the fitness and suitability of the premises and vehicle or vehicles
for such business from the standpoint of health, sanitation and safety, and
that the equipment in such vehicles complies with all the requirements set out
in this subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 4-2B-6) (Ord. passed 5-1-1979)

§ 122.003 INCORRECT MEASURES.
   (A)   If any person shall use, maintain or operate in the city in weighing

   All itinerant peddlers, hawkers, using scales, balances, weights or measures

§ 122.007 WEIGHING OF FEED.
   For the purpose of computing the weight of any hay, straw, grain or mill
feed sold and delivered in the village, or sold elsewhere to be delivered
within the village, avoirdupois weight shall be used, and 100 pounds shall be
and constitute a hundredweight, and ten such hundredweight or 2,000 pounds
avoirdupois shall constitute a ton.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.008 STONE, SAND AND GRAVEL.
   Any person engaged in the business of selling crushed stone, bank sand,
torpedo sand or gravel within the village for delivery in the said village,
shall, in the absence of a contract or agreement in writing to the contrary,
sell the same by standard avoirdupois net weight and in no outer way.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.009 SCALES REQUIRED WHEN.
   (A)   Every person selling or offering for sale any service, commodity,
produce or article of merchandise, sold by weight, shall keep and maintain in a
conspicuous place on his or her premises, scales suitable for weighing such
commodity, produce or article of merchandise, and shall, whenever requested by
the buyer and in the buyer’s presence, weigh the commodity, produce or article
of merchandise sold or offered for sale.
   (B)   Wherever meat, poultry or other articles of merchandise sold by weight
and prepared or wrapped in advance of being sold by the retailer, are being
offered for sale, an accurate computing scale of adequate capacity shall be
placed or set no more than 30 feet from the prepackaged display counter or
service area. A prominent and conspicuous sign shall be placed on or adjacent
to the computing scale, such sign shall read “for customer use” in a type size
no less than two inches in height. Where the prepackaged merchandise is marked
with weight expressed in the standard avoirdupois pound and decimal fractions
thereof, a conversion chart showing the correlation between the decimal
fractions and common fractions of the avoirdupois pound, in a type size no less
than 12-point, shall be prominently and conspicuously displayed.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.010 LOAD LOTS.
   (A)   (1)   Every load of solid fuel of more than 1,000 pounds, or of any
other commodity, produce or other article of merchandise sold in load lots by
weight, delivered by vehicle within the village, shall be weighed by a public
weighmaster.
      (2)   A certificate of weight for each such load, issued by such public
weighmaster, shall be delivered by the driver or person in charge of the
vehicle to the purchaser or consignee of such load, or to his, her or their
agent, at the time of the delivery and before any of the commodity, produce or
article of merchandise is removed from the vehicle, or such certificates shall
be delivered to the Inspector of Weights and Measures, or any of the deputies,
upon demand.
   (B)   When delivery is made, in case no person is present to receive such
commodity, produce or other article of merchandise, and if the purchaser or
consignee, or his or their agent, cannot be located, then the certificate of
weight herein before provided for shall be posted conspicuously at the place of
delivery before any of the commodity, produce or article of merchandise is
removed from the vehicle.
   (C)   No person shall alter any certificate of weight or attempt to use the
same for any other load than the one for which the same was given, or diminish
the quantity of such load after the weighing and before the sale delivery
thereof.
   (D)   (1)   The weight certificate shall remain at all times on the vehicle
conveying the load until it is delivered by the driver to the purchaser or
posted as provided above at the point of delivery.
      (2)   Ice sold in load lots by weight is exempted from all of the
requirements of this section.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.011 CERTIFICATE OF WEIGHT; CONTENTS.
   (A)   The certificate of weight shall show the date of weighing, the gross
weight, the tare and the net weight, the kind and grade of such commodity, the
name and address of the seller and purchaser thereof, the number of the vehicle
(if such vehicle be numbered), the license number of such vehicle and the name
of the person in charge of such vehicle.
   (B)   The certificate of weight for each delivery of solid fuel shall also
show the city of manufacture in the case of coke or manufactured fuel and the
size of the solid fuel in one of the following terms only:
      (1)   Lump or block, the general size of which shall be not less than
four inches in diameter. Egg, the general size of which shall be not less than
two inches in diameter. Range, the general size of which shall be not less than
one and one-half inches in diameter;
      (2)   Nut or stove, the general size of which shall be not less than one
inch in diameter: chestnut, the general size: of which shall be not less than
three-quarters inch in diameter; pea, buckwheat and small nut, the general size
of which shall be not less than three-eighths inch in diameter; and
      (3)   Mine run, which shall be coal as received from the mine without any
variation or sizing. Slack and screening, which shall be such other sizes as
are not heretofore specifically designated.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.012 VERIFICATION OF WEIGHT.
   Any person in charge of a vehicle used for delivering in load lots any
commodity within the village shall, at the request of the Inspector of Weights
and Measures or any of the Inspector deputies, or at the request of the
purchaser thereof at any time after the weighing thereof, produce and deliver
the required certificate of weight for the inspection of the Inspector of
Weights and Measures, Deputy Inspector or the purchaser, and shall upon request
of any such person demanding a verification of weight go to a designated public
scale located in the particular locality where the delivery is to be made or to
any private scale in the particular locality of delivery when the owner thereof
shall consent to such use. The commodity about to be delivered and the vehicle
used for the delivery of the same shall be weighed for the purpose of
ascertaining the gross weight, thereof, and the person in charge of the vehicle
making the delivery shall, after such delivery, return forthwith to the same
scales and there weigh such vehicle for the purpose of verifying the net weight
of such commodity as shown by said certificate of weight; provided, however,
that, if the seller of such commodity or the person in charge of the vehicle
making the delivery requests the privilege of re-weighing such commodity on
another and different scale from that selected by the Inspector of Weights and
Measures, an Inspector Deputy or the purchaser, or upon the scale where the
commodity was originally weighed, said person requesting the verification of
weight shall consent to such re-weighing on some other scale in the particular
locality where such delivery is to be made or upon said scale of original
weighing; and, provided further that, when the person selling or making the
delivery of any load lot of any commodity, produce or article of merchandise
has not as a public weighmaster, weighed such load lot and is not interested
directly or indirectly with the public weighmaster weighing such commodity,
produce or article of merchandise in the operation of such public weighmasters
scale, it shall be the duty of the person in charge of the vehicle used in the
delivery thereof to permit such verification of weight upon condition that the
Inspector of Weights and Measures, or Inspector Deputy, or public weighmaster,
purchaser or consignee making such request shall have kept such load in view
from the location of the scale where such load was originally weighed by the
public weighmaster to the point where such request is made.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.013 DELIVERY TICKET; REQUIRED; CONTENTS.
   (A)   When solid fuel is sold or delivered in lots of less than 1,000 pounds
or any commodity is weighed by a public weighmaster and sold in less than load
lots, the seller shall give a delivery ticket to the purchaser, purchaser’s
agent or the person to whom the delivery is to be made before the delivery of
such commodity, or to the Inspector of Weights and Measures upon, demand.
   (B)   The said delivery ticket shall bear the date of the weighing, the name
and address of the seller, the license number if the seller be a peddler, the
net weight of each kind of commodity to be delivered, the size in the case of
solid fuel and the grade thereof.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.014 WEIGHING MEMORANDUM REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   All railway companies and all persons operating elevators or
warehouses which remain in the village delivery team track yards equipped with
scales shall, upon the delivery by them of any hay, straw, grain or millfeed to
the consignee or to the person having an order from the consignee for the
delivery thereof, where such commodity is removed from such yards in wagon-load
lots or in amounts less than load lots, weigh the same and deliver to the
person in charge of any vehicle furnished, by the consignee, or by the person
having his or her order, a certificate of weight or delivery ticket which shall
comply with all the requirements of this chapter relating thereto, and which
shall show the name or the initials of the railroad company or of the elevator
or warehouse issuing such certificate of weight or delivery ticket, and the
location of the scale upon which such hay, straw, grain or millfeed is weighed.
   (B)   For such weighing and for the issuing of said memoranda, a fee of not
exceeding $0.25 for each load or part of a load so weighed may be charged and
collected.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.015 NET WEIGHT DESIGNATED.
   When any commodity is sold subject to public weighmaster’s weights, the net
weight shown in the weight certificate issued by such public weighmaster shall
be taken to be the true avoirdupois net weight of the same, subject to the
right of re-weighing as herein provided. Net weight, within the meaning of this
chapter, shall be the actual weight of the commodity excluding the weight of
the vehicle, if any, in which it is loaded, and excluding the weight of the
horses and driver of such vehicle or either of them, as the case may be, if
such horses and driver, or either of them, be weighed as of the tare weight.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.016 WEIGHMASTER WEIGHING OWN COMMODITIES.
   Nothing contained in this chapter shall be construed to prevent any person
engaged in the business of selling any commodity which is ordinarily delivered
by vehicle, from becoming a public weighmaster and appointing deputy
weighmasters to weigh the commodity being sold and delivered by such person,
and any weight certificate issued by such person, or the deputies appointed by
the weighmaster, covering commodities sold by such person, shall be of the same
effect as the weight certificate issued by any other public weighmaster.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.017 OBSTRUCTION AFTER RE-WEIGHING.
   Any person, selling and delivering or attempting to deliver any load lot of
any commodity that has been re-weighed on the scale of the public weighmaster
on which it was originally weighed at his or her request, who shall refuse or
fail to allow said load to be delivered to the destination it was originally
billed or sent to, or who shall fail or refuse to have the load, removed from
the vehicle used in the delivery thereof, or who shall hinder or obstruct the
Inspector of Weights and Measures, or any Inspector Deputies, from obtaining
and ascertaining the net weight of the commodity delivered or attempted to be
delivered, shall be fined.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.018 FALSE CERTIFICATE AND DELIVERY TICKETS.
   (A)   (1)   No person shall sell and deliver, or attempt to deliver, any
load lot of any commodity sold in load lot by weight and delivered by vehicle
within the village of a quantity less than that called for by the certificate
of weight; nor shall any public weighmaster or deputy provide the driver or
person in charge of the vehicle used in the delivery thereof, or the person
attempting to deliver the same, with a certificate which, does not correctly
state the information required to be given in §
122.011 of this chapter.
      (2)   No driver or person in charge of such delivery shall fail, neglect
or refuse to deliver to the Inspector of weights and measures or any Inspector
Deputies upon demand the aforesaid certificate, before any part of such load is
removed from the vehicle, nor refuse to comply with his, her or their request
to reweigh the same in order that the weights stated in such certificate may be
verified.
   (B)   No person shall request any public weighmaster or any weighmaster
deputies to weigh any commodity falsely or incorrectly, nor shall any person
request a false or incorrect certificate of weight or delivery ticket.
   (C)   No person selling, delivering or attempting to deliver any commodity
in load lots or in amounts less than load lots within the village, shall
provide the person in charge of the conveyance, or the person actually
delivering or attempting to make said delivery, with a false or fraudulent
certificate of weight or delivery ticket nor provide a certificate of weight or
delivery ticket which is not the result of the actual weighing of the commodity
so sold, delivered or attempted to be delivered.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.019 ILLEGAL OR FALSE WEIGHTS AND MEASURES.
   (A)   No person shall sell, offer for sale, or keep for the purpose of sale,
any commodity quantities or enumerations of less weight or measures than that
represented upon such sale or offer for sale by the vendor or his or her agent
or employee, nor shall any person sell or offer for sale any commodity in any
receptacle having a smaller capacity than is represented at the time of such
offer or sale.
   (B)   No person shall sell or offer for sale articles of dry or liquid
measurement in other than the legal type of measured required therefor.
   (C)   No person weighing or measuring any commodity for sale by dry, liquid,
lineal or superficial measurement, or by any unit of enumeration used in
determining or measuring quantity, or by weight, shall falsify the measure or
weight of such commodity by representing the measure or weight of the same to
be either more or less than the true measure of weight thereof.
   (D)   It shall be unlawful for any person performing services upon any
commodity who shall determine the charge for such services according to the
measure or weight of the commodity upon which the services are performed, to
falsify the measure or weight of the same by representing the measure or weight
to be more than the true measure or weight thereof.
   (E)   No person shall deliver to the purchaser or prospective purchaser any
commodity in quantities or enumeration of less weight or measure than that
offered for sale.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.020 DECEPTIVE PRACTICES.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person:
      (1)   To act, use or employ any deception, fraud, false pretense, false
promise or misrepresentation, or to conceal, suppress or omit any material fact
with intent that others rely upon such concealment, suppression or omission, in
connection with the sale, for cash or on credit, or advertisement of any
merchandise, whether or not any person has in fact been misled; provided,
however, that, nothing herein contained shall apply to the owner or publisher
of newspapers, magazines, publications or printed matter wherein such
advertisement appears, or to the owner or operator of a radio or television
station which disseminates such, advertisement when the owner, publisher or
operator has no knowledge of the intent, design or purpose of the advertiser;
and, provided further that, nothing herein contained shall apply to any
advertisement which is subject to and complies with the rules and regulations
of any of the statutes administered by the Federal Trade Commission;
      (2)   Representing that merchandise new, if it is deteriorated, altered,
reconditioned, reclaimed, used or secondhand shall be construed as a violation
of this section;
      (3)   Representing that merchandise or services are of a particular
standard, grade or quality, or that merchandise is represented to be of a
particular style or model, if it is not, shall be considered a violation of
this section;
      (4)   Failing to deliver ordered merchandise within a period of 60 days
from the date of order or contract, unless otherwise provided therein, unless
the customer is notified in writing of the reason for the delay and such
merchandise is delivered in less than a total of 90 days, or a refund is
offered within 90 days of the date of the order or contract, shall be
considered a violation of this section;
      (5)   Making false or misleading statements of fact concerning the
reasons for, existence of or amounts of price reductions, or engaging in any
other pricing conduct causing confusion or misunderstanding, shall be
considered a violation of this section;
      (6)   Representing that merchandise or services are those of another,
when in fact they are not, shall be considered a violation of this section;
      (7)   Causing confusion or misunderstanding concerning the source,
sponsorship, approval or certification of merchandise or services shall be
considered a violation of this section;
      (8)   Causing confusion or misunderstanding or false or deceptive
representation concerning affiliation, connection or association with, or
certification by another, shall be considered a violation of this section;
      (9)   Representing that merchandise or services have sponsorship or
approval concerning the source of or certification of merchandise or services
when in fact they do not have such approval or sponsorship, shall be considered
a violation of this section;
      (10)   Failing to state a material fact, if such failure tends to deceive
or mislead, shall be considered a violation of this section;
      (11)   Advertising for sale at a stated price, any items when sufficient
quantities of said advertised items are not readily available to be sold to
purchasers at the advertised price during the effective period of the
advertisement for sale, shall be considered a violation of this section. For
the purposes of this division (A)(11), READILY AVAILABLE ITEMS shall mean
available to the customer in an area of the store normally used to display this
type of merchandise, except in a case where the space available for the items
is limited, a sample of the items may be placed in a prominent location,
accompanied by a prominent written notice clearly stating that the items are in
stock and may be obtained upon request and sufficient quantities shall mean
available in quantities sufficient to meet reasonably expected customer demand
through medium response;
      (12)   Charging a higher amount of tax than the legal rate set forth by
laws and regulations existing at the time of sale shall be considered a
violation of this section;
      (13)   Selling outdated merchandise, unless such merchandise is both
physically separated from merchandise that is not outdated and clearly
designated as outdated shall constitute a violation of this section.
         (a)   OUTDATED MERCHANDISE means merchandise that is offered for sale
beyond the date specified by the manufacturer of the merchandise.
         (b)   Such date may or may not be preceded by, but is not limited to,
such terms as “last sale date”, “use by”, “best if used by” or “expires on”.
      (14)   Selling or offering for sale, or keeping with intention of
selling, infant formula that is outdated, shall constitute a violation of this
section. Outdated formula shall be considered unsafe and unwholesome for human
food.
   (B)   For the purpose of this section, the following definitions apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      ADVERTISEMENT. The attempt by publication, dissemination, solicitation or
circulation to induce directly or indirectly any person to enter into any
obligation or acquire any title or interest in any merchandise and includes
every word device to disguise any form of business solicitation, by using such
terms as “renewal”, “invoice”, “statement” or “reminder” to create an
impression of existing obligation when there is none, or other language to
mislead any person in relation to any sought-after commercial transaction.
      MERCHANDISE. Any objects, wares, goods, commodities, intangibles, real
estate or services.
      PERSON. Any natural person or his or her legal representative,
partnership, corporation, (domestic and foreign), company, trust, business
entity or association, and any agent, employee, salesperson, partner, officer,
collector, member, stockholder, associate, trustee or cestui que trust thereof.
      SALE. Any sale, offer for sale or attempt to sell any merchandise for
cash or on credit.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.021 LABELING LEAD-BASED OR HEAVY-METAL-BASED PAINTS.
   Effective upon the passage of this chapter, no person shall sell, or hold
for sale, any lead-based coatings or toxic heavy-metal-based coatings as
defined in this chapter (including paint, lacquer or other applied liquid
surface coatings, and putty), unless said lead-based or toxic heavy-metal-based
coating is in a secure container bearing a label on its principal display panel
on which appears the following statement.
 
WARNING CONTAINS _______________________
 
DRIED FILM OF THIS SUBSTANCE MAY BE HARMFUL IF EATEN OR CHEWED.
 
Read Carefully Cautions on Instruction Panel. The following cautionary statement
(or its practical equivalent) shall be placed on the label, but need not be part of
the warning statement on the principal display panel:
 
KEEP OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN.
 
Do not apply on toys and other children’s articles, furniture, or interior surfaces
of any dwelling or facility which may be occupied or used by children.
 
The blank space in the warning label which follows the word “contains” shall be
filled with either the word “Lead” and/or toxic heavy metal substances which is
present in the amount specified in the definitions contained in sections of this
code.
 
The statements on labels required under the provisions of this section shall be
made in conformance with the following requirements:
 
(a)   The statements shall be presented in such a manner as to be generally
parallel to the declaration of identity and to the base on which the package rests
as it is designed to be displayed and shall be separate from other wording or
designs;
(b)   The word “WARNING” shall be in capital letters of a size not less than 18-
point type and the statements:
 
CONTAINS ___________________________
DRIED FILM OF THIS SUBSTANCE MAY BE HARMFUL IF EATEN OR CHEWED.
KEEP OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN.
 
shall be in capital letters and of a size not less than 12-point type.
 
(c)   The statement:
 
“Read Carefully. Cautions on Instruction Panel” and the instructions (or their
practical equivalent.)
 
“Do not apply on toys and other children’s articles, furniture or interior surfaces
of any dwelling or facility which may be occupied or used by children” shall be in
a size not less than 10-point type.
 
(d)   In a case where the size of the container is too small to accommodate a label
of sufficient size to allow the of the type size set forth herein, a reduced size
of type which is consistent with other printing on the panel involved may be used,
but in no case shall the size be less than 6-point type unless an exemption has
been granted under § 3(c) of the Federal Hazardous Substance Act and § 191.63 of
the regulations under the Federal Hazardous Substance Labeling Act, being U.S.C. §§
1261 et seq.
 
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.022 AUTHORITY; RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The Director of the Department of Revenue is hereby empowered to adopt and
to enforce rules and regulations relating to any matter pertaining to the
administration and enforcement of the provisions of this chapter. The Director
of the Department of Revenue, or any agent or employee designated in writing by
the Inspector is hereby authorized to examine books, papers and records of any
person subject to this chapter, during regular business hours in order to
ensure that such person is in compliance with this chapter. The Director of the
Department of Revenue is also authorized hereby, for good cause shown by
affidavit, to grant extensions not in excess of 60 days in compliance with this
chapter. The Director of the Department of Revenue is also authorized to issue
regulations exempting commodities subject to unit pricing and to add
commodities subject to unit pricing on a showing of respectively, hardship or
good cause.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.023 ENFORCEMENT.
   The Department of the Department of Revenue shall enforce the provisions of
this chapter.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
FUELS AND LIQUIDS
§ 122.035 PUMPS AND LIQUID MEASURING DEVICES.
   (A)   Any person owning, operating or using any automatic or mechanical pump
or liquid measuring device for the purpose of measuring any liquid commodity to
be sold or offered for sale within the village shall provide proper tested
standard measures, and shall each day before making the first sale in the
morning, and always before commencing to sell a new supply of liquid, test the
accuracy of the device so in use.
   (B)   No person shall use such automatic or mechanical pump or device
without first having obtained a certificate of approval from the Inspector of
Weights and Measures, nor shall any person use any such automatic or mechanical
pump device that is incorrect or defective.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.036 MEASUREMENT OF FUEL OIL.
   No person shall sell distillate fuels by any other than liquid measure using
the standard gallon as the unit of measure. No person shall sell or deliver or
attempt to sell or deliver to any purchaser in excess of ten gallons of any
distillate fuel unless measured at the place and time of delivery by measure of
a meter or five-gallon liquid measure, tested and sealed by the Department of
Weights and Measures, provided that deliveries of distillate fuel in quantities
of 2,000 gallons or more or of residual fuel of any quantity may be measured
either through a meter or by vehicle tank which has been tested and sealed by
the Department of Weights and Measures.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.037 DISTILLATE FUELS; DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS AND THE LIKE.
   (A)   Defined. The term DISTILLATE FUELS, as used herein, shall be construed
to mean and include fuel in liquid form which can or may be used for heating
purposes and which has an American Petroleum Institute gravity normally greater
than 22; however, if the oil has a Saybolt Universal viscosity of more than 55
seconds at 100°F, it shall not be included.
   (B)   Meter recording element. Each and every delivery from any vehicle tank
or other wheeled, conveyance of distillate fuels required to be measured by
meter at the place of delivery, shall conform to the following requirements.
      (1)   The meter shall be equipped with a recording element (i.e., a
ticket printing device); this element or register to print upon the delivery
ticket either the gallonage reading before and after delivery or the zero
indications and total number of gallons delivered.
      (2)   Any meter not now equipped with a recording element shall be so
equipped within a period not to exceed 90 days from and after the effective
date of this section.
      (3)   The delivery ticket shall be inserted in the recording element
after the vehicle reaches the place of delivery; and shall be inserted in the
recording element while the vehicle is in transit.
   (C)   Distillate or residual fuel delivery requirements. All vehicle tank
deliveries of either distillate or residual fuels shall conform to the
following requirements.
      (1)   Each vehicle tank, liquid measure devices and appurtenances used in
such delivery shall conform to the requirements prescribed therefor in the
United States Bureau of Standards Handbook 44, in its latest form and in the
laws and regulations of the state.
      (2)   Upon completion of each delivery, the delivery ticket and at least
one duplicate thereof shall be completed, and one copy thereof shall be given
to the purchaser or to an agent of the purchaser or in the absence of both
shall be left at the place of delivery.
      (3)   On each delivery ticket there shall be distinctly and legibly
expressed the date of delivery, the name and address of the seller, the name
and address of the purchaser, the gallonage reading before and after delivery
or the number of gallons delivered, and the signature of the person making the
delivery.
      (4)   All delivery tickets shall be serially numbered and no ticket or
duplicate thereof shall be destroyed, but may be voided and kept on file. At
least one copy of each delivery ticket shall be retained and preserved for a
period of at least two years after the date of delivery and shall be available
for inspection by the Inspector of Weights and Measures and his or her
deputies.
   (D)   False delivery ticket; substitute product.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to deliver or attempt to
deliver to any purchaser any kind or grade of distillate fuel other than that
ordered by the purchaser, unless the purchaser is notified before delivery is
made.
      (2)   Any person who shall furnish to any person making or in charge of a
delivery of distillate fuels, or to any person to whom such a delivery is made,
a false or fraudulent delivery ticket or a ticket which does not show the
actual meter measurement of the quantity delivered shall, upon conviction, be
fined.
      (3)   It shall be unlawful for any person to deliver or attempt to
deliver to any purchaser in the village distillate fuels at an artificially
produced temperature in excess of 60°F.
      (4)   It shall be unlawful for any person making or in charge of delivery
of distillate fuel to refuse, fail or neglect to deliver to the Inspector of
Weights and Measures or to any of the Inspector deputies upon demand therefor,
any ticket evidencing any delivery subject to the provisions of divisions (A)
and (C) above. If the Inspector or deputy desires to retain the ticket, the
Inspector shall make and deliver to the person a signed receipt therefor.
   (E)   Vehicle tank meter; alteration or removal.
      (1)   If after the approval, testing and sealing by the Department of
Revenue of any vehicle tank, meter or measuring device used in delivering
distillate fuels, it shall be necessary to adjust, repair or alter the same or
to remove a meter from a vehicle tank to which it is affixed at the time of
testing and sealing or to install the same on any other vehicle tank, immediate
written notice shall be transmitted in person or by mail to the Department of
Revenue.
      (2)   All adjustable elements on such vehicle tank, meter or measuring
device shall seal with a lead and wire seal by the person or agency making the
adjustment, repair, alteration or removal, pending a retest by the Department
of Revenue.
   (F)   Non-applicability to certain fuel oils. The provisions of §
122.035 of this chapter and divisions (A) through (E) above shall not apply to
fuel oils delivered in packages or in tank cars by railroad, nor to deliveries
by pipeline, boat or barge, nor to deliveries by any method from a refinery,
pipeline terminal or boat or barge terminal into storage at a wholesale
distributing plant of a liquid fuel dealer or distributor.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.038 NEW EQUIPMENT.
   Where any new or additional equipment or appurtenance, except a meter-
recording element or register, is required by the provisions of §§
122.036 and
122.037(A), (B) and (C) of this chapter, for a period of six months from and
after the effective date of said sections, shall be allowed for the procurement
and installation of the same; provided that, the Inspector of Weights and
Measures shall allow additional grace periods of not to exceed six months for
such procurement and installation, if it appears that such additional time is
necessary because the equipment or appurtenance cannot be obtained or installed
during the time there-to-fore allowed.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.039 STANDARD AVOIRDUPOIS WEIGHT.
   The terms AVOIRDUPOIS WEIGHT and STANDARD AVOIRDUPOIS WEIGHT, as used in
this chapter, shall be construed to mean weight expressed in the standard
avoirdupois pound and the decimal or common fractions thereof, or in the
standard avoirdupois pound and ounces and fractions.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.040 SOLID FUEL.
   Every person selling or offering for sale solid fuel in the village shall
sell the same by avoirdupois net weight.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
FOOD ITEMS
§ 122.055 ICE.
   Every person selling ice or offering ice for sale shall, at time of delivery
of any ice sold, weigh the quantity of ice delivered and for that purpose will
be provided with a steelyard balance or other apparatus for weighing such ice
which shall have been duly adjusted and sealed by the Inspector of Weights and
Measures in accordance with the provisions of this chapter. All ice sold within
the city shall be sold by avoirdupois weight unless it is otherwise
specifically agreed upon between the buyer and seller.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.056 FOOD ITEMS TO BE SOLD BY NET WEIGHT; EXCEPTIONS.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to advertise for sale, keep for
the purpose of sale, offer or expose for sale, or sell, except for immediate
consumption on the premises, or when sold as one of several elements comprising
ready-to-eat meals, whether cooked or uncooked, any fruit or fruit products,
vegetables or vegetable products, live and dressed poultry, poultry products,
meat, meat products, non- liquid animal products, fish and fish products,
butter, cheese and other similar dairy products, except eggs, otherwise than by
standard avoirdupois net weight delivered to the purchaser or prospective
purchaser; provided, however, that, any fresh produce may be sold by the bunch,
each of weight subject to restrictions as may be contained in the rules and
regulations of the Director of the Department of Revenue; and, provided that,
any of the said, products, when sold in package form, shall comply with this
code’s requirements for packages.
   (B)   For the purpose of this section, the following shall be deemed to be a
READY-TO-EAT MEAL: a meal comprised of meat, fish or poultry as the main
portion with vegetables and a starch product included.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.057 WEIGHT.
   Whenever the term WEIGHT is used in this chapter, it shall be construed to
mean net weight.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.058 FOOD PACKAGING; WEIGHT AND PRICE MARKING.
   All packages of meat, meat products, poultry, poultry products, fish, fish
products, non-liquid animal products, cheese, fruits and vegetables prepared
and wrapped by the retailer in advance of being exposed or offered for sale by
the retailer shall be accurately weighed and, in addition to the net weight
marked thereon, shall be marked with the price per pound, and the total selling
price; provided, however, that, fresh produce items such as heads of lettuce,
cabbage or items as specified by the rules of the Director of the Department of
Revenue, wrapped in transparent material, shall not be considered “packaged”,
as defined in this section.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.059 TRANSPARENT WRAPPING.
   All meat, poultry and poultry pans which are packaged by the retailer in
advance of being exposed and offered for sale shall be in an entirely
transparent package, manufacture of non-toxic material approved by the Food and
Drug Administration, as being “Food Grade”, which package shall afford a view
of the contents from all sides of such package, exclusive of the label which
shall not cover more than 5% of such package.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.060 USDA GRADE MARK REQUIRED ON MEAT OR POULTRY.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful to advertise, offer for sale, or sell any
perishable meat or poultry prepackaged or otherwise, except processed meats and
poultry such as sausage, luncheon meat, smoked or cooked meat, poultry rolls or
canned poultry, unless it has one of the grade marks established by the U.S.
Department of Agriculture official grading standards, as follows:

   (B)   Failure to have such grade marks in the advertisement and on the

(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.061 GENETICALLY ENGINEERED FOOD.
   (A)   As used in this section, GENETICALLY ENGINEERED FOODS means any food
product that is or contains material that has been genetically engineered
through such techniques as recombinant DNA techniques, cell fusion or
somaclonal variation.
   (B)   (1)   Whenever a food purveyor establishment displays for sale to the
general public genetically engineered foods, the establishment shall post and
maintain in a prominent location near the display a sign that meets the
requirements of this section.
      (2)   The sign shall state the following: “This Food Product Has Been
Genetically Engineered”. The Director of the Department of Revenue may
promulgate rules regulating the size and placement of the type applicable to
signs required by this section.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.062 FRESH BERRIES AND SMALL FRUITS.
   All fresh berries, cherries, currants and other small fruits sold or offered
for sale in the village shall, in the absence of a special agreement in writing
signed by the parties thereto to the contrary, be sold, if in bulk, by standard
avoirdupois net weight, or by numerical count, or in uniform size baskets,
boxes or other receptacles containing one quart or one pint standard dry
measure or multiples thereof, and in no other way. The said receptacles shall
be uniformly and evenly filled throughout said baskets, boxes or other
receptacles in which or out of which such small fruits are sold or offered for
sale shall not be required to be tested and sealed, but the Inspector of
Weights and Measures, or any Inspector Deputies, may at any time test the
capacity of the basket, box or other receptacle in which, or out of which, said
berries, cherries, currants or other small fruits are sold or offered for sale.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.063 NET QUANTITY ON PACKAGES REQUIRED.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful to keep for the purpose of sale or to offer or
expose for sale, or sell, any commodity in package form unless the net quantity
of the contents is plainly and conspicuously marked on the outside of the
package, in terms of weight, measure or numerical count; provided, however,
that, reasonable variations or tolerances shall be permitted, and that these
reasonable variations or tolerances and exemptions shall be those established
by rules and regulations made and promulgated by the Director of Agriculture of
the state; and, provided further that, this section shall not be construed to
apply to those commodities in package form, the manner of sale of which is
specifically regulated by other provisions of this code.
   (B)   For the purpose of this section, the following definitions apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
      IN PACKAGE FORM.
         (a)   A commodity in a package, carton, case, can, box, barrel,
bottle, vial or other receptacle, or in coverings or wrappings of any kind, put
up by the manufacturer, or when put up prior to the order of the commodity, by
the vendor, which may be labeled, branded or stenciled, or otherwise marked, or
which may be suitable for labeling, branding or stenciling, or marking
otherwise, making one complete package of commodity.
         (b)   IN PACKAGE FORM shall be construed to include both the wholesale
and the retail package.
      PACKAGE. Does not include any container in which are packed or contained
packages of a smaller size of a commodity, but this section applies only to the
container directly enclosing the commodity.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.064 REPACKAGING FRUIT AND VEGETABLES.
   Any person selling or offering for sale any fresh or green fruit or
vegetables which have been emptied from and repacked in barrels, boxes, baskets
or other receptacles, shall clearly stamp or write upon the outside of such
barrels, boxes, baskets or other receptacles, in a conspicuous place, the words
“repacked by” and, following such words, the name of the person so re-packing
the said fruit or vegetables.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.065 MILK OR CREAM IN BOTTLES.
   No person shall sell or offer for sale within the village, any milk or cream
in bottles, or in glass jars, unless each of said bottles or glass jars in
which said milk or cream is sold or offered for sale shall have blown into it
or otherwise indelibly and permanently indicated thereon in a legible and
conspicuous manner the capacity thereof: and the Inspector of Weights and
Measures shall have the right at any time to examine any bottle or glass jar in
which milk or cream is sold or offered for sale in the village, or which is
used by any person for the purpose of containing milk or cream to be sold or
offered for sale in order to ascertain whether such bottle or jar is of a
capacity not less than that which it purports to be; provided that, the test of
48 bottles or glass jars to be used for milk or cream sold or offered for sale
containing milk by any person shall be taken by said Inspector, and this
section shall be construed as having been complied with if such number of
bottles or glass jars contain the full capacity herein required; provided
further, however, that, bottles or jars marked “quarter pint” shall contain not
less, than 30 drams; “half pint” not less than 62 drams; “pint” not less than
125 drams; “quart” not less than 252 drams; “three pints” not less than 379
drams; “two quarts” not less than 506 drams; and, provided further that, no
bottle or glass jar shall be considered a legal measure, except for the
distribution, of milk or cream to consumers.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.066 BREAD LOAVES.
   (A)   The standard loaf of bread shall weigh one pound avoirdupois weight.
Every loaf of bread manufactured, procured or kept for sale or sold in the form
of loaves in the city shall be of standard weight or one of the following
weights: one-half of said standard weight, three-quarters of said standard
weight, one and one-quarter times said standard weight, one and one-half times
said standard weight, or multiples of said standard weight. When twin or
multiple loaves are baked, the weight specified in this section shall apply to
each unit of the twin or multiple loaf.
   (B)   The weights specified in this section shall be construed to mean net
weights to be determined by the average weight of at least 12 loaves of any one
unit; provided, however, that, a variation or tolerance of not more than one
ounce per pound in excess or deficiency from the standard unit or marked weight
shall be allowed, and this section will be considered to have been complied
with if the weight of the 12 loaves of the same unit averages out the correct
net weight. Every loaf of bread manufactured, procured or kept for the purpose
of sale, offered or exposed for sale, or sold in the form of loaves in the
village, shall be marked showing the weight of the loaf; and the business name
and address of the maker, baker or manufacturer. If the bread is unwrapped,
this information shall be stated on a label or by pan impression or other
mechanical means, and on wrapped loaves the information shall be stated upon
the wrapper. Each unwrapped loaf of bread, if labeled, shall have affixed
thereon in a conspicuous place, a label of white paper at least one inch
square, or if round, at least one inch in diameter, upon which shall be printed
in black or blue ink in type not smaller or making a less conspicuous letter
than the type commonly known as 12-point, full-face square Franklin Gothic
capital letters and figures, the weight of the loaf. The business name and
address of the maker, baker or manufacturer shall also be printed plainly on
each label. If this information is given by pan impression or other mechanical
means the letters and figures showing the weight shall be plain and legible,
not smaller or making a less conspicuous letter or figure than square full-face
Franklin Gothic capital letters and figures not less than one-half inch in
height in case of wrapped bread the aforesaid information shall be printed
plainly on the wrapper from type not smaller or making a less conspicuous
letter than the type commonly known 24-point, full-face square Gothic capital
letters and figures.
   (C)   The provisions of this section shall not apply to biscuits, buns,
crackers, scones or rolls weighing less than four ounces, nor to what is
commonly known as “stale bread” and sold as such, in case the seller shall at
the time of sale expressly state to the buyer that the loaves of bread so sold
are “stale” bread.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.067 BISCUITS OR ROLLS.
   No biscuits, buns, scones or rolls of bread which weigh less than one ounce
or more than four ounces shall be manufactured, procured, kept for the purpose
of sale, offered or exposed for sale, or sold in the village; provided,
however, that, a variation or tolerance of not more than one ounce per pound in
excess or deficiency from the standard weight shall be allowed, and the
standard weights herein specified shall be determined by averaging the weight
of not less than five dozen biscuits, buns, scones or rolls of bread of any one
unit. This section will be considered to have been complied with if the weight
of not less than five dozen of the same averages out the correct net weight.
Such biscuits, buns, scones and rolls of bread are not required to be labeled.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
PRICING
§ 122.080 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ADVERTISEMENT. Any offer to sell a consumer commodity to the public at
retail by means of any form of public notice, however disseminated or utilized.
   COMPETITIVE PRICING. The use of two prices in advertising the selling price
and the, reference price.
   COMPUTER WAREHOUSE. A warehouse with a data processing system for the
control and distribution of inventory.
   CONSUMER COMMODITY. Any article, product or commodity of any kind or class,
which is produced or distributed for sale retail.
   PERSON. Any individual, association, partnership or corporation.
   REFERENCE PRICE. An advertised price to which a selling price is compared in
advertising which employs comparative pricing. REFERENCE PRICE shall include
the use of terms such as, if perfect, list price, regular price, full price,
retail price, former price or words of similar import.
   SELLING PRICE. The price of which a consumer commodity is sold on an given
date. In the case of commodities weighed by retailers, the SELLING PRICE shall
only be computed by using the price per one pound is the basis for the sale;
provided that, the metric system may be employed where customary.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.081 PRICE MARKING AND DISPLAY.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to display for sale any consumer
commodity unless the selling price is accurately stated in a clear and
conspicuous manner. On any prepackaged consumer commodity, except those sold
through vending machines, the selling price shall be marked directly on the
package.
   (B)   On any consumer commodity which is not prepackaged, the selling price
shall be stated on a sign contiguous to the point of display of the consumer
commodity so priced; provided that, when any consumer commodity is not
prepackaged and is sold out-of-doors, the selling price numerals shall be not
less than three inches in height and one and one-half inches in width and any
fractional numerals shall be not less than one-half the height and width of the
whole numerals.
   (C)   The Director of the Department of Revenue is hereby authorized to
permit the use of alternative price notification procedures which may be of
benefit to the citizens of the village and consumers. The Director of the
Department of Revenue may, in conjunction with such alternative procedures,
exempt classes of persons from the individual pricing requirements of this
section and shall, in such event, adopt rules and regulations consistent with
the objectives of this section to ensure accurate notice to consumers of the
actual selling price of consumer products. Such regulations shall ensure that:
      (1)   The selling price of each consumer commodity is stated in a clear
and conspicuous manner at the location where each such commodity is displayed
for sale;
      (2)   Each sale shall be documented by a receipt given to each purchaser
which shall contain a record of the commodities purchased and the selling price
of each such commodity; and
      (3)   The savings realized by reason of not requiring each individual
pre-packaged commodity to be price-marked shall be passed onto the consumer.
   (D)   No person shall be deemed to comply with such regulations, except
those receiving a certificate from the Director of the Department of Revenue,
after application therefore on such form as the Director of the Department of
Revenue shall prescribe that such person complies with the regulations.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.082 SALES; STATEMENT OF DURATION.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to advertise a “sale” or other temporary
change in prices unless the duration of the sale or other temporary change in
terms of time is disclosed by stating the number of days or termination date;
provided, however, that, where a termination date has been advertised in good
faith, the date may be extended.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.083 REFERENCE PRICE; DISCLOSURE; IDENTICAL, COMPARABLE ARTICLES.
   (A)   Disclosure. It shall be unlawful for any person to advertise a
reference price unless the reference price is disclosed in a clear and
conspicuous manner or can be readily ascertained by disclosure of the dollar,
fraction or percentage reduction in price.
   (B)   Based on sale of identical article. It shall be unlawful for any
person to advertise a reference price based on sales of the identical article
unless the reference price is the actual price at which the article was offered
to the public by the advertiser or by principal competing persons in the
advertiser’s trade area for reasonably substantial period of time in the recent
regular course of business, honestly and in good faith, as determined by
regulations adopted by the Director of the Department of Revenue.
   (C)   Based on sale of comparable article. It shall be unlawful for any
person to advertise a reference price based on sales of a comparable article
unless:
      (1)   The two articles are in fact substantially identical in all
significant respects and such comparability can be established by reference to
generally accepted standards of identity or performance or otherwise; and
      (2)   The reference price of such comparable article is the actual price
at which the article was offered to the public by the advertiser or by
principal competing persons in the advertiser’s trade area for a reasonably
substantial period of time in the recent regular course of business, honestly
and in good faith as determined by regulations adopted by the Director of the
Department of Revenue.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.084 LOWERED PRICES DUE TO UNUSUAL CIRCUMSTANCES.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to advertise in a manner which
expressly or impliedly offers lowered prices on commodities as a result of some
unusual circumstances unless the circumstances are true and the advertised
prices are actually lower than the advertiser’s usual prices.
   (B)   UNUSUAL CIRCUMSTANCES include, but are not limited to, terms such as
“special purchase”, “exceptional purchase”, “clearance”, “manufacturer’s
closeout” and “outdated merchandise”, as the term is defined in §
122.020 of this chapter.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.085 WHOLESALE OR FACTORY PRICES.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to advertise a consumer commodity
for sale by using terms such as “wholesale” or “factory” to describe prices
unless the prices offered to consumers are the same prices as paid by retailers
or as paid by those who purchase directly from the manufacturer or wholesaler
for resale.
   (B)   Location of advertised sale commodity to be readily ascertainable. It
shall be unlawful for any person to advertise a consumer commodity for sale
unless the location of such commodity in the advertiser’s place of business
shall be readily ascertainable by the customer.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999) Penalty, see §
122.999
§ 122.086 COMMODITY UNIT PRICE STANDARDS.
   (A)   (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to offer for sale any of the
commodities listed in this division (A), except items advertised as “sale”
items, unless the unit price information is provided in a clear and conspicuous
manner on a sign or shelf tag which lists the identity and brand name of the
commodity, the quantity declaration of the packaged commodity, the total retail
sales price and the price per unit as set herein below.
Commodities Unit Price Standard
Commodities                             Unit Price Standard
Candy                                   Price per pound
Cereals                                 Price per pound
Cheese, natural and processed           Price per pound
Coffee, tea and cocoa                   Price per pound
Cooking oils and shortening             Price per quart or pound
Deodorants, personal                    Price per ounce
Dry detergents, soap, powders and       Price per pound
cleaners and disinfectants
Foil, film and other rolls of wrapping  Price per 50 sq. ft.

Jellies, preserves and peanut butter    Price per pound

Meat, poultry and sea food              Price per pound

                                        50 units, including ply

Toothpaste                              Price per ounce
 
      (2)   The standard of reference for all categories listed above shall be
the latest edition of the Standard Industrial Classification Manual, published
by the Executive Office of the President, Bureau of the Budget.
      (3)   Any of the consumer commodities listed herein shall be exempt from
these provisions when there is only one brand in only one size appearing in a
retail establishment.
   (B)   The unit price information shall be to the nearest, $0.001 when less
than $1 and to the nearest cent when a dollar or more and shall be presented as
follows:
      (1)   In a retail establishment in which unit price information is
provided in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, that information
shall be displayed by means of a sticker, stamp, sign, label or tag affixed to
the shelf upon which the commodity is displayed, or by means of a sticker,
stamp, sign, label or tag affixed to the consumer commodity itself, stating the
unit price of one or more brands and sizes of a given consumer commodity.
      (2)   Where a sign providing unit price information for one or more sizes
or brands of a given consumer commodity is used, that sign shall be provided
clearly and in a non-deceptive manner in a central location as close as
practical to all items to which the sign refers.
      (3)   If a single sign or tag provides the unit price information for
more than one brand or size of a consumer commodity, then the following
information shall be provided:
         (a)   The identity and the brand name of the consumer commodity;
         (b)   The quantity declaration of the packaged commodity if more than
one package size per brand is displayed;
         (c)   The total retail sales price; and
         (d)   The unit price in accordance with division (A) above.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.087 UNIT PRICE STANDARDS; EXCEPTIONS.
   This section shall not apply to sales at retail by means of vending machines
or by retail establishments that do not have their own computer warehouse
operation or whose annual sales of commodities specified in §
122.086 of this chapter are less than 10% of such establishments total annual
sales.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
§ 122.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person, including any weighmaster or deputy weighmaster, that
shall violate any of the provisions of this chapter shall when no other
specific penalty is herein provided, be fined not less than $10, nor more than
$200, for each offense.
   (B)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.001 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $100,
for each offense.
   (C)   (1)   Any weight, measure, scale, beam, patent balance, steelyards or
other instrument used for weighing that does not conform to the standards of
the state shall be marked “condemned” and the owner thereof shall, within ten
days thereafter, have the same properly adjusted and sealed, as per §
112.003 of this chapter, be subject to a penalty of not more than $10.
      (2)   If any person shall use, maintain or operate in the city in
weighing or measuring, as per §
112.003 of this chapter, any weight, measure, scale beam, patent balance,
steelyard or other instrument which shall not be conformable to the standard of
the state, or shall use in weighing, as aforesaid, any scale beam, patent
balance, steelyard or other instrument which shall be out of order or
incorrect, or which shall not balance, he or she shall be fined for every such
offense not less than $25, nor more than $100.
   (D)   Any weight, measure, scale, beam, patent balances, steelyards or other
instrument used for weighing, as per §
112.004 of this chapter, that does not conform to the standards of this state
shall be marked “condemned” and the owner thereof shall, within ten days
thereafter, have the same properly adjusted and sealed, or be subject to a
penalty of not more than $10 and the Department may at any time after the
expiration of the time aforesaid, seize and destroy any and all such condemned
weights, measures, scales, patent balances, steelyards and other instruments
used for weighing found in use.
   (E)   Any itinerant peddler or hawker found using any ice scale, as per §
122.006 of this chapter, shall be subject to a fine of not less than $10, nor
more than $50, for each offense.
   (F)   Any person violating any of the provisions of § 112.008 of this
chapter shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $100, for each offense.
   (G)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.009 of this chapter shall be fined not less $25, nor more than $200, for
each offense
   (H)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.014 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $50, nor more than $200,
for each offense.
   (I)   Any person, selling and delivering or attempting to deliver any load
lot of any commodity that has been re-weighed on the scale of the public
weighmaster on which it was originally weighed at his or her request, who shall
refuse or fail to allow said load to be delivered to the destination it was
originally billed or sent to, or who shall fail or refuse to have the load,
removed from the vehicle used in the delivery thereof, or who shall hinder or
obstruct the Inspector of Weights and Measures, or any Inspector deputies, from
obtaining and ascertaining the net weight of the commodity delivered or
attempted to be delivered, as per §
122.017 of this chapter, shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $200,
for each offense.
   (J)   (1)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.018(B) of this chapter shall be fined not less than $25, or more than $200,
for each such offense. The penalty provided herein shall be in addition to an
penalty that may be imposed under other relevant sections of this code;
provided that, whenever the re-weighing is done on a scale other than the scale
on which the weighing was originally done, a variance of 1% or less in the net
weight of a load lot between the net weight as set forth in the certificate and
the net weight as ascertained by re-weighing such load shall not be considered
a violation of §
122.018(B) of this chapter.
      (2)   Any person in charge of the conveyance or delivering of any
commodity who shall have in his or her possession or who shall deliver any
false or fraudulent certificate of weight or delivery ticket or any said ticket
or certificate which is not the result of an actual weighting, as per §
122.018(C) of this chapter, shall be fined not less not less $50, nor more than
$200, for each offense.
   (K)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.019 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $500,
for each offense.
   (L)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.021 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $50, nor more than $500,
for each offense.
   (M)   (1)   Any person who shall furnish to any person making or in charge
of a delivery of distillate fuels, or to any person to whom such a delivery is
made, a false or fraudulent delivery ticket or a ticket which does not show the
actual meter measurement of the quantity delivered, as per §
122.037(D) of this chapter, shall, upon conviction, be fined not less than $50,
nor more than $200.
      (2)   Any person failing to seal such adjustable elements or transmit
such notice, as per §
122.037(E) of this chapter, shall be subject to a penalty of not less than $25,
nor more than $200, for each offense.
   (N)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.056 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $200,
for each offense.
   (O)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.058 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $200,
for each offense.
   (P)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.060 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $200,
for each offense.
   (Q)   Any person who owns or controls an establishment that is in violation
of §
122.061 of this chapter shall be subject to a fine of not less than $25, and
not more than $100, for the first offense; not less than $100, and not more
than $250, for the second offense; and not less than $250, and not more than
$500, for a third or subsequent offense. Each day that such violation occurs
shall constitute a separate offense.
   (R)   Any person selling or offering for sale any such small fruits in any
basket, box or other receptacle that is of a capacity different from that
herein before provided, or in any basket, box or other receptacle that is not
uniformly and evenly filled throughout, as per §
122.062 of this chapter, shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $100,
for each offense.
   (S)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.064 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $100,
for each offense.
   (T)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.065 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $2, nor more than $100,
for each offense, and the possession of such bottle or glass jar not so marked
as provided in this section or of a lesser capacity than marked thereon and
used or to be used, or which has been used by such person for the purpose of
containing milk or cream to be sold or offered for sale in the village, shall
constitute a separate and distinct offense.
   (U)   Any person, violating any of the provisions of §
122.066 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $25, nor more than $200,
for each offense.
   (V)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §
122.067 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $50, nor more than $500,
for each offense. Any violation of any of the provisions of §
122.067 of this chapter, in addition to any fine provided for herein, may be
grounds for revocation of any license issued by the village to any such
violator; provided, however, that, nothing herein contained shall be construed
so as to preclude the revocation of any license for violation of any other
provision of this municipal code.
   (W)   Any person violating any of the provisions of §§
122.081 through
122.087 of this chapter shall be fined not less than $50, nor more than $500,
for each offense. Any violation of any of the provisions of §§
122.081 through
122.087 of this chapter, in addition to any fines provided for herein, may be
grounds for revocation of any license issued by the village to any such
violator.
(Ord. 99-111, passed 6-21-1999)
