GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 151.001 CODES ADOPTED.
   (A)   Declaration of purpose.
      (1)   The purpose of this chapter is to establish uniform rules and
regulations for the construction and rehab of buildings, single-family and
duplex homes, including Fire, Electrical, Plumbing, Energy Efficiency and
Property Maintenance Codes, using the (ICC) 2012 Edition, within the corporate
limits of the village.
      (2)   This chapter is not intended, nor shall it be construed, to create
a duty on the part of the village or its officials, employees or agents, to
protect the health, safety or economic interests of any person or entity, and
no person or entity shall have the right to rely on this code, or any action
taken or not taken hereunder, as a basis to assert any claim for any loss,
damage or expense against the village, its officials, employees or agents.
   (B)   Adoption of codes by reference.
      (1)   The Mayor and the Board of Trustees of the village hereby
references the following building codes and amendments thereto. These codes
shall be known as the “Village of Dolton Building Codes” and establish rules
and regulations for the construction of buildings and property maintenance
within the corporate limits of the village. Where any provision of these
building code ordinances conflicts with state law, state law will supersede,
unless provided for within this chapter or the provisions of the adopted codes:
         (a)   International Fire Code (ICC) - 2012 Edition;
         (b)   NEC - National Electric Code - 2011 Edition;
         (c)   International Building Code (ICC) - 2012 Edition;
         (d)   International Residential Code for One- and Two-Family Dwellings
(ICC) - 2012 Edition;
         (e)   International Plumbing Code (ICC) - 2012 Edition;
         (f)   International Mechanical Code (ICC) - 2012 Edition;
         (g)   International Energy Conservation Code - 2012 Edition;
         (h)   International Property Maintenance Code (ICC) - 2012 Edition;
         (i)   International Existing Building Code (ICC) - 2012 Edition; and
         (j)   National Fire Protection Association (NFPA):
            1.   NFPA 13 - Installation of Sprinkler Systems;
            2.   NFPA 72 - National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code - 2013
Edition;
            3.   NFPA 70 - National Electrical Code - 2014 Edition; and
            4.   NFPA 101 - Life Safety Code.
      (2)   The village amendments to these codes are attached to the ordinance
codified herein. A copy of each of the codes with the amendments is on file in
the Village Clerk’s office.
   (C)   Applicability of Building Code. “Name of jurisdiction” shall mean
“Village of Dolton”. The Building Code shall apply in its entirety to all
buildings. In one- and two-family dwellings, the village also requires hard-
wired smoke and carbon monoxide detectors and heat detectors in attached
garages (placed per 2012 Residential Code (ICC)).
   (D)   Legal status. The adoption of this chapter shall not affect any suit
or proceeding now pending in any court, nor shall it affect any legal decision
reached prior to its adoption.
   (E)   Applicable local ordinance and state laws supersede code provisions.
Matters included in the code, but regulated by other applicable local
ordinances or state laws will not be enforced by the Building Department unless
such ordinance or state law requires such enforcement.
   (F)   Building permits. Before beginning any work, except as exempted
elsewhere in this chapter, the owner or his or her authorized agent shall
secure a building permit from the Building Department in accordance with the
applicable Building Code. Upon approval by the Building Department, a permit
card will be issued to the owner. This card shall be posted in a conspicuous
location, visible from the street, for the duration of construction. A building
permit shall be valid for three months. If the project is not completed within
three months, a written request for a one-time extension of the time of
completion shall be submitted to the Building Inspector for approval. If the
project is not completed by the extension date, a new permit must be obtained
for the outstanding work.
   (G)   Amendments to building permits. Any amendment to a building permit
shall be submitted in writing to the Building Department, with appropriate
adjustments to the permit fee. An amendment is required for any changes in
building location, footprint, exiting, exitways, life safety provisions or
significant changes in plumbing, electrical, mechanical and the like. Approval
shall be granted before work is commenced. For other than one- and two-family
dwellings, it shall be the determination of the Planning and Zoning staff
whether the proposed changes merit an amendment to the existing approved permit
or require a new application submission.
   (H)   Work that may be done without a building permit on existing buildings
or structures. Work consistent with § 105.2 (work exempt from permit) of the
International Building Code, or § R105.2 (work exempt from permit) of the
International Residential Code for One- and Two-Family Dwellings.
   (I)   Certificate of occupancy. When a building permit is required on any
building project under this chapter, such building project shall not be used or
occupied, in whole or in part, as provided for in division (F) above, until the
certificate of occupancy/completion shall have been issued by the Building
Department, unless approved in writing. No certificate of occupancy shall be
issued by the Building Department, unless approved in writing. No certificate
of occupancy/completion shall be issued unless there is compliance with this
chapter. A partial/temporary certificate of occupancy/completion, as provided
for in the International Building Code, may be issued for a period not to
exceed 30 days which may be extended at the discretion of the Building
Department. The additional inspections required in order to issue a temporary
certificate of occupancy/completion shall be paid for as established in the
rate and fee schedule adopted by the village.
   (J)   Board of Appeals. The Board of Appeals shall be the Mayor and the
Board of Trustees. Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Building
Department may appeal such decision to the Board of Appeals. The Building Code
Board of Appeals shall have the power, upon an appeal filed with it by any
person aggrieved by a decision of the Building Inspector dealing with the
Building Code, to vary the application of any provision of the Building Code to
any particular case when, in its opinion, the enforcement of the Building Code
would do manifest injustice and would be contrary to the spirit and purpose of
the Building Code and the public interest. Any appeal to the Board of Appeals
shall be taken within 15 days of the date of the decision, except for decisions
that a violation exists. With regard to decisions by the Building Department
that there has been a violation of the Building Code, the applicant and/or
contractor shall have seven days from the receipt of the notice of violation to
appeal the decision of the Building Department. Any person aggrieved by a
decision of the Board of Appeals may appeal such decision to the Markham Court
House.
   (K)   Appendices. The following appendices are attached to the ordinance
codified herein.
      (1)   Appendix A, Application for Building Permit. Application for a
permit shall be made to the Code Official and shall be accompanied by one
complete set of plans and specifications showing the work to be done.
Additional sets of plans shall be provided for, if required by the Building
Department. All plans shall bear the seal of an architect or engineer licensed
by the state, except for single- or two-family residences or any structure
which does not have as its principal structural members reinforced concrete or
structural steel and is two and one-half stories or less and 4,000 square feet
or less in area and is not a building of assembly, church, hospital or school
use.
      (2)   Appendix B, Schedule for Processing Building Permit Applications.
         (a)   Upon submission of a complete application, the Code Official
shall act to approve or deny a building permit within 30 days; provided,
however, that, non-residential applications encompassing more than two dwelling
units shall be approved or denied within 60 days.
         (b)   An application which is incomplete shall be deemed abandoned if
no further action is taken by the applicant within 180 days after the original
filing. All material furnished will be returned to the applicant upon written
request. If construction is not started within 180 days after the date of
approval of the permit, the job will be considered abandoned and 25% of the
building permit fee will be returned to the applicant upon written request. If
an application is withdrawn after code review is conducted, but prior to permit
issuance, 25% of the code review fee will be returned to the applicant upon
written request.
      (3)   Appendix C, Procedures for Handling Non-Compliance.
         (a)   The owner/owner’s representative shall obtain an appointment for
an inspection 24 hours before any work is covered to determine Building Code
compliance. If the Code Official finds work covered the contractor shall, upon
request, uncover the work for inspection. If an owner/contractor is not
available at a scheduled inspection, the owner may be charged a fee as
established in the current rate and fee schedule as adopted by the Mayor and
the Board of Trustees to cover the Building Department costs and will be
required to reschedule immediately the required inspection.
         (b)   If the Code Official determines that work is proceeding without
the required inspections being requested, the building permit will be suspended
and the Code Official shall remove the permit card from the project and no
further work shall be done under the building permit until the suspension has
been lifted. Reinstatement of the building permit will require the contractor
to pay to the Building Department a sum equal to one-half of the original
permit fee or $60, whichever is greater.
         (c)   The provision of this division (K)(3) shall equally apply to the
owner if the owner is performing the work on the building or structure.
(Prior Code, § 8-2A-1) (Ord. 91-150, passed 5-28-1991; Ord. 15-038, passed 7-
24-2015)
§ 151.002 MOVING BUILDINGS.
   (A)   Permit requirements.
      (1)   Permit required. No person shall move any building on, through or
over any street, alley, sidewalk or other public place in the village without
having first obtained a permit from the Building Commissioner.
      (2)   Application for permit. Applications shall state thereon the
proposed route and the number of days it is intended that the building shall
occupy any portion of any street, alley, sidewalk or other public place.
      (3)   Permit fees. Upon the approval of the intended route, a fee of $10
for each day or fraction thereof that it is intended that the building shall
occupy any such portion of any such public place shall be paid and the permit
issued. An additional payment of $5 for each day or fraction thereof over and
above the time stated on the permit, during which any building shall occupy any
such public place, shall be paid.
      (4)   Bond requirements. Every person applying for a permit under this
section shall submit with his or her application a bond in the sum of $50,000,
conditioned on his or her compliance with all the provisions of this section,
and agreeing to pay and holding the village harmless from any judgment, cost
and expense which may be made against it, and conditioned further that the
building moved to the new site shall be completed in accordance with approved
plans and specifications within a period of six months from the date that the
said building is located at the new site. Failure to comply shall forfeit the
bond.
(Prior Code, § 8-12-1)
   (B)   Procedures for moving buildings.
      (1)   Lights and warning devices.
         (a)   Whenever a street or alley is blocked by a house or structure
which is being moved, warnings to that effect shall be placed by the Department
of Streets and Alleys so as to warn vehicles and persons from entering that
portion of the street which is so blocked.
         (b)   The person moving any building through the streets shall keep
warning signs and lanterns or lights at night on the building so as to guard
against any person or vehicle from colliding with it.
      (2)   Utility wires or cables. Whenever it shall be necessary to
interfere with wires or cables of a public utility in moving a building, the
terms of any special or franchise ordinance governing shall apply and the bond
therein specified shall be given.
      (3)   Fire alarm wires. When any such moving building shall approach any
fire alarm wire or pole which shall be endangered by the removal of such
building, it shall be the duty of the mover to notify the Chief of the Fire
Department at least six hours before reaching such wire or pole so that they
may be removed or cared for by the authorities of the village.
(Prior Code, § 8-12-2)
Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.003 DEMOLITIONS.
   (A)   Demolition of open, hazardous residential and commercial buildings.
      (1)   Demolition of hazardous buildings.
         (a)   If a residential or commercial building is three stories or less
in height, and the village’s Chief Building Inspector, upon the advise and
consent of the Housing Department Director and the Fire Chief, determines that
the building is open and vacant and an immediate and continuing hazard to the
community in which the building is located, then the village’s Chief Building
Inspector shall be authorized to post a notice of not less than two feet by two
feet in size on the front of the building. The notice shall be dated as of the
date of the posting and shall state that unless the building is demolished,
repaired or enclosed, and unless any garbage, debris and other hazardous,
noxious, or unhealthy substances or materials are removed so that an immediate
and continuing hazard to the community no longer exists, then the building may
be demolished, repaired or enclosed, or any garbage, debris and other
hazardous, noxious or unhealthy substances or materials may be removed, by the
village.
         (b)   Not later than 30 days following the posting of the notice, the
village’s Housing Department shall do the following:
            1.   Cause to be sent, by certified mail, return receipt requested,
a notice to all owners of record of the property, the beneficial owners of any
state land trust having title to the property, and all lienholders of record in
the property, stating the intent of the village’s Housing Department to
demolish, repair or enclose the building, or remove any garbage, debris or
other hazardous, noxious, or unhealthy substances or materials if that action
is not taken by the owner or owners or lienholders of record;
            2.   a.   Cause to be published, in a newspaper of general
circulation that serves the village, a notice setting forth:
                  i.   The address of the building or description of the real
estate sufficient for its identification;
                  ii.   A statement that the property is open and vacant and
constitutes an immediate and continuing hazard to the community; and
                  iii.   A statement that the village intends to demolish,
repair or enclose the building, or remove any garbage, debris or other
hazardous, noxious or unhealthy substances or materials if the owner or owners
or lienholders of record fail to do so.
               b.   This notice shall be published for three consecutive days.
            3.   Cause to be filed in the office of the Recorder of Deeds and
registrar of titles, a notice setting forth:
               a.   The address of the building or a description of the real
estate sufficient for its identification; and
               b.   A statement that the village’s Housing Department has
initiated an action under this section to cause the demolition, repair or
enclosure of the building or the removal of garbage, debris or other hazardous,
noxious or unhealthy substances or materials located on the property if the
owner or owners or lienholders of record fail to do so.
         (c)   A person objecting to the proposed actions of the village’s
Housing Department may file his or her objection in an appropriate form in a
court of competent jurisdiction.
         (d)   If the building is not demolished, repaired or enclosed, or the
garbage, debris or other hazardous, noxious or unhealthy substances or
materials are not removed, within 30 days of mailing the notice described in
division (A)(1)(b)1. above or within 30 days of the last day of publication of
the notice, whichever is later, the village’s Housing Department shall cause to
be sent, by mail, a final determination to the owners of record, the beneficial
owners of any state land trust having title to the property, and all
lienholders of record in the property, which provides notice that the village’s
Housing Department has determined that the necessary demolition, repair,
enclosure or removal action has not been taken and that the building remains
open and vacant and an immediate and continuing hazard to the community in
which the building is located. The final determination shall include a
statement that, unless a hearing is sought under this section before a court of
competent jurisdiction to object to the proposed actions of the village’s
Housing Department and a copy of the complaint served on the Mayor within ten
days of the mailing of the final determination, the village’s Housing
Department intends to exercise its power to demolish, repair or enclose the
buildings, or to remove any garbage, debris or other hazardous, noxious or
unhealthy substances or materials.
         (e)   The village’s Housing Department may proceed to demolish, repair
or enclose a building or remove any garbage, debris or other hazardous, noxious
or unhealthy substances or materials under this division (A) within a 120-day
period following the date of the mailing of the notice described in division
(A)(1) above if the village’s Chief Building Inspector, upon the advise and
consent of the Housing Department Director and the Fire Chief, determines that
the demolition, repair, enclosure or removal of any garbage, debris or other
hazardous, noxious or unhealthy substances or materials is necessary to remedy
the immediate and continuing hazard. If, however, before the village’s Chief
Building Inspector proceeds with any of the actions authorized by this section,
any person has sought a hearing under this section before a court and has
served a copy of the complaint on the Mayor, then the village shall not proceed
with the demolition, repair, enclosure or removal of garbage, debris or other
substances until the court determines that action is necessary to remedy the
hazard and issues an order authorizing the village to do so.
         (f)   1.   Following the demolition, repair or enclosure of a
building, or removal of garbage, debris or other hazardous, noxious or
unhealthy substances or materials under this division (A), the village may file
a notice of lien against the real estate for the cost of the demolition,
repair, enclosure, or removal within 180 days after the repair, demolition,
enclosure or removal occurred, for the cost and expense incurred, in the
offices of the Recorder of Deeds and Registrar of Titles. The notice of lien
shall consist of a sworn statement setting forth:
               a.   A description of the real estate, such as the address or
other description of the property, sufficient for its identification;
               b.   The expenses incurred by the village in undertaking the
remedial actions authorized by this chapter;
               c.   The date or dates that the expenses were incurred by the
village;
               d.   A statement by the village’s Chief Building Inspector that
the building was open and vacant and constituted an immediate and continuing
hazard to the community;
               e.   A statement by the village’s Chief Building Inspector that
the required sign was posted on the building, that notice was sent by certified
mail to the owners of record and that notice was published in accordance with
this division (A)(1)(f); and
               f.   A statement as to when and where the notice was published.
            2.   The lien authorized by this chapter may thereafter be released
or enforced by the village as provided by state statues.
      (2)   Emergency demolition of hazardous and unsafe buildings.
         (a)   If any building, regardless of whether it is residential,
commercial or industrial, shall be found by the Director of Housing or the Fire
Chief to be in a such a dangerous and unsafe condition to constitute an sever
hazard requiring emergency action, then the Director of Housing or the Fire
Chief shall send written notice to the owner, with proof of delivery, directing
him or her to put such building in a safe condition, to enclose or to demolish
it. Where, upon diligent search, the identify or whereabouts of the owner or
owners of any such building shall not be ascertainable, the notice shall be
mailed to the person or persons in whose name such real estate was last
assessed. If, after 15 days subsequent to the giving of such notice, the owner
fails to put the building in a safe condition, to enclose or to demolish it,
the Housing Director or the Fire Chief may notify the village’s Prosecuting
Attorney and recommend initiation of proceedings in accordance with this
section. Upon receipt of such recommendation, the village’s Prosecuting
Attorney is hereby authorized to apply to the Circuit Court of the county for
an order authorizing the city to demolish, repair or enclose, or requiring the
owner of record to demolish, repair or enclose, the structure. The village’s
Prosecuting Attorney may initiate a court action to obtain the appropriate
order in the Circuit Court of the county to repair, enclose or demolish the
building irrespective of whether a notice as described in this section is sent.
The cost of such demolition, repair or enclosure shall be recoverable from the
owner or owners of such real estate, and shall be a lien thereon as provided by
law.
         (b)   Whenever an emergency exists which requires immediate action to
protect the public health, safety or welfare, the Director of Housing or the
Fire Chief may issue an order, without notice or hearing, directing the owner,
occupant, operator or agent to take appropriate action to correct or abate the
emergency. Nothing in this section prohibits the Director of Housing or the
Fire Chief and/or his or her designee from issuing an emergency demolition
order directing the demolition of a building or structure, or commercial
structure or building that is an imminent threat of danger. The owner,
occupant, operator or agent shall be granted a hearing on the matter upon his
or her request as soon as practicable, but such hearing, in no case, shall stay
the abatement of the emergency.
         (c)   In addition to the actual costs of the abatement, the village
incurs in an action under this section of the village code of ordinances, the
following costs related to the abatement of an emergency under this section
shall be recoverable against the owner(s) of record: mailing costs; fees
related to the recording or releasing of liens; service of process fees; any
attorney fees; and an administrative fee not to exceed $250 reflecting the
resources, including personnel costs, the village expends in abating
emergencies under this section. If payment is not made within 30 days, a lien
shall be recorded with the county’s Recorder of Deeds against the property for
the amount of the costs incurred. The notice of lien shall contain a sworn
statement setting forth:
            1.   A description of the real estate such as the address or other
description of the property sufficient for its identification;
            2.   The expenses incurred by the city in undertaking the remedial
actions authorized under this section;
            3.   The dates the expenses were incurred by the city; and
            4.   A statement by the city official responsible for enforcing the
Building Code that the structure constituted a serious and imminent hazard to
the health and safety of the community.
      (3)   Definitions. For the purpose of this division (A), the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
         COMMERCIAL BUILDING.
            1.   Includes buildings of three stories or less in height, other
than residential buildings, where the whole building or parts thereof are
designed or used as business units, mercantile units, or assembly units;
provided, however, that, COMMERCIAL BUILDING shall not include any building
used entirely as a church, school, library, museum, armory, courtroom or open
air assembly unit.
            2.   COMMERCIAL BUILDING shall also include any other building
where the whole building or parts thereof are designed or used for commercial
purposes, including, but not limited to, a gas filling station, parking
facility, parking garage or motor vehicle repair shop.
         RESIDENTIAL BUILDING. Includes buildings of three stories or less in
height where the whole building or parts thereof are designed or used as
residential units or auxiliary uses to a residential unit, as those terms are
defined herein.
         VACANT. Lacking of habitual presence of human beings who have legal
right to be on the premises or substantially devoid of content. In determining
whether a building or part thereof is VACANT, it is relevant to consider, among
other factors, the percentage of the overall square footage of the building or
floor to the occupied space, the condition and value of any items in the
building and the presence of rental signs on the property.
   (B)   Dangerous garage demolition.
      (1)   (a)   For the purpose of this division (B), the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
            GARAGE. Any stand-alone building, structure, premises or enclosure
within the village, designed primarily for the housing, parking or storage of
five or fewer motor vehicles.
            PUBLIC SAFETY. A garage in a condition that presents an actual and
imminent danger to the public.
         (b)   Such condition may result from, but is not limited to,
structural defects, deterioration or rat or other vermin harborage.
         (c)   Whenever, in the judgment of the village’s Chief Building
Inspector, upon the advice and consent of the Housing Department Director and
the Fire Chief, a garage is a public safety threat, the village’s Housing
Department is authorized to order the garage to be demolished in accordance
with the procedures set forth in division (B)(3) below.
         (d)   Before the village’s Housing Department orders the demolition of
a garage that is a public safety threat, the following procedures shall apply.
            1.   The village’s Housing Department shall first seek to obtain an
affidavit from the owner of the garage, authorizing the village to demolish the
garage.
            2.   In the event that the affidavit specified herein cannot be
obtained, the village’s Housing Department shall, if possible, provide notice
to the owner of the garage by certified mail that the garage will be demolished
within three days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, unless the
owner corrects the conditions creating the public safety threat or seeks a
hearing from the village’s Administrative Hearing Officer. In addition to
providing such mailed notice, if mailed notice is possible, the village’s
Housing Department shall cause the posting of a notice on the garage that the
garage will be demolished within three days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and
legal holidays, unless the owner corrects the conditions creating the public
safety threat or seeks a hearing from the village’s Administrative Hearing
Officer. Such posted notice shall be not less than two feet by two feet in
size.
      (2)   In the event that the owner of the garage fails to correct the
conditions creating the public safety threat or fails to seek a hearing within
three days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, or the provision
of notice provided for in division (B)(1)(d)1. above, the village’s Chief
Building Inspector upon the advise and consent of the Housing Department
Director and the Fire Chief, may provide for the immediate demolition of the
garage.
      (3)   A garage owner seeking a hearing must submit to the village’s
Housing Department a timely written request for a hearing to be conducted by
the village’s Administrative Hearing Officer. Such request shall be deemed
effective when received by the village’s Housing Department, upon receipt of a
timely request for a hearing, the village’s Housing Department shall notify the
Administrative Hearing Officer that an action has been instituted with a
request to conduct a hearing. If, after the hearing, the Administrative Hearing
Officer determines by a preponderance of the evidence that the garage does
constitute a public safety threat, the Administrative Hearing Officer shall
enter an order affirming the determination of the village’s Chief Building
Inspector. If, after the hearing, the Administrative Hearing Officer determines
by a preponderance of the evidence that the garage does not constitute a public
safety threat, the Administrative Hearing Officer shall enter an order
reversing the determination of the village’s Chief Building Inspector. If the
owner of the garage requests a hearing, but fails to appear at the hearing or
fails to request a hearing in a timely manner, the owner shall be deemed to
have waived his or her right to a hearing and the Administrative Hearing
Officer may enter a default order in favor of the village. In the event that an
Administrative Hearing Officer affirms the determination of the village’s Chief
Building Inspector, the village’s Housing Department or its agents or
contractors may enter or access the property and abate the public safety threat
by demolishing the garage in question.
(Ord. 12-567, passed 9-4-2012) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.004 ROOF TEAR-OFFS AND WATER SHIELDS.
   The village hereby amends its adoption of the 2003 Internal Building Code
(IBCO) for residential buildings and the 2003 International Building Code
(IBCO) for commercial buildings to provide that in areas where the average
daily temperature in January is 25°F (-4°C) or less, or when the IBCO
provisions so specifically require, in lieu of normal underlayment, a self-
adhering polymer modified bitumen sheet must be used, and shall extend from the
eave’s edge to a point at least 24 inches (610 mm) inside the exterior wall
line of the building.
(Ord. 06-343, passed 5-15-2006)

BUILDING INSPECTION DEPARTMENT
§ 151.015 DEPARTMENT CREATED.
   There is hereby created the Department of Building Inspection.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-1)
§ 151.016 BUILDING COMMISSIONER.
   (A)   Office created; appointment. There is hereby created the office of the
Building Commissioner of the village who shall be appointed by the President,
by and with the approval of the Board of Trustees.
   (B)   Duties. It shall be his or her duty to see to the enforcement of all
ordinance provisions relating to buildings, zoning or housing and to provide
carpentry maintenance and repair to the municipal buildings of the village.
   (C)   Compensation. The compensation of the Building Commissioner shall be
set annually by the corporate authorities in the annual appropriation
ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-2) (Ord. passed 4-9-1974; Ord. passed 9-3-1974)
§ 151.017 BUILDING INSPECTOR.
   (A)   Appointment, qualifications, term of office. There shall be appointed
by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Board of Trustees,
a Building Inspector. He or she shall be an officer of the village and shall be
under the jurisdiction of the President and Board of Trustees. His or her
appointment shall be until April 30 of each year.
   (B)   Duties. It shall be the duty of the Building Inspector to inspect all
buildings or structures being erected, repaired or altered as frequently as may
be necessary to ensure compliance with this village code.
   (C)   Compensation. The compensation of the Building Inspector shall be set
annually by the corporate authorities in the annual appropriation ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-3)
§ 151.018 ELECTRICAL INSPECTION DIVISION.
   There is hereby established a division within the Building Department which
shall be known as the Electrical Inspection Division, authorized by 65 ILCS 5/
11-37-2 as now or hereafter amended. Such Division shall consist of the
Building Commissioner and the Building Inspector and such other employees as
may be provided from time to time by the corporate authorities.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-4)
§ 151.019 ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR.
   (A)   Office created; appointment; term of office. There is hereby created
the position of Electrical Inspector who shall be appointed by the President
with the advice and consent of the Board of Trustees. His or her term shall
expire on April 30 of each year.
   (B)   Duties.
      (1)   The Electrical Inspector shall make all inspections necessary to
see to the enforcement of all ordinances relating to electricity and no
electric wiring shall be covered until it has been inspected and approved.
      (2)   The Electrical Inspector shall give a certificate of approval to
the owner or person in charge of premises which he or she has inspected where
he or she finds that the electrical apparatus and wiring therein fully comply
with the ordinances of the village.
   (C)   Compensation. The compensation of the Electrical Inspector shall be
set in the annual appropriation ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-5)
§ 151.020 PLUMBING INSPECTOR.
   (A)   Appointment; qualifications; term of office. The Plumbing Inspector
shall be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the
Trustees. No person shall be appointed unless he or she is a resident of the
village and a licensed plumber in accordance with the state’s Plumbers’ License
Law, being 225 ILCS 320/1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended. His or her
appointment shall expire on April 30 of each year.
   (B)   Duties. The Plumbing Inspector shall have immediate supervision of all
work done by plumbers in connection with the plumbing of buildings or
structures in the village and the connecting of such plumbing and drainage with
the sewer and water supply systems of the village. He or she shall investigate
complaints pertaining to the drainage and plumbing of premises; supervise tests
required on both old and new work; and examine all plans as to drainage and
plumbing prior to the issuance of permits for the work proposed to be done. He
or she shall approve such plans if the proposed work in all respects complies
with the requirements of this code and he or she shall point out the
particulars, if any, in which the proposed plans do not conform to the
requirements of this code. He or she shall keep a record of all inspections
made by him or her and shall render a daily report thereof to the Building
Commissioner.
   (C)   Compensation. The compensation of the Plumbing Inspector shall be set
forth in the annual appropriation ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-6)
§ 151.021 ENTRY POWERS.
   The Building Commissioner, the Building Inspector, the Electrical Inspector
and the Plumbing Inspector, in the discharge of their respective duties, shall
have authority to enter any building, structure or premises at any reasonable
hour. Refusal of any person to permit entry to any building, structure or
premises by the Building Commissioner, Building Inspector, Electrical Inspector
or Plumbing Inspector or other village officer as by them designated for the
purpose of inspection as herein provided for, shall be deemed a misdemeanor and
such person, upon conviction of violation of this section, shall be fined.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-7) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.022 STOP WORK ORDERS.
   The Building Commissioner, the Building inspector, the Electrical Inspector
and the Plumbing Inspector shall have the power to order all work stopped on
construction, or alteration, or repair of building in the village when such
work is being done in violation of any provision of any ordinance relating
thereto, or in violation of Ch. 158 of this code of ordinances. Work shall not
be resumed after the issuance of such an order, except on the written
permission of the Building Commissioner; provided, that if the stop work order
is an oral one, it shall be followed by a written stop work order within an
hour. Such written stop order may be served by a police officer.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-8)
§ 151.023 RECORDS KEPT.
   The Building Commissioner, Building Inspector, Electrical Inspector and
Plumbing Inspector shall keep careful and comprehensive records of applications
of permits issued, all inspections made, all reports rendered and all rules and
orders issued. The Building Inspection Department shall retain on file all
permits in connection with building work so long as any part of the building or
structure to which they relate may be in existence. All such records shall be
open to public inspection at reasonable hours, but shall not be removed from
the office of the Building Inspection Department.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-9)
§ 151.024 COOPERATION FROM OTHER VILLAGE OFFICIALS.
   The Building Commissioner, the Building Inspector, the Electrical Inspector
and the Plumbing Inspector may request and shall receive so far as may be
necessary, in the discharge of their duties, the assistance and cooperation of
the Village Engineer in fixing grades, of the Police Department in enforcing
orders, of the Special Prosecuting Attorney in prosecuting violations and of
other village officers and employees.
(Prior Code, § 8-1-10)
BUILDING CODE
§ 151.035 BOCA BASIC BUILDING CODE.
   (A)   There is hereby adopted by the village for the purpose of establishing
rules and regulations for the construction, alteration, removal, demolition,
equipment, use and occupancy, location and maintenance of structures, that
certain Basic National Building Code published by the Building Officials
Conference of America, Inc., as provided for in §
151.001 of this chapter, and from and after the date on which this code shall
take effect the provisions of said Building Code shall be controlling in the
construction of all buildings and other structures contained within the
corporate limits of the village to the extent hereinafter provided.
   (B)   (1)   Whenever the word “municipality” is used in said Building Code,
it shall be held to mean the “Village of Dolton”.
      (2)   Whenever the words “building official” are used in said Building
Code, they shall be held to mean the “Building Commissioner of the Village”.
(Prior Code, § 8-2-1-1) (Ord. passed 5-15-1984)
§ 151.036 BUILDING PERMIT REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Permit required. Before proceeding with the erection, enlargement,
alteration, repair or removal of any building or structure in the village, a
permit for same shall first be obtained by the owner or his or her agent from
the Building Commissioner, and it shall be unlawful to proceed unless such
permit shall first have been obtained from the Building Commissioner.
   (B)   Application for permit; issuance.
      (1)   Application for building permits shall be made by the owner or his
or her agent to the Building Commissioner. When such application is made, a
clear and legible copy of the applicable contract pursuant to which the work is
to be performed and plans in conformity with the provisions of this subchapter,
which have been approved by the Building Commissioner and his or her
assistants, shall be filed with the Commissioner.
      (2)   Any contractor that commences alteration, repair, erection,
enlargement or removal of any building or structure within the village without
first having secured all proper permits shall be subject to, in addition to any
other penalties, the payment of twice the amount of such permits that the
contractor failed to secure prior to commencing work.
   (C)   Building plans.
      (1)   General requirements.
         (a)   The Building Commissioner shall not issue any building permit
unless the plans submitted clearly show that such building or structure with
all its appurtenances, foundations and attachments can be erected entirely
within the limits of the lot or tract of land upon which it is proposed to
erect such building or structure, and no permit shall authorize the use of any
part of any public highway or other public ground for the construction or
maintenance of such building or structure, except as provided by this
subchapter.
         (b)   In all cases, the approved plan, together with building permits,
must be kept on the job while the work is in progress.
         (c)   All such plans and drawings shall be drawn to a scale of not
less than one-eighth inch to the foot, on paper or cloth, in ink, or by some
process that will not fade or obliterate. All distances and dimensions shall be
accurately figured, and drawings made explicit and complete, showing the lot
lines and the location of the exterior lines of the building in relation
thereto, and the entire ventilating, sewerage and drain pipes and the location
of all plumbing fixtures within such building. Each set of plans presented
shall be approved by the Building Commissioner before a permit is granted. No
permit shall be granted or plans approved unless such plans are made and signed
by such persons as are permitted, under the laws of the state, to make plans
for buildings, as provided in An Act to Provide for the Licensing of Architects
and Regulating the Practice of Architecture as a Profession in the State of
Illinois, approved 6-24-1919, being 225 ILCS 305/1 et seq. as now or hereafter
amended, or in An Act to Provide for the Licensing of Structural Engineer,
approved 6-24-1919, being 225 ILCS 340/1 et seq. as now or hereafter amended.
      (2)   Architect or engineer to certify plans. It shall be unlawful for
any architect or structural engineer or other person, permitted under the laws
of the state to make drawings and plans, to prepare or submit to the Building
Commissioner for his or her approval, any final drawings or plans for any
building or structure which does not comply with the requirements contained in
this code. The Building Commissioner shall require that all drawings and plans
submitted for approval be accompanied by a certificate of such architect or
structural engineer preparing such drawing and plans, and that such drawings
and plans have the architect’s or structural engineer’s licensed seal stamped
on the drawings submitted.
      (3)   Alterations to and deviations from plans. It shall be unlawful to
erase, alter or modify any lines, figures or coloring contained upon such
drawings so stamped by the Building Commissioner or filed with him or her for
reference. If, during the progress of the execution of such work, it is desired
to deviate in any manner affecting the construction or other essentials of the
building from the terms of the application or drawing, notice of such intention
to alter or deviate shall be given to the Building Commissioner, and his or her
written assent shall first be obtained before such alteration or deviation may
be made; but alterations in building which do not involve any change in their
structural parts or of their stairways, elevators, fire escapes or other means
of communication or ingress or egress or in lighting or ventilation, and that
are not in violation of any of the provisions of this chapter and the zoning
requirements may be made without the permission of the Building Commissioner.
      (4)   Plan review required. The Building Commissioner or designee shall
review all plans and the fees for such plan review are established as follows:
 
Commercial/business new construction plan fee    $20
Residential new construction plan fee            $15
Remodeling existing commercial/business plan fee $15
Remodeling existing residential plan fee         $10
 
   (D)   Compliance with water and street regulations. Before the Building
Commissioner issues a permit, he or she shall require evidence from the
applicant that payment has been made to the Water Department of the village for
the water to be used or for a water meter for measuring all the water to be
used in the construction of such building. Such applicant shall produce
evidence that he or she has complied with all the requirements of this code
relative to water regulations and shall produce evidence that he or she has
complied with all the requirements of this code as to use of the streets and
alleys of the village by reason of any proposed obstruction or occupation
thereof in and about such building operations.
   (E)   Time limit for construction; extended permits. If, after the permit
required by division (A) above shall have been granted, the operations called
for by the permit shall not be begun within 90 days or are not completed within
one year, then such permit shall be void, and no operations thereunder shall be
begun or completed until an extended permit shall be taken out by the owner or
his or her agent. A fee of 10% of the original cost of permit shall be charged
for such extended permit.
   (F)   Revocation of permits; reissuance. If the work in, upon or about any
building or structure shall be conducted in violation of any of the provisions
of this village code, the Building Commissioner shall revoke the permit of the
building or wrecking operations in connection with which such violation shall
have taken place. It shall be unlawful, after the revocation of such permit, to
proceed with such building or wrecking operations unless such permit shall
first have been reinstated or reissued by the Building Commissioner. Before a
permit so revoked may be lawfully reissued, the entire building and building
site shall first be put into condition corresponding with the requirements of
this village code, and any work or material applied to the same in violation of
this village code shall be first removed from such building, and for such
permit as reissued, the fee required for a new permit shall be paid.
   (G)   Exemptions from permit requirements.
      (1)   A permit will not be required for ordinary repair work incidental
to the upkeep of a building or structure; provided, there is not contemplated
or involved, any change in the classification or any increase in the fire
hazard thereof; nor the removal or installing of any external wall; nor the
removal of any supporting wall, column, post, truss, girder or beam; nor
installing, closing or changing any stair, stair-hall, fire escape, scuttle,
skylight, door, window or other means of communication, ingress, egress,
ventilation or for the admission of sunlight; nor changing the number, location
or connections of the fixtures, traps, vents, waste, soil or drain pipes of the
plumbing system; nor changing the number, location or connections of the
fixtures of the lighting system; nor changing to a different system of lighting
or ventilating; nor recovering of roofs or the renewing of the exterior
woodwork of any frame building, structure or portion thereof.
      (2)   Nothing in this section contained shall be interpreted or construed
to allow any work included in the permit exemptions thereof to be done in any
manner contrary to the requirements of this village code. Violations of this
subchapter in any work not required to be done under a permit shall be subject
to the general penalty provisions of this code the same as if a permit had been
required.
      (3)   Before such repairs shall be made, notification thereof by the
contractor shall be filed with the Building Commissioner if the cost of such
work exceeds $100.
   (H)   Temporary building permits. For the purpose of facilitating the
commencement of lawful building operations, the Building Commissioner may
authorize such operations to commence and proceed for such limited time, not
exceeding 20 days, as the Building Commissioner may deem and fix as sufficient
to allow the owner, his or her architect or agent to complete the filing of
detailed plans and other data required for the issuance of the final permit.
Temporary permits will be revocable at the will of the Building Commissioner.
In case new buildings or structures are to be erected, the work shall not be
carried above the level of the grade line, nor above the level of the first
tier of girders, beams, floor joists or first floor proper. The applicant for a
temporary permit shall furnish the Building Commissioner with sufficient
preliminary plans and data to enable the Building Commissioner to determine
that the work to be commenced and proposed subsequently to be done is of a
lawful nature. The applicant shall pay to the village as a fee for a temporary
permit the sum provided in §
151.038 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 8-2-2) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.037 ANNUAL INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   Annual inspections for certain buildings. The Building Commissioner
and his or her assistants shall make an annual inspection of all theaters and
places of amusement, worship, instruction or entertainment, and also of all
other buildings over two stories in height, except residences. It shall be the
duty of every owner, agent, lessee or occupant of any such building, as is
referred to in this section, to permit the making of such inspection by the
Building Commissioner or by a duly authorized building inspector at any time
upon demand being duly made.
   (B)   Inspection results; remedies. Where the result of such inspection
shall show that such building fails in any respect to comply with the
requirements of this village code, the Building Commissioner shall notify the
owner, agent, lessee or occupant of such building to this effect and shall
specify wherein such building fails to comply with the requirements of this
village code, and it shall thereupon become the joint and several duty of such
owner, agent, lessee or occupant to proceed forthwith to make whatever changes
or alterations may be necessary to make such building comply in all respects
with the requirements of this village code and to complete such changes and
alterations within 30 days after the receipt of such notice.
   (C)   Inspection fee; exemptions. Upon making such annual inspection, it
shall be the duty of the owner to pay to the Village Collector an annual
inspection fee for the same as prescribed in §
151.038 of this chapter; provided, however, that, no charge for such inspection
shall be made against religious, charitable or educational institutions.
(Prior Code, § 8-2-3)

§ 151.039 ADDITIONAL CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATIONS.
   (A)   Multiple-family dwelling units. In addition to the requirements for
apartments as set forth in the Basic Building Code, the following requirements
shall prevail.
      (1)   Face brick is required on all sides of the multiple-family dwelling
units.
      (2)   Concrete flooring shall be provided in all multiple-family dwelling
units.
      (3)   On all solid masonry buildings, all outside walls are to be
insulated with one-inch approved insulation material.
   (B)   Single-family dwelling units. In addition to the requirements for
single-family dwelling units as set forth in the Basic Building Code, the
following shall prevail.
      (1)   The front of each structure shall be of face brick, ornamental
brick or stone, or a combination thereof.
      (2)   The building shall be constructed of a minimum of 50% masonry. No
hollow siding shall be permitted on the balance of the exterior. Only backed
siding shall be allowed.
      (3)   On all solid masonry buildings, all outside walls are to be
insulated with one-inch approved insulation material.
(Prior Code, § 8-2-5)
§ 151.040 SECURITY LOCKING SYSTEMS.
   (A)   Definition. A KEY BOX SYSTEM is a rapid-entry key access system
designed to permit emergency personnel access to a building, which is installed
by the owner of the building in a location on the building as directed by this
section and containing the items as directed by this section.
   (B)   Security locking system required. All buildings, regardless of use or
occupancy, except residential buildings having less than five dwelling units,
which contains two or more separate use and occupancy units; and when access to
or within a structure or an area is unduly difficult because of secured
openings and where immediate access is necessary for life saving or
firefighting purposes, shall have installed an approved key box system.
   (C)   Approval of systems. The Chief of the Fire Department shall review and
approve the type of key box system for use within the village, subject to the
approval of the Village President and Board of Trustees; except that, there
shall be no more than two types of key box systems approved.
   (D)   Location of key box. The Chief of the Fire Department shall require a
key box system to be installed in an accessible location as follows: the
approved key box shall be mounted on the exterior of the building not more than
three feet from the front entrance door, at a height of not more than ten feet
above ground level.
   (E)   Contents of key box. Key boxes shall contain:
      (1)   Keys to locked points of ingress, whether on the interior or
exterior of such buildings;
      (2)   Keys to locked mechanical rooms;
      (3)   Keys to locked electrical rooms;
      (4)   Keys to elevator controls; and
      (5)   Keys to other areas as directed by the Chief of the Fire
Department.
   (F)   Application and effect of provisions.
      (1)   This section shall apply to both new construction and existing
buildings located in the village.
      (2)   Time of application of the requirements established in this section
shall be as follows:
         (a)   Immediately as to all new construction for which a final
certificate of occupancy has not yet been issued as of the effective date
hereof; and
         (b)   One year from the effective date hereof as to all existing
buildings.
(Prior Code, § 8-2-6) (Ord. passed 1-4-1983)
§ 151.041 SMOKE DETECTORS.
   (A)   Smoke detectors required.
      (1)   Every single-family dwelling unit and existing multiple-family
dwelling unit, as defined by the Basic Building Code published by the Building
Officials Conference of America, Inc., as adopted by §
151.035 of this chapter, shall have installed therein approved smoke detectors.
      (2)   Not less than one smoke detector, of an approved type, as described
in division (C) below, shall be installed on every level of a dwelling unit.
Smoke detectors shall also be located in each hallway, stairway, and within ten
feet of each sleeping area on each level of the dwelling.
   (B)   Installation and number of detectors.
      (1)   The smoke detectors shall be installed on the ceiling and at least
12 inches from any wall, or on a wall located 12 inches from the ceiling, and
within ten feet of all rooms used for sleeping purposes, with not less than one
approved smoke detector per living level containing a habitable room or
unenclosed heating plant.
      (2)   Every owner, manager or agent of any building, as described in
division (A) above, shall install in every dwelling unit not less than one
approved smoke detector on the uppermost ceiling, not less than 12 inches from
any wall, or on a wall located 12 inches from the uppermost ceiling of all
interior stairwells, with not less than one detector per living level
containing a habitable room or unenclosed heating plant.
   (C)   Standards for smoke detectors.
      (1)   All approved smoke detectors required in this section shall be the
ionization or photoelectric type, either battery-powered or hard wire 110 volt
AC and shall comply with all the requirements of the Underwriters Laboratories,
Inc. Standard UL 217 (Standard for Safety-Single and Multiple Station Smoke
Detectors) (1976) 2nd Edition, 10-4-1978, as revised 5-19-1983.
      (2)   Smoke detectors shall be the label of a nationally recognized
standards testing laboratory that indicates that the smoke detectors have been
tested and listed under the requirements of UL 217 (1976) 2nd Edition, 10-4-
1978, as revised 5-19-1983.
   (D)   Testing and maintenance in multiple-unit buildings.
      (1)   In a multiple-unit building, the owner shall be responsible for
testing and maintaining detectors in common stairwells.
      (2)   It shall be the responsibility of the tenant to provide and
maintain functional batteries for each detector test and maintain detectors
within dwelling units and to notify the owner or authorized agent in writing of
any deficiencies.
      (3)   The owner shall be responsible for providing each tenant with
written information regarding detector testing and maintenance.
   (E)   Tampering with detectors. It shall be unlawful for any person to
remove batteries or in any way make inoperable smoke detectors as provided for
in this section; except that, this provision shall not apply to any building
owner or manager or his or her agent in the normal procedure of replacing
batteries.
   (F)   Effect of provisions.
      (1)   Multiple-family dwellings. Smoke detectors required by this section
shall be installed within three months from the effective date hereof in all
multiple dwellings, as defined herein.
      (2)   Single-family dwellings. Smoke detectors required in single-family
dwellings, as defined herein, shall be installed within six months from the
effective date hereof.
(Prior Code, § 8-2-7) (Ord. passed 4-3-1985; Ord. 91-155, passed 5-28-1991)
Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.042 WRECKING BUILDINGS.
   (A)   Permit required. It shall be unlawful to proceed with the wrecking or
tearing down of any building or other structure without a permit for such
wrecking or tearing down first being obtained by the owner or his or her agent
from the Building Commissioner.
   (B)   Application for permit; issuance. Application for such permit shall be
made by such owner or his or her agent to the Building Commissioner who shall
issue such permit upon such application and the payment of the fee provided for
in this subchapter.
   (C)   Bond requirements. Before any permit is issued granting authority to
wreck a building or structure for which such permit is required, the person
engaged in the work of wrecking same shall file with the Building Department a
bond of $20,000 with sureties to be approved by the President and Board of
Trustees to indemnify, keep and save harmless the village against any loss,
cost, damage, expense, judgment or liability of any kind whatsoever which the
village may suffer or which may accrue against, be charged to or be recovered
from the village or any of its officials, from or by reason or on account of
accidents to persons or property during any such wrecking operations. Such bond
in each case shall extend over the period of and cover all such wrecking
operations.
   (D)   Supervision; requirements and restrictions. Upon the issuance of such
permit, such building may be wrecked or torn down; provided that, all the work
done thereunder shall be subject to the supervision of the Building
Commissioner and to such reasonable restrictions as he or she may impose in
regard to elements of safety and health; and, provided further that, the work
shall be kept sprinkled and sufficient scaffolding be provided to ensure safety
to human life.
(Prior Code, § 8-2-8)
§ 151.043 OUTSIDE BURGLARY SECURITY WINDOW BARS.
   (A)   Every owner or occupant of any building or structure utilized for
business, industrial or commercial purposes, within the village, shall not
permit bars, grills, roller shutters or other similar security devices to be
attached, hung, affixed or otherwise connected to the outside of windows.
   (B)   The provisions of this section shall apply to all buildings or
structures in which all or any part of the buildings or structures are utilized
for business, industrial or commercial purposes, except those buildings and
structures which are utilized for warehousing purposes.
   (C)   Every owner or occupant of a building or structure in which all or any
part of said building or structure are utilized for business, industrial or
commercial purposes which shall be in violation of these provisions shall have
90 days from the effective date of this section to comply with the provisions
of this section.
(Ord. 97-339, passed 7-21-1997) Penalty, see §
151.999
ELECTRICAL CODE
§ 151.055 SHORT TITLE.
   This subchapter may be cited as the “Electrical Code of the Village of
Dolton”.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-1)
§ 151.056 CHICAGO ELECTRICAL CODE.
   (A)   Code adopted; interpretation.
      (1)   The Chicago Electrical Code, 1985 edition, is hereby adopted by
reference, pursuant to authority of Illinois Revised Statutes; provided that,
in the event any of the provisions of the Chicago Electrical Code are in
conflict with the state law or with any other ordinance of the village, the
state law and such other village ordinance shall prevail.
      (2)   In addition to the three copies of the Chicago Electrical Code
which have been on file for more than 30 days in the office of the Village
Clerk for use and examination by the public and which are presently on file in
the office of the Clerk, at least one copy of the Chicago Electrical Code shall
be kept on file in the office of the Building Commissioner for public
inspection.
   (B)   Penalties. Whoever violates any of the provisions of the Chicago
Electrical Code edition adopted by this section shall, upon conviction thereof,
be punished by a fine in accordance with §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-2) (Ord. passed 5-15-1984) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.057 ELECTRICAL PERMITS.
   No electrical equipment shall be installed or altered except upon a permit
issued by the Electrical Inspection Division. The Electrical Inspection
Division shall issue permits for such installation and alteration of electrical
equipment in all cases where application for such permits shall be made in
accordance with the rules and regulations applicable thereto; provided,
however, that, no permit shall be issued for installation or altering by
contract, electrical equipment, unless the person applying for such permit is
registered in this or another municipality and bonded as an electrical
contractor as required by this village code, and plans and specifications have
been approved by the Electrical Inspection Division.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-3)
§ 151.058 INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   Notice requesting inspection required; failure to request inspection.
Any person installing electric wires or equipment in any building in the
village which is to be hidden from view, shall notify the Building Commissioner
or assistant, in writing, of such intended installation at least 24 hours
before the work is to be covered, and no such work shall be covered until
inspection thereof has been made as herein required. In all cases where such
notice has not been given or such work has been covered without inspection
thereof, as herein provided, the Building Commissioner or assistant is
authorized to take down or remove such portions of the building or structure as
shall be necessary for the inspection of such electric wires or equipment, as
herein required, and the cost of such taking down and replacing the work so
removed by such official shall be borne by the person who has failed to give
notice of the installation thereof, or by the person who has covered the work
after such notice and before inspection thereof as herein provided, as the case
may be.
   (B)   Certificate of inspection. Whenever any electrical equipment has been
installed or altered, no electrical current shall be supplied to or used on
such equipment previous to the inspection of such equipment by the Electrical
Inspection Division and the issuance of a certificate of inspection covering
such installation or alteration; provided that, the Inspection Division may
issue a temporary certificate for the use of electrical current during the
course of construction or alteration of buildings, which temporary certificate
shall expire when the construction or alteration of such building is complete.
   (C)   Entry powers. The Electrical Inspector and his or her assistants shall
have the power to enter buildings or premises at any reasonable hour in the
discharge of their duties, and it shall be competent for them when necessary to
remove any existing obstructions such as laths, plastering or boarding which
may prevent a perfect inspection of the electrical equipment.
   (D)   Interference with Electrical Inspector. It shall be unlawful for any
person to interfere with the Electrical Inspectors in the performance of their
duties.
   (E)   Police to assist Electrical Inspectors. Whenever, in the opinion of
the Electrical Inspector, it shall be necessary to call upon the Police
Department for aid and assistance in carrying out or enforcing any of the
provisions of this subchapter governing the inspection of electrical equipment,
he or she shall have the authority to do so, and it shall be the duty of any
member of the Department of Police, when called upon by the Electrical
Inspector, to act according to the instructions of and to perform such duties
as may be required by the Chief Electrical Inspector in order to enforce or put
into effect the provisions of this subchapter relating to the inspection of
electrical equipment.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-4) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.059 FEES.
   (A)   Inspection fees.   
      (1)   The fees for the inspection of wiring of any buildings or of any
electrical apparatus to be paid to the village shall read as follows.
      (2)   The term CIRCUIT, as used herein, shall mean any set of branch
lighting conditions which have been extended from a distribution center, and
which may be utilized for the transmission of electrical energy.
         (a)   Except in single-family dwellings (division (A)(6) below), the
inspection fee of each nominal 15-ampere and 20-ampere, two-wire circuit,
including fixtures, sockets or receptacles, shall be:
 
Circuits      15 Amperes                    20 Amperes
26 - 50       $3 each additional circuit    $3.50 each additional circuit
51 - 75       $2.50 each additional circuit $3.25 each additional circuit
76 - 100      $2.25 each additional circuit $3 each additional circuit
More than 100 $2 each additional circuit    $2.90 each additional circuit
 
         (b)   For the inspection of a 50-ampere fixed lighting circuit, the
inspection fee shall be three times the amount of a 15-ampere circuit.
      (3)   For the inspection of each two-wire branch lighting circuit,
including fixtures, sockets or receptacles, the fee shall be as provided in
division (A)(2) above.
         (a)   For each three-wire circuit of nominal 15-ampere or 20-ampere,
the fee shall be based on double the number of circuits as provided in division
(A)(2) above.
         (b)   For each three-phase four-wire circuit of capacities of nominal
15-ampere and 20- ampere capacities, the fee shall be three times the number of
circuits as provided in division (A)(2) above.
         (c)   For the inspection of additional outlets on existing circuits
and including the fixtures, sockets or receptacles attached to such outlets,

each of the next 25 lamps; 150 for each of the next 25 lamps; 120 for each of

§ 151.060 DEAD OR DEFECTIVE WIRES.
   (A)   Dead wires. The Building Commissioner shall have the right to cause
all dead wires outside and inside of buildings to be removed at the expense of
the owner of such wires, by giving the owner ten days’ written notice so to do
and, if the owner fails or neglects to remove such wires within ten days after
receipt of such notice, such person shall be subject to a fine of not less than
$5, nor more than $50 for each and every 48 hours such wires are permitted to
remain in place after expiration of the time fixed in such notice for the
removal of same as aforesaid.
   (B)   Defective wires. The Building Commissioner shall have the right to
condemn wires which are defective and dangerous to life or property, and shall
notify the owner of such wires, in writing, to remove or replace the same with
new wires.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-6) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.061 DEFECTIVE WORK.
   (A)   In case the Electrical Inspector or his or her assistants find a
defect in any electrical apparatus or equipment subject to inspection in the
village, such Inspector shall report the same in writing to the persons for
whom the test is being made, using blanks furnished by the village for that
purpose and giving a description of the character of the defect. If the defect
is of a dangerous character, necessitating immediate repair, the Electrical
Inspector shall forthwith condemn the apparatus or equipment for further use,
or until the same is removed, repaired or renewed.
   (B)   If the defect is of a character such that the apparatus or equipment
may be safely operated for a period of some days pending repairs, the
Electrical Inspector shall so report and name the number of days during which
the same may be operated.
   (C)   A duplicate of all such reports shall be promptly filed in the office
of the Building Commissioner.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-7)
§ 151.062 ELECTRICAL CONTRACTORS TO BE LICENSED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of electrical
contractor without being licensed as an electrical contractor.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-8) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.063 NON-LIABILITY OF VILLAGE.
   Any official or employee of the village charged with the administration or
enforcement of this code and acting for the village in the discharge of such
duties shall not thereby be rendered liable personally, and is hereby relieved
of all personal liability, for any and all damage that may accrue to persons or
property as a result of any act required or permitted under the provisions of
this code, and any suit or legal action brought against any official or
employee because of any act performed in the administration or enforcement of
the provisions of this code shall be defended by the Village Attorney until
final termination of the proceedings, and the village shall assume any and all
financial liability thereof.
(Prior Code, § 8-3-9)
PLUMBING CODE
§ 151.075 BOCA BASIC PLUMBING CODE.
   (A)   Code adopted.
      (1)   There is hereby adopted by the village for the purpose of
establishing rules and regulations for the design and installation of plumbing
systems that certain Basic National Plumbing Code published by the Building
Officials Conference of America, Inc., as provided for in §
151.001 of this chapter, and from and after the date on which this code shall
take effect, the provisions of said Plumbing Code shall be controlling in the
design and installation of all plumbing systems contained within the corporate
limits of the village to the extent hereinafter provided.
      (2)   (a)   Whenever the word “Municipality” is used in said Plumbing
Code, it shall be held to mean the “Village of Dolton”.
         (b)   Whenever the words “plumbing official” are used in said Plumbing
Code, they shall be held to mean the “Building Commissioner of the Village”.
   (B)   Amendments to code. The “Fee Schedule” and “Means of Appeal” sections
are hereby entirely deleted from the Basic National Plumbing Code.
   (C)   Application of code provisions. This code is applied to all plumbing,
drain laying and gas fitting done in connection with the construction,
alteration or repairing of any and all buildings, structures or partitions
thereof in the village and same shall be performed by a licensed plumbing
contractor as required by this code.
   (D)   Plumbing systems. There is hereby adopted by the village for the
purpose of establishing rules and regulations for the design and installation
of plumbing systems, the Illinois Plumbing Code as provided for in 77 Ill. Adm.
Code part 890 (1993), and from and after the date on which this code shall take
effect, the provisions of said Plumbing Code shall be controlling in the design
and installation of all plumbing systems contained within the corporate limits
of the village.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-1) (Ord. passed 5-15-1984; Ord. 94-269, passed 11-1-1994)
§ 151.076 PLUMBING PERMITS.
   (A)   Permit required; restrictions. No plumbing equipment including fire
sprinkler system or stand pipe shall be installed or altered, except upon a
permit first issued by the Building Department. The Building Department shall
issue permits for such installation and alteration of equipment in all cases
where application for such permits shall be made in accordance with the rules
and regulations applicable thereto; provided, however, that, no permit shall be
issued for installing or altering by contract such equipment unless the person
applying for such permit is licensed and bonded as a plumbing contractor as
required by this village code and plans and specifications have been approved
by the Building Department.
   (B)   Delay in work; permit revoked. Unreasonable delay in the performance
of any plumbing or draining work shall be deemed a sufficient cause for the
suspension of the license of any such offending plumber. Such plumber shall be
served with a notice granting a period of 48 hours in which to commence or
complete such work. Failure to comply with such notice shall be sufficient
cause for the cancellation of any permit or permits which may have been issued
to said plumber. A new permit may then be issued to any other qualified firm or
person for the work.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-2)
§ 151.077 PLANS AND DRAWINGS.
   (A)   The plans and drawings filed with the Building Commissioner shall show
the entire sewerage, drain, soil, waste, vent and supply pipes and the
locations of plumbing fixtures, water meter and such other details as may be
required within the building or structure. In submitting plans for additional
or reconstruction work, the old or original shall be indicated in black or blue
lines and the new, additional or reconstruction work by red lines.
   (B)   All sizes of pipes and traps shall be plainly marked.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-3)
§ 151.078 INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   Certificate of inspection.
      (1)   The Building Department shall inspect all plumbing installed or
altered, and shall require that it conform to the standards and specifications
applicable thereto and adopted as aforesaid, and upon completion of such
installation or alteration in compliance with such standards and
specifications, shall immediately issue a certificate of inspection covering
such installation or alteration.
      (2)   Whenever any plumbing has been installed or altered, none of said
equipment shall be turned on previous to the inspection of such equipment by
the Building Department and the issuance of a certificate of inspection
covering such installation or alteration; provided that, the Building
Department may issue a temporary certificate for the use of such equipment
during the course of construction or alteration of buildings which temporary
certificate shall expire when the construction or alteration of such building
is complete.
   (B)   Entry powers. The Plumbing Inspector and his or her assistants shall
have the power to enter buildings or premises at any reasonable hour in the
discharge of their duties, and it shall be competent for them, when necessary,
to remove any existing obstructions such as laths, plastering, boarding or
partitions which may prevent a perfect inspection of the equipment.
   (C)   Interference with plumbing inspectors. It shall be unlawful for any
person to interfere with the Plumbing Inspectors in the performance of their
duties.
   (D)   Police to assist Plumbing Inspectors. Whenever, in the opinion of the
Plumbing Inspector, it shall be necessary to call upon the Police Department
for aid and assistance in carrying out or enforcing any of the provisions of
this subchapter governing the inspection of plumbing installations, he or she
shall have the authority to do so, and it shall be the duty of any member of
the Department of Police, when called upon by the Plumbing Inspector to act
according to the instructions of and to perform such duties as may be required
by the Building Committee in order to enforce or put into effect the provisions
of this subchapter relating to the inspection of plumbing installations.
   (E)   Reinspections.
      (1)   The Building Department is hereby empowered to reinspect any
plumbing installations and when such installations are found to be unsafe to
life or property, shall notify the person owning, using or operating same to
place the same in a safe and secure condition and in compliance with the
standards and specifications described herein within such time as the Building
Department shall consider just and reasonable.
      (2)   Upon refusal or willful failure to comply with the requirements of
such notifications, in addition to the penalties otherwise provided herein, the
Building Department may order and compel the cutting off and stopping of such
plumbing installations until such plumbing installations have been placed in a
safe and secure condition and in compliance with the standards and
specifications referred to herein.
      (3)   No inspection fee shall be charged for such reinspection, but in
case it becomes necessary to replace such plumbing installations on account of
defects disclosed by such reinspection, a permit therefor shall be obtained and
an inspection fee paid as provided for in §
151.079 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-4)
