§ 151.082 FIXTURES, ACCESSORIES AND TOILET FACILITIES.
   (A)   Use and care. All plumbing fixtures, such as water closets, urinals,
sinks, lavatories, bath and the like, shall be used only for the purpose for
which they are intended; and all such fixtures shall be kept in a sanitary and
clean condition. No other paper than what is commonly known as “toilet paper”
shall be placed in any water closet or allowed to enter any soil pipe.
   (B)   Requirements.
      (1)   Each dwelling or apartment unit on premises abutting on a sewer or
with a private sewage disposal system shall have at least one water closet, one
handwashing lavatory, one kitchen sink, bathtub and laundry trays for each four
apartments. All other structures for human occupancy or use shall have adequate
sanitary facilities, but in no case less than one water closet and one
handwashing lavatory or other similar fixture for each sex for cleansing
purposes.
      (2)   Each complete bathroom shall be provided with:
         (a)   Grab bar and soap dish at bathtub;
         (b)   Toilet paper holder at water closet;
         (c)   Soap dish at lavatory;
         (d)   Towel bar;
         (e)   Medicine cabinet; and
         (f)   In all cases where shower head is installed, provide a shower
rod or shower door and soap dish.
      (3)   Each half bath shall be provided with divisions (B)(2)(a) through
(B)(2)(f) above.
      (4)   All fixtures shall be securely supported so that no strain is
placed on the connected piping. Unless otherwise recommended by the
manufacturer, bathtub rims at wall shall be supported by metal hangers or end
grain of wood blocks secured to wall construction.
      (5)   Safe pans shall be installed under all tile, terrazzo, concrete or
precast concrete shower floors.
         (a)   Pans shall be of four pound PSF lead or 12 ounces of PSF copper.
         (b)   Surfaces of lead pans exposed to concrete shall be heavily
coated with asphalt compound.
         (c)   Pans laid on wood floors shall be protected against nail popping
by one layer of 30- pound asphalt-saturated felt placed between pans and wood
floors.
         (d)   Sides of pans shall be turned up a minimum of six inches.
Corners shall be formed by folding.
         (e)   Shower drain shall be of the double drainage flange pattern with
weep holes and flashing clamp device for attachment of the safe pan.
         (f)   Shower compartments shall have not less than 1,024 square inches
in floor area and shall not be less than 30 inches in shortest dimension.
         (g)   Shower compartments shall have walls and ceiling constructed of
smooth, non- corrosive and non-absorbent, water-proof materials.
         (h)   Built-in tubs with overhead showers shall have water-proof
joints between the tub and water-proof wall.
      (6)   Drinking fountains:
         (a)   Offices, public buildings, dormitories and other places of
employment provide one drinking fountain per each 75 persons;
         (b)   Theaters and auditoriums provide one drinking fountain for each
100 persons. Over 1,000 persons, add one fixture for each additional 1,000
persons; and
         (c)   Drinking fountain bubblers shall not be installed in conjunction
with, or connected to, a handwashing lavatory.
      (7)   Lavatories or washrooms:
         (a)   Offices, public buildings and other places of employment:
 
No. of Persons No. of Fixtures
1 - 15         1
16 - 35        2
36 - 60        3
61 - 90        4
91 -125        5
1 fixture for each 45 additional persons over 125
 
         (b)   Theaters and auditoriums:
 
No. of Persons No. of Fixtures
1 - 200        1
201 - 400      2
401 - 750      3
1 fixture for each additional 250 persons over 750
 
         (c)   In no case shall there be less than one lavatory for eight
required water closets or urinals and less than one lavatory per toilet room.
Any building category not indicated shall be considered separately by the
Building Department.
      (8)   Slop sinks to be provided as required by the Building Department in
all occupancies.
      (9)   In every building accommodating persons of both sexes, toilet
rooms, when adjoining, shall be separated by a soundproof partition of a
material which cannot be easily cut or defaced. Each toilet room shall be
distinctly marked with respect to the sex which uses it.
      (10)   A room containing a urinal, bath or water closet shall be entirely
separated from any other room or hall by a solid partition extending from floor
to ceiling broken only by the entrance doorway. No window, transom or other
opening shall be made from any such room into an adjoining room, work space or
hallway for the purpose of ventilation.
      (11)   Except in family units, no bathroom or toilet room shall open
directly into a room where food is prepared, stored or served without an
intervening vestibule.
      (12)   Each toilet room shall have at least 12 square feet of floor area
for each water closet and each urinal.
      (13)   Water closet bowls for public use or use of employees shall be of
the elongated type, seats shall be open-front seats constructed of or surfaced
with non-absorbent material.
      (14)   No water closet or urinal shall be located in a room or
compartment which has less than five footcandles of illumination at floor level
and/or which is not vented to the atmosphere by window opening with an openable
glass area of four square feet for one fixture and one additional square foot
for each additional fixture. When impracticable to locate a toilet room on an
outside wall with proper light and ventilation, mechanical ventilation shall be
provided. Mechanical ventilation shall consist of an exhaust fan which shall
operate with a wall switch or shall operate with an automatic timing device and
shall be connected to the outside air by means of a duct. A mechanical system
of ventilation shall provide 12 complete air changes per hour minimum.
      (15)   Restaurants and lunchrooms shall be provided with one water closet
for employees and toilet rooms for each sex. Water closet or urinal
compartments shall never open directly into any bakery- market, restaurant or
into any room where food is being prepared, and shall always be so located as
to be least objectionable as regards to sanitation and privacy.
      (16)   Public garages and automotive gas stations shall provide not less
than one toilet room for each sex.
   (C)   Temporary toilet facilities. Suitable toilet facilities shall be
provided for the use of workers during the construction of any building. These
toilet facilities shall be maintained in a sanitary condition. The closet shall
be properly enclosed to secure privacy and tissue toilet paper must be
provided.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-8) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.083 CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATIONS.
   (A)   Provide at least two sill faucets on every building at convenient
exterior locations. Where faucets are likely to freeze, they shall be of the
frost-proof type or have an individual stop or waste valve.
   (B)   Each individual plumbing fixture or water-supplied appliance shall
have individual approved shut-off valves which will permit each plumbing
fixture or water-supplied appliance to be shut off without interference with
the water supply to any other plumbing fixture or water-supplied appliance;
except that, single-family dwellings with basements may have approved shut-off
valves which shall control the water supply to riser pipes installed in each
branch supply as near as practicable to its connection with the riser pipe or
branch supply line; however, each water closet shall be provided with a shut-
off valve. Each shut-off valve installed shall be accessible for operation at
all times.
   (C)   Buildings with floor slabs, shall have a yard clean-out accessibly
located within five feet of the building wall or foundation.
   (D)   Lead pipe shall not be used.
   (E)   Soldering bushings shall be of heavy red brass.
   (F)   All drains within all buildings, when underground, shall be of service
weight cast iron soil pipe, to a distance beyond the footings or bearing walls
to undisturbed earth, and in no case less than five feet. The building drain
from a point five feet outside the building footing or bearing wall shall be
extra heavy cast iron, vitrified clay or concrete sewer or reinforced concrete
sewer pipe. Cement mortar joints shall not be used in any piping controlled by
this code. Joints in vitrified clay or concrete sewer pipe shall be hot-poured
or precast joints.
   (G)   Subsoil drains shall be provided around the entire perimeter for all
structures with rooms below grade or with crawl spaces. Crawl spaces shall be
provided with a trapped drain. Subsoil drains shall discharge to the sump or
receiving tank, the contents of which shall be automatically lifted and
discharged into the drainage system. The drains shall be made of open-jointed
or horizontally split or perforated clay tile, not less than four inches in
diameter. Subsoil drains shall be laid in three-quarters inch gravel or crushed
rock with a minimum of four inches of gravel or rock circumferentially around
the tile. In the case where sanitary waste enters the sump or receiving tank,
such subsoil drains are to be properly trapped and before entering the sump or
receiving tank, be protected against back pressure by an automatic back
pressure valve accessibly located, or other methods approved by the Building
Department. Access for the purpose of cleaning and removing obstructions in
subsoil drains shall be provided at the high point of such subsoil drains. When
subsoil drains are placed on the inside of the foundation wall in unstable
soil, they shall be located a minimum of two feet from the footing.
   (H)   (1)   All sewers installed in any building shall be overhead sewers
and shall be located and installed above the grade of the adjoining main sewer;
provided, however, this restriction shall not apply to sewers installed in
buildings (without rooms below ground level or crawl spaces) constructed above
ground level in which all sewers or drains are located above the grade of
adjoining main sewer. All sewer drains or subsoil drainage systems shall
discharge directly to a sump or receiving tank so located to receive the
discharge by gravity. Pumps, ejectors or other mechanical devices shall be
provided to lift and discharge the contents of sumps or receiving tanks into
the building drain. Such pump, ejector or other mechanical equipment shall
operate automatically. A backwater valve shall be provided in the outlet line
of every sump or receiving tank. The waste line from the sump or ejector pump
shall be elevated to a point 18 inches from the ceiling of the room in which it
is installed or at least above the finished street grade before connecting to
the soil or waste stack or building drain. Every sump or receiving tank within
a building, receiving the discharge from sanitary drains, storm water or
combined drains, shall be of an 18-inch minimum diameter by 30-inch minimum
depth cast iron, equally durable metal or reinforced concrete with metal
concrete or equal bottom. Every sump or receiving tank receiving the discharge
from open jointed subsoil drainage systems only shall be 18-inch minimum
diameter by 30-inch minimum depth cast iron, equally durable metal, reinforced
concrete or vitrified clay tile with metal, concrete or equal bottom. Every
sump or receiving tank receiving discharge from sanitary drains, storm water or
combined drains shall have a gas-tight cover as approved by the Building
Department and shall have a vent pipe not less than two inches in diameter
where soil waste is received.
      (2)   Sump pumps shall have minimum one-third H.P. ejectors shall have
minimum one-half H.P., 110/220 volt, 60 cycle, 1,750 R.P.M. motors, totally
enclosed fan-cooled repulsion induction with automatic overload protection and
pump with automatic float control, open trash type bronze impeller, mechanical
seal under lower oilete bearing, life seal under ball bearing.
   (I)   Every restaurant, hotel, butcher shop, public institution and similar
buildings shall be provided with an outside catch basin for all kitchen wastes
and other detrimental wastes as determined by the Building Department. Grease
interceptors for other than residential dwellings are subject to approval of
the Building Department.
   (J)   (1)   A grease catch basin located outside a building shall be of
concrete, precast in blocks or monolithic or of block construction laid up in
portland cement mortar with walls not less than five inches thick. The basin
shall be water-tight.
      (2)   The basin shall be not less than 30 inches in diameter below the
top of the highest inlet pipe. The bottom of the basin shall be 24 inches below
the invert of the pipe and the top of the basin shall be 36 inches above invert
of pipe. The outlet pipe shall be trapped. The basin shall be covered with an
all cast iron cover or one-fourth inch thick cast iron lid in a concrete ring
and with a minimum opening of 16 inches. The inverts of the inlet pipe carrying
grease-bearing wastes shall be not less than six inches above the outlet pipe.
Downspouts shall not connect to the basin. Inside catch basins shall be of cast
iron with an air-tight cover.
   (K)   There shall be no floor drains installed in attached garages or
garages located beneath residential dwellings.
   (L)   (1)   The minimum size of any building drain, horizontal branch or
vertical soil or waste stack serving one or more water closets shall be four
inches.
      (2)   The minimum size of the building drain from a point five feet
outside the building wall shall be size six inches.
   (M)   (1)   No vent terminal from a drainage system shall be directly
beneath any door, any window or any other ventilating opening of the building
or of an adjacent building, nor shall any such vent terminal be within 12 feet
horizontally of such an opening unless it is at least five feet above the top
of such opening.
      (2)   There shall be no chases in walls of less than 12 inch nominal
thickness or within the required area of any pier, and no chase in any wall
shall be deeper than one-third the wall thickness. Chases permitted shall not
be cut, but shall be built in as construction progresses. The backs and sides
of all such chases in exterior walls shall be water-proofed and insulated.
Masonry directly over chases shall be supported on steel or equal lintels. All
chases are subject to the Building Department approval.
   (N)   Each gas appliance connected to a piping system shall have an
accessible manual shut-off valve installed upstream of the union or connector
and within six feet of the appliance it serves.
   (O)   Copper tubing shall be installed without joints in or under concrete
slabs.
   (P)   All solder joints shall be made with lead-free solder.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-9) Penalty, see §
151.999

shall be made to conform to all provisions of this subchapter relative to
plumbing in a new building.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-10) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.085 DEFECTIVE WORK; NUISANCE PLUMBING.
   (A)   Defective work.
      (1)   Procedure.
         (a)   In case the Plumbing Inspector or his or her assistants find a
defect in any plumbing installations subject to inspection in the village, such
Inspector shall report the same in writing to the persons for whom the test is
being made, using blanks furnished by the village for that purpose and giving a
description of the character of the defect. If the defect is of a dangerous
character, necessitating immediate repair, the Plumbing Inspector shall
forthwith condemn the apparatus or equipment for further use or until the same
is removed, repaired or renewed. If the defect is of a character such that the
apparatus or equipment may be safely operated for a period of some days pending
repairs, the Plumbing Inspector shall so report, and name the number of days
during which the same may be operated. A duplicate of all such reports shall be
promptly filed in the office of the Building Commissioner.
         (b)   Where a pipe, plumbing fixture or appurtenance of a system of
plumbing is broken, defective or inoperative, its repair or replacement may be
ordered by the Building Commissioner or the Health Inspector. Such repairs
shall be at the expense of the owner of such property or persons in control of
such property.
      (2)   Correction of defects and faults. Any licensed master plumber who
shall neglect, refuse or fail to make good any defect or faults discovered in
his or her work shall not be permitted to do any further or additional work
until the defects or faults have been remedied in a manner satisfactory to the
Plumbing Inspector.
   (B)   Nuisance plumbing. Whenever it shall come to the knowledge of the
Department of Health or the Building Department or complaint shall be made by
the owner or occupant that the plumbing or drainage in any building has become
a nuisance, or is contrary to the provisions and requirements of this
subchapter, or is of faulty construction and liable to breed disease or
endanger the health of the occupants, then the Building Commissioner shall
examine the plumbing or drainage in any such building.
(Prior Code, § 8-4-11)
§ 151.086 LICENSED PLUMBERS REGULATED.

   (B)   Unauthorized use of plumber’s name. No plumber shall allow his or her
name to be used by any other person directly or indirectly for the purpose of
obtaining permits or doing any work under his or her license.

§ 151.087 NON-LIABILITY OF VILLAGE.
   (A)   (1)   In the installation of plumbing and heating equipment ample
provisions shall be made, by providing proper supply tanks, checks, reliefs or
vacuum valves, for the safety of such equipment in the event of the stopping of
the water supply or pressure and to prevent the contamination of the household
water supply or damage to water meters from expansion of the water in any
heating apparatus.
      (2)   The village will not be responsible for any damage that may result
to any plumbing or heating equipment from stopping of the water or pressure on
account of shutting off the water supply to the premises, or the loss of
pressure in the mains through any cause beyond its control, or for the purpose
made necessary in connection with the maintenance and operation of the
waterworks system.
   (B)   When practicable, prior notice shall be provided to affected
consumers.

MINIMUM HOUSING STANDARDS AND PROPERTY MAINTENANCE
§ 151.115 LEGISLATIVE INTENT.
   (A)   The President and Board of Trustees for the village have determined
that it is in the public interest to enforce compliance with certain minimum
housing standards and property maintenance.
   (B)   The village desires to ensure that dwelling units located within the
said village are maintained in a safe manner, consistent with standards
generally accepted in the community.
   (C)   The inherent police power of a unit of local government and a “home
rule” community includes the establishment of such housing standards along with
penalties for the violation thereof.
   (D)   It is the intention of the village to continue to require annual
inspections and licenses of multiple-family dwellings and to provide for
periodic inspections of other dwellings upon the transfer of interest,
ownership or occupancy thereof.
   (E)   It is the purpose of this subchapter to protect the health, safety and
welfare of citizens living within the village and to provide minimum standards
for the maintenance of existing residential dwellings in order to prevent
blight and unsafe living conditions.
   (F)   It is further the intention of the village to provide specific
standards for cooking, heating, sanitary equipment, light and ventilation as
well as minimum space standards per occupant to prevent overcrowding of
dwellings.
   (G)   The additional general purpose of this subchapter is to enforce the
stated objectives to maintain standards of living for the occupants of
dwellings and citizens of the said village to ensure the dignity and comfort of
the residents and to preserve the taxable value of land and buildings
throughout the said village.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-1) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006)

multiple unit dwellings.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-2) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006)
§ 151.117 LICENSE.
   (A)   License required. No person shall operate a multiple dwelling, rooming
house, motel or hotel unless he or she holds a current unrevoked operating
license issued by the village in his or her name for the specific named
dwelling, rooming house, motel or hotel.
   (B)   Application for license; fee. No operating license shall be issued or
renewed unless the applicant owner or operator has first made application
therefor on an application form provided by the village. The village shall
develop such forms and make them available to the public.
   (C)   Issuance of license. The village is hereby authorized, upon
application therefor, to issue new operating licenses and renewals thereof, in
the names of applicant owners or operators of multiple dwellings, rooming
houses, motels or hotels. No such licenses shall be issued unless the multiple
dwelling, rooming house, motel or hotel, in connection with which the license
is sought is found, after inspection by the Housing Inspector, to meet all
applicable requirements of this code pertaining to health and fire prevention
and applicable rules and regulations adopted pursuant hereto, and all laws of
the state regarding hotels, motels and rooming houses.
   (D)   Residency. No operating license shall be issued or renewed for a non-
resident applicant unless such applicant designates in writing to the village
the name of a registered agent in the state for the receipt of service of
notice of violation of the provisions of this subchapter and for service of
process pursuant to this subchapter, and no operating license shall be issued
or renewed for a resident applicant unless such applicant has first designated
a registered agent in the state and county for the receipt of service of
violations of the provisions of this subchapter, when said applicant is absent
from the village for a period of 30 or more days. Such a designation shall be
made in, writing, and shall accompany each application form. The applicant may
designate any person who is a registered agent in the state.
   (E)   Term of use. Every operating license shall be issued for a period of
one year after its date of issuance, unless sooner revoked, and may be renewed
for successive periods not to exceed one year.
   (F)   Conditions of license.
      (1)   Transferability. No license shall be transferable to another person
or to another multiple dwelling or rooming house. Every person holding an
operating license shall give notice in writing to the village within two
working days after having transferred or otherwise disposed of the legal
control of any licensed multiple dwelling or rooming house. Such notice shall
include the name and address of the person or persons succeeding to the
ownership or control of such multiple dwelling or rooming house. This notice
requirement shall be satisfied upon compliance with the provisions of §
151.119 of this chapter.
      (2)   Display of license. Each license shall be displayed on or within
one foot of the mailbox of the multiple dwelling or rooming house.
      (3)   Record of repairs and changes.
         (a)   Every owner or operator of a licensed multiple dwelling, rooming
house, motel or hotel shall keep or cause to be kept an accurate record of all
repairs, alterations and equipment changes related to the provisions of this
subchapter or to any rules and regulations pertaining hereto, and of all
corrections made as a result of inspections by the Housing Inspector. Such
record shall be made available to the Housing Administrator by the owner or
operator when requested.
         (b)   Every owner or operator subject to this section shall be
notified that such record may be used in administrative or judicial proceedings
pursuant to the provisions of this subchapter.
         (c)   The village shall, upon issuance of a license as requested in
this section, advise the licensee of the necessity for such record and the
manner in which such record shall be kept.
   (G)   Inspections; license revocations.
      (1)   Inspections authorized. No operating license shall be issued or
renewed unless the applicant owner or operator agrees in his or her application
to an inspection pursuant to this subchapter, as the Housing Administrator may
require to determine whether the multiple dwelling or rooming house in
connection with which such license is sought is in compliance with the
applicable provisions of this subchapter and with applicable rules and
regulations adopted pursuant hereto.
      (2)   Notice of violation. Whenever, upon inspection of the licensed
multiple dwelling or rooming house, or of the records required to be kept by
division (F)(3) above, the Housing Administrator finds that conditions or
practices exist which are in violation of the provisions of this subchapter or
of any applicable rules and regulations adopted pursuant hereto, he or she
shall serve the owner or operator with notice of such violation in the manner
hereinafter provided. Such notice shall state that unless the violations cited
are corrected within a reasonable time period, the operating license may be
suspended.
      (3)   Re-inspection; suspension of license. At the end of the time
allowed for correction of any violation cited, the Housing Inspector or his or
her designee shall re-inspect the multiple dwelling or rooming house, and if he
or she determines that such conditions have not been corrected, he or she may
issue an order suspending the operating license.
      (4)   Appeals; revocation of license.
         (a)   Any person whose license to operate a multiple dwelling or
rooming house has been suspended shall be entitled to a reconsideration of the
order by an administrative hearing with the Building Commissioner.
         (b)   If no request for reconsideration is filed with the Building
Commissioner within ten days following the issuance of the order of suspension,
the license shall be revoked; except that, prior to revocation, any person
whose license has been suspended may request re-inspection upon a showing that
the violation or violations cited in the notice have been corrected.
      (5)   Specific violations resulting in license revocation.
         (a)   If the licensee is convicted by a court of a violation of any
applicable ordinance of the village, in connection with the licensed building,
then the license shall be subject to revocation without further notice.
         (b)   In the event a condition of extreme hazard to health or safety
is found to exist, the Housing Inspector may immediately revoke the license.
         (c)   Each day a building continues to operate after a license has
been revoked shall constitute a separate violation of this subchapter, subject
to fine as provided in this subchapter.
      (6)   Reinstatement of license. If, upon re-inspection, the Housing
Inspector finds that the multiple dwelling or rooming house in connection with
which the notice of violation was issued is now in compliance with this
subchapter and with applicable rules and regulations issued pursuant hereto, he
or she shall reinstate the license.
   (H)   Penalties. Any licensee violating any of the provisions of this
subchapter shall be subject to a fine and such other penalties as provided in
this subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-3) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.118 ENFORCEMENT OFFICIAL.
   The enforcement official for this subchapter shall be the Housing

(Prior Code, § 8-7-4) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006)
§ 151.119 INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   Right of entry. In order to safeguard the safety, health and welfare
of the public, the Housing Inspector is authorized to attempt at any reasonable
time to obtain consent to entry from any owner, occupant or other person in
charge of a dwelling or structure subject to this code. Such owner, occupant or
other person in charge shall be informed that entry by the Housing Inspector is
sought for the purpose of making an inspection and performing duties under this
code. Failure to give consent to entry under this section shall not be
punishable by fine or imprisonment. Notwithstanding any other provisions of
this code, when the village conducts inspections of a tenant’s apartment in a
multi-family dwelling or any other dwelling that is not owner occupied, the
village must obtain the consent of such tenant or non- owner occupant to
conduct the inspection. If such tenant refuses consent, the village may attempt
to obtain a warrant pursuant to division (D) below and §
151.123 of this chapter.
   (B)   Inspection upon transfer. No owners agent or person in charge of a
one-family dwelling, or multi-family apartment, shall sell or allow any person
to occupy the same as a tenant or lessee unless the owner, agent or person in
charge of such dwelling or structure has notified the Housing Administrator of
the intent to sell or lease such dwelling or structure. Notice shall be in
writing and must be received by the Housing Administrator no less than eight
working days before the proposed sale or lease.
   (C)   Attempted inspection by Housing Inspector. Upon receiving notice of
intent to sell or lease a dwelling or structure as described in division (B)
above, the Housing Inspector shall attempt to inspect such dwelling or
structure to determine whether the dwelling or structure is in compliance with
all of the provisions of this subchapter that pertain to health and safety. The
Housing Inspector shall attempt to make the inspection in no less than within
five working days after receipt of notice set forth in division (B) above. (The
term five days in this instance shall mean any five days during a week or part
thereof, when normal business activities are carried on by the village.) If the
village fails to complete an inspection within this time frame, the village
shall not delay or prevent a sale or lease of a dwelling or structure and shall
not refuse to issue any necessary water or transfer stamps. Failure to consent
to an inspection under this section shall not constitute an offense against the
village and shall not be punishable by fine or imprisonment, nor shall such
failure to consent prevent the sale or lease of a dwelling or structure. Any
inspection conducted pursuant to this subchapter shall be as limited as
possible to allow the Housing Inspector to inspect the dwelling or structure to
determine whether there are violations of the code that pertain to health and
safety. No later than two days before the Housing Inspector is scheduled to
conduct the inspection, the Housing Inspector shall deliver to the owner and
all occupants of the structure or dwelling written notice that includes the
following:
      (1)   The date and time of the inspection;
      (2)   A statement identifying the areas of exterior or interior of the
structure or dwelling to be inspected and a listing of the items that will be
inspected in each area;
      (3)   A statement that the owner, agent or person in charge has the right
to withhold his or her consent to the inspection and require the village to
attempt to obtain a warrant to conduct the inspection;
      (4)   A statement that, if the owner, agent or person in charge withholds
his or her consent to the search, the village may not prevent the sale or lease
of a dwelling or structure (including by refusing to issue any necessary water
or transfer stamps); and
      (5)   A statement that the inspection shall be as limited as possible to
allow the Housing Inspector to inspect the dwelling or structure to determine
whether there are violations of the code that pertain to health and safety
related to electrical, plumbing, structural integrity, security, heating and
fire safety issues.
   (D)   Inspection by warrant. If the owner, agent, occupant or person in
charge of a dwelling or structure does not consent to the attempted inspection
described in division (C) above, the Housing Administrator shall seek, in the
Circuit Court of the county, a warrant in accordance with the appropriate laws
of the state. The warrant shall be for the purpose of making an inspection to
determine whether the dwelling or structure is in compliance with all of the
provisions of this code that pertain to health and safety. The application for
the warrant must include a statement that the inspection will be as limited as
possible to determine whether there are violations of this code that pertain to
health and safety issues related to electrical, plumbing, structural integrity,
security, heating and fire safety issues. A warrant obtained pursuant to this
section shall be executed and an inspection shall be made no less than three
working days before the date of the proposed sale or lease. The term THREE
DAYS, in this instance, shall mean any three days during a week or part
thereof, when normal business activities are carried on by the village. An
owner, agent, occupant or person in charge of a dwelling or structure who is
presented with a warrant obtained pursuant to this section shall not refuse,
impede, inhibit, interfere with, restrict or obstruct entry and free access to
any part of the dwelling, structure or premises where an inspection authorized
by the warrant is sought to be made.
   (E)   Annual inspections. It shall be the policy of the village to inspect
all rental or leased dwelling units or dwelling structures on an annual basis
in connection with the license requirement of §
151.117 of this chapter. Such inspections shall comply with all provisions of
this section.
   (F)   Qualifications. Individuals conducting inspections pursuant to this
subchapter shall be qualified to make such inspections.
   (G)   Inspection report. The Housing Inspector shall provide an inspection
report to the owner, agent, occupant or other person in charge of a dwelling or
structure upon completion of the inspection that identifies those matters which
must be remedied to comply with the provisions of the code that pertains to
health and safety. Upon any reinspection, the Village Inspector shall be
entitled to comply with the provisions of this subchapter that pertain to
health and safety issues, but the Village Inspector shall be prohibited from
raising any new matters or requiring any further remediation not contained in
his or her original report if the conditions existed as of the time the
original inspection. Reinspections must occur within five working days after
the village is notified that the dwelling or structure is ready for
reinspection.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-5) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006)
§ 151.120 APPEALS.
   (A)   Any person to whom any order required by this subchapter is directed
shall comply therewith. Such person shall thereafter, upon petition directed to

of Appeals shall consist of the village’s Building Commission. The Building
Commissioner shall act as Chairperson and will vote in the case under appeal
only if there is a tie vote.
   (B)   Depending upon the findings of the Board at such hearing as to whether
the provisions of this code have been complied with, the Board shall continue
such order or modify or revoke it.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-6) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006)
§ 151.121 CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY.
   (A)   Requirement.
      (1)   If an inspection has been made pursuant to this subchapter, no
owner, agent or person in charge of a one-family dwelling or multi-family
apartment house shall sell, convey, transfer, assign or otherwise dispose of
ownership, by any form of deed, document of conveyance or assignment, either of
title or of the beneficial interest in a trust of any kind, or otherwise, or by
succession in interest through inter vivos conveyance or through bequest or
inheritance, or otherwise, the property unless a water stamp has been issued
and/or allow any person to occupy the same as the owner or as a tenant or
lessee unless the Housing Administrator has issued a certificate of occupancy
for such dwelling or structure. A water stamp and/or certificate of occupancy
shall be issued only if:
         (a)   The Housing Inspector has determined that the dwelling or
structure is in compliance with all the provisions of this code that pertain to
health and safety; and
         (b)   The owner has filed with the Department of Housing, a “roofing
certification” from a roofing contractor licensed and bonded with the state
which certification provides substantially as follows:
            1.   The inspection of the roof reveals that the roof and roof
covering is in satisfactory condition with no evidence of leaks; roof is water-
tight, not worn out and has an estimated physical life of three years; and
            2.   However, no roofing certification shall be required if the
owner, agent or person in charge submits to the Department of Housing proof
that the roof has been replaced or repaired within 12 months from the date of
the proposed sale or lease.
      (2)   Notwithstanding the provisions of division (A)(1) above, an owner,
agent or person in charge of a one-family dwelling or multi-family apartment
house shall be allowed to sell, convey, transfer, assign or otherwise dispose
of ownership, by any form of deed, document of conveyance or assignment, either
of title or of the beneficial interest in a trust of any kind, or otherwise, or
by succession in interest through inter vivos conveyance or through bequest or
inheritance, or otherwise, the property.
         (a)   If the owner, agent or person in charge of the dwelling or
structure has deposited in escrow the following sums of money to secure that
the dwelling or structure will be brought into compliance with all of the
requirements of this code that pertain to health and safety:
 
Investor or lender fee $1,000
Owner occupied fee     $500
 
         (b)   The owner, agent, buyer, conveyee, transferee, assignee or
successor in title, ownership or interest, however accomplished, lessee or
person in charge of the dwelling or structure has entered into an agreement
with the village whereby the buyer, conveyee, transferee, assignee or successor
in title, ownership or interest, or the lessee agrees to bring the dwelling or
structure into compliance with the provisions of this code that pertain to
health and safety within the time period determined by the Housing
Administrator and the village agrees to immediately issue a water stamp and to
issue a certificate of occupancy upon completion of the repairs and remedial
work necessary to bring the dwelling or structure into compliance with the
provisions of this code that pertain to health and safety. No certificate of
occupancy shall issue until the dwelling or structure has been determined to be
in compliance with all of the provisions of this code that pertain to health
and safety.
      (3)   The village shall not refuse to issue a water stamp and/or a
certificate of occupancy on any ground other than the building or dwelling is
not in compliance with the provisions of the code that pertain to health and
safety. By way of example, the village shall not refuse to issue a water stamp
and/or a certificate of occupancy on any grounds related to the village’s
opinion regarding cosmetic concerns. As part of the inspection process, the
village shall not require owners, agents, buyers, lessees or persons in charge
of the dwelling or structure to make any cosmetic changes (e.g., painting
walls, replacing carpet) that are unrelated to legitimate health and safety
concerns. The village shall not administratively suspend the provisions of this
subchapter that permit sales or leases of dwellings or structures pursuant to
division (A)(2) above.
      (4)   Failure of the owner or buyer, conveyee, transferee, assignee or
successor in title, ownership or interest, however accomplished, or lessee to
fulfill the terms of the agreement in division (A)(2) above or to bring the
dwelling or structure into compliance with all of the provisions of this code
identified in the inspection report that pertain to health and safety within
the time period designated in the agreement shall constitute a violation of
this subchapter, such violation continuing until the dwelling or structure is
in compliance with the provisions of this code.
         (a)   If reasonable proof is not received by or shown to the Housing
Administrator or another authorized representative of the municipality
designated by the governing body of the municipality within the period of time
established by the Housing Administrator as the period of time for said repairs
to be completed, the municipality may elect to suspend water services to the
premises pending proof of completion of repairs. The village may, at its sole
option and discretion, provide for temporary water services to the premises as
deemed necessary and appropriate for repairs to be made and completed to the
dwelling or structure.
         (b)   With respect to a repair escrow, if reasonable proof that the
repairs have been completed is not received by or shown to the Housing
Administrator or another authorized representative of the municipality
designated by the governing body of the municipality, within the escrow time
period established by the Housing Administrator as the time period for said
repairs to be completed, the municipality, at its sole and exclusive option,
shall declare the escrowed funds on deposit forfeited, and/or shall issue a
citation violation of this subchapter and/or the escrow repair affidavit or
agreement, and/or shall use the escrow funds to securer or repair the structure
or dwelling in question, so that the structure and property are in compliance
with the municipal local code requirements and applicable ordinances of the
municipality.
         (c)   If, after the lapse of the established time period for repair,
the village secures or repairs the damaged or destroyed structure, the village
shall reimburse itself from the retained repair escrow funds. No more than 15%
of the escrowed funds used by the municipality under this division (A)(4) may
be attributed to the municipality’s administrative expenses, which must be
directly related to the village’s efforts to coordinate, oversee or otherwise
accomplish the repairs that must be made pursuant to the agreement entered into
pursuant to division (A)(2) above. Any unused portion of the retained proceeds
shall be returned to the buyer/owner or lessee.
         (d)   There shall be no liability on the part of, and a cause of
action shall not arise against, the municipality or an agent or employee of the
municipality in the course of enforcing or complying or attempting to comply
with the provisions of this section.
   (B)   Issuance of certificate shall not be construed a warranty. In issuing
a certificate of occupancy, the village does not intend to, nor does it
warrant, ensure or guarantee to the holder thereof, to his or her assignee or
other interested party that there are no violations of this village code or
laws of the state or the United States of America.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-7) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006; Ord. 14-001, passed 2-3-
2014)
§ 151.122 SALE OR LEASE IN ABSENCE OF INSPECTION.
   If an inspection is not made pursuant to the requirements of this
subchapter, nothing herein shall prohibit the sale or lease of a one-family or
multi-family apartment house unless an owner, agent, or person in charge of
such dwelling or structure is interfering with or impeding an inspection
authorized by a warrant obtained pursuant to §§
151.119(D) or
151.123 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-8) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006)
§ 151.123 PROCUREMENT OF WARRANT.
   (A)   A search warrant in connection with this subchapter shall be sought in
the Circuit Court of the county. The Court may consider any of the following
factors along with such other matters as it deems pertinent in its decision as
to whether a warrant shall issue:
      (1)   Eyewitness account of violation;
      (2)   Citizen complaints;
      (3)   Tenant complaints;
      (4)   Plain view violations;
      (5)   Violations apparent from village records;
      (6)   Property deterioration;
      (7)   Age of property;
      (8)   Nature of alleged violation;
      (9)   Similar properties in the area;
      (10)   Documented violations on similar properties in the area;
      (11)   Passage of time since last inspection; and
      (12)   Previous violations on the property.
   (B)   The application for the warrant shall specify the bases on which the
warrant is being sought and shall contain a statement that the inspection will
be as limited as possible to determine whether there are violations of this
code that pertain to health and safety issues related to electrical, plumbing,
structural integrity, security, heating and fire safety issues.
   (C)   The warrant shall provide that any inspection made pursuant to the
warrant shall be as limited in scope as possible to allow the Inspector to
determine whether the structure or dwelling is in compliance with the
provisions of the code that pertain to health and safety related to electrical,
plumbing, structural integrity, heating and fire safety issues.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-9) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006)
§ 151.124 FEES.
   (A)   The fee for a point-of-sale inspection shall be $200 per dwelling.
   (B)   The fee for the annual inspection of a multi-family apartment house
shall be $35 per unit not to exceed $200 for any single apartment house. An
additional inspection fee of $25 per unit will be required for certification to
the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
   (C)   The fee shall be double for any one-family dwelling or multi-family
apartment if actions are taken that do not conform with §
151.119(B) of this chapter.
   (D)   No fee shall be charged for any necessary re-inspection of any
building or dwelling unless the owner, agent, non-owner occupant or person in
charge of the building or dwelling has failed to appear for two previously
scheduled inspections.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-10) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006; Ord. 07-392, passed 4-16-
2007; Ord. 07-410, passed 8-6-2007)
§ 151.125 RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   (A)   The Housing Administrator of the village shall be empowered to
promulgate reasonable rules and regulations not inconsistent with the terms and
provisions of this subchapter in order to enforce the provisions contained
herein.
   (B)   Such rules shall be in writing and copies of this subchapter, such
rules and forms of applications and inspection reports shall be filed and
available for inspection at the office of the Village Clerk and the Housing
Department of the village for a nominal charge.
(Prior Code, § 8-7-11) (Ord. 06-334, passed 2-6-2006)
