FIRE PREVENTION CODE
§ 152.001 CODES AND STANDARDS ADOPTED; INTERPRETATION.
   (A)   The following codes and standards are hereby adopted by reference, and
said codes and standards shall be and are the Fire Prevention Code and
standards of the village:
      (1)   IBC International Building Code - 2012 Edition;
      (2)   IFC International Fire Code - 2012 Edition;
      (3)   IFGC International Fuel Gas Code - latest edition;
      (4)   IEC International Code Council Electrical Code - latest edition;
and
      (5)   NFPA National Fire Protection Association Life Safety Code 101 -
latest edition:
         (a)   NFPA 13 Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems;
         (b)   NFPA 72 National Fire Alarm Code;
         (c)   NFPA 70 National Electrical Code;
         (d)   Applicability of the state-adopted Life Safety Code; and
         (e)   IMC International Mechanical Code - 2012 Edition.
   (B)   If a more recent edition of one of the codes set forth above have been
adopted by another village department, including, but not limited to, building,
plumbing, electrical codes, or if a more stringent code has been adopted, the
more recent or more stringent code shall be followed.
(Ord. 15-048, passed 11-2-2015)
§ 152.002 SMOKE AND HEAT VENTING DEVICES.
   In addition to the provisions of §
152.001 of this chapter, the Fire Chief and the Building Commissioner, acting
jointly, shall have the authority to require such smoke and heat venting
devices, or other fire safety features, which may be necessary and are
consistent with nationally-recognized good practices.
(Ord. 15-048, passed 11-2-2015)
§ 152.003 INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   Purpose. Fire safety inspections will be conducted at business and
commercial properties. The purpose and goal of this fire inspection program is
to encourage a community safe from fire. During these inspections, items such
as construction, occupancy, built-in and portable fire protection equipment,
and other fire safety related issues shall be reviewed.
   (B)   School inspections. All public and private schools in the village
shall be subject to inspection. These school inspections shall be conducted in
the presence of school personnel in order to ensure the fire safety of all
school-aged children. The school inspections shall satisfy the requirements of
the state’s Regional Office of Education (ROE), which requires that all schools
complete a housekeeping inspection during the school year in cooperation with
the local Fire Department.
   (C)   Authority; entry powers. The Building Commissioner, the Fire Chief and
their duly authorized representatives are hereby authorized to make inspections
of all buildings, structures and premises located within the village to
determine their compliance with the provisions of this subchapter. Such
inspections shall be made between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. on any
days, except Sunday and legal holidays, subject to the following condition.
      (1)   Such inspection may take place only if a complaint respecting said
premises has been received by the Fire Chief or the Building Commissioner and
such complaint, in the opinion of the Fire Chief or Building Commissioner
provides reasonable grounds for belief that a violation exists, or such
inspection is undertaken as part of a regular inspection program whereby
certain areas of the village are being inspected in their entirety by the
direction of the Fire Chief or the Village President.
      (2)   Such inspections shall be made by the Building Commissioner, the
Fire Chief or their duly authorized representative upon direction of either
said officers.
      (3)   Any person making such inspection shall furnish to the owner or
occupant of the structure sought to be inspected, sufficient identification and
information to enable the owner or occupant to determine that he or she is a
representative of the village, and to determine the purpose of said inspection.
      (4)   The Building Inspector, the Fire Chief or any duly authorized
representative, upon the direction of either of said officers, may apply to any
court having competent jurisdiction, for a search warrant or other legal
process for the purpose of securing entry to any premises if the owner refuses
to grant entry.
   (D)   Regular inspections of fire hazards; removal ordered.
      (1)   It shall be the duty of the Fire Chief to inspect or cause to be
inspected by officers and members of the Fire Department, as often as may be
necessary, but not less than twice a year in outlying districts and four times
a year in the closely built portions of the village, all buildings, premises
and pubic thoroughfares and private dwellings on complaints, for the purpose of
ascertaining, and causing to be corrected, any conditions liable to cause fire
or any violation of the provisions or intent of any provision of the village
code affecting the fire hazard.
      (2)   Whenever any inspector shall find in any building or upon any
premises of other place, combustible or explosive matter or dangerous
accumulations of rubbish or unnecessary accumulations of wastepaper, boxes,
shavings or any highly flammable materials, and which are so situated as to
endanger property; or shall find obstructions to or on fire escapes, stairs,
passageways, doors or windows that would interfere with the operations of the
Fire Department or egress of occupants in case of fire, the inspector shall
order the owner or occupant to remove the same. The owner or occupant of the
premises or building(s) shall comply with such order subject to appeal within
24 hours to the Fire Chief, as provided in division (E) below.
         (a)   Any owner or occupant who fails to comply with such order within
the time fixed by the Building Commissioner or the Fire Chief, after service of
the order, shall be liable to a penalty as set from time to time by the
President and Board of Trustees.
         (b)   The service of any such order may be made upon the occupant of
the premises to whom it is directed, either by delivering a copy of the same to
such occupant personally or by delivering the same to and leaving it with any
person in charge of the premises, or in case no such person is found, by
affixing a copy thereof in a conspicuous place on the door to the entrance of
the premises. Whenever it may be necessary to serve such an order upon the
owner of the premises, such order may be served either by delivering to and
leaving with the person, a copy of the order or, if such owner is absent from
the jurisdiction of the inspector making the order, by mailing such copy to the
owner’s last known post office address.
   (E)   Inspections resulting from complaints; procedures. The Fire Chief, or
his or her duly authorized representatives, upon the complaint of any person or
whenever it is deemed necessary, shall inspect all buildings and premises
within their jurisdiction. Whenever it is found that any building or other
structure which, for want of repairs, lack of or insufficient fire escapes,
automatic or other fire alarm apparatus or fire extinguishing equipment, or by
reason of age or dilapidated condition, or from any other cause, is especially
susceptible to fire, and which is so situated as to endanger other property or
the occupants thereof, the Fire Chief or his or her duly authorized
representatives shall order such dangerous conditions or materials to be
removed or remedied and the owner or occupant shall comply with such order
within the time set forth in the order. If such order is made by an authorized
representative, the owner or occupant may, within 24 hours, appeal to the Fire
Chief, who shall consider the matter and if, in his or her opinion, the matter
is of sufficient importance, shall notify the President and Board of Trustee
who shall take such action as is appropriate.
(Ord. 15-048, passed 11-2-2015)
§ 152.004 FIRE INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   Purpose and jurisdiction. The express purpose of this section is to
protect and safeguard the safety and welfare of the citizens of the village by
rendering qualified and periodic inspections of commercial and industrial
buildings and structures within the village to discover and correct conditions
which, by reason of faulty construction, age, lack of proper repair, or any
other cause, become especially susceptible to fire or more likely to cause
injury or damage by collapse or otherwise. To ensure the adequacy and periodic
provision of such inspectional services, and to maintain an accurate record of
all inspected premises, a schedule of inspectional fees is established to
offset inspectional expenses. All commercial and industrial buildings and
structures in the village shall be in full compliance with the provisions of
this section, along with all other applicable provisions of this code and the
regulations of the village.
   (B)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      OWNER. Any individual, firm, association, partnership, corporation, trust
or any other legal entity having sufficient proprietary interest in a
commercial or industrial establishment to maintain and manage its operation.
      TENANT. Any individual, firm, association, partnership, corporation,
trust or other legal entity renting or otherwise occupying or using a
commercial or industrial building or structure, or any part thereof, other than
as an owner.
   (C)   Inspectional fees.
      (1)   Commercial, business and industrial properties.
         (a)   Initial inspection fee: $100;
         (b)   Fifteen to 30 calendar day follow-up inspection fee: $0; and
         (c)   All other follow-up inspection fees due to infractions are $100
per inspection until occupancy is approved by the Fire Chief or his or her duly
authorized representative.
      (2)   Unpaid fees. Inspectional fees shall be paid by the tenant of any
property required to be inspected under this subchapter. It shall be the
owner’s responsibility to notify the Village Clerk’s office of the name of each
such tenant. In case of vacant space in any such property, the owner shall be
responsible for the inspectional fee. The owner shall also be responsible for
said inspectional fee if the tenant fails to pay said fee. In that case, the
owner will be notified by the village of non-payment by the tenant and the
owner shall then immediately become responsible for payment of the inspectional
fee. Non-payment may result in a lien against the property.
   (D)   Records.
      (1)   The village’s Building Department shall cause a file to be
maintained and kept current on each commercial, business and industrial
building or structure.
      (2)   A copy of all inspections made by the village shall be placed
therein together with other pertinent data relating to each. Copies of all
inspections shall also be maintained by the Fire Department.
(Ord. 15-048, passed 11-2-2015)
§ 152.005 BUILDING STANDARDS.
   All houses, buildings and structures shall comply with the following
standards.
   (A)   Base building.
      (1)   Sprinkler control.
         (a)   Accessible. Immediate access to Fire Department connections
shall be maintained at all times and without obstruction by fences, bushes,
trees, walls or any other object for a minimum of three feet.
(IFC 912.3)
         (b)   Signs. A metal sign with raised letters at least one inch (25mm)
in size shall be mounted on all Fire Department connections serving automatic
sprinklers, standpipes or fire pump connections. Such signs shall read:
“AUTOMATIC SPRINKLERS” or “STANDPIPES” or “TEST CONNECTIONS” or a combination
thereof as applicable.
(IFC 912.4)
      (2)   Fire Department connection.
         (a)   Accessible. Immediate access to Fire Department connections
shall be maintained at all times and without obstruction by fences, bushes,
trees, walls or any other object for a minimum of three feet.
(IFC 912.3)
         (b)   Caps and plugs. The Fire Code Official is authorized to require
locking caps on Fire Department connections for water-based fire protection
systems where the responding Fire Department appropriate key wrenches for
removal.
(IFC 912.3.1)
         (c)   Inspection, testing and maintenance. All Fire Department
connections shall be periodically inspected, tested and maintained in
accordance with NFPA 25.
(IFC 912.6)
      (3)   Electrical service.
         (a)   Support on building. Electrical equipment shall be secured to
the surface on which it is mounted.
(IEC 110-13)
         (b)   Clearance. Clearance of all service drops shall have vertical
clearance of not less than eight feet from roof surface, ten feet from
electrical service entrance to the building, 15 feet over residential driveways
and those commercial area not subject to truck traffic and 18 feet over public
streets, alleys, roads and parking areas subject to truck traffic.
(IEC 230-24)
      (4)   Gas meters; protection. Above ground gas meters, regulators and
piping subject to damage shall be protected by a barrier complying with IFC 312
or otherwise protected in an approved manner.
(IFC 603.9)
      (5)   Exit discharge; obstruction. A means of egress shall be free from
obstructions that would prevent its use, including the accumulation of ice and
snow.
(IFC 1027.3)
      (6)   Stairway and fire escapes.
         (a)   Obstruction. A means of egress shall be free from obstruction
that would prevent its use, including the accumulation of ice and snow.
(IFC 1027.3)
         (b)   Storage. Required exit accesses, exits or exit discharges shall
be continuously maintained free from obstructions or impediments to full
instant use in case of fire or other emergency. Security devices affecting the
means of egress shall be subject to approval of the Fire Code Official.
(IFC 1027.2)
         (c)   General maintenance. The means of egress for buildings or
portions thereof shall be maintained in accordance with this section.
(IFC 1027.1)
         (d)   Address displayed: duty of owners. Prior to the issuance of an
occupancy permit for any new buildings, additions, alterations or any changes
for which an occupancy permit is required, other than for accessory buildings,
it shall be the owner’s duty to have placed the address of the building in a
location easily observed, clear of obstruction and readable from the roadway,
alley or similar access. House or building numbers shall contrast with the
background, shall be constructed of durable materials, be permanently installed
and be readily visible. Script or written numbers are not permitted. On corner
lots where the building faces the intersecting street, additional numbers shall
also be placed on the side of the building’s street address.
      (7)   Electrical equipment.
         (a)   Shut-offs. A service disconnecting means shall be provided in an
accessible location.
(IEC 230-70)
         (b)   Access to shut-off. Shut-off valves shall be located in places
so as to provide access for operation and shall be installed so as to be
protected from damage.
(IFGC 409.1.3)
   (B)   Inside base building.
      (1)   Entrance/exit.
         (a)   Number. It shall be unlawful to alter a building or structure in
a manner that will reduce the number of exits or the capacity of the means of
egress to less than required by this code.
(IFC 1001.2)
         (b)   Obstruction. A means of egress shall be free from obstructions
that would prevent its use, including the accumulation of ice and snow.
(IFC 1027.3)
         (c)   Reliability. Required exit accesses, exit or exit discharges
shall be continuously maintained free from obstructions or impediments to full
instant use in case of fire or other emergency. Security devices affecting the
means of egress shall be subject to approval of the Fire Code Official.
(IFC 1027.2)
      (2)   Common stairways.
         (a)   Enclosures. Interior exit stairways and interior exit ramps
shall be enclosed with fire barriers. Exit enclosures shall have a fire
resistance rating of not less than two hours where connecting four floors or
more and not less than one hour rating where connecting less than four floors.
(IFC 1019.1)
         (b)   Stairway width. The width of stairways shall be determined as
specified in IFC 1005.1, but such width shall not be less than 44 inches
(1118mm). See IFC 1007.3 for accessible means of egress stairways.
(IFC 1009.1)
         (c)   Stairway doors swing. Interior stairway means of egress doors
shall be operable from both sides without the use of a key or special knowledge
or effort.
(IFC 1008.1.8.7)
         (d)   Maintenance. The means of egress for buildings or portions
thereof shall be maintained in accordance with IFC 1027.1.
(IFC 1027.1)
         (e)   Hardware. Where panic hardware is installed, it shall comply
with the following:
            1.   The actuating portion of the release device shall extend at
least one-half of the door leaf width; and
            2.   A maximum unlatching force of 15 pounds.
(IFC 1008.1.9)
      (3)   Common storage.
         (a)   Condition/housekeeping. Storage of combustible materials in
buildings shall be orderly. Storage shall be separated from heaters or heating
devices by distance or shielding so that ignition cannot occur.
(IFC 315.2)
         (b)   Storage ceiling height. Storage shall not be within two feet or
more below the ceiling in a non-sprinkled area of a building or a minimum of 18
inches below sprinkler head deflectors in sprinklered areas of the building.
(IFC 315.2.1)
   (C)   HVAC equipment base building.
      (1)   Access. The installation shall be readily accessible for the
cleaning of hot surfaces; removing burners; replacing motors, controls, air
filters, chimney connectors, draft regulators and other working parts; and for
adjusting, cleaning and lubricating parts.
(IFC 603.1.5; IFGC 306.1)
      (2)   Proper installation. Heating appliances shall be installed in
accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions, the International Building
Code, the International Mechanical Code, the International Fuel Gas Code and
the ICC Electrical Code.
(IFC 603.5.2)
      (3)   Combustion air. Unvented fuel-fired heating equipment shall not be
located in or obtain combustion air from any of the following rooms or spaces:
sleeping rooms; bathrooms; toilet rooms; or storage closets.
(IFC 603.4.1)
      (4)   Fuel shut-offs. Shut-off valves shall be of an approved type. Shut-
off valves shall be constructed of material compatible with the gas piping.
Shut-off valves installed in a portion of a piping system operating above 0.5
psig shall comply with ASME B 16.33. Shut-off valves installed in a portion of
a piping system operating at 0.5 psig or less shall comply with ANSI Z 21/15 or
ASME B 16.33.
(IFC 409.1.1)
      (5)   Boiler certificate. Upon completion of assembly and installation of
boilers and pressure vessels, acceptance test shall be conducted in accordance
with the requirements of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code. Where field
assembly of pressure vessels or boilers is required, a copy of the completed U-
1 Manufacturer’s Data report required by the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel
Code shall be submitted to the Fire Code Official.
(IMC 1011.1)
      (6)   Clear of combustibles. Open flames such as from candles, lanterns,
kerosene heaters and gas-fired heaters shall not be located on or near
decorative materials or similar combustible materials.
(IFC 308.3.3)
      (7)   Condition of units. The provisions of subchapter shall apply to the
installation, operation and maintenance of fuel-fired appliances and heating
systems, emergency and standby power systems, electrical systems and equipment
and mechanical refrigeration systems.
(IFC 601.1)
   (D)   Common electrical base building.
      (1)   Common panel.
         (a)   Access. A clearance of not less than 30 inches shall be provided
between all electrical service equipment and storage.
(IEC 110-9; IFC 605.3)
         (b)   Property marked. Each disconnecting means shall be legibly
marked.
(IEC 110-22)
      (2)   Circuits.
         (a)   Proper size. Equipment intended to break current at fault levels
shall have a rating sufficient for the system voltage.
(IEC 110-9)
         (b)   Identified. Each service, feeder or branch circuit should be
identified at the point where it originates and shall be legibly marked to
indicate its purpose.
(IEC 110-22)
         (c)   Unused openings. Unused openings in boxes and circuit bodies and
fittings shall be closed. Unused openings in cabinets or cutout boxes shall
also be closed.
(IEC 373-4)
      (3)   Outlets.
         (a)   Proper locations/proper number. Identified electrical hazards
shall be abated. Identified hazardous electrical conditions in permanent wiring
shall be brought to the attention of the Fire Code official responsible for
enforcement of the National Electrical Code.
(IFC 605.1)
         (b)   Covers. Each electrical outlet box shall have a cover, faceplate
or fixture canopy. Open junction boxes and open wiring splices shall be
prohibited. Appropriate covers shall be provided for all switches and
electrical boxes.
(IEC 370-15)
      (4)   Egress/emergency lighting; operational/adequate. The power supply
for means of egress illumination shall normally be provided by the premises’
electrical supply. In the event of a power system failure, illumination shall
be automatically provided form an emergency system for occupancies where two or
more means of egress are required.
(IFC 1026.5)
      (5)   Exit signs.
         (a)   Where required. Exits and exit access doors shall be marked by
an approved exit sign readily visible from any direction of egress travel.
Access to the exits shall be marked by readily visible exit signs in cases
where the exit or path of egress travel is not immediately visible to the
occupants. Exit sign placement shall be such that no point in an exit access
corridor is more than 100 feet (30,480 mm) or the listed distance for the sign,
whichever is less, from the nearest visible exit sign.
(IFC 1011.1)
         (b)   Illumination. Exit signs shall be internally or externally
illuminated.
(IFC 1011.2)
      (6)   Key lock box maintenance (Knox box).
         (a)   Required. Where access to or within a structure or an area is
restricted because of secured openings or where immediate access for life-
saving or firefighting purposes, the Fire Code Official shall be authorized to
require a key box to be installed in an approved location. The key box shall be
of an approved type and shall contain keys to gain necessary access as required
by the Fire Code official.
(IFC 506.1)
         (b)   Maintenance. The operator of the building shall immediately
notify the Fire Code official and provide the new key when a lock is changed or
rekeyed. The key to such lock shall be secured in the key box.
(IFC 506.2)
(Ord. 15-048, passed 11-2-2015)
§ 152.006 TENANT SPACE STANDARDS.
   All tenant spaces shall comply with the following standards.
   (A)   General information.
      (1)   Entrance/exit interior.
         (a)   Number. All rooms and spaces within each story shall be provided
and have access to the minimum number of approved independent exits required by
IFC Table 10181 based on the occupant load, except as modified in IFC 1014.1 or
1018.2.
(IFC 1018.1)
         (b)   Obstructed. A means of egress shall be free from obstructions
that would prevent its use, including the accumulation of ice and snow.
(IFC 1027.3)
         (c)   Reliability. Required exit accesses, exit or exit discharges
shall be continuously maintained free from obstructions or impediments to the
full instant use in case of fire or other emergency. Security devices affecting
means of egress shall be subject to approval of the Fire Code Official.
(IFC 1027.2)
         (d)   Door swing. All means of egress doors shall be of a side-hinged
swing type.
(IFC 1008.1.2)
         (e)   Hardware. Doors, handles, pulls, latches, locks and other
operating devices on doors required to be accessible by Ch. 11 of the
International Building Code, shall not require grasping, tight pinching or
twisting of the wrist to operate.
(IFC 1008.1.8.1)
         (f)   Address/suite number. It is the duty of owners, prior to the
issuance of an occupancy permit for any new buildings, additions, alterations
or any changes for which an occupancy permit is required, other than for
accessory buildings, to place, in a location easily observed, clear of
obstruction and readable from the roadway, alley or similar access, the house
or building number. House or building numbers shall contrast with the
background, shall be constructed of durable materials, be permanently installed
and be readily visible. Script or written numbers are not permitted. On corner
lots, where the building faces the intersecting street, additional numbers
shall also be placed on the side of the building’s street address.
      (2)   Stairways.
         (a)   Enclosure. Interior exit stairways and interior exit ramps shall
be enclosed with fire barriers. Exit enclosures shall have a fire resistance
rating of not less than two hours where connecting four floors or more and not
less than one hour rating where connecting less than four floors.
(IFC 1019.1)
         (b)   Capacity. Where exits serve more than one floor, only the
occupant load of each floor considered individually shall be used in computing
the required capacity of the exits at that floor, provided that exit capacity
shall not decrease in the direction of egress travel.
(IBC 706.1)
         (c)   Door swing. Interior stairway means of egress doors shall be
operable from both sides without the use of a key or special knowledge or
effort.
(IFC 1008.1.8.7)
         (d)   Obstruction/condition. A means of egress shall be free from
obstructions that would prevent its use, including the accumulation of ice and
snow.
(IFC 1027.3)
         (e)   Hardware. Where panic hardware is installed, it shall comply
with the following:
            1.   The actuating portion of the release device shall extend at
least one-half of the door leaf width; and
            2.   A maximum unlatching force of 15 pounds.
(IFC 1008.1.9)
      (3)   Corridors/aisles.
         (a)   Width. The minimum corridor width shall be as determined in IFC
1005.1, but not less than 44 inches.
(IFC 1016.2)
         (b)   Continuity. Fire resistance rated corridors shall be continuous
from the point of entry to an exit, and shall not be interrupted by intervening
rooms.
(IFC 1016.5)
      (4)   Firewalls.
         (a)   Separation. Fire barriers used for separation of shafts, exits,
exit passageways, horizontal exits or incidental use areas, to separate
different occupancies to separate a single occupancy into different fire areas,
or to separate other areas where a fire barrier is required elsewhere in this
code or the International Fire Code, shall comply with IBC 707.
(IBC 706.1.)
         (b)   Fire doors and frames. Means of egress doors shall meet the
requirements of IFC 1008.1. Doors serving a means of egress shall meet the
requirements of IFC 1008.1 and 1017.2. Doors provided for egress purposes in
numbers greater than required by this code, shall meet the requirements of IFC
1008.1.
(IFC 1008.1)
         (c)   Door hardware. Where panic hardware is installed, it shall
comply with the following:
            1.   The actuating portion of the release device shall extend at
least one-half of the door leaf width; and
            2.   A maximum unlatching force of 15 pounds.
(IFC 1008.1.9)
      (5)   Storage.
         (a)   Height. Storage in buildings and structures shall be maintained
two feet or more below the ceiling in non-sprinklered areas of buildings or a
minimum of 18 inches below sprinkler head deflectors in sprinklered areas of
the building.
(IFC 315.2.1)
         (b)   Housekeeping. Storage of combustible materials in buildings and
structures shall be orderly. Storage shall be separated from heaters and
heating devices by distance or shielding so that ignition cannot occur.
(IFC 315.2)
         (c)   “No Smoking” signs. The Fire Code Official is authorized to
order the posting of “No Smoking” signs in conspicuous locations in each
structure or locations in which smoking is prohibited. The content, lettering,
size, color and location of required “No Smoking” signs shall be approved by
the Fire Code Official.
(IFC 310.3)
   (B)   Restaurants; hoods and ducts. Commercial kitchen exhaust systems shall
comply with the International Mechanical Code.
(IFC 60.)
   (C)   Compressed gas.
      (1)   Properly secured. All compressed gas containers, cylinders and
tanks shall be secured to prevent falling caused by contract, vibration or
seismic activity.
(IFC 3003.3.3)
      (2)   Marking. Stationary and portable compressed gas containers,
cylinder tanks and systems shall be marked in accordance with IFC 3003.2.1,
3003.2.2 and 3003.2.3.
(IFC 3003.2)
      (3)   “No Smoking” signs. The Fire Code Official is authorized to order
the posting of “No Smoking” signs in conspicuous locations in each structure or
locations in which smoking is prohibited. The content, lettering, size, color
and location of required “No Smoking” signs shall be approved by the Fire Code
official.
(IFC 310.3)
   (D)   HVAC equipment.
      (1)   Units.
         (a)   Access. The installation shall be readily accessible for the
cleaning of hot surfaces; removing burners; replacing motors, controls, air
filters, chimney connectors, draft regulators and other working parts; and for
adjusting, cleaning and lubricating parts.
(IFC 603.1.5)
         (b)   Heating appliance installation. Heating appliances shall be
installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions, the International
Building Code, the International Mechanical Code, the International Fuel Gas
Code and the ICC Electrical Code.
(IFC 603.5.2)
         (c)   Combustion air. Unvented fuel fired heating equipment shall not
be located in or obtain combustion air from any of the following rooms or
spaces: sleeping rooms; bathrooms; toilet rooms; or storage closets.
(IFC 603.4.1)
         (d)   Fuel shut-offs. Shut-off valves shall be of an approved type.
Shut-off valves shall be constructed of material compatible with the gas
piping. Shut-off valves installed in a portion of a piping system operating
above 0.5 psig shall comply with ASME B 16.33. Shut-off valves installed in a
portion of a piping system operating at 0.5 psig or less shall comply with ANSI
Z 21/15 or ASME B 16.33.
(IFGC 409.1.1)
         (e)   Boiler certificate. Upon completion of assembly and installation
of boilers and pressure vessels, acceptance test shall be conducted in
accordance with the requirements of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code.
Where field assembly of pressure vessels or boilers is required, a copy of the
completed U-1 Manufacturer’s Data report required by the ASME Boiler and
Pressure Vessel Code shall be submitted to the Fire Code official.
(IMC 1011.1).
         (f)   Clear of combustibles. Open flames such as from candles,
lanterns, kerosene heaters and gas fired heaters shall not be located on or
near decorative materials or similar combustible materials.
(IFC 308.3.3)
         (g)   Condition of units. The provisions of subchapter shall apply to
the installation, operation and maintenance of fuel-fired appliances and
heating systems, emergency and standby power systems, electrical systems and
equipment and mechanical refrigeration systems.
(IFC 601.1)
      (2)   Ducts; damper access. Fire and smoke dampers shall be provided with
an approved means of access, large enough to permit inspection and maintenance
of the damper and its operating parts. The access shall not affect the
integrity of the fire resistance rated assemblies. The access shall not reduce
the fire resistance rating assembly. Access points shall be permanently
identified on the exterior by a label having letters not less than one-half
inches (12.7 mm) in height reading: “SMOKE DAMPER” or “FIRE DAMPER”. Access
doors in ducts shall be tight-fitting and suitable for required duct
construction.
(IMC 607.4)
   (E)   Electrical.
      (1)   Control panel.
         (a)   Properly marked. Each disconnecting means required by this code
for motors and appliances, and each service, feeder or branch circuit at the
point where it originates, shall be legibly marked to indicate its purpose,
unless located and arranged so the purpose is evident. The marking shall be of
sufficient durability to withstand the environment involved. Where circuit
breakers or fuses are applied in compliance with the series combination ratings
marked on the equipment by the manufacturer, the equipment enclosure(s) shall
be legibly marked in the field to indicate the equipment has been applied with
a series combination rating. The marking shall be readily visible and state the
following:
 
CAUTION - SERIES COMBINATION SYSTEM
RATED                      AMPERES. IDENTIFIED REPLACEMENT
COMPONENTS REQUIRED. (IEC 110-22).
 
         (b)   Access. A clearance of not less than 30 inches shall be provided
between all electrical service equipment and storage.
(IEC 110-9)
      (2)   Circuits.
         (a)   Proper sizes. Equipment intended to interrupt current at fault
levels shall have an interrupting rating sufficient for the nominal circuit
voltage and the current that is available at the line terminals of the
equipment. Equipment intended to interrupt at other than fault levels shall
have an interrupting rating at nominal circuit voltage sufficient for the
current that must be interrupted.
(IEC 110-9)
         (b)   Identified. Each disconnecting means required by this code for
motors and appliances, and each service, feeder or branch circuit at the point
where it originates, shall be legibly marked to indicate its purpose unless
located and arranged so the purpose is evident. The marking shall be of
sufficient durability to withstand the environment involved. Where circuit
breakers or fuses are applied in compliance with the series combination ratings
marked on the equipment by the manufacturer, the equipment enclosure(s) shall
be legibly marked in the field to indicate the equipment has been applied with
a series combination rating. The marking shall be readily visible and state the
following:
 
CAUTION - SERIES COMBINATION SYSTEM
RATED                      AMPERES. IDENTIFIED REPLACEMENT
COMPONENTS REQUIRED. (IEC 110-22).
 
         (c)   Unused openings. Unused openings in enclosures within the scope
of this subchapter shall be effectively closed to afford protection
substantially equivalent to that of the enclosures within the scope of this
subchapter. Where metal plugs or plates are used with non-metallic cabinets or
cutout boxes, they shall be recessed at least 6.35 mm from the outer surface.
(IEC 373-4)
      (3)   Outlets.
         (a)   Proper location. Hazardous conditions arising from defective or
improperly used or installed wiring, equipment or appliances shall be
remediated.
(IFC 605.1)
         (b)   Proper number. Hazardous conditions arising from improperly used
outlets (multiple pieces of equipment and appliances) shall be remediated.
(IFC 605.1)
         (c)   Covers. each outlet box shall have a cover, faceplate or fixture
canopy. Open junction boxes and open wiring splices shall be prohibited.
Appropriate covers shall be provided for all switch and electrical boxes.
(IFC 605.6)
      (4)   Extension cords.
         (a)   Condition. Extension cords shall not be used as a substitute for
permanent wiring. Extension cords and flexible cords shall not be fixed to
structures, extended through walls, ceilings or floors, or under doors or floor
coverings; nor shall such cords be subject to environmental damage or physical
impact.
(IFC 605.5)
         (b)   Maintenance. Extension cords shall be maintained in good
condition, without splices, deterioration or damage.
(IFC 605.5.3)
         (c)   Temporary wiring. Temporary wiring for electrical power and
lighting installations is allowed for a period not to exceed 90 days. Temporary
wiring methods shall meet the applicable provisions of the National Electrical
Code.
(IFC 605.5, 605.9)
      (5)   Egress/emergency lighting; operational/adequate. The power supply
for means of egress illumination shall normally be provided by the premises’
electrical supply. In the event of a power system failure, illumination shall
be automatically provided form an emergency system for occupancies where two or
more means of egress are required.
(IFC 1026.5)
      (6)   Exit signs.
         (a)   Where required.
            1.   Exits and exit access doors shall be marked by an approved
exit sign readily visible from any direction of egress travel. Access to the
exits shall be marked by readily visible exit signs in cases where the exit or
path of egress travel is not immediately visible to the occupants.
            2.   Exit sign placement shall be such that no point in an exit
access corridor is more than 100 feet (30,480 mm) or the listed distance for
the sign, whichever is less, from the nearest visible exit sign.
(IFC 1011.1)
         (b)   Illumination. Exit signs shall be internally or externally
illuminated.
(IFC 1011.2)
   (F)   Portable fire extinguisher.
      (1)   General requirements. Portable fire extinguishers shall be
selected, installed and maintained in accordance with IFC 906.2 and NFPA 10.
(IFC 906.2)
      (2)   Location. Portable fire extinguishers shall be installed in
locations in accordance with the International Fire Code.
(IFC 906.1)
      (3)   Conspicuous location. Extinguishers shall be located in conspicuous
locations where they are readily accessible and immediately available for use.
In rooms or areas in which visual obstruction cannot be completely avoided,
means shall be provided to indicate the locations of extinguishers.
(IFC 906.6)
   (G)   Flammable liquids.
      (1)   Processing and storage. Preventions, control and mitigation of
dangerous conditions related to storage, use, dispensing, mixing and handling
of flammable and combustible liquids shall be in accordance with IFC 27 and IFC
3401.1.
(IFC 3401.1)
      (2)   “No smoking” signs. Signs shall be posted in storage areas
prohibiting open flames and smoking. Signs shall comply with IFC 3403.5.
(IFC 3404.2.3.1)
      (3)   Fire control. Portable fire extinguishers with a minimum rating of
20-B:C and complying with IFC 906 shall be provided where required by the Fire
Code Official.
(IFC 3406.2.7)
(Ord. 15-048, passed 11-2-2015)
FLAMMABLE LIQUIDS
§ 152.020 STORAGE, HANDLING, MANUFACTURE, TRANSPORTATION, SALE OR USE.
   Storage, handling, manufacture, sale or use of flammable liquids are further
restricted by the approval of the state’s Fire Marshal, Chief of the Fire
Department of the village and the Village President and Board of Trustees and
must be approved by them and a permit issued by the Building Commissioner.
(Prior Code, § 8-5A-1) Penalty, see §
152.999
§ 152.021 APPLIANCES USING FLAMMABLE LIQUIDS.
   The Chief of the Fire Department shall prohibit the use of any type, kind or
make of heating or lighting appliance using inflammable liquids which, after
test by him or her or by the Underwriters Laboratories of Chicago, Illinois, at
the expense of the person interested, is considered as introducing a distinct
hazard to life or property.
(Prior Code, § 8-5A-2)
§ 152.022 STORAGE TANKS.
   (A)   Permit requirements.
      (1)   Application for permit.
         (a)   All applications for permit under this subchapter shall state
the nature of the business of the applicant, the maximum quantity of each class
of liquid to be kept and the location of same while in storage.
         (b)   Every application for a permit for any such tank shall be in
writing, stating specifically the location, the space desired to be used, the
length, breadth and depth, together with the measurement in feet from the
surface of the ground to the top of such tank, and shall contain the plans and
specifications for the construction of said tank, its connections, fittings,
openings and safety appliances.
      (2)   Permit fees. The following are permit fees for each tank for
flammable liquids:
 
Class I and II (gasoline, naphthas and Capacity 121 - 500 gallons       $26
the like)                              Each additional 1,000 gallons or $0.90
                                       fraction thereof
                                       Capacity 121 - 551 gallons       $9
Class III and IV (fuel, oil, petroleum Capacity 551 - 1,000 gallons     $28
and the like)                          Each additional 1,000 gallons or $0.75
                                       fraction thereof
 
      (3)   Transfer and revocation of permit. No permits issued under the
terms of this subchapter shall be transferred or assigned, nor shall any right
or privilege thereunder be transferred or assigned without the written consent
of the Building Commissioner, and any such permit may be revoked by the Village
President and Board of Trustees at any time for just cause.
   (B)   Inspections, certificate of approval. No such tank or outlet shall be
covered over or used and no oil-burning equipment used until the installation,
material and workmanship have been finally inspected, approved and certified in
writing to the Building Commissioner by the Chief of the Fire Department.
(Prior Code, § 8-5A-3) (Ord. passed 5-15-1984)
§ 152.023 REGULATIONS FOR BUSINESSES WITH FLAMMABLE LIQUIDS ON THE PREMISES.
   (A)   Location of businesses.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to locate, build, construct or
maintain any public garage, gasoline filling station or any similar operation,
the storage or filling of tanks, pumps or devices used for the purpose of
storing, drawing off or discharging gasoline, oil or other volatile inflammable
liquid, within 150 feet of any building used as and for a hospital, church or
public or parochial school, measured from the nearest point of such tank or
filling or discharging device used in connection therewith, to the nearest
point of any such building.
      (2)   No retail selling or jobbers’ station shall hereafter be erected or
established within 150 feet of any lot line of property used for hospital,
church or school purposes.
   (B)   Building and premises requirements.
      (1)   Wood construction prohibited. No buildings shall hereafter be
constructed or existing building be altered of frame construction for the
storage, handling, manufacture, sale or use of flammable liquids.
      (2)   Storage rooms. Special rooms for the storage of inflammable liquids
and the handling and use of inflammable liquids shall be constructed as
follows.
         (a)   Walls, floors and ceilings shall be of eight inches of brick or
concrete or four inches of reinforced concrete.
         (b)   Door openings to other rooms or buildings shall be provided with
sills raised to form a liquid-tight space and with self-closing fire doors.
         (c)   Such rooms shall be capable of holding one and one-half times
the maximum amount of inflammable liquids allowed therein.
         (d)   Windows shall be wired glass in metallic sash and frames.
         (e)   No combustible material shall be used in construction except
floor surfacing may be of wood.
         (f)   Proper ventilation in accordance with requirements of the
National Board of Fire Underwriters shall be provided.
         (g)   There shall be no openings to rooms below, except as made
necessary by trade or manufacturing process, and openings to rooms and other
parts of the building above shall be provided with self-closing fire doors or
trap doors.
      (3)   Required exits in certain businesses. In paint and oil stores,
retail stores and jobbers’ plants containing inflammable liquids, at least two
exits shall be provided which shall be so located that the approach to one of
the same will always be away from the point of storage.
      (4)   “No Smoking” signs. The owner, occupant or lessee of any building,
room or portion of building used for the storage, sale or use of inflammable
liquids shall install and maintain signs worded “No Smoking” in such number and
location as the Chief of the Fire Department may require.
      (5)   Room for application of inflammable finishes. Finishing shops for
the application by spraying of inflammable materials shall be of fire-proof
construction or the materials shall be applied in approved spray booths
properly ventilated by exhaust fans.
      (6)   Living rooms over public garages. No living quarters or sleeping
rooms or workshop shall be permitted to be constructed or used over a public
garage as defined in this subchapter, except in case the entire building is of
fire-proof construction or equipped with sprinklers as required by the National
Board of Fire Underwriters. If any such quarters are located above the ground
floor, the stairway to the same shall communicate directly to the ground with
no opening into the vehicle room unless same is protected with an approved
self-closing fire door in a fire-proof partition.
   (C)   Equipment and appliances restricted.
      (1)   Lighting equipment. Lighting shall be by means of incandescent
electric or other approved lamps only. Movable light shall be protected by
vapor-tight globes, enclosed in approved metal cages and shall be fitted with
approved keyless sockets and portable cord. All electric switches and blocks
shall be permanently located at least four feet above the floor in stories
where vehicles containing volatile inflammable liquids are housed; provided,
however, that, switches or blocks located closer than four feet to the floor on
the effective date hereof shall not be required to be removed if, in the
judgment of the Chief of the Fire Department, such installation is safe.
      (2)   Heating equipment and methods.
         (a)   No stove or fuel burning apparatus shall be used or allowed in
any public garage or gasoline filling station.
         (b)   Heating plants, other than approved direct-fired unit heaters,
shall be separated from all spaces by walls providing fire resistance of not
less than four hours and by floors and ceilings providing fire resistance of
not less than two hours. Openings in walls, except as required for pipes and
ducts, shall be limited to one means of access which shall be through a
vestibule protected on each side with a self-closing Class A fire door.
         (c)   Except as provided in divisions (C)(2)(d) and (C)(2)(e) below,
heating shall be by means of radiation or convection from hot water, vapor or
steam heating systems of which the boilers or devices containing combustion
chambers and the fuel storage spaces shall be separated from every space as
required, in division (C)(2)(b) above.
         (d)   Gas-fired or oil-fired unit heaters, subject to the following
provisions shall be permitted.
            1.   The flame shall be protected from drafts of air and contact
with combustible materials.
            2.   Unit heaters shall be so installed that the bottom of the
heater shall not be less than eight feet above the floor. They shall be
constructed and arranged to conform to the requirements of the Recommended Good
Practice Requirements of the National Board of Fire Underwriter’s for the
Construction and Protection of Garages, NBFU Pamphlet No. 88, 1957, with
amendments to date.
            3.   Direct-fired unit heaters specifically approved for use in
garages in the List of Inspected Gas, Oil and Miscellaneous Appliances,
Underwriter’s Laboratories, Inc., November, 1961, with amendments to date,
shall be considered acceptable under the provisions of this subchapter.
         (e)   Electric unit heaters constructed and installed to conform to
the Underwriter’s Laboratories, Inc., Standard for Electric Heating
Appliances”, May 1961, with amendments to date shall be permitted.
      (3)   Electric charging apparatus. Where electric charging apparatus is
installed in a story of a public garage where vehicles containing volatile
inflammable liquids are housed, all such apparatus shall be enclosed in a
compartment constructed of wire screen of not smaller than six-gauge wire, and
not more than two-inch mesh, or otherwise protected against mechanical injury,
subject to the approval of the Chief of the Fire Department. No batteries shall
be tested in any story of a garage where vehicles containing volatile
inflammable liquids are housed, except by means of a volt meter.
      (4)   Gasoline pumps. The pumps or devices placed in public garages for
the purpose of drawing off or discharging volatile inflammable liquid, shall be
set as approved by the Chief of the Fire Department and shall be located on the
ground floor near an entrance or other well ventilated place, and be protected
against mechanical injury. The surroundings shall be kept clean and free from
oil.
      (5)   Use of flame and fire heat. No flame, fire or fire heat shall be
used in any story of a public garage where vehicles containing volatile
inflammable liquid are housed; provided, however, that, forges, emery wheels
and a flame room of incombustible or fireproof material having approved
soldering iron heaters may be used in such stories if enclosed in automatic
fire doors in openings and thoroughly ventilated to the outside.
   (D)   Waste disposal; traps or separators required. There shall be no direct
connection between any garage waste basin, sink, floor drain or waste pipe and
any house drainage or sewer system. All such drains or waste mains to sewer
system shall have intercepting grease, oil and inflammable liquid traps or
separators which will completely separate such substance from water and sewage
and allow their safe and convenient removal. Such traps shall be ventilated in
the same way as is required for tanks holding volatile inflammable liquids.
Grease, oil and the like removed from such traps or separators shall be
disposed of in a method approved by the Chief of the Fire Department.
   (E)   Safety precautions.
      (1)   Cleanliness; waste cans required; care of oily clothes. All garages
must be kept clean. Grease, oil or paint-soaked rags, waste or other
combustible materials of like character shall be kept in approved self-closing
metallic receptacles having metallic legs at least three inches high and
securely braced. One such receptacle shall be provided for each 2,500 square
feet or fractional part thereof of floor area in stories where workshops are
located or vehicles containing volatile inflammable liquids are housed. Such
receptacles shall be safely clear of all combustible surroundings and their
contents shall be safely cleared at least once each day. Oily and greasy
clothing shall be cared for in non-combustible and well vented closets, safely
located.
      (2)   Sand fire extinguishing equipment and supplies. In every public
garage there shall be, in each story in which vehicles containing volatile
inflammable liquids are housed, constantly kept and maintained, convenient
receptacles filled with fine, dry sand to be used for absorbing the waste oils
on the floor. There shall be for fire extinguishing purposes a supply of sand,
chemical extinguishers and fire axes.
   (F)   Use of volatile inflammable liquids.
      (1)   No volatile inflammable liquid shall be kept in a public garage;
except that, contained in soldering iron heaters used in rooms specified in
division (D) above and in the reservoirs of motor vehicles and in the measuring
pumps for filling. The reservoirs of motor vehicles shall be filled directly
through hose from pump of a permanent filling station connected with the main
storage tank. No transfer of volatile inflammable liquids in any public garage
shall be made with open containers. Hose for use in connection with the
permanent filling station shall be Underwriter Laboratory approved hose not
exceeding ten feet in length.
      (2)   No volatile inflammable liquid, except kerosene shall be used in a
public garage for the purpose of cleaning or for any purpose other than filling
the reservoirs of motor vehicles or the filling of soldering iron heater used
in rooms specified in division (D) above.
(Prior Code, § 8-5A-6) Penalty, see §
152.999
§ 152.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.999 of this code of ordinances.
   (B)   Any violation of any provision of §§
152.001 through
152.006 of this chapter, unless otherwise provided for, may be enforced
pursuant to §§
10.030 through
10.043 of this code of ordinances, and as amended from time to time, which
provides for the administrative adjudication of certain ordinance violations.
The Village Administrator may also direct the Village Prosecutor or the Village
Attorney to proceed before any court having competent jurisdiction to enforce
§§
152.001 through
152.006 of this chapter.
(Ord. 15-048, passed 11-2-2015)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 153.001 SIDEWALK CONSTRUCTION.
   (A)   General.
      (1)   Sidewalks required. No building permit shall be issued by the
village unless there is presented as a part of the plans and specifications, a
plot plan showing the location of sidewalks to be constructed at the time of
the construction of the building. Sidewalks must be constructed, where none
exist, by the owner along any part of said property abutting any public street.
      (2)   Deposits required. Any person making application for a building
permit shall, before said permit is issued, deposit with the Village Clerk such
sum of money as may be equal to the cost of the construction of such sidewalks,
as determined by the Village Engineer. In addition to such deposit, the
applicant shall also deposit the sum of $50 with the Village Clerk to guarantee
the removal of debris, the removal of forms and the placing of backfill and the
general cleanup of the premises upon completion of the work; provided, however,
that, no such cash deposits shall be required of applicants who have entered
into an agreement with the village for the construction of residential units in
volume and who have posted surety company bonds to guarantee the performance of
such agreements.
      (3)   Construction specifications. All sidewalks, curbs and combination
of curbs, gutters, driveways and all other exposed concrete to be hereafter
constructed in the village shall be constructed in accordance with the
following plans and specifications.
         (a)   Location. Public sidewalks shall be located eight inches outside
and parallel to property lines in all cases, except in areas zoned for
business. In business zones where buildings are placed on property lines,
sidewalks may be constructed abutting building foundation walls and shall be
six feet in width. Sidewalks of greater width than six feet shall not be
constructed without the approval of the village’s Board of Trustees.
         (b)   Subgrade. Subgrade must be free from all sod, roots, bricks,
boulders and the like. In areas where fill is required, sand or crushed stone
six inches deep shall be used, and each layer shall be thoroughly compacted
before placing such succeeding layer. Cinders, ashes or slag will not be
permitted to be used as fill material at any time.
         (c)   Forms; slab dimensions.
            1.   All forms shall be built in line and grade, mortar-tight and
of a good grade of two inches by six inches lumber or metal. The forms shall
have sufficient bracing to prevent disalignment during construction. The
surface of the forms against which concrete is to be placed shall be oiled.
Forms shall remain in place at least 24 hours after pouring.
            2.   All public sidewalk slabs to be a minimum thickness of not
less than five inches and a width of five feet four inches. Private sidewalk
stabs to have a minimum thickness of not less than four inches and a width of
two feet six inches. Driveway slabs or ribbons to have a minimum thickness of
not less than five inches. The minimum width of slabs to be eight feet six
inches and ribbons two feet and all driveways to extend a minimum of 19 feet
beyond the required front or side yard.
         (d)   Materials of construction.
            1.   Cement shall be of any recognized brand of portland cement;
sand shall be torpedo sand; stone or washed gravel not to exceed one inch in
size; stone and sand must be clean, free from silt, clay or any other foreign
substances.
            2.   All concrete used under these specifications shall be six bag
mix and shall meet the following requirements: the measurements of both fine
and coarse aggregates shall be accurately computed by either weighing or by the
use of a cubic foot gallons per bag of cement, including moisture in the
aggregates; water shall not be added at job site; water to be controlled so
that no free water is on top of slab after placing in forms; air entraining
agent to be used; percent of air entrained to be 6% (plus or minus 1%); maximum
slump: three inches; retempering of concrete not permitted.
            3.   All materials for each batch, including water, shall be mixed
not less than one and one-half minutes after all materials are in the mixer.
Mixing period shall not extend beyond one and one-half hours per batch.
         (e)   Placing concrete.
            1.   All concrete must be placed immediately after mixing and shall
be thoroughly puddled, spaded or vibrated in place in such a manner as to
remove all voids and thoroughly compact and density the mass. Placing of
concrete in forms shall be one continuous operation until one section between
expansion joints is completed.
            2.   In temperatures below 40°F, all materials must be heated, and
no concrete is to be poured when temperature is below 20°F. Poured concrete in
cold weather must be protected from freezing. Concrete shall be maintained at
temperatures of not less than 70°F for three days or 50°F for five days.
         (f)   Expansion joints.
            1.   Expansion joint material for sidewalk shall be a fibrous
material impregnated with asphalt and shall be three-eighths inch in thickness.
            2.   Expansion joints shall be installed at points wherever new
concrete comes in contact with existing structures. Expansion joints shall also
be spaced along length of walk at intervals not to exceed 40 feet on centers;
the top of the joints to be kept five-eighths inch below finished surface.
         (g)   Finishing.
            1.   Sidewalk shall be struck off to a true line and grade, with a
pitch of one-quarter inch per foot across the walk, sloping toward the parkway
or curb. Concrete to be troweled smooth and just before final set, shall be
brushed crosswise to the walk with a fine bristle brush.
            2.   Grooves three-quarters inch deep, minimum, not less than one-
eighth inch or more than one-quarter inch in width, shall be constructed at
right angles to the centerline of the sidewalk. These grooves and all edges of
the walk shall be rounded with an edging tool of one-quarter inch radius. Slabs
shall not be longer than six feet or less than four feet, unless otherwise
approved by the Village Engineer.
         (h)   Curing. All exposed concrete surfaces shall be protected from
drying and satisfactorily cured for a period of not less than seven days after
pouring; curing to be done by continuous spraying of a pigmented membrane
curing compound per village specifications.
      (4)   Curb and gutter. All previous specifications shall apply to curb or
combination curb and gutter, except:
         (a)   A cross-section sketch of curb or curb and gutter must be
submitted to the village for approval;
         (b)   Line and grade shall be determined by the Village Engineer;
         (c)   Expansion joints shall be five-eighths inch in thickness placed
on 40-foot centers, provided with smooth dowel bars three-quarters inch in
diameter, two feet in length, with expansion sleeves placed on one end of dowel
bar. The sleeve end of bar to be greased; and
         (d)   In finishing, all edges to be rounded to dimensions shown on
approved plan. Gutter to be checked with a ten-foot straight edge, with all
high or low spots to be brought to true grade. Final finish to be brushed with
a medium coarse bristle brush. Curb or curb gutter to be scored into ten-foot
sections with edging tool.
(Prior Code, § 7-1-1)
   (B)   (1)   The village agrees to assist in the repair and improvement of
front and corner sidewalks that are deemed by the village to be defective or in
need or repair, on a cost-sharing basis with owner-occupied properties on a 50/
50 basis, to the extent funds are available. For inclusion in this program, the
property must adjoin the defective sidewalk to be repaired. This program does
not encompass the repair of vaulted sidewalks.
      (2)   The property owner(s) must apply to the village for participation
in the program and must submit proof of property ownership with the
application. All applications must be signed by the applicant(s) and notarized.
      (3)   The property owner(s) must submit an application to the Department
of Public Works. After the scope of work has been determined, cost estimates
will be prepared and a bill(s) submitted to the participating property owner
setting forth the total cost of the work to be performed and the property
owners 50% share of the cost.
      (4)   The village shall perform or have the work performed and shall
select and hire all contractors utilized to repair or replace sidewalks under
this program. Residents who hire contractors and/or otherwise have the work
performed outside of the procedures set forth in this division (B) will not be
paid and/or reimbursed by the village.
      (5)   All payments shall be submitted to the Village Clerk’s office in
the form of cash, certified or cashier’s check or money order, prior to the
commencement of any work. All perspective participants who do not timely
respond to the notice and/or submit payment shall be deemed to have declined
participation in the program.
      (6)   Work is scheduled after receipt of payment and award of the
construction contract, if applicable.
(Ord. 00-142, passed 4-17-2000)
§ 153.002 DRIVEWAYS AND CURB CUTS.
   (A)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      DRIVEWAY. A place on private property for the operation of automobiles
and other vehicles.
      DRIVEWAY APPROACH. An area between the traveled roadway of a public
street right-of- way and private property intended to provide access for
vehicles from the roadway of a public street to private property. Such APPROACH
must provide access to something definite on private property such as a
driveway and parking area or a door at least eight feet wide, intended and used
for the entrance of vehicles.
   (B)   Permit regulations.
      (1)   Permit required. It shall be unlawful to construct any curb or
driveway approach or break out or remove any curb without first securing a
permit from the village.
      (2)   Conditions of permit.
         (a)   No driveway approach shall be constructed or used so as to
impede the flow of surface water in the street gutter or a drainage ditch.
         (b)   No driveway approach to residential properties shall be
constructed or used for the sole purpose of a parking space.
         (c)   Driveway approaches to non-residential property shall not be
used for parking space if the parked vehicles protrude into the street so as to
impede the flow of traffic or extend over the sidewalk so as to interfere with
the movement of pedestrians.
         (d)   Non-driveway parkway areas may be used for parking space subject
to the following conditions.
            1.   Parked vehicles shall not protrude into the street so as to
impede the flow of traffic or extend over the sidewalk so as to interfere with
the movement of pedestrians.
            2.   The parkway area shall be paved with an approved dust-proof
surface (i.e., six- inch concrete or two-inch class M1 asphalt or equivalent).
            3.   There shall be a curb provided between the sidewalk and the
parking area located to ensure that no part of the parked cars shall extend
over the sidewalk so as to interfere with the movement of pedestrians.
      (3)   Location of driveway. No driveway approach shall interfere with
municipal or public utility facilities such as poles, traffic signals, sign
posts, catch basins, fire hydrants, crosswalks or other street structures.
Driveway approaches shall be located as to avoid parkway trees and no parkway
trees shall be removed without the approval of the Superintendent of Public
Works.
   (C)   Construction specifications. Driveway approaches shall be constructed
to the following standards.
      (1)   Surface. All driveway approaches which give access to an improved
street with curb and gutters shall be surfaced with a permanent dust-proof
surface, either concrete, bituminous concrete, asphalt, brick or other material
approved by the village.
      (2)   Widths.
         (a)   The total width of driveways measured at the property line on a
parcel of property used for residential purposes shall not exceed one-third the
lot frontage and no single driveway shall exceed 20 feet measured at the
property line.
         (b)   The total width of driveways measured at the property line on a
parcel of property used for non-residential purposes shall not exceed one-half
the lot frontage, and no single driveway approach shall exceed 30 feet measured
at the property line. The width of the driveway approach measured at the curb
shall in no case be greater than five feet more than the width measured at the
property line.
      (3)   Location of drives.
         (a)   On a parcel of property used for residential purposes, a
driveway shall not be located closer than one foot from the property line and
no driveway approach shall extend over the property line extended to the curb;
except that, the flare may extend not more than two feet beyond the property
line extended.
         (b)   On a parcel of property used for non-residential purposes, no
driveway approach shall be located within five feet of the property line or
within ten feet of any other driveway approach as measured at the property
line.
      (4)   Sidewalk grade. Where an existing sidewalk is more than 18 inches
above grade of the street as measured at the gutter line, the Superintendent of
Public Works may permit the sidewalk to be lowered across and adjacent to the
driveway approach. In lowering the walk, no steps shall be permitted and the
maximum sidewalk grade permitted shall be 10%.
(Prior Code, § 7-1-2) Penalty, see §
153.999
§ 153.003 VACATION OF STREETS AND ALLEYS.
   (A)   Petition to vacate.
      (1)   Whenever any person shall seek to have a public street or alley
vacated, such person shall file a written petition with the President and Board
of Trustees. The petition shall contain the following information and furnish
the following documents:
         (a)   The names and addresses of all owners of property adjacent to
the street or alley sought to be vacated;
         (b)   A short statement of the reasons for the request to vacate; and
         (c)   Two contact prints of a plat of the street or alley proposed to
be vacated, said plat being certified by a registered surveyor to the effect
that the plat represents a survey made by him or her and that all geodetic and
dimensional details are correct and containing an accurate legal description of
the area involving the street or alley involved in the petition, and being in
proper form for the approval of the plat. The plat should show all sewers and
all other easements present in said alley or street.
      (2)   The petition shall be referred to the Plan Commission for hearing
and recommendation.
   (B)   Procedures.
      (1)   Conduct of hearing; notices.
         (a)   The Plan Commission shall hold hearings on the application.
Notice of the time and date of such hearing shall be given by mail no later
than five days prior to the hearing to the owners of the property adjacent to
said alley or street. Whenever the Plan Commission shall request, the attorney
for said Commission shall verify the names and addresses of all said adjacent
owners. Notice shall also be posted on the bulletin board of the Village Hall.
It shall be the responsibility of the Chairperson of the Plan Commission to see
that such notice is posted.
         (b)   The first hearing shall be held no later than 30 days following
the date the Board of Trustees determine that the application is in proper form
for referral to the Plan Commission. Any interested person may testify or
present evidence in favor of or against the vacation of said alley or street
and all testimony received shall be under oath.
      (2)   Vote. Each member of the Plan Commission attending the meeting
where a decision is made shall cast a vote on the recommendation made to the
Board of Trustees.
      (3)   Hearing costs. The applicant shall reimburse the village for the
cost of court reporter charges for transcript and time whenever the services of
a court reporter are used for such hearings. The use of a court reporter shall
be in the discretion of the Chairperson of the Plan Commission.
      (4)   Report and recommendation. It is the desire of the Board of
Trustees that the report and recommendation of the Plan Commission be returned
to the President and Board of Trustees no later than 60 days from the date said
application is forwarded to the Plan Commission, although it is recognized that
in certain exceptional cases a longer time may be necessary for the Plan
Commission to properly review and report on this matter.
   (C)   Payment for vacation. In the event a recommendation is made to vacate
said street or alley, the Plan Commission shall make a recommendation as to
whether payment of moneys should be made to the village for the vacation of
said street or alley. In the event a recommendation is made that the alley or
street be vacated without payment therefor, the Plan Commission shall set forth
the reasons for such recommendation.
(Prior Code, § 7-1-3)
§ 153.004 STREET NAMES AND HOUSE NUMBERS.
   (A)   Name and numbering plan. All lots, buildings and structures in the
village shall be numbered in accordance with the following plan.
      (1)   The base line for streets running east and west shall be State
Street and numbers lying east or west of this line shall be designated East
(E.), or West (W.), as the case may be. Streets running north and south shall
be a continuation of streets extending southerly from Chicago; provided that,
the number of each block shall begin with the number 100 or a multiple thereof.
      (2)   Odd numbers shall be on the south and east side of the streets;
even numbers on the north and west sides of the streets.
   (B)   Numbering required.
      (1)   It is hereby made the duty of the owners or occupants of all
buildings situated in the village to number them in the manner provided in this
section.
      (2)   The numbering of lots and parts thereof shown upon the Village
Atlas, now in the office of the Village Clerk, is hereby adopted as the
official numbering of all houses and buildings in the village occupying such
lots. Those owners or occupants whose house or building number does not comply
with the Atlas shall secure the correct building or house number from the
Village Clerk.
      (3)   The Village Clerk shall furnish to each owner or occupant of a
house or building a certificate showing its proper number as it appears on said
Atlas at such times as he or she may see fit or be requested so to do. No
charge shall be made for such certificates.
   (C)   Size and placement of numbers. Each of the figures of every house
number shall be not less than three inches in length and shall be so marked as
to be distinct and easily read. Said numbers shall be placed in a conspicuous
place on the side of or above the front door of the building to which they are
attached.
   (D)   Street name signs.
      (1)   The names of all streets shall be placed and maintained upon at
least one corner of each street intersection in a manner to be directed by the
President and Board of Trustees.
      (2)   No building permit shall be issued and no building erected on any
vacant land in the village which would necessitate the installation of
additional street name signs and standards in that area by the village until an
adequate system of street name signs and standards shall be installed for and
throughout said area by the contractor or subdivider satisfactory to the
President and Board of Trustees. Said system shall be designed to conform to
village specifications. Equipment and materials used shall meet with the
approval of the Village Engineer.
(Prior Code, § 7-1-4)
   (E)   Rear address numbers. New and existing homes, buildings and structures
shall have the approved building or structure address numbers, building numbers
or approved building identification placed on the rear of the home, building,
structure and/or garage, in a position to be plainly legible and visible from
the alley. These numbers and letters shall contrast with their background.
Address numbers shall be Arabic numerals or alphabet letters. Numbers and
letters shall be a minimum of three inches tall (in length) and a minimum of 14
inches wide.

§ 153.005 BUILDING CONSTRUCTION INVOLVING STREETS, SIDEWALKS AND PUBLIC WAYS.
   (A)   Street occupancy during building construction.
      (1)   Street occupancy permit.
         (a)   Permit required. It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit
or store on the roadway, parkway or sidewalk space of any street or in alley,
building materials or any fuels or other supplies for any building or structure
in course of erection, repair or alteration, unless a street occupancy permit
from the Building Commissioner is obtained prior to the act, and any person so
doing shall be subject to the general penalty of this code of ordinances.
         (b)   Application for permit; issuance. All applications for street
occupancy permits shall be made to the Building Commissioner and shall describe
the location of the roadway, parkway or sidewalk space of any street or alley
proposed to be occupied, the use to be made of same and the length of time of
such intended occupation. Should the Building Commissioner approve, he or she
shall issue a street occupancy permit to the applicant; provided, all the
provisions of this code of ordinances as to bonds, fees and all other
requisites in connection with such permit are complied with.
         (c)   Bond required.
            1.   Before the Building Commissioner shall issue a street
occupancy permit, the applicant for such permit shall file with the village on
a form to be furnished by the village, a bond in the penal sum of $5,000 with
surety to be approved by the village and conditioned to indemnify, save and
keep harmless the village from any and all loss, costs, expense or liability of
any kind whatsoever which the village may suffer or be put to, or which may be
recovered from it by reason of the issuance of such permit, or by reason of any
act or thing done, or neglected to be done, under or by virtue of the authority
given in such permit.
            2.   An annual bond may be given to cover street occupancy permits.
      (2)   Limitations on occupancy of streets.
         (a)   The permission to occupy roadway, parkway or sidewalk space of
any street or in alley for the purposes of building is intended only for
imperative use in connection with the actual erection, repair, alteration,
wrecking or removal of buildings and shall terminate with the completion of
such operation. It shall also be unlawful to occupy any such named space under
authority of the street occupancy permit for the storage of articles not
intended for immediate use in connection with the operation for which such
permit has been issued. Failure to immediately remove building or other
material from such occupied space on notice so to do from the Building
Commissioner or Chief of Police shall subject the owner or contractor so
notified to the penalty provided by this code of ordinances.
         (b)   The occupation of a street or alley for the storage of building
material, including temporary sidewalks, shall never extend out beyond the curb
line more than one-third of the way across the street pavement.
         (c)   It shall not be lawful to occupy with building material any
roadway, parkway or sidewalk space of any street or alley other than
immediately in front of the lot or land upon which the building is being
erected; provided that, if the written consent of the owners, tenants or
occupants of properties adjoining the site of any proposed building is first
obtained and filed with the Building Commissioner, the occupation of the
roadway and sidewalk may be extended in front of the property so consenting,
upon the same terms and conditions as those herein fixed for the occupation of
the street in front of the building site.
         (d)   During the progress of building operations, a sidewalk not less
than four feet in width, or an equal width of a clean, hard, paved roadway,
available and made safe for footway, shall at all times be kept open, clean and
unobstructed for the purpose and uses of a passageway in front of such lot or
lots.
         (e)   It is not intended hereby to prohibit the maintenance of a
driveway for the delivery of material across such sidewalk from the curb line
to the building site, but such driveway shall be under the supervision of the
Building Commissioner.
   (B)   Barricades and warning lights.
      (1)   Any excavations for structures to be built within six feet of any
public highway shall at all times be guarded by a substantial railing or
barricade not less than four feet high at lot line.
      (2)   Sufficient red lights shall be displayed and maintained during the
whole of every night at each excavation, pile of material, fence or any other
obstruction on any public highway, to so cast their rays that each excavation,
pile of material, fence or other obstruction shall be in full view of the
public.
      (3)   Whoever maliciously or wantonly, and without legal cause, removes,
extinguishers, diminishes or disturbs a light so placed shall be deemed guilty
of a misdemeanor.
   (C)   Scaffolds on buildings. An outside scaffold on a building not more
than two stories in height standing on or within five feet of the street line
shall have a floor of two inch planks, and at the outer edge thereof, a closed
fence not less than three feet high, when there is no covering over the
sidewalk.
   (D)   Location of materials and structures; obstructing public ways and
appurtenances prohibited.
      (1)   (a)   Materials, fences or sheds shall not be placed within two
feet of any tree, nor within six feet of the rail of any railway, nor render
inaccessible any valve, chamber, manhole, coal chute, fire hydrant, alarm box
or catch basin.
         (b)   All gutters shall be kept free and clear at all times.
      (2)   Mortar boxes or beds shall be so placed and guarded as to protect
the clothing of persons passing and shall be promptly removed from any street,
sidewalk, alley or public way on order of the Building Commissioner or the
Chief of Police.
   (E)   Restoration of streets and sidewalks. Whenever any street, alley or
sidewalk is damaged by the erection or alteration of any building abutting
