158.175 through
158.179 of this chapter:
      (1)   Any conditional use permitted in the R-1 One-Family Dwelling
District;
      (2)   Boarding and lodging houses;
      (3)   Day school or nursery school;
      (4)   Hospitals (but not including animal hospitals), convalescent homes,
rest homes and nursing homes; and
      (5)   Private club, fraternity or sorority house.
(Prior Code, § 10-5F-3)
   (D)   Building height. The same regulations shall apply as permitted in the
R-1 One-Family Dwelling District.
(Prior Code, § 10-5F-4)
   (E)   Minimum lot size.
      (1)   One-family detached dwellings. Every one-family detached dwelling
hereafter erected in this district shall be on a zoning lot having a minimum
area of not less than 4,800 square feet, and a minimum width of not less than
40 feet at the building line; provided that, a lot of record on the effective
date hereof, which has less area and width than herein required and was
recorded under separate ownership from adjoining lots, may be improved with a
one-family detached dwelling if all other requirements of this chapter are met.
      (2)   Two-family dwellings. Every two-family dwelling hereafter erected
or structurally altered shall be on a zoning lot having an area of not less
than 6,000 square feet and a width at the building line of not less than 50
feet at the building line; provided that, where a lot has less width than
herein required and was recorded under separate ownership from adjoining lots
prior to the effective date hereof, such lot may be occupied by a two-family
dwelling, but in no case shall the lot area per dwelling unit be less than
2,500 square feet.
      (3)   Multiple-family dwellings and apartments.
         (a)   Every building hereafter erected or structurally altered as a
multiple-family dwelling or apartment of more than two dwelling units shall
provide a lot area per dwelling unit of not less than 2,100 square feet.
         (b)   No building hereafter erected or structurally altered in the R-
6 Multiple-Family Dwelling District shall have a total lot area of less than
8,400 square feet or a lot width of less than 60 feet at the building line.
      (4)   Planned developments. Minimum lot sizes for planned developments
shall be prescribed by the Zoning Board of Appeals with the approval of the
village’s Board of Trustees at the time a conditional use is authorized.
(Prior Code, § 10-5F-5)
   (F)   Maximum building coverage and units per structure. The maximum
building coverage on a zoning lot shall not exceed 40%. No more than six
dwelling units shall be included in one apartment building or structure.
(Prior Code, § 10-5F-6)
   (G)   Yard requirements.
      (1)   Minimum front yard.
         (a)   On every zoning lot, a front yard shall be provided of not less
than 25 feet. However, where lots comprising 40% or more of all frontage on the
same street and within the same block are developed with buildings having front
yards with a variation of not more than ten feet in depth, the average of such
front yards shall establish the minimum front yard depth for the entire
frontage on such street within the same block, but in no case shall a front
yard of more than 40 feet be required.
         (b)   For buildings exceeding 25 feet in height, the minimum front
yard determined in division (G)(1)(a) above shall be increased by one foot for
each two feet or fraction thereof by which the building height exceeds 25 feet,
but in no case shall a front yard of more than 40 feet be required.
         (c)   Required front yards shall be unobstructed from ground level to
sky, except as otherwise provided in §§
158.175 through
158.179 of this chapter.
      (2)   Minimum side yards. On every zoning lot, side yards shall be
provided as follows.
         (a)   For one-family detached dwellings, two-family and multiple-
dwellings of two stories or less, the same regulations shall apply as in the R-
2 One-Family Dwelling District.
         (b)   For two-, three- and multiple-family dwelling units of more than
two stories in height, the side yard on each side of the main building shall be
increased two feet in width for each additional story added. On corner lots,
there shall be maintained a side yard of not less than 15 feet on the side
adjacent to the street which intersects the street upon which the building
maintains frontage, and in the case of a reversed corner lot there shall be
maintained a setback from the side street of not less than 50% of the front
yard required on the lots in the rear of such corner lots, but such setback
need not exceed 15 feet. No accessory building on said reversed corner lot
shall project beyond the front yard required on the adjacent lot to the rear,
nor be located nearer than five feet to the side lot line of said adjacent
lots.
         (c)   On a lot improved with a non-residential building, there shall
be a side yard of not less than 12 feet on each side of the main structure and
a combined total of side yards of not less than 30 feet.
      (3)   Minimum rear yard.
         (a)   On every zoning lot upon which a building is constructed, there
shall be a rear yard of not less than 25 feet.
         (b)   Required rear yards shall be unobstructed from ground level to
the sky, except as otherwise provided in §§
158.175 through
158.179 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 10-5F-7)
   (H)   Obstructions permitted within yards. The obstructions over required
yards shall be the same as these permitted in the R-1 One-Family Dwelling
District.
(Prior Code, § 10-5F-8)
   (I)   Dwelling standards.
      (1)   Minimum floor area.
         (a)   Single- and two-family dwellings. The minimum floor area
requirements for single-family and two-family dwellings shall be those required
in the R-4 Two-Family Dwelling District.
         (b)   Multiple-family dwellings. The multiple-family dwellings shall
require the following minimum floor areas per unit as well as the following
minimum room sizes.
            1.   One-bedroom units.
               a.   One-bedroom apartment units shall require a minimum floor
area of 750 square feet per unit measured from the interior walls, including
utility rooms located within the interior walls of said unit, but excluding all
other areas not used for living or sleeping purposes (cellars, basements, open
porches). Common areas or rooms used in common with other tenants shall in no
way be included within the minimum floor area requirements. Storage areas
outside of the dwelling unit are not to be considered in determining the
minimum floor area requirements. The rooms within said dwelling unit shall have
the following minimum sizes:
 
Bathroom    50 square feet
Bedroom     150 square feet
Dining area 90 square feet
(However, if used as a kitchen dinette area, then the combined area must have
a minimum of 200 square feet)
Kitchen     100 square feet
Living room 200 square feet
(However, if used as a living-dining combination, the 2 rooms must have
minimum square footage of 300 square feet)
 
               b.   The partitions, closets and hallways within the dwelling
unit shall constitute the other necessary square footage to meet the minimum
requirements.
            2.   Two-bedroom units. Two-bedroom apartment units shall require a
minimum floor area of 975 square feet per unit. The same standards of
measurement and the same minimum room sizes as set forth in division (I)(1)
(b)1. above concerning one-bedroom units shall apply.
            3.   Three-bedroom units.
               a.   Three-bedroom apartment units shall require a minimum floor
area of 1,175 square feet per unit.
               b.   The three-bedroom unit shall require an additional toilet
facility in addition to the one toilet facility.
               c.   The same standards of measurement and the same minimum room
sizes as set forth in division (I)(1)(b)2. above concerning one-bedroom units
shall apply.
      (2)   Construction standards.
         (a)   All multiple-family dwelling structures shall be of solid
masonry construction with face brick on all sides of the structure.
         (b)   Decorative stone or brick may be used where appropriate.
         (c)   The structures shall in all other respects comply with the
Building Code of the village.
(Prior Code, § 10-5F-9)

§ 158.052 R-7 PLANNED SENIOR/ELDERLY FAMILY DWELLING DISTRICT.
   (A)   District regulations. The regulations set forth in this section or set
forth elsewhere in this chapter, when referred to in this section, are the
district regulations in the R-7 Senior/Elderly Family Dwelling District.
   (B)   Special residence district.
      (1)   Permitted uses. Multiple-unit residences, commonly referred to as
senior/elderly housing and accessory uses, including, but not limited to,
chapels, dining halls, craft and game rooms, professional facilities (doctor,
nurse, dentist) therapist, barber and beauty shops and convenience marts, each
of said accessory uses being for the primary use of the residents of the
senior/elderly complex and as special use any special use permitted in the R-
4 and R-5 General Residence District, by compliance with its applicable
district regulations.
      (2)   Lot size requirements.
         (a)   Minimum lot area. Forty thousand square feet.
         (b)   Square feet per building. All structures containing three or
more dwelling units shall provide a minimum area per dwelling as follows:
 
1 bedroom  1,000 sq. ft.
2 bedrooms 1,500 sq. ft.
Any room other than a kitchen, bath, dining or living room shall be considered
as a bedroom for purposes of determining the above requirements for lot area
per dwelling unit.
 
      (3)   Bulk regulations.
         (a)   Yard requirements.
            1.   Minimum front yard. Thirty feet; however for buildings in
excess of 30 feet in height, the front yard shall be increased six inches for
each foot the building exceeds 30 feet to a maximum front yard requirement of
35 feet.
            2.   Minimum side yards. Ten feet for interior side yards and 30
feet for corner side yard.
            3.   Minimum rear yard. Fifteen feet.
            4.   Maximum floor area ratio. 1:50.
         (b)   Maximum height of buildings and structures. Seventy-five feet.
      (4)   Density. Maximum 75 dwelling units per gross one acre.
      (5)   Dwelling standards. Every senior/elderly dwelling shall have a
minimum floor area per dwelling unit, measured from the outside of the exterior
walls, excluding utility rooms, cellars, basements, open porches, breezeways,
garages and other spaces not used during extended periods for living, eating or
sleeping purposes as follows:
 
Dwelling units with 2 bedrooms 700 sq. ft.
Dwelling units with 1 bedroom  540 sq. ft.
 
      (6)   Parking standards. One parking space shall be provided for each
three dwelling units, plus one parking space for each employee assigned to the
complex.
      (7)   Minimum contiguous area. The minimum contiguous area for land zoned
for this use shall be one and one-half acres.
      (8)   Use limitations.
         (a)   Within a senior/elderly complex planned for the use herein
described, provision may be made for barber and beauty shops, gift shops,
commissary-type operations and like amenities for the residents housed therein.
The total square footage of such facilities shall be subtracted from the gross,
area of the complex prior to computing densities.
         (b)   No zoning district hereafter established for this use shall be
altered, modified or enlarged so as to conflict with the regulations outlined
herein.
(Ord. 92-199, passed 12-8-1992)
BUSINESS DISTRICTS
§ 158.065 PURPOSE.
   (A)   The business districts set forth herein are established to protect
public health, to promote public safety, comfort, convenience and the general
welfare, and to protect the economic base of the village and the value of
property.
   (B)   These general purposes include, among others, the following specific
objectives:
      (1)   To promote the most desirable use of land in accordance with a well
considered plan so that adequate space is provided in appropriate locations for
the various types of business uses, thereby protecting and strengthening the
economic base of the village;
      (2)   To place in separate districts those businesses which may create
noise, odors, hazards, unsightliness or which may generate excessive traffic;
      (3)   To permit selected business uses in districts where adjacency to or
inclusion in a residential area has sufficient elements of service or
convenience to such areas to offset the disadvantage;
      (4)   To encourage the grouping in appropriate locations of compatible
business uses which will tend to draw trade that is mutually interchangeable
and so promote public convenience and business prosperity and contribute to the
alleviation of traffic and pedestrian congestion; and
      (5)   To promote for the establishment of off-street parking facilities,
permitted and required, so as to alleviate traffic congestion and so promote
shopping convenience and business prosperity.
(Prior Code, § 10-6-1)
§ 158.066 MERCHANDISE LOADING AND UNLOADING; EXTERNAL LIGHTING RESTRICTIONS.
   Whenever a building is located in a business district and said building is
within 150 feet of any residential district, the following regulations shall
apply.
   (A)   Restrictions on loading or unloading merchandise.
      (1)   There shall be no deliveries or shipments of incoming merchandise
between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.
      (2)   There shall be no trucks or automobiles left standing with the
engines or equipment engines running between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 6:00
a.m.
   (B)   External lighting. All external lighting shall be effectively shielded
as to not project onto any portion of the residential district.
(Prior Code, § 10-6-2)
§ 158.067 OUTDOOR REFUSE STORAGE.
   Whenever a building in any business district uses an outside storage for
placement of garbage and debris, the following regulations shall apply.
   (A)   Refuse containers. The container used for the storage of the garbage
shall be of a type approved by the village’s Superintendent of Public Works.
   (B)   Container storage area.
      (1)   The containers shall be stored in a suitable area and completely
enclosed by a solid fence eight feet in height.
      (2)   There shall be provided a gate with a lock that shall be locked at
all times.
      (3)   There also shall be a suitable covering placed upon the top of said
enclosure.
      (4)   The said enclosure shall be first approved by the Building
Commissioner of the village.
(Prior Code, § 10-6-3) (Ord. passed 6-1-1976)
§ 158.068 B-1 PLANNED BUSINESS CENTER DISTRICT.
   (A)   District regulations. The regulations set forth in this section or set
forth elsewhere in this chapter when referred to in this section are the
district regulations in the B-1 Planned Business Center District.
(Prior Code, § 10-6A-1)
   (B)   Special use; lot size and location. A building or premises shall be
used only for a planned business center, but only on tracts of land of not less
than five acres abutting and contiguous to a highway containing four or more
traffic lanes, and only by special permit issued by the Board of Trustees upon
application to said Board in the following manner.
      (1)   Tentative development plan.
         (a)   Submission of plan; contents. At the time application for a
special permit is made, the applicant shall submit to the Board of Trustees a
tentative development plan for the proposed use and development of the tract of
land as a planned business center. Such tentative development plan shall
include the following:
            1.   A tentative site plan indicating the areas to be developed for
buildings, the anticipated total gross floor space, the areas to be developed
for parking, the points of ingress and egress, including access streets where
required, and the adjustments to be made in relation to abutting land uses and
zoning districts;
            2.   A traffic survey prepared by a traffic consultant setting
forth and analyzing the effects of the proposed planned business center upon
traffic in and outside of the village, and such survey shall not be limited to
the effect on adjacent streets, but shall extend to all of the surrounding
areas affected and shall indicate the anticipated points of origin, the
direction, amount and density of traffic flow to and from the proposed planned
business center;
            3.   An architect’s preliminary sketches of the proposed planned
business center; and
            4.   A tentative statement of the types of business and uses
proposed and the market area proposed to be served.
         (b)   Plan Commission review and recommendations. Upon receipt of the
application for special permit and the tentative development plan as aforesaid,
the Board of Trustees shall refer a copy of the application and tentative
development plan to the Plan Commission for a study and report thereon. The
Plan Commission’s report to the Board of Trustees shall be made within 30 days
from the date of the reference to the Plan Commission. In its report, the Plan
Commission shall make such recommendations as it considers desirable and in the
public interest.
         (c)   Action by Village Board. Upon receipt of the report of the Plan
Commission, the Board of Trustees may approve or disapprove the tentative
development plan and shall proceed to issue or deny a special permit in
accordance with the provisions of this section; provided that, any special
permit issued hereunder shall be strictly conditioned upon the submission,
within 24 months from the date of its issuance, of a final development plan
conforming as nearly as practicable to the tentative development plan as
approved.
      (2)   Final development plan.
         (a)   Submission of plan; contents. Within 24 months from the date the
special permit was first issued, the permittee shall submit a final development
plan to the Board of Trustees which shall conform as nearly as practicable to
the tentative development plan, as approved, and the special permit issued
hereunder. The final development plan shall include:
            1.   A site plan defining the areas to be developed for buildings,
the areas to be developed for parking, the location of pedestrian and vehicular
circulation and the points of ingress and egress, including access streets
where required, the location and height of walls, the provisions for loading
and unloading, the location, size and number of signs and the location and type
of improvements to be made in relation to abutting land uses and zoning
districts;
            2.   A recent traffic survey prepared by a traffic consultant
setting forth and analyzing the effects of the proposed planned business center
upon traffic in and outside of the village, and such survey shall not be
limited to the effect on adjacent streets, but shall extend to all of the
surrounding areas affected and shall indicate the anticipated points of origin,
the direction, amount and density of traffic flow to and from the proposed
planned business center;
            3.   Preliminary engineering plans of the improvements to be
installed;
            4.   Architect’s sketches of the proposed buildings and
landscaping;
            5.   A schedule of construction, including the anticipated
completion date;
            6.   A statement of all the ownership and beneficial interests in
the proposed planned business center; and
            7.   A statement of the types of businesses and uses proposed, the
general market area proposed to be served and such information as may be
available concerning anticipated lessees and tenants.
         (b)   Action by Village Board. If the final development plan conforms
as nearly as practicable to the tentative development plan, as provided herein,
and to the requirements and conditions of the special permit and to the
requirements and conditions of this chapter, the Board of Trustees may approve
said final development plan and direct the Building Commissioner to issue a
building permit or permits upon submission to him of building plans and
specifications.
         (c)   Changes in final development plan. From time to time, the
permittee may make changes in the final development plans submitted herein, but
any such changes shall be made only with the approval of the Building
Commissioner, or, upon his or her denial thereof, with the approval of the
Board of Trustees. The special permit issued shall be changed to reflect such
approved changes.
      (3)   Time schedules for construction.
         (a)   All time schedules and computations of time shall be computed
from and relate back to the date the special permit was first issued. The Board
of Trustees may extend any time limit provided or required herein or in any
special permit issued hereunder; provided that, each such extension may not
exceed 12 months.
         (b)   The Board of Trustees, at any time, may request written reports
on the progress and development of the proposed planned business center.
         (c)   If the Board of Trustees is satisfied that the permittee has
abandoned the development of the proposed planned business center, it shall
hold a public hearing for the purpose of considering the revocation of all
permits issued and action taken hereunder. Written notice of said hearing shall
be sent to the permittee at the business address stated in the application or
special permit. Publication of said hearing shall also be given in accordance
with the provisions of §
158.193 of this chapter.
         (d)   If the Board of Trustees finds that the permittee has abandoned
the development of the proposed planned business center, it may then revoke all
permits issued and action taken hereunder.
      (4)   Compliance with permit provisions and other village regulations;
guarantee of performance. No building permit shall be issued hereunder contrary
to the provisions of the village’s Building Code and all other ordinances,
rules and regulations of the village or as the same may be amended from time to
time. The use and development of the tract of land as a planned business center
shall conform at all times, as nearly as practicable, to the special permit
issued therefor and to the final development plan as finally approved, and no
building permit, certificate of occupancy or other permit shall be issued
unless the building or improvement requested so conforms to the special permit
issued hereunder and the final development plan as finally approved hereunder,
and an adequate agreement, contract and bond has been deposited with the
Village Clerk to guarantee the installation of the requisite water, sewer,
street paving, curbs and gutters, alley paving, sidewalks, street signs and
street lighting facilities.
(Prior Code, § 10-6A-2)
   (C)   Minimum requirements and standards. A planned business center shall
meet the following minimum requirements and standards.
      (1)   Building height. No building or other structure shall exceed three
stories in height (excluding basements), nor exceed 45 feet in height above
grade; provided that, an exception may be made for elevator penthouses, water
towers and decorative building projections.
      (2)   Location restrictions. No building or structure shall be erected or
maintained within 50 feet of any residential boundary line or within 50 feet of
the right-of-way of any arterial highway containing four or more paved traffic
lanes, and no roadway or parking area shall be erected or maintained within 15
feet of the outside edge of the nearest paved traffic lane or any arterial
highway containing four or more paved traffic lanes.
      (3)   Design standards.
         (a)   Generally. A planned business center shall be laid out and
developed as a unit in accordance with an integrated overall design. The
location and arrangement of buildings, parking areas, walks, lighting and
appurtenant facilities shall be adjusted to the surrounding land uses, and any
part of a planned business center not used for buildings, other structures,
parking and loading areas, or accessways shall be landscaped with grass, trees,
shrubs or pedestrian walks.
         (b)   Buffer strips. A buffer strip of not less than 25 feet wide
shall be provided along any residential boundary line abutting or adjoining any
boundary line of the planned business center. Such buffer strip shall be
sodded, planted and shrubbed in such a manner as to form a green area.
      (4)   Off-street parking and loading requirements.
         (a)   Off-street parking spaces.
            1.   There shall be provided not less than six off-street parking
spaces for customers per 1,000 square feet of gross floor space.
            2.   There shall be provided, in addition to any off-street parking
spaces for customers, adequate off-street parking areas for employees.
         (b)   Off-street loading berths. There shall be provided adequate off-
street berths and areas for loading and unloading.
         (c)   Lighting requirements. All off-street parking and loading areas
shall be properly lighted in accordance with sound planning and engineering
practices.
         (d)   Construction specifications. All parking lots and perimeter
roads and loading areas shall have a base course of stone, crushed gravel or
slag, bladed and rolled over subgrades and shall be topped with asphaltic
concrete or bituminous topping.
      (5)   Signs.
         (a)   Signs may be attached to one or more facades, but not to or on
the roof of any building, and the top edges of such signs shall not project
over the roof line or parapet wall line of the building to which they are
attached.
         (b)   Signs, other than directional signs, shall be limited to
advertising the name of the store, its merchandise or services or the planned
business center as a whole.
         (c)   The provisions of any ordinance regulating the erection or
maintenance of signs shall apply, except as modified herein.
      (6)   Lighting restrictions. All primary light sources illuminating the
buildings and planned business center area shall be erected and maintained in
accordance with good lighting engineering practices and shall be so placed,
designed and used that neither the direct nor reflected light therefrom will
adversely affect surrounding property or create a traffic hazard.
      (7)   Use restrictions.
         (a)   Residential uses prohibited. No building shall be used as a
residence; provided that, facilities for a paid custodian, caretaker or
watchman for the premises may be provided.
         (b)   Storage or display of merchandise. No merchandise, material or
equipment shall be stored or displayed for sale in any open areas unless
specifically permitted by the Village President and Board of Trustees, after a
public hearing before the Zoning Board of Appeals as provided in §
158.194 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 10-6A-3)

         (uu)   Optician shops;

         (xx)   Public utility collection offices;
         (yy)   Residential storage warehouse;
         (zz)   Restaurants, tearooms or cafés (excluding drive-in or curb
service, dancing or entertainment);

(Prior Code, § 10-6B-2)

district uses) shall be retail establishments dealing directly with consumers
and shall be subject to the following conditions:
      (1)   Dwelling units and lodging rooms are not permitted below the second
floor;
      (2)   The sale of foodstuffs or articles intended for human consumption
shall be conducted wholly within an enclosed building;
      (3)   Establishments of the “drive-in” type, offering goods or services
directly to customers waiting in parked motor vehicles, are not permitted;
      (4)   There shall be no manufacture, processing or treatment of products
other than those which are clearly incidental and essential to the retail
business conducted on the same premises;
      (5)   Not more than three persons (exclusive of managers, clerks and
drivers) shall be engaged in said manufacture, processing or treatment of
products;
      (6)   Such uses, operations or products shall not be objectionable due to
odor, dust, smoke, noise, vibration or other similar causes. No merchandise,

unless specifically permitted by the Village President and Board of Trustees
and after a public hearing before the Zoning Board of Appeals as provided in §
158.194 of this chapter; and
      (7)   Any exterior sign displayed shall pertain only to a use conducted
within the building.
(Prior Code, § 10-6B-3)
   (D)   Building height. No building shall exceed three stories or 45 feet in
height, except as otherwise provided in §
158.008(A) of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 10-6B-4)
   (E)   Lot size. Every zoning lot for a building hereafter erected or
enlarged shall comply with the lot size requirements of the R-3 District.
Buildings containing mixed residential and business uses shall be located on a
lot having an area of not less than 2,000 square feet per dwelling unit.
(Prior Code, § 10-6B-5)
   (F)   Yard requirements.
      (1)   Transitional yards. Where a B-2 District adjoins a residential
district, transitional yards shall be provided in accordance with the following
regulations.
         (a)   Front yard. When lots in a B-2 District front on a street and at
least 80% of the frontage directly across the street between two consecutive
intersecting streets is in a residential district, the front yard regulations
for the residential district shall apply to the said lots in the business
district.
         (b)   Side yards. In a B-2 District, where a side lot line coincides
with a side or rear lot line of property in an adjacent residential district, a
yard shall be provided along such rear lot line. Such yard shall be equal in
dimension to the minimum side yard which would be required under this chapter
for a residential use on the adjacent property in the residential district.
         (c)   Rear yard. In a B-2 District, where a rear lot line coincides
with a rear lot line of property in an adjacent residential district, a yard
shall be provided along such rear lot line. Such yard shall be 20 feet in
depth, but may begin at a height of 15 feet or one story above grade, whichever
is lower.
         (d)   Front or side yard extensions. In a B-2 District, where the
extension of a front or side lot line coincides with the front lot line of an
adjacent lot located in a-residential district, a yard equal in depth to the
minimum front yard required by this chapter on such adjacent lot in the
residential district shall be provided along such front or side lot line for a
distance of at least 25 feet including the width of any intervening alley, from
such lot in the residential district.
         (e)   Obstructions prohibited. Transitional yards shall be
unobstructed from lowest level to sky, except as allowed in §
158.008(C) of this chapter.
      (2)   Rear yard. In the B-2 District, a rear yard shall be provided for
residential uses located above the first floor; such yard to be not less than
30 feet in depth and to begin at a level no higher than that of the finished
floor of the lowest residential unit.
(Prior Code, § 10-6B-6)
   (G)   Dwelling standards. The maximum floor area ratio of buildings and
structures on a zoning lot in a B-2 District shall be as follows: the floor
area ratio shall not exceed 1:5.
(Prior Code, § 10-6B-7)
   (H)   Off-street parking and loading. Automobile parking and loading
facilities shall be provided as required or permitted in §§
158.115 through
158.125 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 10-6B-8)

MANUFACTURING DISTRICTS
§ 158.085 PURPOSE.
   (A)   The manufacturing districts set forth herein are established to
protect health, safety, comfort, convenience and the general welfare and to
protect the economic base of the village as well as the value of real estate by
regulating manufacturing development in appropriate locations.
   (B)   These general objectives include, among others, the following specific
objectives:
      (1)   To protect established residential areas, and the health of
families living herein, by restricting those nearby manufacturing activities
which may create offensive noise, vibration, smoke, dust, odors, heat, glare,
fire hazards and other objectionable influences to those areas which are
appropriate therefor;
      (2)   To provide adequate space in appropriate locations for most types
of manufacturing and related activities so that the economic base of the
community may be strengthened, and that employment opportunities may be found
in the interest of public prosperity and welfare;
      (3)   To provide more space for manufacturing activities in localities
accessible to rail and highways so that the movement of raw materials, finished
products and employees can be carried on efficiently and with a minimum of
danger to public life and property;
      (4)   To establish proper standards of performance which will restrict
obnoxious manufacturing activities while at the same time encourage and permit
the manufacturing activities which have adopted facilities for the processing
of finished products without adversely affecting the health, happiness, safety,
convenience and welfare of the people living and working in nearby areas;
      (5)   To protect manufacturing districts from incompatible uses of land
by prohibiting the use of such space for new residential development, thereby
preserving the land for a more appropriate use in accordance with the plans for
village improvement and development; and
      (6)   To promote the most desirable use of land in accordance with a
well-considered plan of land use for all of the village to conserve the use of
property, to promote stability of manufacturing activities and related
development, to protect the character and established development in each area
of the community, to enhance and stabilize the value of land and to protect the
tax base of the village.

depth of less than 25 feet, then such average depth shall be the required front

      (2)   Side yards. On every zoning lot in the M-1 District, a side yard
shall be provided along each side lot line. Each side yard shall be not less in
width than 10% of the lot width, but need not exceed ten feet in width.

   (H)   Performance standards. The following requirements shall apply.
      (1)   Noise.
         (a)   The sound pressure level, to be measured as described below,
shall not exceed the following decibel levels in the designated octave bands
when adjacent to the designated types of use districts:

                               All Residential Districts B-1, B-2, B-3

         (b)   Objectionable sounds of an intermittent nature which are not
easily measured shall be controlled as not to become a nuisance to adjacent
uses.
         (c)   Measurement is to be made at the nearest boundary of the nearest
residential area or at any other point along the boundary where the level is
higher. The sound levels shall be measured with a sound level meter and
associated octave band filter as prescribed by the American Standards
Association.
      (2)   Smoke and particulate matter. The emission of smoke or dusts by
manufacturing plants in an amount sufficient to create a general nuisance to
adjoining properties shall be prohibited. Total emission of smoke and
particulate matter shall be limited to the following: all smoke and the
emission of all other particulate matter in quantities sufficient to produce an
opacity at any point greater than Ringelmann 3 is prohibited. The only
exception shall be a plume consisting entirely of condensed steam. A Ringelmann
unit is defined as 20% density for one minute. No more than 15 units of
Ringelmann smoke shall be permitted per hour and no smoke more intense than
Ringelmann 2; except that, during one hour of a 24-hour day, 30 units of smoke
may be emitted, but with no smoke more intense than Ringelmann 3. The total
quantity of emitted solids shall not exceed one pound per hour per acre of lot
area.
      (3)   Odors. No overly objectionable or hazardous odor shall be emitted
by any use permitted in this district in such quantities as to be readily
detectable by an average observer at any point on the boundary line of the
premises or beyond.
      (4)   Toxic matter. Processes and operations of permitted uses capable of
dispersing gases or toxic particulates into the atmosphere must be hooded or
otherwise suitably enclosed. The emission of such toxic gases or particulate
matter shall be from a stack, or in such a manner that they create no hazard to
person or property.
      (5)   Flare and heat. Operations producing intense light or heat shall be
performed within an enclosed building and not be visible beyond any lot line
bounding the property whereon the use is conducted.
      (6)   Vibrations. No uses shall be located and no equipment shall be
installed in such a way as to produce intense, earth-shaking vibrations which
are noticeable at the property lines of the subject premises.
(Prior Code, § 10-7A-8)

NON-CONFORMING BUILDINGS AND USES
§ 158.100 NON-CONFORMING USES.
   (A)   Authority to continue non-conforming use of a building. The lawful use
of a building existing at the time of the adoption of this chapter may be
continued, although such use does not conform with the provisions hereof, and
such use may be extended throughout the building, provided no structural
alterations, except those required by law or ordinance are made therein. If no
structural alterations are made, a non-conforming use of a building may be
changed to another non-conforming use of the same or more restricted
classification. The foregoing provisions shall also apply to non-conforming
uses in districts hereafter changed. Whenever a non-conforming use of a
building has been changed to a more restricted use or to a conforming use, such
use shall not thereafter be changed to a less restricted use.
   (B)   Discontinuance of non-conforming use. In the event that a non-
conforming use of any building or premises is discontinued or its normal
operation stopped for a period of two years, the use of the same shall
thereafter conform to the regulations of the district in which it is located.
   (C)   Repairs, alterations or enlargements. No existing building or premises
devoted to a use not permitted by this chapter in the district in which such
building or premises is located, except when required to do so by law or
ordinance, shall be enlarged, extended, reconstructed or structurally altered
unless such use is changed to one permitted in the district in which such
building or premises is located.
   (D)   Non-conforming use of land. The lawful use of land for storage
purposes and for advertising signs and billboards, which does not conform to
the provisions of this chapter, shall be discontinued within five years from
the date of the approval of this chapter and the same uses of land which became
non-conforming by reason of a subsequent change in this chapter shall also be
discontinued within five years from the date of the change.
(Prior Code, § 10-8-1)
§ 158.101 RESTORATION OF DAMAGED BUILDINGS.
   No building which has been damaged by fire, explosion, act of God or public
enemy to the extent of more than 60% of its value shall be restored, except in
conformity with the regulations of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 10-8-2)

OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING
§ 158.115 PURPOSE.
   The purpose of this subchapter is to alleviate or prevent congestion of the
public streets, and so promote the safety and welfare of the public by
establishing minimum requirements for the off-street parking and loading and
unloading of motor vehicles in accordance with the use to which property is
put.
(Prior Code, § 10-9-1)
§ 158.116 GENERAL PROVISIONS; SCOPE OF REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Scope of regulations; extent of control. The off-street parking and
loading requirements of this chapter shall apply as follows.
      (1)   All buildings and structures erected and land uses initiated after
the effective date hereof shall provide accessory off-street parking or loading
facilities as required hereinafter for the use thereof.
      (2)   When a building or structure erected prior to or after the
effective date hereof shall undergo any decrease in number of dwelling units,
gross floor area, seating capacity, number of employees or other unit of
measurement specified hereinafter for required parking or loading facilities
and, further, when said decrease would result in a requirement for fewer total
parking or loading spaces through application of the provisions of this chapter
thereto, parking and loading facilities may be reduced accordingly; provided
that, existing parking or loading facilities shall be so decreased only when
the facilities remaining would at least equal or exceed the parking or loading
requirements resulting from application of the provisions of this chapter to
the entire building or structure as modified.
      (3)   When a building or structure shall undergo any increase in number
of dwelling units, gross floor area, seating capacity or other unit of
measurement specified hereinafter for required parking or loading facilities,
and further, when said increase would result in a requirement for additional
total parking or loading spaces through application of the provisions of this
chapter thereto, parking and loading facilities may be increased accordingly;
provided that, existing parking or loading facilities shall be so increased
that the facilities would at least equal or exceed the parking or loading
requirements resulting from application of the provisions of this chapter to
the entire building or structure as modified.
   (B)   Plan and drawings required. An application for a building permit for a
new or enlarged building, structure or use shall include therewith a plot plan,
drawn to scale, and fully dimensioned showing any parking or loading facilities
to be provided in compliance with the requirements of this chapter.
   (C)   Existing parking and loading spaces. Accessory off-street parking and
loading spaces in existence on the effective date hereof may not be reduced in
number unless already exceeding the requirements of this chapter for equivalent
new construction, in which event said spaces shall not be reduced below the
number required herein for such equivalent new construction.
   (D)   Permissive parking and loading spaces. Nothing in this chapter shall
prevent the establishment of off-street automobile parking or loading
facilities to serve any existing use of land or buildings, subject to full
compliance with the provisions of this chapter; except that, off-street parking
areas accessory to existing multiple-family structures cannot be located off
the premises containing the main use, unless on a lot adjacent thereto, without
authorization by the village’s Board of Trustees.
   (E)   Damaged buildings, structures and uses. Any building, structure or use
which is in existence and is a conforming use on the effective date hereof and
which subsequently shall be damaged or destroyed by fire, collapse, explosion
or other cause, may be reconstructed, re-established or repaired with or
without off-street parking and loading facilities; except that, parking or
loading facilities equivalent to any maintained at the time of such damage or
destruction shall be restored or continued in operation. However, it shall not
be necessary to restore or maintain parking or loading facilities in excess of
those required in this chapter for equivalent new construction.
   (F)   Schedule of requirements.
      (1)   Requirements governing the number and location of off-street
parking and off-street loading facilities in relation to the use of property
are established in §§
158.120 and
158.122 of this chapter. The parking and loading requirements for any use not
specified therein shall be the same as for a similar specified use, as
determined by §§
158.175 through
158.179 of this chapter.
      (2)   The term FLOOR AREA, as employed in this chapter in the case of
office, merchandising or service types of use, shall mean the gross floor area
of a building or structure used or intended to be used for service to the
public as customers, patrons, clients, patients or tenants, including areas
occupied by fixtures and equipment used for display or sale of merchandise.
FLOOR AREA, for the purpose of this chapter, shall not include any area used
for:
         (a)   Storage accessory to the principal use of a building;
         (b)   Incidental repairs;
         (c)   Processing or packaging of merchandise;
         (d)   Show windows or offices incidental to the management or
maintenance of a store or building;
         (e)   Rest rooms;
         (f)   Utilities; and
         (g)   Dressing, fitting or alteration rooms.
(Prior Code, § 10-9-2)
§ 158.117 USE OF PARKING FACILITIES.
   (A)   Off-street parking facilities accessory to residential uses and
developed in any residential district in accordance with the requirements of
this chapter shall be used solely for the parking of passenger automobiles
owned by occupants of the dwelling structures to which said facilities are
accessory or by guests of said occupants.
   (B)   Under no circumstances shall required parking facilities accessory to
residential structures be used for the storage of commercial vehicles or for
the parking of automobiles belonging to the employees, owners, tenants,
visitors or customers of business or manufacturing establishments, except as
permitted in this §§
158.118 through
158.122 of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 10-9-3-1)
§ 158.118 JOINT PARKING FACILITIES.
   Off-street parking facilities for different buildings, structures or uses,
or for mixed uses, may be provided collectively in any zoning district in which
separate parking facilities for each constituent use would be permitted;
provided that, the total number of spaces so located together shall not be less
than the sum of the separate requirements for each use.
(Prior Code, § 10-9-3-2)
§ 158.119 LOCATION OF PARKING AREAS.
   (A)   Off-street automobile parking facilities shall be located as
hereinafter specified.
   (B)   Where a distance is specified, such distance shall be walking distance
measured from the nearest point of the parking area to the nearest entrance of
the building that said parking area is required to serve:
      (1)   For one- and two-family dwellings, on the same lot with the
building they are required to serve;
      (2)   For three- and four-family dwellings not over two stories in
height, on the same lot or parcel of land as the building they are required to
serve. For the purposes of this requirement, a group of such uses constructed
and maintained under single ownership or management shall be assumed to be on a
single lot or parcel of land;
      (3)   For apartment houses containing four or more dwelling units, on the
same lot or parcel of land as the building they are required to serve, or on a
separate lot or parcel of land not more than 300 feet from the nearest entrance
to the main building being served; provided, the lot or parcel of land selected
for the parking facilities is located in an apartment district or a less
restricted district;
      (4)   For rooming houses, lodging houses, clubs, hospitals, sanitariums,
orphanages, homes for the aged, convalescent homes, dormitories, sorority and
fraternity houses and for other similar uses, the off-street parking facilities
required shall be on the same lot or parcel of land as the main building or
buildings being served, or upon properties contiguous to the zoning lot upon
which is located the building or buildings they are intended to serve; and
      (5)   For uses other than those specified above, off-street parking
facilities shall be provided on the same lot or parcel of land as the main
building being served, or on a separate lot or parcel of land not over 1,000
feet from the entrance of the main building, measured from the nearest point of
the parking area; provided, the separate lot or parcel of land intended for the
parking facilities is located in B or M districts.
(Prior Code, § 10-9-3-3)
§ 158.120 ACCESSORY OFF-STREET PARKING AREAS.
   (A)   Off-site parking facilities. When required accessory off-street
parking facilities are provided elsewhere than on the lot on which the
principal use served is located, they shall be in the same possession, either
by deed or long-term lease, as the property occupied by such principal use, and
the owner shall be bound by covenants filed of record in the office of the
Recorder of Deeds or the Registrar of Titles of the county, requiring the owner
and his or her heirs and assigns to maintain the required number of parking
spaces during the existence of said principal use.
   (B)   Permitted districts for accessory parking. Accessory parking
facilities provided elsewhere than on the same zoning lot with the principal
use served, in accordance with §
158.123 of this chapter, may be located in any zoning district, except as
follows.
      (1)   No parking facilities accessory to an apartment use shall be
located in an R-1, R-2 or R-3 District.
      (2)   No parking facilities accessory to a business or manufacturing use
shall be located in a residential district, except when authorized by the
village’s Board of Trustees as hereinafter prescribed.
      (3)   No parking facilities accessory to a manufacturing use shall be
permitted in a B-1 District.
   (C)   Non-residential parking in residential districts. Accessory off-street
parking facilities serving non-residential uses of property may be permitted in
an R-6 District when authorized by the village’s Board of Trustees, subject to
the following requirements in addition to all other relevant requirements of
this chapter.
      (1)   The parking lot shall be accessory to and for use in connection
with one or more non- residential establishments located in adjoining districts
or in connection with one or more existing professional or institutional office
buildings or institutions.
      (2)   Said parking lot shall be used solely for the parking of passenger
automobiles.
      (3)   No commercial repair work or service of any kind shall be conducted
on said parking lot.
      (4)   No sign of any kind other than signs designating entrance, exits
and conditions of use shall be maintained on said parking lot.
      (5)   The parking lot may be open from 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m., and shall
be closed at all other times; provided, however, that, when supervised by one
or more full-time attendants, the parking lot may be kept open until 12:00
midnight.
      (6)   Each entrance to and exit from said parking lot shall be at least
20 feet distant from any adjacent property located in any residential district,
except where ingress and egress to the parking lot is provided from a public
alley or public way separating the residential areas from the proposed parking
lot.
      (7)   In addition to the foregoing requirements, such parking lots shall
conform to any further requirements and conditions as may be prescribed by the
village’s Board of Trustees for the protection of properties adjacent to and in
the vicinity of the proposed parking lot.
(Prior Code, § 10-9-3-4)
§ 158.121 DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE.
   (A)   Size of parking spaces. A required off-street parking space shall be
an area of not less than 162 square feet nor less than eight and one-half feet
wide by 19 feet long, exclusive of access drives or aisles, ramps, columns or
office and work areas, accessible from streets or alleys or from private
driveways or aisles leading to streets or alleys and to be used for the storage
of parking of passenger automobiles or commercial vehicles under one and one-
half tons’ capacity. Aisles between vehicular parking spaces shall be not less
than 12 feet in width when serving automobiles parked at a 45-degree angle in
one direction, nor less than 20 feet in width when serving automobiles parked
perpendicular to the aisles and accommodating two-way traffic.
   (B)   Determination of number of spaces. When determination of the number of
required off-street parking spaces results in a requirement of a fractional
space, any fraction up to and including one-half shall be interpreted as one
parking space.
   (C)   Open and enclosed spaces. Parking areas may be open or enclosed;
except that, when parking facilities accessory to a multiple dwelling are
located in a residential or B-1 or B-2 District elsewhere than on the same
zoning lot with the principal use served, such parking facilities shall be open
to the sky.
   (D)   Access to streets. Parking facilities shall be designed with
appropriate means of vehicular access to a street or alley in such a manner as
will least interfere with the movement of traffic. No driveway or curb cut in
any district shall exceed 35 feet in width.
   (E)   Signs. No signs shall be displayed in any parking area within any
residential district, except such as may be necessary for the orderly use of
the parking facilities.
   (F)   Required setbacks.
      (1)   No parking space, nor portion thereof, established on the same
zoning lot with a building shall be located within a required front yard.
      (2)   No parking space, nor portion thereof, established on a zoning lot
without a building shall be located closer to any street line than the
established building line on adjacent properties, nor closer than the front
yard setback required for the district in which the parking lot is located.
      (3)   Further, any wall, fence or hedge developed around any parking area
shall be subject to the front yard setback requirements of this chapter in the
same manner as a building or structure.
   (G)   Surfacing.
      (1)   All open off-street parking areas shall be improved with a
compacted macadam base not less than six inches thick, surfaced with asphaltic
concrete or some comparable all-weather, dustless material not less than two
inches thick compacted.
      (2)   Portland cement concrete having a thickness of not less than five
inches for residential and six inches for business or industry may be
substituted in lieu of the above requirement.
   (H)   Screening and landscaping.
      (1)   All open off-street parking areas of six or more cars shall be
effectively screened by a wall, a solid fence or a densely planted compact
hedge along any side which adjoins or is directly across a street or alley from
a property in a residential district or an institutional property.
      (2)   Such wall, fence or hedge shall be at least four feet, but not more
than seven feet, in height and shall be maintained in good condition.
   (I)   Lighting. Provide adequate lighting, and any lighting used to
illuminate an off-street parking area shall be so arranged as to reflect the
light away from adjoining properties.
(Prior Code, § 10-9-3-5) (Ord. 01-162, passed 1-16-2001)
§ 158.122 SPECIAL USE PUBLIC PARKING AREAS.
   Any automobile parking area developed for transient trade and not accessory
to specific main uses or groups of uses for which parking is required by this
chapter, shall be treated as a special use, as defined in §
158.006 of this chapter and as allowed in accordance with the provisions of §§
158.175 through
158.179 of this chapter by the village’s Board of Trustees.
(Prior Code, § 10-9-3-6)

§ 158.124 OFF-STREET LOADING REGULATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   General description of a loading berth. An off-street loading berth
shall be a hard-surfaced area of land, open or enclosed, other than a street or
a public way, used principally for the standing, loading or unloading of motor
trucks, tractors and trailers so as to avoid undue interference with the public
use of streets and alleys.
   (B)   Size. A required loading space shall be not less than ten feet in
width, 25 feet in length and 14 feet in height, exclusive of access aisles and
maneuvering space, except as otherwise specifically dimensioned hereafter.
   (C)   Determination of number of berths. When determination of the number of
required off-street loading berths results in a requirement of a fractional
berth, any fraction up to and including one-half shall be disregarded, and
fractions over one-half shall be interpreted as one loading berth.
   (D)   Location.
      (1)   No permitted or required loading berth shall be closer than 50 feet
to any property in a residential district unless completely enclosed by
building walls, or a uniformly painted solid fence or wall, or any combination
thereof not less than six feet in height.
      (2)   No permitted or required loading berth shall be located within 25
feet of the nearest point of intersection of any two streets.
      (3)   Loading berths open to the sky may be located in any required
yards.
   (E)   Surfacing. All open off-street loading berths shall be improved with a
compacted macadam base, not less than seven inches thick, surfaced with not
less than two inches of asphaltic concrete or some comparable all-weather,
dustless material.
(Prior Code, § 10-9-5)

materials or merchandise from vehicles, off-street loading and unloading
facilities shall be provided in accordance with the following requirements:

SIGNS
§ 158.140 SIGN REGULATIONS.
   Any publicly displayed sign, symbol or notice on a premises to advertise the
business there transacted, or name of person or firm conducting said business
on premises, or directing to some other locale, shall be regulated as in this
subchapter provided.
(Prior Code, § 10-10-1)
§ 158.141 INTERPRETATION.
   The provisions of this subchapter are declared to be further restricted by
all other applicable ordinances of the village, it being the intent of the
village to make the more restrictive provisions apply.
(Prior Code, § 10-10-2)
§ 158.142 SIGNS IN RESIDENTIAL DISTRICTS.
   (A)   Permitted signs. In an R district, the following signs shall be
permitted:
      (1)   For each dwelling unit, one nameplate not exceeding one square foot
in area, indicating name of occupant;
      (2)   For a structure other than a dwelling unit, one identification sign
not exceeding eight square feet, except a church bulletin board which shall not
exceed 18 square feet; and
      (3)   For purpose of orientation, directional signs when established by
the village, not exceeding two square feet. No advertising sign of any other
character shall be permitted.
   (B)   Prohibited signs. It shall be unlawful to place any outdoor
advertising sign or display within a residential district classified as Single-
Family Residential District R-1, R-2 and R-3, and Multiple-Family Residential
R-4, R-5 and R-6, as defined in this chapter; except that, “For Sale Signs” for
existing structures shall be permitted in residential districts subject to the
following: there shall not be more than one sign per zoning lot except that on
a corner lot two signs, one facing each street, shall be permitted. No sign
shall exceed nine square feet, no sign shall be displayed on the parkway, and
no sign shall be placed more than ten feet from the front of the primary
residential structure on the property. A sold sign may be displayed on the
permitted sign, for a period not to exceed ten days. An open house sign may be
displayed on the property on the day of the open house and must be removed
immediately thereafter. Directional signs and/or flags are not authorized by
this section.
(Prior Code, § 10-10-3-1) (Ord. passed 3-20-1984; Ord. 99-113, passed 7-6-1999)
§ 158.143 SIGNS IN BUSINESS DISTRICTS.
   In a B district, the following signs shall be permitted:
   (A)   Any sign which pertains to a use conducted within the main building or
upon the premises and which is not physically attached beyond the boundaries of
the premises or on any part of a public way;
   (B)   Directional signs permitted in the R districts; and
   (C)   Outdoor temporary signs: temporary signs of a paper, plastic, wood or
fabric material are subject to the following restrictions.
      (1)   No such sign shall be of a size larger than 31 feet by five feet
unless otherwise approved by the Building Department.
      (2)   No more than two signs per 3,000 square feet of existing business
structure shall be allowed.
      (3)   Special event signs, additional signs or signs larger than
previously specified must be approved by the Building Department on a 30-day
basis.
      (4)   All outdoor temporary signs must be neat and orderly in appearance.
Any tattered, torn or faded signs must be removed upon notification by the
Building Department.
(Prior Code, § 10-10-3-2) (Ord. passed 7-5-1983; Ord. 93-225, passed 9-7-1993)
§ 158.144 SIGNS IN MANUFACTURING DISTRICTS.
   In an M district, the following signs shall be permitted:
   (A)   Signs identifying the occupant of a building or buildings; and
   (B)   Directional signs permitted as in R districts.
(Prior Code, § 10-10-3-3)
§ 158.145 SIGNS IN ALL DISTRICTS.
   The following conditions shall be observed in all of the use districts.
   (A)   No sign shall be placed in a required front yard except as provided in
§
158.142(B) of this chapter.
   (B)   Notwithstanding any provisions of this chapter, portable electric
signs of any kind are not permitted in any district.
   (C)   Portable signs shall be permitted on a temporary basis subject to the
following restrictions.
      (1)   No such portable sign shall be in any manner attached, connected or
otherwise supplied with electrical current.
      (2)   Portable signs shall be allowed for one 30-day period within any 12
months for special promotions in connection with a licensed business or
commercial establishment within the village.
      (3)   Prior to the use of any portable sign, a permit must be secured
through the village’s Building Department and the fee for such permit shall be
fixed at the sum of $50 for each 30-day display period.
(Prior Code, § 10-10-3-4) (Ord. passed 5-25-1976; Ord. 89-125, passed 10-11-
1989; Ord. 99-113, passed 7-6-1999)
ANTENNAS
§ 158.160 CONSTRUCTION REGULATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Permit required; fee. The owner of any property upon which an antenna
is to be erected shall first obtain a permit from the village. The fee for such
permit shall be $50.
   (B)   Codes and regulations.
      (1)   All antennas shall comply with BOCA and FCC rules and requirements.
      (2)   All antennas utilizing standard line voltage electrical current or
erected for commercial or industrial users shall require compliance with all
electrical codes of the village and a permit for such installation shall
include an electrical inspection and the fee for same.
   (C)   Construction specifications.
      (1)   (a)   All antennas shall be constructed and erected in a secure and
wind-resistant manner.
         (b)   Further, all antennas shall be sufficiently wind-resistant to
withstand winds of 80 mph normally and 70 mph when combined with ice.
      (2)   Antennas shall be no larger in size than is required for the proper
reception or transmission of signals for the application for which such antenna
is erected.
   (D)   Installers. All installers of antennas must be bonded and licensed to
work in the village and maintain proof of insurance as normally required of
other contractors.
(Prior Code, § 10-11-1)
§ 158.161 GROUND-MOUNTED ANTENNAS.
   (A)   Ground-mounted antennas and structure shall not exceed the height
permitted of principal structures in the zoning district in which they are
located.
   (B)   All antennas shall be ground-mounted at the closest allowable location
to the ground except when a higher or different location is required for signal
reception. Additionally, all antennas shall meet height and location
requirements of the zoning regulations of the village for the zoning district
within which such antenna is located.
   (C)   The base of all ground-mounted antennas shall be screened by
landscaping to a minimum height of six feet above ground.
   (D)   (1)   Upon demonstration that a ground-mounted antenna is insufficient
for its intended use and upon application for special use and payment of the
appropriate fee, a roof-mounted antenna may be permitted to be constructed on
the premises.
      (2)   However, such antenna shall not exceed a height of 12 feet above
the height of the building to which it is attached in residential districts.
      (3)   In business and industrial districts, the maximum allowable height
shall be no more than 35 feet above the principal structure to which it is
attached.
(Prior Code, § 10-11-2)
§ 158.162 ZONING REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Antennas shall be an allowable accessory use in all districts where
they are allowable as a principal use.
   (B)   Each antenna shall serve only the principal building located upon the
zoning lot on which said antenna is constructed pursuant to this chapter,
unless otherwise permitted by special use.
   (C)   All antennas located in residential districts and exceeding a width of
three feet shall be constructed so as to permit 50% transparency of light.
   (D)   No antenna may be located less than 50 feet from the front lot line of
the property, except when such antenna is attached to an existing steeple,
chimney or building equipment bulkhead.
   (E)   All setback restrictions otherwise applicable to accessory structures
in the appropriate zoning district shall be applicable to ground-mounted
antennas.
(Prior Code, § 10-11-4) (Ord. 87-138, passed 11-24-1987)
SPECIAL USES
§ 158.175 PURPOSE.
   The principal objective of these zoning regulations is to provide for an
orderly arrangement of compatible building and land uses, and for the proper
location of all types of uses required for the social and economic welfare of
the village. To accomplish this objective, each type and kind of use is
classified as permitted in one or more of the various districts established by
this chapter. However, in addition to those uses specifically classified and
permitted in each district, there are certain additional uses which it may be
necessary to allow because of their unusual characteristics or the service they
provide the public. These special uses require particular considerations as to
their proper location in relation to adjacent established or intended uses, or
to the planned development of the community. The conditions controlling the
location and operation of such special uses are established by the following
provisions of this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 10-12-1)
§ 158.176 PERMITTED SPECIAL USES; AUTHORITY.
   The village’s Board of Trustees shall have authority to permit the following
uses of land or structures, or both, subject to conditions contained herein, if
it finds that the proposed location and establishment of any such use will be
desirable or necessary to the public convenience or welfare and will be
harmonious and compatible with other uses adjacent to and in the vicinity of
